units.la: ILLVSTRISSIMO AC POTENTISSIMO PRINCIPI ET DOMINO, DN. GEORGIO FRIDE- RICO, MARGRAVIO BADENSI ET HOCHBERGENSI Landtgravio Sufenbergensi, Domino in Rotelen & Badenweiler, &c. Principi ac Domino suo clementissimo.
units.tr: MOST ILLUSTRIOUS AND MOST POWERFUL PRINCE AND LORD, LORD GEORGE FREDERICK, MARGRAVE OF BADEN AND HOCHBERG, LANDGRAVE OF SUFENBERG, LORD OF RÖTELN AND BADENWEILER, ETC., HIS MOST GRACIOUS PRINCE AND LORD.

units.la: ILLVSTRISSIME Princeps, Clementissime Domine, quemadmodum Regna huius mundi & Respublicae certas jam inde à condito orbe habuerunt periodos, quibus circumactis, maximis Imperijs & potentissimus Regnis fatales fuerunt, & universales mutationes attulerunt, ut plane novam faciem seu formam induerint, sicut historia dilucide testantur: ita etiam Regnum Christi, seu militans in hisce terris Ecclesia, ab Ascensione Domini in coelos suas periodos, cuprimus in doctrina & externis ritibus habuit. Completuntur periodi autem ista ut plurimum annos circiter quingentos: quamvis negari non possit, hunc periodorum numerum non fuisse perpetuum & universale, & plurima Regna vix dimidium ejus exegisse. Nam si rerum potiantur Principes & Magistratus impij, ac omnis generis scelera & flagitia etiam inter subditos regnent impune, sequuntur justo Dei judicio poenā, quae mutationes accelerando, constitutos terminos aliquot annis ante vertunt.
units.tr: Most Illustrious Prince, most gracious Lord: just as the kingdoms of this world and commonwealths have had certain fixed cycles since the world was founded, and when these have run their course they have proved fatal to the greatest empires and most powerful kingdoms, bringing about universal changes so that they put on an altogether new face or form, as history clearly bears witness, so too the kingdom of Christ, that is, the Church militant on these earth, has had its own cycles from the Ascension of the Lord into heaven, of which the first was marked in doctrine and external rites. These cycles usually last about five hundred years, although it cannot be denied that this number of periods was not constant and universal, and that many kingdoms have scarcely completed half of it. For when impious princes and magistrates hold power, and every kind of crime and vice rages unpunished even among the subjects, then by the just judgment of God punishment follows, which hastens the changes and overturns the appointed limits some years early.

units.la: Si autem de Origine & progressu vera ac falsa doctrina, deq; mutationibus & erroribus in Ecclesia Christi exortis, recte judicare & loqui velimus, semper ad primam periodum, atque adeo ad aureum illam aetatem recurrendum est, in qua Christus aeternus Filius Dei in assumpta humanitate, & sancti Apostoli viva voce ac scriptis docuerunt, velut omnium praestantissimam, incorruptissimam, & caeterarum omnium normam seu regulam certissimam. Si quid enim non solum in principalibus doctrina & Fidei articulis, sed etiam in Ceremonijs & Ritibus externis discrepaverit deinceps, id merito suspectum, vel saltem longe inferiori loco haberi debet. Unde etiam recte ille dixisse videtur, Id verius quod prius, id prius quod a principio.
units.tr: If, however, we wish to judge and speak rightly about the origin and progress of true and false doctrine, and about the changes and errors that have arisen in the Church of Christ, we must always go back to the first period, and so to that golden age in which Christ, the eternal Son of God in his assumed humanity, and the holy Apostles taught by living voice and in writings, as the most excellent and most incorruptible norm, and the most certain rule of all the rest. For if anything has since diverged, not only in the chief doctrines and articles of faith but also in ceremonies and external rites, it deserves to be viewed with suspicion, or at least to be held in far lower esteem. Whence he seems to have spoken rightly as well: that is truer which is earlier, and that is earlier which is from the beginning.

units.la: Docuit autem Christus, impletis suo adventu, adeoq; abrogatis umbris ac typis seu figuris legalibus, jam in Dei cultu hoc unum diligentissime spectandum, quod olim adumbratum fuerit, sic, ut fideles porro non amplius in puerilibus istis ceremoniis & ritibus veteris Testamenti ceu pupis quibusdam, sed in præstandis vera in Christum fidei, & pietatis officiis occupati esse debeant, qui cultus ille Spiritus & Veritatis est, de quo Christus ipse Ioh. 4. cap. loquitur, quòd Deus illo in posterum coli velit. Vt veró nervi quidam essent publicorum conventuum, quibus Christiani homines erudirentur, eisq; externis quibusdam symbolis remissio peccatorum et justitia coram Deo ceu sigillis obsignaretur, huic doctrinæ paucißimas addidit ceremonias, Baptismum videlicet & Cœnam sacram.
units.tr: Christ taught, however, that with his coming the shadows and types or legal figures were fulfilled and so abrogated, so that now in the worship of God this one thing is to be most diligently attended to, namely what was once foreshadowed. Thus the faithful should no longer be occupied with those childish ceremonies and rites of the Old Testament, as with certain dolls, but with performing the duties of true faith in Christ and of piety. This is that worship of Spirit and Truth of which Christ himself speaks in John 4, saying that God wishes to be worshipped in this way from now on. And so that there would be certain sinews of public assemblies by which Christian people might be instructed, and by which the forgiveness of sins and righteousness before God might be sealed to them, as with seals, by certain outward signs, he added to this doctrine very few ceremonies, namely Baptism and the Holy Supper.

units.la: Hanc formam doctrinæ & ceremoniarum, ut simplicissima, ita quoq; perfectissimam & omnibus suis numeris obsolutissimam, sicut à Servatore acceperant, ita etiá fideliter retinuerunt Apostoli, nihil omninò desuo vel assuentes, vel detrahentes, suisque eam tradiderunt successoribus & posteris, quam hi quoque integram, puram & incorruptam ad multos annos conservárunt: testem huius habeo Eusebium, qui ex Egesippo refert, quòd illius tempore in singulis successionibus & civitatibus itase res habere deprehenderit, quemadmodum lex, Prophetæ & ipse Dominus Iesus prædicâssent. Noverunt siquidem adhuc illa aurea secula, corporalem exercitationem paululum habere utilitatis in vera Ecclesia Christi, & humanis traditionibus frustra Deum coli, ijsq; sincera religione sœdissimè corrumpi.
units.tr: This form of doctrine and ceremonies, as it was most simple, so also most perfect and in every respect most complete, just as they had received it from the Saviour, so the Apostles faithfully kept it, adding or subtracting nothing at all, and handed it down to their successors and posterity. These too preserved it whole, pure and uncorrupted for many years. I have as witness Eusebius, who reports from Hegesippus that in his time, in the successions of bishops and in the cities, things were found to be just as the Law, the Prophets and the Lord Jesus himself had foretold. Indeed those golden ages knew that bodily exercise is of little use in the true Church of Christ, that God is worshipped in vain by human traditions, and that worship is most foully corrupted by them in sincere religion.

units.la: Cúm verò status Ecclesiæ trecentis primis annis & aliquot sequentibus prima periodi ad ἀκμὴν summamq; perfectionem pervenisset, natura autem ultra hanc in terris nihil instituat, factâ conversione, cunctæ degenerare & in peius ruere cœperunt. Habuerunt quidem illa quoq; tempora præstantes aliquot & illustres Doctores, tamen omnes prope à puritate & simplicitate doctrinæ Apostolicæ & proximè præcedentis Ecclesiæ nonnihil recesserunt. Ea verò occasione factum est, ut mox in admiratione cœperint esse variæ ἐΦελόξρnσxíεs, quæ etiam in opinione meriti abijsse jam tum videntur. Inprimis verò admiratione dignum est quòd adfinem suum prima hac periodo accelerante, Spiritus Antichristi per Episcopos Romanos semina sui primatus supra omnes alios Episcopos sic impudenter sparsit, ut in hujus periodi fine quasi in aluum & intra viscera Ecclesiæ receptus merito videri queat.
units.tr: But when the state of the Church had reached its peak and highest perfection (ἀκμή) in the first three hundred years and some of the following ones of the first period, and since nature establishes nothing beyond this point on earth, once the turning point had been reached, all things began to degenerate and rush toward worse. Those times, to be sure, also had some outstanding and illustrious teachers, yet almost all of them departed somewhat from the purity and simplicity of the Apostolic doctrine and of the Church immediately preceding them. On that occasion it came about that soon various self-chosen forms of worship [ἐθελοθρησκεῖαι] began to be held in esteem, and even then they seem to have gained a reputation for merit. Especially worthy of wonder is that, as this first period was hastening toward its end, the Spirit of Antichrist so shamelessly sowed through the Roman bishops the seeds of their primacy over all other bishops that at the end of this period it can rightly be seen as though received into the belly and bowels of the Church.

units.la: Facies igitur Ecclesiæ sic nonnihil deformata, tristis fuit circa principium secundæ periodi, quæ paulò ante Gregorij Magni ætatem cœpit, & ad Heinrici Quarti Imperatoris tempora usque duravit: quæ tamen ferri aliquo modo potuisset, nisi in progressu ejus tristiorem, & circa finem tristissimam plané & fœdissimam nasta fuisset. Causæ ejus fuerunt non solùm jasta in priore periodo errorum fundamenta, & quasi spársa semina, sed etiam irruptiones horrendæ barbararum gentium in Europam.
units.tr: The face of the Church was thus somewhat disfigured, and it was sad at the beginning of the second period, which began shortly before the time of Gregory the Great and lasted down to the times of the Emperor Henry IV. Yet it might have been borne in some fashion, had it not in its course grown sadder and, near its end, altogether most sad and foul. Its causes were not only the foundations of error laid in the former period and the seeds, as it were, scattered abroad, but also the horrible irruptions of barbarian peoples into Europe.

units.la: PRÆFATIO.
units.tr: PREFACE.

units.la: pam, quæ annos plus minus centum sexaginta totum Occidentem vexârunt. Hîc dici non potest, quantam in hoc perturbatissimo rerum omnium statu vera religio, pura doctrina, pietas & eruditio in Occidentalibus Ecclesiis jacturam fecerit. In has igitur occasiones intentus hostis humani generis, horribiles & pernitiosas tenebras, ceu nubes quasdam atras, totum cælum occupantes, in Ecclesiam Christi simul induxit, per ipsos Doctores & Ecclesiarum Antistites maximè, quos inter Romanus Episcopus Gregorius Magnus facile primas tenet, qui duarum præcipuè rerum, quæ horribilem inclinationem & ruinam Ecclesiæ attulerunt, Invocationis nimirum hominum mortuorum, & Sacrificiorum pro mortuis, auctor & quasi fundator fuit: Ceremoniis etiam plus quàm Iudaicis & Ethnicis Ecclesiam & religionem Christianam mirum in modum oneravit, quarum splendore & pompâ mentes hominum mirificè captæ & fascinatæ fuerunt.
units.tr: ...pam, which for roughly one hundred and sixty years plagued the whole West. Here it cannot be said how great a loss true religion, pure doctrine, piety and learning suffered in the Western Churches in this most troubled state of all things. Seizing upon these opportunities, the enemy of the human race, intent on mischief, brought into the Church of Christ horrible and pernicious darkness, like dark clouds covering the whole sky, chiefly through the teachers and bishops of the Churches. Among these the Roman bishop Gregory the Great easily holds first place. He was the author and, as it were, the founder of two chief things which brought about the terrible decline and ruin of the Church: the invocation of dead men, and sacrifices for the dead. He also burdened the Church and the Christian religion in a wonderful way with ceremonies more than Jewish and heathen, by whose splendour and pomp men's minds were wonderfully captivated and bewitched.

units.la: Quæ quidem gravia sunt, & piis animis hanc fœdam & deturpatam faciem Ecclesiæ diligenter contemplantibus, suspiria ac tantum non lachrymas movent. Verùm longè infeliciora & tenebricosiora tempora sequuta sunt, rebus subindè justo DEI judicio & vindicta in pejus ruentibus. Antichristus enim paulò ante in utero Ecclesiæ conceptus, sub Bonifacio Romano Episcopo in lucem editus, non amplius in mysterio, sed palam operari cæpit. Nam cultum Deorum alienorum instituit, Sanctos mortuos invocatione statuarum, imaginum, templorum & altarium exstructione honorari præcepit, & statuas ligneas adoratione colendas esse pronunciavit: Synodos, iconolatriam oppugnantes, damnavit, & velut Dictator quidam subditis præcepit, ne ejusmodi Magistratibus, venerationem & invocationem abolentibus, obedientiam ullam præstent; Ceremonias à majoribus suis & prædecessoribus inventas non modò retinuit, sed etiam prodigiosè accumulavit, plus quàm dimidiâ parte secundæ hujus periodi evoluta. Baptismum & Cœnam Domini multis ac variis traditionib. humanis contaminavit, & in alios usus transtulit, quæ à Christo instituta fuerunt. Inter hæc verò Ecclesia & sponsa Christi parùm præsidij habuit, sed ab omnibus orba cœpit fieri, & quasi ovis in medio luporum constituta tanquam præda expósita fuit, Doctoribus ejus omne suam operam Antichristo locantibus, præmia inde amplissima reportantibus, & si qui fuerunt, qui his rebus Ecclesiæ afflictissimis succurrere & auxilium ferre cuperet, mox vel calumniis, vel apertâ vi oppressi, atq; efficacia errorum & omnis generis superstitionum victi fuerunt.
units.tr: These things are indeed grave, and they move devout hearts, as they carefully contemplate this foul and disfigured face of the Church, to sighs and almost to tears. But far more unhappy and darker times followed, as affairs, by the just judgment and vengeance of God, went from bad to worse. For Antichrist, conceived in the womb of the Church shortly before, was brought to light under Boniface, Roman bishop, and began to work no longer in mystery but openly. For he established the worship of alien gods; he commanded that dead saints be honoured by the invocation of statues, images, and the erection of temples and altars; and he declared that wooden statues were to be worshipped with adoration. He condemned the councils that opposed image-worship, and, like a kind of dictator, he ordered his subjects not to render any obedience to such magistrates as abolished veneration and invocation. The ceremonies invented by his elders and predecessors he not only retained but also prodigiously multiplied, the second half of this period having been unrolled. He polluted Baptism and the Lord's Supper with many and various human traditions, and transferred to other uses what Christ had instituted. Meanwhile the Church and the bride of Christ had little protection; she began to be made bereft by all, and, placed like a sheep in the midst of wolves, she was exposed as prey. Her teachers devoted all their effort to Antichrist, reaping from it the richest rewards; and if there were any who wished to help and bring aid to this most afflicted Church, they were soon overwhelmed either by slanders or by open force, and conquered by the power of errors and superstitions of every kind.

units.la: Excepit hunc tristissimum Ecclesiæ statum tertia periodus, quæ initio regni Henrici Quarti Imperatoris cœpit, & se ad annum quingentesimum supra millesimum usque extendit. Hæc verò majorem mutationem Ecclesiæ & Imperijs quàm prior attulit. Nam invexit in Ecclesiam
units.tr: The third period followed this most sorrowful state of the Church. It began at the start of the reign of the Emperor Henry IV and extended to the year one thousand five hundred after the thousandth. This period brought a greater change to the Church and to empires than the former one. For it introduced into the Church...

units.la: PRÆFATIO.
units.tr: PREFACE.

units.la: faciem prorsus novam, nec prioribus seculis unquam visam, regnum vi‑ delicet politiys simile, & ab eo, non dico quod in prima, sed in secunda ad‑ huc periodo fuit diversum. In priore periodo Antichristus majorem principatum seu dominium nactus est artibus suis, quam ipsi conveniret; nihilominus tamen nondum adhuc arbitrio privato omnia administrare in Ecclesiis ausus fuit: In hac vero periodo tertia, non solum, quod media parte secunda periodi circumactã facere coeperat, caput suum extulit supra omnes alios toto orbe Christiano Pastores: sed veluti summus quidam totius orbis Monarcha, sibi soli arrogavit potestatem constituendi & investiendi Episcopos, convocandi Concilia & Synodos, ipsque praesidendi, & ibi pro sua libidine decernendi controversias, praescribendiq; ceremonias religionis formulas: imo quasi nihil aut parum hoc esset, summa audacia in politicum imperium irrupit, sibique regna hujus mundi arrogavit: voluit etiam ipsos Imperatores, Reges ac Principes ceteros a se, Dominos scilicet a servis, regnorum possessionem petere & accipere debere: quin leges quoque praescripsit Imperatoribus ac Regibus, a quibus ipse hucusque leges acceperat: causarum insuper politicarum cognitionem & decisionem sibi soli vendicavit, gloriatusque est, in scrinio pectoris sui omnia jura contineri, & proinde cunctos homines debere pro legibus habere quaecunque ipse dixerit. Hac effreni audacia atque impudentia Monarchiam ex politico & Ecclesiastico regimine mixtam constituit, faciem Imperii Romani prorsus mutavit, seseque supra omne quod dicitur Deus exaltavit.
units.tr: It brought in a face wholly new, never seen in earlier centuries: a kingdom, namely, resembling a political state, and different from that which had existed, I do not say in the first period, but even in the second. In the earlier period Antichrist had gained a greater principality or dominion by his arts than was fitting for him; nevertheless he had not yet dared to administer everything in the churches by private will. In this third period, however, which he had begun to make in the middle of the second, he raised his head above all the other pastors of the whole Christian world. Like a certain supreme monarch of the whole world, he claimed for himself alone the power of appointing and installing bishops, of convoking councils and synods, of presiding over them and there deciding controversies at his own pleasure, and of prescribing ceremonies and formulas of religion. Indeed, as if this were nothing or too little, he burst with the greatest audacity into the political empire and arrogated to himself the kingdoms of this world. He also wished emperors, kings and other princes to seek and receive possession of their kingdoms from him, as lords from servants. Nay, he even prescribed laws to emperors and kings, from whom he himself had hitherto received laws. Moreover he claimed for himself alone the cognizance and decision of political causes, and boasted that all rights are contained in the coffer of his breast, and that therefore all men ought to hold as laws whatever he himself should say. By this unbridled audacity and impudence he constituted a monarchy mixed of political and ecclesiastical government, utterly changed the face of the Roman Empire, and exalted himself above everything that is called God.

units.la: In hac eminentia constitutus Antichristus, in hoc novum suum regnum, ad priores idololatrias, novum & prioribus seculis incognitum DEVM Phanaceum introduxit, quem sacra litera DEVM Maozim nominant, eique peculiare festum magna cum solennitate & reverentia celebrandum instituit. Hic novus Deus occupavit in Ecclesia omnem cultum adorationis & venerationis soli Deo debitum, omniumque oculos & mentes a vero Deo ad se pellexit: Hoc sese in processionibus & theatrica Missa ostentante, conticuit coelestis doctrina.
units.tr: Set up on this height, Antichrist, in this his new kingdom, introduced, besides the earlier idolatries, a new god, the god Maozim (a Phanaceum), unknown in earlier centuries, whom the sacred letters name Maozim, and he instituted for him a special feast to be celebrated with great solemnity and reverence. This new god occupied in the Church all the worship of adoration and veneration owed to God alone, and drew the eyes and minds of all away from the true God to himself. While he displayed himself in processions and in theatrical Masses, the heavenly doctrine fell silent.

units.la: Et quod in primis notandum est, hoc DEO regnante, prodijt etiam novum doctrinae genus in Ecclesia, quod Scholasticam doctrinam appellant, hac occasione: Quum Romani Pontifices non solum errores superioribus seculis introductos, sed jam etiam portentosum illud dogma Transsubstantiationis, tanquam fontem infinitorum aliorum errorum, pertinacitor defenderent, & contra sentientes immani tyrannide persequerentur ac opprimerent, sicut Berengarij & aliorum exempla evidenter docent; factum est, ut illa Theologia, qualiscunque tum fuit, a plerisque negligeretur, nec fere alij, quam pauci Monachi ei adhaerent, & ad juris Civilis studium Italica & Germanica ingenia certatim confluerent.
units.tr: And what must be noted above all, under the reign of this god there also arose in the Church a new kind of teaching, which they call Scholastic doctrine, and this on the following occasion. Since the Roman pontiffs stubbornly defended not only the errors introduced in earlier centuries, but also that monstrous dogma of Transubstantiation, as the source of countless other errors, and persecuted and oppressed those who thought otherwise with savage tyranny, as the examples of Berengar and others clearly show, it came about that that theology, such as it then was, was neglected by most, and hardly anyone except a few monks clung to it, while Italian and German minds eagerly flocked to the study of civil law.

units.la: PRÆFATIO.
units.tr: Preface.

units.la: confluerent. Hoc vero quum ingentem cladem, & tantum non ruinam non solùm Theologiæ istius temporis, sed etiam recenti, nec dum satis confirmatæ Romanorum Pontificum tyrannidi minitari videretur, GRATIANVS Monachus, ut afflictis his suæ partis rebus aliquam opem & auxilium ferret, legum Pontificiarum Volumen consarcinavit & congessit circa annos Christi 1150, quod Decretorum opus nominatur, & hodie pro prima parte juris Canonici seu Pontificij habetur. In eo hierarchiam & tyrannidem Pontificum Romanorum propugnandam susceperat ex Canonum Decretis. In hunc finem excerpsit Canones in hoc Volumine ex quatuor potissimum scriptorum generibus: alios quidem ex Conciliis & Synodis: alios ex Epistolis Decretalibus primorum Pontificum Romanorum, alios ex scriptis Patrum: alios denique ex historiis Ecclesiasticis; sed eâ fide, ut magno cum judicio hæc omnia legenda sint, multa siquidem falsa, commentitia & notha recitat; tum vera impudenter, malitiosè, fallaciter & impiè corrumpit; sæpenumero turpiter errat in authorum & librorum inscriptionibus, Hieronymo adscribit quod tribuendum erat Augustino, aut simili; ex uno Concilio profert Canonem qui alterius est; titulum facit ex Epistola Decretali alicujus Pontificis, in qua tamen nihil tale reperitur: & tamen tanto applausu acceptum approbatumque fuit hoc Opus à Pontificibus Romanis, ut mox Eugenius Tertius secundum id in Consistoriis judicare præceperit. Sequutus mox est Gratianum Petrus Lombardus Parisiensis Episcopus, qui in Theologia versari maluit, quàm in Forensibus litigiosisq; quæstionibus. Itaq; Scholasticæ Theologiæ, qualis tunc erat, fundamenta in quatuor libros, qui sententiarum dicuntur, congessit. Hi quatuor libri, non ex viva verbi DEI scaturigine, sed Patrum duntaxat lacunis desumpti, fuerunt postea totius Scholasticæ doctrinæ basis & fundamentum: Unde ipse etiam vulgò in Scholis Magister Sententiarum appellari cœpit.
units.tr: flocked together. But when this seemed to threaten a huge disaster, and almost the ruin, not only of the theology of that time but also of the recently established and not yet firmly secured tyranny of the Roman Pontiffs, GRATIAN the Monk, in order to bring some aid and help to his party in these afflicted circumstances, compiled and assembled a collection of Pontifical laws around the year of Christ 1150. It is called the Decretorum opus, and today it is held as the first part of the canon law, or Pontifical law. In it he undertook to defend the hierarchy and tyranny of the Roman Pontiffs from the decrees of the canons. To this end he excerpted the canons in this volume from four main kinds of writings: some from councils and synods, some from the decretal epistles of the early Roman Pontiffs, some from the writings of the Fathers, and finally some from ecclesiastical histories. But they must all be read with great judgment, for he recites many things that are false, fabricated and spurious; moreover he shamelessly, maliciously, deceitfully and impiously corrupts true things; he very often errs shamefully in the titles of authors and books, ascribing to Jerome what should be attributed to Augustine or someone similar; he brings forward from one council a canon that belongs to another; he makes a heading from the decretal epistle of some Pontiff, in which nothing of the kind is found. And yet this work was received and approved by the Roman Pontiffs with such applause that soon afterwards Eugenius III ordered that judgments in the consistories be made according to it. Soon after Gratian was followed by Peter Lombard, bishop of Paris, who preferred to occupy himself with theology rather than with forensic and litigious questions. Thus he gathered the foundations of scholastic theology, such as it then was, into four books, which are called the Sentences. These four books, drawn not from the living fountain of the Word of God but only from the gleanings of the Fathers, afterwards became the whole basis and foundation of all scholastic doctrine; whence he himself also began to be commonly called in the schools the Master of the Sentences.

units.la: Sequitur jam media Scholastica prior illa longè deterior, quæ duravit ab anno Christi millesimo ducentesimo vigesimo, ad annum usque millesimum trecentesimum trigesimum, & habuit Albertum M. velut parentem & authorem. Is enim Philosophiam humanam, inprimis Aristotelicam in ipsa adyta Scholarum Theologicarum & penetralia Ecclesiarum intromisit, & in supremo ibi controversarum quæstionum dijudicandarum ac decidendarum gradu & throno, ceu Reginam quandam collocavit: quo factum est, ut Aristoteli & Philosophiæ humanæ, magna cum religionis perniciè, principatus in Schola Christi attributus, & de possessione hereditaria Christus depulsus sit. Superior enim Scholastica Patrum quidem, sed Ecclesiasticorum duntaxat scripta ac dicta verbo DEI exæquavit: hæc vero ulterius progressa, Aristotelis etiam scripta
units.tr: There now follows the middle Scholasticism, the earlier and far worse one, which lasted from the year of Christ 1220 to the year 1330, and had Albert the Great as its parent and author. For he introduced human philosophy, chiefly the Aristotelian, into the very sanctuaries of the theological schools and the innermost parts of the churches, and set it up there as a kind of queen on the supreme throne and in the highest seat for judging and deciding controverted questions. As a result, principacy in Christ's School was granted to Aristotle and human philosophy, to the great ruin of religion, and Christ was driven out of his hereditary possession. For the earlier Scholasticism had put the writings and sayings of the Fathers, but only of the churchmen, on a par with the Word of God; but this later one went further, and also the writings of Aristotle

units.la: PRÆFATIO.
units.tr: PREFACE.

units.la: Verbo Dei in omnibus coparavit, ut qua vestigia exigua illius erga verbum Dei reverentia in Theologorum scholis restarent adhuc, ab hac penitus deleta & conculcata fuerint. Cum enim errores & abusus vel recepti consuetudine, vel à Pontificibus Romanis approbati tueri defendi non possent, si ad verbi Dei lydium lapidem examinarentur, alia fuerunt quarenda præsidia. In hac igitur Scholastica non Prophetarum, non Christi, non Apostolorum, non deniq; Augustini, Hieronymi, Ambrosij & similium, sed Aristotelis tantum fit mentio, eius nomen primo semper loco ponitur, eiusq; scripta pro apodicticis, verbum autem Dei pro opinione saltem probabili habetur, ut ex Occami Centilogio apparet. Hinc evenit, ut qui illis temporibus pro insigni Theologo seu Doctore haberi cuperet, non in Prophetas, Evangelistas, vel Apostolorum Epistolas, sed Aristotelis tantum libros Commentaria scriberet. Fecit hoc primus Albertus M. & eum deinde sequutus Thomas Aquinas, aliiq; non pauci.
units.tr: in all things he equated it with the Word of God, so that whatever small traces of reverence for the Word of God still remained in the schools of the theologians were completely wiped out and trampled underfoot. For since errors and abuses, whether sanctioned by long custom or approved by the Roman Pontiffs, could not be defended if they were tested by the touchstone of the Word of God, other defences had to be sought. In this Scholastic theology, therefore, there is no mention of the Prophets, of Christ, of the Apostles, nor finally of Augustine, Jerome, Ambrose and their like, but only of Aristotle. His name is always placed first, and his writings are held to be demonstrative, whereas the Word of God is held to be at most a probable opinion, as is clear from Occam's Centilogue. Hence it happened that whoever in those times wished to be regarded as a distinguished theologian or teacher did not write commentaries on the Prophets, the Evangelists or the Epistles of the Apostles, but only on the books of Aristotle. Albert the Great did this first, and after him Thomas Aquinas and not a few others.

units.la: Interea vero temporis non cessarunt Canonistæ etiam, sed in evehenda Pontificum Rom. authoritate strenuè laborárut, ad imitationem Gratiani. Reimundus enim Barchinonensis Monachus Hispanus circa annos 1230. iussu Gregorij IX. Decretales edidit, in quibus ne verbulum quidem exstat de institutis veteris Ecclesiæ, nihil in ijs habetur ex S. Scriptura, nihil ex antiquis historijs, nihil ex sanctorum Patrum libris & scriptis, sed nova sunt plane omnia, nec Theologis & Ecclesiarum ministris, leguleis & causidicis ad propugnandam Pontificum Rom. immanem tyrannidem accommodata. Hos etiam Decretales in Scholis publice prælegi & explicari idem Gregorius præcepit. Vidit enim astutissimus homo, Pontificatum Rom. agrè confirmatum iri, nisi legibus latis, ac his quoq; cum authoritate promulgatis & in Scholas ac judicia introductis.
units.tr: Meanwhile, however, the canonists also did not cease, but laboured vigorously to exalt the authority of the Roman Pontiffs, following the example of Gratian. For Raymond of Penyafort, a Spanish monk of Barcelona, around the year 1230, published the Decretals by command of Gregory IX. In them there is not even a little word about the institutions of the ancient Church; nothing is taken from Holy Scripture, nothing from ancient histories, nothing from the books and writings of the holy Fathers, but everything is plainly new, and it is fitted not to theologians and ministers of the Churches, but to lawyers and pleaders, for defending the monstrous tyranny of the Roman Pontiffs. Gregory also ordered these Decretals to be publicly read and expounded in the schools. For that most astute man saw that the papacy of Rome could scarcely be established unless laws were enacted, and these too promulgated with authority and introduced into the schools and the courts.

units.la: Hinc Bonifacius VIII. anno 1295. in Lugdunensi Concilio Sextum Decretalium confirmavit, suo jussu à tribus doctis viris, ut Platina refert, compilatum, eundemque mandavit etiam passim in Scholis prælegi & explicari.
units.tr: Hence Boniface VIII, in the year 1295, in the Council of Lyons, confirmed the Sixth Book of the Decretals, which, as Platina relates, had been compiled by three learned men at his command; and he likewise ordered that it be read and expounded in the schools everywhere.

units.la: Clemens V. superaddidit anno 1308. in Concilio Viennensi librum Clementinarum à se compositum, qui quartam partem juris Pontificij efficit, ac in Scholis similiter prælegendum mandavit, ut Trithemius in Chronico Hirsaugiensi indicat. In utroque opere non alia tractantur, quàm in Decretalibus explicantur, utpote quæ super addita sunt, vel quia in Decretalibus ofcitanter prætermissa fuerunt, vel quòd ampliato jam foro Pontificio, usus ipse forensis digna comprobárit quæ attexerentur. Unde liquet, in quarum rerum explicatione ista librorum congeries & moles maximè insumatur.
units.tr: Clement V added, in the year 1308, in the Council of Vienne, a book of the Clementines composed by himself, which forms a fourth part of the Pontifical law, and he likewise ordered that it be read in the schools, as Trithemius indicates in the Chronicle of Hirsau. In both works there are treated no other things than are explained in the Decretals, since they were added either because they had been carelessly passed over in the Decretals, or because, the papal jurisdiction having now been extended, forensic practice itself had approved matters worth adding. Whence it is clear that in the explanation of these matters this mass and bulk of books is chiefly consumed.

units.la: Et tamen his omnibus postremo loco quasi appendix annexa est cum à diversis Pontificibus, tum verò maximè à Ioanne XXII. circa annas 1320. feries
units.tr: And yet, after all these, as an appendix attached at the end, there are the series of decrees issued by various Pontiffs, and above all by John XXII around the year 1320.

units.la: PRÆFATIO
units.tr: PREFACE

units.la: 1320. feries quaedam Constitutionum, quas Extravagantes vocant. Atq; ita ex Canonum exigua scaturigine à Gratiano collectorum, in vastum quendam Oceanum juris Canonici accessione temporis inundasse videtur. In eo, quo longius progredimur, eó offendimus Canones à pietate & sincera religione longius degenerantes.
units.tr: About the year 1320 there appeared a collection of constitutions which they call the Extravagantes. In this way the small spring of canons gathered by Gratian seems, over the course of time, to have flooded into a vast ocean of canon law. The further we advance in it, the more we find canons degenerating far from piety and sincere religion.

units.la: Sed quasi hoc parum, vel nihil esset, sequitur tertium Scholastice doctrinae genus, anno Christi 1330. & duravit ad annum usque millesimum quingentesimum decimum quintum, fuitque duobus prioribus longè deterrimum & impudentissimum: modestia enim, quæ in prima & media Scholastica adhuc in quadam deliberatione & quæstione posita erant, utrum scilicet Papa Rom. sit simplex homo, an quasi Deus? an participet utramque naturam cum Christo? an Papa sit supra Concilium? an Virgo Maria à peccato omni sit immunis? & aliis sexcentis similibus, de his certa quadam definire & determinare in hac Scholastica coeperunt, suasq; determinationes pro articulis fidei haberi voluerunt: denique nihil tam fuit superioribus seculis vilsumimpium, blasphemum, ineptum & erroneum, quod hæc Scholastica sua audacia, subtilitatibus, argutijs, distinctionibus, sophismatis, exceptionibus & oppositionibus non ausa sit palam propugnare ac defendere.
units.tr: But as if this were too little, or nothing at all, there follows a third kind of Scholastic teaching, beginning in the year of Christ 1330 and lasting until the year 1515. It was far worse and more shameless than the two earlier kinds. For whereas in the early and middle Scholastics these questions were still put forward as matters of deliberation and inquiry (whether the Roman Pope is a mere man or almost a god; whether he shares both natures with Christ; whether the Pope is above the Council; whether the Virgin Mary is free from all sin; and countless other such questions), these men began to define and determine such matters with certainty, and they wished their determinations to be held as articles of faith. In short, in earlier centuries there was nothing so vile, impious, blasphemous, absurd and erroneous that this Scholastic teaching, with its audacity, subtleties, quibbles, distinctions, sophisms, exceptions and objections, did not dare openly to champion and defend.

units.la: Inde Quodlibeta & quodlibetariæ quæstiones natæ, & à Gualtero Pictaviensi Episcopo editæ sunt circa annos Christi 1240. magna omnium admiratione. Sunt autem Quodlibeta libri, in quibus eorum authores in utramque partem, Academicorum more, de quolibet etiam apice Theologico pro & contrà disputant; ut nihil sit apud eos tam certum & definitum, quod non in dubium vocari possit, contrariaque rationes habeat: & qui hoc præstare potuerunt, pro optimis & excellentissimis Doctoribus habiti fuerunt.
units.tr: From this came the Quodlibeta and the quodlibetarian questions, which were published by Walter, Bishop of Poitiers, about the year of Christ 1240, to the great astonishment of all. Quodlibeta are books in which their authors dispute, in the manner of the Academics, on either side of any theological point whatever; so that nothing among them is so certain and settled that it cannot be called into doubt and has no opposing arguments. Those who could accomplish this were regarded as the best and most excellent teachers.

units.la: Ecce igitur, Clementissime Princeps, ut obscurata fuerit prorsus in hac tertia periodo aurea primitiva Ecclesia facies, & mutatus Evangelica doctrina color optimus. Versa est mihi (inquit Dominus apud Ezechiel.) domus Israel in scoriam, & degenerârunt Ecclesiarum Ministri in fæces & excrementa sordida.
units.tr: Behold, therefore, most merciful Prince, how utterly the face of the golden primitive Church was obscured in this third period, and how the excellent colour of the Gospel doctrine was changed. "The house of Israel has been turned into dross" (says the Lord through Ezekiel), and the ministers of the Churches have degenerated into dregs and filthy refuse.

units.la: Durârunt hæ plus quàm Cimmeria tenebræ ab Innocentio Tertio seu ab origine & ortu Mendicantium Monachorum maximè, hoc est, ab anno 1215. CHRISTI Salvatoris, ad initium quartæ periodi, & annum CHRISTI 1517 usque: quando DEUS Optimus Maximus ex immensa gratia humani generis misertus, duo illa clarissima lumina, Lutherum dico & Zwinglium, excitavit, qui primi omnium in Germania & Helvetia densissimas has nebulas & obscurissimas tenebras discusserunt, & Verbum DEI prorsus extinctum atque sepultum in lucem revocârunt, quò toti mundo luceret. Contra hanc vero patefactam
units.tr: These darknesses, thicker than Cimmerian gloom, lasted from Innocent III, or rather from the origin and rise especially of the Mendicant monks, that is from the year 1215 of Christ the Saviour, at the beginning of the fourth period, until the year of Christ 1517. Then God, the Best and Greatest, out of his immense grace and pity for the human race, raised up those two most brilliant lights, I mean Luther and Zwingli, who first of all in Germany and Helvetia dispelled these very dense mists and most obscure shadows, and brought back the Word of God, which had been all but extinguished and buried, into the light, so that it might shine on the whole world. But against this disclosed...

units.la: PRÆFATIO.
units.tr: PREFACE.

units.la: Veritatem mox fremuit, & adhuc hodie fremit ac frendet Satan, instituit Concilia, Synodos, disputationes & Colloquia : cumque hoc conatu nihil proficeret, sed veritas magis magisque emergeret, ad arma confugit, & potentissimos Imperatores, Reges ac Principes adversus renascentem ubique terrarum Evangelij puram doctrinam excitavit, & regna passim omnia bellis civilibus, seditionibus, aliisque horrendis motibus concussit, & summa imis miscuit.
units.tr: Satan immediately raged against the truth, and even today he still rages and gnashes his teeth. He set up councils, synods, disputations and colloquies. When this effort achieved nothing, but the truth emerged more and more, he took refuge in arms and stirred up the most powerful emperors, kings and princes against the pure doctrine of the Gospel, which was springing up everywhere on earth. He shook all kingdoms everywhere with civil wars, seditions and other horrible upheavals, and turned the highest things upside down.

units.la: Verum ne sic quidem conatus eius ex animi sententia succederunt, sed quo magis savijt, eo majores vires & incrementa, DEI benedictione, sumpsit Veritas. Cum igitur hostis humani generis animad verteret, Curiam Romanam, omnis idololatriæ officinam, labescere, & tantum non fœdam ruinam minitari, simulque intelligeret, Clericorum & Monachorum, quantum vis prapingues & crassos ventres, hanc ruinam non posse amplius fulcire ac sustentare, ut afflictis suis rebus mature succurreret, paulo post inchoatam quartam periodum novum fœtum, IESVITAS dico, in lucem edidit. Et hi quidem Satanæ in fulciendo ac sustinendo Antichristi regno strenuam operam locarunt. Unde etiam aufisunt Pontificiam cathedram ruentem, aut ruinam certe minitantem pingere, quam ipsi suis humeris, densa testudine conferti, sustinueret. Non puduit eos nec pudet adhuc hodie veternosos, turpissimos ac perniciosissimos, luce meridiana manifestiores errores, & superioribus seculis subintroductos, jam vero claritate doctrinæ cælestis in hac postrema mundi ætate Dei beneficio detectos, palliare, tegere, verborum lenociniis involuere, rhetoricisque coloribus pingere, maxime autem augustissimæ Catholicæ & Apostolicæ Ecclesiæ titulo ornare: adeoque nihil est tam crassum, tam putidum, tam impurum, tam insulsum, tam impium, tam fabulosum ac falsum in Pontificia lacuna & cloaca, quod novæ isti sectæ non bene oleat.
units.tr: Yet even so his attempts did not succeed as he wished. The more fiercely he raged, the greater the strength and growth the Truth gained, by the blessing of God. When the enemy of mankind therefore saw that the Roman Curia, the workshop of all idolatry, was tottering and threatened a almost shameful collapse, and understood that the Clergy and Monks, with their exceedingly fat and bloated bellies, could no longer prop up and sustain this ruin, he hastened to help his afflicted cause. Shortly after the fourth period had begun, he brought forth a new offspring into the light, the Jesuits I mean. And these men have laboured vigorously for Satan in propping up and sustaining the kingdom of Antichrist. Hence they have also dared to paint the Papal chair as collapsing, or at least threatening to collapse, which they, pressed together in a dense testudo, would hold up on their shoulders. They were not ashamed, and even today are not ashamed, to palliate, cover up, wrap in the wheedling of words and paint with rhetorical colours those old, shameful and most destructive errors, which are more obvious than midday light and were introduced in earlier centuries, and which, by the blessing of God, have now in this last age of the world been exposed by the clarity of heavenly doctrine; and above all to adorn them with the title of the most august Catholic and Apostolic Church. So nothing is so gross, so foul, so impure, so insipid, so impious, so fabulous and false in the Papist pool and sewer that it does not smell sweet to this new sect.

units.la: Attestatur hoc Paulus Florenius Theologiæ Doctor & Profess. in Colloquio cum Christiano Franco Philosophiæ Professore in Cæsareo Jesuitarum Gymnasio Vienna Austriæ anno 1578. 20. Januarij habito. In eius Colloquij initio hæc sunt verba Florenij Jesuitæ ad Francum: Videtur mihi, Christiane, rem omnem sincerius & subtilius contemplanti, nostra hæc, in qua versamur, religio Iesuitica tota ex superstitione, hypocrisi, & ficta quadam, pictaque sanctitate conflata, ultimaque hac mundi senectute a Diabolo excitata: quæ omnes errores, nugas & superstitiones : quæ (uno ut verbo dicam) minus honesto quidem, & quo sane invitus utor, sed huic rei aptissimo planeque necessario) quæ inquam omnia turpissima Papæ stercora (tum graviter per se olentia, tum vero hoc tempore, quo ab eruditis viris crebro commoventur, multo magis fœtentia) sanctitatis jam quadam simulatione condita, teperatave, mæandrisque nescio quibus involuta orbi Christiano iterum venderet,
units.tr: Paul Florenius, Doctor and Professor of Theology, bears witness to this in his colloquy with Christian Franck, Professor of Philosophy, held in the Imperial Jesuit Gymnasium at Vienna in Austria on 20 January 1578. At the start of that colloquy Florenius the Jesuit speaks these words to Franck: It seems to me, Christian, when I contemplate the whole matter more sincerely and subtly, that this religion of ours, in which we are engaged, the Jesuit religion, is wholly compounded of superstition, hypocrisy and a certain feigned and painted holiness, and was stirred up by the Devil in this last old age of the world; that it would sell again to the Christian world all these errors, trifles and superstitions, which (to say it in one word, in a less decent way than I would like, but most fitting and quite necessary for this matter) all these most foul Papal dungs, which both smell heavily in themselves and, now that they are stirred up often by learned men, stink much more, seasoned and tempered with some pretence of holiness and wrapped in I know not what meanderings.

units.la: PRÆFATIO,
units.tr: PREFACE,

units.la: vénderet, pro aromatis, atqz adeó per vim fermé quandã obtruderet ut nihil tam turpe, fœdu & falsum in Ecclesia Romana cernatur, quód hæc novo non artificio, vel mentis aciem præstringendo, vel omnem turpitudinem & falsitatem callidè tegédo pulchrum apparere faceret, atqz verum. Quare optime Christiane considerandum nobis etiam atqz etiam cæseo, in qua religione versemur, ne hanc esse falsam ignorantes, & ipsi à Deo ignoremur. Hæc Florenius.
units.tr: would sell it again as a perfume, and by a kind of force almost thrust it upon them, so that nothing so base, foul and false is seen in the Roman Church that it does not make appear beautiful and true by some new artifice, either by dazzling the edge of the mind or by cunningly covering all its baseness and falsehood. Therefore, good Christian, we must consider again and again, with all care, in what religion we are engaged, lest, not knowing that it is false, we ourselves be unknown to God. So Florenius.

units.la: Et quia à sacra Scriptura, divino Spiritus sancti instinctu edita & inspirata, palám repulsi sunt, eó confugiunt, unde subsidium omninó nullum eis ostenditur, ad Scripta nimirum Patrum, & totius orbis Christiani oculos splendore veteris Ecclesiæ luminum perstringere conantur: Utq hoc facilius efficiant, licentia & potestas data est eis à Pontif. Rom. Gregorio 13. Papa anno 1573. Ian. die 8. ut terras mariaq peragrantes, & bibliothecas omnes perlustrantes, Patrum & Historicorum, tum veterum, tum recentiorum, imó Scholasticorum quoq libros, qui non cum ijs, eorumq doctrina per omnia consentiat, interpolare, voces, sententias, quin etiam integras paginas, addere, assuere, detrahere, mutare, mutilare, nefarieq pro arbitratu & libidine sua corrumpere audeant, quod ipsi honesto, si Dijs placet, titulo seu nomine, Libros repurgare vocant.
units.tr: And since they have been openly rejected by Holy Scripture, which was published and inspired by the divine impulse of the Holy Spirit, they flee to the place where no help at all is shown them, namely to the writings of the Fathers, and they try to dazzle the eyes of the whole Christian world with the brilliance of the lights of the ancient Church. And so that they may do this more easily, licence and power were given to them by Pope Gregory XIII, the Roman Pontiff, in the year 1573 on 8 January, so that, roaming over lands and seas and searching through all libraries, they might dare to tamper with the books of the Fathers and historians, both ancient and more recent, and even of the Scholastics, which do not agree with them and their doctrine in all things: to alter words and sentences, indeed to add, insert, remove, change, mutilate and wickedly corrupt whole pages at their own pleasure and whim. They call this, with an honest-sounding title, God willing, "purging the books."

units.la: Sed quasi hoc nihil, vel parum admodum esset, hoc novum genus hominum, novâ suâ doctrinâ, tubam ac facem fuisse multorum in Europa motuum, bellorum, parricidiorum, seditionum ac turbarum, ipso facto luculeter probat. Docent enim Iesuitæ, pro invalidis & plane nullis haberi debere, pacta, conventa Imperatorum, Regum & Principum, aliorumq Ordinum, etiamsi juramento confirmata, non autem à Rom. Pontifice approbata sint. Ex hoc axiomate docent etiam, Pace religionis inter Principes Germaniæ, non esse obligatoriam, uti per vim extortam. Docent, hoc tempore ad laborandum Pontificijs, ut Lutheranos & Calvinianos, illorumq fautores omnibus modis opprimant. Docent, quando Pontificij Regem vel Principem suum pro tyranno habedu in Collegijs suis decreverint, tu illum abdicare, et seipsos omni obligationis vinculo ac nexu solvere posse. Docent, Imperatores, Reges aliosq Magistratus à subditis necari & interfici posse. Docet, hæreticos Magistratus (hoc est, Evangelicos) pro excomunicatis habendos, si no de facto, tamé de jure: ideoq proscribedos, abdicandos & é medio tollendos esse. Docent, Principes à Rom. religione deficientes, vel salte hæreticis favéntes, abdicandos esse. Docent, hæreticis (Evangelicis) fidem prorsus nullam habedā esse. Docent, Aequivocationibus uti, ijsq Magistratus decipere Pontificijs permissu esse: hoc est, licere sibi alijsq Papistis, non tantum simpliciter manifestā veritate celare, aut negare, sed pie et religiose afferere, perq salute æterna protestari, imó jurare in illa quæ certissime cognoscut fallissima esse; retinendo tantum proprium quendam & reconditum animo sensum, & ejusmodi Aequivocationes pro bona prudentia habendas.
units.tr: But as if this were nothing, or very little, this new kind of men, by their new doctrine, have plainly proved by their very deeds to have been the trumpet and the torch of many movements, wars, murders of fathers, seditions and disturbances in Europe. For the Jesuits teach that the pacts and agreements of emperors, kings and princes, and of other orders, are to be held invalid and altogether null, even if confirmed by oath, unless they have been approved by the Roman Pontiff. From this axiom they also teach that the Peace of Religion among the princes of Germany is not binding, being extorted by force. They teach that at this time the Papists ought to labour to crush by every means the Lutherans and Calvinists and their supporters. They teach that when the Papists have decided in their colleges that their king or prince must be regarded as a tyrant, they may renounce him and release themselves from every bond and tie of obligation. They teach that emperors, kings and other magistrates may be killed and slain by their subjects. They teach that heretical magistrates (that is, Evangelicals) are to be regarded as excommunicated, if not in fact, yet in law; and therefore that they are to be proscribed, deposed and removed from the midst. They teach that princes who fall away from the Roman religion, or at least favour heretics, are to be deposed. They teach that no faith at all is to be kept with heretics (Evangelicals). They teach that the use of equivocations, and by them deceiving magistrates, is permitted to Papists: that is, that it is lawful for them and other Papists not only simply to conceal or deny a plain truth, but to assert piously and religiously, and to protest with eternal salvation, indeed to swear to those things which they know most certainly to be most false, while retaining only a certain private and hidden sense in the mind; and such equivocations are to be counted as sound prudence.

units.la: PRÆFATIO.
units.tr: PREFACE.

units.la: Ac, ut progrediar ulterius quã constitueram, de Verbo Dei & Sacrasanēta Scriptura, hoc est, de Prophetarum & Apostolorū scriptis, à Spiritu sancto Sanctis Dei hominibus inspiratis, docent Iesuitæ, quòd sit Cereus nasus, materia litis, liber hæreticorum, litera muta, mortua, ambigua, obscura, varia, mutabilis, infusficiens, imperfecta: & quæ propterea non ab omnibus Christianis in vernaculis linguis legi debeat. Iesuitæ Colonienses in sua Censura S. Scripturam vocant Sermonem abbreviatum, imperfectam doctrinam, quæ non omnia necessaria ad fidem, bonos mores & beatam vitam conservandam continet. Ex Scriptura certum & ratum intelle&ium dari non posse, sed esse eam plumbeum instrumentum, quod & Catholicus & hæreticus suà sententiæ aptare possit. Quidam V. Volffgangus Hermannus Coloniensis blasphemè asseruit, Scripturas tantum valere, quantum valent Æsopi fabulæ, nisi accederet Ecclesiæ testimonium: & Hosius de Authoritate Scripturæ lib. 3. pag. 197. affirmat, hoc piè ab ipso dici potuisse. Docent porrò, judicem controversiarum de fide & moribus Romanam Ecclesiam esse. Bellarminus lib. 4, cap. 3. asserit, Scripturam sine Traditionibus non admodum necessariam esse: Traditiones autem simpliciter necessarias esse.
units.tr: And, that I may proceed further than I had intended, concerning the Word of God and Sacred Scripture, that is, the writings of the Prophets and Apostles, inspired by the Holy Spirit in holy men of God, the Jesuits teach that Scripture is a wax nose, a matter of strife, a book of heretics, a dead and dumb letter, ambiguous, obscure, various, changeable, insufficient and imperfect; and that for this reason it ought not to be read by all Christians in their vernacular tongues. The Jesuits of Cologne in their Censure call Holy Scripture an abbreviated sermon, an imperfect doctrine, which does not contain everything necessary for faith, good morals and the preservation of a blessed life. They say that no certain and firm understanding can be drawn from Scripture, but that it is a leaden rule, which both the Catholic and the heretic can fit to his own opinion. A certain Wolfgang Hermann of Cologne blasphemously asserted that the Scriptures are worth only as much as the fables of Aesop, unless the testimony of the Church were added; and Hosius, in his work on the Authority of Scripture, book 3, page 197, affirms that this could have been said by him in good faith. Furthermore, they teach that the judge of controversies concerning faith and morals is the Roman Church. Bellarmine, book 4, chapter 3, asserts that Scripture without Traditions is not very necessary, but that Traditions are simply necessary.

units.la: In his non negligenter observanda est Satanæ astutia, nec non Pontificiorum, inprimis Iesuitarum artes ac stratagemata. Iam ab annis aliquot non multum laborant Iesuitæ, circa ipsa religionis Christianæ dogmata, ut vel nostrorum scripta oppugnent, vel sua propugnent ex Scripturis sacris, quod ante hac Papatus defensores facere conabantur, quandoquidem huius generis pugna jam olim infeliciter sibi cederè senserunt. Compendiosiùs igitur visa est ad victoriam via, si semel omnem Scripturæ sacræ authoritatem convellerent, imò totam prosternerent: cumque palam id facere absque summa impietate non possent, saltem eam Pontificis sui arbitrio totam subjicerent, & omne jus cognoscendi, dijudicandi & decidendi controversias religionis non ad Scripturam referrent, sed ad suum Papam traducerent, & sic, si illis credimus, aut concedimus quod volunt, nihil jam Scripturæ sacræ contra Papam amplius valent, nec nobis restat aliud, nisi ut victi manus demus, & colla nostra rursus Romani Pontificis jugo subjiciamus.
units.tr: In these matters the cunning of Satan must not be overlooked carelessly, nor the arts and stratagems of the Papists, especially of the Jesuits. For some years now the Jesuits have not laboured much, concerning the very dogmas of the Christian religion, either to assail the writings of ours, or to defend their own from the holy Scriptures, as the defenders of the Papacy used to attempt before this, since they have long felt that this kind of struggle went badly for them. So the way to victory seemed more expedient, if once they could overthrow the whole authority of Holy Scripture, indeed utterly prostrate it; and since they could not do this openly without the greatest impiety, they would at least make all of it subject to the will of their Pope, and would refer all right of knowing, judging and deciding controversies of religion not to Scripture but transfer it to their Pope; and thus, if we believe them, or grant what they want, the Holy Scriptures no longer avail anything against the Pope, and nothing remains for us but to lay down our arms as conquered men and once again submit our necks to the yoke of the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: Hac, Clementissime Princeps, paulò pluribus commemoro, ut orthodoxi Principes & Magistratus Christiani, Ecclesiarum item Pastores & Antistites quid faciendum sibi sit intelligant. Frendet Satan, frémit Antichristus, tumultuantur Iesuitæ & summa imis miscere conantur: exadversa igitur parte hisce furoribus, motibus & conatibus obviam ire decet & omnes nervos contendere, ut vera Religio & doctrina Verbi DEI in Reformatis Ecclesiis pura puta conservetur, & à fermento Iesuitico strenuè defendatur.
units.tr: I mention these things at somewhat greater length, most merciful Prince, so that orthodox princes and Christian magistrates, as well as the ministers and leaders of the Churches, may understand what must be done by them. Satan rages, Antichrist roars, the Jesuits make an uproar and strive to stir up everything from the bottom; it is therefore fitting to meet these furies, movements and attempts from the opposite side, and to strain every nerve, so that the true religion and the doctrine of the Word of God may be kept entirely pure in the Reformed Churches, and be vigorously defended against the Jesuitical leaven.

units.la: In hunc usum ego quoq; Historiam Iesuiticam conscripsi, non quidem integram, absolutam & perfectam, quod ultro ac libenter fateor, quis enim illorum facinora, dolos ac impostturas hinc inde patratas, commemoret? sed eas tantum, quæ ad manus meas pervenerunt, diligenter & bona cum fide annotavi: In cujus Historiæ libro primo usus sum interdum Helia Hæ fenmulieri testimonijs, qui apud Iesuitas se contulit, & aliquot annos in eorum Collegijs hinc inde vixit, sperans quod apud hujus sodalitij homines vera & Catholicam doctrinam invenire posset. Cum vero apud illos nihil quàm vanas superstitiones, hypocrisim Pharisaicam, falsas opiniones ac turbulentos errores invenisset, eos deseruit, & fuga elapsus ad gremiu orthodoxæ & verae Christi Ecclesiæ rediit. Hic scio quid Iesuitæ in promptu habeant quod respondeant, nempe, Hafenmullerum hunc apostatam, & fui Ordinis desertorem fuisse, ideòque illi in hac causa omne fidem ademptam esse. Si autem ad hunc modum licet argumentari, bone DEVS quot Papistarum Scriptoribus, & quidem non infimæ fortis fides omnis derogabitur? nempe, Staphylo, Rabo, Fraco, Isengrinio, Flascio, Lipsio, & præcipuè Ioanni Pistorio: hos enim & alios multos in vera doctrina inde ab incunte ætate institutos & enutritos fuisse, negari non potest: eos autem splendore mundi & pinguissimis præbendis illectos, ab agnita veritate defecisse, toti orbi Christiano constat: ergo, vel Iesuitarum confessione & testimonio, his ipsis omnis fides deroganda erit in omnibus quæ contra nostros, nostrasque Ecclesias scripserunt.
units.tr: I have written this History of the Jesuits for this purpose too. It is not complete, finished, or perfect, and I freely and gladly admit as much, for who could recount all the crimes, tricks, and frauds they have committed here and there? I have only recorded, diligently and in good faith, those that came into my hands. In the first book of this History I have sometimes made use of the testimony of Helias Hafenmüller, a woman's son, who joined the Jesuits and lived for some years in their colleges here and there, hoping to find true and Catholic doctrine among the members of that brotherhood. But when he found among them nothing but vain superstitions, Pharisaic hypocrisy, false opinions, and turbulent errors, he abandoned them, escaped by flight, and returned to the bosom of the orthodox and true Church of Christ. I know what the Jesuits have ready to answer here: namely, that this Hafenmüller was an apostate and a deserter of their Order, and that therefore all trust in him in this matter must be withdrawn. But if one may argue in this way, good God, how much trust would be taken away from the writers of the Papists, and from men of no small standing? For example Staphylus, Rabus, Fraco, Isengrinius, Flacius, Lipsius, and above all Johannes Pistorius. It cannot be denied that these and many others were instructed and brought up in the true doctrine from their earliest age; and it is well known throughout the whole Christian world that they were lured away from the truth they had acknowledged by the splendour of the world and by very fat benefices. So, either by the confession and testimony of the Jesuits themselves, all trust must be withdrawn from these very men in everything they have written against us and our Churches.

units.la: HANC vero Historiam, Clementissime Princeps, sub felicibus auspicijs nominis V. in lucem prodire tribus potissimum de causis volui. Prima est, quod certo scio, pessimam me gratiam historiæ hujus evulgatione à Iesuitis reportaturum, idemque eventurum mihi, quod Propheta Isaias 9. Capite illis prædicit, qui Basilisci ova conculcant. Si quis enim conculcaverit ova illa, erumpit ex testa vipera, & saevissimè conculcantem insequitur. Conculcat autem ova illa viperina, quicunque dolos, fraudes, imposturas, practicas etiam & consilia sanguinolenta & perniciosa in lucem protrahit, (quod ego in hac Historia aliquo saltem modo facio) & propterea vindictam experiri cogitur. Cum etiam dubium mihi non sit, quin locusta illa (de quibus Ioannes in Apocalypsi 9. Capite vaticinatur) de puteo fumo prodeuntes, quorum cauda similes Scorpionum, inque illis aculei, quibus nocendi hominibus potestas data est, his suis aculeis viperijsque morsibus laborem hunc meum omnibus modis sint impugnaturæ, & convitijs ac maledicis infestationibus, seu maliciosa & mendaci infamatione aliqua caterвaтim contra me sint, pro moresuo, irruitura: Patrono opus habeo, qui me contra viperios istos morsus & locustarum aculeos fortiter defendat ac protegat. Hunc Patronum Celsitudinem V. pra caeteris mihi delegi, quam humiliter rogo & obsecro.
units.tr: I have wished to bring this History into the light, most merciful Prince, under the happy auspices of your name, for three main reasons. The first is that I know well I shall receive the worst thanks from the Jesuits for publishing this history, and that what the prophet Isaiah foretells in chapter 9 for those who trample basilisk's eggs will happen to me. For if anyone tramples those eggs, a viper bursts out of the shell and savagely pursues the one who trampled them. Now whoever brings to light the frauds, deceits, impostures, and also the practices and bloody and pernicious plans, trample those viperous eggs (which I do in this History at least in some measure), and are therefore compelled to suffer vengeance. Nor do I doubt that those locusts (of whom John prophesies in chapter 9 of the Apocalypse, coming out of the smoke of the pit, whose tails are like scorpions' tails, with stings in them, and to whom power to harm men has been given) will attack this labour of mine in every way with their stings and viperous bites, and will rush at me in a swarm, according to their custom, with abusive and insulting attacks, or with some malicious and lying defamation. Therefore I need a patron who will bravely defend and protect me against these viperous bites and the stings of the locusts. I have chosen Your Highness above all others for this patronage, and I humbly ask and beseech you to grant it.

units.la: ꝛ hanc historiam in suam tutelam, patrocinium ac defensionem suscipere dignetur, Altera Dedicationis hujus causa est, quòd non solum in Marchia, seu Ditione ac Dominio V. toto verbi diuini doctrina splendidissimè lucet, eamq; magna animi fortitudine, magnoq; zelo ac singulari studio Celsitudo V. defendit & propagat: quod si in eò perrexerit, DEVM omnipotentem remuneratorem largissimum experietur, neque is Vestro studio, laboribus & sanctis conatibus unquam deerit: apud cunctos autem Veritatis Evangelicæ amantes æternam laudem & gloriam consequetur. Tertia causa est, ut Historia hæc manifestum ac certum sit quasi depositum, testimonium & signum S. P. Q. Tigurini erga Celsitud. Vestram summæ observantiæ, studij & amoris singularis. Quod reliquum est, DEVM Opt. Max. ex animo oro rogóque, ut Celsitudini Vestræ in hac vita contingat optata longævitas: in fide Christi perennis stabilitas: in Imperio firma tranquillitas, in obitu felix immortalitas: in cœlis autem expectata beatitas: per IESVM CHRISTVM Dominum ac Servatorem nostrum unicum, ✠Amen. Tiguri Helvetiorum Metropoli 28. Octobris, anno Christi Salvatoris nostri unici 1619.
units.tr: May he deign to take this history under his protection, patronage and defence. The second reason for this dedication is that the teaching of the divine Word shines most brightly not only in the March, or in your Highness's territory and dominion, and that your Highness defends and propagates it with great courage of spirit, great zeal and singular devotion. If you persist in this, you will experience God Almighty as a most generous rewarder, nor will He ever be wanting to your zeal, labours and holy endeavours; and among all lovers of the Gospel truth you will obtain eternal praise and glory. The third reason is that this History may stand as a clear and certain pledge, as it were a deposit, testimony and sign of the Senate and People of Zurich's highest respect, zeal and singular affection towards your Highness. As for the rest, I earnestly pray and beseech God, most good and most great, that your Highness may enjoy the wished-for long life in this world, lasting steadfastness in the faith of Christ, firm tranquillity in your rule, a happy immortality in death, and the longed-for blessedness in heaven, through Jesus Christ, our one Lord and Saviour. ✠Amen. Zurich, metropolis of the Helvetians, 28 October, in the year 1619 of Christ our one Saviour.

units.la: DE ORIGINE ET AU- THORE IESVITA- RVM ORDINIS Liber Primus. CAPVT I.
units.tr: ON THE ORIGIN AND AUTHOR OF THE ORDER OF JESUITS: Book One. CHAPTER I.

units.la: IRCA annos reparatæ salutis humanæ 1540. IGNATIVS LOIOLA Cantaber Societatis Iesu fratribus initium dedit. Fuit is tam truculentâ animi ferocitate præditus, ut, cûm ex ephebis egressus esset, quemvis obviam sibi vel leves ob causas resistentem percuteret & ferro transverberaret: nec veritus fuit dicere, se manu suâ dextrâ, quâ gladium vibrabat, aëremēp percutiebat, vel invitus Diis hostes suos omnes prostraturum. Bobadilla, unus ex decem Loiolæ Socijs & Iesuitarum Patribus, ingenuè fatetur, eum fuisse hominem militiæ castrisq; assuetum.
units.tr: Around the year of restored human salvation 1540, Ignatius Loyola, a Cantabrian, gave the beginning to the Fraternity of Jesus. He was endowed with such savage fierceness of spirit that, when he had left boyhood, he would strike down and run through with his sword anyone who opposed him, even for slight reasons. Nor was he ashamed to say that with his right hand, which brandished the sword, he struck the air, or, even against the will of the gods, would lay low all his enemies. Bobadilla, one of Loyola's ten companions and a Jesuit father, frankly admits that he was a man accustomed to military service and camps.

units.la: Hanc feritatem, immanitatem & insolentiam Iesuita factus adeo non deposuit, ut Hoffæus, Hasenmullero referente, Romæ in domo Iesuitarum professa Asisiensis, testatus sit, eum nonnullos Societatis suæ fratres flagellorum ictibus ita confecisse, ut præmaturâ morte interierint. Similiter Salmanassar Neapolitanus Iesuita confitetur, Loiolam naturâ ferocem fuisse; durum ac truculentum. Ribadeneira etiam in vita Ignatij scribit, In levibus erratis gravia interdum exempla eum statuisse: quod ab æqualitate & ratione consentanea alienum prorsus est.
units.tr: Once he had become a Jesuit, he did not lay aside this ferocity, cruelty and arrogance. Hoffaeus, as Hasenmüller reports, testified in Rome, in the professed house of the Jesuits at Assisi, that he had beaten some of his fellow members of the Society with the lash so severely that they died before their time. Similarly, Salmeron of Naples, a Jesuit, confesses that Loyola was fierce by nature, hard and savage. Ribadeneira too writes in the life of Ignatius that he sometimes set severe examples for slight faults, which is utterly foreign to equity and reasonable consistency.

units.la: Et qualis per universam vitam fuerit, propria ipsius conscientia ei dictavit, dum sub finem vitæ, Ribadeneirâ teste, seipsum detestabilem dixerit, & professus fuerit, se indignum qui honestè sepeliretur.
units.tr: And what kind of man he was throughout his whole life, his own conscience dictated to him, since at the end of his life, as Ribadeneira testifies, he called himself detestable and declared that he was unworthy to be honourably buried.

units.la: Hæc eius immanis, belluina & truculenta natura in omnes eius discipulos & sectatores derivata est, ut qui nihil aliud quam cædem, sanguinem & interitum piorum & orthodoxorum omnium, quin etiam Regum ac Principum Papisticorum, spirant, sicut in sequentibus indicabitur: hoc autem loco pauca saltem exempla referam. Iacobus Crusius, novitiorum Landspergensium Iesuitarum Rector, Miles, dicebat, esse debuit nostræ Societatis Pater: quia, ut militis est totis viribus in hostem irruere, nec desistere, donec victor evadat: ita nostrum est in omnes irruere, qui Pontifici Romano resistunt, illosque consiliis, dictis & scriptis, invocato etiam seculari brachio, hoc est, igne & ferro, tollere & abolere: sicut Pontifex, & nostra vota contra Lutheranos suscepta, volunt & mandant. Gregorius Baderus in Bavaria Iesuitarum Provincialis Landspergæ Hasenmullero dixit: In urbe Augusta nostri pacem non sunt habituri, nisi curaverimus Evangelicos concionatores eici ac tolli. Item, Nostrorum consilijs Evangelici concionatores Viennâ expulsi sunt, ideo etiam nostri iam ibi in pace docent, & rebus pro animi votis potiuntur. Iesuitæ Coloniensis in Censura sua inquiunt: Nisi Lutherana religio ferro & igne tollatur, Ecclesia Romana pacem & tranquillitatem habere non potest. Rursus Crusius pro concione aliquoties dixit: Non
units.tr: This savage, brutal and cruel nature of his has passed down to all his disciples and followers, so that they breathe nothing but slaughter, blood and the destruction of all the pious and orthodox, and even of Papist kings and princes, as will be shown in what follows. For the present I will report only a few examples. Jacob Crusius, Rector of the Jesuit novices at Landsberg, a soldier, used to say: Our Society ought to have had a father who was a soldier, because, as it is the soldier's part to rush at the enemy with all his strength and not desist until he emerges victorious, so it is our part to rush at all who resist the Roman Pontiff, and to remove and destroy them by counsel, words and writings, even calling in the secular arm, that is, fire and sword, as the Pontiff and our vows undertaken against the Lutherans desire and command. Gregory Bader, Provincial of the Jesuits in Bavaria, said to Hasenmüller at Landsberg: In the city of Augsburg our men will not have peace unless we take care that the Evangelical preachers are cast out and removed. Likewise: By the counsel of our men the Evangelical preachers were expelled from Vienna, and therefore our men now teach there in peace and enjoy their desires. The Jesuits of Cologne say in their Censure: Unless the Lutheran religion is removed by fire and sword, the Roman Church cannot have peace and tranquillity. Again, Crusius, in a sermon, said several times: Not

units.la: A pbrifimum ob hunc finem in Germaniam missi sumus, ut Doctores, Concionatores & Præ-ceptores in scholis & templis agamus, sed ut operam demus, ne Lutherani & Evangelici Protestantes maiora incrementa sumant, sed excindantur. Si id nostrates ab ortu Lutheri fecissent, iam Ecclesia Romana in pace viveret. Verum causa nondum cecidimus: coniungamus mutuas operas, vires & arma, tunc facile poterimus illos exstirpare. Ad hunc finem nisi omnia nostra consilia & actiones direxerimus, periculum est ne nobis idem quod intendimus faciant, & in foveam, quam paramus hæreticis, ipsi nostra negligentia incidamus. Ad eundem modum magnus ille Iesuitarum fautor Andræas Fabricius Cæfarem horatur, ut femur suum gladio accingat, neque patiatur hæreticos vivere. Quid enim, inquit, faciat ursus in vinea, lupus in ovili? Pater Th. Peltanus Augustæ in-ter suos familiares dixisse fertur: Nos tot tantaq; patimur à civibus Augustanis: Si iam mihi Catholici, quorum in urbe maior numerus est quam hæreticorum, obedirent, suaderem, ut omnes occiderent: Sic enim pacem habituri essemus, & Papa in novo Calendario propagado fatis facere possemus: quod nunquam fiet quamdiu in medio nostri protestantes vivere passi fuerimus. Antonius Possevinus Iesuitarum per Germaniam Inquisitor in libello, quem inscripsit, Il Soldato Christiano, Miles Christianus, edito cum Pius V. exercitum in Galliam mitteret auxilio suis, ut adversarios Pontificiæ sedis de medio tollerent, scribit: Omnes Christianos iure obligatos, ut Romanam religionem contra Evangelicorum doctrinam totis viribus & proprij sanguinis effusione tueantur: Pacem & publicum bonum in Ecclesia Romana conservari non posse affirmans, nisi hostes eius exterminentur. Quibus addit: Nisi expuleritis eos, patriam, uxores, liberos, parentes, amicos & opes in tuto possidere non poteritis. Tandem hortatur Duces exercitus istius, ut nihil omnino hæreticis permittant, nec fidem datam servent: Inquisitores clandestinos in eos subornent, domestica & intestina bella inter illos excitari curent: Proditores ac sicarios omnibus locis contra illos instituant: Duces aliter facientes, in Ecclesiam Romanam peccare, inexcusabiles reddi & damnari afferens. In hiis paucis vides Loyolæ naturam immanem & sanguinolentam in sectatoribus suis.
units.tr: We were sent into Germany, in short, for this very purpose: not so that we might act as teachers, preachers and instructors in schools and churches, but so that we might take care that the Lutherans and Evangelical Protestants do not gain greater increase, but are uprooted. If our countrymen had done this since the rise of Luther, the Roman Church would now be living in peace. But as yet we have not succeeded. Let us join our labours, strength and arms, and then we will easily be able to root them out. Unless we direct all our plans and actions to this end, there is danger that they will do to us what we intend, and that through our own negligence we fall into the pit we are preparing for heretics. In the same way that great patron of the Jesuits, Andreas Fabricius, urges the Emperor to gird his thigh with the sword and not allow heretics to live. For, he says, what does a bear do in a vineyard, or a wolf in a sheepfold? Father Th. Peltanus is reported to have said among his intimate friends at Augsburg: We suffer so many and such great things from the citizens of Augsburg. If the Catholics, who are more numerous in the city than the heretics, would now obey me, I would advise that they all be killed. For so we would have peace, and the Pope could go far enough in spreading his new Calendar; which will never happen as long as we allow Protestants to live in our midst. Antonius Possevinus, Jesuit Inquisitor throughout Germany, in a little book which he entitled Il Soldato Christiano, The Christian Soldier, published when Pius V sent an army into France to help his own people and to remove the adversaries of the Papal see, writes that all Christians are bound by law to defend the Roman religion against the doctrine of the Evangelicals with all their strength and with the shedding of their own blood, affirming that peace and the common good cannot be preserved in the Roman Church unless its enemies are exterminated. To these he adds: Unless you drive them out, you will not be able to hold your country, wives, children, parents, friends and wealth in safety. Finally he urges the commanders of that army to permit the heretics nothing at all and not to keep faith with them; to suborn secret informers against them and to take care that domestic and civil wars are stirred up among them; to set up traitors and assassins against them in every place; asserting that commanders who act otherwise sin against the Roman Church and are rendered inexcusable and damned. From these few examples you see the savage and bloodthirsty nature of Loyola in his followers.

units.la: Contulit autem sese Ignatius cum aliis multis sui similibus truculentis, & sanguinem hu manum sitientibus Hispanis, in arcem Pompeiopolitanam munitissimam, eo tempore, quo eam Galli obsederunt, vehementissimeq; oppugnarunt. Cum autem nimis ferociret in obsidioneilla, divina vindicta in ipsum exardescente, factum est, ut æneæ bombardæ pila à Gallis immissa, crus eius dextrum frangeretur: sinistrum quoque lapide de muro excusso graviter circa inguina vulneraretur, & à Gallis caperetur. Noluit tamen divina iustitia mundo irata pœnitentissimum hominem tunc temporis e medio tollere, sed quorundam clementiâ curatus est, ita tamen, ut in utrumq; latus claudicaret, domumq; rediret.
units.tr: Ignatius, moreover, joined himself with many other fierce Spaniards like himself, thirsting for human blood, in the fortress of Pamplona, which was very strongly fortified, at the time when the French besieged it and assaulted it most vehemently. But since he raged too much in that siege, divine vengeance blazed up against him, and it came about that a cannonball of bronze hurled by the French broke his right leg; his left was also seriously wounded near the groin by a stone knocked from the wall, and he was captured by the French. Yet divine justice, angry with the world, did not wish at that time to remove from the world this most penitent man, but he was cured through the mercy of some, though in such a way that he limped on both sides, and he returned home.

units.la: Hoc modo iusto Dei iudicio punitus, militiam deseruit, & lectioni prosanarum librorum, temporis fallendi causâ, totum se tradidit. Cum vero ob claudicationem deformem ab omnibus rideretur, ipseque ad res politicas tractandas se ineptum intelligeret, militaris & politicæ vitæ, cui hucusque plus satis addictus fuerat, pertæsus, vitæ pristinæ genus mutare & aliud instituere proposuit. Contigit autem ut in manus eius venirent Legenda, mendaciorum plenissimæ, quas Vitas seu flores Sanctorum vulgo nominant: tam enim obtusi ingenij erat, ut altiora nec intelligere nec percipere posset. Has tamen, pro more superstitiosorum hominum, avidissime legit, & legentem tanta incessit religio, ut de novo Ordine instituendo cogitare inciperet: Vt rectissime dixerit ille, Desperatio facit Mona-chum.
units.tr: Thus punished by the just judgment of God, he abandoned soldiering and devoted himself entirely to reading profane books, to pass the time.
