units.tr: Nor does it seem right to omit what I have observed in my diligent reading of the authors: that no trustworthy ancient author records false and lying signs of this kind, devised to confirm the worship of alien gods and various superstitions, such as are reported today by the Jesuits about their Ignatius, and which appeared only after the times of Gregory the Great, when every kind of superstition rushed into the Church in droves.

units.la: Frustra igitur Richeomus Iesuita in Expostulatione sua Apologetica cap.74. pag.522. gravissime accusat nostros, inprimis autem Stephanum Pasquierium nobilem Advocatum in Parlamento Parisino, quod summe contemnat & deridmeat in suo Catechismo Iesuitico lib.1. cap.17. pag.187. miracula & visiones Loyolae: Horribile, inquit, dictu cogitatu, est, quam profana maledicta Diagoras Francus (Pasquierium intelligit) effundat in miracula, qua rerum omnium praepotens Deus per Ignatium de Loyola edidit, ut Iesuitarum Ordinem prorsus everteret, eorum institutum perderet, famam profligaret, pacem affligeret, &c.
units.tr: Richeome the Jesuit, therefore, in his Apologetic Expostulation, chapter 74, page 522, vainly accuses our people very grievously, above all Étienne Pasquier, a noble advocate in the Parliament of Paris, because in his Jesuit Catechism, book 1, chapter 17, page 187, he utterly despises and mocks the miracles and visions of Loyola: "It is horrible," he says, "to think or to say what profane curses that Frenchman Diagoras (he means Pasquier) pours out against the miracles which God, almighty over all things, wrought through Ignatius of Loyola, in order to overthrow utterly the Order of the Jesuits, to destroy their institute, to wreck their reputation, to trouble their peace," etc.

units.la: Et Gretserus contra Stenium, Calvinianos Ignatii Loyolae miracula ridentes, similes esse dicit Iudaeis, fidem Christi miraculis derogantibus. Ita claudo & truculento Marano ac profano militi tantundem tribuit, quantum omnipotenti Dei Filio, blasphemia inter Christianos non ferenda.
units.tr: And Gretser, against Stenius, says that the Calvinists, who mock the miracles of Ignatius of Loyola, are like the Jews who detract from the faith of Christ by their miracles. So he ascribes as much to a lame, savage Marrano and a profane soldier as to the almighty Son of God, a blasphemy not to be tolerated among Christians.

units.la: Tandem ob haec miracula, & fidelem operam, sedi Rom. iam nutanti & vacillanti praestitam, canonizatus & in numerum Papisticorum Deorum a Papa relatus est Loyola.
units.tr: Finally, on account of these miracles, and the faithful service rendered to the Roman see, now tottering and wavering, Loyola was canonized by the Pope and placed in the number of the Papistical gods.

units.la: Ediderunt autem Iesuitae tres Concionės in die festo solenni Canonizationis seu Beatificationis Ignatij Loyolae, tanquam a Dominicanis Hispanis habitae fuisse, & in Gallicum Idioma translatae. Titulus namque earum hic erat: Tres eximiae Concionės in solemni festo Canonizationis, sive Beatificationis, gloriosi Patriarchae Beati Beati Ignatij, Fundatoris Societatis Iesu: quarum prima est per Reverend. Patre & Doctorem Petrum de Valderanna, Priorem Conventus S. Augustini Hispalensis: Altera per Reverend. Patrem & Doctorem Fr. Petrum Dozam, Ordinis S. Dominici in Conventu Valentiae: Tertia per Reverendum Patrem Praesentatum, Fr. Iacobum Rebulosam, praedicti Ordinis S. Dominici in urbe Barcelonensi, &c. Excusae Pictaviij per Antonium Menierum impressorem & Bibliopolam Ordinarium Regium Academiae Pictav. anno 1611. Sed fraus suboluit tandem; & deprehensum est, tres has conciones à Iesuitis conscriptas, habitas & publicatas fuisse.
units.tr: The Jesuits published three sermons, supposedly delivered by Spanish Dominicans on the solemn feast day of the canonization or beatification of Ignatius of Loyola, and translated into French. Their title ran thus: "Three excellent sermons on the solemn feast of the canonization, or beatification, of the glorious Patriarch, the Blessed Ignatius, Founder of the Society of Jesus. The first of these is by the Reverend Father and Doctor Peter of Valderrama, Prior of the Convent of St. Augustine at Seville; the second by the Reverend Father and Doctor Fr. Peter Dosa, of the Order of St. Dominic, in the Convent at Valencia; the third by the Reverend Father Presentato, Fr. James Rebulosa, of the aforesaid Order of St. Dominic in the city of Barcelona," etc. Printed at Poitiers by Antoine Mesnier, printer and royal bookseller of the Academy of Poitiers, in the year 1611. But the fraud came to light at last, and it was discovered that these three sermons had been written, delivered and published by the Jesuits.

units.la: In his Concionibus Iesuitae Ignatio suo Loyolae tantum non divinos honores tribuunt, quales S. Scriptura nulli vel Prophetarum vel Apostolorum tribuit, ac Deum faciunt: id quod ex 4. his excerptis articulorum concionum facile intelligetur: in prima concione Petrus de Vualderanna sic inter alia ait pag. 54. & 55. Scimus quidem Moysen virga sua, quam manu ferebat, miracula in aere, in terra, in aqua, in peris & passim, ubi consultum illi visum fuit, stupenda edidisse & admiranda, adeo quidem ut ipsum Pharaonem cum universo exercitu in mare rubrum praecipitarit & submerserit, verum ineffabilis divini nominis; quod virgae isti seu baculo insculptum fuisse Doctus ille estatus Episcopus Avillanus asserit; virtute ista miracula edita fuere. Quod autem creaturae, agnoscentes supremi Regis & Domini sui ordinationes, nomine eius signatas & subscriptas, obedientiam illi praestiterint, hoc non tanti erat faciendum: nec etiam magis nirum vobis videri debet, per Apostolos tot tantaque contigisse miracula, siquidem ea omnia in nomine Dei fiebant, operante videlicet virtute eius & potentia, quam illis concesserat, & tanquam sigillo suo confignarat; cum ait: In nomine meo Daemonia eijcient, linguis loquentur novis, &c. Quod autem Ignatius suomet ipsius proprio nomine chartae inscrito, plura quam ipse Moyses, miracula; & totidem edat, quot Apostoli: quod sigillum jus tantae authoritatis penes creaturas obtineat; ut subito illi obediant; Hoc, hoc ipsum est, quod in summam eius admirationem nos inducat.
units.tr: In these sermons the Jesuits attribute to their Ignatius of Loyola almost divine honours, such as Holy Scripture attributes to no one, either prophet or apostle, and they make him God. This will easily be understood from four excerpts of the articles of the sermons. In the first sermon, Peter of Valderrama says among other things, on pages 54 and 55: "We indeed know that Moses, with the rod which he held in his hand, performed stupendous and admirable miracles in air, in earth, in water, in fire, and everywhere, wherever it seemed good to him, so that he drowned and sank Pharaoh himself with the whole army in the Red Sea; but that these miracles were wrought by the virtue of the ineffable divine name, which, as that learned bishop of Avila asserts, was engraved on that rod or staff. That the creatures, recognising the commands of their supreme King and Lord, signed and subscribed with his name, rendered obedience to him, this was not to be regarded as so great a thing; nor should it seem to you any more wonderful that so many and such great miracles happened through the apostles, since all these were done in the name of God, the virtue and power of God working through them, which he had granted to them and sealed as his own, when he said: 'In my name they shall cast out devils, they shall speak with new tongues,' etc. But that Ignatius, by his own name written on paper, performs more miracles than Moses himself, and as many as the apostles; that his seal should hold such authority over creatures that they suddenly obey him: this, this very thing, is what leads us into the greatest admiration of him."

units.la: Secundus articulus est pag. 81. eiusdem concionis: Quoadusque Ignatio vivere hic contigit, vita eius & mores tam graves, tam sublimes, ipso etiam coelo sic statuente, extiterunt, ut nemini nisi Pontificibus, Divo scilicet Petro & Imperatricibus, Deiparae videlicet Virgini: deinde Monarchae supremo, Deo Patri, eiusque sanctissimo Filio, eos intueri & videre, tanquam ex singulari gratia fuerit concessum.
units.tr: The second article is on page 81 of the same sermon: "As long as it was Ignatius's lot to live here, his life and character were so weighty and so exalted, heaven itself so ordaining, that it was granted to him, as a special grace, to look upon and see no one but the Pontiffs, namely the divine Peter and the Empresses, namely the Virgin Mother of God; and then the supreme Monarch, God the Father, and his most holy Son."

units.la: Tertius est in Concione Fr. Petr. Doz. pag. 111. & pag. 112. Extra dubium est, reliquis religiosorum Ordinum fundatores in favorem Ecclesiae missos fuisse, &c. NOVISSIME AUTEM DIEBUS ISTIS LOCVTVS EST NOBIS IN FILIO SVO IGNATIO, QVEM CONSTITVIT HAEREDEM VNIVERSORVM; &c. Nec ei quicquam in hoc genere laudationis deesse videtur, per quem fecit et secula.
units.tr: The third is in the sermon of Fr. Pietro Doz, pages 111 and 112: "It is beyond doubt that the founders of the other religious Orders were sent in favour of the Church, etc. BUT IN THESE LAST DAYS HE HAS SPOKEN TO US IN HIS SON IGNATIUS, WHOM HE APPOINTED HEIR OF ALL THINGS, etc." Nor does it seem that any praise of this kind is lacking to him, "by whom also he made the worlds."

units.la: Quartus articulus est in Concione Fr. Iacobi Rebulosae pag. 207. Ignatius, inquit, Martyr tam singulari affectu erga S. Patrem Pontificem Romanum, tanquam legitimum successorem Iesu Christi, eiusque vicarium in terris, &c. devotus erat.
units.tr: The fourth article is in the sermon of Fr. Jacobus Rebulosa, page 207: "Ignatius, he says, the martyr, was so singularly devoted in affection to the Holy Father the Roman Pontiff, as the legitimate successor of Jesus Christ and his vicar on earth, etc."

units.la: Cum autem hae Conciones in Galliam importatae essent anno Domini 1611. & sacra Theologiae Facultas Parisiensis die prima Octob. eiusdem anni; post solennem Missam sua ordinaria haberet Comitia in Aula Collegij Sorbonae, tum Magister Ioannes Tilesac, Doctor eiusdem Facultatis, Curio S. Iohannis, Ecclesiastes Parisiensis Ecclesiae, retulit, aliquos Parisinae urbis viros, ad se has tres Conciones detulisse, & scire percupere; utrum Facultas Parisiensis gratam ratamque earundem approbationem habeat; factam à Fr. M. Matthaeo Le Heurs Doctore eiusdem Facultatis, & quid praesertim sentiat de quatuor istis articulis quos modo recensuimus, qui permultis Catholicis offendiculum praebeant. Qua audita supplicatione, & praefatis quatuor articulis mature & diligenter examinatis: Facultas attendens, ex verbis etiam male prolatis haereses nasci, ut apud Magistrum
units.tr: When these sermons had been brought into France in the year of the Lord 1611, and the sacred Faculty of Theology of Paris held its ordinary assembly in the hall of the Sorbonne College on the first of October of that year, after the solemn Mass, Master Jean Tilesac, Doctor of the same Faculty, curate of St John, preacher of the Parisian church, reported that some men of the city of Paris had brought these three sermons to him and were eager to know whether the Faculty of Paris gave its pleasing and firm approval to them, an approval sought by Fr. Matthaeus Le Heurs, Doctor of the same Faculty; and what it thought especially of the four articles we have just listed, which give great offence to very many Catholics. This petition having been heard, and the four articles having been maturely and diligently examined, the Faculty, bearing in mind that heresies arise even from words badly put forth, as in the case of the Master...

units.la: B
units.tr: B

units.la: DE ORIGINE
units.tr: ON THE ORIGIN

units.la: Sententiarum docet Hieronymus (non obstante intercessione Magistri Andreæ Ducal, afferentis, prædicta omnia benignis interpretationibus approbari posse) censuit: Quod ad primum, istam loquendi formulam, qui nomen Creaturæ nomini Dei omnipotentis æquari videtur; præterea extenuantur miracula, eo, quod Dei nomine edita fuerint; denique miracula non ita certa, miraculis indubitatâ fide catholicâ tenendis præferuntur, esse scandalosam, erroneam, blasphemam atque impiam. Quoad secundum, istam assertionem, quæ fingit aliquid boni Deo accessisse ex visione creaturæ, scandalosam esse, ac manifestâ hæresin præse ferre. Quoad tertium, accommodationem huius textus literalis D. Pauli: Novissime autem locutus est nobis in filio Ignatio, &c. alteri quam Christo; esse scandalosam, erroneam, & meram blasphemiam & impietatem redolere. Quoad ultimum articulum, duas habere partes inter se pugnantes, quarum altera alteram destruat: & posterior quidem, Papam esse Vicarium in terris, Catholica est: prior vero, Papam esse legitimum successorem Christi, modum loquendi omnino hæreticum continet.
units.tr: Hieronymus, in his Sentences, judged (notwithstanding the intercession of Master Andreas Ducal, who maintains that all these things can be approved by kindly interpretations) as follows. First, that this form of speech, which seems to equate the name of a creature with the name of the almighty God, is scandalous, erroneous, blasphemous and impious. Moreover, the miracles are belittled because they were performed in God's name, and finally, miracles that are not so certain are preferred to miracles that must be held with the undoubted Catholic faith. Second, that this assertion, which imagines that something good came to God from the vision of a creature, is scandalous and openly savours of heresy. Third, that the application of this literal text of St Paul, "But in these last days he has spoken to us in the Son, Ignatius, etc.," to someone other than Christ is scandalous, erroneous, and smells of sheer blasphemy and impiety. Last, that the final article has two parts that contradict each other, one of which destroys the other: the latter part, that the Pope is the vicar on earth, is Catholic, but the former, that the Pope is the lawful successor of Christ, contains a manner of speaking that is wholly heretical.

units.la: QVAE SIGNA ADVENTVM IESVITARVM PORTEDERINT.
units.tr: WHAT SIGNS PRESAGED THE ARRIVAL OF THE JESUITS

units.la: Circa adventum Ignatij & Iesuitarum monstrum marinum in Norvegia captum est mari procellosò: cui viso, Monachi nomen imposuerunt. Humana in facie videbatur, sed rustica capiteraso & læviz humeros cotegebat velut Monachorum cucullus. Pars infima in caudâ latâ desinebat; media multo erat latior, sagi militaris figura. Hanc effigiem D. Conrado Gesnero Tigurino dono misit illustris Margaretha Navarræ regina. Ea à viro nobili hanc effigiem acceperat, qui simile ad Carolum V. Imperat. in Hispania tunc agente deferebat: ille reginæ affirmavit, se monstrum hoc in Norvegia captum vidisse post gravissimas tempestates undis & fluctibus in littus eiectum: locumque designabat Diezu iuxta oppidum Den Eloph. Eiusdem monstri figuram D. Gesnero retulit Gisbertus, Medicus ex eadem Norvegia Romæ ad se missam esse: Georgius Fabricius eandem imaginem ad Gesnerum misit cum descriptione huiusmodi: Piscis hic captus est in mari Baltico iuxta Elboæ oppidum, quod miliaribus quatuor distat à Coppenhaga, Danici regni metropoli. Caput, collum, humeri, thorax humana specie: caput rasum ut Monachi: de collo, humeris, thorace cucullus quasi pependit, qui nigris & rubeis maculis fuit variatus. Cucullus desinit in fimbriâ, quali perizomate lumbos & femora tegere solemus. Brachiorum loco pinnæ fuerunt, pedum quoque cauda piscis. Totius monstri longitudo quatuor cubitorum: ad regem delatum & tostâ obraritate & miraculum asservatum est: captum anno salutis 1546. Bellonius addit, nullam vocem edidisse, præterquam suspiria quædam, summum mœrorem ac luctum referentia. Huic simile monstrum in Gallico etiam Oceano prope Burdegalas, eodem fere tempore captum, quidam Gallus eidem Gesnero scripsit. Homines in littore ambulantes hoc monstrum libenter allicit, & coram eis super aquas ludit: quod si homine ad mirantem appropinquare viderit, appropinquat etiam ipsum: & si qua potestate homine capit, & trahit in profundum, ut carnibus eius satietur. Hoc monstro marino, Monachum referente, clementissimus Deus mundo significare voluit, emersisse in terris duo Monachorum monstra, Iesuitas videlicet & Capucinos: qui monstri illius ingenium egregie referentes, doctrinâ & eruditione, item verbis & hypocritica sua sanctitate, aliisque multis artibus ad se pellicant homines, & in sui admirationem adducant: quosque sic illaqueatos teneant, hos in profundum barathrum errorum ac superstitionum horribilium demergant, & tandem in abyssum infernalem præcipitent,Proinde ab istis diligentissime cavent qui æternum perire nolint.
units.tr: Around the time of Ignatius and the Jesuits, a sea monster was caught in a stormy sea off Norway, and when it was seen the monks gave it the name "monk." It appeared to have a human face, but with a rustic, shaven head, and it covered its shoulders like a monk's cowl. Its lowest part ended in a broad tail, and its middle was much wider, in the shape of a soldier's cloak. The illustrious Margaret, Queen of Navarre, sent this likeness as a gift to Dr Conrad Gesner of Zurich. She had received it from a noble man, who had brought a similar one to Charles V, the Emperor, then in Spain. He assured the queen that he had seen this monster caught in Norway, cast ashore on the coast after very severe storms and waves, and he pointed out the place, Diezu, near the town of Den Eloph. Gisbert, a physician, reported to Gesner the same monster's likeness, which had been sent to him at Rome from that same Norway. Georgius Fabricius sent the same picture to Gesner with this description: "This fish was caught in the Baltic Sea near the town of Elboa, which is four miles from Copenhagen, the capital of the Danish kingdom. Head, neck, shoulders and chest had a human form; the head was shaven like a monk's; from the neck, shoulders and chest there hung, as it were, a cowl, which was variegated with black and red spots. The cowl ends in a fringe, like the loincloth we commonly use to cover the loins and thighs. In place of arms it had fins, and the lower part of the body was a fish's tail. The whole monster was four cubits long. It was brought to the king, and because of its strangeness it has been kept as a marvel. It was caught in the year of salvation 1546." Bellonius adds that it uttered no voice except certain sighs, expressing the greatest grief and mourning. A certain Frenchman wrote to the same Gesner that a similar monster was caught at about the same time in the Atlantic near Bordeaux. It readily lures men walking on the shore and plays before them on the waters; if it sees a man approaching to admire it, it also approaches him, and by some power it seizes the man and drags him into the depths, to satisfy its hunger with his flesh. By this sea monster, as a monk has explained, the most merciful God wished to signify to the world that two monstrous monks have emerged on earth, namely the Jesuits and the Capuchins. Representing the nature of that monster remarkably well, they entice men by their learning and erudition, likewise by their words, their hypocritical holiness and many other arts, and draw them into admiration of themselves. Those whom they hold thus ensnared they plunge into the deep abyss of errors and horrible superstitions, and at last hurl into the infernal pit. Therefore those who do not wish to perish for ever should take the greatest care to beware of them.

units.la: Referunt etiam historici, an. 1541. qui eu, quo confirmatus fuit Iesuitarum Ordo, sequutus est, in plurimis Europæ provinciis incredibilē ingentiū locustarū multitudinem subitò exorta fuisse. Hæ primò nullas habebat alas, sed magnos dabat saltus: paulo post quatuor adeptæ sunt, tātaque multitudine pvolârunt, ut duo milliaria in longū & latū cubito tenus ita occuparet, ut Solis quoque splendore à toto illo terræ spacio suâ densitate lenfitate excluderent. Dici non posse affirmant earum regionum incolae, quantumdam- nni dederint rebus humi nascentibus, vastantes & depascentes omnia ad radices usque. Transvolasse aiunt aquas, arbores, aedes & obvia quaeque: cumque earum alae succrevissent, fuisse humani digiti magnitudine, & tunc atrocius multo grassatas in ruges, & ea, quae in usus hominum necessarios gignit terra: tota aestate nulla vel vi vel arte earum saevitiam retardari potuisse, sed in autumno demum coelo frigefcente, extinctas esse, atro post se relicto semine, unde sequenti anno alii vermes orti sint. Mortuas pecudes edisse avidissime, porcos imprimis, ut Lauren. Surius testatur in comment. fuisse illis, qui se illis mire farserint: creditumque tum fuit, non absimiles extitisse illis Aegyptiacis, quarum in Exodo fit mentio.
units.tr: Historians also report that in the year 1541, the year after the Order of the Jesuits was confirmed, an incredible multitude of huge locusts suddenly appeared in most provinces of Europe. At first they had no wings but made great leaps; a little later they had four wings and flew in such numbers that they covered two miles in length and breadth, to the height of a cubit, so that with their density they shut out even the splendour of the sun from that whole tract of land. The inhabitants of those regions affirm that it cannot be said how much harm they did to the things growing on the ground, devastating and devouring everything down to the roots. They say they flew over waters, trees, houses and everything in their way; and when their wings had grown, they were the size of a human finger, and then they raged far more savagely against the crops and whatever the earth produces for the necessary uses of men. Throughout the summer they could not be checked by any force or skill of their cruelty, but at last in autumn, when the sky grew cold, they died out, leaving behind them an egg-seed from which other worms arose the following year. They devoured dead cattle most greedily, especially pigs, as Laurentius Surius testifies in his commentary; and those who had eaten them wonderfully swelled up. It was then believed that these were not unlike those Egyptian locusts mentioned in Exodus.

units.la: Hoc prodigio Deus absque dubio Iesuitas & Capucinos nuper natos significare voluit. Locustas enim monachorum greges denotare, ita manifestum est ex Apoc. 9. ut longa probatione non egeat. Et sane haec locustarum istarum descriptio, quae non in me conficta, sed ex Pontificiorum Commentariis desumpta est, Iesuitis & Capucinis egregie convenit. Nam isti quoque ab initio nullos habuere alas, hoc est, in nulla existimatione fuerunt, quum author eorum fuisset aliquandiu miles & literarum omnium prorsus rudis atque ignarus. Literarum autem cum aliqua notitiam acquisivisset, & discipulos nactus esset, pauci tamen erat numero, illique ipsi a clero Rom. valide exagitabantur, multisque molestiis afficiebantur. Mox tamen ac alas nacti sunt, id est, quum in authoritate & existimatione aliqua haberi coepissent, mirum in modum reverunt, & longe lateque dispersi sunt per totam Europam, florentissimis pascuis, hoc est, Ecclesiae Dei maximum inferentes damnum. Quemadmodum vero istae locustae brevi extinctae, & suavissimus cibus porcis factae sunt, ita sperarim ego, novorum istorum Prophetarum interitu praeforibus esse, quum iam videamus, ob deprehensam eorum hypocriticam seu fictam sanctitatem, dolos, fraudes & impostouras, authoritati ipsorum plurimum indies decedere. Quid vero in ultimo illo & uni- versali totius mundi iudicio, quod prope est, Dominus & Servator noster cum illis adfuturus sit, iustus ille iudex & Ecclesiae suae fidelissimus vindex solus novit: quem ego rogo supplex, ut cito cito veniat. Amen.
units.tr: By this portent God undoubtedly wished to signify the Jesuits and Capuchins, recently born. That locusts denote flocks of monks is so clear from Revelation 9 that it needs no long proof. Indeed this description of the locusts, which I have not invented but have taken from the commentaries of the Papists, fits the Jesuits and Capuchins admirably. For these also at the beginning had no wings, that is, they were held in no esteem, since their founder had for some time been a soldier and utterly unlearned and ignorant of all letters. But when he had acquired some knowledge of letters and had gained disciples, they were nonetheless few in number, and those very few were vigorously harassed by the Roman clergy and subjected to many troubles. Yet as soon as they gained wings, that is, once they began to be held in some authority and esteem, they multiplied wonderfully and spread far and wide throughout all Europe, into the most flourishing pastures, that is, inflicting the greatest damage on the Church of God. But just as those locusts were soon extinguished and became the most pleasant food for pigs, so I hope that the destruction of these new prophets is at hand, since we already see that, because their hypocritical or feigned holiness, their tricks, frauds and impostures have been detected, their authority declines more each day. What our Lord and Saviour will do, with those men, at that last and universal judgment of the whole world, which is near, that just Judge and most faithful avenger of his Church alone knows; and I humbly pray him to come quickly. Amen.

units.la: CAPVT II. DE NOMINE IESVITARVM.
units.tr: CHAPTER II. CONCERNING THE NAME OF THE JESUITS.

units.la: Via res & appellatio seu nomen ordinis Iesuitarum novum est, ideo etiam, ut fieri solet, variae ortae sunt de Etymologia nominis Iesuitarum disputationes. Solim autem ego tantam Grammaticorum litem mea facere, sed solumodo varias opiniones recensebo, & deinde lectori liberum permitta iudicium. Quidam igitur Romano more quaesiverunt etymologiam: Sicut enim olim Rom. Imperatores dicebantur Africani, Germanici, Asiatici, &c. non quod amici & socii illorum populorum essent: ita dictos Iesuitas putat, quasi professos & iuratos hostes Iesu. Alii ex histor. Vet. Testamenti παραφρασίας quaesierunt, dictosque putat Iesuitas, quasi Giezitas, vel Eauitas, aut certe Iebusitas. Et historiae sane illae non male ad Iesuitarum secta quadrat. Sunt qui arbitrantur ex Germanica lingua ratione appellationis posse commodius & melius inveniri: nec immerito, quum debeant esse Germanorum Apostoli. Sunt autem huo potissimum in Germanica lingua idiomata. Si itaque iuxta idioma germanicae inferioris vocabulum examinetur, etymologia erit Iesuwett, quasi qui & ipse longe sit a Iesu, & procul abducat a Iesu. In idiomate vero Germaniae superioris dicitur Iesu weitter, quasi Iesu wieder. Est enim inter t. & d. symbolismus usitatus, ut Tunnfherr & Dunnfherr. Et sicut nomina saepe sunt fatalia, ita Iesuitae ipsa appellatione praesi erunt caractere bestiae Apocalypseos. Vocatur autem homo ille peccati a Paulo ἀνομίας, a Ioh. Antichristus. Sicut igitur Germanice ad verbum diceretur Gottes wider und Christowider, ita haec secta vocatur Iesuwider: oppugnat enim praecipue nomen Iesu, quod ipse salvum faciat populum suum a peccatis eorum, Matth. 1. & Act. 4. Non est aliud nomen datum hominibus, in quo oporteat salvari. Sunt praeterea Grammatici quidā, qui per usitatas in Scholis figuras πρόσθεσιν scilic. & ἀφαίρεσιν etymologiā quaerunt, & disputant primā syllabam superfluè additam: vero aut nomine sine figurā appellandos esse Suitas, quos Horatius vocat Epicuri de grege porcos. Et dulcior sanè videri potest haec derivatio, sed ipsi ostendunt tales etymologias in Pontificiae religionis sectatores esse usitatas. Qui enim vocantur Canonici regulares, vitā & factis demonstrant se primā syllabā dempta esse Gulares.
units.tr: The title and designation, or name, of the Order of the Jesuits is new, and so, as usually happens, various disputes have arisen about the etymology of the name Jesuit. I do not intend to take up this great quarrel of the grammarians, but will only set out the various opinions and then leave the judgment free to the reader. Some, in the Roman manner, sought an etymology: just as the Roman emperors were called Africanus, Germanicus, Asiaticus, and so on, not because they were friends and allies of those peoples, so these think the Jesuits are so called as if they were professed and sworn enemies of Jesus. Others sought it from paronyms [παρωνυμίας] in the historical books of the Old Testament, and think the Jesuits are so called as if they were Gizites, or Hivites, or at any rate Jebusites. And those histories indeed fit the sect of the Jesuits not badly. Some think that a more convenient and better name can be found from the German language, and not unreasonably, since they ought to be the Apostles of the Germans. The idioms of German are chiefly of this kind. If, then, the word is examined according to the idiom of Lower Germany, the etymology will be Iesuwett, as if one who is himself far from Jesus and drives others away from Jesus. In the idiom of Upper Germany, however, it is said Iesu weitter, as if Iesu wieder. For there is a common interchange between t and d, as in Tunnfherr and Dunnfherr. And just as names are often fateful, so the Jesuits by their very name will bear the mark of the beast of the Apocalypse. The man of sin is called by Paul lawlessness [ἀνομίας], and by John Antichrist. So just as in German one would say, word for word, Gottes wider and Christowider, so this sect is called Iesuwider, for it chiefly attacks the name of Jesus, who saves his people from their sins, Matt. 1 and Acts 4: There is no other name given to men by which they must be saved. Moreover, some grammarians seek the etymology by the figures customary in the schools, namely addition [πρόσθεσιν] and subtraction [ἀφαίρεσιν], and argue that a first syllable has been superfluously added; or that, without any figure, they should be called Suitas, whom Horace calls the pigs of Epicurus' herd. This derivation may indeed seem the sweeter, but they themselves show that such etymologies are customary among the adherents of the Papist religion. For those who are called Canons Regular show by their life and deeds that, with the first syllable removed, they are Gulares (gluttons).

units.la: Cūm autem Romae vel nata, vel certe confirmata sit haec secta Iesuitarum, volunt nonnulli, non quaerendam esse vel Hebraicam, vel Germanicam, sed Romanam, seu Latinam etymologiam, & concedunt, dictos esse Iesuitas, quòd summa professionis ac vitae ipsorum sit IESVS seu IESVVITA. Sic etiam Gretserus contra Simonem Stenium Iessaeos Iudaeorum ὁμωνύμως contendit esse Iesuitas, ut qui à Iesu Iessaei dicti sint. At vero si hoc verum esset, Philo & Iosephus Iudaei, & propterea Christi ac Iesu nominis hostes, non tam exquisitis laudibus Iessaeos extulissent.
units.tr: Since this sect of the Jesuits was either born or at least confirmed at Rome, some hold that the etymology should be sought not in Hebrew or German but in Roman or Latin, and they concede that the Jesuits are so called because the sum of their profession and life is IESVS or IESVVITA. So also Gretser, against Simon Stenius, contends that the Essenes of the Jews are homonymously called Jesuits, as if they were named Essenes from Jesus. But if this were true, Philo and Josephus, Jews and therefore enemies of Christ and of the name of Jesus, would not have praised the Essenes with such exquisite eulogies.

units.la: Redēne autē, vel secus hoc nomen Ordini illorum tributū sit, postea videbimus.
units.tr: Whether this name was rightly or otherwise given to their Order, we shall see later.

units.la: Nunc inquirendum à quo hunc titulum fatis superbum habeant, & quis eum tribuerit illis. De hoc Ioannes Petrus Maffaeus lib.2. cap.5. Vitae Ignatij Loyolae sic fere scribit: Cum navigationis Hierosolymitanae consilia Ignatio & sociis in irritum cecidissent circa annum 1537. Romam Ignatium contendisse. Orandi autem causa non longe ab urbe templo ingressio, statimque abstractio à sensibus clarissima in luce per speciem illi visi Deum Patrem ostendisse, & Iesu filio, baiulanti crucem, & crudelissimis affectio supplicijs, praesentem Ignatium, sociosque absentes commendasse: quos ille cum infidem ac patrocinium recepisset, ad Ignatium placido ac sereno vultu conversus, haec verba locutus sit: EGO VOBIS ROMAE PROPITIUS ERO: atque hoc ipsum vel inprimis fuisse causa, quod Ignatius confirmatae postmodum Societati salutare potissimum nomen IESV indiderit. Refert idem Ribadeneira in vita Ignatij lib.2. c.12. P. Annibal Codretus quoque Iesuita hunc titulum ad eandem originem refert: scribit enim, Societatem suam hoc nomen assumpsisse, quod caelestis Pater, omnes qui in ea sunt, tanquam Socios adjunxerit & commendarit filio suo Iesu, qui eos etiam pro talibus agnoverit & receperit.
units.tr: Now we must inquire from whom they have this rather proud title, and who assigned it to them. On this, John Peter Maffei, book 2, chapter 5, of the Life of Ignatius of Loyola, writes more or less as follows: When the plans for a voyage to Jerusalem had come to nothing for Ignatius and his companions, about the year 1537, Ignatius hastened to Rome. Entering a temple not far from the city to pray, he was at once withdrawn from the senses into a most clear light, and a vision showed him God the Father, and his Son Jesus carrying the cross and afflicted with the cruellest torments; the Father commended Ignatius, present, and his absent companions; and when Jesus had received them into his faith and protection, turning to Ignatius with a calm and serene countenance, he spoke these words: I WILL BE PROPITIOUS TO YOU AT ROME. And this itself was chiefly the reason why Ignatius afterwards gave the saving name of Jesus to the Society when it was confirmed. The same Ribadeneira reports this in the Life of Ignatius, book 2, chapter 12. Father Annibal Codretus, also a Jesuit, traces this title to the same origin, for he writes: Their Society assumed this name because the heavenly Father has joined and commended all who are in it, as companions, to his Son Jesus, who has also acknowledged and received them as such.

units.la: Quā fide autem haec illorum narratio digna sit, Lector, quaeso, attendat. Maffaeius dicit, hanc visionem vel imprimis causae fuisse, cur Ignatius confirmatae postmodum Societati nomen Iesu indiderit. Si hoc verum est, Ignatius titulum hunc Societati suae dedit, non ante sed post confirmationem demum. Atqui hunc titulum ante confirmationem usurparunt, ut in supplicatione sua ad Paulum III. Papam pro confirmatione impetranda his verbis indicant: Quicunque in Societate nostra, quam Iesu nomine insigniri cupimus, sub crucis vexillo militare vult, &c.
units.tr: Reader, I beg you to consider how worthy of belief this account of theirs is. Maffei says that this vision was chiefly the cause why Ignatius afterwards gave the name of Jesus to the Society when it had been confirmed. If this is true, Ignatius gave this title to his Society not before but only after its confirmation. Yet they used this title before confirmation, as they indicate in their supplication to Pope Paul III to obtain confirmation, in these words: Whoever wishes to serve under the standard of the cross in our Society, which we desire to be marked with the name of Jesus, etc.

units.la: Quaero etiam, si haec visio vere facta est, & Ignatius, cùm primùm Romam venit, illam Petro Leinez, qui post eum Generalis creatus est, ordine exposuit, ut Maffaeius & Ribadeneira referunt, cur occultavit eam Leinez, iis maximè temporibus, quibus summa necessitas postulabat, ut eam manifestaret? Cur eam nō Parlamento & Facultati Theologicae Parisiensi opposuit, cùm interdicerent eis, ne hunc titulum usurparent? In promptu causa est: Quia de hac visione tum adhuc nihil norant, vel tam pudendae fabulae eos tunc adhuc temporis puderet.
units.tr: I also ask: if this vision truly happened, and Ignatius, as soon as he came to Rome, related it in order to Peter Lainez, who was afterwards made General, as Maffei and Ribadeneira report, why did Lainez conceal it, especially at those times when the greatest necessity demanded that he reveal it? Why did they not set it against the Parlement and the Theological Faculty of Paris, when these forbade them to usurp this title? The reason is plain: either they then knew nothing of this vision, or they were still ashamed of so shameful a fable at that time.

units.la: Dicant etiam Iesuitae quo in loco post Christi ascensionem in coelos, à quibus & quo tempore vnquam audita sit vox Patris coelestis. Quis etiam credat Filium Dei coelo descendisse, ut ferocem ac truculentum militem Hispanum, & insignem idololatram alloqueretur, & propitium se Iesuitis futurum diceret Romae, quae Antichristi seu filij perditionis sedes est, quae, ut Abbas Vrspergensis testatus est, per malitiam hominum, non per religionem orbem vicit: ad quam trahit homines non ipsorum devotio aut pura conscientia, sed scelerum multiplicium ciūm cium perpetratio, & litium decisio pretio comparata. An non Christus ipse dixit: Si quis vobis dixerit, Ecce, hic est Christus, ecce illic est, nolite credere. Ab eo igitur tempore, quo Monachatus exortus est, vix crediderim crassius mendacium inter tot myriades fabularum monasticarum a quoquam publicatum fuisse, & tamen eius modi homines orthodoxos mendaciorum subinde insimulant.
units.tr: Let the Jesuits also say in what place, after Christ's ascension into heaven, and by whom and at what time, the voice of the heavenly Father was ever heard. Who would believe that the Son of God came down from heaven to address a fierce and savage Spanish soldier and a notorious idolater, and said he would be propitious to the Jesuits at Rome, which is the seat of Antichrist or the son of perdition, and which, as the Abbot of Ursperg testified, has conquered the world through the malice of men, not through religion? To Rome it draws men not by their devotion or pure conscience, but by the commission of manifold crimes and the settlement of lawsuits bought with money. Did not Christ himself say: If anyone says to you, Behold, here is Christ, or there, do not believe him. From the time when monasticism arose, I could hardly believe that a grosser lie has been published by anyone among so many myriads of monastic fables; and yet men of this kind from time to time accuse orthodox people of lying.

units.la: Cum igitur hoc mendacium olfaceret Montaignes Iesuita, & vanitatem huius fabulae intelligeret, noluit illam defendere, sed alio dolo ac fraude usus est, asseruitque Papam & Concilium hoc titulo Iesuitarum Ordinem coronasse. Idem asserit etiam de la Fon. c. 35, inquiens: Populum sic ordinis huius viros appellasse, quod eorum Societas a sancta Sede de nomine Iesu appellata sit. Et paulo post ait: Iesuita non se Iesuitas nominarunt, sed S. Sedes eos Societatem Iesu appellavit. Ex quo intelligitur, ne hunc quidem de la Fon. fidem aliquam huic fabulae tribuisse, cum mentionem eius nullam prorsus faciat, nec titulum hunc ad visionem illam, sed ad alium authorem referat. Si autem & ipse primam saltem Pauli III. Bullam legisset, facile intellexisset, neque S. Sedem, hoc est, Papam, sed Ignatium cum Socijs hunc titulum iam tum in supplicatione ad Pontificem sibi tribuisse. Sed demus hoc maxime Iesuitis, visione hanc vere facta fuisse, modo illi hoc nobis vicissim dent, Ignatiu Loyolam, vel aliud nomen hoc Societati huic indidisse, a Iesu quidem, sed non a vero illo Iesu Filio Dei, sed ab illo mirabili Iesu, qui Ignatio vertigine correpto, dum Roma proficiscitur, feus viam apparuit, os habitumque gerens monachi, quale hodie Iesuitae circumferunt.
units.tr: Since the Jesuit Montaigne smelled out this lie and understood the vanity of this fable, he did not wish to defend it, but used another trick and fraud, and asserted that the Pope and the Council had crowned this Order with the title of Jesuits. La Fon asserts the same in chapter 35, saying: The people called the men of this Order by this name because their Society was named from the name of Jesus by the Holy See. And a little later he says: The Jesuits did not call themselves Jesuits; the Holy See named the Society the Society of Jesus. From this it is understood that La Fon too gave no credit to this fable, since he makes no mention of it at all, nor refers this title to that vision, but to another author. But if he had at least read the first Bull of Paul III, he would easily have understood that it was not the Holy See, that is the Pope, but Ignatius with his companions who had already then claimed this title for themselves in the supplication to the Pontiff. But grant this to the Jesuits, that the vision really took place, provided they grant us in return that Ignatius Loyola, or someone else, gave this name to the Society: from Jesus indeed, but not from that true Jesus, the Son of God, but from that wondrous Jesus who, when Ignatius was seized by a fit of dizziness as he set out for Rome, appeared to him on the way, bearing the face and habit of a monk, such as the Jesuits carry about today.

units.la: Quemadmodum autem, ut P. Boquinus in Assertione contra Iesuitas docet, vehementer probandum, quod novi isti socij per hanc a se confictam appellationem non obscure significat, se improbare atque adeo damnare antecedentium Ordinum authores, qui his cognomina ab hominum nominibus petita indiderunt, suosque discipulos Franciscanos a Francisco, Dominicanos a Dominico, Benedictinos a Benedicto, Augustinianos ab Augustino, &c. nominarunt (qua re ipsos non exigua schismatu atque superstitionum sparsisse femina constat) & eos revocant ad Iesum Christum, ut unicum verae religionis fontem & caput (a quo illos defecisse sibique effodisse cisternas, quae aquas non continet, illa cognomina testificantur) ita quoque vehementer improbandum, & haec ipsorum audacia atque temeritas reprehendenda, quod repudiato omnium, qui Christo nomen dederunt communi titulo iam olim recepto, cuius author est Spiritus sanctus, & quod apud oes pios maiores summo in honore semper habitum fuit, aliud hactenus in auditu minimeque ipsis convenientem, & cum no parva Christi, omnium piorum Servatoris, contumelia coniunctum, confingere, sibique privata authoritate indere ausi sint. Novum esse Iesuitarum cognomentum nemo est qui nesciat. Novitatem autem cum in omnibus rebus, tum maxime in religionis causa oes pij & docti vehementer fugiendam esse recte praecipiunt, quod & suo exemplo Apostoli confirmarunt. Nam cum Evangelica doctrina novitatis nomine infamaretur initio ab hostibus, ipsos & inprimis Paulum sedulo dedisse operam, ut istam calumniam depellerent, ex ipsorum scriptis manifeste cognoscimus. Et sane nova nomina cur nisi novis rebus significandis inveniantur? Vocabula quidem nova fingere rebus novis, non improbatur ipsi quoque Hieronymo in c. 1. epist. ad Gal. sed tu id faciendum esse idem existimat, dum vel utilitas, vel necessitas suadet vel potius urgent. At cum Iesuitae ad hoc coisse & prodisse videri velint, ut antiquam pietatem restituant, quae ipsos vel utilitas induxere, vel necessitas cogere potuit ad hoc cognomentum confingendum? Primum novo nomine diversum ab eo quod instituerunt, promittunt: atque ita fiunt ipsi a seipsis dissidelt. Deinde vetustae doctrinae atque religioni qui convenit nova appellatio? Nihil certe magis quam veteri vestimento, iuxta sententiam Christi, particula rudis panni. Praeterea si Propheticam & Apostolicam doctrinam pariter & religionem tradere instituerunt, quae stultitia est, remut verissimam ita & vetustissimam nova ac ficta appellatione suspectam odiosamque reddere?
units.tr: Moreover, as P. Boquinus teaches in his Assertion against the Jesuits, it must be strongly condemned that these new associates, by the name they have invented for themselves, clearly signal that they disapprove of, and indeed condemn, the founders of the earlier Orders. Those founders gave their followers names taken from men: they called the Franciscans after Francis, the Dominicans after Dominic, the Benedictines after Benedict, the Augustinians after Augustine, and so on. It is well known that this practice has spread no small seed of schism and superstition. Such names also call those Orders back to Jesus Christ, the one fountain and head of true religion, from whom they are said to have fallen away and dug for themselves cisterns that hold no water. Thus it must also be strongly condemned, and this audacity and rashness rebuked, that they have dared, on their own private authority, to reject the common title that all who have given their name to Christ have long received, a title whose author is the Holy Spirit and which has always been held in the highest honour by all the godly and by our forefathers. In its place they have devised another name, unheard of until now, one that does not suit them and carries no small insult to Christ, the Saviour of all the godly. No one is unaware that "Jesuit" is a new nickname. Yet all the godly and learned rightly teach that novelty must be avoided above all in matters of religion, as in everything else, and the Apostles confirmed this by their own example. For when the Evangelical doctrine was at first slandered by its enemies under the charge of novelty, we know from the Apostles' own writings that they, and Paul above all, took great pains to refute this calumny. And indeed, why are new names invented, unless to signify new things? To coin new words for new things is not disapproved, as Jerome himself says on the first chapter of the Epistle to the Galatians, but he adds that this should be done only when usefulness or necessity suggests it, or rather presses. But since the Jesuits wish it to appear that they came forward to restore ancient piety, what usefulness or necessity could have moved them, or compelled them, to invent this nickname? First, by its new name it promises something different from what they instituted, and so they become at odds with themselves. Second, what fitting relation does a new appellation have to ancient doctrine and religion? Certainly nothing: it is like, according to the saying of Christ, a piece of raw cloth sewn on an old garment. Furthermore, if they have undertaken to hand down the prophetic and apostolic doctrine and religion, what folly is it to make the most true and most ancient religion suspect and odious by a new and invented name?

units.la: DE ORIGINE
units.tr: ON THE ORIGIN

units.la: Videamus etiam num recte fabricata haec appellatio Sectae huic schismatis nota manifeste inurat: ut hoc pacto ipsi criminis rei fiant, de quo nos tamen perpetuo hodie accusant. Deus concordiam & unitatem Ecclesiae suae omnibus modis commendavit: unde etiam eiusdem Patris voluntate & consilio effectum est, ut omnes uno Christianorum nomine dicti notatique fuerint, iam inde ab initio istius per Evangelij praedicationem aggregationis. Ideoque hanc appellationem unitatis illius velut Sacramentum quoddam atque vinculum constat esse. Apparet etiam in eodem cognomine esse inclusam religionis professionem. Hocigitur vinculum unitatis dissolvit quisquis aliam sibi asciscit appellationem, quod etiam Paulus manifeste docet 1. Cor. 1. Abnegationis quoque & defectionis species est, aliud sibi fine ulla necessitate affingere nomen. Extat enim in Gratiano 11. quaest. 3. Paragraphus ex Augustino citatus, qui docet, Eum qui se Christianum esse negat, negati simul Christi convinci. Ac mirabile sane est, quod Iesuitae sic coiisse videri volunt, ut dispersa Ecclesiae membra colligant, interque se coagmentent, cum ipsi interim sine authore, sine causa, malo perniciosoque exemplo separationem in Ecclesia instituerint.
units.tr: Let us see also whether this name, so carelessly devised for this sect, clearly brands it with the mark of schism, so that by this means they themselves become guilty of the very crime for which they now accuse us continually. God has commended concord and unity of his Church in every way. Hence, by the will and counsel of the same Father, it came about that all were called and marked with the one name of Christians from the very beginning of that gathering through the preaching of the Gospel. This name is therefore plainly a kind of sacrament and bond of that unity. It is also clear that a profession of religion is contained in that same appellation. So whoever adopts for himself another name dissolves this bond of unity, as Paul plainly teaches in 1 Cor. 1. To assume for oneself, without any necessity, a different name is also a form of denial and desertion. For in Gratian, 11 q. 3, there is a paragraph cited from Augustine, who teaches that he who denies that he is a Christian is at the same time convicted of denying Christ. And it is truly remarkable that the Jesuits wish to appear to have come together so as to gather the scattered members of the Church and join them to one another, when they themselves, without an author and without cause, have by a bad and harmful example introduced separation into the Church.

units.la: At fortasse dicturi sunt, id se finxisse & assumpsisse cognominis, quo significaret, nomineque ipso profiterentur se esse Iesu cultores, hoc est, in eum se credere, ipsi fidei, omnemque suam salutem ab eo expectare. Sed quae non est curiositas aut vanitas tantum, verum etiam iniquitas, id quod omnibus piis est commune & Christiano cognomine continetur, ac caelesti spiritu authore significatur, paucos sibi vindicare, eiusque rei causa privata authoritate novum sibi confingere & asciscere titulum. Aut si quid privilegij & praerogativae obtendit novus hic Ordo, diploma proferant vere Apostolicum, id est, non a Romana seu Babylonica, sed caelesti curia profectum, & omnibus examinandum iudicandumque exhibeant. Sed nisi me animus vehementer fallit, scio quam ob causam Christianorum cognomine repudiato, novum & prioribus seculis incognitum, Iesuitarum scilicet confinxerint sibi, elegerint istiusmodi in Italia nati homines: nimirum, ne viderentur stupidi & stolidi, quod Italico idiomate per hominem Christianum stolidum ac stupidum significare ac intelligere soleant, ut Christianus Franken, in Iesuiticis castris educatus, in Colloquio suo Iesuitico testatur.
units.tr: But perhaps they will say that they have devised and adopted this title so as to signify, and to profess by the very name, that they are worshippers of Jesus, that is, that they believe in him, trust in him, and expect all their salvation from him. But this is not merely curiosity or vanity; it is injustice, since that which is common to all the pious and is contained in the Christian name, and is signified by the heavenly Spirit as its author, is claimed by a few for themselves, and for this reason they devise and assume for themselves a new title on their own authority. Or if this new Order alleges any privilege or prerogative, let them produce a diploma truly apostolic, that is, one issued not by the Roman or Babylonian court but by the heavenly court, and let them submit it to be examined and judged by all. But unless my mind greatly deceives me, I know why they rejected the name of Christians and devised for themselves a name new and unknown in earlier ages, that of Jesuits, namely men born in Italy who chose this name: surely so that they would not seem stupid and dull, since in the Italian idiom people are accustomed to mean and understand by a stupid and dull Christian man something of this kind, as the Christian Franken, brought up in the Jesuit camps, testifies in his Jesuit Colloquy.

units.la: Obiicit etiam Gretserus contra Stenium, Si fideles recte a Christo nominentur Christiani, se quoque, & fui Ordinis homines ac Socios non minus recte nominari Iesuitas a nomine Iesu. Respondeo: Filius Dei Iesus appellatur ideo, quod nos salvet ab omnibus peccatis nostris, & quod aliunde salus nec peti debeat, nec alibi reperiri possit. Christus autem vocatur ideo, quod a Patre ordinatus & a Spiritu sancto vinctus sit Propheta ac Doctor, qui nobis arcanum consilium & voluntatem Patris de redemptione nostra patefecit: & summus Pontifex, qui nos unico sacrificio sui corporis redemit & assidue pro nobis apud Patrem deprecatur: & Rex, qui nos suo verbo & Spiritu gubernat & partam nobis salutem tuetur & conservat. Ab hoc Christo nos recte Christiani vocamur, quia per fidem sumus membra Christi & unctionis ipsius participes. Iesuitae autem perperam a Iesu sic nominantur: non enim salutem hominibus dant, sed potius auferunt, homines a Iesu Servatore abducendo ad nescio quos tutelares Dios. Addeque quod Christiani vocamur expresse & diserte in scriptura, ut Act. 11. 26, quum Iesuitae nusquam vocentur vel in veteris vel in novi Testamenti libris.
units.tr: Gretser also objects against Stenius: If the faithful are rightly named Christians from Christ, then we too, and the men of our Order and Companions, are no less rightly named Jesuits from the name of Jesus. I answer: the Son of God is called Jesus because he saves us from all our sins, and because salvation ought not to be sought from anywhere else, nor can it be found elsewhere. Christ, however, is so called because he was ordained by the Father and anointed by the Holy Spirit to be Prophet and Teacher, who revealed to us the hidden counsel and will of the Father concerning our redemption; and High Priest, who redeemed us by the single sacrifice of his body and constantly intercedes for us before the Father; and King, who governs us by his Word and Spirit and guards and preserves for us the salvation he has obtained. From this Christ we are rightly called Christians, because through faith we are members of Christ and partakers of his anointing. The Jesuits, however, are wrongly named from Jesus, for they do not give salvation to men, but rather take it away, drawing men away from Jesus the Saviour to I know not what tutelary gods. Add that we are called Christians expressly and clearly in Scripture, as in Acts 11:26, whereas the Jesuits are nowhere named in the books of the Old or New Testament.

units.la: Ad has igitur absurditates, quantum coniicio, leniendas, difficultatesque quas hactenus enumeravimus, tolledas, inventa est ab ipsis cognominis huius Periphrasis, & a quibusdam in ipsorum scriptis praefixa, nimirum Societas Iesu (omisso Iesuitarum nomine) imo etiam Domini de Societate Iesu: vel quod ipsos Iesus nuper admodum allegerit in collegas & socios ad salutem miseris hominibus impertiendam: quod prorsus impium ac blasphemum esset dicere: hoc enim Iesu Christo sic proprium esse, Apostolica testatur doctrina, ut socium nullum admittat: vel quod (quae mitior est interpretatio, pauciora incommoda secum trahit) talem cum Iesu societate habeant, ut ab eo salute quâ omnibus in ipsum credentibus sacræ literæ promittunt, consequantur. Primus autem gradus ad ineundam cum Iesu societatem necessarius, est fides. Deinde ad retinendam cum eo societatem, opus est vitâ Christiano nomine dignâ. Tertius gradus quo societas vera Iesu confirmatur, est tolerantia crucis. Novitium vero Iesu simulatum, vera Christi fide præditum non esse; nec in eo apparere sanctæ vitæ studium: nullum denique conspici in eo crucis Christi vestigium. P. Boquinus in prædicta Assertione cap. 9. & 11. & 13. ita docte & solide probat, ut nec hic titulus ipsis convenire videatur. Et quidam comparatione Iesu & Iesuitarum sequenti Epigrammate, historica plane fide, demonstravit quoque, eos falso sese vel Iesuitas, vel Socios, vel de Societate Iesu nominare. Id Epigramma autem sic habet. Presbyteri, à socio geritis qui nomina IHESV, Dispereamus vos IHESV s amare potest. Humano generi fons & dator ille salutis, Vos contra innocuis omnibus exitio. Cauponantum agmen flagris Templo expulit ille, Et dixit: Precibus est sacer ille locus. Templa dicata DEO per vos SPELVNCA LATRONVM, Per vos facta DEI est, magna taberna, domus. Fraternum passim Lex Christi inculcat amorem: Exultat à vestris quam procul ille choris. Non Vltor Christus, non Sector: vos dare flammis Corpora, vos Christi membra secare juvat. Plebem jussa Patrum, natos servare parentum Exemplis Christi nos monet ordo suis: Contra in honore Magistratus, vel habere parentes, Ignatij patris vos documenta vetant. Ignatij, in cujus juratos verba Magistri Spernere vos homines hinc juvat, inde Deum. Ignatij, cui dote viros fraudare, parentes Prole sua, voti summa caputque fuit. Quisquis obit, vobis cedant Legata necesse est, Nec refert, orbus, an pater ille cluat: Exheredantur nati quoque quam procul absunt A IHESV hæc? Hæres nullius ille fuit. Vos censu patrio dites spoliatis alumnos: Restituì dominis res jubet ille suis. Discipulos sine re paucos sibi junxit IHESVS: Cœtibus in vestris pauper ubique jacet. Nil habuit Christus, vos omnia: nulla suppellex, Nulla domus Christo, culcitra nulla fuit: Vos urbem vestris domibus completis, & orbem Suffulti plumâ variicolore caput. Vos omnes capitis Tonsura coronat, IHESVS Nulla nisi ejusdem plexa corona fuit. Personam fuciqueexpers agitavit IHESVS, Ore nihil vestro pietius esse potest. Vobis larga cavi spirant mendacia folles: At Christus doctus nonnisi vera loqui. Plurima sunt Christi miracula, qualia narrant Nulla domi à vobis edita, multa foris.
units.tr: To soften these absurdities, as far as I can guess, and to remove the difficulties we have listed so far, a periphrasis of this name has been invented by themselves and prefixed in some of their writings, namely the Society of Jesus (leaving out the name of Jesuits), or even Lords of the Society of Jesus; either because Jesus recently chose them as colleagues and companions for bringing salvation to wretched men, which would be altogether impious and blasphemous to say, for the apostolic teaching testifies that this is so proper to Jesus Christ that he admits no companion; or because (which is the milder interpretation and brings fewer inconveniences with it) they have such a fellowship with Jesus that they obtain from him the salvation which the sacred letters promise to all who believe in him. The first step necessary for entering into fellowship with Jesus is faith. Then, to keep that fellowship with him, a life worthy of the Christian name is required. The third step by which true fellowship with Jesus is confirmed is endurance of the cross. But the Jesuit novice is one who pretends to have the true faith of Christ, but has none; in whom no zeal for a holy life appears, and in whom, finally, no trace of the cross of Christ is seen. P. Boquinus in the aforesaid Assertion, chapters 9, 11 and 13, proves this so learnedly and soundly that this title does not seem to suit them either. And someone, by comparing Jesus and the Jesuits in the following epigram, with plainly historical faithfulness, has also shown that they falsely call themselves Jesuits, or Companions, or of the Society of Jesus. The epigram runs thus. Priests, you who bear the names of companions of IHESVS, may you perish, for IHESVS cannot love you. He is the fountain and giver of salvation to the human race; you, on the contrary, are a destruction to all the innocent. He drove the band of hucksters from the Temple with whips and said: that place is sacred to prayers. You have made the temples dedicated to God a den of robbers; through you the house of God has become a great tavern. The law of Christ everywhere urges brotherly love; how far from your choirs he exults. Christ was no avenger, no persecutor; it pleases you to give bodies to the flames and to cut the limbs of Christ. Your order warns us to keep the people under the commands of the fathers and children to keep their parents, following the examples of Christ. On the contrary, the teachings of your father Ignatius forbid you to honour the magistrate or to have parents. You delight to despise men, on the one hand, and God, on the other, by the words of the master sworn to by you, Ignatius, to whom it was the chief vow and purpose to defraud men of their wealth and their children of their parents. Whoever dies, of necessity his legacies fall to you, and it makes no difference whether he was childless or a father. Children too are disinherited: how far are these things from IHESVS? He was heir of nothing. You enrich yourselves with the paternal estate and despoil your pupils; he bids the owner's goods be restored to their lords. IHESVS joined to himself a few disciples without property; in your assemblies the poor lie everywhere. Christ had nothing, you have everything: he had no furniture, no house, no mattress; you have filled the city, your houses, and the world, your head propped up on variously coloured feathers. A tonsure crowns all your heads, while IHESVS had no crown except one of plaited thorns. IHESVS lived without mask or deceit; nothing can be more pious than your mouth. Your bellows breathe out lying wind in abundance, while Christ, being wise, spoke nothing but truth. There are very many miracles of Christ, such as they tell of; none wrought by you at home, many abroad.

units.la: Iesuitae non quantur Iesu vitam.
units.tr: The Jesuits do not imitate the life of Jesus.

units.la: DE ORIGINE
units.tr: ON THE ORIGIN

units.la: Orbe procul nostro: credat Maranus Appella, Non ego: & Autores sit penes ista fides. Fibula cum Christo nil convenit, omnia pugnant. Quid confine Polo scilicet Orcus habet? Aut vobis IHESVS? quos usus instrumento magistro Natura haud agnos, sed probat esse Lupos.
units.tr: Far from our world, let Maranus Appella believe it; I do not. Let faith in such things rest with its authors. A fable agrees with Christ in nothing; everything fights against it. What does Orcus, that neighbour of heaven, hold? Or do you have Jesus? Nature, the teacher of practice, does not prove you to be lambs, but wolves.

units.la: Sed hanc disceptationem decidamus verbis Ludolphi Carthusiani, qui ducentis annis ante adventum Iesuitarum vixit. Hic Ludolphus de vita Christi part. 1. c. 1 o. edita anno 1529, sic inter alia scribit: Christus est nomen gratiae: Iesus est nomen gloriae, honoris & sanctitatis. Sicut enim in hac vita per gratiam Baptismi a Christo dicimur Christiani, sic in caelesti gloria in Domino Iesu dicemur Iesuitae, id est, a Salvatore salvati. Sancti qui in caelis sunt, & fruuntur aeterna gloria, veri sunt Iesuitae, triumphantes & sancti servi Dei: qui vero adhuc in terris degunt, & militant pugnantque in multis periculis, militiae suae nomen retinere & gerere debent, quod est verum Christianorum nomen. Si vero ita se gerunt ut sancti, qui in aeterna gloria sedent super throno salutis, nomen Iesuitarum tum obtinere possunt. Quia verb haberi volunt in numero militantium & pugnantium sub Christi vexillo, Christi quoque nomine contenti sint. Huic Ludolpho longe admodum alium, cum videlicet, qui cripsit Pomerium Sermonum in parte aestivali de Circumcisione Seth: 4: is de nomine Iesu sic scribit: Iesus est nomen Divinum & aeterna salutis: Christus autem dicitur Vnctus, & sic est nomen militiae Christianae, hoc nomen Christiani, quo norunt se tanquam pugiles unctos in pugna contra mundum, carnem, diabolum. Unde in praesenti competit nobis nomen Christi propter militiam salvificam, sed in futuro, quum erimus in salute, competet nobis nomen Iesu, id est, salutis. Liber hic scriptus est an. 1437.
units.tr: But let us settle this dispute with the words of Ludolphus the Carthusian, who lived two hundred years before the Jesuits arrived. In his Life of Christ, part 1, chapter 10, printed in 1529, Ludolphus writes among other things: Christ is the name of grace; Jesus is the name of glory, honour and holiness. For just as in this life we are called Christians through the grace of Baptism, so in heavenly glory we shall be called Jesuits in the Lord Jesus, that is, the saved of the Saviour. The saints who are in heaven and enjoy eternal glory are true Jesuits, triumphant and holy servants of God. Those who still live on earth, fighting and struggling amid many dangers, ought to keep and bear the name of their warfare, which is the true name of Christians. If indeed they conduct themselves as saints, who sit in eternal glory on the throne of salvation, then they may obtain the name of Jesuits. But since they wish to be counted among those who fight under Christ's banner, let them be content with the name of Christ too. Quite different from this Ludolphus is the author of the Pomerium of Sermons, in the summer part, on the Circumcision of Seth, sermon 4, who writes thus about the name of Jesus: Jesus is the divine name of eternal salvation. Christ, however, means "Anointed," and so it is the name of Christian warfare; this is the name of Christians, by which they know themselves to be anointed fighters in battle against the world, the flesh and the devil. Hence the name of Christ fits us in the present, on account of our saving warfare; but in the future, when we are in salvation, the name of Jesus, that is, of salvation, will fit us. This book was written in 1437.

units.la: Haec cum ita sint, non iniuria interdictum est Iesuitis in celeberrimo Conventu Poissiacensi, totius Ecclesiae Gallicanae nomine, ut ab appellatione IESV & IESVITARVM, atque etiam SOCIETATIS IESV deinceps prorsus abstinerent. Factum hoc anno 1561. Decemb. 15. die.
units.tr: Since this is so, the Jesuits were not wrongly forbidden, in the most celebrated Assembly of Poissy, in the name of the whole Gallican Church, to use from then on the appellation of JESUS and of JESUITS, or indeed the title SOCIETY OF JESUS at all. This was done in the year 1561, on 15 December.

units.la: Quicquid sit, quadrant in eos Serapionis Episcopi verba: Propellibus, inquit, ovium, Christum induti, dicunt se quidem, quod non sunt, quod aut sunt, dici nolunt, sed sua improbitatem amictu nominis tegunt, qui commune quidem habent nomen, studeant vero, ut nomen Christi funditus deleant, qui contra Iesum militant, & Iesum invocant.
units.tr: Whatever the case, the words of Serapion the Bishop fit them: They put on Christ, he says, like sheep's clothing, and they say they are what they are not; they do not wish to be called what they are, but they cover their wickedness with the cloak of a name. They have a common name, yet they strive to blot out the name of Christ utterly, since they fight against Jesus while invoking Jesus.

units.la: In Gallia tamen multis in locis a vulgo non Iesuitae, sed IESVASTAE nominati sunt. Imo Anno 1564. in controversia, quam cum Universitate Parisiensi habuerunt, ab Advocatis tantum Iesuitae appellati sunt. Hunc titulum etiam eis tribuit Clarissimus Iurisperitus Carolus Molinaeus in suo Consilio, de Receptione eorum in Regno Galliae: & titulus eius sic quidem habet: An Iesuitae sint recipiendi in Regno Franciae, & admittendi in Universitate Parisiensi. Sic etiam Verforis, Advocatus Iesuitarum, vocat eos in defensione illorum, quam in lucem edidit, pag. 30. Retinuerunt hoc nomen Lutetiae Parisiorum, usque ad id tempus quo ex tota Gallia eiecti sunt.
units.tr: Nevertheless, in many places in France the common people named them not Jesuits but IESVASTAE (Jesus-wasters). Indeed, in 1564, in the dispute they carried on with the University of Paris, they were called Jesuits only by the advocates. The most distinguished jurist Charles Molinaeus also gives them this title in his opinion on their admission into the kingdom of France, whose title reads: Whether the Jesuits are to be received in the kingdom of France and admitted to the University of Paris. Verfor, the advocate of the Jesuits, likewise calls them so in his defence of them, which he published, p. 30. They kept this name at Lutetia of the Parisians until the time when they were driven out of all France.

units.la: Ab eodem etiam in tempore, quo Guilielmus Pratensis Claremontanus Episcopus Cardinal Pratensis F. cum novis Sodalibus supra modum faveret, eis Claremontanae scholae Sodales, suppressso Iesuitarum superbo & ambitioso, sicut iam tum multis videbatur, nomine, aliquandiu nominati fuerunt, Thuano auctore Historiarum lib. 35. pag. 735.
units.tr: At the same time that William Pratensis, bishop of Clermont, the Cardinal Pratensis F., showed exceeding favour to the new Companions, they were for a while called, after the proud and ambitious name of the Jesuits (as many already thought), the Companions of the Clermont school. Thuanus is the author, in his Histories, book 35, p. 735.

units.la: Patres quoque appellari gaudent. Qui vero tales haberi volunt, etiam Patrum officium faciant oportet. Id vero est, per Evangelium gignere liberos in Christo Iesu, hoc est, multos ad fidem Christi adducere, & quasi infantes procreare. Hoc qui praestiterunt Doctores & Pastores in primitiva Ecclesia, merito Patres dicuntur. Quod si officium hoc fideliter facerent etiam hodie Iesuitae, Patrum titulum illis nemo invideret. Atqui pro Evangelio Christi nil nisi commenta humana docent atque tuentur, & pro lacte venena filiis suis instillant. Dum igitur plurimos sui
units.tr: They also delight to be called Fathers. But those who wish to be regarded as such must also perform the office of Fathers. That office is to beget children in Christ Jesus through the Gospel, that is, to bring many to the faith of Christ and, as it were, to give birth to infants. Those who accomplished this among the teachers and ministers of the primitive Church are rightly called Fathers. If the Jesuits too faithfully performed this office today, no one would begrudge them the title of Father. But in fact, instead of the Gospel of Christ, they teach and defend nothing but human inventions, and instead of milk they instil poisons into their children. So while they draw very many of their

units.la: Iesuitae etiam Claremontani Sodales. mos suis artibus & technis ad fidem Pontificiam pertrahunt, liberos illi quidem gignunt, sed Antichristo, non Christo: & Patres quidem dici possunt, at non filii rum Dei, sed Antichristi & gehennae, ut Christus de hypocritis talibus vere pronunciavit Matth. 23.
units.tr: Jesuits, the Claremont Companions, by their arts and devices, to the Papist faith, they indeed beget children, but for Antichrist, not for Christ; and they may indeed be called Fathers, but not sons of God, rather of Antichrist and of hell, as Christ truly pronounced concerning such hypocrites in Matthew 23.

units.la: In Concil. Trident. CLERICI Societatis Iesu appellantur, & Religiosorum ORDO Clericorum Societatis Iesu. KΛῆρος autem, unde Clerus, fortem vel haereditatem significat. Hoc igitur nomine Iesuitae & rasi omnes in Papatu appellari gaudent, quasi ipsi soli sint haeredes Dei & regni eius. D. Petrus autem quoscunque sic fideles appellat.
units.tr: At the Council of Trent they are called the CLERGY of the Society of Jesus, and the ORDER of the Religious is called the Clergy of the Society of Jesus. Now klēros [κλῆρος], from which "clergy" comes, means a lot or an inheritance. Under this name the Jesuits, and all the shaven ones in Popery, therefore delight to be called, as if they alone were the heirs of God and of his kingdom. But St Peter calls all the faithful thus.

units.la: Canonici etiam Regulares dici cupiunt, quod Regulae certae vivendi, non quidem Christi, qua omnes obligamur, quaeque una nobis ad bene beateque vivendum, & ad salutem aeternam consequendam sufficere debebat, sed sui Ignatii Loyolae addicti sint.
units.tr: The Canons Regular also wish to be called so, not because of the fixed rule of living of Christ, by which we are all bound, and which alone ought to suffice us for living well and blessedly and for attaining eternal salvation, but because they are bound to the rule of their own Ignatius of Loyola.

units.la: Dicit etiam Horat. Turselin. in vita Xaverii lib. 2. c. 3. Iesuitas vocatos fuisse in Lusitania & India Apostolos & Apostolicos, sive ex pari numero, sive ex quadam vitae similitudine. Quasi vero octo duodecim Socii semper Apostoli vocadi sint propter parem numerum Apostolorum. Deinde ex nulla vitae similitudine sic vocandi fuerunt, cum nulla vitae similitudo inter Apostolos Christi & Iesuitas demonstrari possit, nam diversa a vita Apostolorum discrepat. Apostoli evitatis Magnatum aulis, spretoque munere huius supercilio, apud plebem & ignobile vulgus diverterunt: Iesuitae vero Regum domos & Gynaecea recta petunt. Apostoli Scholas & Synagogas frequentarunt: Iesuitae Praetoria & Curias scrutantur. Apostoli in Aulis Caesarum, si quando eo abrepti fuerunt, maclati & feris obiecti sunt: Iesuitae Reges Principesque ipsos vel mactandos curant, vel subditis apud eos perniciem machinantur.
units.tr: Horatius Tursellinus, in the life of Xavier, book 2, chapter 3, also says that the Jesuits were called Apostles and Apostolics in Lusitania and India, whether from the equal number or from some likeness of life. As if the eight or twelve companions should always be called Apostles because of the equal number of the Apostles! Nor were they called so from any likeness of life, since no likeness of life can be shown between the Apostles of Christ and the Jesuits, for their life is far removed from that of the Apostles. The Apostles avoided the courts of the great, and, scorning the pride of that office, lodged among the common people and the lowly crowd; but the Jesuits make straight for the houses of kings and their women's quarters. The Apostles frequented schools and synagogues; the Jesuits haunt governors' palaces and law courts. The Apostles, if at any time they were carried off into the courts of Caesars, were slaughtered and thrown to the beasts; the Jesuits contrive either to have kings and princes themselves slaughtered, or to plot their ruin among their subjects.

units.la: Apostoli Christi Evangelium cum omni patientia ac lenitate praedicarunt: Iesuitae nil nisi omnis generis idolomaniás & doctrinas hominum populis obtrudunt, & eos vel denunciata, ni pareant, suprema magistratus indignatione territant, vel praedicata Cruciata in magistratum concitant. Apostoli Christi cor Patrum ad filios & filiorum ad patres, quantum in ipsis fuit, converterunt: Iesuitae liberos contra parentes, & hos contra illos concitant. Apostoli Christi dulcissimum iugum, & per hoc conscientiae libertatem ac pacem praedicarunt: Iesuitae Hispanicae Inquisitionis tyrannicum iugum fidelium cervicibus inetrant. Apostoli Christi omni humana commendatione propriae conscientiae testimonio, legationisque suae authoritate contenti fuerunt: Iesuitae supremi Magistratus mandatis ac severissimis edictis, imo militum cohortibus sese muniunt, ut horum praesidio tuti perniciosas suas artes securius exercere queant. Apostoli Christi quocunque venerunt, nemini molesti fuerunt, aut graves: Iesuitae homines innocentes ex avitis suis sedibus variis technis & artibus expellunt, & eadem sibi occupant. Apostoli sentientes se cum Evangelio suo & doctrina Christi contemptui haberi, nullam graviorem poenam expectierunt, qua ut excusso pedum pulvere abierint, ab omni vindictae cupiditate alienissimi: Iesuitas vero si semel receperis, vel ipsi semet per angustum foramen intruserint, per patentissimas deinceps valvas frustra conaberis eicere: expulsi etiam aut leviter laesi omnes vindictae rationes tentabunt.
units.tr: The Apostles of Christ preached the Gospel with all patience and gentleness; the Jesuits force on the peoples nothing but idolatries of every kind and the doctrines of men, and frighten them, if they do not obey, with the supreme displeasure of the magistrate, or stir up the magistrate with proclaimed crusades. The Apostles of Christ, as far as lay in them, turned the hearts of fathers to their children and of children to their fathers; the Jesuits incite children against parents and parents against children. The Apostles of Christ preached the sweet yoke, and through it the freedom and peace of conscience; the Jesuits fasten the tyrannical yoke of the Spanish Inquisition on the necks of the faithful. The Apostles of Christ were content with the testimony of their own conscience and the authority of their commission, with no human commendation; the Jesuits fortify themselves with the mandates and most severe edicts of the highest magistrate, indeed with troops of soldiers, so that under their protection they may pursue their pernicious arts more safely. The Apostles of Christ, wherever they came, were a burden to no one; the Jesuits expel innocent men from their ancestral homes by various devices and arts, and seize the same houses for themselves. The Apostles, perceiving that they were held in contempt along with their Gospel and the doctrine of Christ, expected no heavier punishment than to shake the dust from their feet and depart, being most far from any desire for vengeance; but the Jesuits, if you have once received them, or if they have pushed themselves in through a narrow opening, you will try in vain to throw them out through the wide-open doors. Even if they are expelled, or slightly hurt, they will attempt every means of revenge.

units.la: Putant alii Apostolorum nomen Iesuitis inditum, quod primi in Indiam fidem ac Christianam religionem importarint. At vero Iesuitas non primo religionem Christianam in Indiam importasse, ideoque illorum Apostolos non fuisse, ex Osorii hist. lib. 1. intelligitur, ubi testatur, in India nuper inventa esse antiqua hominum Christianorum millia. Et Stapletonus libr. 1. de authoritate Script. cap. 14. 5. refert, In India Orientali Lusitanos Christianorum reliquias invenisse. Xauerius etiam Iesuita libr. 1. epistola 1. & lib. 2. epistola 10. scribit: Socotorium Insulam, in circuitu millia passuum ferme centum, totam incoli ab ijs Christianis, qui multis ab hinc annis Papistici sacerdotibus orbati, nihil habeant præter nomen: hos Christianos se esse gloriari, & S. Thomæ Apost. sanctè colere, quod se oriundos prædicent ab eis, quos ille in his locis pepererit. Et lib. 2. epist. 3. Non desunt, inquit, qui S. Thomæ Apost. in Sinas penetrasse confirment, magnumq; eorum numerum ad Christi fidem convertisse. Priusquam Lusitani India in suam redegissent ditionem, Græca Ecclesia eò mittebat Episcopos, qui Christianos, S. Thomæ, eiusq; discipulorum operâ propagatos, tuerentur. Cum primum igitur Lusitani Indiâ potiri cœperunt, unum ex Græcis Episcopis, quos dixi, affirmasse fertur, se cognovisse ab aliis Episcopis, quos in India invenerit, S. Thomam Sinarum finesingressum Evangelio divulgato indigenas plurimos Christo peperisse. Hæc ille. Ioannes Lerius quoque in historia navigationis in Brasiliam scribit, esse sibi à se nibil eius Insulæ relatum, eundem Christum, quem ipse annunciet, fuisse antiquis temporibus in eadem Insula prædicatum, & de salute ab ipso consequenda esse à majoribus traditum, idq; se à parentibus suis audivisse. Putat autem traditionem illam inde à Thoma Apostolo quasi à manu in manum traditam fuisse. Apostolorum igitur nomen, & conversionis hanc gloriam vel Thomas, vel alij Iesuitis præripiunt.
units.tr: Some think the name Apostles was given to the Jesuits because they were the first to bring the Christian faith and religion into India. But that the Jesuits did not first bring the Christian religion into India, and so are not its Apostles, is clear from Osorius, History, book 1, where he testifies that ancient communities of Christians have recently been found in newly discovered India. Stapleton also reports, in On the Authority of Scripture, book 1, chapter 14, section 5, that the Portuguese found remnants of Christians in East India. The Jesuit Xavier, in book 1, letter 1, and book 2, letter 10, writes: "The island of Socotra, about a hundred miles in circumference, is wholly inhabited by Christians who, having for many years been deprived of Papist priests, have nothing but the name. They glory in being Christians and devoutly honour St Thomas the Apostle, because they declare themselves descended from those whom he begot to the faith in these places."
