units.tr: 19. Cleanliness, which contributes both to health and to edification, is to be a concern for all, both as regards themselves and as regards all other things.

units.la: 20. Qui grauem tentationem alicuius noverit, Superiorem admoneat, ut ei ipse pro paterna in suos cura, ac providentia, convenienti remedio possit occurrere.
units.tr: 20. Whoever knows of someone's grave temptation is to inform the Superior, so that by paternal care and foresight for his own people he may be able to meet it with a suitable remedy.

units.la: 21. Quæ à Superioribus circa administrationem agenda sunt, nemo curiose ab aliis exquirat, aut coniecturam faciendo de iis sermonem misceat, sed unusquisque sibi ac muneri suo attendens, quicquid de se, atque aliis constituendum erit, tanquam de manu Dei expectet.
units.tr: 21. No one is to ask others curiously about what the Superiors have to do in administration, nor to mix talk about it with guesswork; but each, attending to himself and to his office, is to await whatever is to be decided about himself and about others as from the hand of God.

units.la: 22. Omnes caput aperiant suis Superioribus, & Sacerdotibus iis, qui Sacerdotes non sunt: discipuli etiam suis præceptoribus. Vnusquisque autem Superiores alloquatur magna cum reverentia: is vero, quem Superior alloquitur, aut reprehendit, humiliter & sine interpellatione audiat.
units.tr: 22. All are to uncover their heads before their Superiors, and before priests those who are not priests; pupils also before their teachers. Each one is to address Superiors with great reverence; and he whom the Superior addresses or reproves is to listen humbly and without interruption.

units.la: 23. Si cui à Superiore denegatum aliquid fuerit, alium Superiorem ne adeat super ea re, quin ei aperiat, quid sibi ab alio fuerit responsum, & quas ob causas negatum.
units.tr: 23. If something has been refused to someone by a Superior, he is not to approach another Superior about the same matter without first disclosing to him what answer he received from the other, and for what reasons it was refused.

units.la: 24. Cui fuerit alicuius rei cura commissa, si impedimentum aliquod intervenerit, mature admoneat aliquem ex Superioribus, ut provideat.
units.tr: 24. Whoever has been entrusted with the care of some matter, if any hindrance arises, is to warn one of the Superiors in good time, so that he may provide.

units.la: 25. Nemo cum ex uno loco in alium proficiscitur, quicquam secum asportet sine facultate Superioris.
units.tr: 25. No one, when setting out from one place to another, is to carry anything with him without the Superior's permission.

units.la: 26. Extra tempora recreationi assignata, hac ratione silentium servandum est, ut nemo loquatur, nisi obiter & perpaucis, aut de rebus necessariis, præsertim in Ecclesia, Sacristia, & Refectorio: in missa vero, concione, mensa, lectionibus, & disputationibus si quid priuatim dicere necesse erit, brevissimè, & submissa voce suggeratur.
units.tr: 26. Outside the times assigned to recreation, silence is to be kept in such a way that no one speaks except briefly and in few words, and only about necessary matters, especially in church, the sacristy and the refectory; at Mass, at the sermon, at table, at lectures and disputations, if something must be said privately, it is to be put forward very briefly and in a low voice.

units.la: 27. Nemo præter eos, qui à Superiore deputati fuerint, loquatur cum iis, qui in prima probatione versantur: excipiuntur tamen usitatæ salutationes, quas cum alij alijs obviij fiunt, charitas religiosa exigit.
units.tr: 27. No one, except those appointed by the Superior, is to speak with those who are in their first probation; yet the customary greetings, which are exchanged when one meets another, religious charity requires.

units.la: 28. Omnes demissa voce, ut religiosos decet, loquantur: nullusque cum alio contendat: sed si qua in re nobis est diversa sententia, eaque videtur manifestanda, rationes modestæ, & cum charitate afferantur, eo animo, ut suus veritati fit locus, non ut in ea re superiores videantur.
units.tr: 28. All are to speak in a low voice, as becomes religious; and no one is to contend with another; but if on some matter we have a different opinion, and it seems right to state it, reasons are to be offered modestly and with charity, with the intention that truth may have its place, and not that one may appear superior in the matter.

units.la: 29. Qui facultate accepta ægrotos invisent, non solum demissa voce loquantur, sed tanta etiam moderatione, ut illis molesti non sint, atq; de iis agant, quæ & exhilarare, & consolari ægrotos, circumstantesq; ædificare in Domino possint.
units.tr: 29. Those who, with permission, visit the sick are not only to speak in a low voice, but with such moderation that they are not a burden to them, and to speak of things that can cheer and console the sick and edify those present in the Lord.

units.la: 30. Caveant sibi omnes ab illo affectu, quo aliæ de aliis nationibus siniistre sentire aut loqui solent, quin potius & bene sentiant, & peculiari affectu diversas à sua nationes prosequantur in Domino, ac proinde nemo bella, contentionesve inter Christianos Principes in colloquium inducat.
units.tr: 30. All are to guard against that attitude by which people are wont to think or speak ill of other nations; rather they are to think well, and with a special affection to embrace nations different from their own in the Lord; and accordingly no one is to bring wars or quarrels among Christian princes into conversation.

units.la: 31. Nemo præter eos, quibus per Superiorem licet, quicquam aliis iubeat, aliosve reprehendat.
units.tr: 31. No one, except those to whom it is permitted by the Superior, is to order anything of others or reprove others.

units.la: 32. In alterius officium nemo se ingerat: in locum vero alieno ministerio deputatu nullus ingrediatur sine facultate Superioris, aut Præfecti illius loci, in rebus necessariis.
units.tr: 32. No one is to thrust himself into another's office; and no one is to enter a place assigned to another's ministry without the permission of the Superior or the prefect of that place, except in necessary matters.

units.la: 33. Nemo in alienum cubiculum ingrediatur sine generali aut speciali Superioris facultate: quod si aliquis intus sit, non prius aperiat ostium, quam post pulsum audiat, Ingredere: & tamdiu aperta sit ianua, quamdiu intus unâ fuerint.
units.tr: 33. No one is to enter another's room without the general or special permission of the Superior; and if someone is inside, he is not to open the door before he hears, after knocking, "Come in"; and the door is to stay open as long as they are together inside.

units.la: 34. Vt ea, quæ religiosos decet, gravitas, & modestia retineatur, nemo alium etiam loco tangat, præterquam in signum charitatis amplexando cum quis aut abit, aut redit peregre.
units.tr: 34. So that the gravity and modesty befitting religious may be kept, no one is to touch another even in place, except when embracing someone as a sign of charity when he departs or returns from abroad.

units.la: 35. Nemo dum mensæ accumbit, cuiquam ex nostris præterquam ei Superiori, qui præest toti Domui aut Collegio, caput aperiat. Et cum aliquid in mensa cuiquam deest, is, qui illi assidet, admoneat eum, qui ministrat.
units.tr: 35. No one, while seated at table, is to uncover his head before any of ours, except the Superior who presides over the whole house or college. And when something is lacking at table for anyone, the one sitting beside him is to tell the one who serves.

units.la: 36. Domi nemo loquatur cum externis, aut alios ad id vocet sine facultate Generali, aut particularis Superioris.
units.tr: 36. At home no one is to speak with outsiders, or call others to do so, without the permission of the General or of the particular Superior.

units.la: 37. Nemo cuiusquam externi ad domesticum, aut domestici ad externum mandata deferat, aut literas, inscio Superiore: seculares autem rumores, qui foris audiuntur, ne teneré, & sine fructu narrentur.
units.tr: 37. No one is to carry messages from an outsider to a member of the household, or from a member of the household to an outsider, or letters, without the Superior's knowledge; and worldly rumours heard outside are not to be told lightly and without profit.

units.la: 38. Nemo quae domi acta, vel agenda sunt, externis referat: nisi Superiori id probari intelligat. Constitutiones vero, aliosve huiusmodi libros, aut scripta quibus Societatis instituturn, vel privilegia continentur, non nisi ex Superioris expresso consensu, ijs communicet.
units.tr: 38. No one is to report to outsiders what has been or is to be done at home, unless he understands that the Superior would approve. He is to share the Constitutions, or other books of this kind, or writings containing the institute or privileges of the Society, with them only with the Superior's express consent.

units.la: 39. Nemo scriptas dabit, aut mittet cuiquam externo, vel domestico instructiones spirituales: aut meditationes, nec exercitia spiritualia Societatis alicui communicabit, nisi a Superiore id approbetur.
units.tr: 39. No one is to give or send in writing to any outsider or member of the household spiritual instructions, or meditations, nor is he to share the Society's spiritual exercises with anyone unless this is approved by the Superior.

units.la: 40. Nemo ab externis consilium petat sine facultate Superioris.
units.tr: 40. No one shall seek counsel from outsiders without the permission of the Superior.

units.la: 41. Nemo cuiusquam negotij, etiam pij, sine facultate Superioris curam suscipiat, nec ad id operam suam promittat, aut se propensum ostendat: secularia vero negotia, ut quae sunt a nostro instituto aliena, & vehementer a spiritualibus avocant, multo magis averti convenit.
units.tr: 41. No one shall take up the care of any business, even a pious one, without the permission of the Superior, nor promise his labour for it or show himself inclined to it. Secular affairs, however, since they are foreign to our Institute and greatly distract from spiritual things, ought to be avoided all the more.

units.la: 42. Omnes, pro ratione sui gradus, data commoda occasione, enitantur piis colloquijs proximum ad meliora promovere: & consilio, ac exhortatione ad bona opera, praesertim ad confessionem excitare.
units.tr: 42. All, according to the measure of their rank, when a convenient opportunity is given, shall strive to advance their neighbour to better things by godly conversation, and to stir him up, by counsel and exhortation, to good works, especially to confession.

units.la: 43. Nullus domo egrediatur, nisi quando, & cum quo Socio Superiori visum fuerit.
units.tr: 43. No one shall go out of the house, except when and with whichever Companion the Superior has judged fit.

units.la: 44. Cum quis facultatem a Superiore petit aliquo eundi, simul etiam aperiat, quo, & cuius rei causa ire velit, praesertim si Praelatus, aut alius vir primarius conveniendus sit: eamque die referat eidem, quid egerit, sicuti ipsum velle intelliget, & respostulaverit.
units.tr: 44. When someone asks the Superior for permission to go somewhere, he shall at the same time state where he wishes to go and for what purpose, especially if a prelate or another man of rank is to be visited. And on the same day he shall report to the Superior what he has done, so that the Superior may understand what he wished and what he has asked.

units.la: 45. Ingressuri, egressurive domo, tintinnabulum nec vehementius, nec crebrius pulsent, quam par est. Nemo autem nisi consueta domus janua egrediatur, vel ingrediatur.
units.tr: 45. Those entering or leaving the house shall ring the bell neither more vigorously nor more often than is proper. No one shall go out or come in except by the usual door of the house.

units.la: 46. Qui domo egrediuntur, signabunt sua nomina, quae prope ostium domus in tabula descripta sunt, & admonebunt janitorem, quo sint profecturi.
units.tr: 46. Those who go out of the house shall sign their names, which are written on a board near the door of the house, and shall tell the doorkeeper where they are going.

units.la: 47. Omnes ante noctem, qui foris sunt, se domum recipiant: nec egredientur ante lucem sine facultate Praepositi, vel Rectoris.
units.tr: 47. All who are outside shall return home before nightfall; and no one shall go out before daybreak without the permission of the Prefect or the Rector.

units.la: 48. Cum quis iter faciens transit per locum, ubi Domus aut Collegium Societatis sit, ad aliud hospitium ne divertat, eius q. qui illic praeest, obedientiae subsit in omnibus, sicut & reliqui, qui in eadem Domo, vel Collegio commorantur. Quod si quis etiam ad negotia tractanda venerit, ea non nisi ex eiusdem consilio, ac directione tractabit.
units.tr: 48. When someone travelling passes through a place where a house or college of the Society is located, he shall not lodge at another inn; and he shall be subject in all things to obedience to the one who presides there, just like the others who dwell in the same house or college. If he has also come to transact business, he shall handle it only with that man's counsel and direction.

units.la: 49. Singuli has regulas, & officiorum suorum habeant atque intelligant, sibique familiares, ac earum memoriam mensibus singulis eis legendis, vel audiendis renovent: quamen peculiaria ministeria Coadjutorum obeunt, eas, quae ad ipsorum officia pertinent, singulis hebdomadis repetant.
units.tr: 49. Each one shall have and understand these rules and the duties of his own office, and shall keep them familiar to himself, renewing their memory by reading or hearing them once a month; but those who perform the particular ministries of the Coadjutors shall repeat those rules which pertain to their own offices every week.

units.la: REGVLAE PROVINCIALIS, DE IIS, QVAE AD EIVS PERSONAM, ET COM- MVNEM TOTIVS PROVINCIAE ADMINI- STRATIONEM SPECTANT.
units.tr: REGULAE PROVINCIALIS: CONCERNING THOSE MATTERS WHICH PERTAIN TO HIS OWN PERSON AND TO THE GENERAL ADMINISTRATION OF THE WHOLE PROVINCE.

units.la: CAPVT PRIMVM.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Qvia Praepositis domorum, & Rectoribus, quod ad eorum personas attinet, in regulis praescribuntur, eo diligentius servare enitatur Provincialis, quo pluribus pro ratione officij sui, vitae spiritualis studio praeire debet.
units.tr: Since the rules prescribe for the superiors of houses and for rectors what concerns their persons, the Provincial should strive to observe them all the more diligently, because by the nature of his office he ought to go before many others in the pursuit of the spiritual life.

units.la: 2. Finem officij sui (quem ante oculos habebit) in eo positum esse intelligat, ut provinciam sibi commissam in acquirenda perfectione, iuxta proprij instituti rationem, & regulas ipsi datas promoveat.
units.tr: 2. He should understand that the end of his office, which he must keep before his eyes, lies in this: that he advance the province committed to him in the acquiring of perfection, according to the character of its own Institute and the rules given to it.

units.la: 3. Imitetur in gubernatione charitatem, mansuetudinem, & benignitatem Christi Domini nostri, ut juxta eam normam, quam tradiderunt Apostoli, non dominans, sed forma facti gregis ex animo, exemplo magis, quam verbo subditos ad perfectionem dirigat.
units.tr: 3. In governing, he should imitate the charity, meekness and kindness of Christ our Lord, so that, according to that norm which the Apostles handed down, not lording it over others but being made a pattern to the flock from the heart, he may lead his subjects to perfection more by example than by word.

units.la: 4. Severitatem suo tempore cum benignitate misceat, suamque auctoritatem per solidas virtutes tueatur, ac dilectionem & curam suorum prae se ferendo modeste, & circumspecte praecipiendo, ita amabilem se reddat, ut omnes fidenter ad illum recurrere possint.
units.tr: 4. He should temper severity with kindness as the occasion requires, and maintain his authority through solid virtues. By showing his affection and care for his men, and by commanding modestly and circumspectly, he should make himself so lovable that all may confidently come to him.

units.la: 5. Solicitè animum ad gubernationem applicet, neque tamen in ea ita distrahatur, ut in studio orationis, & sanctis desiderijs, quibus totam sustentare debet Provinciam, intepescat: quamvis autem ordinarie concionari non debet, si quando tamen per occupationes officij sui commodè licebit, & hoc, & alia Societatis ministeria exercere poterit.
units.tr: 5. He should apply his mind diligently to governing, yet not be so distracted by it that his zeal for prayer and for the holy desires with which he ought to sustain the whole Province grows lukewarm. Although he ought not to preach regularly, if at any time his duties of office conveniently allow it, he may both do this and carry on the other ministries of the Society.

units.la: 6. Nullas regulas, aut ordinationes, aut consuetudines toti Provinciae communes abroget, vel novas inducat inconsulto Generali: sed secundum eas quas habet, gubernet Provinciam.
units.tr: 6. He shall not repeal any rules, ordinances or customs common to the whole Province, nor introduce new ones without consulting the General; but he shall govern the Province according to those which it has.

units.la: 7. Sicut Provincialis, quando necesse est in regulis, ordinationibus, decretis, & in ipsis etiam Constitutionibus cum particularibus dispensare potest: sic cum dispensaverit in rebus majoris momenti, quae videantur urgere, & in quibus sine gravi incommodo Generalis responsum expectari nequeat, debet eum primo quoque tempore de huiusmodi dispensatione, & eius causa admonere.
units.tr: 7. Just as the Provincial may, when necessary, dispense with particular persons in the rules, ordinances, decrees, and even in the Constitutions themselves, so, when he has dispensed in matters of greater importance, which seem urgent, and in which the General's response cannot be awaited without serious inconvenience, he must inform the General of such a dispensation and its reason at the first opportunity.

units.la: 8. Praeter facultates, quae in his regulis conceduntur, habet etiam eas omnes, quae in compendio facultatum Societatis Provincialibus concessae sunt, quas ex compendio ipso intelliget.
units.tr: 8. Besides the faculties granted in these rules, he also has all those which are granted to Provincials in the summary of the Society's faculties, which he will learn from that summary itself.

units.la: 9. Omnes facultates eorum Superiorum, qui Provinciali subordinati sunt, ad ipsum quoque pertinent, ab ipsoque etiam suspendi poterunt, quando ei expedire in Domino videbitur.
units.tr: 9. All the powers of those superiors who are subordinate to the Provincial also belong to him, and he may suspend them whenever it seems good to him in the Lord.

units.la: 10. Potest Provincialis in absentia, vel in periculo vitae constitutus, nominare Viceprovincialem, si Generalis neminem designasset: quo cunq; autem modo constituatur, eadem omnino facultates habeat quas Provincialis, nisi a Generali, vel Provinciali limitentur: rationem tamen administrationis non immutabit.
units.tr: 10. If the Provincial is absent, or placed in danger of his life, he may appoint a Vice-Provincial, unless the General has already designated someone. However he is appointed, the Vice-Provincial shall have exactly the same faculties as the Provincial, unless they are limited by the General or by the Provincial; yet he shall not change the manner of administration.

units.la: DE IIS QVÆ ILLVM AD BONAM PROVINCIÆ ADMINISTRATIONEM IVVABVNT.
units.tr: ON THOSE THINGS THAT HELP THE PROVINCIAL IN THE GOOD ADMINISTRATION OF THE PROVINCE.

units.la: 11. Consultores quatuor habebit à Generali designatos in iis locis, ubi frequentius residet, quoad fieri poterit, cum quibus res graviores communicabit: quod si absentes sint, per transmissas literas: quorum unus ab eodem Generali constitutus, erit eius Admonitor, & socius. In quavis autem Domo, vel Collegio opera Superioris, & eius Consultorum, quos ad consultationem adhibendos iudicaverit, utatur in rebus ijs, de quibus ordinarie consultandum erit.
units.tr: 11. He shall have four consultors, designated by the General, in the places where he resides most often, as far as this can be done, with whom he will share more serious matters; if they are absent, he will do so by letters sent to them. One of these, appointed by the same General, shall be his admonitor and companion. In any house or college, he shall use the work of the Superior and of those of his consultors whom he judges should be called to the consultation, in those matters on which consultation is ordinarily to be held.

units.la: 12. Si expediret praeter Consultores, alios etiam nonnunquam ad Consultationem vocare poterit, & eos quidem, quos de rebus propositis melius judicare posse existimaverit: vel si absentes sint, jubere, ut de rebus ijsdem sententiam suam ad se transmittant.
units.tr: 12. If it is expedient, besides the consultors he may also sometimes summon others to the consultation, namely those whom he thinks better able to judge the matters proposed; or, if they are absent, he may order them to send their opinion on the same matters to him.

units.la: 13. Literas, & scripta, quae pertinent ad rem, de qua consultatio habenda est, saepe dat Consultoribus (nisi quid obstet) ut bene informati sententiam suam melius dicere possint.
units.tr: 13. He often gives the consultors letters and writings that pertain to the matter on which the consultation is to be held (unless something stands in the way), so that, being well informed, they may better state their opinion.

units.la: 14. Cum ordinationes aliquas communes à Generali acceperit, illas Superioribus suae Provinciae sua Provincia & Consultoribus manifestari faciat. Et qua alicuius momenti fuerint, ad gubernationem vel instructionem pertinentes, in libro ad id designato describendas curet.
units.tr: 14. When he has received some general ordinances from the General, he shall make them known to the Superiors of his province, and to his consultors. And those of any importance, pertaining to government or instruction, he shall see to it that they are copied into a book designated for this purpose.

units.la: 15. In proponenda re, de qua deliberandum est, in neutram partem animi sui propen-sionem ostendat, ne consultoribus declinandi in eam partem detur occasio, sed quisque liberius in Domino suam sententiam aperiat.
units.tr: 15. In proposing a matter to be deliberated, he shall show no leaning of his mind to either side, so that the consultors are not given occasion to bend toward that side, but each may more freely open his opinion in the Lord.

units.la: 16. Si quando aliquid occurrerit, de quo non liceat cum Consultoribus agere, potesit iuxta primum, & secundum modum in exercitijs ad electionem faciendam traditum, quid agendum sit, deliberare_.
units.tr: 16. If anything should arise about which it is not permitted to deal with the consultors, he may deliberate on what is to be done, according to the first and second manner taught in the exercises for making an election.

units.la: 17. Libenter se ab alijs admoneri patiatur de ijs, quae ad officium, & personam suam pertinent, & eum praecipue, qui Admonitoris officio fungitur, benigne audiat.
units.tr: 17. He shall willingly allow himself to be admonished by others concerning those things that pertain to his office and person, and he shall kindly hear especially the one who discharges the office of admonitor.

units.la: 18. Habeat secum literas Apostolicas authenticas, & compendium facultatum Societatis, constitutiones, decreta, regulas omnes, & quae a Generali ordinantur, eaque bene intelligat, & observari faciat.
units.tr: 18. He shall keep with him the authentic apostolic letters, a compendium of the faculties of the Society, the constitutions, decrees, and all the rules, and whatever is ordained by the General; he shall understand them well and see that they are observed.

units.la: 19. In loco, in quo diutius ei residendum est, habebit Archivum, in quo asservabit instrumenta authentica, libros, & cetera quae ad officium Provincialis, & communem usum Provinciae pertinent, quae omnia ex catalogo a se subscripto successori tradet.
units.tr: 19. In the place where he must reside for a longer time, he shall have an archive, in which he will keep authentic instruments, books, and the other things that pertain to the office of Provincial and the common use of the province; all of which he will hand over to his successor from a catalogue signed by himself.

units.la: 20. Habeat libellum, in quem referat ea, quae consultanda, vel providenda, vel ad generalem scribenda sunt, ne memoria excidant.
units.tr: 20. He shall have a little book in which he records those things that are to be consulted, or provided for, or written to the General, so that they do not slip from memory.

units.la: 21. Orationes, & Missas ad tempus indicere poterit, etiam in tota Provincia prout sis, quae videbuntur id exigere: modum tamen in ea re non excedat.
units.tr: 21. He may appoint prayers and Masses for a set time, even throughout the whole province, as far as those matters seem to require; yet he shall not exceed due measure in this matter.

units.la: DE SVPERIORIBVS ET SVBORDINATIS ET EORVM OFFICIALIBVS.
units.tr: CONCERNING SUPERIORS AND SUBORDINATES AND THEIR OFFICIALS.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: 1. ETsi Propositos domorum, & Rectores Collegiorum, & Domorum Probationis suae Provinciae constituere non potest: si tamen necesse esset aliquando mutationem facere Superioris alicuius, & periculum esset in mora, vel si is moreretur, poterit aliquem, qui vices Superioris gerat, interim constituere, donec Generalis admonitus pro-videat. Ministros autem, Procuratores & Praefectos studiorum ipse designabit, ac etiam subministros, & Praefectos sanitatis, ubi opus esse judicaverit.
units.tr: 1. Although the Provincial cannot appoint the Superiors of houses, the Rectors of colleges and the houses of probation within his province, yet if at some time it should be necessary to change any Superior, and there were danger in delay, or if one should die, he may appoint someone to discharge the office of Superior in the meantime, until the General, once informed, makes provision. The ministers, procurators and prefects of studies he himself will designate, as well as the sub-ministers and prefects of health, wherever he judges them to be needed.

units.la: 2. Constituat Magistros novitiorum in locis probationem non separatis: a Generali tamen confirmandos, & eos quidem, qui in rebus spiritualibus exercitati sint, & in modo procedendi Societatis nostrae bene probati.
units.tr: 2. He shall appoint the masters of novices in places where the novitiate is not separated, though these are to be confirmed by the General, and those indeed who have been trained in spiritual matters and are well proved in the manner of proceeding of our Society.

units.la: 3. Designabit Praefectos rerum spiritualium in omnibus Collegijs, & domibus prosessis, quales in prima regula officij illorum praescribuntur, itemq; ordinarios nostrorum Cossarios: ex quibus fere conveniret Praefectos rerum spiritualium deligere_.
units.tr: 3. He shall designate the prefects of spiritual matters in all colleges and professed houses, such as are prescribed in the first rule of their office, and likewise our ordinary confessors; from among whom it would generally be fitting to choose the prefects of spiritual matters.

units.la: 4. Deligere poterit Consultores, & Admonitores eorum, qui praesunt in Provincia, ita ut statim suo officio fungi possint: scribet tamen de ijs ad Generalem, ut ab eo confirmentur.
units.tr: 4. He may choose consultors and admonitors for those who govern in the province, so that they can at once perform their office; he shall, however, write about them to the General, so that they may be confirmed by him.

units.la: 5. Praedicatores, & Confessarios ipse constituet: praemisso tamen domestico examine, & approbatione Ordinariorum iuxta formam Concilii Tridentini.
units.tr: 5. He himself shall appoint preachers and confessors, after a domestic examination has been held beforehand, and with the approval of the ordinaries according to the form of the Council of Trent.

units.la: 6. Lectores ordinarios in omnibus classibus, & primarios Officiales, praeter Recto-rem, & Cancellarium in universitatibus deligat: novas tamen lectiones non addat, nec scholas usquam ullas, & praesertim eas, in quibus pueri legendo & scribendo instituantur, quod nec privatim licebit) sine facultate Generalis aperiat.
units.tr: 6. He shall appoint the ordinary teachers in all classes, and the principal officials in universities, apart from the Rector and the Chancellor; he must not, however, add new lectures, nor open any schools anywhere without the General's permission, and especially those in which boys are taught reading and writing (which is not permitted even privately).

units.la: 7. Tueatur auctoritatem Superiorum immediatorum in subditos: ita tamen, ut constet posse omnes ad mediatos recurrere: ideo quicquid agendum, vel immutandum erit, quod ad Immediatorum officium pertineat, per eosdem fieri curabit.
units.tr: 7. He shall maintain the authority of the immediate Superiors over their subjects, yet in such a way that it is clear all may have recourse to the mediate Superiors; therefore he shall see to it that whatever must be done or changed, and which pertains to the office of the immediate Superiors, is carried out through those same persons.

units.la: 8. Si quos ad gubernationem idoneos iudicabit, curet de illis paulatim & negotiis tractandis, & domesticis ministerijs obeundis experimentum sumere, ut & ipsi talenti accepti specimen dare, & Societatis officia eis tuto committi possint.
units.tr: 8. If he judges any men fit for governing, he shall take care to test them gradually in handling affairs and performing domestic ministries, so that they may both give proof of the talent received and the offices of the Society can be safely entrusted to them.

units.la: 30. Observet, si qui detineantur in ministerijs aliquibus, qui magis idonei essent ad alia: eam tamen habeat cujusq; rationem, ut universale bonum semper præferatur.
units.tr: 30. He shall observe whether any are detained in certain ministries who would be more suited to other tasks; yet he shall take account of each case so that the universal good is always preferred.

units.la: 31. Neminem ab obedientia Superiorum immediatorum inconsulto Generali eximat, nisi periculum esset in mora; & tunc certiorem faciat Generalem de persona, & de causis propter quas eam exemerit.
units.tr: 31. He shall not exempt anyone from the obedience of the immediate Superiors without consulting the General, unless there were danger in delay; and then he shall inform the General about the person and the reasons for which he exempted him.

units.la: DE ADMITTENDIS.
units.tr: ON THOSE TO BE ADMITTED.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: 32. Eos ad probationem per se, vel per alios admittere poterit, quos ad institutum nostrum idoneos in Domino judicaverit: cavebit tamen ne cujusquam admissio justam aliquam externorum offensionem aut Societatis nocumentum pariat, quod cum ijs potissimum observandum erit, qui in scholis nostris instituuntur.
units.tr: 32. He may admit to probation, either in person or through others, those whom he has judged in the Lord to be fit for our Institute; yet he shall take care that the admission of anyone does not give rise to a just offence on the part of outsiders or to harm for the Society. This is to be observed especially with those who are being trained in our schools.

units.la: 33. Attendat, ne nimij sint nostri in hominibus ad Societatem alliciendis, sed per virtutes, & bonæ vitæ odorem omnes ad Christum trahere studiosè curent.
units.tr: 33. He shall take heed that our members are not too eager in attracting men to the Society, but shall earnestly see to it that all are drawn to Christ through virtue and the fragrance of a good life.

units.la: 34. Meminerit, quod inepta turba ad institutum nostrum admitti non debet, & observari faciat in hoc diligenter regulas officij Examinatoris.
units.tr: 34. He shall remember that a foolish crowd ought not to be admitted to our Institute, and shall see to it that the rules of the office of Examiner are diligently observed in this matter.

units.la: 35. Quod ad prima quinque impedimenta attinet, etsi Societas in nullo eorum dispensare potest, si tamen in eo, qui admitti petit, dona aliqua Dei illustriora cernerentur, Generalem admoneat: quod si de eiusmodi impedimentis dubitaret, ad eundem recurrat.
units.tr: 35. As for the first five impediments, although the Society can dispense in none of them, if in the person who seeks admission some gifts of God more distinguished were to be seen, he shall inform the General; and if he were in doubt about impediments of this kind, let him have recourse to the same.

units.la: 36. In secundarijs impedimentis dispensandi facultatem habebit, præterquam in deformitate magna aut defectu insigni, qualem habent Eunuchi, & in ætate infra 15. & ultra 50. expletos annos, & in conjugatis etiam in casu, in quo non est impedimentum essentiale.
units.tr: 36. He shall have the faculty of dispensing in secondary impediments, except in great deformity or a notable defect, such as eunuchs have, and in the case of an age under fifteen or over fifty completed years, and in the case of married persons, even where the impediment is not an essential one.

units.la: 37. Poterit in casu aliquo anteponere, & postponere aliqua ex sex experimentis, eaque moderari, & alia in alia permutare, dummodo biennio, & bene probentur Novitij: quod etiam tempus prorogare poterit, si opus esse judicaverit.
units.tr: 37. In some case he may place before or after some of the six trials, and may moderate them, and exchange one for another, provided that the Novices are well tested over two years; this time he may also extend, if he judges it necessary.

units.la: 38. Poterit etiam cum Novitijs in secundo anno probationis circa studia dispensare, habita ratione personarum, locorum, & temporum, prout expedire in Domino judicabit. Si vero cum quibus dispensaverit, extra domum probationis, & seorsum à Collegialibus esse debebunt, sub cura alicujus Sacerdotis ab ipso constituti, qui vicem Magistri novitiorum gerat: ejusque regulas & examinatoris habeat: ex quibus ea servabuntur, quæ commodè servari possunt. Cujusmodi erit, ut per dimidiam horam vesperi orent: sed ijs tantum diebus, quibus à studijs vacaverint.
units.tr: 38. He may also dispense with Novices in the second year of probation as regards their studies, having regard to persons, places and times, as he judges in the Lord to be expedient. But those with whom he has dispensed shall have to be outside the house of probation and apart from the Collegians, under the care of some priest appointed by him, who shall act in the place of the Master of Novices, and they shall have his rules and those of the Examiner; from these shall be observed what can conveniently be observed. Such will be that they pray for half an hour in the evening, but only on those days on which they are free from their studies.

units.la: 39. Coadjutores temporales plures esse non debent, quàm qui necessarij sint ad sublevandas domos, vel Collegia in rebus, quibus occupari Sacerdotes, & Scholastici non possunt, sine detrimento majoris boni.
units.tr: 39. There ought not to be more temporal coadjutors than are necessary to assist the houses or Colleges in those matters with which priests and scholastics cannot be occupied without detriment to a greater good.

units.la: DE DIMITTENDIS.
units.tr: DE DIMITTENDIS.

units.la: CAP. V.
units.tr: CAP. V.

units.la: 40. Facultatem habet dimittendi eos, qui in prima, & secunda probatione ante & post emissa vota versantur: nisi à Præposito generali in illius provinciam destinati, vel de Societate ipsi tam bene meriti essent, ut eorum esset particularis ratio habenda. In his enim casibus inconsulto Generali dimittere non debet: nisi causæ admodum urgentes & graves essent, ita ut minime dubitaretur Generalis mentem hujusmodi futuram esse.
units.tr: 40. He has the power to dismiss those who are in the first and second probation, both before and after the vows have been taken; except where they have been assigned by the Father General to his province, or where they have been so well deserving of the Society that their particular case must be taken into account. In these cases he must not dismiss without consulting the General, unless the reasons are very urgent and grave, so that there would be no doubt that the General would think the same.

units.la: 41. Scholasticos vero approbatos, & Coadjutores non formatos, qui probationem absolverunt, inconsulto Generali non dimittat, nisi in gravibus & urgentibus casibus, & qui ejusmodi sint, ut sine gravi periculo, Generalis responsum expectari nequeat: quem tamen post dimissionem certiorem faciat, adjunctis causis dimissionis. Et in universum diligenter Provinciali dispiciendum est, ut qui minus idonei ad nostrum institutum, & tandem aliquando dimittendi videntur, eos ipse intra biennium probationis dimittat. quod si perastiam tiam probationis tempore aliqui huiusmodi deprehendantur, tempestiue Generalis moneatur, ne cum Societatis jactura diutius, quàm par est, retineantur.
units.tr: 41. He must not dismiss approved Scholastics, or Coadjutors not yet formed who have completed their probation, without consulting the General, except in grave and urgent cases, and cases of such a kind that, without grave danger, the General's reply cannot be awaited. Nevertheless, after the dismissal he shall inform the General, with the reasons for the dismissal attached. In general, the Provincial must look carefully to those who seem less suitable for our Institute and who at some point ought to be dismissed, and he himself shall dismiss them within the two years of probation. But if any such persons are discovered to be obstinate during the time of probation, the General is to be warned in good time, so that they are not kept longer than is proper, to the loss of the Society.

units.la: 42. Provincialis erit, juxta commissam sibi facultatem, auditis suis Consultoribus vel necessitas urgeat, Superiore, & Consultoribus eius loci, ubi tunc erit, qui ipsi videbuntur dignitis judicare de causis sufficientibus ad dimissionem: curabit tamen, ne ad hæc extrema, nisi quàm consultissime, & aliis tentatis remedijs veniatur.
units.tr: 42. The Provincial, according to the faculty committed to him, having heard his Consultors, or the Superior and Consultors of the place where he then is, if necessity presses, shall judge, as seems fit to them, whether the causes are sufficient for dismissal. Nevertheless he shall take care that recourse is not had to these extreme measures, unless after the most careful deliberation and after other remedies have been tried.

units.la: 43. Coadiutores formatos sive spirituales, sive temporales, & Professos nullo modo dimittet.
units.tr: 43. He shall in no way dismiss formed Coadjutors, whether spiritual or temporal, or Professed.

units.la: 44. Circa modum dimittendi observet ea, quæ in secunda parte Constitutionum capite tertio dicuntur: & intelligat, an is qui dimittitur, aliquid Societati dederit, & si quid reddi oporteat, juxta eiusdem capitis declarationem. Scripta verò an secum asportare debeat, consideret ipse diligenter.
units.tr: 44. In regard to the manner of dismissal, he shall observe those things which are said in the third chapter of the second part of the Constitutions; and he shall understand whether the one who is dismissed has given anything to the Society, and if anything ought to be returned, according to the declaration of the same chapter. As to whether he ought to take his writings away with him, let him consider this carefully himself.

units.la: 45. Declaretur ijs, qui dimittuntur, quod liberi maneant à votis simplicibus, si ea juxta formulam Societatis consuetam emiserint.
units.tr: 45. It shall be declared to those who are dismissed that they remain free from the simple vows, if they have taken them according to the formula customary in the Society.

units.la: 46. Circa dimissos aut egressos è Societate, & postea reductos, vel sponte redeuntes, observentur ea quæ in Constitutionibus & Decretis dicuntur: & si admittantur, denuò examinentur & probentur, prout ipsi videbitur, si quis autem semel egressus erit, poterit quidem iterum admitti; sed advertatur, huiusmodi homines raro idoneos ad instituti nostri disciplinam inveniri.
units.tr: 46. In regard to those who have been dismissed or have left the Society, and afterwards are taken back, or return of their own accord, the things which are laid down in the Constitutions and Decrees shall be observed; and if they are admitted, they shall be examined and tested again, as seems fit to him. If anyone has once left, he may indeed be admitted again; but let it be noted that people of this kind are rarely found suitable to the discipline of our Institute.

units.la: DE LITERARVM STVDIIS.
units.tr: ON LITERARY STUDIES.

units.la: CAPVT VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: 47. IN Universitatibus, & Collegijs, in quibus nostri literas profitentur, idoneos, & eruditos Professores pro ratione loci, & debiti constituat. Et si aliquis Lector extraordinarius adjiciendus videretur, Generalem consulat.
units.tr: 47. In the universities and colleges where our men teach the humanities, he shall appoint suitable and learned professors, according to the circumstances of the place and as is due. And if it seems that an extraordinary lecturer should be added, let him consult the General.

units.la: 48. Peculiari cura videat, num Lectiones in scholis nostris, & scholasticæ exercitationes diligenter, assidue, atque ordine habeantur: num Magistri, & Discipuli suum in Domino officium faciant: & si quid opus esse iudicaverit, provideat juxta ea, quæ in quarta parte Constitutionum, & regulis habentur.
units.tr: 48. Let him take particular care to see whether lectures in our schools and scholastic exercises are held diligently, regularly and in good order, and whether the masters and pupils perform their duty in the Lord. If he judges that anything needs to be done, let him provide for it according to what is set out in the fourth part of the Constitutions and the rules.

units.la: 49. Ipsius prudentiæ relinquitur, quid hi, aut illi addiscere debeant juxta ætatem & ingenium uniuscuiusque ad maiorem gloriam Dei: eos autem quos non esse aptos ad studia invenient, ab illis removere poterit.
units.tr: 49. It is left to his own prudence to decide what each of these or those ought to learn, according to age and talent, for the greater glory of God. Those whom he finds unfit for studies he may remove from them.

units.la: 50. In addiscendis disciplinis ordinem servari faciat: efficietque, ut prius Scholastici in lingua Latina solidum iaciant fundamentum, quàm ad alia maiora studia transeant: curabit verò humaniorum literarum studia magni fieri, & eorum, qui eas profitentur, peculiarem curam habeari: & ne in his Professores idonei desint, illorum seminaria & instituet, & conservabit.
units.tr: 50. He shall see that order is kept in learning the subjects, and he shall bring it about that the students first lay a solid foundation in the Latin language before they pass on to other, higher studies. He shall take care that the study of the humane letters is held in high esteem, and that those who profess them receive particular care; and, so that suitable professors are not lacking in these, he shall both establish and maintain seminaries for them.

units.la: 51. Aliarum linguarum studium valde commendatum habeat: Hebraicæ verò ijs tantum concedat, qui in Theologiæ facultate mediocriter eruditi iam sint; aut certè tam humiles, ut spernendum merito sit, hoc studium sine illorum detrimento utile valdè futurum.
units.tr: 51. Let him hold the study of other languages in high commendation. Hebrew, however, he shall grant only to those who are already moderately learned in the faculty of theology, or else so humble that it is rightly thought this study, without loss to them, would be of very great use.

units.la: 52. Designet aliquos, qui & probata virtutis in primis sint, & ingenio polleant, ut absolutis studijs Philosophiæ, & Theologiæ ad ea repetenda privatim, & quietum studium habeant, & positivæ, ac S. Scripturæ se dedant: quo etiam tempore in disputationibus publicis rationem suorum studiorum reddant, ut eas facultates privatim, vel publicè ad suam, vel aliorum utilitatem profiteri possint.
units.tr: 52. Let him designate some men who are outstanding above all in proven virtue and who excel in talent, so that, once their studies of philosophy and theology are completed, they may take these up again in private and have a quiet time for study, and devote themselves to positive theology and Holy Scripture. At that time too they shall give an account of their studies in public disputations, so that they may be able to profess those faculties, either privately or publicly, for their own benefit or that of others.

units.la: 53. Diligenter studeat, ut Præceptores Philosophiæ, cum magno delectu eos Aristotelis interpretes legant, qui contra Christiana dogmata impiè scripserunt, & ita Philosophiam interpretentur, ut Theologiæ scholasticæ, quam nobis commendant Constitutiones, subservire faciant.
units.tr: 53. Let him take care diligently that the teachers of philosophy, with great discrimination, read those interpreters of Aristotle who have impiously written against Christian doctrines, and that they so interpret philosophy that it serves the scholastic theology which the Constitutions commend to us.

units.la: 54. Cum opinionum novitas vel diversitas non modò finem ipsum, quem Societas ad Dei gloriam propositum habet, impedire possit, sed etiam ipsum Societatis statum maximè labefactare: necesse est ingeniorum licentiam in opinionibus vel introducendis vel sectandis, omnibus modis certa aliqua lege coërcere. Quare diligentissimè curent Provinciales iuxta mentem Constitutionum ea exactè ab omnibus nostris, & præcipuè à Professoribus observari, quæ in ratione studiorum præcipiuntur.
units.tr: 54. Since novelty or diversity of opinions can not only hinder the very end which the Society has set before itself for the glory of God, but also greatly weaken the very state of the Society, it is necessary to restrain by some fixed rule, in every way, the licence of minds either in introducing or in pursuing opinions. Therefore let the Provincials most diligently see to it that, according to the mind of the Constitutions, those things which are prescribed in the plan of studies are observed exactly by all our men, and especially by the professors.

units.la: 55. Curet, ut ij, qui propensum animum habent ad aliquam facultatem, in qua possunt insignes evadere, in ea diutius versentur, habita tamen spiritualis profectus ratione, & de talibus Generalem admoneat.
units.tr: 55. Let him see to it that those who have an inclination towards some faculty in which they can become distinguished remain in it for longer, with regard, however, to spiritual progress; and let him advise the General about such men.

units.la: 56. Qui propter ætatem profectiorem, aut alias causas in facultatibus Superioribus & Scholasticis studijs progressum facere non possunt, curabit, ne in illis tempus insumant, sed casibus conscientiæ discendis dent operam, sintque semper aliqui ex nostris, qui huic studio diligenter incumbant, ut Societas copiam habere possit operariorum, qui confessionibus audiendis sint idonei.
units.tr: 56. Those who, on account of their advanced age or other causes, cannot make progress in the higher faculties and scholastic studies, he shall see that they do not waste time on these, but devote themselves to learning cases of conscience; and there shall always be some of ours who apply themselves diligently to this study, so that the Society may have a supply of workers who are fit to hear confessions.

units.la: 57. In singulis domibus, & Collegijs aliquem constituat, qui in casibus conscientiæ benè versatus sit, ut difficultatibus domi & foris occurrentibus satis facere possit.
units.tr: 57. In each house and college he shall appoint someone who is well versed in cases of conscience, so that he may be able to deal adequately with difficulties arising at home and abroad.

units.la: 58. Comœdias, & Tragœdias rarissimè agi permittat, & non nisi Latinas, ac decentes, & prius aut ipse eas examinet, aut alijs examinandas committat: eas verò, atque alias id genus actiones in Ecclesia fieri omnino prohibeat.
units.tr: 58. He shall very rarely permit comedies and tragedies to be performed, and only Latin ones that are decent; and he shall either examine them himself beforehand or entrust them to others for examination. He shall utterly forbid such plays, and other actions of that kind, to be performed in church.

units.la: 59. Sub finem studiorum Generalem de uniuscuiusq; talento admoneat, & quantum singuli profecerint, ei referat.
units.tr: 59. At the end of the studies he shall advise the General about each man's talent and report to him how far each has progressed.

units.la: 60. Curet, ut nullus ex nostris librum aliquem ex una in alteram linguam transferat aut imprimat: absque Præpositi generalis facultate.
units.tr: 60. He shall see that none of ours translates any book from one language into another, or publishes one, without the faculty of the General Superior.

units.la: DE PROMOVENDIS AD ORDINES, ET GRADVS LITERARIOS.
units.tr: ON THE PROMOTION TO ORDERS, AND ACADEMIC DEGREES.

units.la: CAP. VII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII.

units.la: 61. Potest per se, vel per alios præsentare ex nostris eos, quos idoneos iuxta instructionem à Generali traditam censuerit, ad ordines Ecclesiasticos recipiendos.
units.tr: 61. He may present, either himself or through others, those from our members whom he judges fit, according to the instruction handed down by the General, for reception of ecclesiastical orders.

units.la: 62. Quamvis in actibus Scholasticorum communibus exercendi sunt nostri iuxta Constitutiones: nullus tamen ad Philosophiæ, vel Theologiæ gradus, etiamsi idoneus sit, promoveatur sine Præpositi Generalis facultate.
units.tr: 62. Although our members are to be exercised in the common scholastic acts according to the Constitutions, nobody shall be promoted to a degree in Philosophy or Theology, even if he is fit, without the permission of the Father General.

units.la: 63. Cum nostri de Generalis facultate in universitatibus Societatis promovendi sunt ad gradus literarios, si qua in re necessaria ad promotionem erit dispensandum (quod rarissime faciendum est, ne huiusmodi gradus veniant in contemptum) ubi id fecerit, tam de persona quam causa dispensandi admoneat Generalem.
units.tr: 63. When our members are to be promoted to academic degrees in the universities of the Society, with the General's permission, if in any matter something necessary for the promotion requires dispensation (which is to be done very rarely, lest such degrees fall into contempt), then, wherever he has done so, he shall inform the General both of the person and of the reason for the dispensation.

units.la: 64. Etsi Doctoratus, & Magisterij gradus iuxta Constitutiones prædicto modo nostri accipere possunt, nomine tamen Doctoris, vel Magistri ratione gradus, inter se non utantur.
units.tr: 64. Although those of ours may receive the degrees of Doctor and Master in the manner described above according to the Constitutions, they shall nevertheless not use the title of Doctor or Master by reason of the degree among themselves.

units.la: DE PROMOVENDIS IN PROFESSOS, ET COADIV- TORES FORMATOS, AC SCHOLARES.
units.tr: On Those to Be Promoted to Professed Members, Formed Coadjutors, and Scholastics.

units.la: CAP. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: 65. Potest admittere post biennium ad vota simplicia Scholasticorum approbatorum, & Coadiutorum non formatorum, quos in Domino idoneos iudicaverit iuxta Regulas & Constitutiones.
units.tr: 65. He may admit to simple vows, after two years, those approved Scholastics and unformed Coadjutors whom he judges fit in the Lord, according to the Rules and Constitutions.

units.la: 66. Curet autem, ut quam primum aliquis biennii Novitiatus expleverit (nisi iusta de causa differendus videretur) per alios ijs, quæ in examine habentur, hæc vota in sacro ante quam communicet, emittat coram aliquibus domesticis tantum, non tamen inter eos, qui tunc forte vota renovarent, etiam si ea prius ex devotione edidissent.
units.tr: 66. He shall take care that, as soon as anyone has completed two years of Novitiate (unless for a good reason he seems to be deferred), the vows are made by others as in the examination, and that he makes these vows in the sacristy before he communicates, in the presence of members of the household only, but not among those who perhaps at that time renew their vows, even if they had earlier made them out of devotion.

units.la: 67. Si quos, ut indifferentes admiserit (quod raro fieri debet) potest eos applicare ad gradum Coadiutorum, vel Scholasticorum, sicut magis in Domino convenire iudicabit. In hac vero classe indifferentium ultra tempus biennij probationis nemo maneat.
units.tr: 67. If he has admitted some as indifferent (which should rarely be done), he may assign them to the grade of Coadjutors or Scholastics, as he judges more fitting in the Lord. But no one shall remain in this class of the indifferent beyond the two-year period of probation.

units.la: 68. Scholastici simulatã Superiorum arbitrio studia absolverint, tertium probationis annum in Domibus Probationum, peragant: quod si commodè fieri non possit in Domibus Professorum, vel in Collegijs probari eos faciat iuxta regulas novitiatus.
units.tr: 68. Scholastics, as soon as they have finished their studies, shall, at the discretion of their Superiors, spend the third year of probation in the Houses of Probation. If this cannot conveniently be done in the Houses of Professed, he shall have them tested in Colleges according to the rules of the novitiate.

units.la: 69. Finita visitatione consideret, qui sint idonei in sua provincia, ut in Coadiutores formatos spirituales, vel temporales, aut in Professos iuxta Constitutiones, & instructionem à Generali traditam admitti possint; & secundum eandem accurate Generalem informari curet.
units.tr: 69. When the visitation is finished, he shall consider which men in his province are fit to be admitted, as formed spiritual or temporal Coadjutors, or as Professed according to the Constitutions and the instruction handed down by the General; and he shall take care that they are carefully instructed by the General according to the same.

units.la: 70. Antequam admittat eos, qui cum Generalis facultate professionem, vel vota Coadiutorum formatorum emissuri sunt, ea servari curet, quæ ab ipsis erunt facienda: eiusmodi sunt, dispositio bonorum temporalium, si quæ adhuc habuerint, exercitia spiritualia, confessio generalis, & alia, quæ in Constitutionibus, & Decretis congregationum dicuntur, in professione etiam & ijs votis emittendis servetur, & ut publice fiant, & in cæteris omnibus quæ constitutiones præscribunt.
units.tr: 70. Before he admits those who are about to make profession, or the vows of formed Coadjutors, with the General's permission, he shall see to it that those things are observed which they must do themselves: namely, the disposition of temporal goods if they still have any, spiritual exercises, a general confession, and the other things which are set out in the Constitutions and the Decrees of the congregations. In the profession and in the making of these vows the same shall be observed, and they shall be made publicly, and in all other matters which the Constitutions prescribe.

units.la: 71. Qui professionem fecerint, etiam trium votorum, emittant vota illa simplicia, quæ ante professionem emittenda sunt, idque iuxta formulam primæ congregationis, ut à tertia ecognita est: & doctrinam Christianam tam ipsi, quam Coadiutores formati spirituales er quadraginta dies intra annum docent.
units.tr: 71. Those who have made profession, even of the three vows, shall make those simple vows which are to be made before profession, and this according to the formula of the first congregation, as it was acknowledged by the third. And they, as well as the formed spiritual Coadjutors, shall teach Christian doctrine for forty days within the year.

units.la: 72. Habeat librum, in quo eorum nomina scribantur, qui vota solemnia, vel simplicia ante biennium in Domibus, vel Collegijs suæ provinciæ emittunt, iuxta ordinem Præpositorum Domorum, & Rectoribus traditum.
units.tr: 72. He shall keep a book in which the names of those are written who make solemn or simple vows in the Houses or Colleges of his province within the two years, according to the order handed down to the Prefects of the Houses and the Rectors.

units.la: 73. Cum aliqui professionem, vel vota Coadiutorum formatorum fecerint, exempla huiusmodi votorum, & aliorum quinque, quæ professi post emissam professionem faciunt, nomine ipsorum subscripta, ad Generalem quàm primum transmittat.
units.tr: 73. When some have made profession, or the vows of formed Coadjutors, he shall send, as soon as possible, to the General copies of such vows, and of the others which the professed make after their profession, signed in their names.

units.la: 74. Constituat iuxta Constitutiones, ut professi, & Coadiutores spirituales formati suæ provinciæ in Domibus Professis, quantum fieri potest, commorentur.
units.tr: 74. He shall arrange, according to the Constitutions, that the professed and formed spiritual Coadjutors of his province live, as far as possible, in the Professed Houses.

units.la: DE REBVS COLLEGIORVM, ET DOMORVM.
units.tr: On the Property of the Colleges and Houses.

units.la: CAP. IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: 75. Ædificia conservari, & si opus erit, instaurari curet: quod si quæ ædificanda maioris momenti fuerint, ut esset templum, dormitorium, vel aliquid huiusmodi, nisi approbante Generali non fiant, ad quem pertinet formam, & modum nostrorum ædificiorum præscribere.
units.tr: 75. Let him see that the buildings are kept in repair and, if need be, restored. But if any buildings of greater importance are to be erected, such as a church, a dormitory, or something of that kind, they are not to be built without the approval of the General, to whom it belongs to prescribe the form and manner of our buildings.

units.la: 76. Redditus, & reliqua stabilia conservari curet, & an crescat, vel minuantur, intelligat: si quis aut huiusmodi bona augere vellet, vel aliquid donare, poterit id admittere: si tamen conditiones aliquæ exigerentur, non nisi approbante Generali, nullam admittat, & eodem modo, quæ datur Domui professæ accipere, & si quid stabile donatum fuerit, etiam vendere poterit: si tamen domui necessarium pretium non esset, & trecentorum ducatorum valorem excederet, consulat Generalem, ut de eo iuxta ipsius præscriptum disponat.
units.tr: 76. Let him see that the revenues and other fixed property are preserved, and understand whether they are increasing or decreasing. If anyone wishes to increase such goods or to give something, he may admit it. If, however, any conditions are attached, he is not to accept them without the approval of the General. In the same way, he may receive what is given to the professed house, and if something fixed has been given, he may also sell it. If, however, the house does not need the price, and it exceeds the value of three hundred ducats, let him consult the General, so that he may dispose of it according to the General's direction.

units.la: 77. Cum lites, pro rebus præsertim temporalibus, diligenter nostris fugienda sint, non intendat quisquam è nostris omnino lite aliqua absq; consensu Generalis, aut eius, cui expressè suas vices ad hanc rem ille commiserit, nisi in re adeo necessaria, ut eius responsum expectari nequeat, de quo tamen postea ipsum admoneat. Quocirca nitatur Provincialis primum rem compromissione componere. Nostris autem si lis intendatur, curandum etiam diligenter, nisi de ure nostro manifeste constaret, ut aliqua transactione vel concordia res tota componatur: si commode fieri non valeat, poterunt in iudicio se defendere, cum Provincialis potestatem habeat conservandi & defendendi res Collegiorum etiam in iudicio, cum facultate ad ios substituendi, si id necessarium vel conveniens aliquando fuerit.
units.tr: 77. Since lawsuits, especially over temporal matters, are to be carefully avoided by ours, let none of ours enter into any lawsuit at all without the consent of the General, or of the one to whom he has expressly committed his authority in this matter, unless the matter is so necessary that his reply cannot be awaited; of this, however, he should afterwards inform the General. Accordingly, let the Provincial first strive to settle the matter by arbitration. If a suit is brought against ours, care must also be taken, unless our right is clearly established, that the whole matter be settled by some compromise or agreement. If this cannot conveniently be done, they may defend themselves in court, since the Provincial has the power to preserve and defend the property of the Colleges, even in court, with the faculty of appointing others in his place, should this at any time be necessary or fitting.

units.la: 78. Intelligat, an exempla authentica contractuum maioris momenti, præsertim rerum perpetuarum ad Archivium, quod est in urbe penes Præpositum Generalem, missa sint, aliqui mittenda curabit.
units.tr: 78. Let him see whether authentic copies of contracts of greater importance, especially those concerning perpetual matters, have been sent to the archive in the city, which is in the keeping of the Father General; he will take care that some be sent.

units.la: 79. Videat computa inter Superiorem, & Procuratorem transfacta, rationemque exigat accepti & expensi, & resolutionem ultimi sui computi summatim scribi faciat, quam ipse subscribet in libro designato: in hoc autem scripto simul constet tam de summa accepti, & expensi ab ultima visitatione, quam de eo, quod residuum fuerit, vel etiam si quid debiti maneat.
units.tr: 79. Let him examine the accounts drawn up between the Superior and the Procurator, demand a statement of receipts and expenditure, and have the result of the last reckoning briefly written out, which he himself will sign in the designated book. In this writing let it be stated both the sum of receipts and expenditure since the last visitation and what remains, or whether any debt still remains.

units.la: 80. Visitet bona stabilia extra domum, quae sine magno incommodo visitari possint, ut videat, num qua instauratione, vel cultura egeant, & quid ad eorum conservationem opus sit.
units.tr: 80. Let him visit the fixed property outside the house, which can be visited without great inconvenience, to see whether it needs any repair or cultivation, and what is required for its preservation.

units.la: 81. Si Domus vel Collegia cum commoda fundatione offerentur, expendat, quid ad commune bonum ex iis speretur, & an aliquae conditiones exigantur, & an locus sit salubris, & omnia ad Generalem referat, nihil interim certi promittendo.
units.tr: 81. If houses or colleges are offered with a suitable endowment, let him weigh what benefit for the common good may be hoped for from them, whether any conditions are demanded, and whether the place is healthful, and let him refer everything to the General, promising nothing certain in the meantime.

units.la: 82. Magnum aes alienum Collegia vel Domos conflare non sinat, si solvendo fore probabiliter non speret, habita ratione reddituum, & eleemosynarum, quae ordinarie dari solent; nec in iis plures habitare permittat, quam alii possint.
units.tr: 82. Let him not allow colleges or houses to incur a large debt if he does not reasonably expect they will be able to pay it, taking into account the revenues and the alms ordinarily given; nor let him allow more people to live in them than the others can support.

units.la: 83. Quando contribuendum erit ad sumptus communes Provinciae, statuat ipse quid cuique Collegio, vel Domui, servata proportione debita, imponi debeat.
units.tr: 83. When contributions must be made to the common expenses of the Province, let him decide what each college or house ought to be assigned, keeping due proportion.

units.la: 84. In vestitu ratione tria observari faciat: Primum, ut honestus ille sit: Alterum, ut ad usum communem, & approbatum honestorum Sacerdotum eius loci in quo vivitur accommodatus: Tertium, ut professioni pauperta non repugnet.
units.tr: 84. In clothing, have three things observed: first, that it be decent; second, that it be suited to the common and approved usage of respectable clergy of the place where one lives; third, that it not be at odds with the profession of poverty.

units.la: 85. Habitationem, officinas, vestes & reliquam supellectilem, omnia deni diligenter inspiciat: nec necessaria deesse, aut superflua expendi permittat: & rerum mobilium inventarium conferri faciat cum inventario in praecedenti visitatione, vel Provinciali subscripto. Observet etiam, quae teneatur oeconomia ratio.
units.tr: 85. Let him carefully inspect the dwelling, the workshops, the clothing and all the rest of the household goods; let him not permit what is necessary to be lacking or what is superfluous to be spent. Let the inventory of movable goods be compared with the inventory at the previous visitation or with the one signed by the Provincial. Let him also observe what economical order is required.

units.la: DE IIS, QVI BONIS SVIS NONDVM SE ABDICARVNT
units.tr: ON THOSE WHO HAVE NOT YET RENOUNCED THEIR GOODS

units.la: CAPVT X.
units.tr: CHAPTER X.

units.la: 86. Non permittat nostros abdicare se possessione bonorum suorum, nisi quos constantes, & stabiles in sua vocatione cognoverit; atque in ea re maturo semper consilio procedat.
units.tr: 86. He shall not permit our men to renounce the possession of their goods unless he has found them steadfast and stable in their vocation; and in this matter he shall always proceed with mature deliberation.

units.la: 87. Non sinat pactiones inire nostros cum parentibus suis, & quibuscunque aliis de legitima parte, & aliis bonis ad se pertinentibus, nisi illi prius admoneantur, Societatem ipsam ad ea bona nullum ius habere, & Generalis de tota re prius informetur.
units.tr: 87. He shall not allow our men to enter into agreements with their parents or with any others concerning the legitimate portion or other goods belonging to them, unless those persons have first been reminded that the Society has no right to those goods, and the General is first informed of the whole matter.

units.la: 88. Cum quis ex nostris est dispositurus de bonis suis in auxilium Societatis, admoneatur Generalis de eorum valore, & de animo relinquentis, & necessitate etiam Domorum, & Collegiorum Provinciae, si in ea huiusmodi bona sint.
units.tr: 88. When any of our men is about to dispose of his goods in aid of the Society, the General shall be informed of their value, of the intention of the one leaving them, and also of the need of the houses and colleges of the Province, if such goods are located there.

units.la: 89. Si aliqua bona applicabuntur Societati cum facultate Generalis, magnopere curet Provincialis ut cum aedificatione, & charitate, & non cum rigore exigantur, potiusque per Procuratores externos, quam per nostros: expediet quoq;, ut ex his eleemosynae aliquae in pauperes eius oppidi, ubi sunt bona, distribuantur: & ratio dati, & accepti talium bonorum scripto constet, ut ipse aut superior illius Domus, vel Collegij, cuia applicata fuerunt, eam reddere possit ei, qui a Generali fuerit designatus.
units.tr: 89. If any goods are to be applied to the Society with the General's permission, the Provincial shall take care, above all, that they are collected with edification and charity, and not with harshness; and they should be handled through external procurators rather than through our own men. It will also be expedient that some alms be distributed from them to the poor of the town where the goods are; and an account of what is given and received of such goods shall be kept in writing, so that he himself, or the superior of that house or college to which they were applied, may be able to render it to the person designated by the General.

units.la: 90. Non ferat, nostros quicquam petere a parentibus, cognatis, vel amicis: sed omnia eis necessaria a Societate provideantur: intelligatque etiam si quibusdam ad tempus proprietas bonorum temporalium permittitur, usum tamen eorum ad propriam utilitatem nulli esse concedendum.
units.tr: 90. He shall not tolerate our men seeking anything from parents, relatives, or friends; rather, all that they need shall be provided for them by the Society. He shall also understand that, if ownership of temporal goods is granted to some for a time, the use of those goods for their own advantage must be conceded to no one.

units.la: DE MODO, QVO CVM GENERALI, ET ALIIS PRO- VINCIIS, AC EXTERNIS SE HABERE DEBEAT.
units.tr: Of the manner in which he ought to conduct himself towards the Superior General, the other provinces, and outsiders.

units.la: CAPVT XI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI.

units.la: 91. Obedientem, reverentem, ac fidelem, se Præposito Generali exhibeat, & hac re subditis inprimis exemplum præbeat: idq; potissimum curet, ut omnes de suis Superioribus bene sentiant, eiusq; peculiari devotione afficiantur.
units.tr: 91. He is to show himself obedient, respectful and faithful to the Father General, and in this matter he is to give an example above all to his subordinates; and he is to take especial care that all think well of their superiors and are attached to him with a special devotion.

units.la: 92. Perspecta Generali esse cupiat omnia, quæ ad suam Provinciam pertinent, eaq; per Superiores Domorum, & Collegiorum, & Consultores suæ Provinciæ iuxta formulam scribendi manifestari diligenter curet.
units.tr: 92. He should wish the General to know thoroughly all that pertains to his province, and he is to take care to make it known diligently, through the superiors of the houses and colleges and the consultors of his province, according to the form for writing.

units.la: 93. Cogitet de communi bono Societatis, illudq; iuvet: Congregationes Provinciales suo tempore iuxta formulam traditam cogat: si quid annotaverit circa Decreta & Constitutiones, vel quid aliud, quod Congregationem generalem expescat, Præposito Generali scribat, vel Procuratori tertio quoque anno ad eundem venturo tradat.
units.tr: 93. He is to consider the common good of the Society and to help it: he is to convene the provincial congregations at the appointed time according to the form handed down; if he has noted anything concerning the Decrees and Constitutions, or anything else that calls for a general congregation, he is to write it to the Father General, or hand it over to the Procurator who comes to him every third year.

units.la: 94. Si occasio se obtulerit iuvandi alias Provincias, non deest charitatis officio, & literarum communicatione iuxta formulam scribendi, mutua concordia & charitatem foveat.
units.tr: 94. If an occasion presents itself of helping other provinces, he should not be lacking in the duty of charity, and by communicating letters according to the form for writing, he is to foster mutual harmony and charity.

units.la: 95. Benevolos, & devotos conservet, curetq; ut benefactoribus se gratos nostri exhibeat: qui autem adversantur Societati, studeat, ut melius informati reconcilientur.
units.tr: 95. He is to keep well-disposed and devoted persons, and take care that our men show themselves grateful to benefactors; as for those who oppose the Society, he is to strive that, once better informed, they may be reconciled.

units.la: 96. Quæ eleemosynæ externis pauperibus, sive ordinariæ, sive extraordinariæ dari deant, ipse Superioribus præscribet, auditis Consultoribus, pro Collegii vel Domus facultate: Ubi vero habentur bona Ecclesiastica, eleemosynas aliquas fieri providebit in locis præcipue, ubi huiusmodi reditus percipiuntur.
units.tr: 96. As to the alms that are to be given to outside poor people, whether ordinary or extraordinary, he himself shall prescribe them to the superiors, after hearing the consultors, according to the means of the college or house; but where ecclesiastical goods are held, he shall arrange that some alms are made especially in those places where such revenues are received.

units.la: DE COMMVNI RATIONE IVVANDI PROXIMOS.
units.tr: ON THE COMMON MANNER OF HELPING NEIGHBOURS.

units.la: CAPVT XII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XII.

units.la: 97. Intelligat, præsertim sub finem studiorum, qui ex nostris, & quousque, quibusque rationibus domi, & foris externis se communicare debeant: quod tamen nisi probatis & in vocatione stabilibus, discretis, & bene instructis, quique alios ædificare possint, concedendum erit.
units.tr: 97. Let him see to it, especially towards the end of their studies, which of ours, how far, and in what ways they ought to share themselves with outsiders, both at home and abroad. This, however, is to be granted only to those who are proven, stable in their calling, discreet, well instructed, and able to build up others.

units.la: 98. Consideret, num Missæ celebrentur, & Sacramenta alia ministrentur iuxta usum Romanæ Ecclesiæ: concionandi etiam, & doctrinæ Christianæ docendæ motum observet: curetque, ut in his omnibus nostri uniformes sint; & ut finem, quem Societas intendit, asequantur. Præcipue vero circa concionatores invigilet, ut si quis ex iis ad suas se regulas forte non accommodaverit, a concionandi munere amoveatur, & in alijs Societatis ministeriis occupetur.
units.tr: 98. Let him consider whether Masses are celebrated and the other sacraments administered according to the custom of the Roman Church. Let him also watch over the practice of preaching and of teaching Christian doctrine, and take care that our men are uniform in all these things and attain the end which the Society intends. He should be especially vigilant over the preachers: if any of them has perhaps not conformed himself to our rules, he is to be removed from the office of preaching and employed in other ministries of the Society.

units.la: 99. Videat, num & domibus, in Collegijs concionatores, & confessarij ad sua munera idonei sint, & statuat pro ratione instituti & loci, quam frequenter domi, vel foris concionandum vel publice legendam sit, vel doctrina Christiana tradenda: & tempore pestis aliqui ab eo designentur, qui separati ab alijs, proximis iuvandis vacent.
units.tr: 99. Let him see whether, both in the houses and in the colleges, the preachers and confessors are suitable for their duties, and let him determine, according to the nature of the institute and the place, how often sermons are to be given or public lectures read, at home or abroad, or Christian doctrine taught. In a time of plague, let him designate some men who, set apart from the others, are to devote themselves to helping their neighbours.

units.la: 100. Det operam, ut Confessarij maturioris sint ætatis quantum fieri poterit, præsertim qui ad confessiones mulierum audiendas mittuntur: curetque ut nostri gratis, & privilegijs Apostolicis prudenter, & moderate utantur.
units.tr: 100. Let him take care that the confessors are of riper age as far as this can be done, especially those who are sent to hear the confessions of women; and let him see that our men use free-of-charge service and Apostolic privileges prudently and with moderation.

units.la: 101. In iis locis, in quibus simul Domus Professorum, & Collegium fuerit, Societatis ministeria in domo exercenda curabit: In Collegijs vero ea, quæ ad studia literarum, & auxilium spirituale Scholasticorum pertinent, tractanda sunt.
units.tr: 101. In those places where a house of Professed and a college are together, he will see to it that the ministries of the Society are carried out in the house; in the colleges, however, those things are to be handled which pertain to the literary studies and the spiritual help of the scholastics.

units.la: 102. Efficiet, ut in festis, quæ a nostris præcipue celebrari solent, ornatus nostrarum Ecclesiarum sit moderatus ac religiosus, & quoad fieri poterit, sine nimia distractione nostrorum, & molestia externorum.
units.tr: 102. He will bring it about that, on the feasts which our men are accustomed to celebrate especially, the decoration of our churches is moderate and reverent, and, as far as can be managed, without undue distraction of our men and without annoyance to outsiders.

units.la: 103. Non permittat, ut cum Congregationibus externorum, quæ confraternitates dicuntur, nostri misceantur, nec in Domibus vel Collegijs ulli earum coventus agantur, nisi qui ad finem earundem Domorum & Collegiorum in divino obsequio fient.
units.tr: 103. He shall not permit our men to mix with the congregations of outsiders which are called confraternities, nor are any meetings of them to be held in the houses or colleges, unless they are held for the purpose of those same houses and colleges, in the divine service.

units.la: 104. Si examinandi ministerium ab Ordinario iniunctum effugere nostri nulla ratione possint, quamvis de doctrina sufficientia iudicium ferre valeant, illud tamen retineant, ne de admittendis vel non admittendis ferant, sed illud omnino Prælatis relinquatur.
units.tr: 104. If our men can by no means avoid the duty of examining imposed by the Ordinary, then, although they may be able to pass judgment on the sufficiency of doctrine, they are nonetheless to refrain from it, so that they do not pronounce on admitting or not admitting candidates; rather, this must be left wholly to the prelates.

units.la: DE MISSIONIBVS, ET MVTATIONI- BVS NOSTRORVM. CAP. XIII.
units.tr: ON THE MISSIONS AND TRANSFERS OF OURS. CHAPTER XIII.

units.la: 105. Provincialis no abeat a sua Provincia sine Generalis, nec Præpositus, aut Rector a sua Domo, vel Collegio, absque Provincialis facultate, nisi locus esset vicinus, aut sine gravi incommodo Superioris responsum expectari non posset. Reliquorum vero mutationes intra Provinciam Provincialis ipse ne faciat sine causa alicuius momenti.
units.tr: 105. A Provincial shall not leave his Province without the General's permission, nor a Prefect or Rector leave his House or College without the Provincial's permission, unless the place is nearby, or unless a reply from the Superior cannot be awaited without serious inconvenience. As for transfers of the rest within the Province, the Provincial himself shall not make them without some reason of real weight.

units.la: 106. In mittendis operarijs per Provinciam extra Domos, & Collegia, ut in vinea Domini laborent, observet, quæ in Constitutionibus, & Regulis missionum dicuntur: videat tamen, ne Domus, & Collegia necessarijs ministris destituantur.
units.tr: 106.
