In sending workers throughout the Province outside our Houses and Colleges, that they may labour in the Lord's vineyard, he shall observe what is laid down in the Constitutions and in the rules for missions; yet he shall see to it that the Houses and Colleges are not left without the ministers they need.

units.la: 107. Quocunque mittat aliquem, eum per se, vel alium plene instruat, & ordinarie in scriptis tam de modo procedendi, quàm de medijs, quibus eum uti velit ad finem, quem in animo habet.
units.tr: 107. Whomever he sends anywhere, he shall fully instruct him, either himself or through another, and ordinarily in writing, both as to the manner of proceeding and as to the means by which he wishes him to use to reach the end he has in mind.

units.la: 108. Per crebram literarum communicationem iuxta formulam scribendi totius successus certior factus ex eo loco, ubi ipse commoratur, consilio & orationibus, & alijs rationibus eum iuvabit, ut personæ, & negotium postulaverit.
units.tr: 108. By frequent exchange of letters, following the prescribed form of writing, he shall keep himself informed of the whole course of events; and from the place where he himself dwells, he shall help the man with counsel, prayers, and other means, as the person and the business require.

units.la: 109. Optimi quique, & maturiores ad proximos iuvandos, quantum commode fieri poterit, mittantur: & si ei videbitur expedire, alicui Superiori vicinioris Domus, vel Collegij subijciantur.
units.tr: 109. The best and most mature men are to be sent to help their neighbours, as far as this can conveniently be done; and if he judges it expedient, they shall be placed under some Superior of a nearer House or College.

units.la: 110. Cum mutari aliquem oportebit, animad vertat, ut ad eum revocandum, quoad fieri poterit, ijs medijs utatur, ut ij, à quibus evocatur, potius benevoli omnino maneant, quàm offensi, vel male affecti.
units.tr: 110. When someone must be moved, he shall take care that, in recalling him, he uses, as far as can be done, such means that those from whom he is called away remain wholly well-disposed rather than offended or ill-affected.

units.la: 111. Si missum à Superiore, vel à summo Pontifice minus utiliter occupari videret, Generalem admoneat.
units.tr: 111. If he sees that a man sent by a Superior, or by the Supreme Pontiff, is being employed less usefully, he shall admonish the General.

units.la: 112. Extra Provinciam suam neminem mittat, nec etiam ad laborandum in vinea Domini, nisi negotij alicuius, aut peregrinationis causa, aut nisi ei constaret de Generalis voluntate, vel coveniret cum Provinciali illius Provinciæ, ad quam mittere aliquem voluerit: ad Provincias tamen extra Europam, & inter ipsas met, hæ transmutationes sine facultate Generalis ne fiant.
units.tr: 112. He shall send no one outside his own Province, nor even to labour in the Lord's vineyard, unless for the sake of some business or of travel, or unless he is certain of the General's wish, or has agreed with the Provincial of that Province to which he wishes to send someone. Yet transfers to Provinces outside Europe, and between those same Provinces, are not to be made without the General's permission.

units.la: 113. Post cognitam Generalis mortem Provincialis nemine ex ijs, qui jus suffragij habent ex sua Provincia in aliam mittat ante congregationem Provincialem, nisi causa sit adeo urgens, ut ipse & maior pars consultorum ipsius existimet esse mittendum.
units.tr: 113. After the General's death is known, a Provincial shall not send anyone from his Province to another, of those who have the right of suffrage, before the Provincial Congregation, unless the cause is so urgent that he and the greater part of his consultors judge it must be done.

units.la: 114. Cum peregre erit nostris proficiscendum, aliquem, cui maxime confidat, præficiet, cui toto itineris tempore cæteri tanquam Superiori in omnibus obediant.
units.tr: 114. When some of ours must set out on a journey abroad, he shall appoint the man in whom he has the greatest confidence, whom the others shall obey in all things, as their Superior, for the whole time of the journey.

units.la: 115. Ad retinendam religiosam disciplinam, & paupertatis rationem, det operam, ut nostri in profectionibus, quos ipsorum Superiores id præstare posse iudicaverint, in toto, vel in parte pedestri itinere utantur & in equitando solius necessitatis, sive personæ, sive negotiorum ratio habeatur.
units.tr: 115. To preserve religious discipline and the practice of poverty, he shall take care that those of ours on journeys whom their Superiors judge able to manage it, use travel on foot for the whole or part of the route, and ride horses only out of necessity, whether the regard is had to the person or to the business.

units.la: 116. Expensas itinerum solvere eius erit Provinciæ, aut Collegij, aut Domus, in cuius bonum & utilitatem cedit profectio: quod si in ea re dubium esset, arbitrio ipsius auditis Consultoribus statuedum relinquitur: si aliquando tamen inter aliquos Provinciales non conveniret, recurrant ad Generalem.
units.tr: 116. It is the duty of the Province, College, or House in whose good and advantage the journey is undertaken to pay its expenses; but if there were doubt about this matter, the decision is left to his own judgment after hearing his consultors; and if at any time the Provincials cannot agree among themselves, they are to have recourse to the General.

units.la: 117. Quando quis ab uno loco ad alium transfertur, Superior, ad quem talis mittitur, informandus est, quantum ad cognoscendum, & iuvandum eum sit satis. Neminem autem ex uno in alium locum ire permittat, sine literis patentibus.
units.tr: 117. When someone is transferred from one place to another, the Superior to whom he is sent is to be informed of enough to know and help him. He shall not permit anyone to go from one place to another without letters patent.

units.la: DE VISITATIONE. CAP. XIV.
units.tr: CONCERNING VISITATION. CHAPTER XIV.

units.la: 118. Singulis annis per se ipsum singula loca suæ Provinciæ visitet, cum hoc fit valde proprium sui officij, & ibi diutius immoretur, ubi magis erit opus, præsertim in loco ad communicationem cum inferioribus & Generali Præposito magis commodo.
units.tr: 118. Each year he shall visit the individual places of his Province in person, since this is a very proper part of his office; and he shall remain longer where there is more need, especially in the place that is more convenient for communication with the inferiors and for the General Superior.

units.la: 119. Si quando ob causas graviores visitare omnia loca suæ Provinciæ ipse no possit, re cum suis Consultoribus collata, ad ea, quæ non potest, sibi alium substituat. Quamvis omnino curandum sit, ut Domos probationis & scholasticorum seminaria peculiari cura, & per se visitet.
units.tr: 119. If at any time, for weightier reasons, he cannot visit all the places of his Province himself, then, having conferred with his Consultors, he shall substitute another in his place for those he cannot visit. Yet it must by all means be taken care that he himself visits the houses of probation and the seminaries of scholastics with particular diligence.

units.la: 120. Cum ad Domum, vel Collegium aliquod pervenerit, Superiorem interroget, nü aliquid urgeat, cui statim necessario sit remedium adhibendum: & Visitationes præteritas petat, deinde omnes simul benigne alloquatur, eosque ad renovationem in spiritu, & studium perfectionis hortetur.
units.tr: 120. When he arrives at a house or college, he shall first ask the Superior whether anything presses which requires an immediate remedy; he shall ask for the visitations made previously, and then address everyone together kindly, exhorting them to renewal in the spirit and to zeal for perfection.

units.la: 121. Incipiat Visitationem a templo, cuius ostio clauso, videat, quomodo custodiatur sanctiss. Eucharistiæ Sacramentum: mox visitet sacrum infirmorum oleum, & sanctorum reliquias, ex quibus nihil ulla ratione auferatur, altaria, sedes Confessariorum, atque alia, quæ tam in templo, quam in Sacristia ad divinum cultum pertinent.
units.tr: 121. He shall begin the visitation with the church. With its door shut, he shall see how the most holy Sacrament of the Eucharist is kept; then he shall inspect the holy oil of the sick and the relics of the saints, none of which may be removed on any account; the altars, the confessionals, and whatever else pertains to divine worship, both in the church and in the sacristy.

units.la: 122. Postea ad visitationem personarum accedat, & curet, ut omnibus benevolum se exhibeat, ne alicuius mentem subeat suspicio, quod ob sinistras aliquas informationes minus hilarem vultum ipsis ostendat.
units.tr: 122. Afterwards he shall turn to the visitation of the persons, and take care to show himself kindly to all, so that no suspicion arises in anyone's mind that, owing to some unfavourable reports, he shows them a less cheerful face.

units.la: 123. Petat a Superiore, & consequenter a Consultoribus & aliquibus Patrib. antiquioribus, vel præcipuis Officialibus, ut ea, quæ sciunt alicuius moneti de statu Collegij, vel domus, aut de personis referant: quod si iudicaverit expedire, iubere poterit, ut informationes huiusmodi, vel partem earum breviter scribant, & sibi tradant: scripta autem quæ secretum continent, clausa ipse diligentissime servet, caveatque ne minimo quidem indicio eos, qui sibi aliquid referunt, prodat.
units.tr: 123. He shall ask the Superior, and afterwards the Consultors and some of the older Fathers or the chief officials, to report what they know of any matter concerning the state of the college or house, or concerning the persons. If he judges it advisable, he may order such reports, or part of them, to be written down briefly and handed to him; but he shall keep most diligently under seal those writings which contain secrets, and take care that he does not betray by the slightest hint those who report anything to him.

units.la: 124. Huiusmodi informationibus acceptis & consideratis, percurrat cum Superiore catalogum personarum domus, vel Collegij, brevemque de singulis eo capiat informationem.
units.tr: 124. Having received and considered such reports, he shall go through with the Superior the catalogue of the persons of the house or college, and form a brief information about each one.

units.la: 125. Deinde vocet singillatim eos eo ordine qui ei magis convenire videbitur, & singulos seorsum iuxta instructionem sequenti capite positam memoriter potius, quam ex scripto interroget, & quæ advertenda iudicaverit, sibi memoriæ causa scribat: quid vero a quoq; interrogandum sit, illius prudentiæ relinquitur.
units.tr: 125. Then he shall summon them one by one, in the order that seems most suitable to him, and question each separately, according to the instruction given in the following chapter, from memory rather than from a written paper. Whatever he judges worth noting he shall write down for the sake of memory. What he should ask each one is left to his prudence.

units.la: 126. Hortetur omnes ad veritatem sincere dicendam, ne ipsis imputetur, si morbi propter eorum silentium incogniti, & latentes curari non possint: admoneatq; teneri eos servare sub secreto, quicquid cum eo, quod secretum requirit, transfegerint, licet a quovis alio, qui ipso sit inferior, de ea re interrogentur.
units.tr: 126. He shall exhort everyone to speak the truth sincerely, lest the blame fall on them if illnesses remain unknown and hidden on account of their silence and cannot be cured; and he shall warn them that they are bound to keep under secrecy whatever they have discussed with him that requires secrecy, even if they are questioned about that matter by any other who is inferior to himself.

units.la: 127. Non facile credat, si quæ forsan contra alios, præsertim Superiores dicentur, sed ea notet, & expendat, ut veritatem assequatur: Caveatque, ne dum subditos consolari studet, illi debiliores in obedientia, & reverentia erga suos immediatos Superiores reddantur.
units.tr: 127. He shall not readily believe whatever may perhaps be said against others, especially Superiors, but shall note it and weigh it, so that he may arrive at the truth; and he shall take care that, while he strives to console the subjects, they do not become weaker in obedience and reverence toward their immediate Superiors.

units.la: 128. Si quis divisionis, aut differentiones eorum, qui unâ vivunt, inter se, vel cum suo capite auctor esse inveniretur, diligentissime ab ea congregatione, velut pestis, quæ eam potest inficere, si præsens remedium non adhibeatur, separandus est.
units.tr: 128. If anyone is found to be the author of division or of dissensions among those who live together, or between them and their head, he is to be separated most diligently from that congregation, as from a plague which can infect it if no present remedy is applied.

units.la: 129. Visitatio rerum, aut partium domus, iuxta ea, quæ in præcedentibus regulis, præsertim in 9. capite huius officij dicta sunt, fieri debet: in qua simul examinandæ sunt regulæ officialium, qui eiusmodi rerum curam habent: si quid autem non solum informationem, sed inspectionem requirat, ipse per se, aut socium id præstabit.
units.tr: 129. The visitation of the goods or departments of the house must be made according to what was said in the preceding rules, especially in the ninth chapter of this office. In it the rules of the officials who have the care of such things are also to be examined. If any matter requires not only information but inspection, he himself or a companion shall carry it out.

units.la: 130. Summarium Constitutionum, & regulas communes coram Superiore, Consultoribus, & Ministro examinabit, & si quas non observari intellexerit, consideratis causis remedia adhibebit, ut observari possint. Regulas autem Ministri, Consultorum, & Admonitoris, Cocionatorum, & Sacerdotum, itemq; præcipuorum Officialium, ipse per se cum ipsismet examinabit: reliquas vero aliorum Officialium poterit socio, aut alteri coram singulis eorum examinandas committere.
units.tr: 130. He shall examine the summary of the Constitutions and the common rules in the presence of the Superior, the Consultors and the Minister; and if he finds that any are not observed, he shall, having considered the causes, apply remedies so that they can be observed. The rules of the Minister, of the Consultors, of the Admonitor, of the preachers and priests, and likewise of the chief officials, he shall examine himself with those very persons; the remaining rules of the other officials he may entrust to a companion, or to another, to be examined in the presence of each of them.

units.la: 131. Provincialis integram rationem totius anteactæ vitæ, iuxta Constitutiones ab aliis exigat, qui Societatem ingrediuntur: & ab eo tempore, quo ad studia missi sunt ab ijs, qui illis absolutis ad tertium probationis annum peragendum mittuntur. Quod si id aliquando præstare non poterit, substituat ad id ordinarie Superiore Domus, vel Collegij. Singulis vero annis in quacunque Domo, vel Collegio suæ Provinciæ absoluta rerum domesticarum visitatione, aut in ipso visitationis decursu (si id opportunius in aliquibus fore iudicaret) rationem conscientiæ ab omnibus accipiat ab ultima, quam reddiderunt iuxta modum inferius præscriptum. Quod si visitatio circa renovationem votorum inciderit, (quam extra statutum tempus ratione sui adventus in domum aliquam, vel Collegium, præsertim magnum, per unum aut alterum mensem prætermittere, aut differre poterit) ipse ad excipiendas consessiones generales nostrorum, aliquos Patres probatos, & maturiores designabit: eosque, qui sibi confiteri volent, benignè audiet.
units.tr: 131. The Provincial shall require a full account of the whole past life, according to the Constitutions, from those who enter the Society, and from the time when they were sent to their studies by those who, once those are finished, are sent to complete the third year of probation. If he is ever unable to do this himself, he shall ordinarily substitute the Superior of the house or college. Each year, in whatever house or college of his Province, when the visitation of the domestic affairs has been completed, or in the course of the visitation itself (if he judges this more convenient in some places), he shall receive an account of conscience from all, from the last one they rendered, according to the manner prescribed below. But if the visitation happens to fall at the time of the renewal of vows (which, on account of his arrival, he may omit or postpone for a month or so beyond the appointed time in some house or college, especially a large one), he himself shall designate some approved and more mature Fathers to receive the general confessions of ours; and those who wish to confess to him he shall hear kindly.

units.la: 132. Postremum omnium visitet Superiorem Domus, vel Collegij circa ea, quæ ad personam, & officium eius attinent, iuxta officij eius regulas, & ea, quæ ex acceptis informationibus collegerit.
units.tr: 132. Last of all, he shall visit the Superior of the house or college regarding those matters which pertain to his person and office, according to the rules of his office, and the things he has gathered from the information received.

units.la: 133. Visitatione cuiusque Domus, vel Collegij absoluta, & rebus omnibus perspectis, ut laboris sui fructum capiat, denuo omnia, quæ accepit in visitatione, consideret; & ea, quæ maioris momenti sunt, diligentius expendat: quid item clarum, quidque tantum probabile videatur, & de quibus Generalis consulendus est, & quæ cum solo Superiore Domus, vel Collegij, quæ etiam cum Consultoribus, & quæ cum aliis particularibus sint transfigenda, diligenter discernat.
units.tr: 133. When the visitation of each house or college is finished, and all things have been seen, then, so that he may reap the fruit of his labour, he shall again consider everything he has received in the visitation, weigh more carefully those matters which are of greater importance, and carefully distinguish what seems clear from what seems only probable, which matters must be referred to the General, which must be handled with the Superior of the house or college alone, which with the Consultors as well, and which with other particular persons.

units.la: 134. Quæ ad gubernationem spectantia ipsi ordinanda videbuntur, hæc vel illa ijs etiam expendenda tradat, quos de unaquaque re melius iudicare posse confidat. Et antequam multiplicem executionis manum rebus imponat, omnia in orationibus, & Missarum sacrificijs Deo commendet, ut iuxta ipsius divinum beneplacitum dirigantur.
units.tr: 134. Whatever seems to him to be ordered for government, he shall lay before those whom he trusts to judge better in each matter, to be weighed by them as well. And before he puts his many-handed execution to work, he shall commend everything to God in prayers and Mass sacrifices, that it may be directed according to his divine good pleasure.

units.la: 135. Postquam autem apud se omnia constituerit ex præteritæ visitationis memoriali, ubi rerum quæ temporariæ sunt, ordinationes scribuntur, eas quæ executioni mandatæ fuerint, expungat. In libro vero, in quo non nisi maioris momenti ordinationes scribendæ erunt, ipse ea tantum scribet, suaque manu subscribet, quæ cum Generali communicaverit, & ab ipso fuerint approbata.
units.tr: 135. After he has settled everything in his own mind from the memorial of the previous visitation, in which the ordinances concerning temporary matters are written, he shall strike out those which have been carried into execution. In the book, however, in which only ordinances of greater importance are to be written, he shall write only those which he has communicated to the General and which have been approved by him, and he shall subscribe them with his own hand.

units.la: INSTRVCTIO DE IIS, QVÆ IN VISITATIONE INTERROGANDA SVNT. CAPVT XV.
units.tr: INSTRUCTION CONCERNING THOSE THINGS TO BE ASKED IN THE VISITATION. CHAPTER XV.

units.la: QVAE AD GVBERNATIONEM PERTINENT A SVPERIO- RIBVS, ET CONSVLTORIBVS, ET ALIIS, QVIBVS VIDEBITVR, PETENDA.
units.tr: WHAT PERTAINS TO GOVERNMENT, TO BE SOUGHT FROM THE SUPERIORS, THE CONSULTORS, AND OTHERS WHOM IT SEEMS APPROPRIATE TO ASK.

units.la: 1. Interroget, si quid gravius in ea Domo, vel Collegio accidisse extra confessionem intellexerit, & quod remedium sit adhibitum.
units.tr: 1. Let him ask whether he has learned of anything more serious that has happened in that house or college outside of confession, and what remedy has been applied.

units.la: 2. Quomodo servéntur regulæ, quæ ad Novitios pertinent.
units.tr: 2. How the rules that pertain to novices are observed.

units.la: 3. An aliqui, præsertim pueri, aut mulieres ad vota emittenda inducantur, vel ad eorum filia alia observanda indiscrete trahantur.
units.tr: 3. Whether any persons, especially boys or women, are induced to take vows, or are drawn indiscriminately to observe their other practices.

units.la: 4. An aliquis domi nimis affectus videatur ad consanguineos, vel ad eorum subventionem teneatur.
units.tr: 4. Whether anyone at home seems too attached to his relatives, or is bound to support them.

units.la: 5. De numero, & sufficientia Confessariorum, & de frequentia, & fructu confitentium.
units.tr: 5. Concerning the number and sufficiency of the confessors, and concerning the frequency and fruit of those who confess.

units.la: 6. Quomodo litterarum studia vigeant, & quam exacte serventur, quæ de opinionum novitate & diverlitate statuta sunt. Et an aliqui videantur finitis iam studijs educendi è Collegijs.
units.tr: 6. How the study of letters flourishes, and how strictly those things are kept which have been decreed concerning the novelty and diversity of opinions. And whether any seem to be due to be removed from the colleges now that their studies are finished.

units.la: 7. An infirmi, hospitalia, carceres, & triremes (ubi essent) visitentur, & adiuvantur à nostris.
units.tr: 7. Whether the sick, hospitals, prisons, and galleys (wherever they are) are visited and assisted by ours.

units.la: 8. Ex quibus operibus piis iuxta nostrum institutum, maior fructus percipiatur.
units.tr: 8. From which pious works, in accordance with our institute, the greater fruit is received.

units.la: 9. De cura in tradendis spiritualibus exercitiis, & quam exacte illa fiant. Et de vigilantia in puerorum ac rudium in doctrina Christiana institutione.
units.tr: 9. Concerning the care taken in giving the spiritual exercises, and how exactly they are performed; and concerning vigilance in the instruction of boys and the untaught in Christian doctrine.

units.la: 10. De modo conversandi iuxta rationem, & finem nostri instituti.
units.tr: 10. Concerning the manner of living according to the reason and end of our institute.

units.la: 11. De missionibus & earum fructu, & modo procedendi eorum, qui mittuntur.
units.tr: 11. Concerning the missions and their fruit, and the manner of proceeding of those who are sent.

units.la: 12. An aliqui praetextu valetudinis iuvandae a spiritus perfectione degenerent, & a laboribus nostri instituti abhorreant, atque ad otium aspirent.
units.tr: 12. Whether some, under the pretext of restoring their health, degenerate from the perfection of the spirit, shrink from the labours of our institute, and aspire to leisure.

units.la: 13. An erga nostros infirmos, & hospites debita Societatis charitas, & cura exerceatur.
units.tr: 13. Whether the due charity and care of the Society is exercised towards our sick and guests.

units.la: 14. An aliqua ambitionis & proprietatis indicia in aliquo appareant.
units.tr: 14. Whether any signs of ambition and self-interest appear in anyone.

units.la: 15. Quae eleemosyna externis pauperibus dentur.
units.tr: 15. What alms are given to outside poor people.

units.la: QVÆ AB OMNIBVS PETI POSSVNT.
units.tr: WHAT MAY BE ASKED OF ALL

units.la: 16. Quomodo valeat corpore, & viribus, & quomodo ei conveniat ratio victus, vestitus, cubiculi, & exercitationis corporalis, qua utitur.
units.tr: 16. How he fares in body and strength, and what diet, clothing, lodging, and bodily exercise he uses, and whether they suit him.

units.la: 17. Si quid dubitationis, aut difficultatis, si quid etiam ad suam consolationem, instructionem, aut profectum fore putat, confidenter proponat.
units.tr: 17. If he thinks there is any doubt or difficulty, or anything that will bring him consolation, instruction, or progress, let him propose it with confidence.

units.la: 18. Quod ad alios attinet, interrogetur, quomodo tractetur a suis Superioribus, & quid sentiat de illis, tam de personis, quam de officiis eorum.
units.tr: 18. As regards others, he may be asked how he is treated by his Superiors, and what he thinks of them, both as persons and in their offices.

units.la: 19. An aliquis Superior impedierit libertatem subditorum scribendi ad Superiores mediatos, aut quovis modo significaverit, sibi non placere, ut nostri de ipso, aut eius gubernatione, ad eosdem scribant.
units.tr: 19. Whether any Superior has hindered the freedom of subjects to write to higher Superiors, or has in any way indicated that he does not wish our men to write to those same Superiors about himself or his government.

units.la: 20. An noverit extra confessionem aliquid de quavis persona, quod non ei probetur; ut de inobedientia, murmuratione, conspirationibus, praesertim contra Superiores, & si quid parum honestum, & incautum in familiaritate nimia cum aliqua persona accidisset, vel contra de dissensione.
units.tr: 20. Whether he knows, outside confession, anything about any person that is not approved: such as disobedience, murmuring, conspiracies, especially against Superiors; and if anything not altogether honourable or prudent has happened through excessive familiarity with some person, or, on the other side, dissension.

units.la: 21. Quomodo ferventur Domi Constitutiones, Decreta, Regulae, communis ordo, & ordinationes, quae a Praeposito Generali, & aliis Superioribus emanant.
units.tr: 21. How the Constitutions, Decrees, Rules, the common order, and the ordinances that issue from the General Superior and the other Superiors are observed at home.

units.la: 22. Quomodo exerceantur ministeria Societatis erga externos, quod ad modum, & fructum attinet.
units.tr: 22. How the ministries of the Society toward outsiders are carried on, as regards the manner and the fruit.

units.la: 23. Quis sit profectus nostrorum in rebus spiritualibus, & quod omnium in solidis virtutibus acquirendis studium.
units.tr: 23. What progress our men are making in spiritual matters, and the zeal of all for acquiring solid virtues.

units.la: 24. Si de iis etiam, quae pertinent ad alias Domus, & Collegia totius Provinciae aliquid habet, quod alicuius momenti videatur, liberè proponat.
units.tr: 24. If he has anything of some weight to report about those matters which concern other houses and colleges of the whole Province, let him propose it freely.

units.la: PRO SCHOLASTICIS ADDATVR.
units.tr: FOR THE SCHOLASTICS, THIS IS ADDED.

units.la: 25. Quid ingenii, memoriae, virium, & propensionis ad literas in se experiatur.
units.tr: 25. What he finds in himself of talent, memory, strength, and inclination toward letters.

units.la: 26. An occupatione exteriore, vel studijs removeatur, vel distrahatur a rebus spiritualibus.
units.tr: 26. Whether he is drawn away from spiritual things, or distracted from them, by outside occupation or studies.

units.la: 27. An habeat libros necessarios, & an scribat, legat, disputet.
units.tr: 27. Whether he has the necessary books, and whether he writes, reads, and disputes.

units.la: 28. De suo profectu in literis quid sentiat.
units.tr: 28. What he thinks of his own progress in letters.

units.la: 29. An omnia experimenta Societatis fecerit, & quo fructu.
units.tr: 29. Whether he has undergone all the trials of the Society, and with what fruit.

units.la: PRO IIS, QVI IN PROBATIONE VERSANTVR.
units.tr: FOR THOSE WHO ARE IN PROBATION.

units.la: 30. An firmus sit in proposito vivendi, & moriendi in Societate.
units.tr: 30. Whether he is steadfast in his purpose of living and dying in the Society.

units.la: 31. An sit indifferens ad quemlibet gradum, ministeria, & exercitia Societatis, prout obedientia constituerit.
units.tr: 31. Whether he is indifferent to any grade, ministries and exercises of the Society, as obedience shall appoint.

units.la: 32. An exercitia spiritualia, vel aliqua alia experimenta fecerit, & in quibus plus profecerit, & alia, si videbitur, ex Examine.
units.tr: 32. Whether he has undertaken the spiritual exercises or any other trials, and in which he has made more progress, and others, if it seems fit, from the Examination.

units.la: REGVLÆ MODVS ACCIPIENDÆ RATIONIS CONSCIENTIAE.
units.tr: RULE ON THE MANNER OF RECEIVING THE CONSCIENCE REVIEW.

units.la: Quod in summario Constitutionum, praescribitur de manifestanda conscientia, idmagni momenti ad Dei gloriam & Societatis nostræ bonum Pater noster sanctæ memoriæ Ignatius exi-stimavit: quare, ut omni diligentia & animi sinceritate servetur: Provinciali curandum erit. Et cum quisque dixerit, quæ dicere voluerit, iuxta instructionem datam, poterit Provincialis, si qua exi-stimaverit amplius interrog分 ...
units.tr: Our holy Father Ignatius, of blessed memory, judged that what is prescribed in the summary of the Constitutions concerning the manifestation of conscience is of great importance for the glory of God and the good of our Society. Therefore the Provincial shall take care that it is observed with all diligence and sincerity of mind. When each person has said what he wishes to say, in accordance with the instruction given, the Provincial may ask further questions if he thinks any are needed.

units.la: [illegible, ~40 letters]
units.tr: [illegible in the scan]

units.la: REGVLAE PRAEPOSITI DOMVS PROFESSAE.
units.tr: RULES OF THE PREPOSITUS OF THE PROFESSED HOUSE.

units.la: DE IIS, QVÆ AD EIVS PERSONAM, ET TOTIVS DOMVS ADMINISTRATIONEM PERTINENT. CAP. I.
units.tr: CONCERNING THOSE MATTERS WHICH PERTAIN TO HIS PERSON AND TO THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE WHOLE HOUSE. CHAPTER I.

units.la: Omni studio enitatur, ut talis sit, qualis optatur Rector in nostris Constitutionibus, atque eo magis, quod illis præsit; quos viros spirituales, & perfectionis studiosos esse oportet.
units.tr: He should strive with every effort to be such as our Constitutions desire the Rector to be, and all the more so because he presides over men who ought to be spiritual and eager for perfection.

units.la: 2. Primam officij sui curam in eo positam esse intelligat, ut oratione, & sanctis desideriis totā domum velut humeris suis, sustineat; & quæ cumque in iis, quibus præest, ad ipsorum, aliorumque ædificationem, iuxta institutionem nostri rationem, optare debet, prius in seipso præstare studeat.
units.tr: 2. Let him understand that the first care of his office lies in this: that he bear the whole house, as it were on his shoulders, through prayer and holy desires. Whatever he ought to wish for those under his charge, for their own edification and that of others, according to the purpose of our Institute, he should first strive to show forth in himself.

units.la: 3. Communes regulas ipse servet, & particularia in cibo, indumentis & aliarum rerum usu quantum fieri potest, vitet: familiaritate, atque indulgentia cum quibusdam, alios ne offendat.
units.tr: 3. Let him observe the common rules himself, and avoid, as far as possible, special indulgences in food, clothing and the use of other things. Let him not give offence to others by familiarity or indulgence with certain individuals.

units.la: 4. Intra annum, postquam officium Præpositi prima vice inierit, quadraginta diebus Christianam doctrinam eo modo, quo in secunda Congregatione de Rectore expositum est, legat, aut doceat: sed ex causa per alium id munus cum facultate Provincialis obire poterit.
units.tr: 4. Within a year after he has first entered upon the office of Prepositus, let him read or teach Christian doctrine for forty days, in the manner set out in the second Congregation concerning the Rector. For a good reason, however, he may discharge this duty through another, with the permission of the Provincial.

units.la: 5. Consuetudines receptas, & à Generali, vel Provinciali approbatas servet, ac servari faciat: si tamen aliqua alia à Præcedenti Præposito indufta fuerit, non mutet inconsulto Provinciali: ipse vero, nisi suo Superiore approbante, nullam introducat.
units.tr: 5. Let him keep the customs that have been received and approved by the General or the Provincial, and see that they are kept. If, however, some other custom has been introduced by the previous Prepositus, he should not change it without consulting the Provincial. He himself should introduce none, unless his Superior approves.

units.la: 6. Eos, qui domestica obeunt ministeria (exceptis quibusdam, quorum electio ad Provincialem pertinet) prudenter constituat, suas cuique regulas tradat, aliquando visitet, & prout in Domino convenire iudicabit, vel in eisdem ministeriis detineat, vel ab eis removeat. Quia vero officia quædam, ut bene fiant, experientiam requirunt, qui ad ea idonei inveniuntur, non facile mutari debebunt.
units.tr: 6. Let him prudently appoint those who perform domestic ministries (excepting certain posts, whose choice belongs to the Provincial), give each one his own rules, visit them from time to time, and, as he judges fitting in the Lord, either keep them in those ministries or remove them from them. Since certain offices require experience if they are to be done well, those who are found suitable for them should not easily be moved.

units.la: 7. Ut proficere officialibus de subsidio, si necessarium id fuerit, ne labore gravaentur, debebit: ita cum tempus vacuum illis fuerit, ut illud utiliter impendant divino servitio, curabit.
units.tr: 7. He shall take care to provide help for the officials, if this is necessary, so that they are not burdened with labour. And when they have free time, he shall see that they spend it usefully in the service of God.

units.la: 8. Etsi potestatem habet designandi Confessarios suis subditis, ordinarium tamen Confessarium Domus non constituet sine approbatione Provincialis.
units.tr: 8. Although he has the power to assign confessors to his subjects, he shall not appoint an ordinary confessor for the House without the approval of the Provincial.

units.la: 9. Quamvis in virtute obedientiæ iubere possit, non nisi rarissime, & ex gravi aecurgenti causa id faciat.
units.tr: 9. Although he may command in virtue of obedience, he should do so only very rarely, and only for a serious and urgent reason.

units.la: 10. Ordinarias tantum poenitentias imponat, quales sunt parva mensa, publica reprehensio, conclusio in circulo, edere sub mensa, osculari aliorum pedes, orare in refectorio, dicere culpam suam, subtractio cibi usque ad panem, & aquam, si res postulaverit, disciplina publica in refectorio, & alia exercitia humilia, & domestica. 11. Sicut ad Præpositum pertinet dispensare in regulis, & Constitutionibus, & decretis Congregationum generalium cum particularibus, quando necesse erit: sic & cum dispensaverit in rebus maioris momenti, quæ videntur urgere, & in quibus sine gravi incommodo Provincialis responsum expectari non potest, eum primo quoque tempore de huiusmodi dispensatione, ac eius causa admonere.
units.tr: 10. Let him impose only ordinary penances, such as: the small table, public reproof, being shut in the circle, eating under the table, kissing the feet of others, praying in the refectory, confessing one's fault aloud, withdrawal of food to bread and water if the situation requires it, public discipline in the refectory, and other humble and domestic exercises. 11. Just as it belongs to the Prepositus to dispense from the rules, the Constitutions and the decrees of the General Congregations, with particular cases, whenever necessary, so too, when he has dispensed in matters of greater moment, which seem pressing, and in which a reply from the Provincial cannot be awaited without serious inconvenience, he should inform him of such a dispensation and its reason at the first opportunity.

units.la: 12. Nominae eorum, qui vota solemnia, vel simplicia emiserunt, in libro ad hoc parato notentur, in Professis quidem, & Coadiutoribus formatis cum nominibus admittentium, in reliquis vero post biennium cum nominibus celebrantium, adnotato loco, & tempore, iuxta Constitutiones.
units.tr: 12. The names of those who have made solemn or simple vows shall be recorded in a book prepared for this purpose: for the Professed and the formed Coadjutors, together with the names of those who admitted them; for the rest, after two years, together with the names of those who celebrated the vows, with the place and time noted, according to the Constitutions.

units.la: 13. Quas habeat facultates partim ex iis, quæ ipsi in his regulis conceduntur, partim ex compendio facultatum Societatis intelligat, ut in iis, quas non habet, sciat ad Superiorem recurrere.
units.tr: 13. Let him understand what faculties he has, partly from those granted to him in these rules, and partly from the summary of the faculties of the Society, so that in those which he does not have, he knows to have recourse to his Superior.

units.la: DE IIS, QVÆ PRÆPOSITVM AD BONAM ADMIN- ISTRATIONEM IVVABVNT
units.tr: Concerning those things which help the Rector in good administration

units.la: CAP. II.
units.tr: CHAP. II.

units.la: 14. SIT solicitus, ne minister, & reliqui officiales suo desint officio, omissis aliis, quæ possent impedire.
units.tr: 14. Let him take care that the minister and the other officials do not fail in their duty, leaving aside other matters which might hinder this.

units.la: 15. Singulis vel saltem alternis hebdomadis cum suis Consultoribus conveniat, (nisi ro re nata aliquid extraordinarie esset consultandum) deque rebus maioris momenti, quæ temporum, & negotiorum varietate occurrunt, cum illis agat: quamquam ijs auditis, enes ipsum erit de singulis statuendi facultas.
units.tr: 15. Let him meet with his Consultors singly, or at least every other week (unless something extraordinary has to be considered on the spur of the moment), and deal with them about the more important matters which arise from the variety of times and business. Nevertheless, once he has heard them, the decision on each point will be his own.

units.la: 16. Consultores, aliosque omnes, cum ei aliquid proponunt, libenter, & benigne excipiat, præcipue eum, cui Monitoris officium commissum est: efficiatque, ut in sua Domo, quæ in formula scribendi præscripta sunt, serventur.
units.tr: 16. Let him receive the Consultors, and all others, when they put something before him, willingly and kindly, especially the one to whom the office of Monitor has been entrusted; and let him see to it that in his House those things are observed which are prescribed in the formula for writing.

units.la: 17. Habeat librum, in quo scribantur visitationes Domus à Generali approbatæ: in quo iam ordinationes aliæ alicuius momenti, quæ à Generali mittuntur: & quæ perpetuæ sunt, ab ijs, quæ temporariæ sunt, separatim notentur; alia vero, quæ visitator, & Provincialis præscripserint: in alio libro scribantur.
units.tr: 17. Let him have a book in which the visitations of the House approved by the General are written; in it are also to be written other ordinances of some importance which are sent from the General. Those which are perpetual are to be noted separately from those which are temporary; the others, however, which the visitor and the Provincial have prescribed, are to be written in another book.

units.la: 18. Institutum Societatis cognoscat ex lectione literarum Apostolicarum, Constitutionum, & Decretorum generalium Congregationum: magis autem particularia ex lectione regularum tam communium, quam officij sui, & aliorum, qui sub ipsius cura sunt, ac Provincialis, & compendij facultatum Societatis, atque ex observatione consuetudinum receptarum, denique ex recursu ad Superiorem in ijs, de quibus dubitabit.
units.tr: 18. Let him learn the Institute of the Society from reading the Apostolic letters, the Constitutions, and the Decrees of the General Congregations; but more particularly from reading the rules, both the common ones and those of his own office and of the others who are under his care, as well as those of the Provincial, and the compendium of the faculties of the Society; and from observing the customs that have been received; and finally from recourse to the Superior in those matters about which he is in doubt.

units.la: 19. Libellum habeat, in quem referat quæcunque sibi ad bonum Domus statum subinde occurrent, ne memoria excidant, præcipue illa, de quibus ad Generalem, vel Provincialem scribendum putat.
units.tr: 19. Let him have a little book in which he notes down whatever occurs from time to time concerning the good state of the House, so that it does not slip from memory, especially those things about which he thinks he should write to the General or the Provincial.

units.la: 20. Pro occurrentibus necessitatibus communibus, & privatis, Missas, & orationes eorum (moderate tamen) iuxta consuetudinem Societatis applicare poterit.
units.tr: 20. For the needs that arise, both common and private, he may apply Masses and prayers for them (in moderation, however) according to the custom of the Society.

units.la: DE CVRA NOSTRORVM IN SPIRITV
units.tr: Concerning the Care of Our Men in Spirit

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: 21. CVret, ut unicuique in suo officio integram obedientiam cateri præstent, & officiales, Ministro, & sibi etiam omnes: studeatque eisdem exemplo obedientiæ præire, quam se suis Superioribus, quos Christi loco habet, præstare debet.
units.tr: 21. He shall see to it that all the others, and the officials, and the minister himself, render full obedience each in his own office; and he himself should strive to go before them in the example of obedience, which he ought to render to his own Superiors, whom he holds in the place of Christ.

units.la: 22. Det operam, ut Constitutiones, & regulæ observentur: omnibus domesticis cum omni solicitudine invigilet, eosdemque ab ijs, quæ nocere possint domi, & foris defendat, cum accedendo, tum etiam, si quid mali acciderit, remedium adhibendo.
units.tr: 22. He shall take care that the Constitutions and rules are observed; he shall watch over all the household members with every diligence, and defend them from whatever could harm them at home or abroad, both by approaching them and, if any evil has happened, by applying a remedy.

units.la: 23. Efficiat, ut sibi, vel alijs ab ipso deputatis statis temporibus ratio conscientiæ reddatur, iuxta modum, qui in officio Provincialis præscribitur, & instructionem reddendam conscientiæ rationem, à Profeßis quidem, & Coadiutoribus formatis semel in anno, ab aliis vero bis: & aliquos præterea maturiores Patres aßignet, qui eorum confeßiones generales excipiant, nisi Provincialis tunc adßit.
units.tr: 23. He shall arrange that an account of conscience is rendered to himself, or to others assigned by him, at set times, according to the manner prescribed in the office of the Provincial, and the instruction for rendering an account of conscience: the professed and the formed coadjutors once a year, the others twice; and he shall moreover assign some older Fathers who shall hear their general confessions, unless the Provincial is then present.

units.la: 24. Meminerit, ut Scholastici, si qui erunt, & Coadiutores non formati, bis singulis annis circa festa Circumcisionis Domini nostri, & Apostolorum Petri & Pauli vota sua renovent, præmissis ijs, quæ fieri solent.
units.tr: 24. He shall remember that the scholastics, if there are any, and the unformed coadjutors, twice in each year, around the feasts of the Circumcision of our Lord and of the Apostles Peter and Paul, renew their vows, with the customary preliminaries premised.

units.la: 25. Singulis, vel alternis diebus Veneris exhortationem nostris vel ipse faciat, vel aliquis alius, qui rationem nostri instituti bene teneat; in qua agatur de observatione Constitutionum, & regularum; de fraterna charitate, humilitate, patientia, mortificatione, & aliis virtutibus, præsertim de obedientia: tametsi exhortationis loco, spiritualis collatio eisdem de rebus aliquando haberi potest.
units.tr: 25. Either every day or every other day on Friday, he himself or some other who understands our Institute well shall give an exhortation to our men; in which there is to be discussion of the observance of the Constitutions and rules, of brotherly charity, humility, patience, mortification, and the other virtues, especially obedience; although, in place of an exhortation, a spiritual conference on these same matters may sometimes be held for them.

units.la: 26. Crebrò, & magna charitatis significatione alloquatur subditos, eorumque necessitatibus non corporis tantum; sed multò etiam magis animæ, paterno affectu prospiciat. Si quem vero intelligat aliqua tentatione pulsari, præsertim gravi, eius peculiarem curam & solicitudinem non solum per se, sed etiam, si necesse fuerit, per alios gerat: nec remedium longius differendo, difficiliorem morbi curationem reddat.
units.tr: 26. He shall address his subjects often and with great signs of charity, and attend with paternal affection to their needs, not only of body but much more of soul. If he understands that anyone is assailed by some temptation, especially a grave one, he shall take particular care and concern for him, not only himself but also, if necessary, through others; and by delaying the remedy he shall not make the cure of the illness more difficult.

units.la: 27. In correctionibus, & pœnitentijs iniungendis rationem habebit dispositionis personarum, & ædificationis universalis, & particularis earum, ad gloriam Dei.
units.tr: 27. In imposing corrections and penances he shall take account of the disposition of the persons, and of their edification, universal and particular, for the glory of God.

units.la: 28. Nisi prudentia rebus particularibus adhibita aliter procedendum dixerit, illud in correctionibus observet, ut ij, qui peccant, primò in charitate, & dulcedine admoneantur: secundò in charitate quidem, sed eo tamen modo, ut eis confusio, & rubor iniiciatur; tertiò amori, ea quæ timorem incutiant, si opus erit, adijciantur.
units.tr: 28. Unless prudence, applied to particular matters, has said that one should proceed otherwise, he shall observe in corrections that those who sin are admonished, first, in charity and gentleness; second, in charity indeed, but in such a way that confusion and shame are brought upon them; third, if the matter requires it, those things which strike fear are added to love.

units.la: 29. De publicis defectibus, publica debet esse pœnitentia; ijs tantum, quæ ad omnium ædificationem faciunt, declaratis.
units.tr: 29. For public defects the penance must be public; and only those things which bear upon the edification of all are to be declared.

units.la: 30. Poterit mittere interdum aliquem ex suis, ut ostiatim petat eleemosynam, aut ut inserviat hospitali, aut comitetur emptorem, aut in plateis concionetur, Christianam venerabilem doctrinam doceat, prout magis in Domino expedire videbitur, habita ratione ædificationis, & spiritualis utilitatis nostrorum.
units.tr: 31. He may sometimes send one of his men to beg alms from door to door, or to serve in a hospital, or to accompany a buyer, or to preach in the squares and teach Christian venerable doctrine, as seems more expedient in the Lord, taking account of the edification and spiritual profit of our men.

units.la: 31. Delegare poterit Confessario, vel alijs vices suas, ut eas pœnitentias approbent, vel improbent, quas ad maiores sui spiritus professum, assumere quisq; volet. Et, ut nostris, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, facultatem dare possint frequentius quam octavo quoq; die communicandi, quos ea ratione magis in spiritu iuvari in Domino iudicaverint.
units.tr: 31. He may delegate his powers to the Confessor, or to others, to approve or disapprove those penances which each one wishes to undertake for the greater profit of his spirit. And he may give to our men who are not priests the faculty of communicating more often than every eighth day, those whom they have judged to be helped more in spirit in the Lord by this means.

units.la: 32. In danda facultate ieiunandi, sicut & in alijs pœnitentijs concedendis, videat, ne mensuram rectæ rationis excedat: detq; operam, ut omnes intelligant, ad singularitatem non pertinere, si quis ieiunet alijs non ieiunantibus; dummodo ordinaria consuetudo ieiunandi, quæ iuxta Constitutiones non sit, non introducatur.
units.tr: 32. In granting the faculty of fasting, as also in granting other penances, he shall see that he does not exceed the measure of right reason; and he shall take care that all understand that it is not singularity if someone fasts while others do not fast; provided that the ordinary custom of fasting, which is not according to the Constitutions, is not introduced.

units.la: 33. Vnio, & conformitas mutua diligentissimè curanda est, nec ferenda inter ullos domesticorum perturbatio, vel ira mutua: si quid autem huiusmodi acciderèt, curet, ut statim cum satisfactione debita in gratiam invicem redeant.
units.tr: 33. Union and mutual conformity are to be cultivated most diligently, and no disturbance or mutual anger among the household members is to be tolerated; if anything of this kind should happen, he shall see that they are at once reconciled to one another with due satisfaction.

units.la: 34. Tam ipse, quàm omnes alij Sacerdotes, qui ei videbuntur, iuxta Constitutiones, aliquando intra annum officium, vel officia eorum, qui domi inserviunt, ad tempus aliquod obibunt.
units.tr: 34. He himself, as well as all the other priests whom he thinks fit, shall at some time within the year, according to the Constitutions, take on for a period of time the office or offices of those who serve at home.

units.la: 35. Videat scripta, & literas omnes, quæ scribuntur ad domesticos, & quas ipsi alij scribunt, aut aliquem virum fidelem, & qui donum discretionis habeat, domi constituat, qui eas literas reddat, aut non reddat, prout in Domino magis expedire iudicabit, sibiq; referat, si quid inveenerit, quod tanti momenti sit, ut de eo Superior monendus videatur. Res autem vanas, aut quà alia ratione offendere possint, neminem scribere permittat: nec si quillum quenquam habere sinat sine Provincialis facultate.
units.tr: 35. He shall see all the writings and letters that are written to the household members, and those that they themselves write, or he shall appoint at home some faithful man who has the gift of discernment, who shall either deliver those letters or not deliver them, as he shall judge more expedient in the Lord, and report to him if he finds anything of such weight that the Superior seems to need to be warned about it. He shall not permit anyone to write vain things, or things that could give offence in any other way; nor shall he allow anyone to have any such thing without the Provincial's permission.

units.la: 36. Non sint domi arma, nec instrumenta musica, nec libri lascivi, aut vani, nec nova ... recreationes introducantur.
units.tr: 36. There shall be no weapons at home, nor musical instruments, nor wanton or vain books, nor shall new recreations be introduced.

units.la: DE AVXILIO ANIMARVM. CAPVT IV.
units.tr: ON HELP FOR SOULS. CHAPTER IV.

units.la: 7. MEminerit hoc pertinere ad scopum totius Societatis, ut ad animarum salutem & perfectionem cum divina gratia promovendam incumbat, & nostri instituti veritate in Domibus professis praecipue elucescere debere, quae non tam circa media ad hunc finem praeparanda (quemadmodum Collegia) quam circa finem ipsum, & usum mediorum ad eum conferentium versantur.
units.tr: 7. Let him remember that it pertains to the aim of the whole Society to labour for the salvation and perfection of souls, with divine grace promoted; and that the truth of our Institute ought to shine forth especially in the professed Houses, which concern not so much the means to be prepared for this end (as the Colleges do) as the end itself and the use of the means conducive to it.

units.la: 38. Videat, an nostri zelum habeant animarum, & an strenuè, ac diligenter earum salutem procurent, ut ii solent, quos sanctus Dei amor impellit, nec solum immoderatos pro ratione virium labores suscipi non sinat, sed multo etiam minus in proximus invandis negligentiam tolleret.
units.tr: 38. Let him see whether our men have zeal for souls, and whether they procure their salvation earnestly and diligently, as those usually do whom the holy love of God impels. He should not only not allow immoderate labours beyond their strength to be undertaken, but much less should he tolerate negligence in helping neighbours.

units.la: 39. Proponatur populo assiduè in Ecclesia verbum Dei in praedicationibus, & sacrae Scripturae vel doctrinae Christianae lectionibus, quod etiam in aliis Ecclesiis, plateis, & locis praestari potest, quando ad maiorem Dei gloriam conferre videbitur: nominatim verò verorum, & rudium personarum in Christianismo institutionem tanquam propriam nostrae vocationis ministerium valdè commendatum habeat: intelligatque Christianam doctrinam tanendo doceri posse, ubi ad maiorem aedificationem id fore observabitur. Modus autem sive id canendo, sive secus fiat, pro locorum ratione ad aedificationem & maiorem utilitatem exigatur.
units.tr: 39. Let the word of God be set before the people constantly in the Church, in sermons and in readings of Holy Scripture or of Christian doctrine; this may also be done in other churches, squares and places, when it seems to be conducive to God's greater glory. Especially let him hold the instruction of true and ignorant persons in Christianity as a ministry particularly commended to our calling; and let him understand that Christian doctrine can be taught by singing, where it will be observed to be for greater edification. The manner, whether it is done by singing or otherwise, is to be adapted to the circumstances of place for edification and greater usefulness.

units.la: 40. Procuret diligenter nec desint designati Confessarij, qui domi in administratione Sacramentorum confessionis & communionis cum fructu exerceantur: quique extra domum aegrotorum confessiones audire, moriientibus opem ferre, & eos, qui in carceribus, & hospitalibus inveniuntur, visitare, & consolari possint, & reliquis pietatis operibus, quae in literis Apostolicis instituti nostri, & constitutionibus proponuntur, incumbere: sed haec omnia ipse iuxta ordinem à Provinciali praescriptum exequatur, qui pro ratione loci, & conditionum nostrorum metietur, quantum in huiusmodi rebus operae fit ponendum.
units.tr: 40. Let him take diligent care that designated confessors are not lacking, who may be employed at home in administering the sacraments of confession and communion with fruit; and who can hear confessions outside the house, bring help to the dying, visit and console those who are found in prisons and hospitals, and apply themselves to the other works of piety set out in the apostolic letters of our Institute and in the Constitutions. But let him himself carry out all these things according to the order prescribed by the Provincial, who will measure, according to the circumstances of place and of our conditions, how much effort is to be put into such matters.

units.la: 41. Curet, ut nostri in spiritualibus exercitijs tradendis accurate exerceantur, postquam in se fuerint experti: nullus tamen deberet ea tradere, nisi prudentia, ac rerum spiritualium usu satis probatus esset.
units.tr: 41. Let him see that our men are carefully trained in giving the spiritual exercises, after they have experienced them themselves; yet no one ought to give them unless he has been sufficiently proved in prudence and in experience of spiritual things.

units.la: 42. Si operariorum copia suppetet, poterit suos mittere ad alia loca vicina, habito consensu Provincialis, ut similibus operibus charitatis functi, domum, constituto tempore, redeant.
units.tr: 42. If there is a sufficient supply of workers, he may send his men to other nearby places, with the consent of the Provincial, so that, having performed such works of charity, they may return home at an appointed time.

units.la: 43. Non permittat eodem tempore omnes Sacerdotes abesse, sed semper domi, aut in Ecclesia aliqui maneant, qui occurrentibus necessitatibus proximorum satisfacere possint.
units.tr: 43. Let him not allow all the priests to be absent at the same time, but let some always remain at home or in the church who can meet the needs of neighbours as they arise.

units.la: 44. Cum quis praedicationi, lectioni sacrae, aut confessionibus audiendis vacat, provideat, ne studij tempus, aliaveque necessaria illi desint.
units.tr: 44. When someone is devoted to preaching, sacred reading, or hearing confessions, let him provide that he does not lack time for study and other necessary things.

units.la: 45. Si quis ad sacros ordines promovendus, aut in confessarium, vel concionatorem esse eligendus videbitur, Provincialem admoneat.
units.tr: 45. If anyone seems fit to be promoted to holy orders, or to be chosen as confessor or preacher, let him advise the Provincial.

units.la: 46. Si quem ex iis, qui in Ecclesia nostra assiduè ad Sacramenta accedunt, intelligeret vitae suae exemplo alios offendere, quantum in ipso est, remedium per confessarium, vel alium cuem alium conveniente ratione adhibere curet.
units.tr: 46. If he should learn that someone among those who frequently approach the sacraments in our church gives offence to others by the example of his life, let him take care to apply a remedy, as far as lies in him, through the confessor or some other suitable means.

units.la: 47. Non permittat, ut nostri curam mulierum religiosarum, & aliarum quarumcunque suscipiant, ut ordinarie illarum confessiones audiant, vel ipsas regant: quamvis nihil repugnet aliquando apud eas concionari, aut semel unius Monasterij confessiones speciales ob causas audire, quod tamen non fiet, nisi postulent ij, qui eis praesunt.
units.tr: 47. Let him not permit our men to take up the care of religious women or of any others whatever, so as to hear their confessions regularly or to direct them; although there is nothing against preaching to them at times, or hearing the special confessions of one convent once, for particular reasons; which, however, shall not be done unless those who govern them ask for it.

units.la: 48. Etsi proprium Praepositi officium est, Domum sibi commissam diligenter, & fideliter gubernare, neque is propter aliud quidquam huic muneri deesse debet: si quando tamen per officij sui occupationes licebit, & concionari, & confessiones audire, & alia Societatis ministeria exercere poterit, ac debebit.
units.tr: 48. Although it is the proper office of the Superior to govern the house entrusted to him diligently and faithfully, and he must lack nothing in this duty on account of anything else; yet if at any time the occupations of his office allow, he can and ought also to preach, hear confessions, and exercise the other ministries of the Society.

units.la: E
units.tr: E

units.la: REGVLÆ DE ORDINE DOMESTICO.
units.tr: RULES CONCERNING DOMESTIC ORDER.

units.la: CAPVT V.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: 49. Quotidie post orationem matutinam fiat sacrum, cui intersint omnes, qui Sacerdotes non sunt: nisi aliquibus propter peculiares causas aliud tempus ad sacrum audiendum concessum sit.
units.tr: 49. Every day, after morning prayer, Mass shall be celebrated, and all who are not priests shall attend, unless for particular reasons another time has been allowed for hearing Mass for some of them.

units.la: 50. Tempore orationi, et examini assignato, sit aliquis, qui observet, ne omnes ijs vacent, quod et Minister ipse aliquando faciat, et Præpositus huic rei diligenter invigilet.
units.tr: 50. At the time assigned for prayer and examination, someone shall be appointed to observe that no one is idle; the Minister himself sometimes does this, and the Superior shall diligently see to the matter.

units.la: 51. Syndicum domi constituat, ubi Ministri aut Subministri opera ad id non interetur, cuius officium erit observare in omnibus quod ad honestatem, et decentiam externam pertinet, Ecclesiam, et domum in loco publico perlustrando, et si quid, quod non conveniat, annotaverit, Superiori referendo.
units.tr: 51. He shall appoint a syndic for the house, where the work of the Minister or Subminister is not involved, whose duty will be to observe in all things what pertains to honesty and outward decency; he is to go round the church and the house in public places and, if he notices anything unbecoming, report it to the Superior.

units.la: 52. A posteriore prandij signo ad cœnam, otto ut minimum horæ intersint: aliquid vero amplius usque ad refectiunculam vespertinam diebus Veneris, et ieiuniorum, iuxta morem regionis, a tempore autem, quo se nostri cubitum receperunt usque ad signum, quod excitantur, septem.
units.tr: 52. From the sign for the afternoon meal to supper, there shall be at least eight hours; on Fridays and on fast days, however, a little evening refreshment may be taken, according to the custom of the region, and from the time when our men retire to bed until the sign to rise, seven hours.

units.la: 53. Benedictio, et gratiarum actio in refectorio iuxta usum breviarij Romani in prima mensa fiant: in secunda vero, et privata, teneri possunt antiqua benedictio, et gratiarum actio, quæ a singulis submisse, et stando fieri debent.
units.tr: 53. The blessing and thanksgiving at table shall be made in the refectory according to the use of the Roman Breviary at the first table; at the second and private table, the old blessing and thanksgiving may be retained, which each person should say quietly and standing.

units.la: 54. In mensa Sacerdotes præcedant alios ad eum gradum non promotos: sed nec inter Sacerdotes, nec inter eos, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ullus ordo constituatur.
units.tr: 54. At table, priests shall precede the others who have not been promoted to that rank; but no order shall be established either among the priests or among those who are not priests.

units.la: 55. Si aliqua de causa Præpositus prima mensa adesse non poterit, curet, ut Minister adsit.
units.tr: 55. If for some reason the Superior cannot be present at the first table, he shall see to it that the Minister is present.

units.la: 56. A prandio et a cœna hora una: diebus autem Veneris post collationem vespertinam dimidia recreationi religiose impendantur, idq; in uno loco, si commode fieri poterit: sed neque extra huiusmodi horas labores nimium continuari, sine aliqua convenienti relaxatione, sinat.
units.tr: 56. One hour shall be devoted to recreation after dinner and after supper; on Fridays, half an hour after the evening conference, and this religiously and in one place, if it can conveniently be done. Nor shall labours be continued too long outside these hours without some suitable relaxation.

units.la: 57. Conferentia casuum conscientiæ bis singulis hebdomadis habeantur, quibus Sacerdotes omnes, qui commode poterunt, interesse debent: Præside docto aliquo, qui ea, de quibus agetur, luculentius explicare, ac definire possit.
units.tr: 57. Conferences on cases of conscience shall be held twice a week, which all priests who can conveniently attend must join; a learned president shall preside, who is able to explain and settle more clearly the matters to be discussed.

units.la: DE IIS, QVÆ PERTINENT AD RES TEMPORALES.
units.tr: On Those Things That Pertain to Temporal Matters.

units.la: CAPVT VI.
units.tr: Chapter VI.

units.la: 58. Magno, et constanti animo speret a divina bonitate suæ Domui subsidia temporalia adijcienda, si et nostri ad quærendum Dei regnum sibi, et proximis serio incumbant, et ipse ratione indigentiæ, instituti nostri integritatem violari numquam permittat.
units.tr: 58. With a great and steadfast spirit let him hope that temporal aid will be added to his House by divine goodness, provided that our members earnestly devote themselves both to seeking God's kingdom and to the good of their neighbours, and that he himself, on account of need, never allows the integrity of our Institute to be violated.

units.la: 59. Habeat procuratorem, qui eleemosynas petat, cui alios ad eam rem substituere poterit, si necessarium iudicabit, ita tamen, ut quam paucissimi in mendicando occupentur.
units.tr: 59. Let him have a procurator who will seek alms, and he may substitute others for this task if he judges it necessary, provided that as few as possible are occupied in begging.

units.la: 60. Singulis mensibus a Procuratore ratione accepti, et expensi præsente Ministro exigat, ut totius Domus administrationis ratio ipsi constet, eamq; reddere possit cui, et quando per Superiorem constituetur: caveat autem, ne Domus alieno ære gravetur.
units.tr: 60. Every month let him require from the Procurator an account of receipts and expenses, in the presence of the Minister, so that he himself may know the whole management of the House and be able to render that account to whom and when the Superior appoints. He must take care, however, that the House is not burdened with debt.

units.la: 61. In ijs, quæ ad rationem victus, et aliarum rerum vitæ necessariarum, aut convenientium spectant, quam vis curandum est, ut communis illa fit, et valetudini nostrorum accommodata: habenda tamen semper est ratio humilitatis, paupertatis, ac spiritualis aedificationis in Domino.
units.tr: 61. Although care must be taken that the arrangements for food and the other necessities or conveniences of life are common and suited to our members' health, the consideration of humility, poverty and spiritual edification in the Lord must always be kept in view.

units.la: 62. Ut curare debet, ne ij, qui in vinea Domini magno cum proximorum fructu se exercent, necessario subsidio privati maiora bona relinquere cogantur, neve morbo, aut ætate debiles ministerio fraterna charitatis destituantur: ita ijs, qui nostra ratione aliorum indigent opera, adiutores assignare non debet. 63. Aegrotorum vero cura habeatur magna, & observetur diligenter tam in victus ratione, quàm in caeteris quod medicus praescripserit.
units.tr: 62. He must take care that those who exercise themselves in the Lord's vineyard with great benefit to their neighbours are not compelled, for want of private support, to forgo greater goods, nor be deprived through sickness or age of the fraternal charity of ministry. Likewise, he should not assign helpers to those who by our rule need the work of others. 63. Moreover, the care of the sick is to be great, and what the physician has prescribed is to be observed diligently, both in diet and in all other matters.

units.la: 64. Si cui particulari quidpiam ab externo aliquo mittatur, id in communem usum accipiatur, ac dispensetur.
units.tr: 64. If anything is sent from some outsider to a particular member, it shall be received and distributed for common use.

units.la: 65. Caveat, ne Domus ipsa, aliusve Professorum, aut Coadiutorum redditibus Collegiorum, praeterquam in rebus minimis utatur.
units.tr: 65. Let him take care that the House itself, or any of the Professed or Coadjutors, does not use the revenues of the colleges except in the smallest matters.

units.la: 66. Si quid stabile donatum, legatumve Domui fuerit, Provincialem admoneat, ut quam primum vendatur, & pretium in usus necessarios iuxta illius iudicium expendatur: temporis tamen opportunitas ad vendendum non est excludenda.
units.tr: 66. If any fixed property is given or bequeathed to the House, let him advise the Provincial that it be sold as soon as possible, and that the price be spent on necessary uses according to his judgment. Nevertheless, the opportunity of time for selling is not to be excluded.

units.la: 67. Lites forenses fugiat, nec ullam inconsulto Provinciali intentet, nec intentae respondeat, nisi cogatur.
units.tr: 67. Let him avoid lawsuits, and without the Provincial's advice let him bring none, nor answer one brought against him, unless he is compelled.

units.la: 68. Si bona alicuius ex nostris distribuenda essent, si ineundi contractus, si fabrica alicuius momenti, & expensae extraordinariae faciendae, aut si bona offerantur cum aliqua obligatione, rem ad Provincialem deferat.
units.tr: 68. If the goods of any of ours are to be distributed, if contracts are to be entered into, if a building of some importance is to be made, or extraordinary expenses incurred, or if goods are offered with some obligation attached, he is to refer the matter to the Provincial.

units.la: 69. Depositum pecuniae nullum prorsus admittat: aliarum vero rerum non nisi cautissime, dummodo sint eorum, quibus multum debeamus, aut alioqui id officii sine magna offensione, denegari non possit.
units.tr: 69. He must absolutely admit no deposit of money. Of other things he may accept them only with the greatest caution, provided they belong to those to whom we owe much, or else such a duty cannot be refused without great offence.

units.la: 70. Neminem ex nostris in causis civilibus, nedum criminalibus examinari (nisi, qui peccatum obligare potest, compelleret) permittat absque licentia, quam minime dabit, nisi in causis, quae ad religionem Catholicam pertinent, aut alioqui piae sint, & itanni faveant, et non in alterius detrimentum cedant.
units.tr: 70. He must not permit anyone of ours to be examined in civil causes, much less in criminal ones (unless someone who can bind him by sin compels him), without permission. He will give this very rarely, only in causes that pertain to the Catholic religion or are otherwise pious, which favour the faith and do not turn to the detriment of another.

units.la: 71. Nullum domi iumentum equitandi causa ad usum alicuius de ipsa Societate ordinarie habeatur, nisi aut propter continenter infirmam alicuius valetudinem, aut propter publica negotia, id necessarium, & urgens iudicaret Generalis.
units.tr: 71. No beast of burden for riding is ordinarily to be kept for the use of any member of the Society in the house, unless the General judges it necessary and urgent, either because of someone's continually weak health or because of public business.

units.la: DE COMMVNICATIONE CVM EXTERNIS ET GRA- TITUDINE ERGA FVNDATORES, ET BE- NEFACTORES.
units.tr: CONCERNING INTERCOURSE WITH OUTSIDERS, AND GRATITUDE TOWARDS FOUNDERS AND BENEFACTORS.

units.la: CAP. VII.
units.tr: CHAP. VII.

units.la: 1. Mulieres invisere, aut ad eas scribere, nisi in necessitate, aut cum spe magni fructus, nostros non sinat, nec hoc quidem permittat, nisi viris valde probatis, & rudentibus.
units.tr: 1. He shall not allow ours to visit women or write to them, except in necessity or with hope of great fruit; and he shall not even permit this unless to men who are very approved and mature.

units.la: 73. Non permittat foeminas domum nostram ingredi.
units.tr: 73. He shall not permit women to enter our house.

units.la: 74. Curet, ne primarios viros invisere nostri consuescant, nisi sanctô studio piorum operam ducerentur, vel quando intima benevolentia in Domino coniunctí essent.
units.tr: 74. He shall take care that ours do not make a habit of visiting leading men, unless they are engaged in the holy work of the pious, or when they are bound together in the Lord by close goodwill.

units.la: 75. Non sinat offerri munuscula, quae magnatibus ad res maiores obtinendas offerre solent.
units.tr: 75. He shall not allow small gifts to be offered, such as men usually offer to great persons in order to obtain greater things.

units.la: 76. Non permittat, ut nostri cibum capiant apud externos: aut ab eis, cum aegrotant, visitentur, nisi causa non levis momenti ad id concedendum moveret, quam eandem esse oportebit, si quando externus aliquis ad mensam praesertim refectorij, invitandus videtur.
units.tr: 76. He shall not permit ours to take food at the houses of outsiders, nor to be visited by them when they are sick, unless some matter of no small weight should move him to grant this; and this same reason will have to exist if at any time some outsider seems to be invited, especially to the table of the refectory.

units.la: 77. Amicos conservare, & eos, qui male erga nos affecti sunt, praecipue si homines sint non vulgaris auctoritatis, orationibus & rationibus convenientibus in amicitiam revocare, aut saltem, ne adversarij sint, efficere studeat.
units.tr: 77. He shall take care to keep friends, and to win back by fitting words and arguments into friendship those who are ill disposed towards us, especially if they are men of no ordinary authority; or at least to see that they are not adversaries.

units.la: 78. Observet, quae erga fundatores, & benefactores, tam vivos, quam mortuos observanda sunt, eisque gratitudinem exhibeat, & si quam aliam obligationem habet, ei satisfaciat curet.
units.tr: 78. He shall observe what is to be observed towards founders and benefactors, both living and dead, and shall show them gratitude, and shall see to it that he satisfies any other obligation he has to them.

units.la: REGVLÆ DE IIS, QVI ADMITTI PETVNT, AD DOMVM DIVERTVNT, AVT FORAS MIT- TVNTVR.
units.tr: RULES CONCERNING THOSE WHO SEEK ADMISSION AND WHO LODGE IN THE HOUSE OR ARE SENT AWAY.

units.la: CAPVT VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: 79. IN Societatem neminem admittat, nisi à Generali, vel Provinciali id ipsi committatur, sed de iis, qui admitti petunt, ad Provincialem referat, vel scribat, quales illi sint, & quibus domus Dei præditi.
units.tr: 79. No one is to admit anyone into the Society unless this has been specifically entrusted to him by the General or the Provincial. Concerning those who seek admission, he shall report or write to the Provincial, describing what sort of men they are and what gifts of God's house they have.

units.la: 80. Si is, qui admitti petit, ad institutum Societatis valdè idoneus videbitur, & necessitas urgeret, poterit eum tanquam hospitem domi recipere, donec responsum à Provinciali accipiat, vel ad eundem mittere, si expedire iudicaverit.
units.tr: 80. If the man seeking admission seems very well suited to the Society's way of life, and necessity presses, he may receive him at home as a guest until he gets a reply from the Provincial, or send him to the Provincial if he judges it expedient.

units.la: 81. Recedentem sine licentia ab alio loco Societatis, vel ab ea dimissum non admittat, sed si expedire videatur ad Provincialem de eo scribat, & eius ordinationem expectet, illum domi ut hospitem, vel in alio pio loco, si videbitur detento.
units.tr: 81. He is not to admit anyone who has left another house of the Society without permission, or who has been dismissed by it. Rather, if it seems advisable, he shall write to the Provincial about him and await his decision, keeping him at home as a guest, or in another pious place if that seems good, under restraint.

units.la: 82. Charitatem magnam exhibeat erga alios de Societate per domum transeuntes, eosque amanter hospitio excipiat, ac meminerit, si aliquo viatico, aut eleemosyna eos, si indigerent, juvare posse: curet item diligenter dirigere, ac juvare expeditiones hospitum, qui negotiorum causa domi versantur.
units.tr: 82. He is to show great charity toward other members of the Society who pass through the house, and welcome them kindly. He should remember that he can help them with some provision for the journey or with alms if they are in need. He is also to take care to direct diligently and to assist the arrangements of guests who are staying at home on business.

units.la: 83. Externi nisi accipiantur hospitio, ut domi pernoctent, nisi ij sint, quibus multum deberatur, aut id officij sine magna offensione prætermitti non possit: quia in re habeatur praecipua ratio religiosorum, cum necessitatis causa ad nos divertunt.
units.tr: 83. Outsiders are not to be received to spend the night at home, unless they are people to whom we owe much, or unless this kindness cannot be omitted without great offence. In this matter, special consideration is to be shown to religious, since they turn aside to us out of necessity.

units.la: 84. Cum quis domo egredietur, det ei socium convenientem: si quando autem aliquis foras mittitur, is sit, cui merito possit confidere.
units.tr: 84. When someone is going out of the house, he shall give him a suitable companion. If anyone is sent out, he should be one in whom the superior may rightly place confidence.

units.la: 85. Neminem ex sua Domo in alium locum mittat sine literis patentibus.
units.tr: 85. He is not to send anyone from his house to another place without letters patent.

units.la: 86. Si quis experimento comperiretur ferre non posse domus cælum, & male habere con-tinenter cerneretur, vel alia ratione videretur mutandus, Provincialem admoneat, an alio mitti debeat.
units.tr: 86. If anyone is found by experience to be unable to bear the climate of the house, or is seen to be continually unwell, or otherwise seems to need a change, he is to advise the Provincial whether he ought to be sent elsewhere.

units.la: 87. Profecturi ad alia loca ea, quam fottanam vocant, & in alijs interioribus indumentis, quibus utuntur, privari non debent, nisi forte ratio temporis, aut alioqui charitas suadeat melioribus esse commutanda. Reliqua vero omnia, quæ ad iter necessaria erunt, magna charitatis significatione ab eo loco, unde mittuntur, subministrentur, sumptibus tamen eorum, quorum erit expensas itineris solvere.
units.tr: 87. Those who are going to other places should not be deprived of what they call the sottana, or of the other inner garments they use, unless perhaps the season or charity itself suggests that they should be exchanged for better ones. All the other things that will be necessary for the journey are to be supplied with great kindness from the place from which they are sent, though at the expense of those who are to pay the travel costs.

units.la: REGVLÆ RECTORIS, DE IIS, QVÆ AD EIVS PERSONAM, ET TOTIVS COLLEGII ADMINISTRATIONEM PERTINENT.
units.tr: RULES OF THE RECTOR, CONCERNING THOSE THINGS WHICH PERTAIN TO HIS PERSON AND TO THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE WHOLE COLLEGE.

units.la: CAPVT PRIMVM.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: 1. OMnis studio enitatur, ut talis sit, qualis optatur in nostris Constitutionibus; primamque officij sui cutam in eo positam esse intelligat, ut oratione, & sanctis desideriis totum Collegium velut humeris suis sustineat.
units.tr: 1. Let him take every care to be such as is wished for in our Constitutions; and let him understand that the chief part of his office lies in this: that by prayer and holy desires he bears up the whole College, as it were, on his shoulders.

units.la: 2. Communes Regulas ipse servet, & particularia in cibo, indumentis, & aliarum rerum usu, quantum fieri potest, vitet: & familiaritate, atque indulgentia cum quibusdam, alios ne offendat.
units.tr: 2. Let him keep the common rules himself, and, as far as possible, avoid particular practices in food, clothing and the use of other things; and let him not offend others by familiarity or indulgence towards certain individuals.

units.la: 3.
