Intra annum postquam officiû Rectoris prima vice inierit, quadraginta diebus Christianam doctrinam eo modo, quo in secunda congregatione expositum est, legat, aut doceat: sed ex causa per alium id munus cum facultate Provincialis obire poterit. 4. Consuetudines receptas, & à Generali, vel Provinciali approbatas servet, ac servari faciat: Si tamen aliqua alia à præcedenti Rectore inducta fuerit, non mutet in consulto Provinciali: ipse vero, nisi suo Superiore approbante, nullam introducat.
units.tr: 3. Within a year after he first takes up the office of Rector, he is to read or teach Christian doctrine for forty days, in the manner set out in the second congregation; but for a good reason he may discharge this duty through another, with the permission of the Provincial. 4. Let him keep, and see kept, the customs received and approved by the General or the Provincial. If some other custom has been introduced by the previous Rector, he is not to change it without consulting the Provincial; and he himself is not to introduce any new one unless his own Superior approves.

units.la: 5. Eos, qui domestica obeunt ministeria (exceptis quibusdam, quorum electio ad Provinciale pertinet) prudenter constituat, suas cuique regulas tradat, aliquando visitet, & rout in Domino convenire iudicabit, vel in eisdem ministerijs detineat, vel ab eis removeat. Quia vero officia quædam, ut bene fiant, experientiam requirunt, qui ad ea idonei inveniuntur, non facile mutari debebunt.
units.tr: 5. Let him appoint prudently those who perform domestic ministries (with the exception of certain posts whose choice belongs to the Provincial), give each one his own rules, visit them from time to time, and either keep them in those same ministries or remove them from them, as he judges fitting in the Lord. But since certain offices require experience in order to be done well, those who are found fit for them should not readily be changed.

units.la: 6. Vt prospicere officialibus de subsidio, si necessarium id fuerit, ne labore graventur, debebit: ita cum tempus vacuum illis fuerit, ut utiliter illud impendant divino servitio curabit.
units.tr: 6. He shall take care to provide help for the officials, if this is needed, so that they are not burdened by labour; and when they have free time, he shall see that they spend it usefully in divine service.

units.la: 7. Etsi potestatem habet designandi Confessarios suis subditis, ordinarium tamen Confessarium Collegij non constituet sine approbatione Provincialis.
units.tr: 7. Although he has the power to assign confessors to his subjects, he shall not appoint an ordinary confessor for the College without the approval of the Provincial.

units.la: 8. Quamvis in virtute obedientiæ iubere possit, non nisi rarissime, & ex gravi, ac urgenti causa id faciat.
units.tr: 8. Although he may command in virtue of obedience, let him do so only very rarely, and for a grave and urgent reason.

units.la: 9. Ordinarias tantum pœnitentias imponat, quales sunt parva mensa, publica reprehensio, conclusio in circulo, edere sub mensa, osculari aliorum pedes, orare in refectorio, dicere culpam suam, subtractio cibi usque ad panem & aquam, si res postulaverit, disciplina publica in refectorio, & alia exercitia humilia & domestica.
units.tr: 9. Let him impose only ordinary penances, such as eating at the small table, public reproof, remaining in the circle, eating under the table, kissing the feet of others, praying in the refectory, confessing his fault aloud, withdrawal of food down to bread and water if the matter requires it, public discipline in the refectory, and other humble and domestic exercises.

units.la: 10. Sicut ad Rectorem pertinet dispensare in Regulis, Constitutionibus, & Decretis Congregationum generalium cum particularibus quando necesse erit: sic & cum dispensaveit in rebus maioris momenti, quæ videntur urgere; & in quibus sine gravi incommodo Provincialis responsum expectari non potest, eum primo quoque tempore de huiusmodi dispensatione, ac eius causa admonere.
units.tr: 10. Just as it belongs to the Rector to dispense from the Rules, Constitutions and Decrees of the General Congregations with individuals when it is necessary, so too, when he has dispensed in matters of greater moment, which seem urgent, and in which a reply from the Provincial cannot be awaited without serious inconvenience, he is to inform the Provincial of such dispensation and its reason at the earliest opportunity.

units.la: 11. Nomina eorum, qui vota solemnia, vel simplicia emiserunt, in libro ad hoc parato notentur: in Professis quidem, & Coadiutoribus formatis cum nominibus admittentium: reliquis vero post biennium cum nominibus celebrantium, adnotato loco, & tempore, iuxta constitutiones.
units.tr: 11. The names of those who have made solemn or simple vows are to be noted in a book prepared for this purpose: for the Professed and the formed Coadjutors, together with the names of those who admitted them; for the rest, after two years, together with the names of those who celebrated the vows, the place and time being noted, according to the Constitutions.

units.la: 12. Quas habeat facultates, partim ex ijs, quæ ipsi, in his regulis conceduntur, partim ex compendio facultatum Societatis intelligat, ut in ijs, quas non habet sciat ad Superiorem recurrere.
units.tr: 12. Let him understand what faculties he has, partly from those granted to him in these rules, partly from the summary of the faculties of the Society, so that in those he does not have he knows to have recourse to the Superior.

units.la: DE IIS, QVÆ RECTOREM AD BONAM ADMI- NISTRATIONEM IVVABVNT. CAP. II.
units.tr: Concerning the things that help the Rector toward good administration. Chapter II.

units.la: 1. SIT solicitus, ne Minister, & reliqui Officiales suo desint officio, omissis aliis, quæ possent impedire.
units.tr: 1. Let him be careful that the Minister and the other officials do not fail in their duty, setting aside other matters which might hinder this.

units.la: 14. Singulis vel saltem alternis hebdomadis cum suis Consultoribus conveniat, (nisi forte nata aliquid extraordinarie esset consultandum) deque rebus maioris momenti, quæ pro temporum, & negotiorum varietate occurrunt, cum illis agat: quanquam ijs auditis penes ipsum erit de singulis statuendi facultas.
units.tr: 14. Let him meet with his Consultors once a week, or at least every other week (unless perhaps something unexpected needs urgent consultation), and deal with them about matters of greater importance which arise according to the variety of times and business; although, once he has heard them, the power of deciding each matter rests with him.

units.la: 15. Consultores, aliosque omnes, cum ei aliquid proponunt, libenter ac benigne excipiat, & recipiet eum, cui Monitoris officium commissum est, efficiat, ut in suo Collegio, quæ in formula scribendi præscripta sunt, accurate serventur.
units.tr: 15. Let him receive the Consultors and all others gladly and kindly whenever they propose something to him; and let him see to it that the one to whom the office of Monitor has been entrusted keeps accurately, in his College, the things prescribed in the form of writing.

units.la: 16. Habeat librum, in quo scribantur visitationes Collegij à Generali approbatæ, in quo etiam scribantur ordinationes aliæ alicuius momenti, quæ à Generali mittuntur: & quæ perpetuæ fuerint, ab ijs, quæ temporariæ sunt, separatim notentur: alia vero quæ Visitator & Provincialis præscripserint, in alio libro scribantur.
units.tr: 16. Let him have a book in which the visitations of the College approved by the General are written; in which also other ordinances of some importance, which are sent from the General, are written; and those which are perpetual are to be noted separately from those which are temporary. But other matters which the Visitor and the Provincial have prescribed are to be written in another book.

units.la: 17. Institutum Societatis cognoscat ex lectione literarum Apostolicarum, Constitutionum, & Decretorum generalium Congregationum: magis autem particularia ex lectione Regularum, tam communium, quam officij sui, & aliorum, qui sub ipsius cura sunt, ac Provincialis, & Cœpendij facultatum Societatis, atq; ex observatione consuetudinum receptarum ac demum ex recursu ad Superiorem in ijs, de quibus dubitabit.
units.tr: 17. Let him learn the Institute of the Society from reading the Apostolic letters, the Constitutions, and the Decrees of the General Congregations; but more particular matters from reading the Rules, both the common ones and those of his own office and of the others who are under his care, as well as those of the Provincial, and the Compendium of the faculties of the Society; and also from observing the customs that have been received, and finally from recourse to the Superior in those matters about which he is in doubt.

units.la: 18. Libellum habeat, in quem referat quæcunque sibi ad bonum Collegij statum subinde occurrent, ne memoria excidant, præcipuè illa, de quibus ad Generalem scribendum putat.
units.tr: 18. Let him have a little book in which he records whatever occurs to him from time to time concerning the good state of the College, so that it does not slip from his memory; especially those things about which he thinks he should write to the General.

units.la: 19. Pro occurrentibus necessitatibus communibus & privatis, Missas & orationes suorum, moderate tamen, iuxta consuetudinem Societatis applicare poterit.
units.tr: 19. For the common and private needs that arise, he may apply Masses and prayers of his members, moderately, however, and according to the custom of the Society.

units.la: DE CVRA NOSTRORVM IN SPIRITV.
units.tr: ON THE CARE OF OUR MEN IN THE SPIRIT.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: 20. Vret, ut cuiq; in suo officio integram obedientiam Collegiales præstent, & officiales Ministro, & sibi etiam omnes, studeatq; eisdem exemplo obedientiæ præire quam ipse suis Superioribus, quos Christi loco habet, præstare debet.
units.tr: 20. He shall see to it that the members of the college render complete obedience to him in their respective duties, and that the officials render it to the Minister; and he himself should render it to all, and he ought to strive to set an example of obedience, as he himself is bound to render it to his own superiors, whom he holds in the place of Christ.

units.la: 21. Det operam, ut Constitutiones, & Regulæ observentur: omnibus Collegialibus cum omni solicitudine invigilet, eosdemque ab iis, quæ nocere possint, domi & foris defendat, cum præveniendo, tum etiam, si quid mali acciderit, remedium adhibendo; itaut in virtutibus, & literis proficiant.
units.tr: 21. He shall take pains that the Constitutions and Rules are observed. He shall keep a watchful eye on all the members of the college with the greatest care, and defend them, at home and abroad, from whatever could harm them, both by forestalling it and, if any evil should befall, by applying a remedy; so that they may make progress in virtues and in letters.

units.la: 22. Efficiat, ut sibi, vel aliis ab ipso deputatis statis temporibus ratio conscientiæ reddatur à suis, iuxta modum, qui in officio Provincialis præscribitur, & instructionem ad reddendam conscientiæ rationem: & aliquos præterea maturiores Patres assignet, qui eorum confessiones generales excipiant, nisi Provincialis tunc adsit.
units.tr: 22. He shall arrange that at set times an account of conscience is rendered by his men to himself, or to others appointed by him, according to the manner prescribed in the office of the Provincial and the instruction for rendering an account of conscience. Besides this, he shall assign some more mature Fathers to hear their general confessions, unless the Provincial is then present.

units.la: 23. Meminerit, ut Scholastici, & Coadjutores non formati bis singulis annis circa festa Circumcisionis Domini nostri, & Apostolorum Petri & Pauli, vota sua renovent; præmissis ijs, quæ fieri solent.
units.tr: 23. He shall remember that the Scholastics and the Coadjutors not yet formed renew their vows twice a year, about the feasts of the Circumcision of our Lord and of the Apostles Peter and Paul, after the preliminaries that are customary have been observed.

units.la: 24. Singulis, vel alternis diebus Veneris exhortationem nostris vel ipse faciat, vel aliquis alius, qui rationem nostri instituti bene teneat, in qua agatur de observatione Constitutionum & Regularum, de fraterna charitate, humilitate, patientia, mortificatione, & aliis virtutibus, præsertim de obedientia, tametsi exhortationis loco spiritualis collatio eidem de rebus aliquando haberi poterit.
units.tr: 24. On each Friday, or on alternate Fridays, he shall himself give an exhortation to our men, or some other who knows our Institute well shall give it, in which there is to be discussion of the observance of the Constitutions and Rules, of fraternal charity, humility, patience, mortification, and other virtues, especially obedience; although at times a spiritual conference on these matters may be held in place of the exhortation.

units.la: 25. Crebrò, & magna charitatis significatione alloquatur subditos, eorumq; necessitatibus non corporis tantum, sed multò etiam magis animæ, paterno affectu prospiciat. Si quem vero intelligat aliqua tentatione pulsari, præsertim gravi, eius peculiarem curam, & solicitudinem, non solum per se, sed etiam, si necesse fuerit, per alios gerat: nec remedium longius differendo, difficiliorem morbi curationem reddat.
units.tr: 25. He shall address his subordinates often, and with great signs of charity, and provide for their needs, not only of the body but much more of the soul, with a fatherly affection. If he perceives that anyone is assailed by some temptation, especially a grave one, he shall take special care and concern for him, not only himself but also, if necessary, through others; and by deferring the remedy for too long he shall not make the cure of the illness more difficult.

units.la: 26. In correctionibus, & pœnitentijs injungendis rationem habebit dispositionis perfoNarum, & ædificationis universalis, & particularis earum ad gloriam Dei.
units.tr: 26. In imposing corrections and penances he shall take account of the disposition of the persons, and of their edification, both universal and particular, for the glory of God.

units.la: 27. Nisi prudentia rebus particularibus adhibita aliter procedendum dictaverit, illud in correctionibus observet; ut ij, qui peccant, primò in charitate, & dulcedine admoneantur; secundò in charitate quidem, sed eo tamen modo, ut eis confusio, & rubor injiciatur: tertio amori ea, quæ timorem incutiant, si opus erit, adijciant.
units.tr: 27. Unless prudence, applied to particular circumstances, dictates that one should proceed otherwise, he shall observe this in corrections: that those who sin are first admonished in charity and gentleness; second, in charity indeed, but in such a way that confusion and shame are put upon them; third, if need be, that those things which cause fear are added to love.

units.la: 28. De publicis defectibus publica debet esse pœnitentia, ijs tantum, quæ ad omnium ædificationem faciunt, declaratis.
units.tr: 28. For public faults the penance should be public, only those things being declared which serve the edification of all.

units.la: 29. Poterit mittere interdum aliquem ex suis, ut østiatim petat eleemosynam, aut ut inserviat hospitali, aut comitetur emptorem, aut in plateis concionetur, Christianam vel doctrinam doceat, prout magis in Domino expedire videbitur, habita ratione ædificationis & spiritualis utilitatis nostrorum.
units.tr: 29. He may sometimes send one of his men to beg alms from door to door, or to serve in a hospital, or to accompany a buyer, or to preach in the squares, or to teach Christian doctrine, as shall seem more expedient in the Lord, having regard to the edification and spiritual profit of our men.

units.la: 30. Delegare poterit Confessario, vel aliis vices suas, ut eas pœnitentias approbent, vel improbent, quas, ad majorem sui spiritus profectum, assumere quisq; volet.
units.tr: 30. He may delegate his powers to a Confessor, or to others, to approve or disapprove those penances which each one wishes to undertake for the greater advancement of his spirit.

units.la: 31. In danda facultate ieiunandi, sicut & in aliis pœnitentijs concedendis, videat ne mensuram recta rationis excedat: detque operam, ut omnes intelligant ad singularitatem non pertinere, si quis jejunet aliis non jejunantibus: dummodo ordinaria consuetudo jejunandi, quæ juxta Constitutiones non fit, non introducatur.
units.tr: 31. In granting permission to fast, as also in granting other penances, he shall see that it does not exceed the measure of right reason; and he shall take pains that everyone understands that it is not singularity if someone fasts while others do not fast, provided that the ordinary custom of fasting, which according to the Constitutions is not made, is not introduced.

units.la: Unio, & conformitas mutua diligentissimè curanda est, nec ferenda inter ullos domesticorum perturbatio, vel ira mutua: si quid autem hujusmodi accideret, curet, ut statim cum satisfactione debita in gratiam invicem redeant.
units.tr: Mutual union and conformity are to be most diligently cultivated, and no disturbance or mutual anger among the members of the household is to be tolerated; if anything of this kind should occur, he shall see to it that they immediately return to harmony with one another, with due satisfaction given.

units.la: Tam ipse, quam omnes alij Sacerdotes, qui ei videbuntur, juxta Constitutiones, aliquando intra annum, officium vel officia eorum, qui domi inserviunt, ad tempus aliquod obibunt.
units.tr: He himself, as well as all the other Priests whom he judges fit, shall, according to the Constitutions, at some time within the year, perform for a set period the office or offices of those who serve at home.

units.la: Non permittat nostros Scholasticos frequentius, quam octavo quoque die communicare, nisi particulares ob causas, habita magis ratione necessitatis quam devotionis: diebus tamen solemnibus in hac re dispensare poterit. Coadjutoribus vero, & ijs, qui literis non dant operam, longe facilius concedi poterit, ut etiam intra hebdomadam communicent, & Præfecto rerum spiritualium aut Confessario delegari, ut id concedat ijs, quos ea ratione magis in spiritu juvari in Domino judicabit.
units.tr: He shall not permit our Scholastics to communicate more often than every eighth day, except for particular reasons, with regard had more to necessity than to devotion; on solemn days, however, he may dispense in this matter. To the Coadjutors, and to those who do not devote themselves to letters, it may be granted much more easily that they communicate even within the week; and it may be delegated to the Prefect of spiritual matters or to the Confessor to grant this to those whom, in the Lord, he judges to be helped more in the spirit in this way.

units.la: Videat scripta, & literas omnes, quæ scribuntur ad domesticos, & quas ipsi aliis scribunt, aut aliquem virum fidelem, & qui donum discretionis habeat, Domi constituat, qui eas lectas reddat, aut non reddat, prout in Domino magis expedire judicabit, sibique referat, si quid invenerit, quod tanti momenti sit, ut de eo Superior monendus videatur: res autem vanas, aut quæ alia ratione offendere possint, neminem scribere permittat: nec sigillum quemquam habere sinat sine Provincialis facultate.
units.tr: He shall see all writings and letters which are written to members of the household, and which they write to others; or he shall appoint at home some faithful man who has the gift of discretion, who shall read them and hand them over or not, as he shall judge more expedient in the Lord, and report to him if he finds anything of such importance that the Superior seems to need to be warned of it; but he shall not permit anyone to write vain things, or things that could give offence in any other way; nor shall he allow anyone to keep a seal without the Provincial's permission.

units.la: Non sint in Collegio arma, nec instrumenta musica, nec libri lascivi, aut vani, nec novæ ullæ recreationes introducantur.
units.tr: There shall be in the College no weapons, no musical instruments, no wanton or frivolous books, and no new recreations are to be introduced.

units.la: DE LITERARVM STVDIIS.
units.tr: ON THE STUDY OF LETTERS.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: Neminem ad inchoanda studia admittat, nec eos, qui ad illa ex Provincialis commissione admissi fuerint, ad aliam facultatem promoveat, absque eiusdem Provincialis approbatione, cui post maturam considerationem, & examen, de unoquoque suo tempore significabit, quid sentiat.
units.tr: He shall admit no one to begin his studies, nor advance to another faculty those who have been admitted to them under the Provincial's commission, without the approval of that same Provincial, to whom, after mature consideration and examination, he shall report at the proper time what he thinks of each one.

units.la: Impedimenta removeat, quæ a studijs animos Scholasticorum avocant, qualia sunt nimiæ mortificationes, vel devotiones, vel externæ occupationes. Et circa illorum valetudinem peculiari cura animadvertat, ut & in laboribus mentis, modum servet, & in ijs, quæ ad corpus pertinet, religiosa commoditate tractentur, ut diutius in studijs perseverare tam in literis addiscendis, quam in eisdem exercendis ad Dei gloriam possint.
units.tr: He shall remove the hindrances which draw the minds of the scholastics away from their studies, such as excessive mortifications, or devotions, or outside occupations. And with particular care he shall watch over their health, so that they keep to a measure in the labours of the mind, and that what pertains to the body is handled with a religious consideration, so that they may be able to persevere longer in their studies, both in learning letters and in exercising them, to the glory of God.

units.la: Videat, quomodo Professores omnes suo munere fungantur, curetque diligenter a Philosophiæ & Theologiæ Professoribus ea servari circa opinionum diversitatem, quæ in Constitutionibus, & ratione studiorum præscripta sunt. Intelligat etiam per se, vel per alios, quo modo Scholastici in suis studijs proficiant: quod si animadverteret aliquem in ijs inutiliter tempus terere, ad Provincialem referat.
units.tr: He shall see how all the professors perform their duty, and shall carefully take care that the teachers of philosophy and theology observe the rules laid down in the Constitutions and in the plan of studies regarding the diversity of opinions. He shall also understand for himself, or through others, how the scholastics are making progress in their studies; and if he should notice anyone wasting time in them to no purpose, he shall refer the matter to the Provincial.

units.la: Singulis hebdomadis dies unus saltem a prandio Scholasticis ad quietem destinatus sit, in quo eos ad hortum, aut prædium Collegij, vel alio exercitij corporis, vel recreandi animi gratia mittere poterit: In reliquis autem studiorum intermissionibus sequatur ordinem a Generali, vel Provinciali constitutum.
units.tr: Let at least one day each week, from after dinner, be set aside for the scholastics' rest, on which he may send them to the garden or the farm of the College, or to some other bodily exercise or for the refreshment of the mind. In the other intervals from study he shall follow the order laid down by the General or the Provincial.

units.la: Etsi præceptorem publicum in scholis instituere non poterit absque Provincialis facultate, ad tempus tamen necessitatis gratia id facere poterit.
units.tr: Although he may not establish a public teacher in the schools without the Provincial's permission, he may nevertheless do so for a time, in case of necessity.

units.la: In actibus promovendorum ad gradus literarios (ad quos nostri sine facultate Generalis promoveri non possunt) si qua in re alicuius momenti dispensatione opus esset, Provincialem admoneat.
units.tr: In the acts of those being promoted to literary degrees (to which our men cannot be promoted without the General's permission), if any dispensation of some importance were needed, he shall advise the Provincial.

units.la: Constitutiones, sive regulæ, quæ ad Scholasticos Societatis pertinent, publice in Refectorio bis, aut ter singulis annis legantur.
units.tr: The Constitutions, or rules, which pertain to the scholastics of the Society, shall be read publicly in the refectory twice or three times each year.

units.la: Sub finem studiorum cuiusque, suarum esse partium Rector intelligat, audito Confultoribus Provincialem de uniuscuiusque talento admonere: & quantum singuli profecerint, referre, & num aliqui ad sacros ordines promovendi sint, aut in Confessarios, aut Concionatores, aut Lectores eligendi, proponerū.
units.tr: Toward the end of each one's studies, the Rector should understand that it is his part, after hearing his consultors, to advise the Provincial about each one's talent, and to report how much each has progressed, and to propose whether any of them are to be promoted to holy orders, or chosen as confessors, preachers, or lecturers.

units.la: DE ORDINE DOMESTICO. CAP. V.
units.tr: CONCERNING DOMESTIC ORDER. CHAPTER V.

units.la: Quotidie post orationem matutinam fiat sacrum, cui intersint omnes, qui Sacerdotes non sunt: nisi aliquibus propter peculiares causas aliud tempus ad sacrum audiendum concessum sit.
units.tr: Every day, after morning prayer, Mass shall be celebrated, and all who are not priests shall attend it, unless for particular reasons another time has been granted to some for hearing Mass.

units.la: Quando nostri ad sacram communionem accessuri sunt, praesertim diebus Dominicis, curet, ut in Ecclesia (si commodè fieri poterit) id faciant, separati tamen ab externis quantum locus feret.
units.tr: When our men are to receive holy communion, especially on Sundays, the Rector shall see that they do so in the church, if this can conveniently be done, but kept separate from outsiders as far as the place allows.

units.la: Tempore orationi, & reliquis exercitiis assignato, sit aliquis, qui observet, num omnes in iis vacent, quod etiam Ministri & ipsemet Rector aliquando faciat.
units.tr: During the time assigned to prayer and the other spiritual exercises, someone shall be appointed to observe whether everyone is occupied with them. The ministers and the Rector himself shall sometimes do this too.

units.la: Syndicum domi constituat, ubi Ministri, aut Subministri opera adiuvari non uteretur, cuius officium erit observare in omnibus, quod ad honestatem, & decentiam externam pertinet, Ecclesiam & domum in locis publicis perlustrando, & si quid quod non conveniat, annotaverit, Superiori referendo. Praeter hunc alios particulares Syndicos in classibus singulis habeat, qui, quantum fieri poterit, ex prudentioribus, & maturioribus deligantur.
units.tr: He shall appoint a house overseer, who, where the ministers or assistant ministers cannot be helped by his work, shall watch over everything that pertains to decency and outward propriety, going through the church and the house in the public places. If he notes anything unseemly, he shall report it to the Superior. Besides him, he shall have other particular overseers in each class, chosen, as far as possible, from the more prudent and mature men.

units.la: Omnes, praeter illos, quos ipse iudicaverit excipiendos, horae quadrantem ante prandium, vel coenam, corporis exercitationi tribuant.
units.tr: All, except those whom the Rector himself judges to be excused, shall give a quarter of an hour before dinner or supper to physical exercise.

units.la: A posteriore prandii signo ad coenam, octo ut minimum horae intersint: aliquid vero amplius usque ad refectionem culam vespertinam diebus Veneris, & ieiuniorum, iuxta morem regionis: a tempore autem, quo se nostri cubitum receperint usque ad signum, quo excitantur, septem.
units.tr: From the signal after dinner until supper, there shall be at least eight hours of attendance; and somewhat more, up to the evening collation, on Fridays and fast days, according to the custom of the region. From the time our men retire to bed until the signal by which they are roused, there shall be seven hours.

units.la: Benedictio, & gratiarum actio in refectorio iuxta usum breviarij Romani in prima mensa fiant: in secunda vero, & privata, retineri possunt antiqua benedictio, & gratiarum actio, quae a singulis submisse & stando fieri debent.
units.tr: The blessing and thanksgiving at table shall be made in the refectory according to the use of the Roman breviary at the first table. At the second and private tables the old blessing and thanksgiving may be retained, which everyone should say quietly and standing.

units.la: In mensa Sacerdotes praecedant alios ad eum gradum non promotos, sed nec inter Sacerdotes, nec inter eos, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ullus ordo constituatur.
units.tr: At table the priests shall go before those not promoted to that rank; but no order shall be established either among the priests or among those who are not priests.

units.la: Si aliqua de causa Rector primae mensae adesse non poterit, curet, ut minister adsit.
units.tr: If for some reason the Rector cannot be present at the first table, he shall see that a minister is present.

units.la: Dominicis diebus, & festis, si commodè fieri poterit, & aliis etiam, si Superiori videatur, sint aliqui pro multitudine Scholarium a Superiore delecti, qui inter cenandum pro lectione concionem habeant, quibus conveniens aliquod tempus eodem die ad seperandum pro Superioris arbitrio dandum erit.
units.tr: On Sundays and feast days, if it can conveniently be done, and on other days too if it seems good to the Superior, there shall be some men chosen by the Superior, in proportion to the number of scholastics, who during supper shall deliver a sermon from reading. For these men a suitable time on the same day shall be given for rest, at the Superior's discretion.

units.la: A prandio & a coena hora una: diebus autem Veneris post collationem vespertinam dimidia recreationi religiosè impendatur, idque in uno loco, si commodè fieri poterit: sed neque extra huiusmodi horas labores nimium continuari sine aliqua conveniente relaxatione sinat.
units.tr: One hour shall be devoted to recreation after dinner and after supper; on Fridays, half an hour after the evening collation. This recreation shall be taken devoutly, and if possible in one place. Outside these hours, he shall not allow labours to be carried on too long without some suitable relaxation.

units.la: Scholastici omnes, ubi aliqua fuerit eorum copia, pro more Societatis (nisi quis eximendus videretur) diebus saltem Dominicis ad finem recreationis post prandium in tonis, seu ratione concionandi exerceantur, de iis crebro tractantes, quae ad sui abnegationem, & in virtutibus profectum, & fraternam charitatem spectant.
units.tr: All the scholastics, where there is a sufficient number of them, shall be exercised, according to the custom of the Society (unless someone seems to be excused), at least on Sundays, toward the end of the recreation after dinner, in delivering speeches in the tones of preaching; and they shall often discuss those matters which concern self-denial, progress in virtues, and brotherly charity.

units.la: DE IIS, QVÆ PERTINENT AD RES TEM- PORALES. CAPVT VI.
units.tr: Concerning those things which pertain to temporal affairs. Chapter VI.

units.la: Singulis mensibus a Procuratore rationem accepti, & expensi praesente Ministro exigat, ut totius domus administrationis ratio ipsi constet, eamque reddere possit cui, fit cui, & quando per Superiore constituetur: caveat ante, ne Collegiû ære alieno gravetur.
units.tr: Once a month he is to require from the Procurator an account of receipts and expenditures, in the presence of the minister, so that he himself may know the accounts of the whole administration of the house, and be able to render them to whomever shall be appointed by the Superior, and when. He is to take care beforehand that the college is not burdened with debt.

units.la: 58. In ijs, quæ ad victum, vestitum, & habitationem, & alia corpori necessaria pertinent, curet: ut quamvis sit, in quo probetur virtus, & sui ipsius abnegatio, non desit tamen, quo sustentetur natura, habita convenienti ratione personarum in Domino. Cùm Scholasticis verò in ijs, quæ ad vestitum attinent, magis quàm cum ijs, qui probantur, exterioris decentiæ ratio habeatur.
units.tr: 58. In those matters which pertain to food, clothing, lodging, and other things necessary for the body, he shall see to it that, although there may be some in whom virtue and self-denial are tested, nevertheless what sustains nature is not lacking, with due regard being had to the persons in the Lord. But with the scholastics, in matters that concern clothing, more regard is to be paid to outward decency than with those who are being tested.

units.la: 59. Ægrotorum cura habeatur magna, & observetur diligenter tam in victus ratione, quàm in cæteris, quod Medicus præscripserit.
units.tr: 59. Great care is to be taken of the sick, and what the physician has prescribed is to be carefully observed, both in the matter of diet and in other respects.

units.la: 60. Si cui particulari quidpiam ab externo aliquo mittatur, id in communem usum accipiatur, ac dispensetur.
units.tr: 60. If anything is sent from some outsider to any particular person, it is to be received and distributed for common use.

units.la: 61. Caveat, ne qua Domus Professorum, aut aliquis eorum, vel Coadjutorum formatorum redditibus Collegij sui, præterquam in rebus minimis utatur, nisi is, eidem Collegio necessarius sit, aut conveniens, ut in eo commoretur.
units.tr: 61. He shall take care that no house of the Professed, nor any one of them, or of the formed Coadjutors, uses the revenues of his college for anything beyond very small matters, unless that person is necessary to the college or it is fitting for him to dwell in it.

units.la: 62. Lites forenses fugiat, nec ullam inconsulto Provinciali intentet, nec intenta respondeat, nisi cogatur.
units.tr: 62. He shall avoid lawsuits, and shall not bring any without consulting the Provincial, nor answer one brought against him unless he is compelled to.

units.la: 63. Si bona alicujus ex nostris distribuenda essent, si ineundi contractus, si fabrica alicujus momenti, & expensæ extraordinariæ faciendæ, aut si bona offerantur Collegio cum aliqua obligatione, rem ad Provincialem deferat.
units.tr: 63. If the goods of any of ours are to be distributed, if contracts are to be entered into, if a building of some importance or extraordinary expenses are to be undertaken, or if goods are offered to the college with some obligation attached, he shall refer the matter to the Provincial.

units.la: 64. Depositum pecuniæ nullum prorsus admittat: aliarum verò rerum non nisi cautissimè, dummodo sint eorum, quibus multum debeamus, aut alioqui id officij sine magna offensione, denegari non possit.
units.tr: 64. He shall admit no deposit of money at all; of other things, he shall admit them only most cautiously, provided they belong to those to whom we are much indebted, or else such a service cannot be refused without great offence.

units.la: 65. Neminiem ex nostris in causis civilibus, nedum criminalibus examinari (nisi qui ad rectatum obligare potest, compelleret) permittat absque licentia, quam minimè dabit, nisi in causis, quæ ad religionem Catholicam pertinent, aut alioqui piæ sint, & ita uni faveant, ut non in alterius detrimentum cedant.
units.tr: 65. He shall not permit anyone of ours to be examined in civil cases, much less in criminal ones (unless one who could compel him to repentance by obligation), without permission, which he will very rarely give, except in cases that pertain to the Catholic religion, or are otherwise pious and so favour one party that they do not turn to the detriment of another.

units.la: DE AVXILIO ANIMARVM, COMMVNICATIONE CVM EXTERNIS, ET GRATITVDINE ERGA FVNDATORES, ET BENEFA- CTORES.
units.tr: Concerning the Help of Souls, Communication with Outsiders, and Gratitude Towards Founders and Benefactors.

units.la: CAP. VII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII.

units.la: Det operam, ut à nostris ministeria Societatis juxta Provincialis præscriptum, & cujusque talentum exerceantur non solùm in nostra, sed etiam in aliis Ecclesiis, ac ceribus & aliis locis, quantum commodè fieri poterit, nominatimque ministerium doctrinæ Christianæ commendatum habeat.
units.tr: He shall take care that our men exercise the ministries of the Society, according to the prescription of the Provincial and each one's talent, not only in our own churches but also in other churches, in cities and other places, as far as it can conveniently be done; and he shall especially keep the ministry of Christian doctrine recommended.

units.la: 67. Curet, ut nostri spiritualibus exercitijs tradendis accuratè exerceantur, postquam ipsi in se fuerint experti: nullus tamen deberet ea tradere, nisi prudentia, ac rerum spiritualium usu satis probatus esset.
units.tr: 67. Let him see to it that our men diligently give the spiritual exercises after they have themselves experienced them; yet no one should give them unless he has been sufficiently proven in prudence and in the practice of spiritual matters.

units.la: 68. Non permittat, ut nostri curam mulierum religiosarum suscipiant, & aliarum quamcunque, ut ordinariè illarum confessiones audiant, vel ipsas regant, quamvis nihil reputant aliquando apud eas concionari, semel aut unius Monasterij confessiones speciales ob ausas addire: quod tamen non fiet, nisi postulent ij, qui eis præsunt.
units.tr: 68. He shall not permit our men to take up the care of religious women, or of any others whatsoever, so as to hear their confessions regularly or to direct them, although they may sometimes preach among them; or to hear special confessions once, or for the sake of some particular reason, of one monastery. This shall not be done, however, unless those who preside over them request it.

units.la: 69. Etsi proprium Rectoris officium est, Collegium sibi commissum diligenter, ac fideliter gubernare, neque is propter aliud quicquam huic muneri deesse debet: si quando tamen officij sui occupationes licebit, & concionari, & confessiones audire, & alia Societatis ministeria exercere poterit.
units.tr: 69. Although it is the proper office of the Rector to govern the College entrusted to him diligently and faithfully, and he ought not to be lacking in this office for any other reason, nevertheless, if at any time the occupations of his office allow, he may both preach, hear confessions, and exercise the other ministries of the Society.

units.la: 70. Mulieres invisere, aut ad eas scribere, nisi in necessitate, aut cum spe magni fructus, ostros non sinat, nec hoc quidem permittat, nisi viris valde probatis & prudentibus.
units.tr: 70. He shall not allow our men to visit women or write to them, except in necessity or with the hope of great fruit; and even then he shall not permit it except to men who are very well proven and prudent.

units.la: 71. Non permittat fœminas Collegium nostrum ingredi.
units.tr: 71. He shall not permit women to enter our College.

units.la: 72. Curet, ne primarios viros invisere nostri consuescant, nisi sancto studio piorum operum lucrentur, vel quando intima benevolentia in Domino coniunctí essent.
units.tr: 72. He shall take care that our men do not get into the habit of visiting leading men, unless they gain them for holy zeal in pious works, or when they are joined in intimate friendship in the Lord.

units.la: 73. Non sinat offerri munuscula, quae magnatibus ad res maiores obtinendas offerri solent.
units.tr: 73. He shall not allow small gifts to be offered, such as are customarily offered to great men to obtain greater things.

units.la: 74. Non permittat, ut nostri cibum capiant apud externos, aut ab eis, cum aegrotant, visitentur, nisi causa non levis momenti id concedendum moveret: quam eandem esse oportebit, si quando externus aliquis ad mensam, praesertim refectorij, invitandus videretur.
units.tr: 74. He shall not permit our men to take their meals with outsiders, or to be visited by them when they are sick, unless some matter of no slight importance should move him to grant this; and the same shall have to be the case if any outsider should seem to be invited to the table, especially the refectory table.

units.la: 75. Amicos conservare, et eos, qui male erga nos affecti sunt, praecipue si homines sint non vulgaris auctoritatis, orationibus et rationibus convenientibus in amicitiam revocare, vel saltem, ne adversarij sint, efficere studeat.
units.tr: 75. He shall strive to keep friends, and to recall to friendship by fitting words and arguments those who are ill disposed towards us, especially if they are men of no ordinary authority, or at least to bring it about that they are not adversaries.

units.la: 76. Observet, quae erga fundatores, et benefactores, tam vivos quam mortuos observanda sunt, eisdem gratitudinem exhibeat: et aliis obligationibus si quas Collegium habet, satisfieri curet.
units.tr: 76. He shall observe what must be observed towards founders and benefactors, both living and dead, and shall show them gratitude; and he shall see to it that whatever other obligations the College has are satisfied.

units.la: DE IIS, QVI ADMITTI PETVNT, AD CO- LLEGIVM DIVERTVNT, AVT FORAS MITTVNTVR.
units.tr: Concerning those who ask to be admitted to the College, who turn aside to it, or who are sent away

units.la: CAP. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: 77. IN Societatem neminem admittat, nisi à Generali, vel Provinciali id ipsi committatur, sed de iis, qui admitti petunt, ad Provincialem referat, vel scribat, quales illi sint, et quibus donis Dei praediti.
units.tr: 77. Let him admit no one into the Society unless this has been entrusted to him by the General or the Provincial. Concerning those who ask to be admitted, he shall report to the Provincial, or write to him, as to what sort of men they are and what gifts of God they have.

units.la: 78. Si is, qui admitti petit, ad institutum Societatis valde idoneus videbitur, et necessitas urgeret, poterit eum tanquam hospitem Domi recipere, donec responsum à Provinciali accipiat, vel ad eundem mittere, si expedire iudicaverit.
units.tr: 78. If the one who asks to be admitted seems very suited to the Society's way of life, and necessity presses, he may receive him at home as a guest until he gets a reply from the Provincial, or he may send him on to the Provincial, if he judges this expedient.

units.la: 79. Recedentem sine licentia ab alio loco Societatis, vel ab ea dimissum non admittat, sed si expedire videretur, ad Provincialem de eo scribat, et eius ordinationem expectet, illo domi ut hospite, vel in alio pio loco, si videbitur, detento.
units.tr: 79. He shall not admit anyone who has left another house of the Society without permission, or who has been dismissed by it. If it seems expedient, he shall write to the Provincial about him and await his decision, while keeping the man at home as a guest, or in another pious place if that seems best.

units.la: 80. Charitatem magnam exhibeat erga alios de Societate per Collegium transeuntes, eosque amanter hospitio excipiat, ac meminerit se aliquo viatico, aut eleemosyna eos, si indigerent, iuvare posse: curet item diligenter dirigere ac iuvare expeditiones hospitum, qui negotiorum causa domi versantur.
units.tr: 80. He shall show great charity towards the others of the Society who pass through the College, and shall receive them kindly into his hospitality, remembering that he can help them, if they are in need, with some provision for the journey or with alms. Likewise he shall carefully see to it that he directs and assists the journeys of guests who are at home on business.

units.la: 81. Externi ne accipiantur hospitio, ut domi pernoctent, nisi iij sint, quibus multum debeatur, aut id officij sine magna offensione praetermitti non possit; quae in re habeatur praecipua ratio religiosorum cum necessitatis causa ad nos divertunt.
units.tr: 81. Outsiders are not to be received into hospitality so as to lodge at home overnight, unless they are those to whom much is owed, or unless the duty cannot be omitted without great offence. In this matter, special regard is to be had for religious men, when they turn aside to us out of necessity.

units.la: 82. Cum quis domo egredietur, det ei socium convenientem: si quando autem aliquis solus foras mittitur, is sit, cui meritò possit confidere.
units.tr: 82. When someone is going out from the house, he shall give him a suitable companion. If at any time someone is sent out alone, he should be one in whom he can rightly place confidence.

units.la: 83. Neminem ex suo Collegio in alium locum mittat sine litteris patentibus.
units.tr: 83. He shall send no one from his College to another place without letters patent.

units.la: 84. Si quis experimento comperiretur ferre non posse Collegij caelum, et male habere continenter cerneretur, vel alia ratione videretur mutandus, Provincialem admoneat, ut alio mitti debeat.
units.tr: 84. If anyone should be found by experience unable to bear the climate of the College, and should be seen to be continually unwell, or should seem in some other way to need to be moved, he shall advise the Provincial that he ought to be sent elsewhere.

units.la: 85. Profecturi ad alia loca, ea, quam fortunam vocant, et aliis interioribus indumentis, quibus utuntur, privari non debent, nisi forte ratio temporis, aut alioqui charitas suaderet, melioribus esse commutanda. Reliqua vero omnia, quae aditer necessaria erunt, magna charitatis significatione ab eo loco, unde mittuntur subministrentur, sumptibus tamen eorum, quorum sit expensas itineris solvere.
units.tr: 85. Those about to set out for other places must not be deprived of the so-called fortune, and of the other inner garments they use, unless perhaps the season or charity itself should suggest that they be exchanged for better ones. All the rest that will be necessary for the journey shall be supplied from the place from which they are sent, with a great sign of charity, though the cost shall be borne by those whose duty it is to pay the expenses of the journey.

units.la: REGVLAE E- XAMINATORIS.
units.tr: RULES FOR THE EXAMINER.

units.la: QVAE IN EXAMINATORE REQVIRANTVR, ET QVID PRAESTARE DEBEAT. CAPVT PRIMVM.
units.tr: WHAT IS REQUIRED OF THE EXAMINER, AND WHAT HE OUGHT TO ACHIEVE. CHAPTER ONE.

units.la: QVI examinat eos, qui Societatem ingredi petunt, habeat oportet cognitionem rerum eiusdem Societatis, ac zelum boni progressus ipsius, ut nulla ratione dimoveri ab eo possit, quod magis in Domino convenire iudicaverit.
units.tr: The one who examines those who ask to enter the Society ought to have knowledge of the affairs of that Society and zeal for its good progress, so that he cannot be turned from what he judges more fitting in the Lord by any consideration.

units.la: 2. Moderatus admodum sit in admittendi desiderio: nam ut par est solicite cooperari vocationi divinae, ut augeatur in Societate numerus operariorum vineae Christi: ita diligenter curandum est, ne quis admittatur, nisi qui illis Dei donis praeditus sit, quae ad ipsius gloriam hoc institutum exigit.
units.tr: 2. He should be very moderate in his desire to admit anyone. For just as it is right to cooperate diligently with the divine call, so that the number of workers in the vineyard of Christ may increase in the Society, so care must be taken that no one is admitted unless he is endowed with those gifts of God which this institute requires for his glory.

units.la: 3. Quando aliquis Societatem ingredi petit, primus ipse agat cum eo, ut intelligat quae eius dotes, et vocatio: si quis autem clare deprehenderetur ineptus ad institutum Societatis, Superiori significet, et acceptaab eo facultate, illum consilio, et si quid aliud charitas suggerit, admonitum, statim dimittat: alios vero ad eos mittat, qui a Superiore designati fuerint, ut cum illis colloquantur.
units.tr: 3. When someone asks to enter the Society, the examiner himself should first deal with him, so that he understands what his gifts and calling are. If anyone is clearly found unfit for the Society's way of life, the examiner should inform the Superior and, having received his permission, dismiss that person at once, after advising him and admonishing him in whatever other way charity suggests. He should send others to those designated by the Superior, so that they may speak with them.

units.la: 4. Postquam omnes designati, eum, qui admitti desiderat, allocuti fuerint, curet examinator, ut a Superiore vocentur, et referant, quid de eo sentiant: Superior autem, quid facto opus sit, constituet.
units.tr: 4. After all those designated have spoken with the one who wishes to be admitted, the examiner should see that they are called before the Superior and report what they think of him. The Superior will then decide what needs to be done.

units.la: 5. Si ille, qui ingredi cupit, nulli fuerit domi satis notus, intellecto eius nomine, et eorum, quibus cognitus est, extra domum inquiri poterit, cuiusmodi homo ille sit: iuvabit etiam ad hoc ipsum, si ad Sacramenta in Ecclesia nostra frequenter accedat. Quod si adhuc de eo dubitaretur, non parum confert, si in spiritualibus exercitiis constituatur: quinis peractis, si res nondum constaret, intelligat a Superiore utrum differendum responsum, an omnino dimittendus sit.
units.tr: 5. If the one who wishes to enter is not sufficiently known at home, his name may be made known and inquiry may be made outside the house, among those who know him, as to what sort of man he is. It will also help for this very purpose if he frequently approaches the Sacraments in our Church. But if doubts about him still remain, it is of no small benefit to place him in the spiritual exercises. When the five days are completed, if the matter is still not settled, he should learn from the Superior whether his answer should be postponed or he should be dismissed altogether.

units.la: BREVE EXAMEN, QVO VTI DEBET CVM IIS QVI INGREDI PETVNT.
units.tr: A SHORT EXAMINATION, IN WHAT MANNER IT SHOULD BE CONDUCTED WITH THOSE WHO SEEK TO ENTER.

units.la: CAPVT II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: IN primis qui admitti vult, interrogetur decenter de quinque impedimentis essentialibus, prudenter tamen, ut ea impedimenta esse, quae a Societate excludunt, ille non intelligat, ne verum occultandi occasionem accipiat.
units.tr: FIRST, the one who wishes to be admitted should be questioned courteously about the five essential impediments. Yet this should be done prudently, so that he does not understand which impediments are those that exclude one from the Society, lest he gain an opportunity for concealing the truth.

units.la: 7. Si aliquod ex iis impedimentis in quoquam detegeretur, non est quod ulterius procedatur, sed quoad fieri poterit, cum consolatione dimittatur: si tamen in eo dona aliqua Dei illustriora cernerentur, prius oporteret rem omnem cum Superiore conferre.
units.tr: 7. If any of these impediments is discovered in anyone, there is no reason to proceed further. Rather, he should be dismissed, as far as possible, with kindness. If, however, some more notable gifts of God were seen in him, the whole matter should first be discussed with the Superior.

units.la: 8. Si nullum tale impedimentum esset, ulterius interrogetur, an omnino decreverit seculum relinquere, quibus de causis, aut quomodo desideria haec ei in mentem venerint, et quam diu tea habuerit, an in hac animi sententia remissior aliquando factus fuerit, et quatenus.
units.tr: 8. If there is no such impediment, he should be questioned further: whether he has altogether decided to leave the world, for what reasons, or how these desires came into his mind; how long he has held them; whether he has ever become less firm in this resolve of mind, and to what extent.

units.la: 9. A quo tempore deliberaverit Societatem ingredi, et quid ipsum impulerit, ut hoc potius quam aliud institutum amplecteretur. An a quoquam, praesertim e nostris primum ad id motus fuerit. Num deliberatum habeat animi propositum vivendi et moriendi in Domino in hac Societate. Et an fuerit in eam alias admissus, et quare sit egressus.
units.tr: 9. From what time he has deliberated on entering the Society, and what moved him to embrace this institute rather than another. Whether he was prompted to it by anyone, especially by one of ours. Whether he has firmly resolved to live and die in the Lord in this Society. And whether he has been admitted to it before, and why he left.

units.la: 10. Num habeat aes alienum, aut alias obligationes. Num morbum aliquem occultum, vel manifestum, et an haereditarium, vel defectum in aliqua sui parte patiatur.
units.tr: 10. Whether he has debts or other obligations. Whether he suffers from any hidden or manifest disease, whether hereditary, or any defect in some part of his body.

units.la: 11. Interrogetur de ætate, Patria, Parentibus, & eorum conditione, an rerum tempoporalium penuria premantur, & an ea causa, vel quacunque alia necessario ipsius opera in- digeant, aut probabiliter indigere possint.
units.tr: 11. He should be asked about his age, his homeland, his parents and their circumstances, whether he is burdened by a lack of temporal goods, and whether, for that reason or any other, he needs, or is likely to need, his services.

units.la: 12. An sit ex legitimo matrimonio, num à progenitoribus iam olim Christianis, an à modernis; vel haereticis descendat. An aliquis ex eius progenitoribus notatus fuerit, vel declaratus ob aliquem errorem contra nostram Christianam, & Catholicam religionem.
units.tr: 12. Whether he is born of a lawful marriage, and whether he descends from parents who were long ago Christian or from recent ones, or from heretics. Whether any of his ancestors has been noted or declared for some error against our Christian and Catholic religion.

units.la: 13. Si literis praeditus est, interrogetur, ubi eis operam dederit, quantum profecerit: Ingenii autem & iudicij specimen ex sermone, & aliis conijcere licebit.
units.tr: 13. If he is educated in letters, he should be asked where he has studied and how far he has progressed. The measure of his intellect and judgment may be inferred from his speech and other things.

units.la: 14. Si Coadiutor est futurus, petatur de aetate, ac viribus: an omnino forte Marthae contentus futurus sit, & num aliquam artem noverit: & observetur, an ad virtutem, & devotionem propensus sit.
units.tr: 14. If he is to be a lay brother, he should be asked about his age and strength, whether he will be content at all with the part of Martha, and whether he knows some craft; and it should be observed whether he is inclined to virtue and devotion.

units.la: 15. Tandem curandum est, ut qui admitti desiderant, summam nostri instituti, probationesque, ac difficultates, quae in eo sunt, bene intelligant: De iis vero, quae hic interrogantur, aut de instituto explicanda dicuntur, plura, aut pauciora iuxta personarum qualitatem, & cognitionem inquiri, & explicari poterunt.
units.tr: 15. Finally, care must be taken that those who desire to be admitted understand well the summary of our institute, its trials, and the difficulties that are in it. Concerning those things which are asked here, or which are said to be explained about the institute, more or fewer may be inquired into and explained, according to the quality and knowledge of the persons.

units.la: 16. Reliqua, quae ad officium examinatoris, pertinent, si quando cum ijs qui in prima probatione sunt, vel aliis nostris illi obeunda erunt, petat ex officio Magistri Novitiorum.
units.tr: 16. As for the remaining matters that pertain to the office of the examiner, if at any time he must perform them with those who are in the first probation, or with others of ours, he should seek them as part of his office from the Master of Novices.

units.la: 17. Caeteri vero à Superiore designati, ut cum illis colloquantur qui admitti petunt, eisdem fere interrogationibus utentur; exceptis ijs; quae interrogato ruborem inijcere possunt.
units.tr: 17. The others designated by the Superior to converse with those who ask to be admitted will use almost the same questions, except those which might cause the one questioned to blush.

units.la: REGVLÆ MAGISTRI NOVITIORVM.
units.tr: RULES OF THE NOVICE MASTER.

units.la: DE IIS, QVÆ AD EIVS PERSONAM, ET INSTRV- CTIONEM PERTINENT.
units.tr: CONCERNING THOSE THINGS WHICH PERTAIN TO HIS PERSON AND INSTRUCTION.

units.la: CAPUT PRIMUM.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Rem esse magni momenti sibi commissam intelligat; quandoquidem ex prima Novitiorum institutione, pendet maiori ex parte eorundem profectus, & ipses nostrae Societatis in Domino, curetque ut in dies per studium propriae perfectionis, instrumentum aptius ad eos iuvandos reddatur.
units.tr: He should understand that the charge committed to him is of great importance, since the progress of the novices, and in large part their spiritual welfare in the Lord, depends on their initial formation. Let him see to it that, through the study of his own perfection, he becomes day by day a more suitable instrument for helping them.

units.la: 2. Amabilem se praestet, & vitae integritate, ac discretione ita se gerat, ut omnes, qui in probatione sunt, ad eum in suis tentationibus confidenter confugiant, eiq; seipsos confidenter aperiant, & ab eo consolationem & auxilium in omnibus in Domino sperent.
units.tr: 2. Let him show himself lovable, and by his integrity of life and discretion conduct himself so that all who are under probation may confidently come to him in their temptations, open themselves to him with confidence, and hope from him for consolation and help in all things in the Lord.

units.la: 3. In Domibus probationis separatis praeter has regulas officij sui, habeat etiam regulas, & omnes facultates aliorum Rectorum, exceptis ijs, quae Novitiatui non conveniunt.
units.tr: 3. In separate houses of probation, besides the rules of his own office, let him also have the rules and all the faculties of other Rectors, except those that do not suit the novitiate.

units.la: 4. Habeat socium Sacerdotem fidelem & in rebus spiritualibus exercitatum à Provinciali designatum, qui in ijs, quae in Noviciatu agenda sunt, fit eius Coadiutor. Habeat etiam aliquem fratrem ex antiquioribus in virtute probatum, & prudentem, qui iuxta ordinem obedientiae, significet unicuique exercitia exteriora, in quibus occupandi sint, & manu ducat illos, cum opus est, ad illa facienda.
units.tr: 4. Let him have a fellow priest, faithful and experienced in spiritual matters, designated by the Provincial, who will be his coadjutor in those things that are to be done in the novitiate. Let him also have some brother from among the older members, proven in virtue and prudent, who, in accordance with the order of obedience, indicates to each the external exercises in which they are to be occupied, and leads them by the hand to perform them when necessary.

units.la: 5. In Domo probationis coniuncta Domui Professorum vel Collegio, habitatione tamen distincta, Magister Novitiorum erit subordinatus Praeposito, vel Rectori: non tamen erit sub obedientia Ministri, sicut nec eius socius: in ea autem Domo vel Collegio communis cognatio fit communis, mensa aliqua Novitijs & eorum Magistro designata.
units.tr: 5. In a house of probation joined to a house of professed members or to a college, though with separate lodging, the Master of Novices shall be subordinate to the Prepositus or Rector. Yet he shall not be under the obedience of the Minister, nor shall his companion be. In that house or college, however, common recreation is held in common, and some table is assigned to the novices and their Master.

units.la: 6. Hic Magister Novitiorum poenitentias in Noviciatu tantum suis Novitijs imponere poterit, extra vero non nisi consulto Superiore.
units.tr: 6. The Master of Novices may impose penances only on his own novices, and only within the novitiate; outside it, he may do so only after consulting the Superior.

units.la: 7. Habeat hic idem Magister Novitiorum potestatem ordinariam absolvendi à casibus reser- vatis referendis. ius reservatis Novitios, qui sub ipsius cura degunt, nisi eius Superiori haec facultas aliqua de causa restringenda videretur.
units.tr: 7. The same Master of Novices shall have the ordinary power of absolving from reserved cases, with regard to the novices who live under his care, unless his Superior judges that this faculty should be restricted for some reason.

units.la: 8. Versatum esse oportebit in lectione librorum spiritualium, ut deceptiones, quae in spiri- tuali vita accidunt, non tantum experimento, sed etiam lectione intelligat. Quibus auem utiliter ipse uti poterit, ij fere sunt, qui in subiecto catalogo numerantur. Novitiis vero eos tantum legendos tradet, qui nostro instituto conveniunt, ne quid ab eo alienum haujant, aut quacumque ratione quicquam detrimenti capiant.
units.tr: 8. He will need to be well versed in reading spiritual books, so that he understands the deceptions that occur in the spiritual life not only by experience but also by reading. Those books which he himself may use profitably are, for the most part, those listed in the catalogue below. He is to give novices only those books to read that agree with our Institute, lest they imbibe anything foreign to it or suffer harm in any way.

units.la: LIBRI AD VSVM MAGISTRI NOVITIORVM ACCOMMODATI.
units.tr: BOOKS SUITED TO THE USE OF THE NOVICE MASTER.

units.la: Basilij Ascetica, & Regulae. Gregorij Moralia. Augustini Confessiones, & Meditationes. Bernardus. Bonaventurae Opuscula. Cassianus. Homiliae Dorothei, Macharij, Caesarij Arelatensis Episcopi. Opuscula Ephrem, Nili, Esaiae Abbat. Diadocus. Ugo de S. Victore de Claustro animae. Ricardus de S. Victore. Vmbertus de eruditione Religiosorum. Innocentius de contemptu mundi. Thomas de Kempis de imitatione Christi, & alia eius opuscula. Vincentij tractatus de vita spirituali. Ludovici Blosij opera.
units.tr: The Ascetica and Rules of Basil. The Moralia of Gregory. The Confessions and Meditations of Augustine. Bernard. The little works of Bonaventure. Cassian. The Homilies of Dorotheus, of Macarius, and of Caesarius, Bishop of Arles. The little works of Ephrem, of Nilus, and of Isaiah the Abbot. Diadochus. Hugh of St Victor, On the Cloister of the Soul. Richard of St Victor. Humbert, On the Education of Religious. Innocent, On Contempt of the World. Thomas à Kempis, On the Imitation of Christ, and his other little works. The treatises of Vincent on the spiritual life. The works of Louis Blosius.

units.la: Dionysij Carthusiani opuscula. Albertus Magnus de Virtutibus. Epistolae Catharinae Senensis. Landulphus de vita Christi.
units.tr: The little works of Denys the Carthusian. Albert the Great, On the Virtues. The Letters of Catherine of Siena. Landulf, On the Life of Christ.

units.la: HISTORICI.
units.tr: HISTORIANS.

units.la: Gregorij Dialogi. Gregorius Turonensis De gloria Confessorum, & vita S. Martini. Eusebij Historia Ecclesiastica. Severus Sulpitius de vita S. Martini. Vitae Patrum selectae. Vitae SS. Lipomani & Surij. Petrus Damianus. Petrus Cluniacensis de miraculis. Literae Indicae. Vita Patris N. Ignatij, & alij similes ad Novitiorum utilitatem accommodati: ex quibus desumet aliquos pro illorum usu.
units.tr: The Dialogues of Gregory. Gregory of Tours, On the Glory of the Confessors, and the Life of St Martin. Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History. Severus Sulpicius, On the Life of St Martin. Selected Lives of the Fathers. The Lives of Saints Lipomanus and Surius. Peter Damian. Peter of Cluny, On Miracles. Letters from the Indies. The Life of our Father Ignatius, and others like them, adapted to the benefit of the novices; from these he will select some for their use.

units.la: DE PRIMA PROBATIONE.
units.tr: ON THE FIRST PROBATION.

units.la: CAPUT II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: Postquam in Domino statuetur, ad probationem aliquem admittendum esse in domo, vel habitatione separata primae probationis: hospitum more duodecim dies, vel viginti & amplius, prout Superiori videbitur, diversetur: ut eo tempore de ijs, quae pertinent ad Societatem, ipse certior reddatur, & Societas eundem plenius in Domino cognoscat.
units.tr: Once it has been settled in the Lord that a candidate is to be admitted to probation, he should be lodged in a house or separate residence of first probation, lodging like a guest for twelve days, or twenty and more, as the Superior sees fit, so that during that time he may be better informed about the things that pertain to the Society, and the Society may come to know him more fully in the Lord.

units.la: 10. Postridie ei declarabitur, quomodo in eo loco se gerere debeat, ac nominatim ne verbo, aut scripto (nisi Superiori aliqua de causa non levis momenti aliud videretur) cum externis, vel domesticis agat, praeterquam cum ijs, quos ad id Superior designaverit.
units.tr: 10. The next day it shall be explained to him how he ought to conduct himself in that place; and in particular that he is not to deal with outsiders or members of the household by word or in writing (unless the Superior, for some reason of no small weight, decides otherwise), except with those whom the Superior has designated for this purpose.

units.la: 11. Librum completum examinis absque declarationibus, Latina lingua pro ijs, qui im intelligunt, & vulgari pro alijs habeat, nec non & eisdem linguis Summarium Constitutionum, & regulas communes habere debet.
units.tr: 11. He should have the complete book of the examination, without explanations, in Latin for those who understand it and in the vernacular for the others; and likewise, in these same languages, a summary of the Constitutions and the common rules.

units.la: 12. Elapsis duobus aut tribus diebus examinari accuratius incipiat, & relinquatur ei scriptum praedictum examen, ut solus id maturius consideret, nisi in aliquo particulari aliud examen brevius proponendum esse Superior iudicaverit.
units.tr: 12. After two or three days he should begin to be examined more closely, and the said examination should be left with him in writing, so that he may consider it alone and more maturely, unless the Superior judges that a shorter examination on some particular point should be put to him.

units.la: 13. Postea literae Apostolicae Julij III. anno 1550. & Summarium Constitutionum, & Regulae communes eidem ostendantur, & relinquantur, ut omnia per otium magis consideret: is vero, qui literas Apostolicas Latinas non intelligerent, satis esset earum summam declarare.
units.tr: 13. Afterwards the apostolic letters of Julius III of the year 1550, together with the summary of the Constitutions and the common rules, are to be shown to him and left with him, so that he may consider everything at leisure; but for those who do not understand the Latin apostolic letters, it is enough to explain their substance to them.

units.la: 14. Ordo examinandi esse debet, in primis proponere, ac prosequi, quæ quatuor primis capitibus examinis continentur: deinde ea, quæ speciatim ad literatos pertinent, vel Coadjutores, vel Scholares, aut indifferentes: quamvis autem omnibus integrum examen relinquatur, non sunt tamen omnes particulariter examinandi, nisi de ijs, quæ ad utrumque pertinent, & si quid alicuius momenti occurrerit, quod Superiorem scire opporteat, scripto notabit.
units.tr: 14. The order of examining should be this: first to propose and pursue those matters which are contained in the first four chapters of the examination; then those which pertain specifically to the literate, or to the coadjutors, or to the scholastics, or to the undecided; although the whole examination is left to everyone, not all are to be examined in detail, except on those points which apply to each. If anything of some importance arises which the Superior ought to know, he shall note it in writing.

units.la: 15. In his omnibus proponendis, & declarandis paulatim procedatur, ut qui examinantur, res omnes nostri instituti, iuxta ipsorum gradum bene percipiant, ad suam majorem satisfactionem, & stabilitatem: & illa præsertim sunt magis explicanda, quæ postea aliquam difficultatem afferre possent, ut de animi promptitudine ad serviendum Deo ubique, & in re quavis, de manifestatione suorum defectuum iuxta Constitutiones, de indifferentia ad gradus Societatis in Scholaribus, & literatis, & de manifestatione conscientiæ, statutis temporibus.
units.tr: 15. In proposing and explaining all these things, one should proceed gradually, so that those being examined may grasp all the matters of our Institute well, according to their own level, for their greater satisfaction and steadfastness; and especially those points should be explained more fully which might afterwards cause some difficulty: such as readiness of spirit to serve God everywhere and in any matter, the manifestation of one's defects according to the Constitutions, indifference to the grades of the Society among scholastics and the literate, and the manifestation of conscience at the appointed times.

units.la: 16. Si quis ad studia maiorem propensionem quam par esset, & minorem indifferentiam, quam ad alia ministeria Societatis præferret, & videretur nihilominus ad ea minus aptus, non tantum proponatur ei scriptum examen, ut reliquis, sed & accurate illi explicetur, interrogeturque an patienter se dimitti sinet a Societate, dummodo ab omni voto ac promissione liber maneat.
units.tr: 16. If anyone shows a greater inclination to studies than is fitting, and less indifference than he should toward the other ministries of the Society, and seems nonetheless less apt for them, he should not only be given the written examination, as the others are, but the matter should also be explained to him carefully, and he should be asked whether he would willingly allow himself to be dismissed from the Society, provided he remains free of every vow and promise.

units.la: 17. Admoneatur, ut vere omnino, ac sincere respondeat: nam aliter multa gravia incommoda inde oriri possent: & nihilominus admonere Confessarium oportet, ut si quis vere non respondisset, eius de ea re conscientiam stimulet.
units.tr: 17. He is to be admonished to answer truly and sincerely in every respect, for otherwise many serious inconveniences could arise from it; and nevertheless the Confessor ought to admonish him, so that if anyone had not answered truthfully, he may stir his conscience about that matter.

units.la: 18. Si quid erit in interrogationibus, quod secretum requirat, id observabitur, ut par est, & interrogato placuerit: declaretur tamen ei, quod iuxta Constitutiones licebit remota omnem Superiori manifestare.
units.tr: 18. If there is anything in the questions that requires secrecy, it shall be observed as is fitting and as the one questioned is content; yet it is to be declared to him that, according to the Constitutions, he may at any time, without exception, disclose it to the Superior.

units.la: 19. Promittat rettulurum se omnia bona sua post unum annum ab ingressu, quandocunque injunctum a Superiore ei fuerit: & declaretur, quod actus huius promissionis, nec votum est, nec solum propositum, sed promissio simplex, illa conditione affecta, si ipse perseveraverit, & Superior ei injunxerit.
units.tr: 19. He is to promise that he will hand over all his goods after one year from his entrance, whenever the Superior shall enjoin it on him; and it is to be explained that the act of this promise is neither a vow nor merely a purpose, but a simple promise, bound by the condition that he persevere and that the Superior enjoin it on him.

units.la: 20. Hoc tempore primæ probationis per quinque vel sex dies accurate informentur prædicto modo de ijs, quæ ad institutum, & ad ipsos pertinent, & lectione alicujus pij libelli, qualis esset de imitatione Christi, subinde recreentur.
units.tr: 20. During this time of first probation, for five or six days he is to be thoroughly informed in the aforesaid manner about the things that pertain to the Institute and to himself, and from time to time he is to be refreshed by the reading of some devout little book, such as the one on the Imitation of Christ.

units.la: 21. Coadjutores vero temporales, qui legere non didicerunt, aut qui minus ad hæc tractanda idonei videbuntur, quamvis in propria vocatione iuxta ipsorum captum, plene instituendi sunt: poterunt tamen hoc tempore aliquo exercitio corporali, aut labore manuum, judicio Superiorum occupari, sejuncti tamen ab alijs.
units.tr: 21. Temporal coadjutors, however, who have not learned to read, or who seem less fit for these matters, although they are to be fully instructed in their own vocation according to their capacity, may nevertheless during this time be occupied, at the judgment of the Superiors, with some bodily exercise or manual labour, but kept apart from the others.

units.la: 22. Deinde qui literis operam dederunt, de singulis facultatibus, in quibus versati sunt, singulas prælegant lectiones coram eis, qui a Superiore ad eorum talentum cognoscendum in doctrina, & proponendi modo sunt constituti, & postea exhortationem unam quisque faciat.
units.tr: 22. Then those who have devoted themselves to letters shall each recite, before those appointed by the Superior to judge their talent in doctrine and their manner of proposing, a single lesson from each of the subjects in which they have been trained; and afterwards each shall deliver one exhortation.

units.la: 23. Tum si quis, antequam fuerit in Societatem admissus, spiritualia exercitia non fecerit, hoc primum experimentum (ut sequenti capite, ubi de experimentis agitur, mox dicetur) iuxta 4. c. Exa. f. 10. aggrediatur, & iuxta exercitia suo tempore generaliter confiteatur, nisi ante ingressum, fuerit alicui de Societate, generaliter confessus: tunc enim satis erit, si ab eo tempore generalem confessionem incipiat: & eodem tempore conscientiam suam Superiori, aut ei, quem Superior designaverit, aperiat, iuxta Pa. 1. Const. c. 4. f. 6. & si ab aliqua censura virtute nostrorum privilegiorum absolutus fuerit, admoneatur quod si non perseveraverit, in eandem reincidet. Declaretur etiam illi, si qua vota cum admhuc esset in seculo emisit (præterquam religionis determinatæ) in nostra Societate tam diu suspensa esse, dum ipse in Societate manserit: quod si recesserit, eadem obligatione teneri, qua ante ingressum tenebatur. Expleto autem tempore huius experimenti, sanctis. Eucharistiæ Sacramentum accipiet, & communem domum habitationis ingrediatur, ubi cum alijs versari, & in fecunda probatione diutius exerceri Novitij solent.
units.tr: 23. Then, if anyone has not made the spiritual exercises before being admitted into the Society, he shall begin this first experiment (as will be said shortly in the following chapter, where experiments are discussed) according to chapter 4 of the Examen, paragraph 10, and in accordance with the exercises he shall make a general confession at the appropriate time, unless before entering he has made a general confession to someone of the Society; for then it will suffice that he begin a general confession from that time. At the same time he shall open his conscience to the Superior, or to the one whom the Superior designates, according to Part 1, Constitution chapter 4, paragraph 6. And if he has been absolved from some censure by virtue of our privileges, he is to be warned that if he does not persevere he will fall back into the same. It is also to be declared to him that any vows he made while still in the world (other than to a specific religious order) are suspended for as long as he remains in our Society; but if he withdraws, he will be bound by the same obligation that held him before entering. When the time of this experiment has been completed, he shall receive the Sacrament of the Eucharist and enter the common dwelling, where the novices are accustomed to live with the others and to be exercised more at length in the second probation.

units.la: 24. Si vel cuiusquam valetudo, vel aliqua temporis aut personæ ratio persuaserit, non esse tam diu hæc mentalia exercitia continuanda, antequam exercitia aggrediatur, per quas tuor vel quinq; dies vacare, & separatim recreari poterit: vel si Magistro Novitiorum videretur, facta confessione generali: & per aliis exercitijs prima hebdomadæ. Sed quando hæc relaxatio longius ob valetudinem aut aliam rationem protrahenda Magistro Novitiorum visa fuerit, poterit sumpta Eucharistia etiam ad communem convictum admitti; & ubi firmior fuerit, sua exercitia peraget.
units.tr: 24. If the health of anyone, or some consideration of time or person, persuades that these mental exercises should not be continued so long, then before beginning the exercises he may have four or five days free and be refreshed separately; or, if it seems so to the Master of Novices, after a general confession is made, he may take up the other exercises of the first week. But when this relaxation is judged by the Master of Novices to need to be prolonged longer on account of health or some other reason, he may, after receiving the Eucharist, also be admitted to the common life; and when he has grown stronger, he shall carry out his exercises.

units.la: 25. Si Superior iudicaverit eum domi retinendum, curet, ut in libro ad id designato, quæ penes se Procurator habere debet, scribatur quicquid unusquisq; domum attulerit, cum subscriptione eius qui examinatus est, & ut hæc alicubi separatim asserventur, quousque biennio expleto consueta vota emiserit.
units.tr: 25. If the Superior judges that he should be kept at home, he shall see to it that whatever each one has brought into the house is written in the book designated for this purpose, which the Procurator ought to keep in his own possession, with the signature of the one who was examined; and that these things are kept somewhere separately until, after two years have been completed, he makes the usual vows.

units.la: 26. In alio libro, quem apud se habebit, notabit diem & annum ingressus uniuscuiusque, incipiendo à die, quo primum probationem intravit, & nomen, & patriam, & quod contentus sit observare omnia ei proposita. Quando vero aliqui in Coadiutores temporales, & indifferentes admittentur, speciatim id scripto declaretur, quod ut tales examinati, & admissi fuerint: & hæc, qui examinatus est, manu sua subscribat, & si scribere nescit, alius nomine scribat.
units.tr: 26. In another book, which he himself shall keep, he shall note the day and year of each one's entrance, beginning from the day on which he first entered probation, and his name, his homeland, and that he is content to observe all that has been set before him. When, however, some are admitted as temporal coadjutors and undecided, it is to be declared in writing specifically that they were examined and admitted as such; and the one who was examined shall sign this with his own hand, and if he does not know how to write, another shall write it in his name.

units.la: DE SECVNDA PROBATIONE.
units.tr: On the Second Probation.

units.la: CAPVT III. De Experimentis.
units.tr: CHAPTER III. On the Experiments.
