units.la: 27. IN primis diligenter curet, ut Novitij sex illis experimentis, quæ in Constitutionibus traduntur, feria, & cum desiderato fructu exerceantur, intelligat, præcipuam Noviciatus partem in his probationibus positam esse.
units.tr: 27. Above all, let him take care diligently that the novices perform, on the appointed days and with the desired fruit, those six experiments which are laid down in the Constitutions, and let him understand that the chief part of the novitiate lies in these probations.

units.la: 28. Exercitia spiritualia primum singulis, eo quo protedunt ordine præscripto tempore atque exactè tradantur, secundum uniuscuiusque dispositionem, & captum, iuxta regulas libri Exercitiorum: prætermissis tamen his, quæ ad electiones spectant: ut inde, præter alia, certam, ac nostro instituto consentaneam, mente, & voce, orandi rationem habeant, quam in posterum servare debebant.
units.tr: 28. The Spiritual Exercises are to be given to each one first, in the order prescribed, at the appointed time and exactly, according to the disposition and capacity of each, following the rules of the book of Exercises, but omitting those things which pertain to the elections; so that they may thereby acquire, among other things, a certain manner of praying, both in mind and voice, consonant with our Institute, which they ought to observe in the future.

units.la: 29. Quoad secundum experimentum, quo hospitalibus per mensem servire debent, videbit ipse quid magis expediat, an nostros ibidem cibum capere, & dormire, an vero per aliquot horas quotidie ministerium ægris impendere.
units.tr: 29. As for the second experiment, in which they must serve the hospitals for a month, he himself will see what is more expedient: whether our men should take their food and sleep there, or rather devote some hours each day to ministering to the sick.

units.la: 30 In hac probatione advertat, ne nostri nimio fervore suæ valetudini noceant, aut periculo contagionis alicuius morbi se exponant: admonebitq;, ne ingrediantur partem illam Xenodochij, ubi mulieres habitare solent.
units.tr: 30. In this probation he shall take care that our men do not harm their health through excessive zeal, or expose themselves to the danger of contagion from any disease; and he shall warn them not to enter that part of the hospital where women are accustomed to live.

units.la: 31. Mense alio ad peregrinandum sine pecunia mittantur, ostiatim pro Christi amore mendicando, ut ad incommoditatem comedendi, & dormiendi assuescant, & ut omni spe abiecta, quam in pecunijs, & rebus alijs creatis possent constituere, eam integrè, & vera cum fiducia in Domino constituant.
units.tr: 31. In another month they are to be sent on pilgrimage without money, begging from door to door for the love of Christ, so that they may grow accustomed to the discomfort of eating and sleeping, and so that, with every hope abandoned which they might place in money and other created things, they may place it wholly and with true confidence in the Lord.

units.la: 32. Advertendum, ne imbecilles, aut tenerioris ætatis his peregrinationibus notabile detrimentum patiantur, ne fiant asperiore hyeme, aut ferventiore æstate: illisq; regulas Peregrinorum, literas patentes, & cum opus erit, particularem etiam instructionem tradet, & ab ultimo loco ad quem perveniunt, testimonium à Superiore Domus, vel Collegij Societatis, si ibi fuerit, vel ab alio fide digno secum ferant, quod suam devotionem secuti sine illa cuiusque querela eo pervenerint: & in secundo, quinto, & sexto experimento, iuxta constitutiones idem servetur.
units.tr: 32. Care must be taken that the weak or those of tender age do not suffer notable harm from these pilgrimages, nor undertake them in a harsher winter or a hotter summer. He shall give them the rules for pilgrims, open letters, and, when needed, particular instruction as well; and from the last place to which they come they shall bring with them a testimonial from the Superior of the House or College of the Society, if there is one there, or else from another trustworthy person, stating that, having followed their devotion, they arrived there without anyone's complaint. In the second, fifth and sixth experiments the same is to be observed according to the Constitutions.

units.la: 33. In quarto experimento, quo in officijs abiectis exercentur, advertat, ne nimia corporis fatigatione, spiritus obruatur: & à Scholasticis fiat potius ad propriam cuiusque abnegationem, & humiliationem, quam pro domestica aliqua necessitate. Dum autem hæc probatio fit in Domo probationis, vacabit qui ita probatur, ab aliis exercitijs aliorum Novitiorum exceptis conferentijs, & exhortatione ordinaria.
units.tr: 33. In the fourth experiment, in which they are exercised in abject offices, he shall take care that the spirit is not overwhelmed by excessive bodily fatigue; and the scholastics should undertake these offices chiefly for the sake of each one's own self-denial and humbling, rather than for some domestic need. While this probation is carried out in the House of Probation, the one so tested shall be free from the other exercises of the novices, except the conferences and the ordinary exhortation.

units.la: 34. Cum hæc probatio non fit in Domo probationis, sed in Domibus professis, aut Collegijs, sit aliquis, qui Novitiorum peculiarem curam gerat, ubi in recreatione separati sint, adiunctis aliis, à quibus in Domino adiuvari possint.
units.tr: 34. When this probation is not carried out in the House of Probation, but in professed houses or colleges, let there be someone who takes special care of the novices, where they are kept apart at recreation, with others added who can help them in the Lord.

units.la: 35. In docenda doctrina Christiana pueros, ac personas rudes, publice vel privatim, pro ut occasio se obtulerit, & in Domino ei commodius visum fuerit, tanquam in propria nostri instituti Novitios exercendos curabit, habita personarum ratione.
units.tr: 35. In teaching Christian doctrine to children and uneducated persons, publicly or privately, as occasion offers and as seems more suitable in the Lord, he shall see to it that the novices are exercised in this as in a proper work of our Institute, with regard had to the persons.

units.la: 36. In confessionibus audiendis, & praedicatione Divini verbi domi, aut foris, circa finem primi anni probentur, qui ad huiusmodi ministeria idonei invenientur, & bonae ædificationis specimen in dederint; eo tamen modo, ne tanquam operarij ordinarij ad ministeria haec exercenda exponantur, sed brevi tempore, & ad probationem.
units.tr: 36. Those who are found suitable for such ministries, and have given a sample of good edification, shall be tested near the end of the first year in hearing confessions and in preaching the divine Word at home or abroad; yet in such a way that they are not exposed to these ministries as ordinary workers, but for a short time and by way of probation.

units.la: 37. Tametsi exercitia spiritualia exactè omnibus in principio tradenda sunt, quoad reliqua tamen experimenta, si quod eorum permutandum, aut multum moderandum iudicaret, id ne faciat inconsulto Provinciali: quamquam anteponere, aut postponere ipse ea poterit, pro ratione personarum, temporum, aut locorum.
units.tr: 37. Although the Spiritual Exercises must be given exactly to all at the beginning, as for the remaining experiments, if he judges that any of them should be changed or considerably moderated, he must not do so without consulting the Provincial; though he himself may place them before or after, according to the circumstances of persons, times or places.

units.la: 38. Advertat, ut hæ probationes inter se debitis spatijs distinguantur, ita, ut Novitij una peracta, aliquandiu ad solita exercitia Domus probationis redeant, ut corpore, & spiritu recreati, uberiorem fructum ex praeteritis laboribus colligant, ea tamen ratione, ut intra annum omnes absolvantur. Quod si peculiari aliqua de causa, hæ probationes ad secundum annum differenda viderentur, prius Provinciali consulatur.
units.tr: 38. Let him take care that these probations are distinguished from one another by due intervals, so that, when one has been completed, the novices return for a while to the usual exercises of the House of Probation, that refreshed in body and spirit they may gather richer fruit from their past labours; yet in such a way that all are finished within the year. But if for some special reason these probations seem to be deferred to the second year, the Provincial shall first be consulted.

units.la: 39. Praeter hæc experimenta, alia fieri hoc biennio probationis possunt, & hæc eadem ex parte repeti, quando in Domino ita expedire iudicaverit, & quidem omnia cum maturitate, & prudentia, ædificatione etiam exteriorum, sunt facienda.
units.tr: 39. Besides these experiments, others may be made during these two years of probation, and these same may in part be repeated whenever he judges it expedient in the Lord; and indeed all things are to be done with maturity and prudence, with regard also to the edification of outsiders.

units.la: DE INSTITVTIONE ET REGIMINE NOVITIORVM.
units.tr: ON THE INSTRUCTION AND GOVERNANCE OF NOVICES.

units.la: 40. NE fiant mortificationes publicae, nisi ordinariae, iuxta Constitutiones, ut sunt praeter solita experimenta; petere ostiatim eleemosynam, comitari Emptorem, ad comportanda ea quae emuntur, indui vestibus vilioribus, quae tamen religiosos deceant; & alia id genus, ut in officio Rectoris dicitur.
units.tr: 40. Public mortifications shall not be undertaken except the ordinary ones, according to the Constitutions, such as are over and above the usual trials: begging alms from door to door, accompanying the purchaser to carry what has been bought, wearing coarser clothing which nevertheless befits religious, and others of that kind, as is stated in the office of the Rector.

units.la: 41. Convenit, ut qui probantur, vestitus ratione ad mortificationem, & abnegationem sui, & ad mundum eiusque vanitatem sub pedibus conculcandam iuventur, & id quidem quantum consuetudo, officium, & personarum circumstantia patientur. Discretioni autem eius relinquitur, habita ratione ædificationis, an cum eisdem vestibus, quas ex saeculo tulerunt, incedere sint permittendi, an vero cum alijs eas permutari oporteat.
units.tr: 41. It is fitting that those who are being tested be helped, in respect of clothing, towards mortification and self-denial, and towards trampling the world and its vanity under foot; and this indeed as far as custom, duty and the circumstances of the persons allow. But it is left to his discretion, having regard to edification, whether they are to be permitted to go about in the clothes they brought from the world, or whether it is right to exchange these for others.

units.la: 42. Conferet, ut aliquando occasionem praebeat ijs, qui probantur, exercendi obedientiae & paupertatis virtutem; eosdem tentando ad maiorem ipsorum utilitatem spiritualem, in hoc tamen mensura, iuxta uniuscuiusque vires, observetur.
units.tr: 42. It will be useful at times to give those who are being tested an occasion of exercising the virtue of obedience and poverty, testing them for their greater spiritual profit; yet in this a measure is to be observed, according to the strength of each one.

units.la: 43. In poenitentijs, & corporis afflictionibus advertat, ne nimius huiusmodi rerum usus tantopere vires debilitet, ut postea ad ministeria nostri instituti inutiles reddantur; nec contra, tanta in illis fit relaxatio, ut fervore spiritus refrigescente, humani ac inferiores affectus intalescant.
units.tr: 43. In penances and bodily afflictions he shall take care that such practices are not used so excessively that they weaken their strength so greatly that they are afterwards rendered useless for the ministries of our Institute; nor, on the other hand, that there be such relaxation in them that, with the fervour of spirit growing cold, human and lower affections grow strong.

units.la: 44. Lectiones fiant de his, quae ad institutum pertinent, & continentur Literis Apostolicis, Regulis, & Constitutionibus, praecipue vero de ijs, quae in examine, & tertia parte habentur, aut de alijs quae eo referuntur, mutata interdum materia, ut taedium tollatur: modus vero lectionum facilis sit, & simplex, & ad Novitiorum animos ad instituti amorem, & solidarum virtutum perfectionem promovendos accommodatus.
units.tr: 44. Lectures shall be given on those matters which pertain to the Institute and are contained in the Apostolic Letters, the Rules and the Constitutions, especially on those things which are treated in the examination and in the third part, or on other matters that relate to these, the subject being varied at times so that weariness is removed; the manner of the lectures, however, shall be easy and simple, and adapted to fostering in the minds of the novices a love of the Institute and the attainment of solid virtues.

units.la: 45. Explicetur brevi enarratione doctrina Christiana, ac modus bene, & cum fructu confitendi, communicandi, Missam audiendi, & eidem decenter ministrandi, orandi itidem meditandi, & libros denique pios legendi pro captu uniuscuiusque tradatur.
units.tr: 45. The Christian doctrine is to be explained by a brief exposition, and the manner of confessing, communicating, hearing Mass well and with profit, and of serving at it becomingly, as well as of praying and meditating likewise, and finally of reading pious books, is to be taught according to each one's capacity.

units.la: 46. Admoneat crebrò Novitios, ut in omnibus rebus Deum quærant, & in suis actibus intentionem puram ad Dei beneplacitum dirigant, ut familiares cum Deo in spiritualibus devotionis exercitijs esse curent: & tandem ita sint instructi Novitij, ut nihil persectionis, quod divina gratia consequi possint in absoluta nostri instituti observatione, prætermittant.
units.tr: 46. He shall often admonish the novices to seek God in all things, and to direct a pure intention to God's good pleasure in their actions, and to take care to be familiar with God in the spiritual exercises of devotion; and at length the novices are to be so instructed that they omit nothing of perfection which they can attain by divine grace in the complete observance of our Institute.

units.la: 47. Omnes perfectos habeat, ut magis illis prodesse possit, ad quod juvabit, cum illis frequenter singulatim agere, & rationem ab unoquoque rerum suarum fiduciter exigere: in his autem privatis colloquijs magnam utilitatem positam esse sciat.
units.tr: 47. He should have all of them under his care, so that he may be more useful to them; to this end it will help to deal with them frequently one by one, and to demand with confidence an account of their affairs from each one; he should know that a great benefit lies in these private conversations.

units.la: 48. Det operam, ut Novitij religiosam modestiam præ se ferant, juxta Constitutiones, & regulas, quæ de ea conscriptæ sunt, in quibus tempore Novitiatus diligenter instituendi erunt.
units.tr: 48. He shall take pains that the novices display religious modesty, according to the Constitutions and the rules written concerning it, in which they are to be diligently instructed during the time of the novitiate.

units.la: 49. Cognoscat, quem procedendi modum in oratione, & examine fervent: & petat interdum, an contra aliquem defectum adhibeant examen particulare, & quando resistunt tentationibus, an proprijs remedijs utantur: In acquirendis virtutibus, quam rationem teneant: & intelligat demum, an in his omnibus præstent ea, quæ ab ipso acceperunt.
units.tr: 49. He shall learn what method of procedure they follow in prayer and in the examination, and from time to time he shall ask whether they use the particular examen against some defect, and when they resist temptations, whether they use their own remedies; what plan they keep in acquiring virtues; and finally he shall understand whether in all these things they excel in what they have received from him.

units.la: 50. Si aliquis solicitetur, vel perturbetur ab hominibus, qui in via spiritus non bene procedunt, & expediat illum in alium locum transferri, Provincialem tempestive monEAT.
units.tr: 50. If anyone is disturbed or troubled by men who do not progress well in the way of the spirit, and it is expedient to transfer him to another place, he shall duly advise the Provincial.

units.la: 51. Si duo in eodem cubiculo habitent, alter eorum eiusmodi sit, ut minime dubitetur, quin alter sit eius Societate profecturus, & eadem ob causam inter cubicula, quæ seorsum unicuique uniorum assignantur, par est, aliquos maturos ex antiquioribus intermisceri.
units.tr: 51. If two live in the same cell, one of them should be of such a kind that there is no doubt the other will leave the Society for that reason; and for the same cause it is proper that some mature men from the senior members be mixed among the cells which are assigned separately to each of the younger ones.

units.la: 52. Si aliquando permittendum videretur, ut aliquis consanguineos, vel amicos, quos in oculo habebat, alloqueretur, coram aliquo à Superiore ad id designato, id fiat, & breviter, nisi particulares ob causas aliud statueret Superior totius Domus, vel Collegij.
units.tr: 52. If at any time it should seem right to permit someone to speak with relatives or friends whom he had in view, let it be done in the presence of someone designated for this by the Superior, and briefly, unless the Superior of the whole house or college decides otherwise for particular reasons.

units.la: 53. Novitij non sunt, ut plurimum, assignandi in officios nostris, qui adeunt domos secularium, nec debent habere officia publica, in quibus necessarium sit agere cum externis, ut Emptoris, Ianitoris, & Sacristæ.
units.tr: 53. Novices are, for the most part, not to be assigned to our offices which visit the houses of secular people, nor should they hold public offices in which it is necessary to deal with outsiders, such as those of purchaser, doorkeeper and sacristan.

units.la: 54. Videat, num aliqui in schedulis, Novitijs assignandi sint, ut cum eis loqui possint, eorum exemplo, & colloquijs proficiant in Domino, & si cum alijs sine facultate egerint, debitam eis pœnitentiam iniungat.
units.tr: 54. Let him see whether any of them are to be assigned to schedules, so that they may speak with them, and profit in the Lord by their example and conversations; and if they have dealt with others without permission, let him impose a suitable penance upon them.

units.la: 55. Admoneat eos, ne vota ante biennium emittant sine Superioris facultate, quam in primo anno Novitiatus, solus Provincialis re mature considerata dare poterit. Horum autem, qui hæc vota semel apud se ex licentia Superioris, juxta formulam Societatis, emiserint, memoria in libro aliquo asservetur, & postea tempore Novitiatus, his in annis latutis temporibus, seorsum ab alijs, qui biennium expleverunt, ipsi simul inter se illa renovabunt.
units.tr: 55. He shall admonish them not to take vows before the two years are over without the Superior's permission, which in the first year of the novitiate only the Provincial, after mature consideration, can give. Of those who have once taken these vows with the Superior's licence, according to the formula of the Society, the memory of them is to be kept in some book, and afterwards, during the novitiate, in these years at the appointed times, separately from the others who have completed the two years, they shall renew those vows among themselves.

units.la: 56. Diligenter observare debet in toto probationis decursu, an ineptus aliquis, aut inutilis nostro instituto probabiliter futurus sit: in quo maior habenda est ratio boni communis Societatis ad gloriam Dei, quam particularis cuiusque: quid autem sentiat in hac re, ad minimum sexto quoque mense ad Provincialem scribat, ut ipse provideat.
units.tr: 56. Throughout the whole course of the probation he must carefully observe whether anyone is likely to prove unfit or useless for our Institute; in which case the good of the Society as a whole, for the glory of God, is to be weighed above that of each individual; and what he thinks about this matter he shall write to the Provincial at least every sixth month, so that he himself may make provision.

units.la: 57. De singulis etiam sub finem biennij ad eundem scribat, ut cum illius facultate convicta vota Societatis emittant, aut diutius probentur: prius autem quam vota emittant, per hebdomadæ spatium se colligant, & aliqua exercitia spiritualia, præter alia, quæ prescripta sunt, faciant.
units.tr: 57. Towards the end of the two years he shall also write to the same about each one, so that, with his permission, those who have been convinced may take the vows of the Society, or be tested longer; but before they take their vows, they shall gather themselves together for a week and perform some spiritual exercises besides those that have been prescribed.

units.la: 58. Scholastici, qui studijs absolutis tertium probationis annum peragunt, in variis experimentis, & speciatim in nonnullis iam dictis, quam vis illis prius jam perfunctis fuerint, probentur. Huius autem probationis tempore in schola affectus se exerceant, & in rebus spiritualibus, & corporalibus, quæ ad profectum in humilitate, & abnegatione universi amoris sensualis, voluntatis, & judicij proprij, & ad maiorem cognitionem, & amorem Dei conferunt, insistant.
units.tr: 58. Scholastics, who after finishing their studies undertake the third year of probation, are to be tested in various trials, and especially in some already mentioned, although they have previously gone through them. During the time of this probation they shall exercise themselves in the school in the affections, and shall devote themselves to those spiritual and bodily matters which contribute to progress in humility and in the denial of all sensual love, of will and of one's own judgment, and to a greater knowledge and love of God.

units.la: 59. Adhibeat diligentiam, ut Coadjutores temporales in modo orandi juxta Constitutiones instruantur, eosque mysteria Rosarij doceat, & privatim instruat, ut ad suâ vocationem ministeria afficiantur, & forte Marthæ contenti sint.
units.tr: 59. He shall take care that the temporal coadjutors are instructed in the manner of prayer according to the Constitutions, and he shall teach them the mysteries of the Rosary and instruct them privately, so that they may be disposed to their ministries according to their vocation, and may perhaps be content with the part of Martha.

units.la: 60. Exhortationibus ordinarijs omnes intersint. Coadjutores tamen temporales, & indifferentes non interrogentur in Conferentijs, nisi cum rerum & personarum delectu, nec ad Tonos conveniant: & ij quidem per sex menses ad minimum in domo probationis sint, reliquo autem biennij tempore, sic sub cura Magistri erunt: ut aliis officijs ad instar aliorum Coadjutorum vacare possint, & tempus ordinarium orationis Domus, vel Collegij, ubi agent, habeant: experimenta tamen, ad quæ apti fuerint, intra annum absolvant.
units.tr: 60. All shall attend the ordinary exhortations. The temporal coadjutors and the indifferent, however, are not to be questioned in the Conferences except with a choice of matters and persons, nor are they to gather for the Tones; and these are to be at least six months in the house of probation, but for the rest of the two years they will thus be under the care of the Master, so that they may be free for other duties in the manner of the other coadjutors, and have the ordinary time of prayer of the house or college where they work; they are, however, to complete the trials for which they were fit within the year.

units.la: 61. Quando erit concio domi, vel in Ecclesia, quam Novitij sint audituri, eo die à Lectionibus, & Conferentijs, & Tonis liberi erunt.
units.tr: 61. When there is a sermon at home or in the church which the novices are to hear, on that day they shall be free from lectures, conferences and the Tones.

units.la: 62. Singulis hebdomadis, die una à solitis exercitijs vacent, in qua aliquid honestæ recreationis poterunt sumere domi vel foris.
units.tr: 62. Once a week they are to be free from the usual exercises for one day, on which they may take some honest recreation at home or abroad.

units.la: DE EXAMINE SEMESTRI NOVITIORVM.
units.tr: ON THE SIX-MONTHLY EXAMINATION OF NOVICES.

units.la: 63. Exto quoque mense per biennium probationis, literas Apostolicas & Regulas unusquisque videre, & considerare debet, Et examen, relicto secundo & tertio capite, & aliis, quæ ad gradum suum non pertinent, ut Regula 12. & 13. dictum est, deinde postquam hæc omnia viderit, interrogetur.
units.tr: 63. In the sixth month of the two years of probation, each one ought to read and consider the Apostolic letters and the Rules, leaving aside the second and third chapters and other matters that do not pertain to his rank, as was said of Rules 12 and 13. Then, after he has read all these things, he is to be questioned.

units.la: 64. An prædictis omnibus contentus sit, an vero aliquid dubij, vel difficultatis circa ea occurrat, quæ experimenta peregerit, & quo modo in illis se habuerit.
units.tr: 64. Whether he is content with all the foregoing, or whether any doubt or difficulty arises for him concerning them; what experiments he has undergone, and how he has conducted himself in them.

units.la: 65. An vires sibi corporales, & spirituales suppetere sentiat ad labores perferendos, qui in Societate requiruntur: num deliberatum habeat animi propositum vivendi & moriendi in hac Societate IESV Domini nostri.
units.tr: 65. Whether he feels that he has the bodily and spiritual strength to endure the labours required in the Society; and whether he has a settled purpose of mind to live and to die in this Society of Jesus our Lord.

units.la: 66. Examen hoc factum notetur scripto, ut constet. Quod si quid novi occurrat, aut si qua mutatio alicuius momenti accidat, Superiorem certiorem reddat.
units.tr: 66. This examination, once held, is to be recorded in writing, so that it may be established. If anything new arises, or if some change of importance occurs, he is to inform the Superior.

units.la: 67. Demum qui sic examinatus est, reddet rationem conscientiæ suæ Superiori, aut ei quem Superior delegaverit, & ab ultima confessione generali incipiendo generaliter confitebitur Sacerdoti, qui fuerit à Superiori designatus.
units.tr: 67. Finally, the one who has been examined in this way shall give an account of his conscience to the Superior, or to the one whom the Superior has appointed, and beginning from his last general confession, he shall make a general confession to the priest whom the Superior has designated.

units.la: DE ORDINE DOMVS PROBATIONIS.
units.tr: ON THE ORDER OF THE HOUSE OF PROBATION.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: 68. Novitij mane post pulsum campanæ, dum surgunt, dum se induunt, & lectum delicenter operiunt, aliquas orationes ad Deum fundant, aut aliquid in Domino meditentur, & reliquo semihoræ spatio, pia aliqua lectione, aut alia ratione ad orationem se præparare poterunt.
units.tr: 68. When the novices rise in the morning after the ringing of the bell, as they dress and gently make their beds, they may offer some prayers to God or meditate on something in the Lord, and in the remaining half hour they may prepare themselves for prayer by some pious reading or in some other way.

units.la: 69. Postea integram horam orationi mentali, aut vocali, vel meditationi dent, iuxta cuiusque captum, & Magistri Novitiorum instructionem.
units.tr: 69. Afterwards they are to devote a full hour to mental prayer, or vocal prayer, or meditation, according to each one's capacity and the instruction of the Master of Novices.

units.la: 70. Absoluta oratione, media illis conceditur hora ad lectum, & cubiculum componendum, & ad dispiciendum, quem fructum ex oratione collegerint.
units.tr: 70. When prayer is finished, they are allowed a half hour to tidy the bed and cell, and to consider what fruit they have gathered from the prayer.

units.la: 71. Post hæc, Missam devote, & reverenter audiant, quâ absoluta, intersint lectioni seu exhortationi, quæ de rebus spiritualibus bis in hebdomada, per dimidiam horam, illis fiet: reliqua autem dimidia statim repetent audita, & conferent inter se terni, aut quaterni, sine ulla disputatione, sed cum humilitate, & modestia.
units.tr: 71. After this they are to hear Mass devoutly and reverently. When it is over, they are to attend the reading or exhortation on spiritual matters, which will be given to them twice a week for half an hour. The other half hour they shall immediately repeat what they have heard, and confer together in groups of three or four, without any dispute, but with humility and modesty.

units.la: 72. Sequenti die, ijs de rebus, ut melius ad praxin reducantur, eadem hora fient collationes, hac ratione, ut lectione præcedenti breviter per unum, aut plures à Magistro designatos repetita, proponat aliquis, quomodo vincatur talis tentatio, aut difficultas in re propositâ, aut unde oriatur hoc, vel illud impedimentum, & quid remedij possit adhiberi, & alia similia: postquam autem aliqui dixerint, quid sibi occurrat, Magister constituet, quid tenendum sit.
units.tr: 72. On the following day, so that these matters may be better put into practice, there shall be conferences in the same hour, in this way: after the previous reading has been briefly repeated by one or more designated by the Master, someone shall propose how such a temptation or difficulty in the matter proposed may be overcome, or whence this or that hindrance arises, and what remedy may be applied, and other such things. But after some have said what occurs to them, the Master shall decide what is to be held.

units.la: 73. Reliquo toto tempore usque ad examen, quod semper ante prandium fiet, per quartam horae partem in suis officijs, aut in aliquo exercitio corporali, aut labore manuum à Magistro Novitiorum praescripto occupabuntur: aliquid tamen temporis quotidie praesertim ante prandium, tribuant Regulis, & Doctrina Christiana, & alijs, quae judicio Magistri Novitiorum cuiq; convenient, addiscendis, & memoriae mandandis.
units.tr: 73. For the rest of the time until the examination, which shall always take place before dinner, they shall be occupied for a quarter of an hour in their duties, or in some bodily exercise, or in manual labour prescribed by the Master of Novices. Nevertheless, each day they shall devote some time, especially before dinner, to learning by heart and committing to memory the Rules, the Christian Doctrine, and other things which the judgment of the Master of Novices judges suitable for each one.

units.la: 74. Post examen sequatur prandium, quo absoluto horam integram recreationi dabunt, tam qui in priore, quam qui in posteriore mensa pransi erunt. Tempore autem recreationis poterunt mutuo colloqui, dumodo pauciores quam quatuor non conveniant, nisi aliter Magistro videretur. Agent autem de exemplis vitae Christi, vel Sanctorum, aut de his, quae cum edificatione in Societate fiunt, aut de re aliqua utili in Domino.
units.tr: 74. After the examination, dinner follows; when it is finished they shall give an entire hour to recreation, both those who have dined at the first table and those who have dined at the second. During recreation they may talk with one another, provided that not fewer than four gather together, unless the Master should decide otherwise. They shall speak of examples from the life of Christ or of the Saints, or of those things which are done with edification in the Society, or of some other useful matter in the Lord.

units.la: 75. Expleto recreationis tempore, audito campanae pulsu, sese ad cubicula recipiant, (praeter eos, qui in aliquibus officijs occupati erunt) ut aliquid legant, vel scribant, vel quid aliud agant, juxta Magistri praescriptum.
units.tr: 75. When the time of recreation is over, at the sound of the bell they are to withdraw to their cells (except those who are occupied in some duties), to read or write something, or to do something else, according to the Master's prescription.

units.la: 76. Post finitam horam, omnes cum Magistro convenient, & pensum aliquod eorum quae antea memoriae mandaverint, reddent. Postea explicabitur illis bis singulis hebdomadis, per dimidiam horam Doctrina Christiana, deinde eam recitabunt uno stante, & interrogante, & alijs respondentibus vel sese invicem interrogantibus, & instruantur in modo docendi illam, juxta morem regionis. Uno vero die cuiusq; hebdomadae, fiant Toni.
units.tr: 76. When the hour is finished, all shall meet with the Master and render some task of those things which they have previously committed to memory. Afterwards the Christian Doctrine shall be explained to them twice a week for half an hour; then they shall recite it, one standing and questioning while the others answer or question one another, and they shall be instructed in the manner of teaching it according to the custom of the region. On one day of each week, the chants (Toni) shall be practised.

units.la: 77. His expletis, ad sua officia, vel ad aliquid legendum, aut ad alias occupationes se conferent: deinde ante ultimam horam, quae coenam praecedit, per semihoram orationi vacabunt: ipsam vero horam ultimam, sequentem ante coenam, partim officijs domesticis, partim corporali exercitationi, vel alijs occupationibus quas Magister praescripserit, impendent.
units.tr: 77. When these things are completed, they are to betake themselves to their duties, or to some reading, or to other occupations. Then, before the last hour, which precedes supper, they shall devote a half hour to prayer; that last hour, which comes before supper, they shall spend partly on household duties, partly on bodily exercise, or on other occupations which the Master has prescribed.

units.la: 78. Post Coenam horam integram recreationi dabunt, reliquo tempore usque ad examen quod semper fiet antequam cubitum eant per quartam horae partem) poterunt aliquid legere, vel alia ratione se ad orationem sequentis diei praeparare, vel aliud facere, pro arbitrio Magistri Novitiorum.
units.tr: 78. After supper they shall give a full hour to recreation. For the remaining time until the examination, which shall always take place before they go to bed (for a quarter of an hour), they may read something, or prepare themselves for the prayer of the following day in some other way, or do something else, at the discretion of the Master of Novices.

units.la: 79. Novitios inter se conversari non convenit: sed silentium invicem, & cum alijs observare, nisi in rebus in quibus loqui necesse sit, excepto recreationis tempore, de quo jam supra dictum est.
units.tr: 79. It is not fitting for the novices to converse among themselves, but they are to keep silence towards one another and towards others, except in matters in which it is necessary to speak, apart from the time of recreation, of which something has already been said above.

units.la: DE EXAMINE EORVM, QVI BIENNIO ABSO- LVTO IN SCHOLASTICOS APPROBATOS ADMITTVNTVR.
units.tr: ON THE EXAMINATION OF THOSE WHO, AFTER TWO YEARS, ARE ADMITTED AS APPROVED SCHOLASTICS.

units.la: CAP. V.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: 80. Postquam quis biennium Novitiatus, peractis experimentis, expleverit, & adinterrogationes, quae sexto quoque mense fiunt, responderit, antequam vota Scholasticorum emittat, interrogetur.
units.tr: 80. After someone has completed two years of the novitiate, with the trials finished and having answered the questions that are put every sixth month, he is to be questioned before he takes the vows of a Scholastic.

units.la: 81. An velit se duci sinere circa ea, quibus studere debet, ac studiorum modum, & tempus juxta quod Superiori videbitur.
units.tr: 81. Whether he is willing to be directed in the subjects he ought to study, and in the manner and time of his studies, according as it seems good to the Superior.

units.la: 82. An contentus futurus sit eodem, atque alij, modo in Collegio agere, nulliusque privilegijs, aut praerogativis omnium minimum, qui in eo fuerint anteire, omnem sui curam Superiori relinquendo.
units.tr: 82. Whether he will be content to act in the College in the same way as the others, claiming no privileges or prerogatives, and to be the least of all who are in it, leaving all care of himself to the Superior.

units.la: 83. An statuerit omnino apud se, studijs absolutis, ac probationibus peractis, Societatem ad vivendum in ea & moriendum, ingredi in eo gradu, quem Superior constituerit, ad maiorem Dei gloriam.
units.tr: 83. Whether he has firmly resolved in himself, once his studies are finished and his probations completed, to enter the Society to live and die in it, in whatever rank the Superior appoints, for the greater glory of God.

units.la: 84. Admoneatur, quod votis post biennium ab ipso emissis non poterit sine facultate Generalis a Societate nostra recedere, nec ad aliam religionem, excepta Carthusiensium, transfire, sub poena excommunicationis ipso facto incurrenda juxta Bullam Pij V. anno 1565. expeditam.
units.tr: 84. He is to be warned that, having taken his vows after two years, he cannot leave our Society without the permission of the General, nor pass over to another religious order, except that of the Carthusians, under pain of excommunication incurred by the very fact, according to the Bull of Pius V issued in the year 1565.

units.la: REGVLÆ DE EXAMINE SCHOLASTICORVM STVDIIS ABSOLVTIS. CAPVT VI.
units.tr: RULES CONCERNING THE EXAMINATION OF SCHOLASTICS WHO HAVE COMPLETED THEIR STUDIES. CHAPTER VI.

units.la: S Cholastici studijs suis absolutis, statim postquam ad tertium annum probationis peragendum missi fuerint, generatim interrogandi sunt, an firmi in sua deliberatione, & voti, & promissione Deo oblatis, antequam ad studia se conferrent, permaneant, ut eorum status melius cognoscatur, & ipsi magis in Domino juvari possint.
units.tr: When the scholastics have completed their studies, and as soon as they have been sent to undertake the third year of probation, they are to be asked in general whether they remain firm in their resolve, and in the vow and promise made to God before they devoted themselves to study, so that their condition may be better known and they may be helped more effectively in the Lord.

units.la: 86. Interrogentur etiam, & examinentur particulatim eisdem interrogationibus, & examine, quo sexto quoque mense, antequam ad studia mitterentur, interrogati fuerunt, ut Superioribus eorum memoria renovetur, & mutatio, si aliqua in rebus iam affirmatis accidit differet, cognoscatur.
units.tr: 86. They are also to be questioned, and examined one by one, with the same questions and examination by which they were questioned every sixth month before they were sent to their studies, so that their Superiors may have the matter brought back to mind and may learn of any change that has occurred in those points already affirmed.

units.la: 87. Postremò reddent rationem vitæ suæ inchoando ab eo tempore, quo eam reddiderunt, quando ad studia missi sunt.
units.tr: 87. Finally, they shall give an account of their life, beginning from the time at which they last gave it, when they were sent to their studies.

units.la: REGVLÆ MODESTIAE.
units.tr: RULES OF MODESTY.

units.la: 1. IN conversatione nostrorum, illud in universum dici potest, ut in omnibus exterioribus actionibus appareat in nostris modestia, & humilitas conjuncta cum religiosa maturitate: speciatim autem hæc observanda erunt.
units.tr: 1. In the conduct of our men, this may be said in general: that in all outward actions there should appear in ours modesty and humility joined with religious maturity; but these things in particular are to be observed.

units.la: 2. Caput huc illud leviter non moveatur, sed cum gravitate, ubi opus erit: & si opus non sit, teneatur rectum cum moderata inflexione in partem anteriorem, ad neutrum latus deflectendo.
units.tr: 2. The head should not be moved lightly, but with gravity, where need requires; and if there is no need, it should be held upright with a moderate inclination forward, not tilted to either side.

units.la: 3. Oculos demissos ut plurimum teneant: nec immoderatè eos elevando, nec in hanc, aut illam partem, circumflectendo.
units.tr: 3. They should keep their eyes lowered for the most part, neither raising them immoderately nor turning them this way or that.

units.la: 4. Inter loquendum, cum hominibus præsertim alicuius auctoritatis, non defigatur aspectus in eorum vultus, sed potius sub oculos.
units.tr: 4. When speaking, especially with men of some authority, the gaze should not be fixed on their faces, but rather directed below their eyes.

units.la: 5. Rugæ in fronte, ac multò magis in naso evitentur: ut serenitas exterius cernatur, quæ interioris sit indicium.
units.tr: 5. Wrinkles on the forehead, and much more on the nose, should be avoided, so that a serenity may be seen outwardly, which is a sign of the inner mind.

units.la: 6. Labia nec nimis compressa, nec nimium diducta.
units.tr: 6. The lips should be neither pressed together too tightly nor parted too widely.

units.la: 7. Tota facies hilaritatem potius præseferat, quàm tristitiam, aut alium minùs moderatum affectum.
units.tr: 7. The whole face should display cheerfulness rather than sadness, or any other less moderate emotion.

units.la: 8. Vestes sint mundæ, & cum religiose decentia compositæ.
units.tr: 8. Garments should be clean and arranged with religious propriety.

units.la: 9. Manus, si non sustinenda veste occupentur, decenter quietæ teneantur.
units.tr: 9. The hands, unless they are occupied in holding up a garment, should be kept quiet and becomingly still.

units.la: 10. Incessus sit moderatus sine notabili festinatione, nisi necessitas urgeret: in qua tamen, quantum poterit, decoris ratio habeatur.
units.tr: 10. The gait should be measured, without noticeable haste, unless necessity urges; yet even then, as far as possible, a regard for decorum should be kept.

units.la: 11. Omnes denique gestus, ac motus eiusmodi sint, qui apud omnes ædificationem pariant.
units.tr: 11. Finally, all gestures and movements should be of such a kind as to produce edification in everyone.

units.la: 12. Si plures simul erunt, ordinem præscriptum à Superiore bini, vel terni incedendo servent.
units.tr: 12. If several are together, they should keep the order prescribed by the Superior, walking in pairs or threes.

units.la: 13. Si loquendum fuerit, meminerint modestiæ, & ædificationis, tum in verbis, tum in ratione, ac modo loquendi.
units.tr: 13. If they have to speak, they should remember modesty and edification, both in their words and in their manner and mode of speaking.

units.la: INSTRVCTIO AD REDDENDAM CON- SCIENTIAE RATIONEM, IVXTA MOREM SOCIETATIS.
units.tr: INSTRUCTION FOR GIVING AN ACCOUNT OF CONSCIENCE, ACCORDING TO THE CUSTOM OF THE SOCIETY.

units.la: Intelligant singuli, dum rationem conscientiae sunt reddituri, quanti momenti Pater noster sanctae memoriae Ignatius id duxerit, ad maiorem Divinae bonitatis gloriam: ut subditi magis in spiritu cum gratia uberiori proficiant, ac tanto maiore cum diligentia, amore, & solicitudine juvari, & a periculis conservari possint, ut quae in Examine, & Constitutionibus toties commendantur, & summarij Constitutionum praescribuntur de reddenda ratione conscientiae, exactè serventur. Proinde unusquisque magna cum puritate, sub sigillo confessionis, aut secreti, aut quacunque ratione ei placuerit, & ad maiorem ipsius consolationem fuerit, totam animam suam integrè manifestam faciat, nullam rem celando, quae Domini universorum offenderit, post ultimam rationem redditam conscientiae: vel verè aperiat eos defectus, qui magis ab eo tempore gravant ipsius animam.
units.tr: Let each one understand, when he is about to give an account of his conscience, how great a weight our Father of holy memory, Ignatius, attached to this, for the greater glory of the goodness of God: so that the subjects may make progress in the Spirit, with more abundant grace, and may be helped and preserved from dangers with all the greater diligence, love and solicitude. Thus what is so often commended in the Examen and the Constitutions, and what is prescribed in the summary of the Constitutions concerning the giving of an account of conscience, may be exactly observed. Accordingly, let each one, with great candour, under the seal of confession, or of secrecy, or in whatever way it pleases him and will be most comforting to him, lay open his whole soul completely, concealing nothing that has offended the Lord of all since the last account of conscience was given; or at least let him disclose those defects which have weighed more heavily upon his soul since that time.

units.la: Capita vero, quibus conscientiae ratio reddi debet, haec fere erunt: ex quibus cum tam ea, quae ad plenam sui manifestationem dicenda putaverint, petant a Superiore, ut eos interrogando juvet, ac suppleat, si quid esse judicet, quo ad maiorem Dei gloriam & eorum notitiam scire velit.
units.tr: The heads on which an account of conscience ought to be given will in general be these. From these, after they have considered what they think should be said for a full disclosure of themselves, let them ask the Superior to help them by questioning them and to supply anything he judges he wishes to know, for the greater glory of God and for his own knowledge of them.

units.la: 1. An vivat contentus iuxta suam vocationem.
units.tr: 1. Whether he lives content in accordance with his vocation.

units.la: 2. Quomodo se habeat circa obedientiam, etiam intellectus, paupertatem, castitatem, & sum aliarum virtutum, & quarum praecipue studio intentus sit.
units.tr: 2. How he stands with regard to obedience, including that of the intellect, poverty, chastity, and the rest of the virtues, and which of them he is especially intent on cultivating.

units.la: 3. An sentiat aliquas animi perturbationes, aut tentationes molestas, & de facilitate, seu difficultate, & modo eis resistendi, & ad quos affectus, vel peccata sit magis propensus & incitatus.
units.tr: 3. Whether he feels any disturbances of mind or troublesome temptations, and about the ease or difficulty of resisting them and the manner of doing so, and to which affections or sins he is more prone and inclined.

units.la: 4. An contra Constitutiones, vel Regulam aliquam, vel ordinationem Superiorum firmum judicium habuerit, vel contra eam disputaverit.
units.tr: 4. Whether he has held a firm judgement against the Constitutions, or some rule, or some ordinance of the Superiors, or has disputed against it.

units.la: 5. Quid sentiat de ipso instituto Societatis, & mediis, quibus illa nititur ad suum finem consequendum, & quem experiatur in se zelum animarum.
units.tr: 5. What he thinks of the very institute of the Society, and of the means on which it relies to attain its end, and what zeal for souls he experiences in himself.

units.la: 6. Quomodo spiritualibus rebus sit affectus, quantum temporis orationi tribuat, & num vocali, an potius mentali juvetur, & utrum plus temporis tribuat, & quem modum in orando teneat.
units.tr: 6. How he is affected towards spiritual things, how much time he gives to prayer, and whether he is helped by vocal or rather by mental prayer, and whether he devotes more time to it, and what method he keeps in praying.

units.la: 7. Num in usu rerum spiritualium consolationem & devotionem habeat, an vero contra desolationem, ariditatem, & vagationem animi patiatur, & quomodo in iis se gerat.
units.tr: 7. Whether he finds consolation and devotion in the practice of spiritual things, or on the contrary suffers desolation, dryness and wandering of mind, and how he conducts himself in these states.

units.la: 8. De fructu, quem ex communione, confessione, examine, praesertim particulari, & aliis exercitiis spiritualibus percipiat.
units.tr: 8. Concerning the fruit which he gains from communion, confession, examination, especially the particular examination, and other spiritual exercises.

units.la: 9. Num post ultimam rationem conscientiae, quam reddidit, maiorem an minorem fructum fecerit, & quem animum experiatur ad perfectionem consequendam.
units.tr: 9. Whether, since the last account of conscience which he gave, he has made greater or less progress, and what disposition he experiences for attaining perfection.

units.la: 10. Quomodo observet, quae ex Constitutionibus & Regulis tum communibus, tum officij sui ad eum pertinent.
units.tr: 10. How he observes those things which pertain to him from the Constitutions and Rules, both the common ones and those of his office.

units.la: 11. De mortificationibus, poenitentijs, & aliis exercitationibus, quae faciunt ad spiritus profectum: & in specie de praeparatione ad injurias, & ad alia, quae ad Christi crucem pertinent, ferenda, atque de eorum desiderio.
units.tr: 11. Concerning mortifications, penances, and other exercises which serve the progress of the spirit: and in particular concerning the preparation to bear injuries, and other things that pertain to the cross of Christ, and concerning the desire for them.

units.la: 12. De socijs, & quomodo ex eorum conversatione proficiat in Domino, & an aliquibus sit familiaris, quam aliis.
units.tr: 12. Concerning his companions, and how he advances in the Lord from their company, and whether he is more familiar with some than with others.

units.la: 13. An aversionem animi sentiat ab aliquo, & an offensus sit in aliquo a Superioribus vel Officialibus, vel quavis alia persona.
units.tr: 13. Whether he feels an aversion of mind towards anyone, and whether he has taken offence at anyone among the Superiors or officials, or any other person.

units.la: 14. An tentationes aliquas sit passus, quas alij intellexerint, praesertim circa vocationem.
units.tr: 14. Whether he has suffered any temptations which others have noticed, especially concerning his vocation.

units.la: REGVLÆ PEREGRINORVM.
units.tr: RULES FOR PILGRIMS.

units.la: PErsuadeant sibi, peregrinationis finem non tam esse corporis defatigationem; & ut multum iter conficiant, quàm ut ex ea fructum aliquem spiritualem percipiant: atq; ex eo fine, & iter ipsum, & cæteros peregrinationis labores moderentur.
units.tr: Let them persuade themselves that the purpose of a journey is not so much the weariness of the body, nor that they may cover much ground, as that they may gain some spiritual fruit from it; and let them regulate by that purpose both the journey itself and the other labours of the pilgrimage.

units.la: 2. Litanias simul omnes quotidie in ipso itineris ingressu: vel Itinerarium dicant, nec orationem; & consuetas examina prætermittant, & alias etiam Regulas observent, quantum ratio itineris permittet.
units.tr: 2. Let them not recite all the litanies together at the very start of the journey, or may say the Itinerary instead, and not the usual prayer; and let them omit the customary examinations and observe the other rules as far as the nature of the journey allows.

units.la: 3. Studeant frequenti oratione, & meditatione comitem itineris sibi Christum facere: & colloquijs interdum piis, & religiosis, ac lectione alicuius libri pij molestias itineris levare poterunt. Quòd si cum externis in via, aut in hospitijs egerint; meminerint pro ratione sui gradus habitare ratione temporis & personarum, sermones de rebus spiritualibus inducere, & fructum aliquem, quoad poterunt efficere.
units.tr: 3. Let them strive, by frequent prayer and meditation, to make Christ their companion on the road; at times they will be able to lighten the troubles of the journey with pious and devout conversations, and by reading some devout book. But if they have dealings with outsiders on the way or in inns, let them remember to introduce talk of spiritual matters, as far as their rank, the time and the persons allow, and to bring about some fruit from it so far as they can.

units.la: 4. Eleemosynas simpliciter pro Christi amore petant: ut omni ípe illa abiecta, quam in pecunijs, & rebus creatis habere possunt, integrè, vera cum fide & ardenti amore eam in suo creatore; ac Domino constituant: memores, à Christo Domino Apostolos sine sacculo, & peramissos: ipsum etiam Dominum non habuisse, ubi caput reclinaret.
units.tr: 4. Let them ask for alms simply for love of Christ, so that, having cast aside entirely every desire for the money and created things they may have, they establish that alms in their Creator and Lord with true faith and burning love; mindful that Christ the Lord sent out the Apostles without a purse and without provisions, and that the Lord himself had nowhere to lay his head.

units.la: 5. Indigentia, & penuria rerum corpori necessariarum probari exoptent, ut ad incomoditatem cibi, somnive capiendi libenter assuescant: injurias verò, illusiones, & opprobria, quæ in itinere inferri contigerit, patienter cum Dei gratia ferant; gaudeantque materiam præberi sibi imitandi aliquo modo Christum Dominum eiusque vestibus; atque insignibus seipsos induendi.
units.tr: 5. Let them desire to be tested by want and shortage of the things necessary for the body, so that they willingly grow accustomed to meagre food and to taking rest; and let them patiently bear, with the grace of God, the wrongs, mockery and reproaches that happen to be inflicted on them on the journey, and rejoice that they are given the occasion of imitating Christ the Lord in some measure, and of clothing themselves with his garments and his marks.

units.la: 6. Qui maioribus pollent ad viam peragendam viribus, eos, qui sunt infirmiores, subsequi & non præcedere debent: & iter cuiusq; diei horum debilium infirmitate commensuretur; quod si quis viribus destituretur, jumento, aut alia ratione juvari debet: qua in re non quantitatis personarum, sed necessitatis, & charitatis fraternæ ratio est habenda.
units.tr: 6. Those who are stronger and able to complete the journey should follow those who are weaker, not run ahead of them; and the daily stage of each day should be measured by the weakness of these feeble ones. If anyone is without strength, he ought to be helped with a beast of burden or in some other way; in this matter the consideration to be had is not of the number of persons but of need and fraternal charity.

units.la: 7. Si quis in morbum inciderer, ita ut ulterius progredi non posset, nec expediret reliquos ibi morari trahere; si vicinum esset Collegium, aut Domus Societatis, eo esset æger (si modò morbus patiatur) deducendus: alioqui aliquis ex nostris illi erit socius relinquendus: ut consolationi eis sit, & auxilio: ægro autem viribus restituto, cæptum iter ambo prosequentur.
units.tr: 7. If anyone should fall ill, so that he cannot go further, and it would not be expedient for the rest to be delayed there by dragging him along, then, if there is a college or house of the Society nearby, the sick man (if indeed his illness allows it) is to be taken there; otherwise one of ours is to be left with him as a companion, to be a comfort and help to him; and when the sick man has regained his strength, both shall continue the journey they had begun.

units.la: 8. Si in via ab honesto, & pio amico invitarentur, posset, qui præest, hospitalitatis beneficium admittere: tunc autem curare debent verbis, & religioso exemplo hospites ædificatos in Domino relinquere.
units.tr: 8. If they were invited on the road by an honest and pious friend, the one who is in charge may accept the kindness of hospitality; but then they must take care to leave the hosts edified in the Lord by their words and by religious example.

units.la: 9. Eiusdem ædificationis, & exempli in omnibus hospitijs meminisse debent: sobrietatis etiam in mensa; & modestiæ in conversatione nunquam obliviscantur.
units.tr: 9. They must always remember this same edification and example in all inns; and they must never forget sobriety at table and modesty in conversation.

units.la: 10. Cum in itinere ad Collegia, vel Domos Societatis divertent, studeant omnes bonum ædificationis odorem exemplo vitæ, ac morum, nostris relinquere. De rebus verò aut personis aliorum Collegiorum, aut Domorum nihil loquantur, aut tractent; nisi ad ædificationem.
units.tr: 10. When on the journey they stop at colleges or houses of the Society, let all strive to leave behind among ours a good odour of edification by the example of their life and conduct. But they are to say or discuss nothing about the affairs or persons of other colleges or houses, unless for edification.

units.la: 11. Si transfierint per locum, ubi Domus, aut Collegium Societatis sit, nihil ab externis, nec pro se, nec pro alijs petant, aut accipiant sine facultate Superioris eiusdem Domus vel Collegij.
units.tr: 11. If they pass through a place where there is a house or college of the Society, they are to ask for or accept nothing from outsiders, either for themselves or for others, without the permission of the Superior of that house or college.

units.la: 12. Omnes alij, qui iter faciunt ex nostris equites, aut pedites, has regulas peregrinorum suo modo, quantum fieri potest, etiam servent, & tam peregrini, quàm reliqui, qui iter faciunt, patentes literas sui Superioris habere curent.
units.tr: 12. All others of ours who travel on horseback or on foot are to observe these rules for pilgrims in their own way, as far as possible; and both pilgrims and all the rest who travel are to take care to have letters patent from their Superior.

units.la: REGVLAE MINISTRI.
units.tr: THE RULES OF THE MINISTER.

units.la: 1. EIus officium erit, Præpositum, vel Rectorem juvare, in iis, quæ in genere, vel in particulari ei commendabit: nec dispensandi, aut mutandi, aut quidquam faciendi, nisi ex eiusdem præscripto, facultatem habebit.
units.tr: 1. His office shall be to assist the Prefect or Rector in those things which he commends to him, either in general or in particular. He shall have no authority to dispense, alter, or do anything, except in accordance with the Superior's direction.

units.la: 2. Valde commendatum sibi existimet, quod pertinet ad observationem Constitutionum, Regularum, Ordinum communium, & approbatarum Consuetudinum Domus, vel Collegij: ideoque habeat in scriptis, & aliquando legat, tam communes omnium, quam particulares Superioris, & Officialium Regulas, & eosdem Officiales suas habere, intelligere, atque observare curet.
units.tr: 2. Let him regard as especially entrusted to him whatever pertains to the observance of the Constitutions, Rules, common Orders, and approved customs of the House or College. Therefore let him have in writing, and read from time to time, both the common rules of all and the particular rules of the Superior and of the officials; and let him see to it that these officials have, understand, and observe their own rules.

units.la: 3. Officiales visitet quoties opus fuerit, observando, quomodo suum officium exequantur: quod saltem alternis diebus faciet: frequenter etiam visitabit cubicula, & alia loca domus, ut videat, quomodo omnia se habeant.
units.tr: 3. He shall visit the officials as often as necessary, observing how they carry out their duties; this he shall do at least every other day. He shall also visit the cells and other places of the house frequently, to see how everything is kept.

units.la: 4. Cum quis ab officio aliquo amovetur, curet, ut in suum successorem instruat de ratione exercendi illud, iuxta regulas, & Consuetudines à Superiore approbatas.
units.tr: 4. When anyone is removed from some office, let him see to it that he instructs his successor in how that office is to be exercised, according to the rules and customs approved by the Superior.

units.la: 5. Animadvertat in temporum mutationibus, quomodo in Collegio vel Domo fieri debeat horarum, ciborum, vestiumque mutatio, & Superiori in memoriam reducat, præsertim bis in anno, sub initium veris, & autumni: observet etiam crebrò num aliquid deest ex necessariis, aut abundet: eorumque potissimum rationem habeat, qui in corporis cura minorem de se ipsis solicitudinem gerunt: curetque, ut adsit, cum Medicus ægros inviset.
units.tr: 5. Let him take note of the changes of the seasons, and remind the Superior how the change of hours, meals, and clothing is to be made in the College or House, especially twice a year, at the beginning of spring and autumn. Let him also often observe whether anything necessary is lacking or in excess; and let him take particular account of those who take less care of themselves in matters of bodily health. Let him also see that he is present when the physician visits the sick.

units.la: 6. Quotidie hora sibi designata, de rebus omnibus domus ratione Superiori reddat, à quo excipiet in libello ad id parato, quæ ei facienda committet, & cum primum commodè poterit, eidem referat, quæ executus fuerit.
units.tr: 6. Each day, at an hour set aside for this, let him give the Superior an account of all the affairs of the house; from the Superior he shall receive, in a notebook prepared for the purpose, the things he is to do, and as soon as he conveniently can, let him report to him what he has carried out.

units.la: 7. Redigat Superiori in memoriam ea, quæ necessaria domui iudicabit, ut de emendis rebus ad victum, & vestitum necessariis suis temporibus de fratrum nimio, aut exiguo labore, de sanitate, & similibus.
units.tr: 7. Let him remind the Superior of those things which he judges necessary for the house: as to the purchase of food and clothing needed at the proper times, concerning the excessive or insufficient labour of the brethren, their health, and similar matters.

units.la: 8. Notet, ac referat Superiori tam defectus, si quos vel Domi, aut in Collegio animadverterit, vel aliunde intellexerit, quàm quæcunque alia quæ ad bonam gubernationem convenientia ei occurrent: tum etiam circa res sibi commissas, & quasvis alias, ut quomodo fenoftri habeant circa Obedientiam, orationem, ædificationem, & in omnibus virtutis profectum & studium.
units.tr: 8. Let him note and report to the Superior both the defects, if he notices any at home or in the College, or learns of them elsewhere, and whatever other matters suited to good government occur to him; and likewise concerning the things entrusted to him and any others, such as how the members of the community stand with regard to obedience, prayer, edification, and progress and zeal in all virtue.

units.la: 9. Curet per ædituum, vel aliquem alium designatum observari, an omnes die statuto communicaverint: & si quis intra tempus designatum ad confessionem, aut communionem non accederet, intelligat à Superiore, num subtrahendus ei sit cibus corporis, donec cibum spiritus sumat.
units.tr: 9. Let him see, through the sacristan or some other appointed person, that all have communed on the appointed day; and if anyone has not come to confession or communion within the appointed time, let him learn from the Superior whether his bodily food should be withheld from him until he takes the food of the spirit.

units.la: 10. Peculiarem habeat curam, ut domus munda sit, & omnia ubique decenter suis locis composita, sed præcipuè in iis, quæ ab externis videri solent.
units.tr: 10. Let him take especial care that the house is clean and that everything is decently arranged in its place everywhere, but above all in those things which outsiders are wont to see.

units.la: 11. Noctibus singulis portas domus, quibus in publicum exitur, videat an bene clausæ sint.
units.tr: 11. Each night let him see whether the doors of the house through which one goes out to the public are well closed.

units.la: 12. Designet aliquem ex commissione Superioris, qui communes lucernas domus opportuno tempore incendat, & extinguat, qui item publicas fenestras suo tempore aperiat, & claudat, ac pro abluenda facie, & manibus in loco destinato aquam infundat, & pro iis extergendis, mantilia, ab iis, quæ in usum refectorij sunt, distincta adhibeat, quæ alia non Sacerdotibus, alia Sacerdotibus destinata erunt, & bis saltem in hebdomada mutantur.
units.tr: 12. Let him appoint someone, by the Superior's commission, to light and extinguish the common lamps of the house at the proper time, who likewise shall open and close the public windows at their time, and who shall pour water in the designated place for washing the face and hands; and for drying these, separate towels from those used in the refectory shall be employed, some destined for non-priests and others for priests, and these shall be changed at least twice a week.

units.la: 13. Studeat animos Patrum, & Fratrum inter se per benevolentiam, & præsertim cum Superiore per obedientiam uuire, & si quid minus æquo animo aliquis ferret, velit potius in se (quoad fieri potest) quam in Superiorem, causam reijci, veluti in iniungendis pœnitentijs, quas ipse juxta præscriptum Superioris imponet, & tam in eis, quam in reprehensionibus ab animi perturbatione caveat, charitatemque præse ferendo studeat, ut illi quibus pœnitentias imponet, merito sibi iniungi cognoscant.
units.tr: 13. Let him strive to unite the minds of the Fathers and Brothers with one another through goodwill, and especially with the Superior through obedience; and if anyone should bear something with less than an even temper, let him prefer (as far as possible) that the cause be laid upon himself rather than upon the Superior, as in the imposing of penances, which he himself shall impose according to the Superior's prescription; and in these, as in reproofs, let him guard against agitation of mind, and strive to show charity, so that those on whom he imposes penances may recognise that they are rightly enjoined upon them.

units.la: 14. Si quando absente Superiore aliquid acciderit, quando adeo urgeat, ut commode Superior expectari nequeat, id Minister, auditis Consultoribus, exequi poterit, quamvis in specie non sit ipsi commissum: dummodo existimet iuxta Superioris mentem id fore, statim redeunti quod factum fuerit, referat. Quod autem sibi ordinarie agendum erit, absente Superiore, ab eo curet intelligere.
units.tr: 14. If at any time, in the Superior's absence, something should happen which is so urgent that the Superior cannot conveniently be waited for, the Minister, after hearing the Consultors, may carry it out, even though it has not been specifically committed to him; provided he judges that it will be according to the Superior's intention, and he shall report what has been done as soon as the Superior returns. As to what is ordinarily to be done by him in the Superior's absence, let him take care to learn it from the Superior.

units.la: 15. Si Subministrum habuerit, utatur eius opera in iis, quæ commode per se facere non poterit, iuxta præscriptum Superioris: si vero non habuerit, alternis saltem diebus singula cubicula visitet, & alia quæ in officio Subministri continentur, suppleat.
units.tr: 15. If he has an assistant, let him use his services in those things which he cannot conveniently do himself, according to the Superior's direction; but if he has none, let him visit each cell at least every other day, and supply whatever else is included in the office of the assistant.

units.la: REGVLÆ CONSVLTORVM.
units.tr: Rules for the Consultors.

units.la: Intelligant quanti momenti sit eorum officium, ut Superiores eorum consilio, & relatione adiuti melius, & facilius gubernare possint.
units.tr: Let them understand how great the importance of their office is, so that the Superiors, aided by their counsel and report, may govern better and more easily.

units.la: 2. Sint amatores boni communis, illudque in omnibus consultationibus præ oculis habeant, atque ut divinæ inspirationi dent locum, & sanriora sint eorum consilia, in suo sensu non nimis abundent.
units.tr: 2. Let them be lovers of the common good, and keep it before their eyes in all consultations; and, so that they may give place to divine inspiration, and their counsels may be sounder, let them not overly abound in their own sense.

units.la: 3. In Consultationibus synceram intentionem habeant, & a perturbatione liberam, ut fideliter, & debita cum modestia Charitatis, & Obedientiæ memores sententiam dicant.
units.tr: 3. In consultations let them have a sincere intention, free from disturbance, so that they may give their opinion faithfully and with due modesty, mindful of charity and obedience.

units.la: 4. Sint inter se maxime Charitate coniuncti, & alter alterum honore prævemiat, atque apud alios alter alterius existimationem verbis factisque tueatur. Si vero contingat aliquem in Consultationibus diversa aut etiam singularis esse sententiæ, nemo ullam ab eo alienationem vel habeat, vel ostendat.
units.tr: 4. Let them be most closely joined to one another in charity, and let each anticipate the other in honour, and let each defend the good name of the other, by word and deed, before others. If, however, it should happen that someone in the consultations holds a different or even a peculiar opinion, no one is to harbour or show any estrangement from him.

units.la: 5. Rem, de qua consultatur, bene intelligant: nec sint in dicendo præcipites: sed negotio secum considerato, & oratione præmissa: præcipue cum de rebus agitur difficilibus, sententiam suam aperiant: quod si quid ex tempore discutiendum proponeretur, & sibi maturius considerandum iudicarent, Superiori significabunt.
units.tr: 5. Let them understand well the matter under consultation, and let them not be hasty in speaking; but, having considered the business with themselves and after prayer, let them state their opinion, especially when the matters are difficult. If something were proposed for discussion on the spur of the moment, and they judged that it needed more mature consideration, they are to signify this to the Superior.

units.la: 6. Explicare breviter debent sententiæ suæ rationes: quod si ad rem confirmandam aliorum rationes essent dissolvendæ, id etiam modeste faciant.
units.tr: 6. They ought to explain briefly the reasons for their opinion; and if the reasons of others had to be overturned in order to confirm the matter, let them do this modestly too.

units.la: 7. Cum Superior Consultoribus auditis aliquid statuerit, iudicium ipsi suum illius iudicio submittent: neque extra consultationem, aut quod statutum fuerit, sibi displicere, aut se in alia fuisse sententia significabunt: laudent potius Superioris consilium apud alios, atque tueantur. Quod si ob rei, de qua agitur, gravitatem, adhuc sentirent ad alium Superiorem esse rem deferendam, quod nihil monitione sua se effecturos, sperarent, re prius apud se maturius considerata, & oratione præmissa, ad immediatum illius Superiorem, aut si is non provideat, ad Supremum id facere ne prætermittant.
units.tr: 7. When the Superior, having heard the Consultors, has decided something, they are to submit their own judgment to his; and they are neither to show displeasure outside the consultation at what has been decided, nor to signal that they had been of another opinion; rather, let them praise the Superior's counsel before others and defend it. But if, on account of the gravity of the matter under discussion, they still think the matter should be referred to another Superior, because they hope that nothing will be accomplished by their admonition, let them not fail to do so, having first considered the matter more maturely with themselves and after prayer: to the immediate Superior of that man, or, if he does not provide, to the Supreme one.

units.la: 8. Etiamsi non interrogentur, si quid tamen in mentem venerit, quod ad commune bonum, vel alicuius personæ particularis pertineat, poterunt id Superiori proponere, ut is statuat, num ea de re fit deliberandum, nec ne.
units.tr: 8. Even if they are not asked, if something has come to mind which pertains to the common good or to the good of some particular person, they may propose it to the Superior, so that he may decide whether or not the matter is to be deliberated.

units.la: 9. Consultores neque ea, quæ quisque in consultatione senserit, neque ea, quæ propositæ sunt, aut definita, alij significare debet: præcipue cum res ipsæ secretum exigunt. Superioris autem erit ea, quæ definientur, promulgare: cum opus esse iudicabit.
units.tr: 9. Consultors ought not to disclose to others either what each one has thought in the consultation, or what has been proposed or decided, especially when the matters themselves demand secrecy. But it will be for the Superior to publish what is decided, when he judges it necessary.

units.la: 10. De literis ad Superiores suo tempore mittendis, servent diligenter quæ in formula scribendi à Consultoribus exiguntur. Et hæ litera sigillo, quod apud Admonitorem erit, obsignatæ mittantur: nec quisquam eorum sciat, quid alius scripserit.
units.tr: 10. Concerning letters to be sent to the Superiors at the proper time, let them carefully observe what the Consultors are required to follow in the form of writing. And let these letters be sent sealed with the seal which is kept by the Admonitor, and let no one of them know what another has written.

units.la: 11. Si quis ex nostris ad Generalem scripserit, & literas Admonitori, aut alicui ex Consultoribus ultoribus tradere voluerit: is acceptas cum suis, aut sub sua propria manus inscriptione, ad Generalem mittendas curabit.
units.tr: 11. If anyone of ours writes to the General and wishes to hand his letters to the Admonitor, or to any one of the Consultors, let that person take care that they are sent on to the General either with his own enclosure or under his own handwritten superscription.

units.la: 12. Si quid circa victum, vestitum, labores, & occupationes Superioris, aut circa gubernationem moderandum, augendum vel mutandum censerent, illum praemissa oratione admonendum curent, quod fere per Admonitorem faciant.
units.tr: 12. If they judge that something concerning the food, clothing, labours and occupations of the Superior, or concerning his government, ought to be moderated, increased or changed, let them take care to advise him, after prayer, which they commonly do through the Admonitor.

units.la: 13. Si quis cum eis de difficultate aliqua sua, aut perturbatione agat, ita eum suis monitis & consilio juvare studeant, ut semper, quantum possint, existimationem Superioris tueantur.
units.tr: 13. If anyone deals with them about some difficulty of his own or some disturbance, let them strive to help him with their admonitions and counsel in such a way that they always, as far as they can, preserve the good name of the Superior.

units.la: 14. Ad omnia melius obeunda Superiorum suorum, & aliorum Officialium Regulas teneant, Constitutionesque & reliqua omnia, quae ad nostrum institutum, & administrationem pertinent, familiaria sibi reddant.
units.tr: 14. In order to discharge all their duties better, both towards their Superiors and towards the other officials, let them keep the Rules, and make familiar to themselves the Constitutions and all the rest that pertain to our institute and administration.

units.la: 15. Ita suum munus exequantur, ut nullam gubernationis partem sibi assumant, atque a submissione se gerant, ut caeteris Obedientiae exemplum praebeant.
units.tr: 15. Let them so perform their office that they assume no part of the government for themselves, and let them conduct themselves with submission, so that they may provide an example of obedience to the others.

units.la: REGULAE ADMONITORIS.
units.tr: RULES OF THE ADMONITOR.

units.la: 1. EA modestia & humilitate officium suum obeat, ut subditum decet erga Superiorem, quem Christi loco habet: niti enim debet, ne huius muneris occasione, reverentia atque Obedientia interior, vel exterior in ipso debilior reddatur.
units.tr: 1. He shall discharge his office with such modesty and humility as befits a subject toward a Superior, whom he holds in the place of Christ. He must take care that, through the occasion of this office, his inward reverence and obedience, or his outward obedience, be not made weaker in himself.

units.la: 2. Animad vertat autem, ne reverentia haec, & Obedientia fidelitatem, aut necessariam libertatem opprimat, quo minus Superiorem admoneat de iis, quae praemissa oratione, pronuncianda in Domino judicabit.
units.tr: 2. Let him take care, however, that this reverence and obedience do not so oppress his fidelity, or the freedom that is necessary, as to keep him from admonishing the Superior about those things which, after prayer, he judges must be spoken before the Lord.

units.la: 3. Admoneat Superiorem de iis, quae maior pars Consultorum ei dicenda judicaverit: de aliis vero, quae sive ipsi in mentem venient, sive ab aliis suggerentur, non faciet eum admonebit, sed de iis duntaxat, quae non levis momenti post orationem esse censuerit, sive illa ad personam, sive ad officium Superioris pertinebunt, juxta Constitutiones et Decreta.
units.tr: 3. Let him admonish the Superior about those things which the greater part of the Consultors have judged should be told to him. As for other matters, whether they come into his own mind or are suggested by others, he shall not admonish the Superior about them, but only about those which, after prayer, he has judged to be of no slight importance, whether they pertain to the person or to the office of the Superior, in accordance with the Constitutions and Decrees.

units.la: 4. Ea, quorum Superiorem admonuerit, meminerit tacitus apud se servare: quam vis interrogatus a Consultoribus de iis, quae ipsi commississent dicenda vel a Superioribus, rationem sui officii eis debebit reddere.
units.tr: 4. Whatever matters he has admonished the Superior about, he shall remember to keep them silently to himself; although, when questioned by the Consultors about things that they had entrusted to him to be told, or that had been entrusted to him by the Superiors, he must give them an account of his office.

units.la: 5. Cum Superior cuiuspiam rei admonitus, illi remedium non adhibuerit, Admonitor rit, cum debita submissione iterum, & saepius eum commonefacere: quod si emendationem consperat, facta prius oratione, id Superiori significet.
units.tr: 5. When a Superior, having been admonished about some matter, has not applied a remedy to it, the Admonitor shall, with due submission, admonish him again and more often. But if he perceives that there is amendment, he shall, after prayer first made, signify this to the Superior.

units.la: 6. Admonitoris erit, ordinarias epistolas Consultorum suis temporibus colligere, atque ad mediatos Superiores mittere, nisi eas illi alia via mittere voluerint, simulque referet eis, utrum illi scripserint an non.
units.tr: 6. It shall be the Admonitor's task to collect the ordinary letters of the Consultors at their appointed times and send them to the intermediate Superiors, unless they have wished to send them by another way; and at the same time he shall report to them whether they have written or not.

units.la: 7. Caveat, ne occasione sui officij debitam subordinationem, & observantiam subditorum erga suos Superiores aliqua ex parte imminuat, aut debilitet.
units.tr: 7. Let him take care that, through the occasion of his office, he does not in any way diminish or weaken the due subordination and observance of subjects toward their Superiors.

units.la: 8. Sigillum apud se habeat, quo suas, & Consultorum ac aliorum nostrorum literas, ad eum detulerint, qui ad mediatos Superiores scribere voluerint, obsignare possit. Hoc tamen nulla ratione, sine facultate Superioris, uti licebit, nisi in iis literis, quae ad Superiores mediatos scribentur.
units.tr: 8.
