Let him keep by him a seal, with which he may seal the letters of his own and of the Consultors and of other members of ours which are to be delivered to the one who wishes to write to the intermediate Superiors. Yet he may on no account use this seal without the permission of the Superior, except for those letters which are written to the intermediate Superiors.

units.la: REGVLÆ FORMVLA SCRIBENDI.
units.tr: The Form of Writing Letters

units.la: 1. Magnopere juverit ad animorum unionem in Societate, literarum ultro citroque missarum inter inferiores, & Superiores frequens commercium: & crebrò alios de alijs certiores fieri, & audire, quæ ex variis locis ad ædificationem, & eorum, quæ geruntur, cognitionem, afferuntur.
units.tr: 1. Much will be gained for the union of souls in the Society by a frequent exchange of letters sent back and forth between inferiors and superiors, and by keeping one another often informed and hearing what is reported from various places for edification and for knowledge of what is being done.

units.la: 2. Superiores Domorum, & Rectores scribant singulis hebdomadis ad suum Provincialem in Europa, in Indijs vero, ut suis Provincialibus visum fuerit commodum & opportunum.
units.tr: 2. The superiors of houses and the rectors shall write every week to their Provincial in Europe; in the Indies, however, they shall write as often as their Provincials think fitting and expedient.

units.la: 3. Scribant autem ad suum Provincialem de statu personarum, & rerum omnium, non solum quæ inter nostros, sed etiam quæ per ministeria Societatis erga externos in Domibus suis, vel Collegijs fiunt, & non tantum de his, quæ recte se habent, sed etiâ de his quæ secus sunt, & quoad fieri poterit, curent, ut omnia tanquam præsentia Provincialis cernat.
units.tr: 3. They shall write to their Provincial about the condition of persons and of all matters, not only those concerning our own members but also those done in their houses or colleges through the ministries of the Society toward outsiders, and not only about what goes well but also about what goes amiss. As far as possible they shall take care that the Provincial sees everything as if he were present.

units.la: 4. Primo quoque tempore ad suum Provincialem scribant Superiores Domorum, & Rectores de obitu eorum, qui in suis locis decesserunt: Provincialis vero reliquos de sua Provincia admonebit, ut quam primùm solitis suffragijs, & orationibus eorum animæ juvenVA.
units.tr: 4. At the earliest opportunity the superiors of houses and the rectors shall write to their Provincial about the death of anyone who has died in their places. The Provincial, for his part, shall remind the rest of his Province that the souls of the dead should be helped as soon as possible by the customary suffrages and prayers.

units.la: 5. Missi ad fructificandum in agro Domini, scribant ad suum Provincialem, aut ad eum, quem ille designaverit, singulis hebdomadis, vel quoties ipsis fuerit præscriptum, ut per crebram literarum communicationem, quantum fieri potest, totum successum suarum missionum illi declarent.
units.tr: 5. Those sent to bear fruit in the Lord's field shall write to their Provincial, or to the man he appoints, every week, or as often as they are instructed, so that by frequent correspondence they may report to him, as fully as possible, the whole outcome of their missions.

units.la: 6. Provinciales Superioribus Domorum, & Rectoribus, ac ijs, qui in missionibus versantur, singulis mensibus, personis autem privatis, quibus, & quando opus erit, scribant.
units.tr: 6. Provincials shall write to the superiors of houses, to the rectors, and to those engaged in missions every month, and to private persons whenever and as often as there is need.

units.la: 7. Provinciales omnium Provinciarum Europæ scribant ad Generalem semel quolibet mense: Rectores autem, & Superiores Domorum, & Magistri Novitiorum tertio quoque mense.
units.tr: 7. The Provincials of all the Provinces of Europe shall write to the General once every month; the rectors, superiors of houses and masters of novices shall write every third month.

units.la: 8. Provinciales Indiarum scribent Præposito Generali, quando se obtulerit navigationis commoditas: Rectores vero, & Superiores Domorum, ac Magistri Novitiorum ex Indijs semel, ex Brasilia, & nova Hispania bis in anno, si se obtulerit occasio.
units.tr: 8. The Provincials of the Indies shall write to the Preposite General whenever an opportunity for sailing presents itself. The rectors, superiors of houses and masters of novices from the Indies shall write once a year, and those from Brazil and New Spain twice a year, if an occasion offers.

units.la: 9. Prædicti omnes extraordinariè sibi mutuò scribant, quoties necessitas urgebit.
units.tr: 9. All those named above shall write to one another outside the regular schedule whenever necessity requires.

units.la: 10. Superiores Domorum, & Collegiorum, & Magistri Novitiorum scribant ad Generalem, quæ alicujus momenti fuerint, etiamsi approbante Provinciali fiant: illa verò potissimum scribant, in quibus Provincialis admonitus, vel non providet, vel providere nequit, vel post quam Provincialis cum illis tractaverit, ipsi ab eius judicio dissentiunt: sed tunc quidem addant, quid Provincialis responderit, & quibus rationibus ipsi ab eo differant, interim tamen eiper omnia obediant.
units.tr: 10. The superiors of houses and colleges, and the masters of novices, shall write to the General about matters of some importance, even when these are carried out with the approval of the Provincial. They shall write above all about those matters in which, after being reminded, the Provincial either does not provide, or cannot provide, or, after the Provincial has discussed them with them, they differ from his judgment. In such cases they shall add what the Provincial answered and on what grounds they differ from him, yet meanwhile they shall obey him in all things.

units.la: 11. Cum Provinciales scribent Generali, curabunt ut statum Domorum, & Collegiorum suorum, ac totius Provinciæ bene explicent, & suppleant si quid intellexerint, quod Superiores Domorum, & Collegiorum minùs declaraverint, & in universum ita scribere debent, ut Generalis omnium rerum, omnium personarum ac Provinciarum statum, quo ad eius fieri possit, ante oculos habeat.
units.tr: 11. When the Provincials write to the General, they shall take care to explain fully the condition of their houses and colleges and of the whole Province, and to supply whatever they have learned that the superiors of houses and colleges have described too sparingly. In general they ought to write in such a way that the General may have before his eyes, as far as possible, the condition of all matters, all persons and all Provinces.

units.la: 12. Generalis ad Provinciales scribet secundo quoque mense: ad Rectores vero & Præpositos Locales sexto quoque mense, nisi aliqua necessitas prius ad respondendum suadeat.
units.tr: 12. The General shall write to the Provincials every second month, and to the rectors and local Preposites every sixth month, unless some necessity earlier urges a reply.

units.la: 13. Si quis nostrorum aliud per literas cum Præposito Generali, aut cum suo aliquo mediato Superiore tractare velit, ne impediatur: nec ipsorum literæ ad eos scriptæ aperiantur, neque mediatorum Superiorum ad ipsos.
units.tr: 13. If any of our members wishes to treat some matter by letter with the Preposite General, or with one of his own intermediate superiors, he shall not be hindered: neither shall letters written to them be opened, nor letters from their intermediate superiors to them.

units.la: 14. Literæ nostrorum, quæ negotia continent, solum ad Præpositum Generalem & non ion alios, qui cum ipso agant, destinentur: poterit tamen ad eos scribi, ut illi tractari, & expedire curent.
units.tr: 14. Letters of our members that deal with business shall be addressed only to the Preposite General and not to others who deal with him; yet they may be written to those others so that they may see to it that the matter is handled and despatched.

units.la: 15. Litera negotiorum ad quorum expeditionem Procuratoris Generalis opera, aut informatione opus erit, proprijs literas ad Præpositum Generalem scribantur, adiecta exterius litera P. sub inscriptione earum.
units.tr: 15. Letters on business for the despatch of which the work or information of the Procurator General will be needed shall be written in a separate letter to the Preposite General, with the letter P added on the outside under the address.

units.la: 16. Negotia maioris momenti, ex utraque India & Brasil. terni exemplis scribantur, quorum autem ex reliquis Provincijs, si fit periculum ne literæ intercidant, vel certè in proximis literis earum summa repetatur: & ut inveniantur, cum opus fuerit, quæ scripta sunt ad Generalem, exemplum eiusmodi literarum, vel earum summam in libro aliquo, qui scribunt, apud se retineant.
units.tr: 16. Matters of greater importance from both Indies and from Brazil shall be written in three copies; from the other Provinces, if there is a risk that letters may be lost, at least the substance shall be repeated in the next letters. And so that, when needed, they may find what has been written to the General, they shall keep by them a copy of such letters, or a summary of them, in some book which they keep.

units.la: 17. Si quid secreti scribendum, vel soli Superiori committendum sit, seorsum in propria epistola scribatur, quæ cum alijs in eodem fasciculo colligata includatur, adiecto exterius (soli) sub inscriptione eiusdem epistolæ: quod si eiusmodi epistola sola mitteretur, alia charta involvatur, quæ absque (soli) inscriptionem habeat.
units.tr: 17. If anything secret must be written, or must be entrusted only to the superior, it shall be written separately in its own letter, which shall be enclosed, tied together with the others in the same bundle, with the word (soli) added on the outside under the address of that letter. If such a letter were sent alone, it shall be wrapped in another sheet of paper, which bears no (soli) inscription.

units.la: 18. In rebus, quæ secretum requirunt explicandis, his vocabulis utendum erit, ut ea intelligi nisi à Superiore non possint: modum autem præscribet Generalis.
units.tr: 18. In explaining matters that require secrecy, words shall be used in such a way that they cannot be understood except by the superior; the General shall prescribe the manner.

units.la: 19. Nullus inferior, nisi morbo impeditus literas ad Superiorem ex sua commissione scribere faciat.
units.tr: 19. No inferior, unless prevented by illness, shall have letters written to a superior on his own commission.

units.la: 20. Consultores Rectorum, & Superiorum Localium literas obsignatas ad Provinciale habeant bis in anno, mense Ianuario, & Iulio, & ad Generalem singulis annis mense Ianuario: Consultores vero Provincialium ad Generalem mense Ianuario & Iulio, nisi res aliqua urgeret, ut de illa, etiam extra hæc tempora scribendum iudicarent.
units.tr: 20. The consultors of rectors and local superiors shall have sealed letters for the Provincial twice a year, in the months of January and July, and for the General once a year in January. The consultors of the Provincials shall write to the General in January and July, unless some matter were urgent, so that they judge it should be written about even outside these times.

units.la: 21. Ijs literis syncere, & sine amplificatione, omnique privato, aut humano respectu remoto, significabunt, quid sibi de Superioribus, quorum sunt Consultores, & de eorum administratione, ac rerum statu scribendum in Domino videatur, orationé tamen præmissa, & reprius diligenter considerata.
units.tr: 21. In those letters they shall state sincerely and without exaggeration, and free of every private or human consideration, what seems to them, in the Lord, to be written concerning the superiors whose consultors they are, and concerning their administration and the condition of affairs; yet a prayer shall be sent first, and the matter carefully considered beforehand.

units.la: 22. Vt Rector Universitatis de omnibus Præceptoribus, & alijs de Societate: ita etiam Cancellarius & Consiliarij Universitatis de ipso, ac alijs scribent semel singulis annis mense Ianuario Præposito Generali, & bis in anno mense Ianuario, & Iulio Provinciali.
units.tr: 22. Just as the Rector of the University writes about all the teachers and others of the Society, so too the Chancellor and councillors of the University shall write about him and the others once a year in January to the Preposite General, and twice a year, in January and July, to the Provincial.

units.la: 23. Hujusmodi literæ Consultorum, & horum officialium Universitatis mittantur obsignatæ, nec quisquam eorum sciat, quid alius scripserit.
units.tr: 23. Letters of these consultors and of the officials of the University shall be sent sealed, and none of them shall know what another has written.

units.la: 24. Quivis Præpositus, & Rector habeat librum, in quo scribantur Visitationes Domus, vel Collegij à Generali approbata, in quo etiam scribantur ordinationes aliæ aliquius momenti, quæ à Generali mittuntur: & quæ perpetuæ fuerint, ab ijs quæ temporariæ sunt, separatim notentur: alia vero, quæ Visitator, & Provincialis præscripserint, in alio libro scribantur.
units.tr: 24. Every Preposite and Rector shall keep a book in which the visitations of the house or college approved by the General are written, and also in which other ordinances of some importance sent by the General are written. Those that are permanent shall be noted separately from those that are temporary. Other matters which the Visitor and the Provincial have prescribed shall be written in another book.

units.la: 25. Si quid scribendum esset de rebus, quæ externorum aliquem attingerent, ita scribatur, ut etiam si littera in eius manus inciderent, offendi non possit.
units.tr: 25. If anything had to be written about matters that touch some outsider, it shall be written in such a way that, even if the letter should fall into his hands, he cannot be offended.

units.la: DE LITERIS ANNVIS.
units.tr: ON THE YEARLY LETTERS.

units.la: 26. Superiores Domorum, atque Rectores curent ea observari, quæ indies in eorum Domibus Collegijsque per nostros Dominus operari dignatur, quæque ad nostrorum consolationem, ac proximorum ædificationem pertinent, ex quibus seligant optima quæque, atque in ordinem redacta, sub finem cuiusque anni ad suum Provinciale mittant.
units.tr: 26. Superiors of the houses and rectors shall see to it that those things are noted down which the Lord daily deigns to work through our men in their houses and colleges, and which pertain to the consolation of our own people and the edification of neighbours. From these they shall select the best, arrange them in order, and send them to their Provincial at the end of each year.

units.la: 27. Provinciales ex omnibus Superiorum Localium, atque Rectorum sua Provinciæ, & eorum, qui in Missionibus versantur, epistolis rejectis vel additis, ijsque quæ viderint, singulis annis mense Ianuario, rerum gestarum capita Latinè collata, ex quibus deinde una littera annales Romæ conficiantur, manu ipsorum subscripta Romam ad Generalem destinent.
units.tr: 27. Each year, in the month of January, the Provincials shall send to the General at Rome a summary of the year's events, drawn up in Latin, made from the letters of all the local superiors and rectors of their province and of those who work in the missions, with whatever they have rejected or added and whatever they have seen fit. From these, one yearly letter shall then be compiled at Rome, signed by their own hand.

units.la: 28. In ea compendiaria narratione hic ordo servabitur: Recensebunt initio numerum nostrorum in universum, tum etiam singulis Domibus, Collegijs, & Missionibus nomi‐ natis, quot sint in iis Sacerdotes, Præceptores, Scholastici & Coadjutores temporales, i‐temque quot admissi sint eo anno in Societatem, quotque è vita decesserint: neque deinde ne‐ cesse erit ad singula Collegia aut loca redire, nisi aliquid in iis contigerit peculiari narra‐ tione dignum.
units.tr: 28. In this condensed narrative the following order shall be observed. First they shall give the number of our men in total, and then, naming each house, college and mission, how many priests, teachers, scholastics and temporal coadjutors are in each, and likewise how many were admitted into the Society that year and how many died. Afterwards it will not be necessary to return to each college or place, unless something has happened there worthy of a particular account.

units.la: 29. Agent primò de professu nostrorum in Domino, & explicabunt, si quid in eo ge‐ nere ædificationem facere possit: deinde de ministerijs Societatis erga proximos, ut de concionibus, lectionibus sacris, doctrina Christiana, & exercitijs spiritualibus, visitatione carcerum & hospitalium, reconciliatione dissidentium, de pœnitentium frequentia, & de aliis nostri instituti pijs operibus: ita tamen ut ea tantum commemorentur, quæ sunt alicuius momenti. Item de Scholis, & discipulorum numero, & professu, præsertim in Vniuersitatibus & Collegijs maioribus: de bona item Societatis existimatione, de contradictionibus autem, & persequutionibus, si quæ fuerint, ea tantum attingant, quæ ædificationi fore videbuntur. Dicent etiam de piorum erga nostros charitate, & eleemosynis paulò insignioribus.
units.tr: 29. They shall first speak of the profession of our men in the Lord, and explain, if anything of that kind can build up others. Then they shall deal with the ministries of the Society towards neighbours: sermons, sacred lectures, Christian doctrine, spiritual exercises, visiting prisons and hospitals, reconciling those at odds, the number of penitents, and other pious works of our Institute; but only those things shall be mentioned which are of some importance. Likewise concerning the schools, the number of pupils and their progress, especially in universities and major colleges; also the good reputation of the Society. As for opposition and persecutions, if there have been any, they shall touch only on those which seem likely to serve edification. They shall also speak of the charity of the pious towards our men and of alms that are somewhat notable.

units.la: 30. Hæc omnia exponent, quam plenissime fieri poterit (semper tamen vitata nimia prolixitate) adhibitis omnibus circumstantijs, etiam nominibus eorum, qui eas res gresse‐ runt, ut si opus fuerit, aliquando conscribi possit historia. Qua etiam de causa cum aliquid occurret dignum memoria, quod tamen propter aliquam causam non expediat omnibus vul‐ gari, id scribent separatim integrè, & perfectè: in illa autem communi narratione vel omnino reticebunt, vel ea tantum excerpent, quæ ædificationi esse possunt. Et quæ ad externos pertinent, ita narrentur, ut in ea ipsa domo aut ciuitate, ubi scribuntur, ac ubique publicè legi citra cuiusquam offensionem possunt.
units.tr: 30. They shall set out all these things as fully as can be done (always avoiding excessive length), with all the circumstances, and also the names of those who carried them out, so that a history may be written at some time if need be. For this reason too, when something worthy of memory occurs which, for some cause, is not expedient to make common knowledge, they shall write it up separately, in full and complete form; in the common narrative they shall either omit it altogether or extract only what can serve edification. And those matters which pertain to outsiders shall be so narrated that they can be read publicly, without offence to anyone, in the very house or city where they are written and everywhere.

units.la: 31. Cum literæ annuæ Romæ confectæ ad Prouincias mittentur, legantur quam primum in singulis Domibus & Collegijs. Et ut Coadjutores nostri temporales ex Latinis etiam li‐ teris fructum aliquem percipiant, sit aliquis, qui illarum summam, aut interpretationem a‐ liquo modo explicet: neque ultra duas hebdomadas retineri debent, ut ad reliqua loca citius deferantur: postquam verò ubique perlectæ fuerint, in præcipua Domo, vel Collegio eiusdem Prouinciæ asseruentur, & simul consuantur.
units.tr: 31. When the yearly letters have been completed at Rome and sent to the provinces, they shall be read as soon as possible in each house and college. And so that our temporal coadjutors may also gain some benefit from the Latin letters, there shall be someone who explains their substance or translation in some way. They must not be kept more than two weeks, so that they may be carried more quickly to the remaining places; but once they have been read through everywhere, they shall be preserved in the principal house or college of the same province, and at the same time bound together.

units.la: DE CATALOGIS ET INFORMATIONI‐ BVS ANNVIS.
units.tr: Concerning the Catalogues and the Annual Reports.

units.la: 32. Ad clariorem omnium nostrorum cognitionem, Superiores Domorum, & Collegiorum, duos Catalogos conficiant ante id temporis, quo Procuratores Prouinciarum ad Generalem veniunt, ita exactè, ac si nunquam missi fuissent. In primo describantur omnes, qui in suis Domibus, vel Collegijs, ac missionibus sunt, in quo continetur uniuscuiusque nomen, cognomen, patria, ætas, vires, tempus Societatis, studiorum, & ministeriorum, quæ exercuit, & gradus in literis, si quos habet, & an Professus, vel Coadjutor sit, &c. & à quo tempore.
units.tr: 32. For a clearer knowledge of all of us, the Superiors of the Houses and Colleges shall draw up two catalogues, before the time when the Provincial Procurators come to the General, and do so as exactly as if they had never been sent. In the first shall be described all who are in their Houses or Colleges, or in the missions, recording for each one his name, surname, country, age, strength, the time of his admission to the Society, the studies and ministries he has undertaken, his degree in letters, if he has any, whether he is a Professed member or a Coadjutor, and so on, and from what time.

units.la: 33. In secundo Catalogo dotes, & qualitates uniuscuiusque describantur, videlicet, ingenium, judicium, prudentia, experientia rerum, profectus in literis, naturalis complexio, & ad quæ Societatis ministeria talentum habeat: quæ omnia diligenter, re Deo priùs commendata, & maturè considerata, & omni priuato affectu semoto, syncerè, & breviter perstrin‐genda erunt, & utrunque catalogum ad suum Provincialem mittant.
units.tr: 33. In the second catalogue the gifts and qualities of each one shall be described, namely: intellect, judgement, prudence, experience of affairs, progress in letters, natural temperament, and for which ministries of the Society he has talent. All these things are to be set down carefully, after first commending the matter to God and considering it maturely, with every private affection set aside, and described sincerely and briefly; and they shall send both catalogues to their Provincial.

units.la: 34. Sub finem cuiusque anni interiecti, tertium etiam alium brevem catalogum ad Prouincialem mittant, continentem nomina, & ministeria, in quibus unusquisque nostrorum occupatur: mittant etiam supplementum primi, & secundi catalogi, in quo ea tantum adnotabunt, quæ eo anno de novo occurrerint addenda: ut qui in Societatem interim fuerint admissi, aut ab ea defuerint, vel quot mortui sint, vel alia quavis causa:
units.tr: 34. At the end of each intervening year they shall also send a third, brief catalogue to the Provincial, containing the names and the ministries in which each of our members is occupied. They shall also send a supplement to the first and second catalogues, in which they will note only those things that have newly arisen during that year and must be added: such as who have in the meantime been admitted into the Society, or have left it, or how many have died, or any other cause.

units.la: 35. Hunc tertium catalogum & supplementum primi & secundi catalogi totius Prouinciæ, cum narratione pro annuis literis, de qua dictum est, ad Generalem mittet Prouincialis ialis mense Ianuario: primum vero, & secundum per Procuratorem Provinciae, ad eundem, sigillo suo obsignatos, perferendos curabit: Quod si quid ipsi in his catalogis, & informationibus notandum addendumve videretur, id seorsum ad Generalem scribat.
units.tr: 35. The Provincial shall send this third catalogue, and the supplement to the first and second catalogues of the whole Province, together with the narrative for the annual letters of which we have spoken, to the General in the month of January. He shall also see to it that the first and second catalogues, sealed with his own seal, are carried to the same by the Procurator of the Province. If anything in these catalogues and reports seems to him to need noting or adding, he shall write about it separately to the General.

units.la: REGVLAE PRAEFECTI RERVM SPIRITVALIVM.
units.tr: RULES OF THE PREFECT OF SPIRITUAL MATTERS.

units.la: Praefectus rerum spiritualium cognitionem instituti Societatis, & zelum boni progressus ipsius habeat, & in Obedientia, & Humilitate exemplum aliis praebeat, & amabilem se eis exhibeat, ut ad eum omnes confugiant, confidenterque sua omnia detegant, & ab eo consolationem, & auxilium spererent in Domino.
units.tr: The prefect of spiritual matters should have knowledge of the Society's institute and zeal for its good progress, and should set an example to others in obedience and humility; he should show himself approachable, so that everyone may take refuge in him, confidently disclose all their concerns, and hope for consolation and help from him in the Lord.

units.la: 2. Instruat nostros privatim, secundum uniuscuiusque captum, quomodo interius, & exterius se habere debeant, & ad id exhortetur, & in memoriam redigat, & amanter admoneat, praesertim ut puram habeant intentionem divini servitii, & familiaritatem cum Deo in spiritualibus devotionis exercitijs, & zelum sincerum animarum.
units.tr: 2. He should instruct our members privately, according to each one's capacity, on how they ought to conduct themselves inwardly and outwardly; he should exhort them to this, remind them, and admonish them lovingly, especially that they have a pure intention of divine service, familiarity with God in the spiritual exercises of devotion, and sincere zeal for souls.

units.la: 3. Petat quem procedendi modum in oratione, & examine habeant, & si contra aliquem effectum examen particulare faciant, & si contra inordinatos affectus propria remedia adhibeant, & in solidis virtutibus acquirendis, praesertim in Obedientia quid observent, & poenitentijs, & aliis devotionibus.
units.tr: 3. He should ask what method they follow in prayer and examination, and whether, if they make a particular examination against some fault, they apply proper remedies against disordered affections; and what they observe in acquiring solid virtues, especially in obedience, and in penances and other devotions.

units.la: 4. Sicubi in his a rectitudine deflexerint, eos dirigat, iuxta modum Societatis: erga cuius institutum, curet, ut omnes bene affecti sint, & det operam, ut orandi & meditandi modos, quos docuit Pater noster Ignatius in libro Exercitiorum, retineant, & ut illo libro familiarissime utantur, videatque, ne dum nostri devotionem habere procurant, caput laedant, ut vires corporis nimis debilitent.
units.tr: 4. Where they have departed from rectitude in these matters, he should set them right according to the manner of the Society, toward whose institute he should see that all are well disposed; and he should take pains that they keep the modes of prayer and meditation which our father Ignatius taught in the book of the Exercises, and that they use that book most familiarly. He should also see that, while our members strive for devotion, they do not harm their head, so as to weaken the strength of the body too much.

units.la: 5. Versatum ipsum esse oportebit in lectione librorum spiritualium, & unicuique determinat tempus, & modum cum fructu eos legendi, qui sint faciliores, & nostro instituto magis convenientes.
units.tr: 5. He himself should be well versed in reading spiritual books, and he should fix for each person a time and manner of reading with profit those books which are easier and more suited to our institute.

units.la: 6. Peculiarem habeat curam consolandi afflictos, & tepidos exhortandi, remedia pro cuiusque infirmitate, vel necessitate adhibendo: qualia sunt, frequentius communicare, plus temporis orationi impendere, Exercitia spiritualia facere, plus aliquid poenitentiae assumere, libros aliquos spirituales legere, & similia. Quae autem ex his ipse concedere possit, & in quibus ad Superiorem recurrendum sit, ab eo intelligat.
units.tr: 6. He should take particular care to console the afflicted and to exhort the lukewarm, applying remedies suited to each one's weakness or need, such as communicating more often, devoting more time to prayer, making the spiritual exercises, undertaking some additional penance, reading certain spiritual books, and the like. He should learn from the Superior which of these he may grant himself, and in which cases recourse must be had to the Superior.

units.la: 7. Parem quoque adhibeat diligentiam, ut Coadjutores temporales quieti sint, & forte Marthae contenti, & pro eorum captu illos instruat, mysteriaque Rosarij doceat, ut maiore devotione illud recitare possint.
units.tr: 7. He should likewise take equal care that the temporal coadjutors are quiet and content with their lot, like Martha, and he should instruct them according to their capacity, teaching them the mysteries of the Rosary so that they can recite it with greater devotion.

units.la: 8. Doceat omnes, ut praemissa oratione, & cum magna reverentia ad Sacramentum altaris accedant, & post eius perceptionem per aliquod temporis spatium orent, & gratias agant.
units.tr: 8. He should teach everyone to approach the sacrament of the altar, after prayer and with great reverence, and after receiving it to pray and give thanks for some space of time.

units.la: 9. Praeter eos, quos satis instructos Superior iudicaverit, cum unoquoque agere de his ultra mensem ne differat: saepe vero consideret, quem fructum bonorum operum ex oratione, & ex reliquis rebus spiritualibus colligant, ut in dies magis in Domino proficiant.
units.tr: 9. Except for those whom the Superior judges sufficiently instructed, he should not delay beyond a month to speak with each one about these matters; he should often consider what fruit they gather from prayer and from the other spiritual exercises, so that they may advance more and more day by day in the Lord.

units.la: 10. In his autem omnibus videat, ne ordo unicuique praescriptus impediatur, ac praesertim studia illorum, qui literis dant operam, nisi cum Superior aliter iudicaverit.
units.tr: 10. In all these matters he should see that the order prescribed for each one is not hindered, especially the studies of those who devote themselves to letters, unless the Superior judges otherwise.

units.la: 11. Curam peculiarem habeat Novitiorum, si qui Domi, vel in Collegio fuerint, nisi a Superiore aliunde prospectum sit, & ergo eos observare studeat ea, quae iuxta Magistri Novitiorum, & examinatoris Regulas observari commode poterunt.
units.tr: 11. He should take special care of the novices, if there are any at home or in the College, unless provision has been made for them elsewhere by the Superior; and therefore he should strive to observe those things which can conveniently be observed according to the Rules of the Master of Novices and of the examiner.

units.la: REGVLÆ
units.tr: RULES

units.la: REGVLÆ PRAEFECTI ECCLESIAE.
units.tr: RULES OF THE PREFECT OF THE CHURCH

units.la: CVret, ut Aedituus Regulas suas obserVet, quas Præfectus ipse apud se etiam habeat. 1. Præbeat illi catalogum singulis diebus Sabbathi, quo dies festi, ac jejuniorum proximæ hebdomadæ contineantur, ut eum in refectorio reciter in cœna diei Dominicæ sequentis.
units.tr: He shall see that the sacristan observes his rules, which the Prefect himself also keeps by him. (1) He shall give him a list on every Saturday of the feast days and fasts falling in the following week, so that it may be read out in the refectory at supper on the following Sunday.

units.la: 2. Singulis diebus Sabbathi vesperi in Sacristia scripto proponat, quemadmodum quotidie Sacra sint facienda sequenti hebdomada, & quo ordine rem divinam in Altari summo facturi sint, qui ad hoc fuerint designati.
units.tr: (2) On every Saturday evening he shall post in the sacristy, in writing, how the Masses are to be said each day of the coming week, and in what order those designated for this purpose are to celebrate at the high altar.

units.la: 3. Detur opera, ne in Altari maximo desit unquam Sacrum, quo tempore celebrari solet, habeaturque ratio, ne plura Sacra simul inchoentur, sed commode omnia suis spatiis distinguantur.
units.tr: (3) He shall take care that Mass is never missing from the high altar at the usual time, and he shall see that several Masses do not begin at once, but that all are suitably spaced out in their own times.

units.la: 4. Curam gerat Missarum, & orationum, quæ pro defunctis Societatis, & pro Fundatoribus, & Benefactoribus, ac pro ipsa Societate fieri debent, quas ex subjecto catalogo intelliget: & catalogum earum, quæ secundum nostrum institutum, & ex præscripto Generalis ordinarie faciendæ sunt, referat in duas tabellas, quarum alteram appendat in Sacristia, alteram in alio conveniente loco, quæ initio cuiusque mensis publice in Refectorio legetur.
units.tr: (4) He shall oversee the Masses and prayers that ought to be offered for the deceased members of the Society, for the Founders and Benefactors, and for the Society itself, which he will learn from the attached list. He shall also draw up a catalogue of those that are ordinarily to be said according to our Institute and the General's directions, in two tables: one he shall hang in the sacristy, the other in another suitable place, and it shall be read publicly in the refectory at the beginning of each month.

units.la: 5. Cum Superior aliquid in Sacro Deo commendari, aut Sacra ipsa, quæ ab omnibus fiient, applicari ad finem aliquem jusserit, curet scribi in schedula in Sacristia affigenda.
units.tr: (5) When the Superior has ordered that something be commended to God in the Sacrifice, or that the Masses which all are to say be applied to some intention, he shall see that it is written on a notice to be posted in the sacristy.

units.la: 6. Quæ cunq; autem ex his non ab omnibus facienda erunt, ea Præfectus unicuique privatim significanda curabit.
units.tr: (6) Whatever of these things are not to be done by everyone, the Prefect shall take care to notify privately to each person concerned.

units.la: 7. Librum habeat, ubi mandata Superiorum de his rebus, si aliquandiu duratura, aut statim facienda sint, scribantur, ne memoria excidat, & cum fuerint adimpleta, deleantur.
units.tr: (7) He shall keep a book in which the Superiors' instructions on these matters are written down, whether they are to last for some time or are to be done at once, so that they do not slip from memory; and when they have been carried out, they are to be crossed out.

units.la: 8. In Collegiis & Domibus probationum curet juxta ordinem Superiorum de candelis danda Fundatoribus juxta Constitutionem.
units.tr: (8) In the colleges and houses of probation he shall see that candles are given to the Founders, according to the Constitution and the order of the Superiors.

units.la: 9. Si quando externi Sacra aliqua fieri postulaverint, se Superiorem consulturum respondeat: nisi eius animum perspectum jam habeat.
units.tr: (9) If outsiders ever ask for some Mass to be said, he shall answer that he will consult the Superior, unless he already knows the Superior's mind.

units.la: 10. Externos Sacerdotes ad faciendum Sacrum in nostro templo, non sine delectu admittat, sed eos tantum, qui ædificationi sint, præsertim notos, idq; juxta ordinem Superiorum: & intelligat an a suo Ordinario legitimam habeant facultatem.
units.tr: (10) He shall not admit outside priests to say Mass in our church without discrimination, but only those who will be an edification, especially those who are known, and this in accordance with the Superiors' order. He shall also ascertain whether they have legitimate faculties from their own Ordinary.

units.la: 11. Videat an Sacerdotes Regulas suas observent, & num barbam, & coronam decenter tonsam habeant.
units.tr: (11) He shall see whether the priests keep their rules, and whether they have their beards and tonsure properly trimmed.

units.la: 12. Per se, vel alium a Superiore designatum, promovendos ad Sacerdotium instrui curet, & videat ut ad Romanæ Ecclesiæ ritum tam ij, quam omnes Sacerdotes se accommodent, & ne confessiones audiant, nisi sint legitime approbati.
units.tr: (12) He shall either himself, or through another designated by the Superior, see that those to be promoted to the priesthood are instructed, and he shall see that both these and all priests conform to the rite of the Roman Church, and that they do not hear confessions unless they have been legitimately approved.

units.la: 13. Animadvertat, nulla pro Sacris faciendis aut confessionibus audiendis eleemosynæ admittantur.
units.tr: (13) He shall take care that no alms are accepted for saying Masses or hearing confessions.

units.la: 14. Nulla sit in Ecclesia arcula, in qua Eleemosynæ conjiciantur, sive pro nobis, sive pro aliis.
units.tr: (14) There shall be no money box in the church into which alms are put, whether for us or for others.

units.la: 15. Det operam, ut sanctissimum Domini nostri Corpus decenter in custodia conservetur, diligenter cavens, ne unquam in ea Sacramentum desit, habita communicantium ratione, & ut saltem decimo quinto quoq; die innovetur, & Sacris absolutis in tabernaculo clavi obseretur.
units.tr: 15. He shall take care that the most holy Body of our Lord is kept decently in custody, taking diligent care that the Sacrament is never lacking in it, with regard to the number of communicants; and that it be renewed at least every fifteenth day, and that, once the sacred rites are finished, it be locked up in the tabernacle with a key.

units.la: 16. Quando nostri in templo communicaverint, curet Præfectus, ut id faciant separatim ab externis.
units.tr: 16. When our people have communicated in the church, the Prefect shall see to it that they do so separately from outsiders.

units.la: 17. Oleum Sancti, ut oportet, asservatum singulis annis renovet, & Sanctorum reliquias (quæ quidem mobiles fuerint) in tabernaculo ad id deputato decenter custodiat: si quando autem devotionis causa ostendenda erunt, duo cerei accendantur: atq; huius tabernaculi clavem unam ipse habeat, & alteram diversam Præpositus, aut Rector.
units.tr: 17. Let him renew the holy oil each year, as is fitting, when it has been kept; and let him keep the relics of the saints (those, that is, which are portable) decently in the tabernacle set apart for them. If they must be displayed for the sake of devotion, two candles shall be lit. The Provost or Rector shall hold one key to this tabernacle himself, and the Provost holds a different one.

units.la: 19. Cruces, Calices, ornamenta, & reliqua id genus, ut par est, custodiantur: nec desint velamina ad cooperiendos calices, & alia ad divinum cultum, & ornatum necessaria.
units.tr: (19) Crosses, chalices, vestments and similar things are to be kept as is fitting, and there must be no lack of veils for covering the chalices, and of other things necessary for divine worship and adornment.

units.la: 20. Mutari faciat Altarium, & Sacerdotum ornamenta, quod ad colorem attinet hac vita temporum, & Festorum ratione, juxta ritum Romanae Ecclesiae.
units.tr: (20) He shall have the altar cloths and the priests' vestments changed, as to colour, according to the season of the year and the feasts, in keeping with the rite of the Roman Church.

units.la: 21. Cum templum ornandum fuerit, nihil sine facultate Superioris ad tam rem commodato ab externis petat: detque operam, ut quod acceptum fuerit, accurate custodiatur, & dominis quam primum reddatur.
units.tr: (21) When the church is to be decorated, he shall ask for nothing from outsiders on loan for this purpose without the Superior's permission. He shall also see that whatever has been received is carefully kept and returned to its owners as soon as possible.

units.la: 22. Si templum instauratione, aliqua in parte indiguerit, aut aliis ad divinum cultum necessariis, provideat, sicut ipsi a Superiore fuerit praescriptum.
units.tr: (22) If the church needs repair in some part, or other things necessary for divine worship, he shall provide them, as the Superior shall prescribe to him.

units.la: 23. Superiori in memoriam redigat, ut aliquos designet, qui de concionibus, & modo concionandi judicare possint: quorum saltem unus concioni interfit, ut Concionatorem, cum opus fuerit, & Superiori videbitur, admonere possit.
units.tr: (23) He shall remind the Superior to designate some men who can judge the sermons and the manner of preaching, of whom at least one should attend a sermon, so that he may admonish the preacher when necessary and as the Superior thinks fit.

units.la: 24. Conciones & lectiones templi, horae spatium superare non debet: eo vero ordine Missae dicantur, ne impediant, quo minus conciones tempore praefixo inchoentur.
units.tr: (24) The sermons and the readings in the church must not exceed the space of an hour; and the Masses are to be said in such an order that they do not hinder the sermons from beginning at the appointed time.

units.la: 25. Advertat ne viri in templo, mulierum locum occupent, neve ex adverso earum quantum fieri poterit, maneant.
units.tr: (25) He shall see that men do not occupy the women's place in the church, nor, on the opposite side, remain there as far as can be helped.

units.la: 26. Curet ne domi desint Confessarij, qui necessarij in templo nostro sunt, & ut confessiones vesperi decenti hora absolvantur.
units.tr: (26) He shall see that confessors who are needed in our church are not absent from it at home, and that confessions are heard in the evening at a suitable hour.

units.la: 27. Pridie Palmarum Confessarios admoneat, ut Constitutionem illam observent, quae ad externos ad suas Parochias dimittendos Eucharistiae sumendae gratia pertinet, & ante id tempus, si consuetudo regionis id postulaverit.
units.tr: (27) On the day before Palm Sunday he shall remind the confessors to observe the Constitution concerning the sending of outsiders to their own parishes to receive the Eucharist, and this before that time too, if local custom requires it.

units.la: 28. Officia Hebdomadae Sanctae, & Vesperae (si haec dicetur,) fiant tono simplici more Sanctorum sine cantu etiam firmo, nisi ubi Generalis Praepositus dispensaverit: id autem quod de vesperis dictum est, de Benedictione candelarum, & ramorum intelligatur.
units.tr: (28) The offices of Holy Week, and Vespers (if these are to be said), are to be performed in a simple tone, after the manner of the saints, without even firm chant, unless the General Provost has granted a dispensation where it is needed. What has been said of Vespers is to be understood also of the blessing of the candles and of the palms.

units.la: 29. Cum aliquid petendum erit pro Ecclesia, aut usu Sacristiae, intelligat in ea re Superioris voluntatem, eamque exequatur: cumque pecuniae alicuius momenti summa dabitur, aut colligetur, eam deponat apud Procuratorem in scrinio aliquo, cuius clavem unam Superior habeat, & alteram diversam ipse Praefectus.
units.tr: (29) When something is to be requested for the church, or for the use of the sacristy, he shall understand the Superior's will in the matter and carry it out. And when a sum of money of some importance is given or collected, he shall deposit it with the Procurator in some chest, of which the Superior shall have one key and the Prefect himself another, different one.

units.la: 30. Librum habeat, in quo eleemosynarum, quae Ecclesiae usibus dantur, & expensarum rationes constent.
units.tr: (30) He shall keep a book in which the accounts of the alms given for the church's uses, and of the expenses, are recorded.

units.la: 31. Panni omnes lintei semper mundi serventur, & separatim corporalia, atque etiam purificatoria (quae quatuor cruces in angulis habeant) laventur, & utriusque abutio, & cineres eorum, quae vetustate consumpta comburuntur, in sacram piscinam mittantur.
units.tr: (31) All linen cloths shall always be kept clean, and the corporals, as well as the purificators (which are to have four crosses at the corners), shall be washed separately; and the ashes of those that are worn out and burned, as well as the water in which these were washed, shall be poured into the sacred piscina.

units.la: 32. Catalogum unum rerum omnium Ecclesiae mobilium, quae alicuius momenti sunt, custodiat: in altero vero illa scribantur, quae aut nova sibi traduntur, cum die, anno, & cui sunt vetustate consumuntur, ut possit cum exigetur, prioris catalogi rationem reddere: saepe etiam res pretiosiores inspiciet, ne aut laedantur, aut amittantur, arcus in quibus servantur, & Sacristiae januis bene clausis, & munitis.
units.tr: (32) He shall keep one catalogue of all the movable goods of the church that are of some value; and in a second he shall write down those things that are newly handed over to him, with the day, year and to whom they belong, and those that are consumed by age, so that when required he can give an account from the earlier catalogue. He shall also often inspect the more precious things, so that they are neither damaged nor lost; the chests in which they are kept, and the doors of the sacristy, are to be kept well closed and secured.

units.la: 33. Cum nostrorum aliquis extremum diem obierit, spatio diei naturalis decenter teneatur, nisi ratione mali odoris, aut ex alia justa causa, anteverti hoc tempus Superiori posse videretur.
units.tr: (33) When one of our men has died, the body is to be kept decently for the space of a natural day, unless, on account of a bad smell or some other just cause, it seems to the Superior that this time may be shortened.

units.la: 34. Observetur circa vestitum Sacerdotum mortuorum, quod de viventibus dicitur in Constitutionibus, ut scilicet utamur eo modo, quo Sacerdotes honesti eius regionis, in qua versamur, uti solent: fratres vero qui Sacerdotes non sunt, sepeliantur eo modo induti, quo alii Clerici honesti, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, sepeliri solent.
units.tr: (34) Regarding the vestments of deceased priests, what is said of the living in the Constitutions is to be observed: namely, that we use the manner that the respectable priests of the region where we live are accustomed to use. Brothers who are not priests, however, are to be buried in the dress in which other respectable clerics who are not priests are customarily buried.

units.la: 35. Curam suscipiet sepulchri, candelarum, precum, quae consueto more dicuntur, rerumque aliarum, quae ad eam rem erunt necessariae.
units.tr: (35) He shall take charge of the grave, the candles, the prayers said in the customary manner, and the other things that will be necessary for that purpose.

units.la: MISSARVM, ET ALIARVM SACRORVM QVÆ NOSTRÆ SOCIETATIS CAUSA FIUNT, CATALOGVS
units.tr: CATALOGUE OF MASSES AND OTHER SACRED OBSERVANCES WHICH ARE MADE FOR THE SAKE OF OUR SOCIETY

units.la: SACRA IVXTA NOSTRVM institutum à Sacerdotibus So- cietatis ordinariè facienda.
units.tr: Sacred observances to be performed ordinarily by the Priests of the Society, according to our institute.

units.la: Singulis annis.
units.tr: Every year.

units.la: 1. IN principio cuiusque anni unusquisque Sacerdos Missam celebret pro nostra Societate.
units.tr: 1. At the beginning of each year, let every Priest celebrate Mass for our Society.

units.la: 2. Singulis annis præscripto die, in quo memoria fundationis Collegii vel Domus fit, Missa cum solennitate pro Fundatore proprii Collegii, vel Domus, celebretur: & reliqui Sacerdotes, qui in eadem sua Sacrificia offerant.
units.tr: 2. On the prescribed day each year, on which the memory of the foundation of the College or House is kept, let a Mass be celebrated with solemnity for the Founder of the particular College or House, and let the other Priests who are present offer their Sacrifices for the same intention.

units.la: Singulis mensibus.
units.tr: Every month.

units.la: 3. In principio cuiusque mensis unusquisque Sacerdos Missam celebret pro nostra Societate.
units.tr: 3. At the beginning of each month, let every Priest celebrate Mass for our Society.

units.la: 4. Initio cuiusque mensis omnes Sacerdotes, qui in Collegio, vel Domo fuerint, pro Fundatore proprii Collegii, vel Domus, & benefactoribus vivis, & c.
units.tr: 4. At the beginning of each month, all the Priests who are in the College or House shall offer for the Founder of the particular College or House, and for living benefactors, etc.

units.la: Singulis hebdomadis.
units.tr: Every week.

units.la: 5. Singuli Sacerdotes pro illis de Societate, qui extra Provinciam moriuntur, semel in quavis hebdomada Missæ sacrificium offerant.
units.tr: 5. Individual Priests shall offer the sacrifice of the Mass once in each week for those of the Society who die outside the Province.

units.la: 6. Singulis hebdomadis, ubicunque fuerint decem, vel pauciores Sacerdotes, pro nostra Societate una Missa, à designato à Superiore dicetur: duæ verò, si fuerint plures, quàm decem: tres atque ita deinceps in reliquis decadibus, si numerus id permittit.
units.tr: 6. Each week, wherever there are ten or fewer Priests, one Mass for our Society shall be said by a priest designated by the Superior; but two if there are more than ten, and three, and so on in the remaining tens, if the number allows it.

units.la: 7. Singulis hebdomadis pro Benefactoribus vivis, & defunctis propriæ Domus vel Collegii, præter eas quæ pro Fundatore dicuntur, una, aut duæ, aut plures Missæ pro numero Sacerdotum prædictum.
units.tr: 7. Each week, for the living and deceased benefactors of the particular House or College, besides those which are said for the Founder, one, or two, or more Masses, according to the number of the aforesaid Priests.

units.la: ORATIONVM,
units.tr: OF PRAYERS,

units.la: L AE OGVS
units.tr: L AE OGVS

units.la: ORATIONES IVXTA NO- STRVM institutum, abiis, qui Sacer- dotes non sunt, ordinarie faciendae:
units.tr: Prayers, according to our institute, to be said ordinarily by those who are not priests:

units.la: Singulis annis:
units.tr: Every year:

units.la: ET singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ad eandem intentionem integrum Rosarium Dominae nostrae, videlicet centum quinquaginta Aue Maria, & quindecim Pater noster, aut tres coronas recitent.
units.tr: Likewise, each of those who are not priests shall recite, for the same intention, a whole Rosary of Our Lady, namely one hundred and fifty Hail Marys and fifteen Our Fathers, or three chaplets.

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt ad eandem intentionem unam coronam, aut tertiam partem Rosarij recitent.
units.tr: And each of those who are not priests shall recite, for the same intention, one chaplet, or a third part of the Rosary.

units.la: & benefactoribus vivis, & defunctis cuiuscunque collegio, vel Domino habitaverint, pro eis
units.tr: ...and for living and dead benefactors of whatever college, or of the house in which they have lived, for them.

units.la: Singulis mensibus.
units.tr: Every month:

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ad eandem intentionem tertiam Rosarij partem, aut unam coronam recitent.
units.tr: And each of those who are not priests shall recite, for the same intention, a third part of the Rosary, or one chaplet.

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ad eandem intentionem unam coronam, aut tertiam Rosarij partem recitent: defunctis semel Missae sacrificium offerant.
units.tr: And each of those who are not priests shall recite, for the same intention, one chaplet or a third part of the Rosary, and for the dead shall offer the sacrifice of the Mass once.

units.la: Singulis hebdomadis.
units.tr: Every week:

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ad eandem intentionem unam coronam, aut tertiam Rosarij partem recitent.
units.tr: And each of those who are not priests shall recite, for the same intention, one chaplet or a third part of the Rosary.

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, in quavis hebdomada ad eandem intentionem septem Pater noster, & septem Aue Maria recitent.
units.tr: And each of those who are not priests shall recite, in every week, for the same intention, seven Our Fathers and seven Hail Marys.

units.la: Vtem, si fuerint plures, quam viginti: & erunt Sacerdotum fuerit maior.
units.tr: Likewise, if there are more than twenty, and the number of priests is greater...

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, in quavis hebdomada ad eandem intentionem septem Pater noster, & septem Aue Maria recitent.
units.tr: And each of those who are not priests shall recite, in every week, for the same intention, seven Our Fathers and seven Hail Marys.

units.la: um offerantur, servando ordinem modo
units.tr: ...be offered, observing the order in the manner

units.la: 8. Singulis hebdomadis Missa sel-mel pro Fundatore proprii Collegii, vel Domus, & benefactoribus vivis, & defunctis à designato à Superiore celebretur.
units.tr: 8. Each week one Mass shall be celebrated once for the founder of the proper college or house, and for living and dead benefactors, by the one designated by the Superior.

units.la: 9. In Domibus & Collegiis, quae saltem viginti ex nostris alere possunt, etiam si non habeant proprium Fundatorem, fiant pro iis vivis, & defunctis, qu-runt, eadem Sacra quae pro Fundatoribus
units.tr: 9. In houses and colleges which can support at least twenty of ours, even if they do not have a proper founder, the same Masses as are said for founders shall be made for those living and dead who...

units.la: SACRA AB EISDEM EX-traordinarie facienda
units.tr: Sacrifices to be offered by the same men extraordinarily

units.la: 10. Cum primum Societas in Collegii alicuius possessionem venerit, quilibet Sacerdos ter Sacrum faciat pro superstite Fundatore ipsius, ac Benefactoribus.
units.tr: 10. As soon as the Society comes into possession of any college, each priest shall offer three Masses for its surviving founder and for the benefactors.

units.la: 11. Cum ex hac vita idem Fundator excesserit, singuli Sacerdotes ter Sacrum pro anima illius, & Benefactorum faciant.
units.tr: 11. When the same founder has departed from this life, the individual priests shall offer three Masses for his soul and for the benefactors.

units.la: 12. Idem iudicium erit de Communitatibus, vel Rebus, quae non moriuntur: fient enim tria Sacra pro viventibus, & tria pro defunctis earum. Sic etiam faciendum, quando plures simul fundationem constituunt.
units.tr: 12. The same judgment shall hold for communities, or for properties, which do not die: three Masses shall be offered for the living, and three for their dead. The same is to be done when several together establish a foundation.

units.la: 13. Cum primum Societas in alicuius Domus professe possessionem venerit, quilibet Sacerdos intra illam Provinciam ter Sacrum faciat pro superstite Fundatore ipsius, ac benefactoribus: & quando vita functus fuerit, alia tria Sacra ab eisdem pro animabus illius & benefactorum fiant.
units.tr: 13. As soon as the Society comes into possession of a professed house, each priest within that province shall offer three Masses for its surviving founder and for the benefactors; and when he has died, three other Masses shall be offered by the same for the souls of him and of the benefactors.

units.la: 14. Pro Communitatibus vero, & pluribus, qui simul Domus professae fundationem constituunt, fiant intra eandem provinciam, quae de Collegiis dicta sunt num. 10. 11. 12.
units.tr: 14. For communities, however, and for several who together establish the foundation of a professed house, the things said of colleges in nos. 10, 11 and 12 shall be done within the same province.

units.la: 15. In domo, vel Collegio ubi quis de Societate decesserit, singuli Sacerdotes pro eo tria Sacra in aliis vero Provinciae locis duo sacra faciant.
units.tr: 15. In a house or college where any member of the Society has died, each priest shall offer three Masses for him; but in other places of the province, they shall offer two Masses.

units.la: 16. Cum de obitu cuiusque nostro-Et unus ex iis, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, à Superiore designatus, ad eandem intentionem unam coronam, aut tertiam partem Rosarij recitet.
units.tr: 16. When word of the death of any one of ours... and one of those who are not priests, designated by the Superior, shall recite, for the same intention, one chaplet or a third part of the Rosary.

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ad eandem intentionem pro eisdem facere debent easdem orationes, quæ pro Fundatoribus ordinariè fieri solent.
units.tr: And each of those who are not priests shall, for the same intention, make for them the same prayers which are ordinarily made for founders.

units.la: eorum fundationem notabiliter adiuvē-rus ordinarie fieri solent.
units.tr: ...of those who notably aided their foundation, are ordinarily made.

units.la: ORATIONES AB EISDEM extraordinarie faciendæ.
units.tr: EXTRAORDINARY PRAYERS TO BE SAID BY THE SAME PERSONS

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ad eandem intentionem, Rosarium integrum aut tres coronas recitent.
units.tr: Likewise, each of those who are not priests shall recite, for the same intention, the whole Rosary or three chaplets.

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ad eandem intentionem Rosarium integrum, aut tres coronas recitent.
units.tr: Likewise, each of those who are not priests shall recite, for the same intention, the whole Rosary or three chaplets.

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, integrum Rosarium aut tres coronas pro viventibus Communitatibus, & totidem pro defunctis earum recitabunt. Similiter facient, quando plures simul fundationem constituunt.
units.tr: Each of those who are not priests shall recite the whole Rosary or three chaplets for the living members of the communities, and as many for their deceased members. They shall do the same when several together establish a foundation.

units.la: Et singuli eiusdem Provinciæ, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, integrum Rosarium, aut tres coronas pro superstite Fundatore, ac benefactoribus: & quando vita functus fuerit, alterum Rosarium integrum, aut tres coronas pro animabus illius ac benefactorum recitent.
units.tr: Each person of the same province who is not a priest shall recite the whole Rosary, or three chaplets, for the founder while he survives, and for the benefactors; and when he has died, another whole Rosary, or three chaplets, for the souls of him and of the benefactors.

units.la: Et singuli eiusdem Provinciæ, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ad eandem intentionem faciant, quæ de Collegijs, eisdem numeris dicta sunt.
units.tr: Each person of the same province who is not a priest shall act for the same intention, with the same numbers, as has been stated concerning the colleges.

units.la: Et singuli eiusdem Domus, aut Collegij, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, pro eo tres coronas, aut tres partes Rosarij: pro aliis verò eiusdem Provinciæ duas coronas, aut duas partes Rosarij recitent.
units.tr: Each person of the same house or college who is not a priest shall recite three chaplets, or three parts of the Rosary, for that founder; but for others of the same province, two chaplets, or two parts of the Rosary.

units.la: Et singuli qui Sacerdotes non sunt, in suis orationibus illius animam Deo commendent, pro cuiusque devotione.
units.tr: Each of those who are not priests shall commend his soul to God in his prayers, according to each one's devotion.

units.la: Et omnes, qui Sacerdotes non sunt,
units.tr: And all who are not priests

units.la: Constitutiones frequenter orare pro universa Ecclesia, ac pro iis praesertim, qui maioris sunt momenti ad eius universale bonum, cuiusmodi sunt Principes Ecclesiastici, & seculares, & alii, qui multum prodesse, vel obesse bono animarum possunt: & pro amicis, & benefactoribus viventibus, & vita functis; & pro aliis, in quorum auxilium peculiariter ipsi, & reliqui de Societate in variis locis inter fideles, & infideles, incumbunt, & etiam pro male affectis erga nostram Societatem; idem iuxta Constitutiones curare debent.
units.tr: shall, as the Constitutions require, frequently pray for the whole Church, and especially for those who are of greater importance to its universal good, such as ecclesiastical and secular princes, and others who can greatly help or harm the good of souls; and for friends and benefactors, living and dead; and for others on whose behalf they themselves and the rest of the Society labour in various places among the faithful and the unbelievers; and also for those ill disposed towards our Society. They must likewise attend to these things according to the Constitutions.

units.la: SACRA EX PRÆSCRIPTO P. N. Generalis ab unoquoque Sacerdote Societatis ordinarie facienda; ORATIONES EX PRÆSCRIPTO P. N. Generalis à singulis, qui Sacerdotes non sunt ordina- rie faciendæ.
units.tr: MASSES TO BE SAID ORDINARILY BY EACH PRIEST OF THE SOCIETY, ACCORDING TO THE PRESCRIPT OF OUR FATHER GENERAL; PRAYERS TO BE SAID ORDINARILY BY EACH OF THOSE WHO ARE NOT PRIESTS, ACCORDING TO THE PRESCRIPT OF OUR FATHER GENERAL

units.la: 18. Vnusquisque Sacerdos singulis mensibus duo Sacra faciat, alterum pro Indiis, & Gentium conversione: alterum pro regionibus Septentrionalibus, & Haereticorum reductione, & in aliis Sacrificiis, & orationibus eadem Domino commendabit.
units.tr: 18. Each priest shall celebrate two Masses each month, one for the Indies and the conversion of the Gentiles, the other for the northern regions and the reclaiming of heretics; and in other sacrifices and prayers he shall commend these same causes to the Lord.

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, unam coronam, aut tertiam partem Rosarij pro Indijs, & Gentium conversione: & alteram coronam, aut tertiam Rosarij partem pro regionibus Septentrionalibus, & Haereticorum reductione recitent, & in aliis orationibus eadem Domino commendabunt.
units.tr: Each of those who are not priests shall recite one chaplet, or a third part of the Rosary, for the Indies and the conversion of the Gentiles, and another chaplet, or a third part of the Rosary, for the northern regions and the reclaiming of heretics; and in other prayers they shall commend these same causes to the Lord.

units.la: 19. Singulis hebdomadis unusquisque Sacerdos Sacrum unum ad intentionem Reverendi Patris nostri Generalis faciat, & in aliis Sacrificiis, & orationibus eadem Domino commendabit.
units.tr: 19. Each week every priest shall celebrate one Mass for the intention of our Reverend Father General, and in other sacrifices and prayers he shall commend this same intention to the Lord.

units.la: Et singuli, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, ad eandem intentionem unam coronam, aut tertiam Rosarij partem recitent, & in aliis Orationibus eandem Domino commendabunt.
units.tr: Each of those who are not priests shall recite, for the same intention, one chaplet, or a third part of the Rosary, and in other prayers they shall commend the same intention to the Lord.

units.la: Non intendimus per ea, quae superius recensentur, excludi reliqua Sacra, & orationes omnes, quae pro occurrentibus necessitatibus à Superioribus imponi ad tempus solent.
units.tr: By what has been listed above we do not intend to exclude the other Masses and all the prayers which superiors are accustomed to impose for a time, for emergent needs.

units.la: REGVLÆ SACERDOTVM
units.tr: THE RULES FOR PRIESTS

units.la: Quae de Disciplina religiosa in Regulis, & instituto nostro servanda omnibus pro posita sunt, ea Sacerdotes, pro ratione sui gradus, sibi praecipue dicta existiment & observent.
units.tr: Let the priests, according to their rank, consider and observe as addressed especially to themselves all that has been laid down in the Rules and in our Institute concerning religious discipline to be kept by everyone.

units.la: 2. Divinum officium nitantur attentè, devotè, & opportuno tempore recitare.
units.tr: 2. Let them strive to recite the divine office attentively, devoutly, and at a suitable time.

units.la: 3. Ita vivere studeant, ut quotidie merito celebrare possint: ad idque conducet (quamvis ex Constitutione octava, ut minimum quoque die confiteri teneantur) sapius in hebdomada confiteri.
units.tr: 3. Let them study to live in such a way that they can celebrate Mass worthily each day. To this end it will help (although under the eighth Constitution they are bound to confess at least once a day) to confess more often in the week.

units.la: 4. Caerimonias Missae ex usu Romano accurate unusquisque observet: in eaque celebranda pronunciationem, & quamcunque aliam, exteriorem actionem ita moderetur, ut non minus aliorum aedificationi, quam propriae devotioni serviat, & ideo semihoram in faciendo Sacro nec multum excedat, neque ita brevis sit, ut illam non expleat.
units.tr: 4. Let each one observe the ceremonies of the Mass carefully, according to the Roman custom. In celebrating it, let him so regulate his pronunciation and all his other outward actions that they serve the edification of others no less than his own devotion. For this reason he should not exceed half an hour in saying Mass, nor be so brief that he does not complete it.

units.la: 5. Qui in summo Altari Sacra facturi sunt, simulatque campanae se vocantis pulsum audierint, vel admoniti fuerint, ad vestes Sacerdotales induendas se conferant, ut in tempore exire ex Sacristia possint.
units.tr: 5. Those who are going to say Mass at the high altar, as soon as they hear the bell's summons or are warned, should betake themselves to put on their priestly vestments, so that they can leave the sacristy on time.

units.la: 6. Salutare tradendae doctrinae Christianae ministerium pueris, ac rudibus quod à sui origine nostra Societas tanto affectu complexa est, pari omnes studio promovere curent. 7. Intelligant sibi ratione peculiari incumbere, ut exercitiorum spiritualium, quae tantopere ad Dei obsequium conferre cernuntur, usum valde familiarem habeant: quo, & alios ad ea suscipienda adducere, & in eo tam utili armorum spiritualium genere tractando dexteritatem habere possint.
units.tr: 6. Let all of them take care to promote with equal zeal the ministry of teaching Christian doctrine to children and the unlearned, which our Society from its origin has embraced with such affection. 7. Let them understand that they have a special duty to be very familiar with the spiritual exercises, which are seen to contribute so greatly to the service of God, so that they may both lead others to undertake them and have skill in handling this most useful kind of spiritual weapon.

units.la: 8. Omnes ij, quibus ex Obedientia confessiones audiendi sanctum munus commissum est, multum ad id afficiantur, & tanquam nostri instituti valde proprium magni faciant.
units.tr: 8. All those to whom the holy task of hearing confessions has been entrusted by obedience should be much devoted to it, and hold it in high regard as something very proper to our Institute.

units.la: 9. Nemo ad confessiones audiendas accedat, nisi a Superiore deputatus, & qui simul intelligat, quam facultatem ad hoc munus ab eo habeat.
units.tr: 9. No one should approach to hear confessions unless he has been deputed by the Superior, and at the same time understands what faculty he has from him for this office.

units.la: 10. Modum ea Sacramenta ministrandi, quae Sacerdotes nostrae Societatis tractare possunt, perspectum omnes habeant, in eoque uniformes sint, quantum regionum varietas patitur: formam tamen & rationem absolvendi ab excommunicatione, & aliis censuris, & peccatis, eandem omnes sequantur, attendantque, ne ex modo utendi facultatibus Societatis, Ordinarij, & Parochi jure offendi possint.
units.tr: 10. Let all have a thorough knowledge of the manner of administering those sacraments which the priests of our Society may handle, and let them be uniform in this, so far as the variety of regions allows. Nevertheless, let all follow the same form and method of absolving from excommunication, from other censures, and from sins, and let them take care not to give offence by the way they use the faculties of the Society, of the Ordinary, and of the parish priest.

units.la: 11. In casibus conscientiae, ijsque praesertim qui ad censuras, casus reservatos, & restitutiones pertinent, sese diligenter exerceant: earumque rerum compendia, & brevem interrogandi methodum, ac contra singulorum peccatorum species, exempla & dicta Sanctorum, atque alia salutaria remedia comparare studeant.
units.tr: 11. In cases of conscience, especially those that pertain to censures, reserved cases, and restitutions, let them exercise themselves diligently. Let them study to gather summaries of these matters and a brief method of questioning, as well as examples and sayings of the Saints and other salutary remedies against the particular kinds of each sin.

units.la: 12. Confessarij inter seipsos, & in modo procedendi cum poenitentibus conformes esse curent: & quantum res tulerit, ita aliorum Confessariorum existimationi unusquisque consulat, ut omnes intelligant, mutuo charitatis & uniformis doctrinae vinculo, Societatis Confessarios in Christo esse colligatos.
units.tr: 12. Let the confessors take care to be agreed among themselves, and in their manner of dealing with penitents. And as far as circumstances allow, let each one so consult the esteem of the other confessors that all may understand that the confessors of the Society are bound together in Christ by the bond of mutual charity and uniform teaching.

units.la: 13. Vocati ad Ecclesiam ad Confessiones audiendas, statim cum animi alacritate eo se conferant: & quo major poenitentium multitudo futura est, eo magis tempestive ab aliis occupationibus se expediant.
units.tr: 13. When called to the church to hear confessions, let them go there at once with cheerfulness of spirit; and the greater the number of penitents to be expected, the more promptly let them free themselves from their other occupations.

units.la: 14. In templo confessiones, dum concio fit, vel sacra lectio, nemo audiat.
units.tr: 14. In the church, no one should hear confessions while a sermon or a sacred reading is being given.

units.la: 15. Confessarij ita audiant poenitentes, ut mutuum aspectum fugiant: sic enim attentius & liberius audient: quod si locus non erit eiusmodi, ut tabula Confessarii a confitente dividat, manus interposita inter faciem propriam, & confitentem, qui ad latus esse debet, id praestabit.
units.tr: 15. Let confessors hear penitents in such a way as to avoid meeting each other's gaze, for in this way they will listen more attentively and more freely. But if the place is not such that a screen separates the confessor from the one confessing, let him place his hand between his own face and the penitent, who ought to be at his side; this will serve the purpose.

units.la: 16. In audiendis confessionibus, foeminarum praesertim, severos potius se, quam familiares exhibeant: in universum tamen paterna quaedam, & spiritualis gravitas in eis eluceat.
units.tr: 16. In hearing confessions, especially those of women, let them show themselves stern rather than familiar. Nevertheless, in general, a certain fatherly and spiritual gravity should shine forth in them.

units.la: 17. Eos, qui crebrius confitentur, maxime foeminas, breviter expediant, nec de rebus id confessionem non pertinentibus in confessione loquantur: extra confessionem vero, si oportebit eas alloqui, longum sermonem ne misceant, & oculos modeste demissos habeant.
units.tr: 17. Those who confess more often, especially women, let them dispatch briefly, and let them not speak in confession of matters that do not pertain to confession. Outside of confession, if they must speak with them, let them not engage in a long conversation, and let them keep their eyes modestly lowered.

units.la: 18. Quando quis a Superiore mittetur ad confessiones foeminarum audiendas, vel alia de causa eas adierit, locus, quem Superior ipsi designabit, quamdiu cum foeminis Sacerdos loquetur, eo in loco erit; unde videre eos, sed non, quae secreta esse oportet, audire possit, quantum loci dispositio patietur: quod si non pateretur, curet omnino Sacerdos, ne ostium sit clausum, neclocus obscurus.
units.tr: 18. When anyone is sent by the Superior to hear the confessions of women, or has gone to them for some other reason, the place which the Superior assigns to him shall be the place where the priest speaks with the women for as long as he speaks with them. From there he may be able to see them, but not hear what ought to be secret, so far as the arrangement of the place allows. But if the arrangement did not allow this, let the priest take care above all that the door is not shut and the place is not dark.

units.la: 19. Particularium personarum, praesertim foeminarum, curam nemo suscipiat: & quam vis Confessarius pro suo munere in vita spirituali poenitentem instituat, nullius tamen obedientiam admittat.
units.tr: 19. Let no one take on the care of particular persons, especially women. And although the confessor, in discharge of his office, guides the penitent in the spiritual life, let him nevertheless admit no one's obedience.

units.la: 20. Si quis uni confiteri solitus, ab eodem alium Confessarium adeundi facultatem petierit, vel ea non petita adierit, id sibi gratum esse Confessarius benigne ostendat.
units.tr: 20. If anyone who is accustomed to confess to one man asks leave to go to another confessor, or goes without asking, let the confessor kindly show that he is pleased by this.

units.la: 21. Ut sanitatis etiam ratio ad Dei gloriam habeatur, confessiones, mane ad horam usque prandij tantum audiant: ita, ut cum signum primae mensae audietur, studeant se ita accommodare, ut ad secundum accedant: nisi forte poenitentium necessitas aliud exigat.
units.tr: 21. So that account may be taken of health too, for the glory of God, let them hear confessions in the morning only, up to the hour of lunch. When the signal for the first meal is sounded, let them endeavour to adapt themselves so as to come to the second, unless perhaps the need of the penitents requires otherwise.

units.la: 22. Nemini aut petere, aut accipere quidquam licet, sive ab ijs, quorum confessiones audiverit, sive ab alijs, quod vel in pauperes distribuat, vel alteri [?] factionis nomine restituat: nisi Superior, cum opus esset, secus faciendum iudicaret.
units.tr: 22. It is not lawful for anyone to ask for or accept anything, either from those whose confessions he has heard or from others, to distribute to the poor or to restore to another on behalf of the faction, unless the Superior, when there is need, judges that it should be done otherwise.

units.la: 23. Etsi vota ad perfectionis statum pertinentia, ut sancta laudari debent, & circa ea Confessarij consilium; sed magna cum consideratione, dare possint: quia tamen non humanam, sed divinam vocationem requirunt; nemo ad ea emittenda quemquam inducat: verum ad orationem tales hortetur, ut à Deo adjuti, vocationem suam melius intelligant, & exequantur.
units.tr: 23. Although vows pertaining to the state of perfection ought to be praised as holy, and confessors may give counsel about them, but with great deliberation, nevertheless, since they require not a human but a divine calling, no one should induce anyone to take them. Rather, let him exhort such people to prayer, so that, helped by God, they may better understand and carry out their vocation.

units.la: 24. Si quos viderint ad Religionem propensos, no facile ad unam potius, quàm ad alia, ad hoc, quàm ad illud Monasterium invitent: sed liberam illis suam electionem relinquant: poterunt tamen petentibus consilium eas Religiones, vel Monasteria proponere, quæ illis magis commoda in Domino judicaverint.
units.tr: 24. If they see some who are inclined to religious life, let them not readily invite them to one order rather than another, or to this monastery rather than that one. Rather let them leave the choice free to them. Nevertheless, they may propose to those who ask for counsel those religious orders or monasteries which they have judged more suitable for them in the Lord.

units.la: 25. Nullius eius, quorum audit confessiones, certum vestimenti genus, hunc aut illum habitum, vel colorem præscribat: tametsi omnes ad honestum, & suo statui convenientem vestitum hortari possint.
units.tr: 25. Let no one prescribe for any of those whose confessions he hears a particular kind of dress, this or that habit, or colour. Still, all may be urged to dress decently and suitably to their station.

units.la: 26. Ut pium est, ad frequenter communicandum fideles exhortari: ita quos ad id propensos viderint, admonere debent, ne crebrius, quam octavo quoque die accedant, præsertim si matrimonio sint conjuncti.
units.tr: 26. As it is good to exhort the faithful to communicate frequently, so those whom they see inclined to this should be warned not to come more often than every eighth day, especially if they are married.

units.la: 27. Admoneat eos, qui sibi confitentur, à Dominica Palmarum ad Dominicam in Albis inclusivè, eo tempore (nisi aliud consuetudo loci postulaverit) debere semel in sua Parochia communicare, exceptis Peregrinis, & ijs, qui facultatem haberent, & reliquis, quos jus excipit.
units.tr: 27. Let them admonish those who confess to them that from Palm Sunday to Low Sunday inclusive, during that time (unless the custom of the place requires otherwise), they ought to communicate once in their own parish, except for strangers, those who have a faculty to do otherwise, and the others whom the law excepts.

units.la: 28. Qui vocantur ad juvandos eos, qui morti vicini sunt, ea in promptu habeant, quæ eo tempore, in quo tantum est momenti, si fieri possint, tamdiuque illis adsit, quamdiu sola necessitas postulabit. Caeterum etsi cum opus est, ægrotos ad condenda testamenta hortari conveniat, ijs tamen conficiendis non assistant.
units.tr: 28. Those who are called to help those who are near death should have ready the things which are needed at a time of such great importance. If possible, they should stay with the sick for as long as necessity alone requires. Moreover, although when need arises it is fitting to urge the sick to make their wills, they should not assist in drawing them up.

units.la: REGVLÆ CONCIONATORVM.
units.tr: THE RULES FOR PREACHERS.

units.la: Regulæ, quæ Sacerdotibus propositæ sunt, eas sibi Concionatores inprimis commendatas existiment, nec minore cura, quàm ceteri observent.
units.tr: Let the preachers regard the rules set before the priests as especially commended to themselves, and observe them with no less care than the others.

units.la: 2. Memores sint, vocatos se esse ad reducendas animas suo creatori: quod cum sit opus omnium difficillimum, summo studio media illa adhibeant, quæ instrumentum cum Deo conjungunt: eiusmodi sunt solidæ virtutes, ac præcipuè charitas, pura intentio divini servitij, familiaritas cum Deo in spiritualibus devotionis exercitijs, & zelus syncerus animarum ad gloriam divinæ majestatis.
