units.tr: 2. Let them remember that they have been called to bring souls back to their Creator. Since this is the most difficult work of all, let them with the greatest zeal use those means which join the instrument to God: these are solid virtues, and above all charity, pure intention in the divine service, familiarity with God in the spiritual exercises of devotion, and sincere zeal for souls to the glory of the divine majesty.

units.la: 3. Enitantur cum Dei gratia esse cæteris exemplo: ut non minus vita, quàm doctrina ad omnem virtutem proximos alliciant.
units.tr: 3. Let them strive, with the grace of God, to be an example to others, so that they draw their neighbours to every virtue no less by their life than by their teaching.

units.la: 4. Lectioni S. Scripturæ, ac Patrum præcipuè incumbant: conferet etiam peculiari studio vidisse Evangelia toto anno currentia, & in eis ea, quæ usui esse possunt, adnotasse itemque compendium fecisse explicationis rerum ad fidem, & Christianam vitam necessariarum, atque in communes locos redegisse omnia, quæ ad virtutum commendationem, & peccatorum destinationem pertinent.
units.tr: 4. Let them devote themselves especially to the reading of Holy Scripture and of the Fathers. It will also help to have studied the Gospels read through the whole year with particular care, to have noted in them what may be of use, to have made a summary of the explanation of the things necessary for faith and Christian life, and to have arranged under common headings all that pertains to commending virtues and condemning sins.

units.la: 5. Conferet vidisse præceptiones, si quas de modo concionandi illi tradunt, qui bene hoc munus obierunt: bonos audivisse Prædicatores, & in concionibus Domi, vel in alijs locis minus frequentibus se exercuisse.
units.tr: 5. It will help to have seen the precepts, if any, which those who have discharged this office well hand down about the manner of preaching; to have heard good preachers; and to have practised preaching at home or in other less frequented places.

units.la: 6. Optare debent, ut admoneantur, si quid in concione corrigendum videbitur ijs, qui Superiore ad id deputati fuerint, & humili, & grato animo id accipere.
units.tr: 6. They ought to wish to be admonished, if anything in a sermon seems to need correcting, by those who have been appointed by the superior for this purpose, and to receive it with a humble and grateful mind.

units.la: 7. Ita operam suam in celebrioribus concionibus libenter impendant, ut non minus se in docendos pueros, & alios rudes instruendos, faciles, & paratos exhibeant.
units.tr: 7. Let them willingly devote their labour to the more celebrated sermons, yet show themselves no less ready and prepared to instruct boys and other ignorant persons.

units.la: 8. Si quando occasio tulerit, ut alios eodem tempore concionari velit, quantum in ipsis erit, libenter cedant.
units.tr: 8. If at any time an occasion arises in which he wishes others to preach at the same time, let them, as far as lies in them, willingly give way.

units.la: 9. Ea populo proponant, quae ad captum, & utilitatem auditorum erunt accommodata, ijsq; insistant, quae ad Christi institutionem, atq; ad extirpanda vitia, & virtutes inferendas valent, & a rerum subtilium curiosa tractatione se abstineant.
units.tr: 9. Let them set before the people things adapted to the understanding and profit of the hearers, and let them keep to those things which serve Christ's teaching, the uprooting of vices and the instilling of virtues, and abstain from a curious treatment of subtle matters.

units.la: 10. Commendare debent Confessionis, & Eucharistiae frequentem usum, in bonis operibus profectum, & perseverantiam, Ecclesiasticarum caerimoniarum observationem, & caeremoniarum, quae ad cultum divinum pertinent, eamque obedientiam, quae Principibus & Praelatis, qui Dei in terris vices gerunt, exhibenda est.
units.tr: 10. They ought to commend frequent use of confession and the Eucharist, progress and perseverance in good works, observance of ecclesiastical ceremonies and of those ceremonies which pertain to divine worship, and that obedience which is due to princes and prelates, who bear God's place on earth.

units.la: 11. Commendabunt etiam peculiari ratione poenitentiae, & misericordiae opera, sanctarum precum, & aliarum piarum devotionum exercitia, utilium librorum lectionem, & bonam filiorum educationem.
units.tr: 11. They shall also commend, in a particular manner, repentance, works of mercy, the practice of holy prayers and other pious devotions, the reading of useful books, and the good upbringing of children.

units.la: 12. Cum experientia doceat, & sanctae memoriae Pater Ignatius scriptum reliquerit, nihil utilitatis percipi ex iis concionibus, in quibus Principes, & Magistratus Resp. Praelati, & alij Ecclesiastici in particulari reprehenduntur; Concionatores nostri ab hujusmodi reprehensionibus abstineant.
units.tr: 12. Since experience teaches, and Father Ignatius of holy memory has left it in writing, that no profit is gained from those sermons in which princes and magistrates, prelates and other churchmen are rebuked individually, let our preachers abstain from such rebukes.

units.la: 13. Caveant, ne religiosos aliorum ordinum, quos revereri, & observare debent, etiam acriter videantur reprehendere: & quamvis nostros ad maiora in virtute progressus excitare possint, praesertim in domesticis exhortationibus: reprehensionem tamen alicujus particularis, vel ipsius Societatis ne attingant.
units.tr: 13. Let them take care not to appear to rebuke sharply members of other religious orders, whom they ought to revere and respect. And although they can stir our men to greater progress in virtue, especially in domestic exhortations, let them not touch upon the rebuke of any particular person, or of the Society itself.

units.la: 14. Ne rumoribus populi moveantur, ut nova, & parum confirmata in publicum afferant: & multo minus ea populo proponant, quae alioqui dubia, & incerta sunt.
units.tr: 14. Let them not be moved by the rumours of the people to bring new and little-confirmed things before the public; and much less let them set before the people things which are otherwise doubtful and uncertain.

units.la: 15. Curent, ut rationem, & modum, quem observare debent in rebus populo denuntiandis, & certis pauperibus aliisque piis operibus commendandis, a Superiore accipiant.
units.tr: 15. Let them receive from the superior the principle and manner which they ought to observe in announcing matters to the people and in commending certain poor persons and other pious works.

units.la: 16. Caveant omnino, ne facetijs, aut inutilium rerum narratione cocionem contemptibilem faciant, ijsve auditores ad risum moveant, vel contra, ut ad fletum excitent, speciem aliquam populo proponant, a communi in Societate concionandi consuetudine alienam; nisi in aliquo particulari casu ad communem aedificationem pertinere Superior, pro ratione loci, judicaret.
units.tr: 16. Let them by all means take care not to make the sermon contemptible by jokes or the telling of useless things, nor to move the hearers to laughter or, conversely, to stir them to tears, nor to set before the people any show foreign to the common custom of preaching in the Society; unless the superior, according to the circumstances of the place, judges that something in a particular case pertains to the common edification.

units.la: 17. Ea quae dicturi sunt, diligenti praemeditatione, & peculiari ad Deum recursu (quatenus per tempus licebit) paranda erunt.
units.tr: 17. What they are going to say must be prepared with diligent forethought and special recourse to God (as far as time allows).

units.la: 18. Caveant arrogantiam, & ostentationem in concione, humilitatemque, cui ex intimo cordis affectu studere debent, in omni actione prae se ferant: quod si aliquid prose, aut Societate cogantur respondere, ea modestia satisfaciant, ut tanquam Christi, non suam agere videantur.
units.tr: 18. Let them beware of arrogance and ostentation in preaching, and let them show in every action the humility which they ought to pursue from the depths of the heart. If they are compelled to answer anything before the public or on behalf of the Society, let them satisfy with such modesty that they seem to act not as their own but as Christ's.

units.la: 19. Modus concionandi, qui a Scholastico diversus esse debet, ita sit ad docendum comparatus, ut ad animorum motum praecipue dirigatur: cumq; quaestio aliqua earum, quae ad fidem, aut mores pertinet, modo aliquo tractanda erit, non ita exacte proponantur argumenta, quibus contraria pars confirmatur (nisi auditorium id postulet) ut simpliciores ipso pronendi modo offendi possint: sed eo pacto res exponatur, ut illi ex data explicatione solutionem eorum, quae sibi in mentem venerint, aut ab aliis audiverint, facile colligant.
units.tr: 19. The manner of preaching, which ought to differ from that of the schoolmen, should be so arranged for teaching that it is chiefly directed to moving the feelings. When some question of those which pertain to faith or morals has to be treated, the arguments by which the opposing side is confirmed should not be set out so exactly (unless the audience requires it), lest the simpler folk be offended by the very manner of presentation; rather, the matter should be so expounded that they may readily gather from the explanation given the solution of the objections which have come into their minds or which they have heard from others.

units.la: 20. Nefint affectati, aut verborum lenocinia sectentur, nec studio politioris sermonis libros habeant familiares, ex quorum lectione detrimentum in spiritu accipiant, & seculare aliquid redoleant.
units.tr: 20. Let them not be affected, nor pursue verbal allurements; nor, through a zeal for more polished speech, keep books at hand from whose reading they take harm to the spirit and acquire a worldly flavour.

units.la: 21. In laudibus, & reprehensionibus a nimijs exaggerationibus: & ab omni specie adulationis abstineant.
units.tr: 21. In praises and rebukes, let them abstain from excessive exaggerations and from every appearance of flattery.

units.la: 22. Gestus corporis sit modestus, & in quo gravitas quaedam religiosa praecipue eluceat: vocemq; accommodent ad res quas tractabunt: proinde eam, ubi non est opus, ne praeter modum extollant, aut deprimant.
units.tr: 22. Bodily gesture should be modest, and in it a certain religious gravity should especially shine forth. Let them adapt the voice to the matters they will treat, and where there is no need, not raise or lower it beyond measure.

units.la: 23. In concionibus, & lectionibus templi, spatium horae ne excedant.
units.tr: 23. In sermons and lectures in the church, let them not exceed the space of an hour.

units.la: REGVLAE EORVM, QVI IN MISSIONI- BVS VERSANTVR.
units.tr: RULES FOR THOSE WHO ARE ENGAGED IN MISSIONS.

units.la: 1. Cum scopus, ad quem tendit Societas, sit, varias mundi partes, ex obedientia Summi Pontificis, vel Superioris Societatis peragrando verbum Dei praedicare, consessiones audire, & reliquis quibuscunq; poterit medijs uti ad animas, divina aspirante gratia, juvandas: quicunq; in hujusmodi missionibus versantur, sibi persuadeant, rem maximi ponderis in Societate sibi commissam esse, atque ita se comparare studeant, ut apta Dei instrumenta ad rem tantam esse possint.
units.tr: 1. Since the aim toward which the Society strives is to preach the word of God, hear confessions and use all other means that may be available for helping souls, by travelling through various parts of the world at the command of the Supreme Pontiff or of the Superior of the Society, and with divine grace breathed into the work, those who are employed in such missions should be persuaded that the matter entrusted to them by the Society is of the greatest weight. They should therefore strive to prepare themselves so that they may be fit instruments of God for so great a task.

units.la: 2. Quia vocationis nostrae est, vitam agere in quavis mundi plaga, ubi majus Dei obsequium, & animarum auxilium speratur: unusquisque paratus esse debet, ut in ea vineae Christi parte, atque operae se exerceat, quod ipsi commissum fuerit, sive per varia loca discurrendo, sive in quibusdam continenter residendo.
units.tr: 2. It is our vocation to live in any part of the world where greater service to God and help for souls may be hoped for. Each one ought to be ready to labour in whatever part of Christ's vineyard and in whatever work has been committed to him, whether by moving from place to place or by remaining continuously in certain places.

units.la: 3. Unusquisque plenam in his, ac liberam sui dispositionem Superiori, qui eum Christi loco dirigit, relinquat: poterit tamen motus animi, aut cogitationes, quae in contrarium occurrunt, illi proponere, subijciendo suum sentire, & velle ei, quod ipse in Domino judicaverit.
units.tr: 3. Each one should leave his whole and free disposition in these matters to the Superior, who directs him in Christ's place. Nevertheless, he may set before the Superior any movements of mind or thoughts that arise to the contrary, submitting his own opinion and will to what the Superior has judged in the Lord.

units.la: 4. Ei, qui mittendus erit, plurimum conveniet, ut intelligat a Superioribus scopum suae missionis, & effectum, cuius gratia mittitur: id quod in scriptis, si fieri potest, habere curabit.
units.tr: 4. It will be most suitable for the one who is to be sent to understand from his Superiors the aim of his mission and the result for which he is sent. He should take care to have this in writing, if it can be done.

units.la: 5. Cum oppidatim missi fuerint ad fructificandum in agro Domini, dabunt operam, quoad fieri poterit, ut more pauperum Evangelium praedicent: proinde & pedites, vel in toto, vel in parte iter facient, si eos Superior id praestare posse judicaverit, & ex eleemosynis, vel oblatis, cum aedificatione emendicatis vivent: nisi alia ipsis a Superiore sustentationis ratio sit constituta.
units.tr: 5. When they have been sent into towns to bear fruit in the Lord's field, they will take pains, as far as possible, to preach the Gospel in the manner of the poor. Accordingly, they shall also make their journeys on foot, either wholly or in part, if the Superior judges that he can allow this, and they shall live by alms or offerings, begged in a way that edifies, unless the Superior has established some other means of support for them.

units.la: 6. Si nullum eis a Superiore designatum fuerit hospitium, intelligant sibi ad aliquod hospitale, tanquam ad hospitium pauperum esse divertendum: si tamen honestum id sit, atque ad exercenda ex eo ministeria Societatis accommodatum: alioqui convenientius erit, ut in domum pij alicujus, & exemplaris Ecclesiastici, aliumve eiusmodi locum se recipiant, in quo cum aedificatione manere possint.
units.tr: 6. If no lodging has been assigned to them by the Superior, they should understand that they are to lodge at some hospice, as at a hostel for the poor, provided this is respectable and suited to carrying out the Society's ministries from there. Otherwise it will be more fitting for them to withdraw into the house of some pious man of exemplary ecclesiastical life, or into some other such place, where they can stay with edification.

units.la: 7. Cum ingressi fuerint loca ea, in quibus ordinarij residen t, eos quam primum adeant, suamq; operam illis submisse offerat, & facultatem ad exercenda Societatis ministeria modeste, ac religiose petant, eosq; omnes tum Ecclesiasticos, praecipue Parochos, quam saeculares, quorum auctoritate, aut favore opus habent, benevolos sibi facere studeant.
units.tr: 7. When they have entered the places where the ordinaries reside, they should go to them as soon as possible, offer their services humbly, and modestly and devoutly ask for permission to exercise the Society's ministries. They should also strive to win the goodwill of all of them, both ecclesiastics, especially parish priests, and laymen, whose authority or favour they need.

units.la: 8. Cum eo pervenerint, ubi diutius immorari debent, prudenter, ac mature operam dabunt, ut notitiam habeant probatorum virorum, & pietate, ac rebus agendis insigniorum, quorum informatione, vel auxilio juvari possint ad ministeria Societatis majore cum fructu in animarum exercenda.
units.tr: 8. When they have arrived at a place where they ought to stay for some time, they will act prudently and promptly to become acquainted with men of proven virtue, distinguished for piety and for their activity, through whose information or help they may be assisted in exercising the Society's ministries to greater fruit for souls.

units.la: 9. Qui in missione Superior erit, initio suscipiendorum operum, vel quando major subsidij necessitas cernitur, (quod res magni momenti sint, vel difficultates graves incidant) applicabit, curabitque applicari Missas & Orationes, ut omnia cedant ad majorem Dei gloriam & proximorum utilitatem.
units.tr: 9. The Superior in a mission, at the beginning of the works to be undertaken, or whenever a greater need for help is evident (because the matters are of great importance or serious difficulties have arisen), shall apply, and shall see that Masses and prayers are applied, so that everything may turn out to the greater glory of God and the benefit of neighbours.

units.la: 10. Si ijs, qui mittuntur non fuerit injunctum, ut medio aliquo utantur limitato, quale esset, vel legere, vel praedicare, &c. in ijs tantum se exercebunt, quibus Societas uti solet, juxta Constitutiones: conferre tamen illa cum eo Superiore, qui eis propior fuerit, semper erit securius.
units.tr: 10. If those who are sent have not been enjoined to use some limited means, such as reading or preaching, etc., they will employ themselves only in those things which the Society customarily uses, according to the Constitutions. It will always be safer, however, to confer these matters with the Superior who is nearest to them.

units.la: 11. Media spiritualia, quibus juxta institutum Societatis, & beneplacitum Superiorum uti poterunt, fere sunt ministerium verbi Dei in praedicationibus, sacris lectionibus privatisve exhortationibus, & colloquijs, Sacramentorum confessionis, & Eucharistiae administratio, Exercitiorum spiritualium traditio, dissidentium reconciliatio, casuum conscientiae ad Ecclesiasticos, eorumq; officij magis privata explicatio, & Christianae doctrinae adpueros, ac alios rudes publica declaratio.
units.tr: 11. The spiritual means which, in accordance with the Society's institute and the good pleasure of the Superiors, they may use are chiefly: the ministry of the word of God in sermons, sacred lectures or private exhortations, and conversations; the administration of the sacraments of confession and the Eucharist; the giving of the spiritual exercises; the reconciliation of those at variance; the referral of cases of conscience to ecclesiastics, and the more private explanation of their duties; and the public declaration of Christian doctrine to children and other ignorant persons.

units.la: 12. Corporalibus etiam pietatis operib. quantum spiritualia permittent, & vires patientur, incubere poterunt, ut infirmos, praecipue in Xenodochijs, per se, vel per alios juvando, & pauperes, ac in custodijs detentos, quatenus licebit, eodem modo sublevando.
units.tr: 12. They may also apply themselves to the corporal works of piety, as far as spiritual duties allow and their strength permits: helping the sick, especially in hospitals, either personally or through others, and likewise relieving the poor and those held in prisons, as far as it is permitted.

units.la: 13. Etsi certus ordo in nostris ministerijs exercendis praescribi non potest: plerumque tamen utilius erit, & securius ab humilioribus inchoare, ut a doctrina Christiana pueris explicanda, ab aegrotis hospitalium invisendis, eorumque & aliorum magis indigentium confessionibus audiendis.
units.tr: 13. Although a fixed order cannot be prescribed for carrying out our ministries, it will usually be more useful and safer to begin with the humbler tasks, such as teaching children Christian doctrine, visiting the sick in hospitals, and hearing the confessions of these and of others who are in greater need.

units.la: 14. Quamquam humana media non solum spernenda non sunt, sed etiam cum opus est, prudenter, & religiose adhibenda, divinis tamen, & nostri instituti magis proprijs praecipue utendum est, in eisq; magis fidendum: orandusq; Deus, ut ijs omnibus det eam efficaciam, quae sit propositio fini consequendo necessaria.
units.tr: 14. Although human means are not only not to be despised but are also to be employed prudently and devoutly when necessary, we must nevertheless make use chiefly of divine means, and those more proper to our institute, and place our greatest trust in them; and God must be prayed to give all these means that efficacy which is necessary for attaining the proposed end.

units.la: 15. Juxta eam Charitatis regulam, quas e Apostolus omnia omnibus faciebat, ut omnes lucri faceret, expediet nonnunquam, ut ingenio eorum, cum quibus agent, initio se attemperent (quatenus ratio & virtus ferent) ita tamen, ut meminerint ad id tande eos cum Dei gratia perducere, quod illis in Domino magis conferre judicabunt.
units.tr: 15. In accordance with that rule of charity by which the Apostle became all things to all, that he might gain all, it will sometimes be expedient at first to accommodate oneself to the disposition of those with whom one deals (so far as reason and virtue allow), yet in such a way that they remember to lead them, with the grace of God, at last to that which they judge to be more profitable for them in the Lord.

units.la: 16. Eam animi magnitudinem, & aequabilitatem retinere studeant, ut & prosperis successibus, & adversis superiores sint: quo nullo eventa fracti, nec religiosae modestiae nec sanctae libertatis, nec bonae de se conceptae existimationis, quae ad fructum colligendum necessaria est, quicquam amittant.
units.tr: 16. They should strive to keep such greatness and evenness of mind that they are superior both to prosperous and to adverse outcomes, so that, broken by no event, they may lose nothing of religious modesty, holy freedom, or the good opinion of themselves that is necessary for gathering fruit.

units.la: 17. Si quos erga se, aut Societatem male affectos esse intellexerint (praesertim non vulgaris auctoritatis homines) aut qui nostra ministeria impediant, non solum pro eis orabunt, sed etiam convenientem aliquam rationem inibunt, ut eos amicos aut saltem non adversarios faciant. Ad quam rem non parum conferet, si data occasione, instituti nostri rationem illis exponant, nullumq; officij genus praetermittant, quo illos cum opportunum fuerit, syncere, ac religiose demereri, & conciliare possint.
units.tr: 17. If they understand that some people are ill disposed towards them or towards the Society (especially men of no common authority), or who hinder our ministries, they shall not only pray for them but also adopt some suitable plan to make them friends, or at least not adversaries. To this end it will contribute not a little if, when the occasion arises, they explain the purpose of our institute to such men, and omit no kind of duty by which they may, when it is opportune, sincerely and devoutly win their favour and conciliate them.

units.la: 18. Si quando Praelatum aliquem in visitanda dicecesi comitabuntur, nihil se in negotijs ad visitationem spectantibus, aliisve id genus ad jurisdictionem pertinentibus immiscean t, sed ijs tantum ministerijs attendant, quae sunt nostri instituti propria.
units.tr: 18. If at any time they accompany some prelate in visiting a diocese, they shall not meddle in any affairs pertaining to the visitation or other matters of that kind belonging to jurisdiction, but shall attend only to those ministries which are proper to our institute.

units.la: 19. Quamvis optare debeant, ut in sua quisque vocatione proficiat, aequumq; est, ut pro suo munere ad eam rem omnes hortentur: nullam tamen reformandi Cleri, aut Monialium, aliorumve Religiosorum curae partem admittant: sic enim fiet, ut & munus suum sine impedimento exequi: & populum ad uberiorem fructum ex visitatione percipiendum sine offensione disponere possint.
units.tr: 19. Although they ought to wish that each person may advance in his own vocation, and it is fitting that all should encourage this according to their office, they shall nevertheless admit no part in the reform of the clergy, of nuns, or of other religious. For in this way it will come about that they can perform their own duty without hindrance, and dispose the people, without offence, to receive a richer fruit from the visitation.

units.la: 20. Cum praeter id, quod eis fuerit peculiari ratione injunctum, res aliqua divini servitij se obtulerit, in qua possint sine detrimento suae missionis suam operam ponere, opportunitatem, quam Deus ad eam dederit, quantum in eodem convenire judicabunt, e manibus elabi non sinent.
units.tr: 20. Whenever, apart from what has been enjoined on them in a particular way, some opportunity for divine service presents itself in which they can apply their labour without detriment to their mission, they shall not allow the opportunity that God has given for it to slip from their hands, so far as they judge it fitting in that place.

units.la: 21. Si in locis designatis diutius residendum erit, locumq; de derint praecipua negotia (quae nunquam propter alias occasiones, licet bonas, divini obsequij posthabebunt) excursiones aliquas facere, si eas cum fructu fore judicabunt, non erit inconveniens.
units.tr: 21. If they must remain for a longer time in the appointed places, and the chief business is lacking there (which they shall never postpone to other occasions, however good, of divine service), it will not be inappropriate to make some excursions, if they judge that these will be fruitful.

units.la: 22. Sine facultate Superioris nulli Confraternitati, Congregationi ve statuta condent, seu vetus illa fit, seu nova instituenda videatur. De nova autem instituenda, & quae nullifit in usu, non prius agent, quam Superiorem consulant.
units.tr: 22. Without the permission of the Superior they shall not draw up statutes for any confraternity or congregation, whether an old one exists or a new one seems to be needed. Concerning a new one to be founded, and one that is not yet in use, they shall not act before consulting the Superior.

units.la: 23. Quae Deo auctore perficient, ea quantum licebit, ita constituant, ut stabilia sint, & diu durare possint. Quod facilius obtinebunt, si res convenienti ordine disponant, earumq; bonum progressum ijs commendent, quorum exemplo, auctoritate, studio, & diligentia, facile conservari, & promoveri possint.
units.tr: 23. As far as possible, they shall so arrange whatever they accomplish with God's help that it may be stable and able to last a long time. They will obtain this more easily if they set matters in a suitable order and commend their good progress to those by whose example, authority, zeal and diligence they can easily be preserved and advanced.

units.la: 14. Scribent ad eum, quem designaverit ille, à quo missi sunt, singulis hebdomadis, vel quoties ipsis fuerit constitutum, & quantum fieri poterit, totius successus eum certiorem reddant, quemadmodum personae, & negotia exegerint, ut consilio, & aliis auxilijs juvari possint.
units.tr: 14. They shall write to the one whom he who sent them has appointed, every week, or as often as shall have been prescribed for them, and, as far as it can be done, they shall keep him fully informed of the whole outcome, as the persons and the business require, so that they may be aided by his counsel and other help.

units.la: 25. Cum propter nullas occupationes intermittendum sit propriae perfectionis studium, diligenter animadvertant, ne praetextu procurandae aliorum salutis, propriae perfectionis oblivisc antur, ipsamq; propriam salutem ea ratione in discrimen adducant: sed saepe illud Domini mente revolvant: Quid prodest homini, si universum mundum lucretur, animae verò suae detrimentum patiatur? sibique illud D. Pauli unusquisque dictum existimet, Attende tibi, & doctrinae, insta in illis, hoc enim faciens, & teipsum salvum facies, & eos qui te audiunt.
units.tr: 25. Since the pursuit of their own perfection must not be interrupted on account of any occupations, let them take careful heed that, under the pretext of promoting the salvation of others, they do not forget their own perfection and thereby put their own salvation in peril. Rather, let them often turn over in their mind that saying of the Lord: "What does it profit a man if he gains the whole world but suffers the loss of his soul?" And let each one take to himself that saying of St. Paul: "Take heed to yourself and to the teaching; persist in these things, for in doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you."

units.la: 26. Hanc ob rem caveant, ne consueta in Collegijs, ac Domibus orandi, & examinanda conscientia exercitia imminutant, nisi si quando necessitas, aut in eventu aliquo charitas illud faciendum postularet. Conversationem cum saecularibus nimiam non habeant, aut incautam, aut quae saecularem sapiat: sed in omnibus se integritatis, & gravitatis exemplum praebeant: atque in summa Regularum Societatis, sive earum, quae omnibus communes sunt, sive quae ipsorum officij propria, quantum locus patitur, observationem non praetermittant.
units.tr: 26. For this reason let them take care not to diminish the customary exercises of prayer and examination of conscience in the colleges and houses, unless necessity or some act of charity in a particular case should require it. Let them not have too much, or incautious, or worldly-minded, dealings with secular people; rather, in all things let them show an example of integrity and gravity; and, in sum, let them not neglect the observance of the Rules of the Society, whether those common to all or those proper to their own office, as far as the place allows.

units.la: 27. Praeter haec, si pro ratione diversarum regionum, & missionum qualitate, alia quaedam à Superioribus constituenda videbuntur: ea in peculiaribus instructionibus addita, pari diligentia observanda erunt.
units.tr: 27. Besides these, if, in view of the circumstances of the various regions and the nature of the missions, some other matters seem to the Superiors to need to be laid down, these, added in the special instructions, shall be observed with equal diligence.

units.la: REGVLÆ PROCVRATORIS GENERALIS
units.tr: REGULATIONS OF THE PROCURATOR GENERAL

units.la: 1. IN omnium negotiorum tractatione perpetuo memor sit instituti Societatis, quae Dei omnipotentis gloriam quaerens, profectui animarum invigilat. Ipse igitur verbo, & exemplo eos omnes aedificet, quibuscum versatur, & in his, quae ad officium suum spectant, fidelitatem, prudentiam, & dexteritatem habere studeat, atque eos sibi benevolos conservet, quorum opera ad negotia peragenda indiget.
units.tr: 1. In the conduct of all business he shall always keep in mind the purpose of the Society, which, seeking the glory of almighty God, watches over the progress of souls. Let him therefore edify all those with whom he deals by word and example, and in matters that concern his office let him strive to show fidelity, prudence and skill, and keep well disposed towards those whose help he needs to carry out his business.

units.la: 2. Ad eum pertinent negotia omnia ad expeditiones, lites, & quosvis contractus, sibi a Generali commissos ineundos spectantia, quae ad universa Societatis Collegia vel Domos eius, vel etiam ad particulares personas pertinebunt.
units.tr: 2. His responsibility covers all business concerning expeditions, lawsuits and any contracts that the General has committed to him to enter into, whether these affect the whole Society's colleges or houses, or private individuals.

units.la: 3. Superintendat non solum iis, quae a Procuratore, & Solicitatore externo curantur, sed etiam Socijs, qui illi dabuntur adjutores, quod ad negotia attinet: & si qui Romae fuerint Procuratores Societatis rerum particularium, vel etiam Provinciarum, ab ipso dirigentur, prout Generali videbitur.
units.tr: 3. He shall oversee not only what is handled by the Procurator and external solicitor, but also the Fellows who are assigned to them as assistants in business matters. If there are Procurators of the Society in Rome for particular affairs or for provinces, he shall direct them as the General sees fit.

units.la: 4. Nihil, quod ad expeditiones, lites, aut graviora negotia pertineat, incipiet agere, nisi a Praeposito Generali, per se, vel per alium approbatum sit, & ei commissum, ut exequatur. Quod si Generalis rem consultatione indigere judicabit, solicitet ut maturè de ea statuatur, praecipuè si res festinatione egere videatur: si quid autem ex ijs, quae statuuntur, ipsi videretur non convenire, proponat suam sententiam, & rationes quibus movetur.
units.tr: 4. He shall undertake nothing relating to expeditions, lawsuits or more serious business unless it has first been approved by the Superior General, either by himself or through another, and he has been commissioned to carry it out. If the General judges that a matter needs deliberation, he shall press for a prompt decision, especially if the matter seems to require haste. If anything decided seems to him unsuitable, he shall set out his own opinion and the reasons that move him.

units.la: 5. Illud verò praecipuè ante oculos habeat, ut antequam litem ullam intendat, res controversa (si fieri possit) concordia aut compromissione componatur: si quando tamen ad litem descendendum erit, memor sit ut magnam pacem interius exteriusque custodiat, & semper ad istam concordiam se paratum esse, contrariae parti innotescat.
units.tr: 5. Above all he should keep before his eyes that, before bringing any lawsuit, a disputed matter should be settled, if possible, by agreement or arbitration. If he must nevertheless go to law, let him remember to maintain great peace within and without, and make it known to the opposing party that he is always ready for such an agreement.

units.la: 6. Curet diligenter, ut recte, & solide fiant, quae expedienda, vel alia ratione agenda erunt. quod si periti juris, aut curiales consulendi sint, maximè idonei eligantur: idem de officialibus, per quos res est transigenda, intelligatur.
units.tr: 6. He shall take care that what must be done by way of expedition or otherwise is done correctly and soundly. If legal experts or court officials are to be consulted, the most suitable ones should be chosen; the same applies to the officials through whom the business is to be transacted.

units.la: 7. Conferat eum Praeposito Generali, eique reddat rationem eorum, quae facit, & quo in statu instata sint negotia, aut illi, qui à Præposito designabitur: quòd si rerum difficultas extraordinarium favorem, aut diligentiam exigere videatur, eidem significet, & auxilia, quæ opportuna visa erunt, petat.
units.tr: 7. He shall confer with the Superior General and give an account of what he is doing and of the state in which the business stands, or else with the one whom the Superior General designates. If the difficulty of the affairs seems to require extraordinary favour or diligence, he shall report this to him and ask for such help as seems appropriate.

units.la: 8. Rationem quoque reddet status negotiorum, eorumque persecutionis, vel expeditionis, ijs qui de negotijs scribunt, suas verò literas legendas dabit illi Assistenti, ad cuius Provinciam negotia pertinebunt.
units.tr: 8. He shall also give an account of the state of the business, and of its pursuit or despatch, to those who write about business matters; but he shall give his own letters to be read by the Assistant to whose province the business belongs.

units.la: 9. Rationum libros conficiat, in quibus sigillatim omnia quæ recepit, scribantur, & quas pecunias quibus in rebus expenderit, ut tam clara & distincta ratio dati & accepti sit; ut ipso etiam absente supputari possit, quid singulæ Provinciæ, Domus, Collegium, aut particulares personæ dederint, aut debeant Procuratori, aut quid eis à Procuratore debeatur. Quod ut commodius observetur, singulis saltem annis ad Nativitatis Dominicæ festum rationum omnium summam colliger, & scribet, atque ad eos, quorum intererit, mittet: si quid autem pecuniæ superexit, eisdem significabit, ut pro ipsorum arbitrio de ea disponatur.
units.tr: 9. He shall keep account books in which everything he receives is written down item by item, and what money he has spent on which things, so that the account of debit and credit is so clear and distinct that, even in his absence, it can be calculated what each province, house, college or private person has given or owes to the Procurator, or what is owed to them by the Procurator. So that this may be observed more conveniently, he shall at least once a year, at the feast of the Lord's Nativity, collect and write out the sum of all the accounts and send it to those concerned; and if any money is left over, he shall inform them so that it may be disposed of at their discretion.

units.la: 10. Librum habeat, in quo scribat beneficia omnia Ecclesiastica, quæ singularum Provinciarum Collegijs sunt unita, & horum etiam catalogum, ubi tempus, in quo fuit facta unaquæque unio, & valor etiam annotetur, animadvertatque, ut antequam adveniat dies prescriptus solvendi quindennia, Rectores Collegiorum, ad quæ huiusmodi uniones pertinent, diligenter admoneat, ut opportuno tempore pecunias Romam mittant.
units.tr: 10. He shall keep a book in which he writes down all the ecclesiastical benefices united to the colleges of each province, and a catalogue of these, noting the time at which each union was made and also its value. He shall take care that, before the prescribed date for paying the quindennial dues arrives, he diligently warns the Rectors of the colleges to which such unions belong, so that they send the money to Rome at the proper time.

units.la: 11. Curet, ut à Provincijs mittantur pecuniæ, quas contribuere debent ad sumptus necessarios in Procuratores, ut cum opus fuerit, in advocatos, latores literarum, & alios simile faciendos: utque Romæ sint eo tempore, quo illis sunt solvendæ, eademque diligentia, quæ sibi deberi ex libro rationum colliget, ut reddantur, curabit.
units.tr: 11. He shall see that money which the provinces must contribute for the necessary expenses of the Procurators is sent to them, for use when needed on advocates, letter-bearers and others of the kind; and that it is in Rome at the time when it must be paid out. With the same diligence with which he gathers from the account book what is owed to him, he shall see that it is repaid.

units.la: 12. Cum pecunia Procuratori ad negotia conficienda transmittetur, si tantum literæ bancharia, quæ de credito dicuntur, mittantur, nihil capiat, nisi quantum & quando pro negotio conficiendo opus erit: si verò bancharia literæ ad certam aliquam summam, quæ jam alibi soluta est, capiendam missæ fuerint, & ea ipsa jam jam ad negotia expedienda erit necessaria, ne tum quidem à mercatore, præsertim locuplete, & spectatæ fidei educatur, donec numeranda sit: si verò non tam cito erit necessaria, vel de fide mercatoris non tam certò constaret, primò quoque tempore ab eo accepta pecunia, eam si alicuius momenti fuerit, reponat in arca sub duplici clavi, quarum alteram ipse, & alteram diversam socius habeat.
units.tr: 12. When money is sent to the Procurator to carry out business, if only letters of credit, which are called bancharia, are sent, he shall draw only as much, and when, as the business requires. But if letters of credit have been sent for drawing some definite sum that has already been paid elsewhere, and that very sum is about to be needed immediately to despatch the business, then he shall not even draw it from a merchant, especially a wealthy one of proven good faith, until it is to be paid out. If, however, it is not needed so soon, or the merchant's good faith is not so certain, he shall, as soon as possible after receiving the money, place it, if it is of any amount, in a chest under a double lock, one key of which he himself holds and the other a companion.

units.la: 13. Scripturas, bullas, & brevia authentica, quæ in Archivio conservantur, non nisi exigente necessitate accipiet: acceptas verò, quam primum commodè poterit, reddat: cæteras autem scripturas, Procuratoris instrumenta, literas negotia continentes, quamdiu necessaria fuerint, & demum quæcunque ad officium eius pertinent, & quæ nec perpetuò necessaria sunt, nec semper servanda erunt, ipse custodiat ordinatè, & distinctè, facto eorum omnium inventario, cubiculum, sit clavi obseratum.
units.tr: 13. He shall take the writings, bulls and authentic briefs kept in the archive only when necessity demands, and return them as soon as he conveniently can. The other writings, the Procurator's instruments, letters concerning business, for as long as they are needed, and finally whatever belongs to his office, which are not always needed nor must always be kept, he shall keep himself, in good order and distinctly, after making an inventory of all of them, in a room locked with a key.

units.la: 14. Informationes ad se missas in omnibus expeditionibus habeat præ oculis, ut ad eas omninò supplicationes conformentur: deinde animadvertat, ut bullæ, & brevia, quæ expediuntur, cum supplicationibus concordent.
units.tr: 14. He shall keep before his eyes the information sent to him in all expeditions, so that the supplications are entirely made to conform to it; and then he shall see that the bulls and briefs that are issued agree with the supplications.

units.la: 15. In librum referat summam omnium negotiorum, quæ ei commendantur, resq; majoris momenti, quæ in eorum progressu peragentur, ibidem brevi, ac diluculo ordine conscribat.
units.tr: 15. He shall enter in a book the summary of all the business entrusted to him, and of the more important matters that occur in its progress, writing them down there briefly and in order, early in the day.

units.la: 16. Exempla literarum, quas ad varias Provincias, & loca scribit de negotijs, in librū peculiarem referat: & cum memoralia, informationes, supplicationes, vel alia scripta alicuius momenti alijs dabit, exemplum eorum apud se servet.
units.tr: 16. He shall enter the copies of the letters he writes about business to various provinces and places in a special book; and when he gives memoranda, information, supplications or other writings of some importance to others, he shall keep a copy of them himself.

units.la: 17. Regulas Cancellariæ habeat, Bullas, & brevia quæ à summo Pontifice fiunt, sematn eisq; animadvertat, quid novi contineatur: quod si in Cœnæ Domini Bulla aliquid addetur, aut mutaretur, eam statim ad omnes Provincias transmittat: motus etiam proprios universales, conscio tamen Præposito Generali, Provincialibus mittet.
units.tr: 17. He shall have the rules of the Chancery, and shall keep watch on the bulls and briefs issued by the Supreme Pontiff, and note what new matter they contain; and if anything is added to or changed in the Bull of the Lord's Supper, he shall send it at once to all the provinces. He shall also send to the provincials the universal motu proprio decrees, with the Superior General's knowledge.

units.la: 18. Cum Præpositus Generalis adire voluerit, creatum novum Pontificem, ut juxta Constitutiones suæ Sanctitati Obedientiam, votumque Societatis declaret, redigat illi Procurator in memoriam, ut videat, an expediat ab eo impetrare confirmationem gratiarum, & privilegiorum Societatis.
units.tr: 18. When the Superior General wishes to approach a newly created Pontiff, the Procurator shall remind him that, in accordance with the Constitutions, he should declare to His Holiness the obedience and vow of the Society, and see whether it is expedient to obtain from him confirmation of the graces and privileges of the Society.

units.la: 19. Subditus sit Superioribus Collegij, præterquam in iis, quæ ad sui officij executionem spectant.
units.tr: 19. He shall be subject to the superiors of the college, except in those matters which pertain to the execution of his own office.

units.la: REGVLAE PROCVRATORIS DOMVS PROFESSAE.
units.tr: RULES OF THE PROCURATOR OF THE PROFESSED HOUSE.

units.la: 1. IN omnium negotiorum tractatione perpetuo memor sit instituti Societatis, quæ Dei omnipotentis gloriam quærens, profectui animarum invigilat. Curet igitur ipse verbo, & exemplo præsertim humilitatis, & patientiæ eos omnes ædificare, quibus cum conversatur, atque eos sibi benevolos conservare, quorum opera ad negotia peragenda indiget: & cum opportunerit, de instituti nostri ratione illos informet.
units.tr: 1. In handling all business he shall always keep in mind the purpose of the Society, which, seeking the glory of almighty God, watches over the progress of souls. Let him therefore take care, by his word and especially by his example of humility and patience, to edify all those with whom he deals, and to keep well disposed towards him those whose help he needs to carry on the business; and, when the opportunity arises, let him inform them about the principles of our institute.

units.la: 2. Quærat diligenter eleemosynas, easque simpliciter, & amore Domini petat, nec non & eas augere, ac conservare studeat, opportuneque eos visitet, à quibus petenda erunt.
units.tr: 2. Let him seek alms diligently, asking for them simply and for the love of the Lord; let him also strive to increase and preserve them, and visit at suitable times those from whom they are to be asked.

units.la: 3. Habeat Catalogum eorum, qui ordinarie, & extraordinarie eleemosynas faciunt, & de his certiorem faciat Superiorem, ac videat, ne sua negligentia aliquos prætermittat, quorum beneficio domus juvari possit.
units.tr: 3. Let him keep a list of those who give alms, both regularly and occasionally, report these to the Superior, and see to it that through his negligence he does not overlook any from whose kindness the house could be helped.

units.la: 4. Animadvertat, quid, à quibus petere debet, juxta id quod unusquisque facilius, & commodius suo tempore dare possit: & caveat ne in petendis eleemosynis gravis, vel molestus externus sit, ita ut ad eos, cum oportuerit, gratus semper pateat aditus nostrorum.
units.tr: 4. Let him consider what should be asked, and from whom, according to what each person can give more easily and conveniently at his time; and let him take care that he is not a burdensome or troublesome outsider in asking for alms, so that access to them may always stand open to our men when it is needed.

units.la: 5. Habeat socium à Superiore designatum, cuius opera utatur in his, quæ ad suum ossicium pertinent, præter alium (ubi opus erit) qui in virtute, & conversatione probatus, possit eleemosynas ordinarias per domos colligere.
units.tr: 5. Let him have an associate designated by the Superior, whose help he may use in those matters which pertain to his office; and besides this, (where there is need) another man, proven in virtue and conduct, who can gather the ordinary alms from house to house.

units.la: 6. Procuratoris erit, quascunque eleemosynas recipere, & quæcunque afferuntur donum, in libro quodam ad id designato, quotidie scribere.
units.tr: 6. It shall be the procurator's duty to receive whatever alms are given, and to write down daily whatever is brought as a gift, in a book designated for this purpose.

units.la: 7. Videat in quærendis, vel admittendis eleemosynis, ne præjudicium fiat puritati instituti, quod attinet ad eius ministeria, gratis omnino exercenda.
units.tr: 7. In seeking or accepting alms, let him see that no harm is done to the purity of the institute, as far as its ministries, which must be exercised entirely without payment, are concerned.

units.la: 8. Pecunia undecunque provenerit, si alicuius momenti fuerit, judicio Superioris in arca reponatur ad id designata. Huius Præpositus clavem unam, & ipse Procurator alteram diversam custodiat: in eadem liber asservabitur, in quo scribetur pecuniæ summa, tam eius quæ infertur, quam eius quæ effertur: si quando autem cogente aliqua necessitate pecunia in arcam non inferretur, nihilominus accepti, & expensi summa semel in hebdomada in eodem libro scribatur, ac si in ea reponeretur.
units.tr: 8. Whatever money comes in, from whatever source, if it is of any considerable amount, shall be placed, at the Superior's judgment, in a chest designated for this purpose. The Prefect keeps one key and the procurator himself keeps another, different one. In the same chest a book shall be kept, in which the sum of money, both what is brought in and what is taken out, shall be written. If at any time, under some pressing necessity, money could not be put into the chest, nevertheless the total of receipts and expenditures shall be written in the same book once a week, just as if it had been placed there.

units.la: 9. Quoties ex arca pecuniam accipiet, eius summam, & diem in libro suarum rationum adscribat, in altera vero parte libri, expensi ratio constet.
units.tr: 9. Whenever he takes money from the chest, he shall enter the amount and the day in the book of his accounts, and on the other side of the book the record of expenditure shall stand.

units.la: 10. Procurator in libro ad hoc designato, quem penes se habere debet, scribat omnia quæ unusquisque Novitiorum domum attulerit, cum eiusdem subscriptione, & ea Custodiet, nisi fit pecunia, quam separatim custodiet in arca, ubi pecuniæ domus reponuntur, donec, biennio expleto, Novitius consueta vota Societatis emittat.
units.tr: 10. The procurator shall write, in the book designated for this purpose which he must keep in his own possession, everything that each novice brings into the house, with the novice's signature, and he shall keep it safe, except for money, which he shall keep separately in the chest where the house's money is placed, until, after two years have been completed, the novice takes the customary vows of the Society.

units.la: 11. Singulis mensibus dati, & accepti rationem Superiori reddet, & debita etiam indicabit, quo ipse domus statum prorsus intelligat.
units.tr: 11. Each month he shall render an account of money given and received to the Superior, and shall also report debts, so that the Superior may fully understand the state of the house.

units.la: 12. Diligenti cura asservabit in Archivio ad hoc designato instrumenta originalia, & titulos, quibus constat de iure eorum, quæ domus ad usum, & propriam habitationem possident, suis locis reposita, ut facile inveniri possint. Archivij autem duæ claves diversæ erunt, quarum alteram Præpositus, alteram ipse habebit Procurator.
units.tr: 12. He shall carefully keep in the archive designated for this purpose the original instruments and titles which establish the right to the property the house holds for its use and its own dwelling, placed in their proper places so that they can easily be found. There shall be two different keys to the archive, one of which the Prefect and the other the procurator himself shall have.

units.la: 13. Item seorsum habebit hæc eadem instrumenta, & titulos manu Notarij publici subscriptos, ut fidem faciant, si aliquando in judicio præsentari necesse sit.
units.tr: 13. Likewise he shall keep apart copies of these same instruments and titles, signed by a public notary, so that they may provide proof if they ever need to be produced in court.

units.la: 14. Prate 14. Praeterhaec Procurator librum habebit, in quo summa quaedam horum instrumentorum, & titulorum contineatur: cum autem contractus maioris momenti, praesertim rerum perpetuarum fient, redigat in memoriam Praeposito ad Archivium, quod est in urbe penes Praepositum Generalem, eorum exempla authentica mittenda esse.
units.tr: 14. Besides this, the procurator shall have a book in which a summary of these instruments and titles is contained. When contracts of greater importance are made, especially those concerning perpetual matters, he shall remind the Prefect that authentic copies of them are to be sent to the archive in the city, which is held by the Superior General.

units.la: 15. Cubiculum clavi obseratum habeat, & asservabit scripturas, quibus ad Procuratorium munus indigebit, cumque aliquas ex Archivio accipiet, earum in libro, qui in eodem Archivio erit, annotato die, mense, & anno memoriam relinquet, quas cum suo tempore restituet, ex eodem libro expunget.
units.tr: 15. He shall keep his room locked, and shall keep safe the writings which he needs for the office of procurator. When he takes any from the archive, he shall leave a record of them, noting the day, month and year, in the book which is kept in that archive; and when the time comes he shall return them and strike the entry from the same book.

units.la: 16. Cum toti domui necessaria providere ipse debeat, juxta Superioris ordinem, curet, ut res omnes, praecipue diu duraturae, quam opportune emantur: ne aut non perinde bonas, aut non aequo pretio cogatur comparare: caveat etiam ne dum nimium pecuniae parcit, non bonas, aut insalubres res emat.
units.tr: 16. Since he must himself provide for everything the whole house needs, according to the Superior's order, he shall take care to buy all goods, especially those meant to last a long time, at the right moment, so that he is not forced to buy goods that are not equally good or not at a fair price; he shall also beware, lest in being overly sparing of money he buy goods that are not good or are unwholesome.

units.la: 17. Emptori pecunias ad quotidianos sumptus submi-nistrabit, a quo singulis diebus expensarum exiget rationem ex codice, summam vero in librum suum ipse referet.
units.tr: 17. He shall supply money for daily expenses to the buyer, from whom he shall demand an account of the expenses each day from the ledger, and he himself shall enter the sum in his own book.

units.la: 18. Videat num ea, quae empta sunt, illaesa conserventur, atq; animadvertens aliqua, non ut oportet conservari, aut expendi, Superiorem, vel Ministrum admoneat.
units.tr: 18. He shall see whether the things that have been bought are kept safe and unharmed, and if he notices anything not kept or spent as it should be, he shall warn the Superior or the Minister.

units.la: REGVLAE PROCVRATORIS COLLEGII, ET DOMVS PRO- BATIONIS.
units.tr: Rules of the Procurator of the College, and of the House of Probation.

units.la: 1. IN omnium negotiorum tractatione perpetuo memor sit instituti Societatis, quae Dei omnipotentis gloriam quaerens, profectui animarum invigilat. Curet igitur ipse verbo, & exemplo eos omnes aedificare, quibuscum conversatur, atq; eos sibi benevolos conservare, quorum opera ad negotia peragenda indiget.
units.tr: 1. In the management of all affairs, he shall always keep in mind the purpose of the Society, which, seeking the glory of almighty God, watches over the progress of souls. He shall therefore take care to edify by word and example all those with whom he deals, and to keep well disposed towards him those whose work he needs in order to carry out his business.

units.la: 2. Procuratoris erit conservare res temporales suae curae commissas, & eas curare, tanquam bona propria Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Cum autem toti Collegio necessaria providere ipse debeat, juxta Superioris ordinem, ad eum pertinebit proventus quoscunque Collegii, vel Domus probationis, & eleemosynas, ubi petendas a Rectore intellexerit, exigere ac recipere: syngraphas vero solutionis, quando opus erit, ipse dabit subscriptas a Rectore, aut a se, illius commissione.
units.tr: 2. It shall be the Procurator's task to preserve the temporal goods committed to his care and to look after them as if they were the own goods of our Lord Jesus Christ. Since he must provide what is necessary for the whole College, according to the order of the Superior, it shall be his responsibility to collect and receive all the revenues of the College or House of Probation, and the alms, where he learns from the Rector that they are to be sought. He shall himself issue the promissory notes for payment when needed, signed by the Rector, or by himself under the Rector's commission.

units.la: 3. Omnes Collegij proventus, & tempora, quibus colligendi sunt, in peculiari libro scribet, & seorsum summam contractuum & locationum, quae ad breve tempus fiunt: seorsum etiam quascunque res, aut pecunias ex fructibus Collegii perceperit, addito a quibus, & quando ea provenerint: eleemosynae autem alio in loco scribantur.
units.tr: 3. He shall write all the revenues of the College, and the times when they are to be collected, in a special book, and separately the sum of the contracts and leases made for a short period. He shall likewise record separately whatever goods or money he has received from the income of the College, adding from whom and when they came; alms, however, shall be written down in another place.

units.la: 4. Singulis mensibus dati & acceptirationem Rectori reddet, debitaq;, & credita Collegij indicabit, quo ipse domus statum prorsus intelligat.
units.tr: 4. Every month he shall render to the Rector an account of receipts and expenditure, and shall indicate the debts and credits of the College, so that the Rector may fully understand the state of the house.

units.la: 5. Pecunia, undecunq; ea provenerit, si alicuius momenti fuerit, judicio Superioris, in arca reponetur ad id designata: huius Rector clavem unam, & ipse Procurator alteram diversam custodiat: in eadem liber asservabitur, in quo scribetur pecuniae summa, tam eius quae infertur, quam eius, quae effertur, si quando autem cogente aliqua necessitate pecunia in arcam non inferretur, nihilominus accepti, & expensi summa in eodem libro statim scribatur, ac si in ea reponeretur.
units.tr: 5. Money, from whatever source it comes, if it is of some amount, shall be placed, at the Superior's judgment, in a chest designated for this purpose. The Rector shall keep one key and the Procurator himself another, different one. In the same chest a book shall be kept in which the sum of money is to be written, both what is brought in and what is taken out. If, however, through some pressing necessity money is not put into the chest, the sum received and spent shall nonetheless be written at once in the same book, just as if it had been placed there.

units.la: 6. Quoties ex arca pecuniam accipiet, eius summam, & diem in libro suarum rationum adscribat: in alia vero parte libri, expensi ratio constet.
units.tr: 6. Whenever he takes money from the chest, he shall enter the sum and the day in his account book; on another side of the book the record of expenditure shall stand.

units.la: 7. Procurator in libro ad hoc designato, quem penes se habere debet, scribat omnia, quae unusquisque Novitiorum domum attulerit, cum eiusdem subscriptione, & ea Custodi pestium asservanda tradet, nisi sit pecunia, quam separatim custodiet in arca, ubi pecunia Collegij reponuntur, donec, biennio expleto, Novitius consueta vota Societatis emittat.
units.tr: 7. In the book designated for this purpose, which he must keep himself, the Procurator shall write down everything that each of the novices brings into the house, together with the novice's signature, and he shall hand these items over to the keeper to be kept safe, except for money, which he shall keep separately in the chest where the College's money is placed, until, after two years have been completed, the novice takes the customary vows of the Society.

units.la: 8. Emptori pecunias ad quotidianos sumptus subministrabit, à quo singulis diebus expensarum exiget rationem ex codice: summam vero in librum suum ipse referet.
units.tr: 8. He shall supply the steward with money for daily expenses, and from him he shall demand an account of expenses every day from the ledger; the sum, however, he shall himself transfer to his own book.

units.la: 9. Curet, ut res omnes, præcipuè diu duraturæ quàm opportunè emantur, ne has non perindebonas, aut non æquo pretio cogatur comparare: caveat etiam ne dum nimium in pecuniæ parcit non bonas, aut insalubres res emat.
units.tr: 9. He shall take care that all goods, especially those intended to last a long time, are bought at the right moment, so that he is not forced to buy goods that are poor or not of fair price. He shall also beware lest, while being too sparing with money, he buy goods that are of poor quality or unwholesome.

units.la: 10. Videat num ea, quæ empta sunt, illa sic conferventur, atque animadvertens aliqua, non ut oportet conservari, aut expendi, Superiorem, vel Ministrum admoneat.
units.tr: 10. He shall see whether the things that have been bought are preserved as they ought to be, and if, noticing that some are not being kept or spent as they should be, he shall admonish the Superior or the Minister.

units.la: 11. Advertat, num ea, quæ à Collegio possidentur, reparatione indigeant, seu domus, seu prædia, seu quidvis aliud, ut ad Superiorem referat: si quid autem vendendum videretur, eodem inconsulto, ne faciat.
units.tr: 11. He shall consider whether the things possessed by the College need repair, whether houses, estates, or anything else, so that he may report to the Superior; but if anything seems to need selling, he shall not do so without the Superior's consultation.

units.la: 12. Omnia, quæ speciem habent secularis negotiationis, in colendis videlicet agris, vendendis in foro fructibus, & similibus, intelligat prohibita esse nostris.
units.tr: 12. He shall understand that all things that have the appearance of secular trade, namely in cultivating fields, selling produce in the market, and the like, are forbidden to our members.

units.la: 13. Nihil, quod ad locationes, contractus, aut debita contrahenda, aut alia alicuius momenti negotia pertineat, faciat, nisi ipsi à Superiore commissum sit: si quid autem ex iis, quæ jubentur, ipsi videretur non expedire, eidem proponat modestè suam sententiam, & rationes, quibus moveatur.
units.tr: 13. He shall do nothing that pertains to leases, contracts, the incurring of debts, or other business of any importance, unless it has been committed to him by the Superior. If he thinks that any of the things commanded to him are not advisable, he shall modestly set out to the Superior his opinion and the reasons that move him.

units.la: 14. Excipiet in codicem lites, si quæ forte erunt, & quæ gravioris momenti circa eas fient, continenter & summatim annotabit.
units.tr: 14. He shall record in the register any lawsuits that may arise, and whatever of greater importance happens in connection with them, noting it continually and in summary form.

units.la: 15. In tribunalibus judicum non compareat, nisi quando aliqua necessitas plurimùm urgere Superiori videretur, sed per externos Procuratores nostra negotia in publicis judiciis peragantur.
units.tr: 15. He shall not appear in the courts of judges unless some necessity seems to the Superior to press very urgently; our business shall be conducted in public courts through external procurators.

units.la: 16. Illud verò præcipuè ante oculos habeat, ut antequam litem ullam intendat, res controversa (si fieri possit) concordia aut compromissione, consulto Superiore, componatur: si quando tamen ad litem descendendum erit, memor sit, ut magnam pacem interius exterius que custodiat, & semper ad justam concordiam ipsum paratum esse contrariæ parti innotescat.
units.tr: 16. Above all he shall keep before his eyes that, before he brings any lawsuit, the matter in dispute shall be settled (if it can be) by agreement or arbitration, with the Superior's consent. If, however, he must go to law, he shall remember to keep great peace inwardly and outwardly, and make it known to the opposing party that he is always ready for a just agreement.

units.la: 17. Curet diligenter, ut recte, & solidè fiant, quæ expedienda erunt: quod si peritis juris consulendi sint, maximè idoneos eligat. Idem de cæteris officialibus dictum intelligatur.
units.tr: 17. He shall take care that what has to be done is done properly and soundly; if legal advice is needed, he shall choose the most suitable experts. The same is to be understood of the other officials.

units.la: 18. Conferat cum Superiore, eique reddat rationem eorum, quæ fecit, & quo in statu negotia sint, aut ei, quem ille designabit: quod si rerum difficultas extraordinariam favorem, aut diligentiam exigere videatur, eidem significet, ut auxilia, quæ opportuna visa erunt, petantur.
units.tr: 18. He shall confer with the Superior and give him an account of what he has done and of the state in which affairs stand, or to whomever the Superior designates. If the difficulty of the matters seems to require extraordinary favour or diligence, he shall signify this to the Superior, so that the aids that seem opportune may be sought.

units.la: 19. Diligenti cura asservabit in Archivio ad hoc designato instrumenta originalia, & titulos, quibus constat de jure eorum, quæ à Collegio possidentur, suis locis repositæ, ut facile inveniri possint. Archivij autem duæ claves diversæ erunt, quarum alteram Rector, alteram ipse habebit Procurator.
units.tr: 19. He shall keep with diligent care in the archive designated for this purpose the original instruments and title deeds which establish the right to what the College possesses, placed in their proper places so that they can be easily found. There shall be two different keys to the archive, one held by the Rector and the other by the Procurator.

units.la: 20. Seorsum habebit hæc eadem instrumenta, & titulos manu Notarij publici subscriptos, ut fidem faciant, si aliquando in judicio præsentari necesse fit.
units.tr: 20. He shall keep these same instruments and title deeds apart, subscribed by the hand of a public notary, so that they may carry authority if at any time they need to be presented in court.

units.la: 21. Præter hæc Procurator librum habebit, in quo summa quædam horum instrumentorum, & titulorum continetur: cum autem contractus maioris momenti, præsertim rerum perpetuarum, fient, redigat in memoriam Rectori ad Archivium, quod est in urbe penes Præpositum Generalem, eorum exempla authentica mittenda esse.
units.tr: 21. Besides these, the Procurator shall have a book in which a certain summary of these instruments and title deeds is contained; and when contracts of greater importance, especially those concerning perpetual property, are made, he shall remind the Rector that authentic copies are to be sent to the archive in the city kept by the General Prepositus.

units.la: 22. Cubiculum clavi obseratum habeat, & asservabit scripturas, quibus ad Procuratorium munus indigebit: cumque aliquas ex Archivio accipiet, earum in libro, qui in eodem Archivio erit, notato die, mense, & anno, memoriam relinquet: quas cum suo tempore restituet, ex eodem libro expugnet.
units.tr: 22. He shall keep his room locked and shall retain the writings that he needs for the office of Procurator; and when he takes any from the archive, he shall leave a record of them, noting the day, month, and year in the book that is kept in that archive; and when he returns them at the proper time, he shall strike them out from the same book.

units.la: 23. In libellum referet quæcunque à Superiore ipsi facienda injungentur, ne memoria excidant, & effectu frustrentur.
units.tr: 23. He shall write in a little notebook whatever the Superior enjoins on him to do, so that it does not slip from memory and go unperformed.

units.la: 24. Intelligat, qui sint illi potissimum, qui beneficia magni momenti in Collegium contulerunt. contuleτunt, & eorum catalogum habeat, & Superiorem certiorem faciat, ut juxta modum professionis nostræ, gratì in illos esse possimus.
units.tr: 24. He shall find out who are those most of all who have conferred benefits of great importance on the College, and shall keep a list of them, and inform the Superior, so that, in keeping with the manner of our profession, we may be grateful to them.

units.la: REGVLÆ PRAEFECTI LECTORVM AD MENSAM.
units.tr: Rules of the Prefect of Readers at Table.

units.la: Vret, ut idoneì in lectores mensæ à Superiore destinentur, & eos instruat, ut alta, clara, & distincta voce legant.
units.tr: 1. He shall see to it that suitable men are appointed by the Superior as readers at table, and he shall train them to read in a loud, clear and distinct voice.

units.la: 2. Det operam, ut lector prævideat diligenter lectionem, ut bene, & emendatè proferat, & in dubijs ad se recurrat.
units.tr: 2. He shall take care that the reader carefully previews the reading, so that he pronounces it well and correctly, and that he has recourse to the Prefect in cases of doubt.

units.la: 3. Admoneat lectorem, ut si quid perperàm pronunciaverit, corrēctus repetat, & emendatè iterum proferat.
units.tr: 3. He shall admonish the reader that if he has mispronounced anything, he is to be corrected, repeat it, and pronounce it correctly again.

units.la: 4. Habeat à Superiore assignatos sibi socios, ut in neutra mensa desit, qui lectorem corrigat, eosque juxta has Regulas instruat.
units.tr: 4. He shall have companions assigned to him by the Superior, so that at neither table is there a lack of someone to correct the reader; and he shall instruct them according to these Rules.

units.la: 5. Initio lectionis in prima, atq; etiam (nisi nostrorum paucitas aliud suaserit) in secunda mensa in prandio, & Cœna legatur caput de Scriptura sacra novi vel veteris Testamenti, cui succeedat semper aliquis liberiùs ac facilìs juxta indicem inferiùs præscriptum, & habeatur peculiaris ratio Coadjutorum, ut pro arbitrio Superiorum aliquid vernacula lingua ad illorum etiam consolationem legatur.
units.tr: 5. At the beginning of the reading, at the first table and also (unless the small number of our men suggests otherwise) at the second table, at dinner and at supper, a chapter from Holy Scripture, of the New or Old Testament, shall be read; this shall always be followed by something rather freer and easier, according to the list prescribed below. Special consideration shall be given to the Coadjutors, so that, at the discretion of the Superiors, something may also be read in the vernacular for their consolation.

units.la: 6. In celebrioribus festis legatur aliquid omisso capitulo scripturæ, ex Patrum homiliis, & tractatibus, quod ad historiam, & celebritatem festi pertineat, & à Dominica in passione usque ad Pascha, post lectionem scripturæ de passione Domini tractatus aliquot ì eadem legantur.
units.tr: 6. On the more solemn feasts, something from the homilies and treatises of the Fathers shall be read in place of the chapter of Scripture, provided it pertains to the history and celebration of the feast; and from Sunday in Passiontide until Easter, after the reading of Scripture on the Passion of the Lord, several treatises shall be read on the same.

units.la: 7. Cùm afferuntur literæ annuæ, & Indicæ, quàm primùm legantur.
units.tr: 7. When the annual and Indian letters are brought, they shall be read as soon as possible.

units.la: 8. Initio cujuscunq; mensis Summarium Constitutionum, Regulæ communes, & Epistola P. N. Ignatij de Obedientia legantur.
units.tr: 8. At the beginning of each month, the Summary of the Constitutions, the Common Rules, and the Letter of Father Ignatius on Obedience shall be read.

units.la: 9. Vesperi absoluta lectione, seu prædicatione legatur martyrologium vulgare sequentis diei: quo verò die fit abstinentia, caput aliquod ex libro de imitatione Christi, cum martyrologio: cum verò jejunatur, nihil legatur vesperi, sed martyrologium legatur ad prandium.
units.tr: 9. In the evening, after the lecture or sermon is finished, the common martyrology of the following day shall be read; on the day of abstinence, a chapter from the book On the Imitation of Christ shall be read, together with the martyrology; but when there is a fast, nothing shall be read in the evening, and the martyrology shall be read at dinner.

units.la: LIBRI DIVINÆ SCRIPTVRÆ, QVÆ IN REFECTORIO LEGENTVR.
units.tr: THE BOOKS OF HOLY SCRIPTURE WHICH ARE READ IN THE REFECTORY.

units.la: Ex novo Testamento, omnia integrè legentur. Ex veteri, Pentateuchus, præter Leviticum. Historiales omnes, & Sapientiales, præter Cantica. Prophetales, præter capita aliquot obscuriora.
units.tr: From the New Testament, everything is to be read in full. From the Old, the Pentateuch, except Leviticus. All the historical and Sapiential books, except the Canticles. The Prophetical books, except some of the more obscure chapters.

units.la: LIBRI, QVI POST LECTIONEM SCRIPTV- RÆ LEGI POSSVNT.
units.tr: BOOKS WHICH MAY BE READ AFTER THE READING OF SCRIPTURE.

units.la: Historia Ecclesiastica Eusebij Cæsariensis. Historia Ecclesiastica Nicephori Callisti. D. Gregorij Dialogi. Historia Ecclesiastica Bedæ. Vita Sanctorum Aloysij Lipomani. Vita Sanctorum Surij. Severus Sulpitius de Beato Martino. Gregorius Turonensis de gloria Confessorum. Electæ Epistolæ D. Hieronymi. Chrysostomus de orando Deum, de providentia, & de Sacerdotio.
units.tr: Eusebius of Caesarea's Ecclesiastical History. Nicephorus Callistus's Ecclesiastical History. St Gregory's Dialogues. Bede's Ecclesiastical History. The Lives of the Saints by Aloysius Lipomanus. The Lives of the Saints by Surius. Severus Sulpicius on Blessed Martin. Gregory of Tours on the Glory of the Confessors. Selected Letters of St Jerome. Chrysostom on prayer to God, on providence, and on the priesthood.

units.la: Ambrosius de fuga seculi, de bono Mortis.
units.tr: Ambrose on flight from the world, and on the good of death.

units.la: Augustin. sermones, Meditationes, Confessiones, & alia eiusdem opuscula & tractatus
units.tr: Augustine's sermons, Meditations, Confessions, and his other little works and treatises.

units.la: D. Bernardi de interiori domo, & aliquot sermones & tractatus. (tur
units.tr: St Bernard's On the Interior House, and some sermons and treatises.

units.la: Homiliæ Patrum selectæ.
units.tr: Selected homilies of the Fathers.

units.la: D. Bonaventuræ stimulus divini amoris.
units.tr: St Bonaventure's Goad of Divine Love.

units.la: Thomas de Kempis de imitatione Christi, & aliquot ex eiusdem auctoris opusculis.
units.tr: Thomas à Kempis, On the Imitation of Christ, and some of the same author's minor works.

units.la: Catechismus Romanus.
units.tr: The Roman Catechism.

units.la: Litera Indicæ.
units.tr: Letters from the Indies.

units.la: 10. Præter hos libros poterunt quidem alij legitimi vulgares, tum Latini, sed examinati, & approbati à Provinciali: atq; illi esse debent, qui & pietatem promoveant, & vocationis propriæ propositum confirmare possint.
units.tr: 10. Besides these books, other approved vernacular books may also be read, both in Latin and in the vernacular, provided they have been examined and approved by the Provincial. They must be books that both promote piety and can confirm one in the purpose of his own vocation.

units.la: 11. De singulis libris suo tempore prælegendis in mensa juxta indicem præscriptum, prius conferet cum Superiore, ut ille constituat, quid legendum sit.
units.tr: 11. Concerning each book to be read aloud at table at its proper time, according to the prescribed index, he shall first consult the Superior, so that the Superior may determine what is to be read.

units.la: 12. Catalogum à Superiore habeat eorum, qui in refectorio commodè concionari possunt, ex quibus Superior ipse eligat, qui statis diebus concionentur, & eos præscripto tempore admonebit, quâ de re sint concionaturi.
units.tr: 12. He shall have from the Superior a list of those who can preach suitably in the refectory. From these the Superior himself shall choose who is to preach on the set days, and he shall remind them at the appointed time what they are to preach on.

units.la: REGVLÆ PRAEFECTI SA- NITATIS.
units.tr: Rules of the Prefect of Health.

units.la: Præfecti sanitatis munus erit, superintendere iis, quæ ad corporis bonam valetudinem pertinent conservandam in sanis, (in iis præsertim, qui ex ætate, aut alijs de causis sunt debiliores) tum restituendam in ægrotantibus.
units.tr: The office of the prefect of health shall be to oversee those things which pertain to preserving good bodily health in the well (especially in those who are weaker by reason of age or other causes), and also to restoring it in the sick.

units.la: 2. Præsit Infirmario, & cæteris quibus cura ægrotorum commissa erit, detq; operam, ne desit Medicus, adsitq; eo veniente, præsertim ubi morbi qualitas id postula verit, & quicquid ab eo præscriptum fuerit, studeat, ut executioni mandetur: & ubi videret ægrotorum cubicula salubria non esse, ad Superiorem referat.
units.tr: 2. He shall preside over the infirmary and over the others to whom the care of the sick has been committed, and shall take care that a physician is never lacking, and that he is present when the physician comes, especially where the nature of the illness requires it; and whatever has been prescribed by him, he shall see to it that it is carried out. And if he sees that the sick-rooms are not healthy, he shall report this to the Superior.

units.la: 3. Observet, num quis ex nimia fatigatione corporis, aut spiritus plus æquo laboret, vel alia de causa morbi periculo se exponat, & superiori significet.
units.tr: 3. He shall observe whether anyone labours more than is right from excessive fatigue of body or mind, or exposes himself to danger of illness for some other reason, and he shall report this to the Superior.

units.la: 4. Si in cibis, aere, frigore, aut alia quapiam in re aliquid probabili ratione animadverterit, quod communi omnium, vel alicujus saluti prodesse, vel obesse possit, Superiorem admoneat.
units.tr: 4. If he notices anything, on probable grounds, in food, air, cold, or some other matter, which could benefit or harm the health of all or of some one person, he shall advise the Superior.

units.la: 5. Curet, ut infirmarius Regulas suas observet, quas apud se etiam habebit.
units.tr: 5. He shall see that the infirmarian observes his own rules, which he shall also keep by him.

units.la: REGVLÆ PRAEFECTI BI- BLIOTHECÆ.
units.tr: RULES OF THE PREFECT OF THE LIBRARY.

units.la: 1. Indicem librorum prohibitorum in Bibliotheca habeat, & videat, ne forte ullus sit inter eos ex prohibitis, aut alijs, quorum usus communis esse non debet.
units.tr: 1. He shall have an index of the prohibited books in the library, and shall see that there is none among them that is prohibited, or otherwise of a kind whose use ought not to be common.

units.la: 2. Bibliotheca clausa sit, cuius claves ipse habeat & illis tradat, qui eas, juxta Superioris judicium, habere debebunt.
units.tr: 2. The library shall be kept locked; he himself shall hold the keys and hand them over to those who are to have them, according to the judgment of the Superior.

units.la: 3. Libri omnes eo ordine in Bibliotheca collocentur, ut singulis facultatibus suus certus sit locus proprio titulo inscriptus.
units.tr: 3. All books shall be arranged in the library in such order that each branch of learning has its own fixed place, marked with its proper title.

units.la: 4. Singuli libri tituli exterius inscribantur, ut facile cognosci possint.
units.tr: 4. The title of each book shall be written on the outside, so that they can be easily recognised.

units.la: 5. Omnium librorum, qui domi sunt, catalogum habeat, diversarum facultatum auctoribus ordine alphabethico in diversas classes distributis.
