units.tr: 5. He shall have a catalogue of all the books that are in the house, with the authors of the various branches of learning arranged alphabetically and distributed into different classes.

units.la: 6. In alio catalogo, divisis etiam per classes facultatibus, ij libri scribantur, qui in no[illegible, ~4 letters]strorum orum usum extra Bibliothecam concessi sunt: qui vero intra dies octo restituendi exhuntur, in tabula in hunc usum parieti appensa notentur: quibus redditis, quod fuerat riptum, deleatur:
units.tr: 6. In another catalogue, likewise divided into classes of learning, he shall write down those books which have been lent out of the library for use elsewhere. Those which are to be returned within eight days shall be noted on a board hung on the wall for this purpose; when they have been returned, the entry shall be deleted.

units.la: 7. Nullum librum ex Bibliotheca cuipiam dabit sine Superioris licentia speciali, aut generali, & advertat, ne quis librum, etiam cum licentia, se inscio accipiat.
units.tr: 7. He shall give no book from the library to anyone without a special or general permission from the Superior, and he shall take care that no one receives a book, even with permission, without his knowledge.

units.la: 8. Curet, ut Bibliotheca valde munda, & composita sit, quam in hebdomada bis verrt, & semel ex libris pulverem excutiet: cavere etiam debet, ne libri humiditate, aut alia laedantur.
units.tr: 8. He shall see that the library is kept very clean and in good order; it is to be swept twice a week, and the dust shaken from the books once a week. He must also take care that the books are not harmed by damp or anything else.

units.la: 9. Quando intellexerit domi deesse aliquos libros necessarios, aut aliquos valde utiles in lucem editos esse, certiorem faciat superiorem, ut si illi visum fuerit, emantur: si vero domi libri inutiles fuerint, eundem admoneat, an cum aliis melioribus commutentur.
units.tr: 9. When he learns that some necessary books are lacking in the house, or that some very useful books have been published, he shall inform the Superior, so that, if it seems good to him, they may be bought; but if books in the house are useless, he shall likewise advise him whether they should be exchanged for better ones.

units.la: 10. In loco publico, praesertim in magnis Collegiis sint quaedam communiores libri, quos unusquisque pro ratione suorum studiorum uti possit.
units.tr: 10. In a public place, especially in large colleges, there should be certain more commonly used books, which each person may use according to the nature of his studies.

units.la: 11. Habeat librum, in quo ea omnia judicio Superioris selecta diligenter scribantur, quae in suo Collegio publice exhibentur, ut Comoedia, Dialogi, Orationes, & id genus alia: Conclusiones vero singulorum annorum, quae publice defendentur, simul confutas in bibliotheca asservet.
units.tr: 11. He shall keep a book in which are carefully written all those items, chosen by the judgment of the Superior, which are publicly performed in his college, such as comedies, dialogues, orations and other things of that kind; and he shall keep in the library, likewise, the theses of each year that are publicly defended.

units.la: 12. Si aliqui libri extra domum accommodato darentur, adhibeat diligentiam ut reperentur suo tempore: & in aliquo interim libro notabit, quinam illi libri sint, & qui eos accommodaverit.
units.tr: 12. If any books are lent out of the house, he shall take care that they are recovered in due time; and in the meantime he shall note in some book which books these are and to whom he has lent them.

units.la: REGVLAE SVBMINISTRI.
units.tr: RULES OF THE SUB-MINISTER.

units.la: Subminister est instrumentum Ministri, & aliorum Superiorum, ad res particulares obeundas, & executioni mandandas.
units.tr: The sub-minister is the instrument of the Minister and of the other Superiors, for carrying out particular duties and putting orders into execution.

units.la: 2. Nihil ordinat, sed tantum est executor, & exactor actionum domesticarum, juxta modum & ordinem sibi a Superioribus praescriptum.
units.tr: 2. He orders nothing himself, but is only the executor and overseer of domestic affairs, according to the manner and order prescribed to him by the Superiors.

units.la: 3. Et eius praecipua cura, ut omnia, quae attinent ad culinam, refectorium, penum, cellarium, vinariam, & aquariam, bene, & ordine, & tempore suo parata sint, & ministrentur: ideatque, ut cubicula sint decenter composita, quae alternis saltem diebus visitabit.
units.tr: 3. His chief care is that everything that pertains to the kitchen, refectory, pantry, cellar, wine-store and water-store is prepared and served well, in good order and on time. He shall also see that the bedrooms are decently arranged, and he shall visit them at least every other day.

units.la: 4. Curet, ne nostri per Domum vel Collegium vagentur, vel intempestive colloquantur: denique ut unusquisque in suo officio versetur, & contineatur.
units.tr: 4. He shall take care that our men do not wander about the house or college, or talk at unseasonable times; in short, that each one keeps to his office and remains within it.

units.la: 5. Referet de omnibus rebus quotidie ad Ministrum, ad Praepositum vero vel Rectorem, quoties eis visum fuerit.
units.tr: 5. He shall report on all matters daily to the Minister, and to the Prefect or Rector whenever they see fit.

units.la: 6. Nullam injunget poenitentiam, sed de defectibus domesticis admoneat Ministrum, vel alium Superiorem: poterit tamen impositas poenitentias nomine alicujus Superioris aliis denunciare.
units.tr: 6. He shall impose no penance himself, but shall inform the Minister or another Superior of domestic faults. He may, however, announce to others penances imposed in the name of some Superior.

units.la: 7. Erit Superior nostrorum, qui Sacerdotes non sunt: Sacerdotibus tamen aliquid ingere poterit nomine alicujus Superioris.
units.tr: 7. He shall be the Superior of our men who are not priests; yet he may impose something upon the priests in the name of some Superior.

units.la: REGVLAE AEDITVI.
units.tr: RULES OF THE SACRISTAN.

units.la: Praefectto Ecclesiae obediat in omnibus quae ad templi ministerium pertinent.
units.tr: He shall obey the Prefect of the church in all matters that pertain to the ministry of the temple.

units.la: 2. Servet modestiam in incessu, vultu, sermoneque: tam in templo, quam in sacristia: ijs vero, qui aliquid exigunt, satisfacere cum adificatione studeat per se, vel ad Praefectum recurrendo, aut ipsos ad eum remittendo: si quando vero necesse erit cum mulieribus loqui, id oculis demissis, & quam brevissime faciat.
units.tr: 2. He shall keep modesty in his bearing, his countenance, and his speech, both in the temple and in the sacristy. He shall take care to satisfy those who make demands upon him with edification, either himself or by referring them to the Prefect, or by sending them back to him. If it should ever be necessary to speak with women, he shall do so with eyes lowered and as briefly as possible.

units.la: 3. Dum sacris inseruit, attentus ad suum ministerium cum devotione, & aedificatione [illegible, ~12 letters] fit. Nec ante eum qui celebrat, aut ad latus ex aequo, sed aliquanto posterius maneat, utatur vero tono, qui congruat cum eo, quo Sacerdos utitur: omnia recte proferat, nec celeriter nimium, nec nimis lente. Denique in iis fit bene instructus, & cateros, qui Sacerdotibus ministrabunt, eadem doceat.
units.tr: 3. While he serves at the sacred rites, let him be attentive to his ministry, with devotion and edification. He shall not stand before the one who celebrates, nor at his side on the same level, but remain somewhat behind him, and he shall use a tone of voice that agrees with the one the priest uses. Let him pronounce everything correctly, neither too quickly nor too slowly. Finally, let him be well instructed in these things, and let him teach the others who will minister to the priests the same.

units.la: 4. Curet, & vestimenta, quae sacrum facturus induitur, sint recte aptata; ipsumque circumquaque intueatur, antequam e sacristia exeat.
units.tr: 4. Let him also take care that the vestments which he puts on when about to perform the sacred rite are properly fitted, and let him look himself over on every side before he leaves the sacristy.

units.la: 5. Diligenter det operam, ut Sacerdotes, qui Sacrum facere volunt, quam primum ministros habeant juxta ordinem sibi a Superiore praescriptum; & quotidie unumquemque eorum, qui ordine in summo Altari Missas dicturi sunt, opportuno tempore admoneat.
units.tr: 5. Let him diligently take pains that the priests who wish to celebrate Mass have ministers as soon as possible, according to the order prescribed for him by the Superior; and let him remind each of those who are to say Mass at the high altar in turn, at a suitable time, every day.

units.la: 6. Tot habebit appensa sudariola in Sacristia, quot fuerint Domi Sacerdotes, inscriptis singulorum nominibus, & addito uno, vel pluribus pro extraordinariis.
units.tr: 6. He shall have hanging in the sacristy as many towels as there are priests in the house, each inscribed with the name of its owner, with one or more added for extraordinary occasions.

units.la: 7. Dum Sacra fiunt, accendat, ut minimum, candelas duas, & cum sanctissimum Sacramentum elevatur, facem, aut cereum: quo tempore etiam tintinnabulum pulsetur: accendet etiam facem, cum aliis sanctissimum Sacramentum ministrabit; ipseque confessionem generalem eorum vice recitabit.
units.tr: 7. While the sacred rites are performed, he shall light at least two candles, and when the most holy Sacrament is elevated, a torch or a wax candle; at that time the bell is also to be rung. He shall also light the torch when he assists others in administering the most holy Sacrament, and he himself shall recite the general confession in their place.

units.la: 8. Curet, ut vinum, quod in Sacrificium paratur, sit bonum, & merum, ac mundum, eoque ipso die haustum: similiter & aqua, & ampullae sint munda, & decenter cooperta.
units.tr: 8. He shall see that the wine prepared for the sacrifice is good, unmixed and clean, and drawn on that same day; likewise the water and the cruets are to be clean and decently covered.

units.la: 9. Hostias faciat, quam fieri poterit, pulchras, eo numero, ut & Missis, & communionibus sufficiant.
units.tr: 9. He shall make the hosts as beautiful as possible, in such number that they suffice both for the Masses and for the communions.

units.la: 10. Ante Missas, & conciones, ac lectiones, pulsset campanam, prout sibi praescriptum erit. Det etiam signum salutationis B. Mariae in aurora, in meridie, & vesperi: det etiam signum, cum primum quis ex nostris vita functus fuerit: ut omnes, pro cujusque devotione illius animam Deo commendent.
units.tr: 10. Before Masses, sermons and lessons, he shall ring the bell as prescribed for him. He shall also give the signal for the salutation of the Blessed Virgin Mary at dawn, at midday and in the evening. He shall also give the signal as soon as any one of ours has departed this life, so that everyone, according to his devotion, may commend that soul to God.

units.la: 11. Si quando propter universalem aliquam causam in reliquis Ecclesiis campanae pulsentur, ipse etiam juxta Superioris praescriptum pulsabit.
units.tr: 11. If on account of some general cause the bells are rung in the other churches, he shall also ring them according to the Superior's prescription.

units.la: 12. Pridie quam fit habenda concio, disponat scamna in templo, juxta solitum morem.
units.tr: 12. On the day before a sermon is to be held, he shall arrange the benches in the church according to the customary practice.

units.la: 13. Det operam, ut nullo modo lumen desit ante sanctissimum Sacramentum, neque interdiu, neque noctu.
units.tr: 13. He shall take care that a light is never lacking before the most holy Sacrament, neither by day nor by night.

units.la: 14. Ex iis Sacerdotibus, quos habet a Superiore designatos, vocet diligenter ad templum qui nominatim petuntur ad confessiones audiendas: quod si nominatim non petuntur ad confessiones audiendas, eos juxta ordinem sibi praescriptum accersat, & quantum in ipso est, det operam, ut omnibus, qui confiteri volunt, satisfiat.
units.tr: 14. From among the priests whom he has as designated by the Superior, let him diligently summon to the church those who are specifically requested to hear confessions; but if they are not specifically requested to hear confessions, let him call them according to the order prescribed for him, and, as far as lies in him, take pains that all who wish to confess are satisfied.

units.la: 15. Si qui Missas, aut orationes petant, ad Praefectum recurrat, vel ad eum illos remittat.
units.tr: 15. If any ask for Masses or prayers, let him refer them to the Prefect, or send them back to him.

units.la: 16. Si quis aliquid quaereret, in quo eia Janitore melius satisfieret, eum ad portam domus remittat, & eos etiam, qui per portam, qua a templo in domum patet aditus, ingredi vellent, nisi viri essent ejusmodi, ut eorum peculiaris esset habenda ratio, prout a Superiore fuerit instructus: nunquam autem porta ea aperta relinquatur.
units.tr: 16. If anyone asks something which could be better answered by the porter, let him send him to the gate of the house; and let him also (send back) those who wish to enter by the gate through which there is access from the church into the house, unless they are men of such a kind that special consideration must be taken of them, as he has been instructed by the Superior. The gate, however, must never be left open.

units.la: 17. Curet, ut nunquam illic aqua desit, ubi lavantur manus: & sint lintea convenientia munda pro Sacerdotibus, ad manus solas ante, & post Sacrum extergendas.
units.tr: 17. He shall see that water is never lacking where the hands are washed, and that there are suitable clean linen cloths for the priests, to dry the hands only, before and after the Sacrifice.

units.la: 18. Provideat, ut aqua benedicta in pila non desit.
units.tr: 18. He shall provide that holy water is not lacking in the font.

units.la: 19. Si quando eleemosynae Missarum, vel Confessionum gratia offeruntur, eas non admittat: si quid tamen alioqui in Altaribus, aut alias templi locis repererit, aut in usum templi oblatum fuerit, id Praefecto tradet.
units.tr: 19. If alms are offered on account of Masses or confessions, he shall not accept them; but if he finds anything otherwise on the altars or in other places of the church, or if something is offered for the use of the church, he shall hand it over to the Prefect.

units.la: 20. Templi portas mane, sed non ante auroram aperiat: easdemque vesperi circa solis occasum diligenter observet: quod etiam faciet circa meridiem, nisi Superior in casu aliquo secus faciendum judicaret: & quotidie noctu claves Ecclesiae ad Superiorem deferat.
units.tr: 20. He shall open the doors of the church in the morning, but not before dawn; and he shall diligently watch over them in the evening about sunset. He shall also do this about midday, unless the Superior judges that in some case it should be done otherwise; and every night he shall carry the keys of the church to the Superior.

units.la: 21. Quamdiu templum erit apertum, diligenter curet, ne unquam sine custode relinquatur, sed semper, aut ipse, aut alius in eo sit, vel in sacristia, itaut & videre templum & custodire possit.
units.tr: 21. As long as the church is open, he shall take diligent care that it is never left without a guard, but that always either he himself or another is in it, or in the sacristy, so that he can both see the church and keep watch over it.

units.la: 22. Advertat, ne quis in templo deambulet, neve strepitus in eo audiatur: eos vero, qui loquuntur altius, modeste, ut decet, admonebit.
units.tr: 22. He shall take heed that no one walks about in the church, nor that any noise is heard in it; those who speak too loudly he shall admonish, modestly and as is fitting.

units.la: 23. Det operam diligenter, ut altaria sint munda, & bene praeparata, & pro ratione eorum ornata, atque ut vasa sacra, ornamenta, & cetera omnia, quae ad divinum cultum pertinent, in suis locis apte, & decenter reponantur, & conserventur.
units.tr: 23. He shall diligently take pains that the altars are clean and well prepared, and adorned according to their character, and that the sacred vessels, the ornaments and all the other things which pertain to divine worship are properly and decently put away and kept in their places.

units.la: 24. Videat, ut templum sit mundum, & bis singulis hebdomadis, ac saepius, si necesse sit, praesertim in festorum solemnium vigiliis, scopis mundetur: canes etiam ex templo abigat.
units.tr: 24. He shall see that the church is clean, and that it is swept twice each week, and more often if necessary, especially on the vigils of solemn feasts; he shall also drive dogs out of the church.

units.la: REGVLAE INFIRMARII.
units.tr: RULES OF THE INFIRMARIAN.

units.la: 1. Curam habeat infirmorum, quorum aegritudo simulatque ei indicata fuerit, si censeret rem esse alicuius momenti, Praefectum, & Superiorem admoneat.
units.tr: 1. He shall take care of the sick. As soon as he is told of an illness, if he judges it to be of some importance, he shall inform the Prefect and the Superior.

units.la: 2. Cum quis in morbum incidit, a Superiore intelligat, num statim Medicus vocandus sit, qui unus ordinarie esse debet, nisi ingravescente morbo, aut in quibusdam aliis casibus, alio Medico opus esse Superior judicaverit: & quoties Medicus aegrotos invisat, adsit ipse.
units.tr: 2. When someone falls ill, he shall learn from the Superior whether a doctor should be called at once. Ordinarily there should be only one doctor, unless the illness grows worse or in certain other cases the Superior judges that another doctor is needed. Whenever the doctor visits the sick, the Infirmarian himself shall be present.

units.la: 3. Studeat, ut quae aegrotanti danda sunt, & opportune emantur, & bona sint, & bene praeparata administrentur.
units.tr: 3. He shall see that what is to be given to the sick person is bought in good time, is good in quality, and is well prepared when it is served.

units.la: 4. Curet, ut aegrotorum cubicula sint valde munda: lecti concinne sternantur, & ramusculis, & huiusmodi aliis decumbentes oblectet.
units.tr: 4. He shall see that the sickrooms are very clean, that the beds are neatly made, and that he cheers those lying in them with small branches and similar things.

units.la: 5. Aegrotum consolari, & exhilarare studeat, non solum rebus a Medico probatis, sed verbis etiam spiritualibus, & latis, habeat etiam libros, quorum lectione aegroti recreari, & juvari in spiritu possint.
units.tr: 5. He shall take pains to console and cheer the sick, not only with remedies approved by the doctor but also with spiritual and edifying words. He shall also have books by whose reading the sick may be refreshed and helped in their spirit.

units.la: 6. Intelligat a Superiore, quos ex nostris ad aegrotos invisendos, ac recreandos accerire debeat: caveat autem, ne dum infirmis placere studet, aliquid fiat, quod eis nocere ulla ratione possit.
units.tr: 6. He shall learn from the Superior which of ours he should summon to visit and cheer the sick. He must take care, however, that in trying to please the sick he does nothing that could in any way harm them.

units.la: 7. Medicinalia, & cuncta, quae aegrotantium usui necessaria sunt, habere ipse debet, nisi Pharmacopola domi sit, & in loco convenienti ea custodire & saepius revisere, ut incorrupta conserventur: & quando opus fuerit, ut de novo suo tempore conficiantur, curare juxta ordinem Superioris.
units.tr: 7. He himself must keep medicines and everything else needed for the use of the sick, unless there is an apothecary in the house. He shall store them in a suitable place and inspect them often, so that they stay uncorrupted. When need arises, he shall see that they are prepared afresh at the proper time, according to the Superior's direction.

units.la: 8. Nihil omnino eorum, quae a Medico praescribentur, praetermittat, aut mutet: ordinem etiam observet temporum praefixorum, quibus prandium, coenam, syrupum, caeteraque medicamenta det, omnia scripto excipiens, quae Medicus praescripserit.
units.tr: 8. He shall omit or change nothing at all of what the doctor prescribes. He shall also observe the fixed times at which he gives lunch, supper, syrup and the other medicines, writing down everything the doctor has prescribed.

units.la: 9. Advertat, quo die quis coeperit aegrotare, & qua hora febres aegrotu & corripiant, & referant: tum ut Medicum, & Superiorem admoneat, tum ut cibum tempestive praebeat.
units.tr: 9. He shall note the day on which someone began to be ill, and the hour at which the fever seizes and grips the sick man and returns. He shall report this both to the doctor and to the Superior, and he shall provide food at the proper time.

units.la: 10. Si morbus sit contagiosus, supellex separari debet, ne cuiquam noceat.
units.tr: 10. If the illness is contagious, the furnishings must be kept apart so that they harm no one.

units.la: 11. Convalescentes e lecto surgere non permittat, priusquam id Medicus concesserit, & peram det: ut ea convalescentibus praebeantur, quae Medicus praescripserit, quoad Superioris satis visum fuerit.
units.tr: 11. He shall not allow convalescents to get up from bed until the doctor has permitted it. He shall give them the pera, so that the convalescents are provided with whatever the doctor has prescribed, for as long as the Superior thinks fit.

units.la: 12. Patienter & cum Charitate tum ipse, tum socii eius ferant molestias, & difficultates, quae interdum in curandis infirmis accidere solent. Quemadmodum autem diligenter curare debet, ne debita ministeria aegrotis desint, ita etiam animadvertere, ne nimiae vigiliae, immoderatique labores, aut morbi contagio vel propriae ipsius, vel sociorum saluti noceant.
units.tr: 12. He himself and his companions shall bear with patience and charity the troubles and difficulties that sometimes arise in caring for the sick. Just as he must take care diligently that the sick do not lack the services due to them, so he must also watch that excessive vigils, immoderate labours, or the contagion of the illness do not harm his own health or that of his companions.

units.la: 13. Cum gravitas morbi id postulaverit, Superiorem certiorem reddat, ut aegrotus antequam judicii usu privetur, omnia Sacramenta accipiat: quod si aegrotus, diu licet, sine periculo decumbat, curet ut octavo quoque die pro more Societatis communicet: ne huiusmodi spirituali fructu, & consolatione privetur, nisi aliqua ratio judicio Superioris impediat.
units.tr: 13. When the gravity of the illness requires it, he shall inform the Superior, so that the sick man may receive all the Sacraments before he loses the use of his judgment. If the sick man lies ill for a long time without danger, he shall see that on every eighth day he receives Communion in the manner of the Society, so that he is not deprived of such spiritual fruit and comfort, unless some reason, in the Superior's judgment, prevents it.

units.la: 14. Ingrauescente morbo Superiorem admoneat: ut orationibus omnium domesticorum valdè peculiaribus infirmum juvari faciat: idque eo magis, quo morti propinquiorem videret: & ut morienti quo plures poterunt ex nostris adsint, qui eum animo siorem reddant, ijsque auxilijs juvent, quæ eo tempore conveniunt, ac cum primùm vita functus fuerit, Ædituum admoneat.
units.tr: 14. When the illness grows worse, he shall inform the Superior, so that the sick man may be helped by the prayers of all in the household, especially those set apart for this purpose, and all the more so the nearer he sees death to be. And so that as many of ours as possible may be present for the dying man, to strengthen his spirit and to help him with those aids that suit that time, he shall tell the sacristan as soon as the man has departed this life.

units.la: 15. Prouideat, ut eorum corpora, qui ad meliorem vitam migrarint, ad sepulturam consueto regionis more præparentur, & ut spatio diei naturalis decenter teneantur, nisi ratio nemali odoris ante verti posse hoc tempus Superiori videretur.
units.tr: 15. He shall see that the bodies of those who have passed to a better life are prepared for burial in the customary manner of the region, and that they are kept decently for the space of a natural day, unless the Superior judges that the odour of the body requires this period to be shortened.

units.la: 16. Præfecto sanitatis obediat in omnibus, quæ ad hoc officium pertinent, qui si nullus fuerit constitutus, Præfecti munere ipse fungatur.
units.tr: 16. He shall obey the Prefect of health in all matters that pertain to this office. If no such Prefect has been appointed, he himself shall perform the duties of the Prefect.

units.la: REGVLAE IANITORIS.
units.tr: THE RULES OF THE PORTER.

units.la: 1. Nomina omnium domesticorum prope ostium domus in tabula scripta sint, ubi notis quibusdam illi designabuntur, qui egredientur: neminem vero foras exire permittat, qui facultatem à Superiore generalem aut particularem non habeat: & ab ijs, qui egrediuntur, quo eant, intelligat.
units.tr: 1. The names of all the household members shall be written on a board near the door of the house, with certain marks indicating those who go out. He shall allow no one to go outside who does not have permission from the Superior, general or particular, and he shall learn from those who go out where they are going.

units.la: 2. Nihil cuiquam nunciabit intempestiuè, ut cum in mensa sedetur, nisi aut res esset necessaria, aut persona mittentis conditio aliud exigeret.
units.tr: 2. He shall announce nothing to anyone at an unseasonable time, such as while people are seated at table, unless the matter is urgent or the rank of the sender requires otherwise.

units.la: 3. Literas omnes, & schedulas, quæ domesticis mittuntur, Superiori tradat: ij vero, a quos dabuntur, eas esse acceptas: ne intelligant: caveat etiam ne alicuius domestici literas aut quid simile externis det injussu Superioris.
units.tr: 3. He shall hand over to the Superior all letters and notes sent to members of the household. He shall take care not to give the letters of any member, or anything similar, to outsiders without the Superior's order, and he shall see that those to whom they are given have received them, so that they do not go astray.

units.la: 4. Cum aliqui ex Societate peregrè veniunt, januam ingressi dicat, ut illic expectent dum Superior de adventu eorum sit certior.
units.tr: 4. When some members of the Society arrive from abroad, he shall bid them enter the doorway and wait there until the Superior has been informed of their arrival.

units.la: 5. Festinet ad januam, cum tintinnabulum pulsari audit, & cum res patietur, per fenestellam venientes expediat: porta non aperta.
units.tr: 5. When he hears the bell rung, he shall hurry to the door and, as circumstances allow, deal with those who come through the little window, with the door not opened.

units.la: 6. Si quis ab externis quæratur, qui domi non sit, modestè intelligat, quis sit ille qui petit & quid velit, ut id redeunti, si opus sit, cum facultate Superioris significare possit.
units.tr: 6. If anyone from outside asks for someone who is not at home, he shall politely find out who the person is who is asking and what he wants, so that he can report this to the returning member, if necessary, with the Superior's permission.

units.la: 7. Talem cum omnibus conversandi modum teneat, ut discretione, modestia, & spiritualibus verbis singulos ædificatos, & contentos à se dimittere studeat.
units.tr: 7. He shall keep such a manner of dealing with everyone that he takes care to send each person away edified and content, by his discretion, modesty and spiritual words.

units.la: 8. Cum externi aliquem e nostris alloqui volent, Superiorem adibit, qui si ad id facultatem dederit, diligenter eum, qui petitur, quæret; & ad locum colloquijs destinatum, eo remittet.
units.tr: 8. When outsiders wish to speak with one of ours, he shall go to the Superior, who, if he gives permission for this, shall have the person sought carefully looked for, and send him to the place set aside for conversations.

units.la: 9. De eleemosynis, quæ ad januam mittentur, Superioris mentem intelligat, illiusq; ordinem sequatur, & si alicuius momenti sint, Procuratorem certiorem faciat.
units.tr: 9. He shall understand the Superior's wishes concerning the alms that are sent to the door, follow his order in this, and, if the gifts are of some importance, inform the Procurator.

units.la: 10. Si quando Prælati, aut Magnates domum intrarint, curet si commodè possit, ut Sacerdos aliquis eos comitetur, dum Superiorem ipse accerset.
units.tr: 10. If prelates or nobles ever enter the house, he shall see, if he conveniently can, that some priest accompanies them while he himself fetches the Superior.

units.la: 11. Cum pauperes eleemosynæ causa ad januam accedunt, benignè respondeat, & sedulo quærat, quidnam eis erogari possit, juxta Superioris arbitrium, idq; illis cum charitate distribuat.
units.tr: 11. When poor people come to the door seeking alms, he shall answer them kindly, carefully ask what may be given to them according to the Superior's judgment, and distribute it to them with charity.

units.la: 12. Mulieres, si quando ad ostium accedunt, paucis verbis dimittat, aut si pluribus opus esse videretur, in Ecclesiam eas mittat ad Ædit​uum, ubi responderi ipsis poterit.
units.tr: 12. If women ever come to the door, he shall dismiss them with a few words; or, if it seems that more must be done, he shall send them into the church to the sacristan, where they can be answered.

units.la: 13. Obserata semper janua sit, clavisq; in porta ne relinquatur: loca etiam porta vicina munda servet, & ut juxta januam omnes summisså voce loquantur, curet.
units.tr: 13. The door shall always be kept locked, and the key shall not be left in the door. He shall also keep the places near the door clean, and see that everyone speaks in a low voice near the door.

units.la: 14. Portas domus ante noctem claudat: exinde verò eas nullius causa aperiat, nisi de Præpositi vel Rectoris expressa licentia: & antequam cubitum eat, claves eidem tradens, si quis foris maneat, illi renunciabit.
units.tr: 14. He shall close the doors of the house before night; after that he shall open them for no reason except by express permission of the Provost or Rector. And before he goes to bed, he shall hand the keys to the same person, and tell him if anyone remains outside.

units.la: 15. Nihil custodiendum à quoquam externo recipiat, absq; Superioris jussu.
units.tr: 15. He shall receive nothing to be kept from any outsider without the Superior's order.

units.la: 16. Quoties Medicus domum ingredietur, signum dabit campana, ut Minister, & cæteri qui debent adesse possint.
units.tr: 16. Whenever the physician enters the house, the bell shall give the signal, so that the minister and the others who ought to be present may be able to attend.

units.la: 17. I... 17. In Collegijs, in quibus Scholæ externis aperiuntur, signum campana dabit pro initio lectionum, ac fine: & Gymnasia statis temporibus aperiet, atque claudet, nisi horum cura alijs demandetur.
units.tr: I... 17. In the colleges in which schools are opened to outsiders, the bell shall give the signal for the beginning and end of the lessons; and he shall open and close the gymnasia at set times, unless the care of these is entrusted to others.

units.la: REGVLAE CVSTODIS VESTIVM.
units.tr: RULES OF THE KEEPER OF THE CLOTHES.

units.la: 1. Servare debet omnem supellectilem, sive lineam, sive laneam, & quicquid ad indumenta, & ubi opus fuerit, etiam ad calceamenta attinet: quae diligenti cura, ut rem pauperum Christi, custodiet.
units.tr: 1. He must keep all the household linen, both linen and woollen, and whatever pertains to clothing and, where needed, to footwear as well; he shall guard these with careful diligence, as the property of the poor of Christ.

units.la: 2. Inventarium rerum, quas ipse custodit, si alicuius momenti sint, in libro habeat, & seorsum scribat, quae de novo fiant, addito die, mense, & anno, ut cum a Superiore jubebitur, possit sui muneris rationem reddere.
units.tr: 2. If the things he keeps are of any significance, he shall have an inventory of them in a book, and shall write separately what is newly acquired, adding the day, month and year, so that when the Superior orders it, he may be able to give an account of his office.

units.la: 3. Vestes ordine dispositas servet, & novas, & integras a vetustioribus sejungat, & ne corrumpatur, videat: eas etiam aptandas, & resarciendas curet, ut decet religiosam paupertatem: quas vero non amplius usui nostrorum futuras judicabit, eas Superiori ostendat, ut ille, quid de eis faciendum sit, statuat.
units.tr: 3. He shall keep the garments arranged in order, and separate the new and intact from the older ones, and see that they are not spoiled; he shall also take care that they are mended and repaired, as befits religious poverty. Those which he judges will no longer be of use to our people he shall show to the Superior, so that he may decide what is to be done with them.

units.la: 4. Quae singuli Novitij domum attulerunt, ea alicubi separatim asservabit, inscripto nomine eius qui attulit: donec biennio expleto consueta vota Societatis emittat.
units.tr: 4. He shall keep in some place apart whatever items each novice has brought into the house, with the name of the one who brought them written on them, until after two years have been completed and they take the customary vows of the Society.

units.la: 5. Singulis mensibus omnia domus vestitabit cubicula: ut ex Superioris arbitrio, si quid eis desit, suppleri possit: si quid etiam superfluum inveneri t, in vestiaria officina custodiatur.
units.tr: 5. Every month he shall visit all the bedrooms of the house, so that, at the Superior's discretion, whatever they lack may be supplied; and if anything superfluous is found, it shall be kept in the clothing store.

units.la: 6. Inspiciat etiam quinam vestibus indigeant, ut Superiori dicat, eiusq; ordinem exequatur, eo vero inconsulto nihil cuiquam dabit. Coadjutores autem temporales fottanis dimidio palmo brevioribus, quam Sacerdotes, & pallio fottanis breviori utantur.
units.tr: 6. He shall also examine who needs clothes, so that he may tell the Superior and carry out his directions; but without consulting him he shall give nothing to anyone. The lay coadjutors shall wear cassocks half a palm shorter than the priests', and a cloak shorter than the cassock.

units.la: 7. Lineipanni lotori, sive externus ille sit, sive domesticus, scripto numero dentur, & accipiantur.
units.tr: 7. Linen for the laundry, whether from outside or from the house, shall be given and received by a written number.

units.la: 8. Subuculae singulorum, quae statura induentium convenire debent, signis particularibus internoscantur, ne permisceri contingat.
units.tr: 8. The undershirts of each person, which ought to fit the stature of the one wearing them, shall be distinguished by particular marks, lest they happen to be mixed up.

units.la: 9. Pannos lineos omnes, quos utendos Refectorij Præfecto, Coquo, alijsq; ministris dividet, numerato det, & recipiat.
units.tr: 9. All the linen cloths which he distributes to the prefect of the refectory, the cook and the other servants for use, he shall give and receive by count.

units.la: 10. Sabbathi vespere linea munda per omnia cubicula distribuat: Dominica vero die mane ex ijsdem cubiculis immunda colligat: & an omnia, quae dederat, recipiat, animadvertat.
units.tr: 10. On Saturday evening he shall distribute clean linen through all the bedrooms; on Sunday morning, however, he shall collect the soiled linen from the same bedrooms, and take note whether he receives everything he had given out.

units.la: 11. Aestivo tempore linteamina munda pro lectis decimoquinto quoq; die: hyberno vero post tres hebdomadas distribuat, ubi id fieri poterit.
units.tr: 11. In summer he shall distribute clean bed linen every fifteenth day, but in winter after three weeks, where this can be done.

units.la: 12. Haec omnia custos vestium præstabit, nisi eius officium in magno aliquo Collegio, aut Domo in plures personas distribuere necesse sit.
units.tr: 12. The keeper of the clothes shall perform all these duties, unless in some large college or house it is necessary to distribute his office among several persons.

units.la: REGVLAE EMPTORIS.
units.tr: THE RULES OF THE BUYER.

units.la: 1. Diligens sit in emendis ijs, quae ad quotidianum usum Superioris arbitrio, domum comportanda sunt, eaque tempestive Dispensatori tradat: emat autem res bonas, & quam commodissimo pretio poterit, licet longius sint petendae.
units.tr: 1. He shall be careful in buying those things which must be brought into the house for the daily use of the Superior, at his discretion, and shall hand them over to the Steward in good time. He shall buy goods of good quality, at the lowest price he can obtain, even if they must be sought from further away.

units.la: 2. Adnotet pecuniae summam, quam a Procuratore in dies accipiet, & quas in res eam expendet: & rationem eiquotidie reddat dati, & accepti: quid autem sequenti die empturus sit, a Ministro intelliget.
units.tr: 2. He shall note the sum of money which he receives each day from the Procurator, and the items on which he spends it, and shall render an account each day of what has been given and received. He shall learn from the Minister what he is to buy on the following day.

units.la: 3. Curet quantum poterit, eos quibuscum aget discretione, ac modestia aedificare: & quatenus eius officium decet, religiosis verbis in spiritu juvare.
units.tr: 3. He shall take care, as far as he can, to edify those with whom he deals by discretion and modesty, and, so far as his office befits, to help them with pious words in the Spirit.

units.la: REGVLÆ REGVLAE DISPENSATORIS.
units.tr: Rules of the Steward (Dispensator)

units.la: IN rebus distribuendis ordinem Superioris sequatur, & quamvis communiter aequalitatem inter omnes servare debet: habeat tamen infirmorum, & convalescentium rationem, prout ei fuerit praescriptum.
units.tr: In distributing things he shall follow the order of the Superior; and although he ought generally to keep equality among all, he shall nevertheless take account of the sick and of those recovering, as it has been prescribed to him.

units.la: 2. Vinum in mensa ponendum aqua temperabit, ubi, & quantum Superiori videbitur.
units.tr: 2. He shall dilute the wine to be placed on the table with water, where and how much the Superior thinks fit.

units.la: 3. Quae ex mensis superfuerint, diligenter conservabit, memor pauperta-tis, ut & domesticis, & externis pauperibus juxta ordinem Superioris, usui esse possint.
units.tr: 3. He shall carefully keep whatever is left over from the tables, mindful of poverty, so that it may be of use both to the members of the household and to the outside poor, according to the Superior's order.

units.la: 4. Curam habeat conservandi res ad victum necessarias, quae ipsi committentur, claudat, safeque custodiat, advertens ne corrumpantur: quod si corruptionis sit periculum, Superiorem admoneat. Ut autem haec melius observet, visitet saepe Penum, & alia loca, ubi illa reconduntur.
units.tr: 4. He shall take care to preserve the provisions necessary for food which are committed to him; he shall lock them up and guard them safely, taking heed that they do not spoil. If there is danger of spoiling, he shall warn the Superior. In order to observe these things better, he shall often visit the pantry and the other places where those things are stored.

units.la: 5. Tam Penum, quam reliqua omnia, quae in eo sunt, munda habeat.
units.tr: 5. He shall keep the pantry, and all the other things that are in it, clean.

units.la: 6. Antequam penitus absumantur cibi, qui domi reconduntur, Superiorem admoneat, ut alij coemi tempestive possint.
units.tr: 6. Before the foods stored at home are entirely used up, he shall warn the Superior, so that others may be bought in good time.

units.la: 7. Curet concinnanda dolia, & purganda cum opus est, ad novum vinum infundendum, cuius rei, cum tempus impendet, Superiorem admonebit.
units.tr: 7. He shall see to it that casks are prepared, and cleaned when necessary, for pouring in the new wine; he shall give warning of this matter when the time draws near.

units.la: REGVLÆ PRAEFECTI RE- FECTORII.
units.tr: RULES OF THE PREFECT OF THE REFECTORY.

units.la: Vt refectorium, & quae eius usibus serviunt, omnia esse quam mundissima.
units.tr: He shall see that the refectory and whatever serves its use are all kept as clean as possible.

units.la: 2. Ne aqua manibus abluendis, aut mantilia extergendis desint, advertat: horum autem (quae bis in hebdomada saltem mutabuntur) alia Sacerdotibus, alia non Sacerdotibus destinata erunt.
units.tr: 2. He shall take care that there is water for washing hands and towels for drying them. Of these towels, which are to be changed at least twice a week, some shall be set aside for the priests and others for those who are not priests.

units.la: 3. Mantilia singulis saltem hebdomadis semel, mappa vero, quae singulis singula serviunt, bis munda ponentur: omnia autem lintea numerato & accipiat, & reddat.
units.tr: 3. Towels shall be put out clean at least once a week, and napkins, which serve each person individually, twice. He shall receive and return all the linen by count.

units.la: 4. Curet, ne vasa, & caetera in refectorio necessaria desint, & ut quam maxime munda sint: cultellos autem frequenter acuere faciat.
units.tr: 4. He shall see that the vessels and other things needed in the refectory are not lacking, and that they are kept as clean as possible. He shall also have the knives sharpened often.

units.la: 5. Parvam mensam paratam habeat.
units.tr: 5. He shall keep a small table ready.

units.la: 6. Signum campana temporibus suis dabit convenienti ad primam, & secundam mensam: sed ante primum pulsum (qui quarta parte horae secundum praecedat) a Coquo intelligat, an finit omnia parata.
units.tr: 6. The bell shall be rung at the proper times for the first and second tables. But before the first stroke (which shall come a quarter of an hour earlier), he shall learn from the cook whether everything is ready.

units.la: 7. Mensae rebus necessariis paratae esse debent, cum campana signum primo dabitur: quae autem ad potum pertinent, circa secundum signum apponantur: & aquae, ac vini vasa supra orbes collocentur.
units.tr: 7. The tables should be set with what is necessary when the bell is first rung. Drinks should be put out about the second signal, and the water and wine vessels placed on the trays.

units.la: 8. Sit certus locus iis, qui curae Infirmarij subsunt, quibus nihil, nisi quod ab eo praescriptum erit, apponat: servet autem cum omnibus aequalitatem, nisi secus necessitatis causa esset a Superiore monitus, sine cuius arbitrio, neque jentaculum, neque aliud quicquam ulli concedet.
units.tr: 8. Those under the care of the infirmarian shall have a fixed place, and he shall serve them only what the infirmarian has prescribed. He shall keep equality among all, unless the Superior has advised otherwise because of need; without the Superior's judgement he shall grant no one breakfast or anything else.

units.la: 9. Priusquam e mensa surgatur, inferantur orbes aliquot in mensam, ut quisque locum suum mundet: quam primum vero pro secunda praeparata omnia habuerit, signum tampana[?] dabit: providebit, ne desint, qui ministrare debent.
units.tr: 9. Before the tables are cleared, some dishes shall be brought in so that each may clean his place. As soon as he has everything ready for the second table, he shall give the bell signal. He shall see that those who have to serve are not missing.

units.la: 10. Quae ex mensis superfuerint, colliget, atque illi trades, ad quem id ex officio pertinet: sive Coquus is, sive Dispensator sit.
units.tr: 10. He shall gather up what is left on the tables and hand it over to the person whose duty it is, whether that is the cook or the steward.

units.la: 11. Nomina eorum, qui domi tam in refectorio, quam extra vescuntur, in quadam tabula habeat, & eos qui cibum ceperint, notabit: ut intelligat, quinam supersint, & Coquum, qui portiones distribuit, commonefaciet. 12. Mensis expeditis mantilia plicentur, verraturque refectorium: & si quis inter comedendum silentium non servaverit, aut aliquid minus modestum fecerit, ipse Superior significabit.
units.tr: 11. He shall have in a certain register the names of those who eat at home as well as in the refectory, and of those outside, and shall mark those who have taken food, so that he knows who is missing, and he shall remind the cook who distributes the portions. 12. When the tables are cleared, the napkins shall be folded and the refectory swept. If anyone has not kept silence while eating, or has done anything less becoming, the Superior himself shall be informed.

units.la: 13. Habeat a Ministro catalogum, in quo scriptum sit, quinam, & quibus diebus in prima, & secunda mensa ministraturi sint, eumque ordinem servet. Intelligat etiam Sabbatho, quinam per hebdomadam sequentem in refectorio legere debeant: eosque faciat seriores.
units.tr: 13. He shall have from the minister a list stating who is to serve at the first and second tables, and on which days, and he shall keep to that order. On Saturday he shall also learn who is to read in the refectory during the following week, and shall make them the later readers.

units.la: 14. Catalogum habeat rerum, quae in refectorio serviunt: ut cum ratio ab eo requiritur, in promptu sit, & in loco ad id designato eas custodiat.
units.tr: 14. He shall keep a list of the things used in the refectory, so that when an account is required of him it is ready to hand, and he shall keep them in the place assigned for them.

units.la: 15. Ad finem recreationis, quae una hora post primam mensam, altera post secundam a randio, & cena durare debet, distincta signa campana dabit.
units.tr: 15. At the end of the recreation, which ought to last one hour after the first table and another after the second, that is, after lunch and supper, he shall give the bell signals at distinct intervals.

units.la: REGVLAE COQVI.
units.tr: THE RULES OF THE COOK.

units.la: 1. IN iis omnibus, quae ad suum munus pertinent, munditiam servet ipse, & ab aliis servandam curet, detque operam, ut omnia recte, & opportune parentur, ea praesertim, quae ad aegrotos pertinent.
units.tr: 1. In all those matters which pertain to his office, let him keep cleanliness himself, and see to it that others keep it too; and let him take care that everything is prepared properly and at the right time, especially those things which pertain to the sick.

units.la: 2. Carnes, piscesque, & alia, quae ad mensam portanda sunt, dum secat, & distribuit, distributis minime contrectet, sed fuscinula, aut cultello ad eam remutatur.
units.tr: 2. Meats, fish, and other things which are to be brought to the table: while he carves and distributes them, let him by no means touch the portions once they are distributed, but turn them over with a fork or a knife.

units.la: 3. Semihora, aut saltem quarta hora parte, antequam in mensa sit sedendum, praeparati cibi omnes esse debent.
units.tr: 3. Half an hour, or at least a quarter of an hour, before the community is to sit down at table, all the prepared food ought to be ready.

units.la: 4. Circa qualitatem, & quantitatem portionum ordinem a Superiore datum sequetur.
units.tr: 4. He shall follow the order given by the Superior concerning the quality and quantity of the portions.

units.la: 5. Coquere, aut aliud quidpiam pro aliquo particulari parare, Infirmario tantum excepto, neminem sinet, neque ipse faciet sine Superioris facultate.
units.tr: 5. He shall not allow anyone to cook, or to prepare anything separately for any individual, except for the infirmary; nor shall he himself do so without the permission of the Superior.

units.la: 6. Scriptum in codice habeat catalogum rerum, quarum est usus in coquina, quas ipse servare debet.
units.tr: 6. Let him have in a written book a catalogue of the things used in the kitchen, which he himself ought to keep.

units.la: 7. Diligenter advertat, ne plura quam necessaria sint, ligna comburantur. Hanc similiter diligentiam in rebus, quas consumit, adhibebit, ne quid non necessarium insumatur: ut religiosam paupertatem decet.
units.tr: 7. Let him take care diligently that no more wood is burned than is necessary. He shall likewise apply this diligence to the things he uses up, so that nothing unnecessary is consumed, as befits religious poverty.

units.la: 8. Quae ex mensa supersunt, aliquo traduntur, conservabit, memor paupertatis: ut & domesticis, & externis pauperibus usui esse possint, juxta ordinem Superioris.
units.tr: 8. Whatever is left over from the table he shall keep set aside, mindful of poverty, so that they may be of use both to the members of the household and to outside poor, according to the Superior's order.

units.la: 9. Si quem haberet adjutorem, curet, ut eum verbo, & exemplo suo adificet, praesertim Novitios.
units.tr: 9. If he has any helper, let him see to it that he edifies him by word and by his own example, especially the novices.

units.la: REGVLAE EXCITATORIS.
units.tr: THE RULES OF THE WAKER

units.la: 1. MEdia saltem hora parte ante caeteros cubitum erat, eodemque temporis spatio ante alios mane surgat, & hora constituta campanam pulsset, statimque ad omnia cubicula lumen deferens, cunctos excitet: quo ut certius, & melius praestare possit, horologium excitatorium a Superiore habeat.
units.tr: 1. He is to go to bed at least half an hour after the others, and he is to rise at the same interval before the rest in the morning. When the bell has been rung at the appointed hour, he is to carry a light straight to every cell and wake everyone. So that he can do this more surely and better, he should have an alarm clock supplied by the Superior.

units.la: 2. Quarta hora parte ab excitatione elapsa, cubicula rursus invisei, ac si quos nondum surrexisse comperiat, Superiori nunciet.
units.tr: 2. When a quarter of an hour has passed since the waking, he is to visit the cells again and report to the Superior any whom he finds have not yet got up.

units.la: 3. Post aliam quartam horae partem ad orationem pulsabit, ita ut ab excitatione ad orationis usque initium, semihora intercedat: absoluto vero tempore orationi deputato, finis signum dabit.
units.tr: 3. After another quarter of an hour he will ring for prayer, so that half an hour lies between the waking and the beginning of prayer. When the time allotted to prayer has run out, he will give the signal for its end.

units.la: 4. Si quorum opera indigebit propter multitudinem eorum, quos excitare, aut visitare debet, eos a Superiore petet, quos servare eosdem regulas curabit: si qui autem debiles, aut valetudinarii erunt, eos juxta ordinem Superioris excitabit.
units.tr: 4. If, because of the number of those whom he has to wake or visit, he needs help, he is to ask the Superior for men who will keep the same rules; and if there are any who are infirm or sickly, he is to wake them in the order the Superior prescribes.

units.la: 5. Si quem videret communem illam regulam minus observantem, qua omnes decenter cooperti dormire jubentur, Superiorem monebit.
units.tr: 5. If he sees anyone not keeping that common rule by which everyone is ordered to sleep decently covered, he is to warn the Superior.

units.la: REGVLÆ NOCTV CVBICVLA VISITANTIS.
units.tr: Rules for the Visitor of the Bedrooms at Night.

units.la: HOra à Superiore præscripta ad nocturnum conscientiæ examen pulsabit, transfactoque quadrante signum dabit ad cubandum.
units.tr: At the hour prescribed by the Superior, he shall ring the bell for the nightly examination of conscience, and when a quarter of an hour has passed, he shall give the signal to go to bed.

units.la: 2. Elapsa quarta horæ parte à cubandi signo, singula cubicula adibit, & an omnes ad lectum se receperint, ac lucernas extinxerint, videbit: si quos invenerit extra lectum, aut qui lucernas non extinxerint, Superiori renunciabit.
units.tr: 2. When a quarter of an hour has elapsed since the signal to retire, he shall go to each bedroom and see whether everyone has gone to bed and put out the lamps. If he finds anyone out of bed, or anyone who has not put out his lamp, he shall report it to the Superior.

units.la: DE OBEDIENTIAE VIRTV- TE, EPISTOLA N.P. IGNATII.
units.tr: On the Virtue of Obedience, a Letter of Our Father Ignatius.

units.la: IGNATIVS LOYOLA FRATRIBVS SOCIETATIS Iesu, qui sunt in Lusitania, gratiam, & amorem Christi Domini sempiternam.
units.tr: Ignatius Loyola to the brethren of the Society of Jesus who are in Portugal: everlasting grace and love of Christ the Lord.

units.la: Magnam animi voluptatem capio, fratres in Christo carissimi, cum asseritur ad me, quam acri studio conatuque ad summam virtutis, ac divini obsequij perfectionem enitamini, beneficio illius, qui vos, ut ad hoc vitæ institutum vocavit, sic in eodem proposito sua clementia retinet, dirigitque ad beatum finem, ad quem, qui sunt ab ipso electi, perveniunt.
units.tr: Dearest brethren in Christ, I take great joy in hearing how eagerly and zealously you strive after the highest virtue and the perfection of divine service. This is the work of his kindness who called you to this way of life and keeps you in the same purpose, guiding you to that blessed end which all whom he has chosen reach.

units.la: Atque ego sane, cum vos omnibus donis ornamentisque spiritualibus perfectos, tum vero (quod alias ex me cognovistis) in primis Obedientiæ virtute præstantissimos esse cupio, idque non solum ob eximia quædam, ac singularia eius bona, quæ tot, tamque illustribus sacrarum literarum testimoniis, atque exemplis in testamento aque novo, ac veteri comprobantur: sed etiam quod (ut est apud S. Gregorium) Obedientia sola virtus est, quæ virtutes cæteras menti infert, infertasque custodit. Hæc dum floruerit, florebunt proculdubio reliquæ: edentque fructus, quales & ego in animis vestris exopto, & suo jure postulatis, qui humanum genus neglectæ Obedientiæ scelere afflictum ac perditum, salutari ipsemet Obedientia reparavit, Factus obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem Crucis.
units.tr: Indeed, I desire that you be perfected in every gift and spiritual adornment, and above all (as you have known from me on other occasions) that you be outstanding in the virtue of obedience. This is not only because of its remarkable and singular benefits, which are confirmed by so many and such illustrious testimonies and examples of Sacred Scripture in both the New and the Old Testament, but also because (as St Gregory says) obedience is the only virtue that brings the other virtues into the mind and keeps them there once brought in. While it flourishes, the rest will undoubtedly flourish too, and they will bear such fruit as I also wish for in your hearts. You rightly claim this, since it was by obedience itself that the human race, afflicted and lost through the crime of neglected obedience, was restored to health: "made obedient unto death, even the death of the cross."

units.la: Ab aliis religiosis ordinibus facilius patiamur superari nos jejunijs, vigilijs, & caeteris victus cultusque asperitate, quam suo quique ritu, ac disciplina sancte suscipiunt: vera quidem, ac perfecta Obedientia, abdicationeque voluntatis atque judicij maxime velim, fratres charissimi, esse conspicuos, quicunque in hac Societate Deo Domino nostro deserviunt, eiusdemque Societatis veram, germanamque sobolem hac quasi nota distingui, qui numquam intueantur personam ipsam, cui obediunt, sed in ea Christum Dominum, cuius causa obediunt. Siquidem Superiori, nec si prudentia, bonitate, cæterisve quibuslibet divinis donis ornatus, instructusque sit, propterea obtemperandum est: sed ob id solum, quod vices gerat Dei eiusdemque auctoritate fungatur, qui dicit: Qui vos audit, me audit, & qui vos spernit, me spernit: nec contra sive consilio, aut prudentia minus valeat, quidquam idcirco de Obedientia remittendum, quatenus ille Superior est: quando illius personam refert, cuius sapientia falli non potest, supplebitque ipse, quicquid ministro defuerit sive probitate, aliisque ornamentis caret: siquidem diserte verbis Christus Dominus cum dixisset: Super Cathedram Moysi sederunt Scribae, & Pharisaei, protinus addidit, Omnia ergo, quæcunque dixerint vobis servate, & facite: secundum opera vero eorum nolite facere. Quocirca sedulò vos in eam curam, atque exercitationem incumbere cupio, ut Christum Dominum in Superiore quolibet agnoscere studeatis, in eoque divinæ Majestati reverentiam, atque Obedientiam summa cum religione præstare. Quod vobis minùs mirum videbitur, si animad verteritis præceptum esse ab Apostolo, ut Superioribus etiam secularibus, ethnicisque pareamus, ut Christo: ex quo omnis potestas bene instituta descendit: sic enim ille ad Ephesios, Obedite Dominis carnalibus cum timore, & tremore in simplicitate cordis vestri, sicut Christo: non ad oculum servientes, quasi hominibus placentes, sed ut servi Christi facientes voluntatem Dei ex animo, cum bona voluntate servientes sicut Domino, & non hominibus. Atque hinc existimare poteritis ipsi, cum sit religiosus quispiam regendum, ac moderandum alteri traditus, non solùm ut Superiori, sed etiam nominatim ut Christi partes agenti: quo illum loco apud animum suum habere, utrum ut hominem an ut Christi vicarium debeat intueri.
units.tr: We may more readily accept being surpassed by other religious orders in fasting, vigils and the other hardships of diet and dress than in the holy discipline and rule that each of them observes. I most earnestly wish, dearest brethren, that all who serve God our Lord in this Society be distinguished by true and perfect obedience and by the surrender of will and judgment. Let them be marked by this as the true and genuine offspring of this Society: they never look at the person to whom they obey, but at Christ the Lord in that person, for whose sake they obey. For a superior is not to be obeyed because he is endowed with prudence, goodness or any other divine gifts, but for this alone: that he takes the place of God and exercises God's authority, who says, "He who hears you hears me, and he who despises you despises me." Nor, on the other hand, should anything be withdrawn from obedience because a superior has less counsel or prudence, insofar as he is a superior. For he bears the person of him whose wisdom cannot err, and he himself will make up for whatever the minister lacks in uprightness or other ornaments. Christ the Lord said plainly: "The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. Therefore whatever they tell you, keep and do; but do not do according to their works." Accordingly I want you to apply yourselves diligently to this care and exercise, so that you strive to recognise Christ the Lord in any superior whatever, and in him render reverence and obedience to the divine majesty with the utmost devotion. This will seem less strange to you if you consider that the Apostle commands us to obey even secular and heathen superiors as we obey Christ, from whom all rightly constituted power descends. So he writes to the Ephesians: "Obey your earthly masters with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as to Christ; not serving to the eye, as men-pleasers, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart, with good will serving as to the Lord and not to men." From this you may judge for yourselves that when a religious is handed over to be governed and directed by another, he must regard that superior not only as a superior but expressly as one who acts in the place of Christ. He must hold in his mind the question of whether he ought to look on him as a man or as the vicar of Christ.

units.la: Iam verò illud etiam vobis clarè compertum esse, ac in animis vestris penitus infidere vehementer cupio, infirmam, & valdè imperfectam esse primam illam Obedientiæ formam, quæ mandata duntaxat opere exequitur: nec virtutis nomine dignam, nisi ad alterum gradum ascendat, qui voluntatem Superioris suam efficit, & cum ea ita concordet, ut non solùm in effectu executio appareat, verùm etiam in affectu consensio: sicque idem velit uterque, idem nolit. Atque propterea in sacris literis legimus, Melior est Obedientia, quàm victimæ: siquidem (ut S. Gregorius docet) per victimas aliena caro, per Obedientiam verò voluntas propria mactatur: quæ quidem pars animi, quoniam est adeò præstans, sic fit, ut eius oblatio Domino, ac Creatori nostro per Obedientiam facta, magni fit æstimanda.
units.tr: Furthermore, I earnestly wish you to be clearly assured and to have deeply fixed in your minds that the first form of obedience, which carries out only the commands in deed, is weak and very imperfect. It does not deserve the name of virtue unless it rises to the second degree, which makes the superior's will its own and agrees with it so closely that there is agreement not only in the execution, which appears in the outward act, but also in the affection, so that both will the same thing and both refuse the same thing. Therefore we read in Holy Scripture: "Obedience is better than sacrifice." For, as St Gregory teaches, through sacrifices the flesh of another is slain, but through obedience one's own will is slain. Since this part of the soul is so excellent, its offering made to the Lord and our Creator through obedience must be held in great esteem.

units.la: Quanto in errore, quamque periculoso versantur, non dico solùm ij, qui in ijs, quæ ad carnem, & sanguinem pertinent, sed illi etiam, qui in rebus alioquin admodum sanctis, ac spiritalibus, ut jejunijs, precationibus, aliisve quibuscunque pietatis operibus, fas putat à præscripto Superioris, ac voluntate discedere. Audiant quod sapienter admonet Cassianus in Collatione Danielis Abbatis: Vnum sane, inquit, atque idem inobedientiæ genus est, vel propter operationis instantiam, vel propter otij desiderium, seniorís violare mandatum, tamque dispendiosum, est pro somno, quàm pro vigilantia Monasterij statuta convellere: tantum denique est Abbatis transfire præceptum, ut legas: quantum si cotemnas, ut dormias. Sancta fuit actio Marthæ, sancta contemplatio Magdalenæ, sancta pœnitentia & lacrymæ, quibus pedes Christi Domini rigabantur: sed hæc omnia nimirum oportuit fieri in Bethania, quàm vocem domum Obedientiæ interpretantur: ut ea re, quemadmodum ait S. Bernard. nobis significare voluisse Dominus videatur, nec studium bonæ actionis, nec otium sanctæ contemplationis, nec lacrymam pœnitentis extra Bethaniam illi accepta esse potuisse.
units.tr: I do not speak only of those who are in error and danger in matters that concern flesh and blood, but also of those who think it lawful to depart from the superior's command and wishes in things otherwise very holy and spiritual, such as fasting, prayers or any other works of piety. Let them hear what Cassian wisely warns in the Conference of Abbot Daniel: "There is indeed one and the same kind of disobedience, whether, because of the urgency of work or from desire for leisure, one violates the elder's command. It is just as harmful to overturn the monastery's rules for the sake of sleep as for the sake of vigilance. In short, to pass over the abbot's command in order to read is as bad as to despise it in order to sleep." The action of Martha was holy, the contemplation of Magdalene was holy, and so were the repentance and tears with which the feet of Christ the Lord were watered. Yet all these things had to be done in Bethany, which they interpret as the house of obedience. As St Bernard says, the Lord seems to have wished to signify by this that neither zeal for good action, nor leisure for holy contemplation, nor the tear of the penitent could have been acceptable to him outside Bethany.

units.la: Quocirca voluntates vestras, fratres charissimi, quoad eius fieri poterit, omninò deponite: libertatem conditori vestro, quam vobis ipsemet elargitus est, in eius ministris libere tradite, ac dicate. Nolite exiguum vestri liberi arbitrij fructum putare, quod liceat vobis illud, à quo id accepistis, eidem per Obedientiam plenè reddere. Quod cum facitis, nõ modò non perditis ipsum, verùm etiam augetis, atque perficitis, quippe qui vestras omnes voluntates certissima rectitudinis regula moderamini voluntate divina, quam videlicet interpretaturis, qui vobis Dei nomine præsidet.
units.tr: Therefore, dearest brethren, as far as it can be done, lay down your wills entirely. Freely hand over and dedicate the liberty which your Creator himself has bestowed on you to his ministers. Do not think it a small fruit of your free choice that you may give back to him from whom you received it, fully and through obedience. When you do this, you not only do not lose it but even increase and perfect it, since you govern all your wills by the most certain rule of rectitude, the divine will, which he who presides over you in God's name is to interpret for you.

units.la: Itaque diligenter illud etiam cavendum est, ne Superioris nllo umquam tempore voluntatem (quam ducere pro divina debetis) ad vestram detorquere nitamini: id enim esset non vestra divinæ conformare, sed divinà vestræ voluntatis norma regere velle, eiusdem divina sapientia ordinem invertentes. Sane quàm magnus est error, & quidem eorum quos amor sui obcæcavit, obedientes existimare sese, cum Superiore ad id, quod ipsimet volunt, aliqua ratione pertraxerint. Sanctum Bernardum in hac re præclarè exercitatum audite: Quisquis, inquit, vel aperte, vel occultè satagit, ut quod habet in voluntate hoc ei spiritualis pater injungat: ipse se seducit, si forte sibi quasi de Obedientia blandiatur: neque enim in ea re ipse Prælato, sed magis ei Prælatus obedit. Quæ cum ita sint, quisquis ad Obedientiæ virtutem velit pervenire, oportet ad hunc secundum Obedientiæ gra. dum ascendat, ut Superioris non solum jussa exequatur, sed etiam eius voluntatem suam faciat, seu potius suam exuat, ut divinam à Superiore expositam induat.
units.tr: Therefore also take diligent care never to strive to turn the superior's will (which you ought to hold as divine) toward your own. That would be to wish not to conform your will to the divine, but to govern the divine by the norm of your own will, thus inverting the order of his divine wisdom. Indeed, how great is the error of those whom self-love has blinded, who think themselves obedient because they have somehow drawn their superior to what they themselves want! Listen to St Bernard, who was well practised in this matter: "Whoever, openly or secretly, labours so that the spiritual father enjoins on him what he already has in his will, deceives himself if he flatters himself that this is obedience; for in such a case he does not obey the prelate, but rather the prelate obeys him." Since this is so, whoever wishes to attain the virtue of obedience must rise to this second degree of obedience, so that he not only carries out the superior's orders but also makes the superior's will his own, or rather puts off his own will in order to put on the divine will as set forth by the superior.

units.la: Qui vero se totum penitus immolare vult Deo, praeter voluntatem, intelligentiam quoque, qui tertius & summus est gradus Obedientiæ, offerat necesse est, ut non solum idem velit, sed etiam ut idem sentiat, quod Superior, eiusque judicio subijciat suum, quoad potest devota voluntas intelligentiam inflectere. Quæ vis animi tametsi non ea, qua voluntas pollet, libertate prædita est, atque ipsa natura fertur eius assensus in id quod sibi veri speciem præbet: tamen multis in rebus, in quibus videlicet cognita veritatis evidentia vim illi non infert, potest voluntatis pondere in hanc potius quam in illam partem inclinari. Quæ res cum incidunt, debet quisquis obedientiam profitetur, inclinare sese in sententiam Superioris. Etenim cum Obedientia sit quoddam holocaustum, quo totus homo sine ulla prorsus imminutione Conditori suo, ac Domino per manus ministrorum in charitatis igne immolatur: cumque sit eadem renunciatio quædam integra, per quam omni suo iure sponte decedit religiosus, ut divinæ providentiæ Superioris dueu gubernandum, ac posside ndum ultro sese addicat, ac mancipet: negari non potest, quin obedientia comprehendat non solum executionem, ut imperata quis faciat & voluntatem, ut libenter faciat, sed etiam judicium, ut quaecunque Superior mandat, ac sentit, eadem inferiori & recta, & vera esse videantur, quatenus, ut dixi, vi sua potest voluntas intelligentiam flectere.
units.tr: Whoever wishes to offer himself wholly and entirely to God must also offer his understanding, beyond his will. This is the third and highest degree of obedience. He must not only will what the Superior wills, but also think what the Superior thinks, and subject his own judgment to the Superior's. His devoted will must bend the understanding as far as it can. This power of the mind does not have the freedom that the will possesses, and by its own nature it gives assent to whatever presents the appearance of truth to it. Yet in many matters, where the evidence of the truth does not force the mind, the weight of the will can incline it toward one side rather than the other. When such matters arise, whoever professes obedience ought to incline himself toward the opinion of the Superior. For obedience is a kind of holocaust, by which the whole man is offered in the fire of charity to his Creator and Lord, through the hands of ministers, without any diminution at all. It is also a kind of complete renunciation, by which the religious man freely gives up all his right, so that he may be governed and possessed by the divine providence working through his Superior, and willingly surrenders and gives himself over to it. It cannot be denied, then, that obedience comprises not only the carrying out of what is commanded, so that a man does it, and the will, so that he does it gladly, but also judgment, so that whatever the Superior commands and thinks seems to the inferior both right and true, insofar as, as I have said, the will by its own power can bend the understanding.

units.la: Utinam hanc mentis, & judicij Obedientiam, ita & intelligerent homines, & exerent, ut grata Deo est, ac omnibus, qui in religione viount, necessaria. Nam ut in corporibus, globisque coelestibus, ut alius alium afficiat, moveatque, requiritur, ut certa quaedam convenientia & ordine inferior orbis Superiori subjiciatur: sic in hominibus, cum alter alterius auctoritate movetur, quod per Obedientiam fit, oportet, ut is, qui ab alterius nutu pendet, subserviat, & obsecundet, ut virtus ab imperante ad eum derivetur, & influat. Hæc autem obtemperandi, obsecundandique ratio constare non potest, nisi voluntas ac judicium inferioris cum Superioris voluntate, ac judicio congruat.
units.tr: Would that people understood and practised this obedience of mind and judgment as it is pleasing to God and necessary for all who live in religion! For just as in bodies and in the heavenly spheres, so that one moves and affects another, a certain fitting order is required, by which the lower sphere is subject to the higher, so among men, when one is moved by the authority of another, which happens through obedience, it is necessary that the one who depends on another's nod should serve and comply, so that power may flow and be derived from the commander to him. But this manner of obeying and complying cannot stand unless the will and judgment of the inferior agree with the will and judgment of the Superior.

units.la: Iam vero si finis, & causa Obedientiæ spectatur, quemadmodum voluntas, ita & judicium in eo, quod nobis convenit, decipi potest: ergo sicuti, ne voluntas erret, cum Superioris voluntate conjungitur: sic intelligentia, ne fallatur, ad Superioris intelligentiam conformanda est. Ne innitaris prudentiae tuae, sacra litera monent: atque in rebus etiam humanis censent sapientes, vere prudentis esse, suaipsius prudentiam minime fidere: præsertim in rebus suis, quarum homines animo perturbato fere boni judices esse non possunt. Quod si in rebus nostris, alterius etiam non Superioris judicium, atque consilium nostro anteponendum est, quanto magis ipsius Superioris, cui nos ut Dei vicem gerenti, ac divinae voluntatis interpreti moderandos tradidimus? In causis vero personisque spiritualibus eo maior etiam cautio proculdubio est necessaria, quo gravius spiritualis viae periculum, dum sine frenis consilij discretionisve in ea decurritur. Qua de re commode Cassianus in Collatione Abbatis Mosi ait: Nullo alio vitio tam præcipitem Diabolus monachum pertrahit, ac perducit ad mortem: quam cum eum neglectis consilijs seniorum, suo judicio pertuaserit, definitionique confidere.
units.tr: Indeed, if we look at the end and cause of obedience, then just as the will, so the judgment too can be deceived about what is good for us. Therefore, just as the will is joined to the will of the Superior so that it does not err, so the understanding must be conformed to the understanding of the Superior, so that it is not deceived. Holy Scripture warns us not to rely on our own prudence, and even in human affairs the wise hold that it belongs to true prudence not to trust one's own prudence at all, especially in one's own affairs, in which men with troubled minds can scarcely be good judges. If in our affairs the judgment and counsel of another, not even a Superior, ought to be placed before our own, how much more ought that of the Superior himself, to whom we have handed ourselves over to be guided as one who acts in God's place and interprets the divine will? In spiritual causes and persons, moreover, undoubtedly even greater caution is necessary, the more serious the danger of the spiritual way when one runs through it without the reins of counsel and discretion. On this matter Cassian, in the Conference of Abbot Moses, rightly says: The devil draws and leads a monk headlong to death by no other vice so much as when, having neglected the counsels of the elders, he persuades him to trust his own judgment and decision.

units.la: Præterea nisi hæc Obedientia judicij existat, fieri non potest, ut vel consensus voluntatis, vel executio talis fit, qualem esse oportet: natura enim ita comparatum est, ut animi nostri vires, quæ appetitivæ dicuntur, sequantur apprehensivas: & nisi adhibita vi, voluntas, judicio repugnante, din obtemperare non poterit. Quod si forte quis aliquo temporis spatio obediat per communem illam apprehensionem, qua censetur, perperam etiam præcipienti parendum esse: certe id stabile, ac fixum esse non potest: atque ita perseverantia deficit, vel saltem Obedientiæ perfectio, quæ in promptè, & alacriter obediendo consistit: non enim ibi potest esse alacritas, ac diligentia, ubi est animorum, sententiarumque disserentio: perit etiam exequendi studium, & celeritas, cum ambigitur, expediat nec ne, facere quod jubemur: perit celebris illa Obedientiæ caeca simplicitas, cumapud nos ipsos in quaestionem ionem vocamus recte ne præcipiatur, an secus: atq; etiam fortasse damnamus Superiorem quod ea mandet, quæ nobis non ita jucunda sunt: perit humilitas, quoniā etsi ex altera parte paremus, ex altera tamen nosmetipsos Superiori præferimus: perit in rebus arduis fortitudo: perit denique (ut summatim complectar) virtutis huius vis omnis ac dignitas: succedunt autem in eorum locum dolor, molestia, tarditas, lassitudo, obmurmurationes, excusationes, aliaq; vitia, non sane levia, quibus Obedientia pretium, ac meritum prorsus extinguitur. Itaq; sanctus Bernardus, de iis, qui graviter ferunt imperata minus sibi suavia, sic ait: Hæc si molestè capetis sustinere, si dijudicare Prælatum, si murmurare in corde: etiamsi interius impleas, quod jubetur, non est hæc virtus patientiæ, sed velamentum malitiæ. Quod pax, & tranquillitas animi quæritur, certè hac non fruetur is, qui habet intra se causam perturbationis, atque tumultus, dissensionem videlicet iudicij proprij ab Obedientia legis. Atq; idcirco, tuendæ concordiæ causa, quæ Societatis omnis est vinculum, tantopere urgetur Apostolus, ut id ipsum omnes sapiant, & dicant: nimirum ut consentientibus & dictis & voluntatibus, mutuo foveantur, & conserventur. Iam si unum eundemq; oportet esse membrorum sensum, & capitis: facile cernitur, utrum sit æquius, caput membris, an membra capiti consentire. Atq; ex his quidem quæ dicta sunt hactenus, satis apparet, Obedientia judicij quàm sit necessaria. Quàm vero sit eadem ipsa perfecta grataque Domino, inde primum ostenditur, quod eam præstantissima pars hominis, ac pretiosissima Domino consecratur: deinde quod obediens ita sit holocaustum vivum, gratumq; Majestati divinæ, cum nihil suimet omnino retineat: postremò quod magna est huius certaminis difficultas: frangit enim seipsum Dei causa obediens ipsemet, resistitq; naturali propensioni, quæ omnibus hominibus insita est ad suam complectendam, sequendamque sententiam. Ex his igitur rebus efficitur, ut Obedientia etiamsi proprie voluntatem perficere videatur, quippe quam reddit ad nutum Superioris promptam, ac paratam: nihilominus ad intelligentiam quoque ipsam, ut diximus, pertinere debeat, eamque inducere ad sentiendum id ipsum, quod sentit Superior: sic enim fiet, ut omnibus connixi viribus, & voluntatis, & intelligentiæ, ad executionem celerem atque integram veniamus. Videor mihi vos, fratres charissimi, audire dicentes, de virtutis quidem huiusce necessitate jam non ambigere, illud vero, ut cognoscatis vehementer optare, quo pacto ad eius perfectionem pervenire possitis: Huic ego quæstioni cum sancto Leone, ita respondeo. Nihil arduum est humilibus, & nihil asperum mitibus: modò non desit vobis humilitas, non desit mansuetudo: non utiq; deerit Deo benignitas ad vos adjuvandos, ut quæ sibi promisistis, ea præstare possitis, animo non solum æquo, sed etiam libenti. Præterea vobis tria nominatim propono, quæ ad Obedientiam judicij comparandam multum juvant. Primum illud est, ut, quemadmodum initio dixi, non intueamini in persona Superioris, hominem obnoxium erroribus, atque miseriis: sed Christum ipsum, qui est sapientia summa, bonitas immensa, charitas infinita, qui nec decipi potest, nec vos vult ipse decipere. Et quoniam conscii vobismet estis, vos Dei amore jugum Obedientiæ subijisse, ut in Superioris voluntate sequenda, voluntatem divinam certius sequeremini: nolite dubitare, quin pergat fidelissima Domini charitas, eorum ministerio, quos vobis præfecit, vos deinceps gubernare, & rectis itineribus ducere. Itaque Superioris vocem, ac jussa non sensu at Christi vocem excipite: siquidem Apostolus etiam in hanc sententiam scribens ad Colossenses, cum ad obtemperandum Præpositis subditos adhortatur, ait: Quodcunq; facitis, ex animo operamini sicut Domino, & non hominibus: scientes, quod à Domino accipietis retributionem hereditatis, Domino Christo servite. Sanctus vero Bernardus, Sive Deus (inquit) sive homo vicarius Dei mandatum quodcunque tradiderit, pari profecto obsequendum est cura, pari reverentia deferendum, ubi tamen Deo contraria non præcipit homo.
