Atque in sanctissimo Eucharistiae Sacramento esse vere, realiter & substantialiter corpus & sanguinem, una cum anima & divinitate Domini nostri Iesu Christi, fierique conversionem totius substantiae panis in corpus, & totius substantiae vini in sanguinem, quam conversionem Catholica Ecclesia Transsubstantiationem appellat. Fateor etiam, sub altera tantum specie, totum atque integrum Christum verum ac Sacramentum sumi. Constanter teneo Purgatorium esse, animas ibi detentas fidelium suffragijs juvari. Similiter & sanctos, una cum Christo regnantes, venerandos & invocandos esse, eosque orationes Deo pro nobis offerre, atque eorum reliquias venerandas esse. Firmiter affero imagines Christi, ac Deiparae semper Virginis, nec non aliorum sanctorum habendas & retinendas esse, atque eis debitum honorem ac venerationem impertiendam. Indulgentiarum etiam potestatem a Christo in Ecclesia relictam fuisse, illarumque usum Christiano populo maximè salutarem affirmo. Sacram Catholicam & Apostolicam Rom. Ecclesiam, omnium Ecclesiarum matrem & magistram agnosco, Romano Pontifici, B. Petri Apostolorum Principis, successori, ac Iesu Christi Vicario veram obedientiam spondeo ac juro. Cetera item omnia a sacris Canonibus & Oecumenicis Conciliis, ac praecipue a S.S. Tridentina Synodo tradita, definita & declarata, indubitater recipio atque profiteor, simulque contraria omnia, atque haereses quascunque, ab Ecclesia damnatas & reiectas & anathematizatas, ego pariter damno, reijcio & anathematizo. Hanc veram Catholicam fidem, extra quam nemo salvus esse potest, quam in praesentia sponte profiteor: & veraciter teneo, eandem integram & immaculatam usque ad extremum vitae spiritum constantissime, Deo adjuvante, retineri, doceri & praedicari, quantum in me erit curaturum.
units.tr: But if any of those who have made the three vows aspire to higher things, and wish to be promoted either to Doctors or to Masters, or if any of the Protestants who are willing to devote themselves to Papist idolatry, they must swear in this form according to the Council of Trent, as it stands at the beginning of the Council of Trent: I, N. N., most firmly admit and embrace the Apostolic and ecclesiastical traditions, and the other observances and constitutions of the same Church. Likewise I admit the Sacred Scripture according to that sense which holy Mother Church has held and holds, to whom it belongs to judge of the true sense and interpretation of the Sacred Scriptures; and I will never accept or interpret it except according to the unanimous consent of the Fathers. I also profess that there are seven true and proper Sacraments of the New Law, instituted by Jesus Christ our Lord, and for the salvation of the human race, though not all are necessary for each individual: namely Baptism, Confirmation, the Eucharist, Penance, Extreme Unction, Orders and Matrimony; and that they confer grace, and that of these Baptism, Confirmation and Orders cannot be repeated without sacrilege. I also receive and admit the rites approved and accepted by the Church in the solemn administration of all the aforesaid Sacraments. I embrace and accept all and each of the things which have been defined and declared in the most holy Synod of Trent concerning Original Sin and Justification. I likewise profess that in the Mass a true, proper and propitiatory sacrifice is offered to God for the living and the dead. And that in the most holy Sacrament of the Eucharist there is truly, really and substantially the body and blood, together with the soul and divinity, of our Lord Jesus Christ, and that there takes place a conversion of the whole substance of the bread into the body, and of the whole substance of the wine into the blood, which conversion the Catholic Church calls Transubstantiation. I also confess that under one kind only the whole and entire Christ, true God and Sacrament, is received. I firmly hold that there is a Purgatory, and that the souls detained there are helped by the suffrages of the faithful. Likewise, that the saints who reign with Christ are to be venerated and invoked, that they offer prayers to God for us, and that their relics are to be venerated. I firmly affirm that the images of Christ, and of the ever-Virgin Mother of God, as well as of the other saints, are to be had and kept, and that due honour and veneration are to be given to them. I also affirm that the power of indulgences was left by Christ in the Church, and that the use of them is most salutary for the Christian people. I acknowledge the holy Catholic and Apostolic Roman Church as the mother and mistress of all churches; I promise and swear true obedience to the Roman Pontiff, successor of the blessed Peter, prince of the Apostles, and Vicar of Jesus Christ. Likewise I unhesitatingly receive and profess all the other things handed down, defined and declared by the sacred Canons and the Ecumenical Councils, and especially by the most holy Synod of Trent; and at the same time I likewise condemn, reject and anathematize all contrary things and all heresies whatever condemned, rejected and anathematized by the Church. This true Catholic faith, outside of which no one can be saved, which I now freely profess and truly hold, I will, God helping, most constantly keep, teach and preach whole and unstained until my last breath, as far as it lies in me to do so.

units.la: Obligatio trium votorum professorum qui ad altiora aspirant. Ego idem N. spondeo, voveo ac juro, sic me Deus adjuvet; & haec sancta Dei Evangelia. Nulli ergo omnino hominum liceat hanc paginam nostrae ordinationis, inhibitionis, derogationis, voluntatis, statuti, decreti & mandati infringere, vel eius au ausu temerario contraire. Si quis autem hoc attentare praesumpserit, indignationem omnipotentis Dei, ac B. Petri ac Pauli, Apostolorum eius, se noverit incursurum. Datae Romae apud S. Petrum. Anno incarnationis Dominicae 1564. Ibid. Novemb. Pontificatus nostri anno 5.
units.tr: The obligation of the three vows of those professed who aspire to higher things. "I, the same N., promise, vow and swear, so help me God, and these holy Gospels of God. Let it therefore be permitted to no man whatsoever to infringe this page of our ordination, prohibition, derogation, will, statute, decree and mandate, or to act against it by any rash daring. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed Peter and Paul, his Apostles. Given at Rome, at St Peter's. In the year of the Lord's incarnation 1564, in November, the fifth year of our pontificate."

units.la: Cum autem hi trium votorum Professi, hoc modo Ecclesiae Romanae se devoverunt ac obligarunt, tum a Generali suo in Rectores, Sacerdotes seu Patres, Confessarios, Concionatores, Praefectos spirituales, Praeceptores, Coadiutores spirituales, & temporales vel formatos & formandos adiutores, in Scholasticos & Idiotas dividuntur, quorum novissimi dicuntur Novitij, hoc est, qui nuper ordinem Iesuiticum ingressi sunt.
units.tr: Since, then, those professed of the three vows have thus devoted and bound themselves to the Roman Church, they are divided by their General into: rectors, priests or fathers, confessors, preachers, spiritual prefects, teachers, spiritual coadjutors, and temporal coadjutors, whether already formed or still to be formed; and into scholastics and lay brothers [idiotae]. Of these last, the latter are called novices, that is, those who have recently entered the Jesuit order.

units.la: DE IESVITARVM RECTORIBVS SEV REGENTIBVS.
units.tr: Concerning the Rectors or Regents of the Jesuits.

units.la: Rectores & Regentes in Collegiis, domibus & residentiis primatum tenent. Rectores tamen proprie dicuntur, qui Iesuitae; Regentes vero, qui etiam exteris praesunt, eoque secundum suas regulas regunt.
units.tr: The rectors and regents hold the first place in the colleges, houses and residences. Those are properly called rectors who are Jesuits; the regents, however, also preside over outsiders, and govern them according to their own rules.

units.la: Potestas Rectoris in Collegio libera & absoluta est: quicquid ille ordinat vel facit, nemo ipsi contradicere audet, nisi in poenas inobedientibus constitutas incurrere velit. Hic ea, quae Socijs praecipit, ex Generalis sententia, & Ignatij legibus sumit; eam ob causam etiam rigidissime delinquentes punit. Regentes vero nonnihil in exteros mitiores & humaniores sunt, quia nullis votis sunt obstricti. Quicquid in Collegio desideratur & constituendum est, id a Rectore petitur & expectatur. Si hic quid negat alicui, rationem eius non expetat, neque ab alio postulet, sed tacens gratiasque agens, in humilitate abeat, quasi voti compos factus esset.
units.tr: The power of the rector in a college is free and absolute: whatever he orders or does, no one dares to contradict him, unless he wishes to incur the penalties established for the disobedient. He takes what he prescribes to the companions from the judgment of the General and the laws of Ignatius; for this reason he also punishes even the most rigorous offenders. The regents, however, are somewhat milder and more humane towards outsiders, because they are bound by no vows. Whatever is lacking in the college and must be established is sought and expected from the rector. If he refuses anyone something, that person does not ask for his reason, nor demand it from another, but goes away in humility, silent and giving thanks, as if he had obtained his wish.

units.la: In Musaeo etiam Rectoris Societatis arcana, privilegia, literae & thesauri asservantur. Ad pecuniae tamen arcam solus claves non habet, sed custodiuntur ab tribus quos Generalis ad hoc ordinat: nimirum a Rectore, Ministro & Sacerdote aliquo, quorum quilibet clavem habet. Nulli autem soli conceduntur claves, quod antehac aliqui Rectores, multo auri pondere collecto, Societatem reliquerunt & aurum ablatum in suos usus converterunt.
units.tr: In the museum of the rector of the Society the secrets, privileges, letters and treasures are kept. Yet he alone does not hold the keys to the money chest; rather it is guarded by three whom the General appoints for this purpose: namely the rector, a minister and some priest, each of whom has a key. No one alone is granted the keys, because some rectors in the past, after gathering a great weight of gold, left the Society and turned the gold taken away to their own uses.

units.la: Rectoris etiam officium est, ut singulis mensibus singulorum mores & progressus Provinciali significet, qui deinde Generalem de iis certiorem facit.
units.tr: It is also the duty of the rector to report to the provincial each month on the conduct and progress of each member, who then informs the General of these matters.

units.la: Hos Rectores vel Seniores & similes his rarissime ex Nobilibus extra Italiam & Hispaniam, sed ex plebe tantum eligunt & adoptant. Quod cur fiat, coniectura non est difficilis: generosa nempe nobilitatis pectora erga patriam ita afsecta norunt, ut suis consiliis & practicis ea minus commoda & opportuna statuant. Interim his rebus fit, ut cum Iesuitis suum ventrem indigenae suis opibus explere & suffarcire cogantur: caput tamen Hispanico & Italico cerebro repletum habeat, ad cuius nempe sensum reliquum corpus moveatur.
units.tr: These rectors, or seniors and the like, they very rarely choose and adopt from the nobility outside Italy and Spain, but only from the common people. Why this is done is not a difficult guess: they know that the noble spirit, so disposed towards its country, would in its own counsels and practices determine less advantageous and suitable measures. Meanwhile it comes about through these arrangements that the natives are compelled to fill and stuff their bellies with their own wealth for the Jesuits, yet the head is kept filled with a Spanish and Italian brain, by whose sense the rest of the body is moved.

units.la: DE IESVITARVM MINISTRIS SEV OECONOMIS.
units.tr: ON THE MINISTERS, OR STEWARDS, OF THE JESUITS.

units.la: Rectori dignitate proximi sunt Ministri, quos nos Oeconomos vocamus. Hi singulis diebus Sabbathis a Rectore accipiunt quomodo, quantum & qualiter res pecuniarias & ad victum spectantes per septimanam dispensare debeant. Horum est omnes in genere, praeter Rectorem observare, admonere, & in regulis Societatis ac exercitijs Collegiorum recte informare. Si quos deprehendunt in egulas delinquentes, illis poenitentiam aliquam iniungunt.
units.tr: Next in rank to the Rector are the Ministers, whom we call stewards (Oeconomi). Every Sabbath they receive from the Rector instructions on how, how much and in what manner they are to dispense the money and the goods needed for food during the week. It is their task, in general, to observe everyone except the Rector, to admonish them, and to instruct them correctly in the rules of the Society and in the exercises of the Colleges. If they find anyone breaking the rules, they impose some penance on him.

units.la: Est etiam Ministri curare suppellectilē domus: ne quid vel intereat, vel peratur, vel amittatur: debet etiam cellae & culinae prospicere, ne quid rerum necessariarū desit, sed ut omnia suo tempore emantur & dispensentur. Penes hunc ergo est cura & custodia domus. Idem etiam cum secularibus agit, ut Priores & Abbates in Monachorum coenobijs, & Oeconomi in Monasterijs.
units.tr: It is also the duty of the Minister to take care of the household furnishings, so that nothing perishes, is spoiled or is lost. He must also look after the storerooms and the kitchen, so that none of the necessary supplies runs short, but that everything is bought and distributed at the proper time. The care and custody of the household therefore rests with him. He also deals with secular people in the same way that the Priors and Abbots do in the monastic cloisters, and the stewards (Oeconomi) do in the monasteries.

units.la: 8. DE IESVITARVM SACER- DOTIBVS.
units.tr: 8. Of the Priests of the Jesuits.

units.la: Sacerdotum seu Patrum est, secundum Loyolae Regulas, quotidie pro vivis & mortuis, pro Pontifice Romano, pro Societatis incremento, & ad promerendam exstirpationem Evangelicorum sacra facere & Missas celebrare, & horas canonicas servare, officium ​ēque, vel in horto, vel in templo, vel in cubili, vel in museo, vel in dormitorio, vel in circuitu, vel in alio loco demurmurare. Coferunt se quoque interdum ad exercitium aliquod corporale, mediocre tamen, qualia sunt, bibliothecam curare, hortulos plantare, libros legere, scribere, pingere, aut quid mile agere, quo diei taedium levant.
units.tr: According to the Rules of Loyola, it is the duty of the priests, or Fathers, to offer sacred rites and celebrate Masses every day for the living and the dead, for the Roman Pontiff, for the growth of the Society, and to earn the extirpation of the Evangelicals; and to observe the canonical hours, murmuring the office, whether in the garden, in the church, in the bedroom, in the study, in the dormitory, in the cloister walk, or in some other place. They also sometimes betake themselves to some bodily exercise, though a moderate one, such as looking after the library, planting little gardens, reading books, writing, painting, or doing some other thing of the kind, by which they relieve the weariness of the day.

units.la: Eorum etiam est, in eos, qui Sacerdotes non sunt, animadvertere, & delinquentes paterne admonere, vel Superiori ea, quae minus recte fieri videt, deferre. Singulis quoque diebus Veneris ad Iuniores & Novitios exhortationes instituere debent: quarum finis sit, mundi contemptum, Societatis amorem, abnegationem sui, & perfectam obedientiam in omnibus, secundum Societatis institutum, iuniorum animis instillare.
units.tr: It is also their task to take note of those who are not priests, to admonish offenders in a fatherly way, or to report to the Superior whatever they see being done less properly. Moreover, every Friday they must hold exhortations for the juniors and novices, whose aim is to instil into their minds contempt of the world, love of the Society, self-denial, and perfect obedience in all things, according to the Society's institute.

units.la: 9. DE IESVITARVM POENI- TENTIARIIS.
units.tr: 9. ON THE JESUITS' PENITENTIARIES.

units.la: Poenitentiarij Romae dicuntur, qui ibidem apud S. Petrum integrum diem sedent, ut ibi confessiones audiant. His mandatur, ut diligenter in haereticos, uos sic vocant, inquirant. Si quos in confessionibus intelligant Evangelicis fidere & de religione Romana dubitare, neque Papam pro Vicario Christi in terris agnoscere, eos non absolvant, nisi statim revocent. Si contra disputent, ad Inquisitores remittant. Ab illis miserrime, non secus quam malefici a carnificibus, torquentur. Diligenter etiam cavent, ne quisquam Evangelicorum scripta in suis aedibus habeat. Si quos in confessione cognoscunt, aut hospitia Evangelicis dare, ut familiaritatem cum illis contrahere, eos excommunicant, & magistratui, ceu proditorum fautores, puniendos indicant, non obstantibus decretis, quae praecipiunt arcana confessionis nulli revelanda esse. Tandem peccatis omnibus cognitis pro qualitate eorum poenitentias iniungunt, & homines in primis ad crebras confessiones adhortantur.
units.tr: They are called Penitentiaries at Rome, who sit there at St Peter's for the whole day in order to hear confessions. They are charged to inquire diligently after heretics, as they call them. If in confessions they learn of anyone who trusts in the Evangelicals and doubts the Roman religion, and does not acknowledge the Pope as Vicar of Christ on earth, they are not to absolve such a person unless he at once recants. If he argues the contrary, they are to hand him over to the Inquisitors, by whom he is tortured most wretchedly, no differently than criminals are tortured by executioners. They also take great care that no one among the Evangelicals keeps their writings in his house. If they come to know through confession of anyone who gives lodging to Evangelicals, or who enters into familiarity with them, they excommunicate that person and point him out to the magistrate to be punished as a supporter of traitors, notwithstanding the decrees which order that the secrets of confession are not to be revealed to anyone. Finally, once all sins have been known, they impose penances according to the nature of each, and they above all exhort people to frequent confession.

units.la: 10. DE IESVITARVM CONFESSARIIS.
units.tr: 10. OF THE CONFESSORS OF THE JESUITS.

units.la: Confessarij apud Iesuitas vocantur, qui in casibus reservatis satis instructi, in Iesuiticis & Cathedralibus templis, quatuor ieiuniorum temporibus, ertas occupant sedes, in quibus accedentium confessiones audiunt. Hi confitentes secundum regulas ipsis praescriptas examinant, & plenariam circumstantiarum enumerationem extorquent: sine qua irritam absolutionem, & eum, qui peccati circumstantiam aliquam reticet, sacrilegum esse dicunt. Examinat autem primo confitentes de peccatis occultis & cogitationū erratis: secundo de verbis; tertió de factis: quarto de omissis: quinto de scriptis: sexto de venialibus, actuali-bus & tandem de mortalibus. Et ut haec rite peragant, ex Decalogo confitentes examinant, & ab hoc ad Ecclesiae praecepta digrediuntur: & in haec qui peccat, graviore sustinet poenitentiam, quam qui in Decalogum deliquit. Ab his descendunt ad septem mortalia peccata, hinc ad quinque sensus, ad peccata aliena, ad neglecta misericordiae opera, denique ad inquisitionem articulorum Pontificiorum veniunt. Si qui etiam apud Iesuitas peccata sua confitentur, ii singulares a Papa consequuntur indulgentias.
units.tr: The confessors among the Jesuits are those who, being sufficiently instructed in the reserved cases, take their seats in the Jesuit and cathedral churches during the four fasting seasons, in the designated places, and hear the confessions of those who come. They examine the penitents according to the rules prescribed for them and extract a full enumeration of the circumstances. Without this they say the absolution is void, and they declare that whoever withholds any circumstance of his sin is guilty of sacrilege. They examine the penitents in this order: (1) first, about secret sins and errors of thought; (2) second, about words; (3) third, about deeds; (4) fourth, about omissions; (5) fifth, about writings; (6) sixth, about venial and actual sins; and finally about mortal sins. To carry this out properly, they examine the penitents by the Decalogue and from it pass on to the precepts of the Church, and the one who sins against these bears a heavier penance than the one who has transgressed the Decalogue. From these they go down to the seven deadly sins, then to the five senses, to the sins of others, to neglected works of mercy, and finally they come to the questioning about the articles of the Papists. If any confess their sins to the Jesuits, they obtain special indulgences from the Pope.

units.la: II. DE IESVITARVM CONCIO- NATORIBVS.
units.tr: II. Of the Jesuit Preachers.

units.la: Concionatores Iesuitarum sunt, qui vices Parochorum in concionandi munere subeunt. In quibus enim locis Iesuitae Collegia, domus vel residentias habent, ab eius loci Episcopo, Decano & Parocho petunt, ut sibi concionandi facultatem dent: quam ipsi ob Papae auctoritatem, qua muniuntur, non audent negare. Hi conciones suas non ad Prophetica & Apostolica scripta dirigunt, sed ad mandatum Papae, secundum Tridentini Concilij Canones & Scholasticorum commenta. Optimi ex ipsis videntur, qui atroces in Evangelicos invectivas instituunt, populumque adversus illos exstimulant.
units.tr: The preachers of the Jesuits are those who take on, in the office of preaching, the role of the parish priests. In those places where the Jesuits have colleges, houses or residences, they ask the bishop of that place, the dean and the parish priest to give them permission to preach; and they do not dare to refuse this themselves, on account of the authority of the Pope by which they are protected. These men do not direct their sermons to the prophetic and apostolic writings, but to the Pope's command, according to the canons of the Council of Trent and the commentaries of the Schoolmen. The best of them seem to be those who launch savage invectives against the Evangelicals and stir up the people against them.

units.la: 12. DE SPIRITVALIBVS IESVITARVM PRAEFECTIS.
units.tr: 12. Concerning the Spiritual Prefects of the Jesuits.

units.la: Spirituales Praefecti Iesuitarum dicuntur, qui in Collegiis & domibus Iesuitis, iuniores & novitios observant, ne primam, uti loquuntur, charitatem quam ad Societatem attulerunt, deserant, sed semper in Societatis spiritu prosiciant, & seniioribus similes efficiantur. Horum igitur est conscientias scrutari & in exercitijs spiritualibus iuniores informare. Ad hos, si qui novitijs iniciuntur scrupuli vel tentationes, confugiunt: a quibus tentationes bonae malae, & vicissim malae bonae redduntur.
units.tr: The Spiritual Prefects of the Jesuits are those who, in the colleges and houses of the Jesuits, watch over the younger members and novices, so that they do not abandon the first love, as they say, which they brought to the Society, but always make progress in the spirit of the Society and become like the older members. It is their task, therefore, to examine consciences and to instruct the younger members in the spiritual exercises. To these men the novices have recourse if any scruples or temptations come upon them; and by these men good temptations are made bad, and conversely bad ones good.

units.la: Officium quoque illorum est, iunioribus tradere & commendare devotos libellos: illisque praescribere quae ad mensam legere debeant, observare insuper, ut rite ac debitis horis spiritualia officia perficiantur. Non obsequentibus poenitentias iniungunt: si his non emendantur, Rectori eos deferunt, qui ieiunia, cilicia & flagella eis admovet, quibus vel inviti, nisi mori malint, parere coguntur.
units.tr: It is also their duty to hand over and recommend devotional little books to the younger members, to prescribe to them what they ought to read at table, and moreover to see that spiritual duties are carried out properly and at the appointed hours. Those who do not comply they impose penances upon; if they are not corrected by these, they report them to the Rector, who applies fasting, hair shirts and whips to them, to which they are compelled to submit, even against their will, unless they would rather die.

units.la: 13. DE PRAECEPTORIBVS IE- SVITARVM.
units.tr: 13. Of the Teachers of the Jesuits.

units.la: IEsuitarum Praeceptores hi sunt, qui in Scholis & Academijs suos discipulos in religione, linguis & artibus, ad praescriptum Inquisitoris, Visitatoris & Provincialis institutum & docent. Horum quidam publici sunt, quidam domestici. Publici sunt, qui gradum intra vel extra Societatem sunt consequuti & publice docent. Domestici, qui solum discipulos domi privatim exercent, & audita ab illis rursus exigunt. Hi nullum pro laboribus suis habent stipendium, propter regulam ipsis praescriptam: Gratis accepistis, gratis date. Quod si autem a Principibus & Academiarum patronis illis pro laboribus praestitis aliquot coronatorum millia ad Collegia mittuntur, ambabus manibus, non ut mercedem, sed ut eleemosynam illa accipiunt.
units.tr: The teachers of the Jesuits are those who, in their schools and academies, instruct their pupils in religion, languages and arts, according to the prescribed method of the Inquisitor, the Visitor and the Provincial. Some of these are public and some are domestic. Public teachers are those who have obtained a degree inside or outside the Society and teach publicly. Domestic teachers are those who train pupils only privately at home and in turn demand from them what they have been taught. These receive no pay for their labours, because of the rule prescribed for them: "You have received freely, give freely." But if princes and patrons of the academies send some thousands of crowns to the colleges as payment for their services, they receive them with both hands, not as wages but as alms.

units.la: Praeter hoc aliud etiam apud Iesuitas Praeceptorum genus est, quod praeficitur iis, quos Papistici Principes & nobiles sua munificentia alunt, & vulgo Beneficiarij vocantur. Præceptores hi, non ut reliqui Professores, intra Iesuitarum collegia manent, sed cum Beneficiariis illis in ipsorum ædibus, quas Stipendiarias nominant, vivunt, in quorum fidem & vitam inquirunt diligenter. In huiusmodi stipendiatorum domo, singulis mensis, ad quam octo ordinantur, Inspector & Præceptor præficitur Iesuita, qui audita ab illis exigit, eosque non tantum in Philosophicis studiis instituit, sed etiam in Pontificiorum erroribus informat, & qui sunt inter illos maximæ spei adolescentes, variis illecebris & promissis ad Societatis ingressum sollicitant; quo fit, ut multi contra parentum suorum voluntatem Iesuitæ fiant.
units.tr: Besides these, there is another kind of teacher among the Jesuits, who is placed over those whom the Papist princes and nobles support out of their generosity, and who are commonly called Beneficiaries. These teachers, unlike the other professors, do not remain within the Jesuit colleges but live with those Beneficiaries in their own houses, which they call stipendiary houses, and they carefully inquire into their faith and conduct. In the house of such stipendiaries, to which eight are assigned, a Jesuit is set over each group as overseer and teacher; he demands an account of what has been taught and instructs them not only in philosophical studies but also informs them in the errors of the Papists. Among them, those young men of greatest promise are pressed with various enticements and promises to enter the Society; as a result, many become Jesuits against the wishes of their parents.

units.la: DE IESVITARVM SERVIS SPI- RITUALIBUS.
units.tr: ON THE SPIRITUAL SERVANTS OF THE JESUITS.

units.la: Servi seu Coadjutores Iesuitarum spirituales dicuntur, qui consiliis & scriptis suis senatum Iesuiticum iuvant. His licet quidem sua consilia superioribus referre, edita, ut non curent, sive illa recipiantur, sive repudientur, siquidem eorum sit, non imperare, sed consilia vel sententiam suam in medium proferre, aut scripto significare, liberum tamen superioribus relinquere, ut eligant quod ipsis optimum videtur. In Synedrio ergo assident, & suam sententiam dicunt; sin autem secedere iubentur, & Generalis cum Assistentibus, quid faciendum sit, decreverit, licet illud ipsis videatur, contra tamen nec hiscere quidem audent. Spirituales autem vocantur, quod eorum sit, circa res spirituales Iesuitarum, hoc est, omnis generis errores & idolomanias Papisticas ac Iesuiticas occupari.
units.tr: The spiritual servants or Coadjutors of the Jesuits are those who assist the Jesuit senate by their counsels and writings. They are indeed permitted to lay their counsels before their superiors, but they must not mind whether these are accepted or rejected; for it is their part not to command but to set forth their counsel or opinion, or to signify it in writing, while it is left free to the superiors to choose whatever seems best to them. So they sit in the Synedrion and state their opinion; but if they are ordered to withdraw, and the General with his Assistants has decided what is to be done, then, even if it seems good to them, they do not dare so much as open their mouths against it. They are called spiritual because it is their business to occupy themselves with the spiritual affairs of the Jesuits, that is, with every kind of error and Papistical and Jesuitical idolatry.

units.la: Hi omnes, qui trium votorum Professos sequuntur, generali nomine Coadjutores spirituales dicuntur, qui nuncupatis prius votis paupertatis, castitatis & obedientiae, bestiam hanc adiuvant in pervertendis & traducendis ad primam belluam animabus. Quo in re quo quisque aptior & diligentior exstiterit, eo citius ad professionem admissus membrum huius Societatis efficitur.
units.tr: All of these, who follow the Professed of the three vows, are called by the general name of spiritual Coadjutors. Having first taken the vows of poverty, chastity and obedience, they help this beast in perverting souls and drawing them over to the first beast. In this matter, the more apt and diligent each one proves himself, the sooner he is admitted to profession and becomes a member of this Society.

units.la: DE SCHOLASTICIS ET NOVITIIS IESVITARVM.
units.tr: ON THE SCHOLASTICS AND NOVICES OF THE JESUITS.

units.la: Scholastici & Novitii in eum finem in collegiis aluntur, ne Societas hæc tandem deficiat: sed ut putrescentibus veteribus membris in recentioribus & novis semper conservetur. Eorum autem est, cuiuscunque ordinis, status vel conditionis ante ingressum fuerint, mundum, ut ipsi loquuntur, deserere, seipsos abnegare, bona sua relinquere, a parentibus auffugere, amicis valedicere, & ab omnibus, quae mundus amat, abhorrere; naturalem parentum affectum, in spiritualem, hoc est, in Iesuiticorum sociorum amorem convertere, omnium suorum, atque adeo sui ipsius quoque oblivisci. Praeterea a corporis obsequio & indulgentia quam longissime recedere; sensibus repugnantia appetere; carnis societatem disciplinis, hoc est, secundum Iesuitas, flagellis, ferulis, flagris & aliis spontaneis corporis supplicis eicere.
units.tr: The scholastics and novices are maintained in the colleges for this purpose: that this Society may not at last fail, but may always be preserved in its younger and newer members, as its older members decay. It is their duty, whatever order, rank or condition they belonged to before entering, to forsake the world (as they themselves put it), to deny themselves, to leave their goods behind, to flee from their parents, to bid farewell to friends, and to shun all that the world loves; to turn natural affection for parents into spiritual love, that is, love of the Jesuit companions, and to forget all their own things and even themselves. Besides this, they must withdraw as far as possible from the service and indulgence of the body; they must seek out what is opposed to the senses; and they must drive out fellowship with the flesh by discipline, that is, according to the Jesuits, by scourges, rods, whips and other voluntary punishments of the body.

units.la: Novitiorum Magister in his omnibus eos exercet, ac instar stultorum vexat, donec sibi ipsis in totum emoriantur, & non sibi amplius, sed soli Papae, vel Iesuitarum Patribus vivant. Hoc Iesuitis est Deo vivere, Christo inseri, & in mortem ius baptizari ac sepeliri.
units.tr: The Master of Novices exercises them in all these things and harasses them like fools, until they die completely to themselves and live no longer for themselves, but only for the Pope or the Fathers of the Jesuits. To the Jesuits, this is to live to God, to be grafted into Christ, and to be baptized and buried into death.

units.la: Ad perpetuo autem occultandam, confervandam & augendam superstitionem & idololatriam Iesuitae Novitiis suis intellectum, si quem habent, ipsumque sensum ligant. Pater enim eorum Ignatius Loyola in epistola quae in Collegiis Iesuitarum singulis mensibus ad mensam legitur, monet & iubet ferio, ut ea, quae Superior iubet, caeca obedientia simpliciter perficiant; quaeque ipse facit caeco iudicio praetereant, non considerantes, an bonum vel utile sit, necne quod praecipitur. Qua quidem in re Iesuitae Canonistas egregie imitantur, perniciosissimos summorum Pontificum adulatores & mundi totius seductores. Hi enim dist. 40. c. Si Papa. orbi Christiano persuadere iam aliquot seculis conati sunt, Romanum Pontificem tantae esse dignitatis authoritatisque, ut licet inutilis & remissus in suis operibus esset, imo innumerabiles populos caterвaтim in gehennam duceret, totum mundum destrueret, nemo tamen ex ipso huius facti vel posset, vel deberet rationem quaerere. Sic prorsus quoque; imo multo peius Societas Iesuitarum suos alumnos instituit, cum docet: Quaeque Superior iubet, quaeque ipse fecit, non solum judicanda non esse, multoque minus reprehendenda; sed etiam tanquam bona & sancta (sic enim Pater eorum Ignatius in eadem epistola loquitur) praesupponenda: quo nimirum omnis tandem stultitia, idololatria & superstitio Sanctitatis nomen obtineant, locoque reliquiarum Societatis colantur.
units.tr: To keep this superstition and idolatry perpetually hidden, preserved and increased, the Jesuits bind the understanding of their novices, if they have any, and their very sense as well. For their father Ignatius Loyola, in a letter which is read at table in each of the Jesuit colleges every month, admonishes and orders the brothers that they simply carry out, with blind obedience, whatever the Superior commands, and that they pass over with blind judgment whatever he himself does, not considering whether what is enjoined is good or useful. In this matter the Jesuit canonists imitate him splendidly, being the most pernicious flatterers of the supreme Popes and seducers of the whole world. For they (dist. 40, c. Si Papa) have for some centuries tried to persuade the Christian world that the Roman Pontiff is of such dignity and authority that, although he be useless and remiss in his works, indeed although he lead countless peoples in droves into hell and destroy the whole world, yet no one may or ought to ask an account of this deed from him. Just so, or rather far worse, the Society of Jesuits trains its pupils, when it teaches: whatever the Superior orders, and whatever he himself has done, is not only not to be judged, much less to be found fault with, but is even to be presupposed as good and holy (for so their father Ignatius speaks in the same letter). By this means, of course, all folly, idolatry and superstition at last obtain the name of holiness and are worshipped in place of the relics of the Society.

units.la: DE IESVITARVM SERVIS TEMPORALIBVS SEV COADIVTORIBVS FORMATIS
units.tr: On the Temporal Servants, or Formed Coadjutors, of the Jesuits

units.la: Coadjutores temporales totius Societatis sunt Servi & membra Societatis non tantum in voto simplici, sed etiam solenni. Eorum est totum Societatis corpus fovere, curare, victum & amictum ei parare, omniaque negotia domestica tractare. In horum numerum ac ordinem referendi sunt officiales & artifices: ut sunt coci, sutores, sartores & similes; quorum artificiis in Societate indigent. Respuunt enim exterorum artificum operas, ne illorum doli manifestentur. Habent autem nullius rei conficiendae licentiam, sed omnia ad iussum & nutum Rectoris facere coguntur. Si quid emendum sit, ipsis a Rectore annumeratur pecunia certa, pro qua ea quae Rector iubet, semper tamen optima, emere, & cum primum domum reversi fuerint, rationem reddere, & reliquam pecuniam Rectori restituere tenentur. Empta deinde quoque pro Rectoris voluntate & arbitrio dispensare & erogare.
units.tr: The temporal coadjutors of the whole Society are servants and members of the Society, bound not only by a simple vow but also by a solemn one. It is their task to look after the whole body of the Society, to care for it, to provide its food and clothing, and to manage all its domestic affairs. Among them are counted the officials and craftsmen, such as cooks, shoemakers, tailors and the like, whose skills the Society needs. For they refuse the services of outside craftsmen, lest their tricks be exposed. They have no licence to make anything on their own account, but are obliged to do everything at the command and nod of the Rector. If something is to be bought, a fixed sum of money is counted out to them by the Rector, and with it they must buy what the Rector orders, always of the best quality. Once they have come home, they must give an account and return the remaining money to the Rector. Then they dispense and spend what has been bought, according to the Rector's will and judgement.

units.la: Temporales vero dicuntur, quod tantum temporalibus rebus occupentur, & in rerum humanarum dispensatione versentur, & ea iussu Rectoris peragant quae ipsis cum secularibus efficienda incumbunt. Ne tamen nomine Temporalium offendantur, dicunt illos non minores esse merito, quam reliquos, eodem Spiritu res mundanas, quo illi Spirituales tractent. Quia non sibi ipsis, nec hominibus, sed Socijs Christi Iesu, imo ipsi Iesu inserviant. Illosque totreceptaturos coronas, quot labores subeant pro Societatis Patribus, qui in tractatione rerum spiritualium occupentur, & curent, ut Societas floreat, augeatur & dilatetur. Denique, si qui ex his ante Societatis ingressum legere vel scribere nescient, regula prohibentur, ne ullam literam in Societate addiscant, sed idiotae & fratres ignorantiae maneant. Sic enim habet regula: Nemo illorum, qui praficitur alicui functioni domesticae, legere vel scribere discat, aut si quid horum fiat, nihil amplius addiscat, neque alios ipse doceat, absque permissu Praepositi generalis: sed illis sancta in simplicitate & humilitate Domino nostro Iesu Christo servire sufficiat.
units.tr: They are called temporal because they are occupied only with temporal things, are engaged in the management of human affairs, and carry out at the Rector's command the tasks that fall to them to perform alongside secular people. Lest they take offence at the name "temporal", they say that these men are not inferior in merit to the rest, since they handle worldly matters with the same Spirit with which the others handle spiritual ones. For they serve not themselves or other men, but the companions of Christ Jesus, indeed Jesus himself. They say that these men will receive as many crowns as the labours they undergo on behalf of the Fathers of the Society, who are occupied with spiritual affairs and take care that the Society flourishes, grows and spreads. Finally, if any of them could not read or write before entering the Society, the rule forbids them to learn any letter in the Society, but they are to remain simple and brothers in ignorance. For the rule says this: No one of those who is placed over any domestic office is to learn to read or write, or, if either of these should happen, he is to learn nothing further, nor is he himself to teach others, without the permission of the Father General; but it is enough for them to serve our Lord Jesus Christ in holy simplicity and humility.

units.la: Qui plura scire cupit de gradibus & generibus Ordinis Iesuitici, legat Heliae Hafenmulleri historiam, & Christiani Franken in suo Colloquio Iesuitico, qui ambo olim fuerunt Iesuitarum mancipia, sed facti tandem liberi servi Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Whoever wishes to know more about the grades and kinds of the Jesuit Order, let him read the history of Elias Hafenmuller, and Christian Franken in his Jesuit Colloquy, both of whom were once slaves of the Jesuits, but who became free servants of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Officium Coadiutorum temporalium.
units.tr: The office of the temporal coadjutors.

units.la: Temporales servi cur dicantur.
units.tr: Why temporal servants are so called.

units.la: CAPVT VI. DE CONFIRMATIONE ORDI- NIS, REGVLAE, CONSTITVTIONVM TOTIVSQVE OECONOMIÆ IESVITARVM.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI. CONCERNING THE CONFIRMATION OF THE ORDER, RULE, CONSTITUTIONS, AND THE WHOLE ECONOMY OF THE JESUITS.

units.la: IGNATIVS Loyola ut supra in vita eius indicavimus quoque, cum aliquot annis Lutetiæ Parisiorum literis operam navâsset, tandem Anno Domini 1536 in Hispaniam revertitur, adscitis decem novæ suæ religionis sociis: ij erant P. Faber, Fr. Xavier, Iacobus Laynes, Claudius Gajus, Iohannes Coduri, Alphonsus Salmeronius, Simon Rodericus Lusitanus, & Nicolaus Bovadilla. Sequenti anno, qui fuit vicesimus septimus supra millesimum quingentesimum, Romam se contulerunt, ut à Romano Pontifice in terram sanctam abeundi licentiam impetrarent.
units.tr: Ignatius Loyola, as we have also indicated above in his life, after he had spent some years at Paris in literary study, finally returned to Spain in the year of the Lord 1536, taking with him ten companions of his new religion. These were Peter Faber, Francis Xavier, James Laynez, Claude Jay, John Codure, Alphonsus Salmeron, Simon Rodrigues the Portuguese, and Nicholas Bobadilla. In the following year, which was the twenty-seventh after the year one thousand five hundred, they went to Rome, to obtain from the Roman Pontiff permission to set out for the Holy Land.

units.la: Ante vero quàm Romam venissent, Venetiis in pauperum hospitijs, quæ Xenodochia & Nosodochia appellant, ita versati sunt, eamque diligentiam & solicitudinem in ægrorum ibi morbis curandis, vulneribus obligandis, molestâ, gravi ac putidâ sanie abstergendâ impenderunt, ut omnes in sui admirationem peraxerint. Datâ vero Romæ licentiâ à Papa proficiscendi in Syriam, Venetias redeunt; ibi cognoscunt, ob pacem inter Turcas & Venetos, per id tempus rutam, nulli tuto Hierosolymam navigare licere. Mutatâ igitur sententiâ, septem ex illis sacris initiari & ad Sacerdotium promoveri voluerunt. Cùm vero Ecclesiastica lege, ex Pauli III. institutione caveatur, ne quis sacris initietur, qui ut hæreditarijs, aut Ecclesiasticis bonis, unde honestè vivere posset, caruerit, hi jovi Apostoli amplissimam sibi hæreditatem esse Deum ipsum lautissimum quoque patrimonium, nudos nudum Christum sequi affirmârunt, pro quo egere, extremam quoque penuriam pati, maximas opes ducerent. Quod copiosissimum esse, & Sacerdote Christiano dignissimum patrimonium cum iudicaret Verallus Archiepiscopus Rosanensis, qui per id temporis Venetijs Apostolicæ sedis Legatus fuit, postea Cardinalis factus, perpetuam spontaneamque paupertatem Deo ante eius pedes promiserunt: illoque patrimonio constituto, ex illis septem sunt Sacerdotio inaugurati: facultas quoque illis data est ut secretas atque occultas peccatorum confessiones liberè ubique audire possent.
units.tr: Before they came to Rome, however, they spent time in Venice in the hospices for the poor, which they call xenodochia and nosodochia, and they devoted such diligence and care there to curing the sick, binding up wounds, and cleansing away foul, grievous and putrid matter, that they drew everyone's admiration. Once they had received from the Pope at Rome permission to set out for Syria, they returned to Venice; there they learned that, because of the peace between the Turks and the Venetians, which was then in force, it was not safe for anyone to sail to Jerusalem. Having therefore changed their plan, they wished to be initiated into the sacred orders and promoted to the priesthood. But since ecclesiastical law, under the institution of Paul III, provides that no one who lacks an inheritance or ecclesiastical goods by which he could live honourably be admitted to holy orders, these self-styled apostles declared that God himself was their most ample inheritance and their most sumptuous patrimony, that they, naked, followed the naked Christ, and that to lack for him and suffer extreme poverty they counted the greatest riches. When Verallo, Archbishop of Rossano, who at that time was Legate of the Apostolic See at Venice and was afterwards made a Cardinal, judged this to be a most abundant and most worthy patrimony for a Christian priest, they promised before his feet perpetual and voluntary poverty; this patrimony being established, seven of them were then ordained to the priesthood. The faculty was also granted to them to hear secret and private confessions of sins freely everywhere.

units.la: Ab eo tempore cæperunt per urbes Venetæ ditionis in Italia prædicare. Postea simul omnes se Romam contulerunt Anno Christi 1538. In itinere ἐκστασιν quandam seu raptum Ignatius finxit. Socios enim præire iubet: ipse vero ad sacellum quoddam, quasi in eo oraturus, divertitur: dumque nimis diu emaneret, socij regrediuntur ad sacellum, suum Ignatium quærunt; qui conspectis illis in faciem prodidit, & aliquandiu, quasi extra se raptus esset, iacuit. Paulò post à sim-ulata ecstasi evigilans Socijs dicit: Visum habui, pergimus Romam, ubi nos dura pati oportet. Sed præsentibus animis sitis. B. Maria promisit se nostram fore patronam.
units.tr: From that time they began to preach through the cities of the Venetian dominion in Italy. Afterwards all of them together went to Rome in the year of Christ 1538. On the journey Ignatius feigned a certain ecstasy or rapture (ἔκστασιν). For he ordered his companions to go on ahead, while he himself turned aside to a certain little chapel, as if he were going to pray there; and when he stayed away too long, the companions returned to the chapel and sought their Ignatius, who, when he saw them, showed himself and lay for some time as if he had been carried out of himself. Shortly afterwards, waking from his simulated ecstasy, he said to his companions: "I have had a vision; let us go on to Rome, where we must suffer harsh things. But be of good courage. The Blessed Virgin has promised that she will be our patroness."

units.la: Vbi Romam venissent, gravissimis molestijs à Clero Rom. exagitati sunt; inprimis autem Augustiniani Eremitani Ignatio & Socijs eius restiterunt, eosque multorum scelerum accusarunt. Metuebant enim Sacerdotes & Monachi, necque sine causa, ne sua bona & Monasteria ab his Socijs aliquando occuparentur.
units.tr: When they had come to Rome, they were harassed by the most grievous troubles from the Roman clergy; above all the Augustinian Hermits opposed Ignatius and his companions, and accused them of many crimes. For the priests and monks feared, and not without reason, that their own goods and monasteries might one day be seized by these companions.

units.la: Multi etiam Cardinalium ac Episcoporum tum temporis Ignatio Loyolæ vehementer resistebant, maximè vero Bartholomeus, Guidiccionus Cardinalis, qui cum alijs duobus Regulam Ignatij examinandam tradidit Paulus III. Regulæ confirmationem dissuaserunt vehementer, ac pristinas Religiones potiùs reformandas, quàm novas instituendas, rectè prudenterque iudicârunt.
units.tr: At that time many of the Cardinals and Bishops also strongly resisted Ignatius Loyola, most of all Bartholomew Guidiccioni, the Cardinal, who, together with two others, was given Ignatius's Rule to examine by Paul III. They strongly dissuaded the confirmation of the Rule, and judged, rightly and prudently, that the older religious orders ought rather to be reformed than new ones founded.

units.la: L. Ægre etiam tulit Pontifex ipse, quod maiorem in Regula promitterent Generali suo Iesuitæ, quam sibi obedientiam. Sed horum prudentia Ignatij astutia opprimebatur: nam mutato hoc capite Regulæ, Papæ eandem potestatem quam Generali Ordinis concesserat tribuit: nimirum, ut summo Pontifici ad nutum præsto forent Socij, & omnino ad eam normam vitam dirigerent suam, quæ à se esset constituta, simul etiam promiserunt Pontifici diligentem institutionem puerorum. Quod quidem Papa Tibure tunc commorans, libentissime audivit, & Societatem approbavit 5. Non. Octob. Anno 1540. Atque ita præter omnium opinionem hæc nova Pharisæorum & hypocritarum Societas in tutela & patrocinium Romani Pontificis suscepta, & multis eorundem legibus, ac privilegiis 37. præ cæteris Monachorum Ordinibus munita & confirmata est.
units.tr: L. The Pontiff himself also took it ill that the Jesuits promised their General greater obedience in the Rule than they gave to him. But the prudence of these men was overcome by the cunning of Ignatius: for, this chapter of the Rule having been changed, he granted to the Pope the same power that he had granted to the General of the Order, namely that the companions should be at the Supreme Pontiff's beck and call, and should direct their whole life according to the norm laid down by him; at the same time they also promised the Pontiff diligent instruction of children. The Pope, then staying at Tivoli, heard this most willingly, and approved the Society on the 5th day before the Nones of October in the year 1540. And so, beyond everyone's expectation, this new society of Pharisees and hypocrites was taken under the protection and patronage of the Roman Pontiff, and was fortified and confirmed with many of his laws and privileges, and with thirty-seven more than the other orders of monks.

units.la: Duobus igitur dolis, impostu-ris ac fraudibus à Paulo 3. confirmatione sui Ordinis extorserunt & impetrarunt Iesuitæ: primo, promissione absolutæ obedientiæ erga sedem Romanam in omnibus, quæ eis præceperit, sive miserit eos ad Turcas, sive ad quoscunque alios infideles, etiam in partibus quas Indias vocant, existentes, sive quoscunque hæreticos, seu schismaticos, seu etiam ad quosvis fideles. Secundo, promissione Institutionis puerorum & rudium in Christianismo, decem præceptorum & aliorum rudimentorum. Neutrum autem præstiterunt: pauci in Indias proficiscuntur vel ad alios infideles, tota agmina sunt in orbe Christiano, ut ibi turbas, seditiones ac bella inter Christianos excitent: abiecta etiam puerorum institutione, adultiores tantum in Philosophia & Theologia instituunt.
units.tr: By two frauds, impostures and deceits, therefore, the Jesuits extorted and obtained from Paul III the confirmation of their Order: first, a promise of absolute obedience to the Roman See in all things that it should command, whether it sent them to the Turks, or to any other infidels, even those existing in the regions called the Indies, or to any heretics or schismatics, or even to any faithful. Second, a promise of instructing children and the unlearned in Christianity, in the Ten Commandments and other rudiments. Yet they have done neither: few set out for the Indies or to other infidels, while whole troops are throughout the Christian world, there to stir up tumults, sedition and wars among Christians; and, neglecting the instruction of children, they teach only their elders in philosophy and theology.

units.la: CAPVT VII. PRIVILEGIA à PONTIFICIBVS ROMANIS IESVITIS CONCESSA.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII. PRIVILEGES GRANTED TO THE JESUITS BY THE ROMAN PONTIFFS.

units.la: Quum igitur præter omnium opinionem hæc nova Pharisæorum & hypocritarum Secta & Societas in tutelam & patrocinium Romani Pontificum semel suscepta esset, mox eam multis privilegiis, præ cæteris Monachorum Ordinibus, immodice munierunt & extulerunt, eosque ipsos insolentissimos, arrogantissimos & audacissimos fecerunt.
units.tr: Since this new sect and society of Pharisees and hypocrites, beyond everyone's expectation, had once been taken under the protection and patronage of the Roman Pontiffs, they soon fortified and exalted it immoderately with many privileges, above the other monastic orders, and made those very men most insolent, arrogant and audacious.

units.la: Nam Paulus III. Rom. Pontifex in prima Bulla Iesuitis potestatem concessit I. pro libitu & arbitrio, in suæ Societatis usum & incrementum, Regulas & Constitutiones tot quotquot volunt condere: quarum tamen omnium scopus & finis sit, Confirmatio Pontificiæ sedis, ac Iesuiticæ Societatis ampliatio.
units.tr: For Paul III, Roman Pontiff, in his first Bull granted the Jesuits the power: (1) to draw up as many rules and constitutions as they wish, at their pleasure and discretion, for the use and increase of their Society, though the aim and end of all of them must be the confirmation of the Papal see and the expansion of the Jesuit Society.

units.la: II. Ignatio tribuit facultatem recipiendi 60. Socios: Ad hunc enim numerum Societas ista anno 1540. restricta fuerat. Astutè certè & callidè consilium, tum ut in eo numero artes ac vires Iesuitarum explorarent, tum si ere sua non videretur, eos facilius supprimeret. Iesuitæ vero, quos harum angustiarum tædebat, omnes nervos contendere, ut ex iis eluctari possent. Mirum igitur quàm sacramentis suam fidem suaque corpora devoverint, quaque frote supra monachalem audaciam commendarint. Nō potuit igitur Pontifex tam propta & lubentia mancipia aspernari, quæ vel sine mercede sola artis suæ confidentia servire gestiebant. Paulo post igitur Pontifex definitum hunc numerum in indefinitum auxit: ita ut nunc Iesuitarum Generali liceat, tot suscipere Socios, quot idoneos nancisci poterit.
units.tr: (2) He gave Ignatius the faculty of receiving sixty companions, for the Society had been restricted to this number in 1540. It was certainly a shrewd and cunning plan, both so that they could test the arts and strength of the Jesuits within that number, and so that, if the arrangement did not seem to their advantage, he could more easily suppress them. The Jesuits, however, weary of these restrictions, strained every nerve to break free of them. It is remarkable how they pledged their faith and their bodies by oath, and with what effrontery they surpassed monastic boldness. The Pontiff could not therefore spurn such ready and willing servants, who eagerly served even without wages, relying only on the confidence of their craft. Soon afterwards, therefore, the Pontiff enlarged this fixed number into an unlimited one, so that now the Jesuit General may take on as many companions as he can find suitable.

units.la: III. Omnibus anathemata & maledictionem minatur, qui hanc Societatem, ruinosæ Romanæ sedis conservatricem juvare renuant, vel impedire ea conentur.
units.tr: (3) He threatens with anathemas and curses all who refuse to help this Society, the preserver of the ruinous Roman see, or who attempt to hinder it.

units.la: In secunda Bulla his Socijs Anno 1543. egregia tribuit encomia, quibus illorum officiū depinxit. Primo enim affirmat, quod per eos religionis succrescat incrementum. Secundo tribuit illis fidei orthodoxæ dilatationē. Tertio divini nominis laude: quod sint nod sint in Theologia exercitati: Lutetiæ Parisiorum graduati, & à Spiritu Sancto afflati. Quarto, quod animarum sint zelantes.
units.tr: In the second Bull, in 1543, he bestowed splendid praises on these companions, by which he described their office. First, he affirms that through them religion grows. Second, he ascribes to them the spread of the orthodox faith. Third, he praises them in the name of God: that they are trained in theology, graduates of Paris, and inspired by the Holy Spirit. Fourth, that they are zealous for souls.

units.la: In tertia Bulla, cum Iesuitarum artes in seducendis hominibus Paulus III. videret, & agnosceret ipsos præreliquis Ordinibus omnibus Pontificiæ doctrinæ & idolomaniæ propagandæ studiosè invigilare, necnon profectu illorum animadverteret, noluit hanc suam novam creaturam, ut reliquos Monachos inter luxuriosa tecta latitare: sed comptulos abscq; cuculla prodire: hominum negotijs se immiscuare: Scholas & templa occuparet, sedulamq; operam navare, ut omnia Pontificia officia recte, & secundum Papæ voluntatem & nutum curentur, ne quid detrimenti Romana Ecclesia acciperet. Numerum igitur sexaginta Sociorum abogavit, liberumq; Ignatio & successoribus reliquit, quemlibet petentem in Societatem recipere. Concessit insuper illis facultatem ubicunque locorum pro lubitu concionandi, & quorumcunque utriusque sexus ad eos undecunque accedentium consessiones audiendi, & confessionibus eorum diligenter auditis, ipsos & eorum singulos ab omnibus & singulis eorum peccatis, criminibus, excessibus & delictis, quacunque gravibus & enormibus, etiam Sedi Apostolicæ reservatis, & à quibuscunque exijs casibus resultantibus sententijs, censuris & poenis Ecclesiasticis (exceptis in Bulla contentis, quæ in die Coenæ Dominicæ solita est legi) absolvendi, ac eis pro commissis poenitentiam iniungendi. Concessit etiam potestate vota, peregrinationes, &c. pro tempore commutandi: Missam ante diei exortum, & post meridiem celebrandi: Euchristica Sacramenta administrandi: Officium Romanum novum, non ex præcepto, sed ex liberate dicendi. Item, ut Assistentes sint & Cardinales, quæ resistetes Iesuitis compescant, & rebelles in eos tollant. Factum Pr-íd. Idus Martias Anno 1543.
units.tr: In the third Bull, Paul III, seeing the Jesuits' arts in seducing men, and recognising that they, beyond all the other orders, were diligently watchful in spreading Papal doctrine and idolatry, and noticing their progress, did not want this new creature of his to lurk among the luxurious houses like the other monks. Instead, they were to go out in light cloaks without cowls, to involve themselves in men's affairs, to occupy schools and churches, and to take diligent care that all Papal offices be carried out rightly and according to the Pope's will and nod, lest the Roman Church suffer any harm. He therefore fixed the number of sixty companions, and left it free to Ignatius and his successors to admit into the Society whoever sought admission. He further granted them the power to preach wherever they pleased, and to hear the confessions of anyone of either sex who came to them from anywhere; and, having heard their confessions diligently, to absolve them and each of them from all and each of their sins, crimes, excesses and offences, however grave and enormous, even those reserved to the Apostolic See, and from whatever cases and resulting sentences, censures and ecclesiastical penalties (except those contained in the Bull which is customarily read on Maundy Thursday), and to impose penance on them for what they had committed. He also granted the power to commute vows, pilgrimages and so on as circumstances required; to celebrate Mass before sunrise and after noon; to administer the Eucharistic sacraments; and to recite the new Roman Office not as a precept but at their liberty. Likewise, that cardinals should be assistants who restrain those resisting the Jesuits and remove rebels against them. Done the day before the Ides of March, 1543.

units.la: In quarta Bulla Paulus III. 1546. ad instantiam Iesuitarum potestatem illis fecit ut socios suos in certas distinguant species, admittant scilicet & suscipiat Coadjutores spirituales & temporales, Sacerdotes & Seculares. Horum autem officium exprimunt attributo Coadjutorum: quorum officium est, in omnibus, ad nutu tamen Rectoris, Societatem adiuvare. Et hi sunt reliquorum ministri & servi: quales sunt eamentes vendentes, coqui, sutores, sartores, pistores, cellarij. Hi, quod tatum circa res occupantur externas, nec, ut reliqui, misificent, vel horas canonicas celebrent Temporales vocantur, vel Seculares ut paulo ante diximus. Reliquos vero, qui Missas peragunt, vocant Patres Spirituales.
units.tr: In the fourth Bull, Paul III, in 1546, at the instance of the Jesuits, gave them the power to divide their companions into certain classes, namely to admit and receive spiritual and temporal coadjutors, priests and laymen. They express the office of these coadjutors by the title "coadjutors", whose duty is, in all things, to help the Society, though at the nod of the Rector. These are the servants and slaves of the rest, such as money-changers, cooks, shoemakers, tailors, bakers and cellarers. Since they are occupied only with external matters, and do not, like the others, say Mass or celebrate the canonical hours, they are called temporal or secular, as we said a little above. The rest, who perform Masses, they call Spiritual Fathers.

units.la: Ne autem Seculares hi Coadiutores putent se non tot habere meritas, quot consequuntur illi qui etiam Professionis suæ votum, quo sese corporibus & animabus Papæ in mancipia tradunt, suscepererunt: ideo facit illis Patribus potestatem etiam hos Coadjutores ad sacros ordines promovendi, & participes reddendi meritorum, quibus gaudent Iesuitæ Professi, illi nempe qui peculiari voto se Papæ devoverunt.
units.tr: Lest these lay coadjutors think they do not earn as many merits as those who have also taken the vow of profession, by which they surrender their bodies and souls to the Pope as slaves, he therefore gave those Fathers the power to promote these coadjutors also to holy orders, and to make them sharers in the merits which the professed Jesuits enjoy, namely those who have devoted themselves to the Pope by a special vow.

units.la: In quinta Paulus III. Cal. Novemb. Anno 1549. Iesuitas mirifice commendat: nempe quod sint ager fertilis in Domino: quod uberes animarum fructus pariant: quod verbo & exemplis prosint: quod sint pij Patres & oculi mentis Papæ. Vult etiam, Generalem, plenariam & omnimodam, eamq; liberam potestatem habere, omnes Iesuitas, secundum suas institutiones gubernandi: nec sit ille ulli Cardinalium vel Episcoporum, verum soli & uni Pontifici subjectus. Cum quo etiam solo, res Societatis & Sedis Apostolicæ conferendæ, consilia & rationes tractet. Ne autem Generalis ille Pontificatum affectet, vel quid cum suis vel aliis, contra Ecclesiæ Rom. auctoritatem præsumat, concedit Socijs, has & alias ob causas Generalem suum, qui alias tum per suos primatum Papæ tuetur, perpetuus esse debet, amovendi, aliumq; secundum suas regulas substituendi. Sin autem Papæ tantum primatum, Apostolicæ Sedis auctoritatem & Societatis suæ dignitatem quærat, posse illum etiam inconsulto Papa suos quocunq; velit emittere & revocare, nulla temporis li-mitatione adhibita. Hinc est crebra illa Iesuitarum mutatio.
units.tr: In the fifth Bull, Paul III on 1 November 1549 commends the Jesuits wonderfully: that they are a fertile field in the Lord; that they bear abundant fruit of souls; that they profit by word and example; that they are pious Fathers and the eyes of the Pope's mind. He also wills that their General have full, plenary and unlimited power, and free power, to govern all Jesuits according to their institutes; and that he be subject to no Cardinal or Bishop, but to the one Pontiff alone. With him alone he is to treat the affairs of the Society and of the Apostolic See, and to confer on counsels and plans. Lest the General aspire to the Papacy, or presume anything with his own men or others against the authority of the Roman Church, he grants to the companions that, for these and other reasons, their General, who otherwise defends the primacy of the Pope through his men, must be perpetual, though he may be removed and another substituted according to their rules. But if he seeks only the primacy of the Pope, the authority of the Apostolic See and the dignity of his Society, he may send out and recall any of his men whenever he wishes, even without consulting the Pope, with no limit of time. Hence arises that frequent shifting of the Jesuits.

units.la: Concedit praeterea Generali quod possit absolvere omnes haereticos confitentes cum irregularibus dispensare: absolutos, nisi Societatem ingredi, vel vota emittere velit, retrahere: cogere suos, ut vel ipsi, vel ei, quem ordinaverit, confiteantur: suos devotorios nullum nisi Carthusiensem ordinem ingredi posse. Generali datur etiam potestas, Iesuitas alium Ordinem sine venia ingressos, maxime apostatas, ut loquuntur, factos, aut in Societate insolentes, vel contradicentes, vel illorum Regulas in apertum producentes, vel illorum vota revelantes, in quocunque habitu tangerit inveniri, excommunicare, et si opus sit, auxilio brachij secularis invocato, liberè et licitè invadere, captivos ducere, et pro arbitrio tractare.
units.tr: He further grants the General that he may absolve all confessing heretics, dispense with irregularities, and withdraw those absolved unless they wish to enter the Society or take vows; that he may compel his men to confess either to themselves or to whomever he appoints; and that his devoted men may enter no order except the Carthusian. The General is also given the power to excommunicate, wherever they may be found and in whatever dress, any Jesuits who have entered another order without permission, especially those who have become apostates, as they say, or who are insolent or contradictory within the Society, or who make its Rules public, or who reveal its vows; and, if necessary, invoking the aid of the secular arm, to attack them freely and lawfully, take them captive, and treat them at his discretion.

units.la: Deinde Iesuitarum maximas opes vult esse omnino liberas, socios vult esse nulli tributarios, nullius exactioni, vectigali, censui vel usuris subiectos, una cum tota Societate. Sic enim verba Bullae habent: Ipsa vero Societas et illorum bona, ab omni superioritate, jurisdictione et correctione omnium sunt exempta, liberata, et sub protectione Papae.
units.tr: Then they want the Jesuits' very great resources to be entirely free; they want the companions to be subject to no tribute, no exaction, tax, levy, census or usury, together with the whole Society. For the words of the Bull are: But the Society itself and its goods are exempt from all superiority, jurisdiction and correction of all, are freed, and are under the protection of the Pope.

units.la: Tribuit etiam eis, Oratoria et usum Altaris portabilis. Dum enim per Christianorum loca exploratores et proditores agunt, neque ubique altaria consecrata, in quibus Missam celebrent, habere possunt, secum altare vel mappulam, in illum usum deputatam, portant.
units.tr: He also granted them oratories and the use of a portable altar. For since they act as scouts and traitors through Christian lands, and cannot have consecrated altars everywhere on which to celebrate Mass, they carry with them an altar or altar-cloth set apart for that use.

units.la: Adhaec non solum Iesuitas, aut illorum bona, sed etiam ipsorum Regulas ab omnium Praelatorum censura exemptas esse vult. Sic enim habent verba Bullae: Nulli Praelatorum, excepto Papa, licere, vel concessum esse constitutiones Iesuitarum sub censuram sumere: aut sumentem nihil efficere, illiusque conatum nullius esse roboris. Hinc etiam Iesuitae, ut supra quoque indicatum est, suis in Regulis mandant, ne quis illis cuiquam extraneorum concedat vel communicet, vel quidquam de illis referat dicto vel scripto.
units.tr: Moreover, he wills that not only the Jesuits and their goods but also their Rules be exempt from the censure of all prelates. For the words of the Bull are: No prelate, except the Pope, may take up the constitutions of the Jesuits under censure, nor is he permitted or granted to do so; and if he attempts it, he accomplishes nothing, and his attempt has no force. Hence also the Jesuits, as was indicated above, order in their Rules that no one should grant or communicate them to any outsider, or report anything about them by word or in writing.

units.la: Mandat etiam aliis hominibus, ut Iesuitas illorumque substantias defendant.
units.tr: He also commands other men to defend the Jesuits and their property.

units.la: Permisit etiam in hac Bulla, ut quicunque, velint neglecto suo parocho, Iesuitarum Missas audire, et ab ipsis Sacramentum percipere, id impune facere possint.
units.tr: In this same Bull he also permits that whoever wishes, neglecting his own parish priest, may hear the Masses of the Jesuits and receive the sacrament from them, and may do so with impunity.

units.la: Concedit item Papa Paulus in eadem Bulla, ut tot Sacerdotes curent ab Episcopis Romanis radi, chrismari, ungi et consecrari, quot voluerint.
units.tr: Pope Paul also grants in the same Bull that as many priests as they wish may be tonsured, chrismed, anointed and consecrated by Roman bishops.

units.la: Permittit etiam, Ut ad haereticos ire, et in illorum regionibus liberè commorari, cumque ijsdem versari possint, de licentia tamen Generalis vel Praepositi, a quibus in ijs locis necessaria petunt et recipiunt. Huiusmodi Iesuitarum multi, nunc habitu studiosorum, nunc nobilium, modo alio atque alio circumvagantur; qui etiam se mirifice apud homines insinuare noverunt, indeque fit, ut saepe Principum, Theologorum, Ecclesiarum, Scholarum et Rerumpubl. res et statum melius, quam illi ipsi norint. Et has suas proditorias artes hoc sophismate excusant, quod Papa id mandarit ac iusserit.
units.tr: He also permits that they may go among heretics and live freely in their lands, and associate with them, provided they have the licence of the General or the Provost, from whom they seek and receive what they need in those places. Many Jesuits of this kind wander about in many guises, now as students, now as nobles, and in one disguise or another. They also know how to insinuate themselves wonderfully among people, and so it often happens that they know the affairs and condition of princes, theologians, churches, schools and commonwealths better than those people know them themselves. And they excuse these treacherous arts by this sophism, that the Pope has commanded and ordered it.

units.la: Ne autem in his expediendis, aliis forte negotiis impediantur, ideo vult haec ipsa Bulla, ut ab omni visitatione et cura Monialium, vel aliarum religiosarum personarum liberi et immunes sint.
units.tr: Lest they be hindered in carrying out these matters by other business, this same Bull wills that they be free and immune from all visitation and oversight of nuns or other religious persons.

units.la: Eadem Bulla Papa ab omni contributione Iesuitarum bona exemit. Non tenentur Iesuitae, inquit, solvere decimam bonorum, vel aliam dare contributionem; seu procurationem, nec Papalem, nec Canonicalem portionem. Etiamsi prius fuerunt illa bona sub censu: nisi fit id specifice et expresse in literis Apostolicis. Ab omni quoque Episcoporum iure, interpellatione et impedimento eximit. Adhaec Episcopis mandat, ut illorum domos et templa consecrent: impedientes vero illorum vel Scholas, vel templa reprehendit; et desistere nolentes excommunicat, illorumque bona Iesuitis tribuit.
units.tr: The same Bull frees the Jesuits' goods from every contribution. The Jesuits are not bound, it says, to pay a tithe of their goods or to give any other contribution or procuration, neither the papal nor the canonical portion. This holds even if those goods were previously subject to a tax, unless this is stated specifically and expressly in apostolic letters. He also exempts them from all the jurisdiction, interference and obstruction of bishops. Further, he orders the bishops to consecrate their houses and churches; he rebukes those who hinder their schools or churches, excommunicates those who refuse to desist, and assigns their goods to the Jesuits.

units.la: Ne quoque desint homines qui Iesuitas in Papatu fulciendo adiuvent, dat illis ut illis facultatem quoscunque volunt irregulares & feculares recipere & ad sua ministeria promovere. Hinc dixit Landspergensium Iesuitarum Rector Anno millesimo quingentesimo octogesimo quarto. Sunt in Romana Ecclesia ordines, quorum aliqui non nisi doctos, alij non nisi nobiles, alij non nisi ex legitimo conjugio natos recipiunt: at nobis auctoritate Pontificia permissum est, bonos & malos, fures & latrones, quoscunque volumus recipere: modo se Papæ & nobis subjiciant, nosque secundum Societatis institutum juvent.
units.tr: So that there may be no lack of men to help the Jesuits in upholding the Papacy, he gives them the power to receive and promote to their ministries whatever irregular and lay persons they wish. Hence the rector of the Jesuits at Landsberg said in the year 1584: "There are orders in the Roman Church, of which some accept only the learned, others only nobles, others only those born of lawful marriage; but to us it has been permitted by papal authority to receive good and bad, thieves and robbers, whomever we wish, provided they submit themselves to the Pope and to us and help us according to the institute of the Society."

units.la: Vt etiam Iesuitarum ædes, collegia, templa & scholæ frequententur, & ro sacrosanctis colantur, hominesque in illis offerant, addit Bulla; Eum qui Iesuitarum Ecclesiam aliquam, vel alium pium eorum locum à Præposito signatum, semel in anno visitaverit, indulgentiam plenariam omnium peccatorum consequi.
units.tr: So that the houses, colleges, churches and schools of the Jesuits may be frequented, venerated as holy, and that people may make their offerings in them, the Bull adds: whoever visits any church of the Jesuits, or another pious place of theirs marked out by the Provost, once in the year obtains a plenary indulgence of all sins.

units.la: Tandem in hac Bulla datur illis potestas absolvendi etiam ab ijs, quæ Papa sibi in Bulla Cœnæ reservavit, & omnia quæ sunt Episcoporum peragere: qualia sunt ordinare, ungere, chrismare, adiurare, exorcizare, confirmare, reformare, indulgentias distribuere, divortia facere, cum consanguineis dispensare, templa consecrare, campanas baptizare, statuta nova facere, & similia, quæ in Papatu Episcoporum sunt propria.
units.tr: Finally, in this Bull they are given the power to absolve also from those cases which the Pope reserved to himself in the Bull of the Lord's Supper, and to perform all the functions of bishops: such as ordaining, anointing, chrismating, adjuring, exorcising, confirming, reforming, distributing indulgences, granting divorces, dispensing with blood relatives, consecrating churches, baptising bells, making new statutes, and the like, which in Papistry are proper to bishops.

units.la: Vult etiam, Ne quis his Iesuitarum ausis se opponat, aut super ea appellet. Præsipit quoque Principes, Prælatos & alios in regno suo potentes jurare, ne quis Iesuiticam Societatem inquietet, vel privilegijs spoliet, vel impediat: inobedientes anathemate ferit, & seculáris brachij gladio punire jubet. Hanc Bullam Iesuitæ Mare magnum vocant, quod in ea omnis generis privilegia ipsis non aliter, quam in Oceano navibus onerarijs merces advehantur.
units.tr: It also wills that no one oppose these audacious acts of the Jesuits or appeal against them. He further orders princes, prelates and others powerful in his kingdom to swear that no one will disturb the Jesuit Society, despoil it of its privileges, or hinder it. He strikes the disobedient with anathema and orders them punished by the sword of the secular arm. The Jesuits call this Bull the Great Sea, because in it privileges of every kind are carried to them just as merchant goods are carried by freight ships on the ocean.

units.la: Dignissimus certe est Iesuitarum Ordo tali confirmatore & patrono Paulo Tertio Pontifice. Ante mortem eius editus est libellus Italicus, cum Præfatione ad Afcanium Columnam, quem ille profligarat; In hoc libello author varia & immanissima quidem scelera recenset, & Antichristum illum appellans, Innocentio Pontifice, inquit, conjectus in vincula fuisti; Præsul iniquissime, proter homicidia duo, & commissum parricidium, matre nimirum & nepote tuo quodam veneno sublatis, ut omnis ad te confluet hereditas, cumque deinde liber factus, non dubitares ambire galerum purpureum, & ter esses a Collegio repudiatus, germana tua soror Iulia Farnesia, tandem pervicit. Cum enim copiam sui non se facturam esse deinceps minaretur, Alexander Sextus Pontifex, offensionem veritus, & iram illius, in Cardinalium te cœtum allegit. Alteram deinde sororem, pro familiæ tuæ consuetudine arum pudicam, interemisti quoque veneno. Per Anconitanam provinciam cum esses Legatus, Iulio Secundo Pontifice, puellam eius civitatis nefarie circumvenisti, nando dissimulans quis esses, teque pro nobili quopiam gerens ex legati familiaribus, illam vitiasti: quod quidem facinus puellæ patruelis, Cardinalis Anconitanus, urbe apta, coram Clemente Pontifice captivo, tibi gravissimis verbis objecit. Nicolaus Quercæus, cum Laura Farnesia, tua nepte, conjuge sua te congredientem, deprehenait, & pugione tibi vulnus incussit, cuius etiamnum cicatrix apparet. De filia tua Constantia, quacum toties rem habuisti, quid dicam? etenim ut ea liberius potiri posses, maritum eius Bosium Sfortiam sustulisti veneno, qui cum nequitiam vestram animadvertisset, incredibilem animo dolorem concepit, nec ynquam postea visus est hilaris. Libidine porro Commodum & Heliogabalum longe superas: idque tot spuriis tuis doceri potest. Filias suas Loth vitiavit ignarus & ebrius: tu vero sobrius, non modo cum nepte, sed etiam cum sorore congressus es atque filia. Iam illud, quod in Faensem Episcopum admisit sceleratus ille tuus filius Petrus Aloisius, quam est dictu foedum & horrendum facinus? Cum in Adriani mole captivus detineretur Clemens Pontifex, teque legaret ad Cæsarem, libertatis recuperandæ causa, nonprius iter voluisses ingredi, quàm ille Parmensem Episcopatum, nepoti tuo Farnesio, tunc decem annorum adolescenti, permitteret. Eo facto, ludificasti nihilominus illum, & Genuam ubi pervenisses, morbo te detineri simulabas. Quam vero nundinationem in sacris bonis non exercuisti Cardinalis? & postquam factus es Pontifex, Deum immortalem, quàm turpiter Ecclesiæ Romanæ facultates dilapidasti? Non tepudet, summam præfecturam atque munus contulisse nefario tuo filio, cum aureorum millibus annuis quadraginta, totidemque fere nepoti Octavio: ne quid interim dicam, quæ quantaque bona profuderis in tuæ familiæ fœminas omneis, & Sanflorianas neptes. Turcarum postea mentionem audies inferre, qui miseræ jam incumbant Italiæ. Quid eo facis, ut expilandi populi causam aliquam habeas & occasionem, qui sub te Domino gravissimum onus & intolerabile profectò sustinet. Duci Ferrariensi Mutinam atque Rhegium vendidisti: Parmam & Placentiam, quas Ecclesiæ Romanæ minimè acquisiveras, alienasti, quod Clementem certè Pontificem facere puduit. Ut familiam domumque tuam locupletares, præter fas & æquum alios exagitasti, & eos, qui servitutem illam ferre non poterant, aut recusabant, bello es persecutus: id Perusini docent, inter alios, & Afcanius Columna. Qui subsidij loco suis imperat quotannis extra ordinem aureorum millia trecenta, qui novum subinde vectigal imponit, modò salis, modò caeterarum rerum, qui nunc decimas, nunc dimidiam fructuum partem exigit, ille sane pro Christiani sanguinis hoste merito debet haberi. Turcica classis, te Pontifice, per Ecclesiæ Romanæ fines navigavit incolumis, non itapridem, quando Barbarossa mare nostrum fuit ingressus. Occultum igitur illud, quod cum Barbaris habes commercium, animam tibi præscindit, quo minus Turcici belli nomen in posterum obducas.
