units.la: Probationum regulæ, secundum quas magistri Novitiorum eosdem primâ, cundâ & tertiâ probatione, examinare debent diligentissimè inquirendo.
units.tr: The rules of trials, according to which the masters of novices must examine the same men most diligently in the first, second and third trial.

units.la: Regula, quæ tit. de Magistris Novitiorum capite secundo, vers. quinquaesimo primo de consuetudine condiscipulorum traditur, observatu dignsisima est, & talis, ut in omnibus Collegiis ubi professionis ratio habetur, exactissime servanda: id quoque recte monitum videtur, quod ingeniorum delectu magis boni communis ad gloriam Dei, quàm particularis cuiusque ratio habenda sit.
units.tr: The rule given under the title on the masters of novices, chapter 2, verse 51, concerning the company of fellow students, deserves the greatest notice, and is such that it must be most exactly kept in all colleges where a profession is made. It is also rightly warned that in choosing minds, regard should be had to the common good for the glory of God rather than to the particular advantage of each.

units.la: Ad magnitudinem quoque secularis Iesuitarum potentiæ pertinet, exactisma illa per universum orbem Correspondentia, cuius utilitas & forma repræsentantur in Titulo de formulâ scribendi, ubi versu primo dicitur, quòd commercium frequens literarum inter inferiores & superiores, maximè ad unionem in Societate servandam faciat, ad audienda ea, quæ ex variis locis ad disificationem, & eorum, quæ geruntur cognitionem adferuntur, & ostendiar in sequentibus versiculis, quibus modis illud commercium fit exercendum. Verum vers. undecimo, manifestè apparet, eam correspondentiam non ad domorum & Collegiorum suorum statum cognoscendum tantum pertinere, sed ad ipsius status politici arcana scrutanda: additur enim, ut totius provinciæ statum bene explicent & suppleant, si quid intellexerint, quod Superiores domorum Collegiorum minùs declaraverunt, & in universum ita scribere debet, ut generalis omnium rerum, omniumq; personarum ac provinciarum statuum, quoad eius fieri possit, ante oculos habeat. Quis quaso nunc Iesuitas exactissimos omnium rerum exploratores & perrimatores esse negaverit? cùm hæc ipsi iis scriptis fateantur. Quis nunc negaverit Iesuitas sub prætextu religionis rena & imperia scrutari & petere?
units.tr: To the greatness of the Jesuits' worldly power also belongs that most exact correspondence throughout the whole world, whose usefulness and form are set out under the title on the form of writing. There, in verse 1, it is said that a frequent exchange of letters between inferiors and superiors especially serves to keep unity in the Society, to hear the news brought from various places for edification, and to know what is happening. The following verses show in what ways this exchange is to be carried on. But in verse 11 it is plainly evident that this correspondence serves not only to know the state of their houses and colleges, but to search out the secrets of the political state itself. For it is added that they should explain and supplement the condition of the whole province, if they have understood anything which the superiors of the houses and colleges have not declared fully, and that in general they should write in such a way as to keep before their eyes, as far as possible, a general picture of all affairs, of all persons, and of the states of the provinces. Who, I ask, will now deny that the Jesuits are the most exact spies and searchers out of everything, since they themselves confess this in those writings? Who will now deny that the Jesuits, under the pretext of religion, search out and seek after kingdoms and empires?

units.la: Verum cùm tantam vaferrimi hi veteratores ex sola correspondentia utilitatem ad unionem inter Romanenses tuendam, sentiant, non abs re est, quod illi qui Reges & Principes Romanenses in sua manu habent, isdem persadeant, ut gravibus propositis pœnis, Evangelicos, ab illo literarum commercio absterreant, hoc enim medio illis sublato, neque de communibus periculis, neque de artibus & machinationibus quæ in illos consuuntur, invicem præmonere penitus possunt, nec mutuis consiliis & ope iuvari: deinde si correspondentia Iesuitis Tyrannidis Romanæ propagatoribus ad unionem suam longe lateque propagandam & diffundendam summè sit utilis; consequitur, ut eiusdem defectus, Evangelicis & liberis Statibus maximas haud dubiè adferat incommoditates, isdemque ob id per coniuratos Romanenses prohibita, ut ita rebellium gentes internis discordiis relinquerentur, illisque piscatio illa hominum in aquis turbatis eo liberior remaneat, qui in tenebris ambulant, lucem oderunt: huius communionis & commercij Christiani utilitas, quia tanti momenti est, pro concionibus & scriptis publicis pro dignitate omnibusque & singulis tam Regibus, Principibus & Magistratibus Christianis & liberis, quàm Rectoribus & Professoribus veritatis commendanda est, ut Anrichristi fraudibus retectis, Ecclesiæ Christi adversus eas tepestive & fortiter caveri, & locustarum & viperarum illarum agmina, in puteum abyssi, unde prodierunt, repelli & præcipitari queant ocyus possint: tantùm semper erunt privata (quæ in publicorum neglectu periclitantur, neque extra eorum tutelam salva esse possunt) ut tolerabilius esse credatur, in publicis perire privata, præ nimio privatorum studio male publica curando, quàm ad modicum privatis simultatibus & actionibus suspensis, pro salute publica adversus communem hostem vigilare; & in publicis privata tueri.
units.tr: But since these most crafty old campaigners perceive such great usefulness from correspondence alone for maintaining unity among the Romanists, it is not out of place that those who hold the Roman kings and princes in their hand should persuade them, by proposing heavy penalties, to frighten the Evangelicals away from that exchange of letters. For once this means is removed, they can no longer warn one another of common dangers, nor of the arts and machinations contrived against them, nor be helped by mutual counsel and aid. Further, if correspondence is most useful to the Jesuits, the propagators of Roman tyranny, for extending and spreading their unity far and wide, it follows that its lack must undoubtedly bring the greatest inconveniences to the Evangelical and free states. For this reason it is forbidden by the Roman conspirators, so that the rebellious nations may be left to internal discord, and that fishing for men in troubled waters may remain freer for them, those who walk in darkness and hate the light. The usefulness of this Christian communion and exchange, since it is of such moment, must be commended in sermons and public writings, with due dignity, to all and each of the Christian and free kings, princes and magistrates, as well as to the rulers and professors of the truth. Thus, with the frauds of Antichrist exposed, the Church of Christ may be guarded against them in good time and bravely, and those swarms of locusts and vipers may be driven back and thrown quickly into the pit of the abyss from which they came. Private matters will always remain (these are endangered when public matters are neglected, and cannot be safe outside their protection), so that it may be thought more tolerable that private matters perish amid public ones, through excessive devotion to private affairs and poor care of public ones, than that, with private quarrels and activities set aside for a little while, we keep watch for public safety against the common enemy, and protect private matters within public ones.

units.la: Notandum quoque est, quod de Præfecto Rerum Spiritualium statuitur, ut nimirum secundum cognitionem instituti Societatis zelo magno diligenter illud promoveat & tepidos exhortetur, &c. tanta enim est pluriuum oscitatio, ut neque frigidi neque calidi, nulloque affectu aut commiseratione ducantur, modo sibi bene sit, quîa in re quàm necessarium sit charitatis doctoribus, tepiditatem & oscitantiam illam non tantum charitate Christiana, sed & viris bonis indignißimam, decantare, omnes perpendere velim, qui se eiusdem Christi membra esse sciunt & profitentur; an autem minimum hominis membrum dolere possit, cui tota totius corporis sensum?
units.tr: It must also be noted what is laid down about the Prefect of Spiritual Affairs, namely that, according to the knowledge of the Society's institute, he should diligently promote it with great zeal and exhort the lukewarm, and so on. For such is the drowsiness of most people that they are moved neither by coldness nor by heat, nor by any feeling or compassion, provided that it goes well for themselves. How necessary it is for teachers of charity to denounce that lukewarmness and drowsiness, which is most unworthy not only of Christian charity but even of good men, I would like everyone to consider who knows and professes himself to be a member of the same Christ. For can the smallest member of a man feel pain when the whole body has its sense?

units.la: Quòd autem institutum Iesuitarum non tantùm ad privatæ rei amplificationem & magnitudinem, sed ad omnia totius orbis regna sub Romanæ Sedis iugum reducenda, tendat, supra ostensum est; verum quod contra nullos maiore odio quàm adversus hæreticos & Septentrionales ferantur, ex eo constat, quòd in Catalogo Missarum & Orationum ad finem præcipitur, ut frequentia osserantur sacrificia & circumvolutentur Rosaria, pro Septentrionalium & hæreticorum reductione: hoc cum multos ex illis lateat, aut si isdem notum esse possit, non satis sibi ab eo caveant; movendi & serió hortandi esse videntur, ut tanti micidas maiore quàm ante odio prosequantur, ac Duplum illis iuxta doctrinam D. Iohannis Apocal. 18. retribuant.
units.tr: That the institute of the Jesuits aims not merely at enlarging and magnifying its own private affair, but at bringing all the kingdoms of the world under the yoke of the Roman See, has been shown above. But that they bear no greater hatred against anyone than against heretics and Northerners is clear from this: in the Catalogue of Masses and Prayers it is commanded at the end that sacrifices be offered frequently and rosaries be recited round and round for the conversion of the Northerners and heretics. Since many of these men lie hidden, or, if they can be known to them, the Jesuits do not take sufficient care to guard against them, they seem to need to be moved and earnestly exhorted to pursue such murderers with greater hatred than before, and to repay them double, according to the teaching of St. John in Apocalypse 18.

units.la: Operarios, quibus ex obedientia confessionis audiendi sanctum munus committur, in tit. Regulæ Sacerdotum vers. 5. volunt, multum ad id assici, & tàquam sui instituti valde proprium, magnificare, nec sine magna causa. Nihil enim aptius est, nõ solum ad familiarum & matrimoniorum, sed & imperiorum, Regnorum & Rerumpub. arcana scrutanda, unde etiam in Venetorum Repub. Auricularis confessio illis penitus interdicta, sed nihil est, si serpentis cauda feriatur, tenendum est caput, si venenum devitare velimus.
units.tr: The workers to whom the holy office of hearing confession is committed by the obedience of the confessional, they want (in the title of the Rules for Priests, verse 5) to be much devoted to this and to magnify it as very proper to their institute, and not without great cause. For nothing is better suited not only for searching out the secrets of families and marriages, but also of empires, kingdoms and commonwealths; for which reason auricular confession was completely forbidden to them even in the Venetian Republic. But it is nothing, if we wish to avoid the poison, to strike the tail of the serpent; the head must be held.

units.la: Libidinis quoque suspicionem à se avertere omni cura conantur, in vers. 18. suprad. tit. ut & in Sùmario Constit. vers. 8. & seq. maximè autem in confessionibus mulierum. Verùm quæ illorum in iis impudicitiæ in omnibus locis, ubi illi lupanaria sua spiritualia collocârunt, palàm est, & recens Brûtrû tensibus in agro Baliliensi. Sic quoq; avaritiæ studiū à se multis huius libri titulis & in aliis suis scriptis, varissimè tegere conātur: speciosè autem in ultimo vers. tituli suprad. ubi Confessores monentur, ut ægrotos, cum opus sit, ad condenda testamenta adhortentur, sed iis conficiendis non assistant. Quod quàm diligenter ab illis alienarum hæreditatum cæptoribus observetur, ex Collegijs, Domibus vel suppellectilibus, fundis & redditibus illorum satis apparet: ideoque vel hîc vel in Summatio Constitut. vers.23. & seqq. Iesuitica paupertas, ut murus religionis firmus, exemplis diuitiarum illorum illustranda.
units.tr: They also try with all care to turn away from themselves suspicion of lust, in verse 18 of the aforesaid title, as also in the Summary of the Constitutions, verse 8 and following, and especially in the confessions of women. But what their impurity in these matters is, in all the places where they have set up their spiritual brothels, is plain, and recently in the countryside of Basel. So too they try in many ways to cover over their zeal for greed, in the titles of this book and in their other writings; but they do so speciously in the last verse of the aforesaid title, where confessors are urged to encourage the sick, when need arises, to make their wills, but not to be present at drawing them up. How diligently they observe this in seizing the inheritances of others is sufficiently evident from their colleges, houses, furnishings, estates and revenues. Therefore, either here or in the Summary of the Constitutions, verses 23 and following, Jesuit poverty, as a firm wall of religion, must be illustrated by the examples of their riches.

units.la: Concionatorum Regulæ tradunt, illos quidem lectioni S. Scripturæ incumbere debere, sed præcipuè Patrum, tanquam si Patres Patre ipso sanctius docuissent, à fontibus suos ad riuulos seducendo, quæ illorum perversitas comprobatur regula 6. præfecti, lectores ad mensam, ubi in celebrioribus festis præcipitur liquid legi omisso capite Scripturæ, ex Patrum homilijs & tractatibus, neglecta lectione Scripturarum, tanquam nimis vulgari & cotidiana, indigna ut celebrioribus diebus audiretur.
units.tr: The rules for preachers teach that they ought to devote themselves to reading Holy Scripture, but especially the Fathers, as though the Fathers had taught more holily than the Father himself, leading people away from the fountains to the streamlets. Their perversity is shown by the sixth rule of the prefect, concerning readers at table, where on more solemn feasts it is commanded that something be read, with the chapter of Scripture omitted, from the homilies and treatises of the Fathers, Scripture being neglected as too common and everyday, and unworthy to be heard on the more solemn days.

units.la: Decima Concionatoribus regula iniungit, ut populum obedientiam eâ doceant, quæ Principibus & Prælatis, qui Dei in terris vices gerunt, à subditis exhibenda est: Vbi notandum verba qui Dei in terris, intelligenda esse, Dei terrestris, id est, Pontificis, cui cæca obedientia parendum est, vices gerit: Nam iis qui vices illius non gerunt, sub pœna excommunicationis prævaricatores illi prævaricando obtemperare prohibuerunt.
units.tr: The tenth rule enjoins on preachers that they teach the people obedience of the kind that is to be shown by subjects to princes and prelates, who bear the place of God on earth. Here it must be noted that the words "who bear the place of God on earth" are to be understood as bearing the place of the earthly God, that is, of the Pope, to whom blind obedience must be rendered. For to those who do not bear his place, under penalty of excommunication, they have forbidden the transgressors to obey, by transgressing.

units.la: Quod ipsi Iesuitæ in Gallijs & alibi exemplis irrefutabilibus demonstrarunt, docentes, Regem sibi rebellem à quovis legitimè cædi & occidi posse.
units.tr: This the Jesuits themselves have demonstrated by irrefutable examples in France and elsewhere, teaching that a king who is rebellious against them may be lawfully slain and killed by anyone.

units.la: Astutè præcipitur in 19. Regula Concionatorum, ut non ita exactè proponant argumenta, quibus contraria pars confirmetur, ne simpliciores ipso propoendi modo offendi possent: sciunt enim veteratores, isti veritatis argumenta superstitionis figmentis longè firmiora, ideoque fraude tacendi, illa simplices celanda esse statuunt.
units.tr: Shrewdly it is laid down in the 19th rule for preachers that they should not set out the arguments by which the opposing side is confirmed too exactly, lest the simpler sort be offended by the very manner of proposing them. For these cunning men know that the arguments of truth are far firmer than the fictions of superstition, and therefore they decide that by the fraud of silence those arguments must be concealed from the simple.

units.la: Concionatorum regula vigesima illi suis prohibent verborum lenocinia, ũ in eo solo lenones illi laborent, ut mendacia sua verborum & rerum lenocinijs velent, id testantibus ipsorum concionibus & scriptis quotidianis, quæ impudentissimis mendacijs conferta, & per verborum exquisitissimorum fila consuta conspiciuntur.
units.tr: The twentieth rule for preachers forbids them the enticements of words, in which alone those pimps labour, to veil their lies with the enticements of words and things. Their daily sermons and writings bear witness to this; they are stuffed with most shameless lies and are seen to be stitched together with threads of the most exquisite words.

units.la: Quæ in prima & secunda Regula Missionum referuntur, de πολυπραγμοσύνη & tyrannide per omnes mundi plagas aucupanda, directoribus Pontifice Romano & Societatis Generali, ea quidem supra tacta sunt, sed ex hisce mis-sionum regulis exactius examinatis, multo quàm ante, apertius, Regibus, Principibus & Magistratibus ob oculos exponitur, eo fine, ut ab hierarchiæ ilius fraudibus sibi & melius & vigilantius, quàm hactenus, caveant, & in missos illos in posterum diligentius animadvertant: aliàs timendum esset, ne negligentioribus vigilantissimi illi imponant.
units.tr: What is related in the first and second rules of the Missions, concerning the meddling and tyranny to be sought after in every corner of the world, by the directors, the Roman Pontiff and the General of the Society, has indeed been touched upon above; but these mission rules, examined more exactly, set it before the eyes of kings, princes and magistrates far more clearly than before, to the end that they may guard themselves against the frauds of that hierarchy both better and more vigilantly than hitherto, and may watch the men sent out more diligently in future. Otherwise it would have to be feared that those most vigilant men would deceive the more careless.

units.la: In octava eiusdem Tit. regula notatur, quomodo se in bonorum virorum notitia circumforanei illi insinuare debeant, quò efficacius operari possint.
units.tr: In the eighth rule of the same title it is noted how those vagrant men ought to insinuate themselves into the acquaintance of good men, so that they may work more effectively.

units.la: Cautissimum est, quod regula 19. d. Tit. traditur ad evitandum æmulationes Eodia aliorum Ecclesiasticorum, ut nimirum missi nullam reformandi Cleri ut monialium aliorumve religiosorum curæ partem admittant, sed machinas suas in imperitum vulgus dirigant, illud enim facile futurum esse aucupantibus sciunt, quia superstitioni natura dedltum.
units.tr: Most cautious is what is handed down in rule 19 of the said title, for avoiding the rivalries of other ecclesiastics, namely that the missionaries should admit no part in reforming the clergy, nuns or other religious, but should direct their machinations at the unskilled crowd. For they know it will be easy for those who lay snares, since superstition is innate in human nature.

units.la: Opportunitates, quas Deus ad institutū Iesuitarum promovendum, missis labit, è manibus sibi elabi sinere non debere, oculatissimi & vaferrimi illi suis commendant regula 2 o. dicti tit. ad factiones nimirum in alienis regnis excitandas, quibus illa tandem sub iugum Sedis Romanæ reducantur, in quo solo summum sedis illius bonum consistere, omnibus notum est, quade re quoq; non omnem ipsis conversationem cum secularibus, sed incautam tantum & nimiam prohibent, ut regula 26. ne detegantur ipsorum machinationes, alias & ea quæ in peculiaribus instructionibus a Superioribus præscribuntur, pari diligentia & providentia exequi iubentur, in eum finem illis non cum secularibus tantum agere mandatur, sed & in seculares ipsos se transsubstantiare ad parricidia Regum & Principum eo commodius patranda, & proditiones factionesque machinandas.
units.tr: The opportunities which God allows the missionaries to promote the Jesuit institute they must not allow to slip from their hands; these most sharp-sighted and crafty men commend this in rule 20 of the said title, namely for stirring up factions in foreign kingdoms, by which those kingdoms may at last be brought under the yoke of the Roman See, in which alone, as is known to all, the chief good of that see consists. On this matter too they forbid not all intercourse with secular persons, but only careless and excessive intercourse, as in rule 26, lest their machinations be detected; and what is prescribed to them in their special instructions by their superiors they are ordered to carry out with equal diligence and foresight. To this end they are commanded not only to deal with secular persons, but even to transform themselves into secular persons, so that they may more conveniently carry out the murders of kings and princes and devise treasons and factions.

units.la: Quod verba hæc Institutum Societatis in hoc libro toties & cum tanta commendatione repetuntur, non absque aliquo magno mysterio est: & procul dubio aliquid monstri in se continent. Illud apparet in regulis procuratoris Generalis, quod Societas magna tributa Sedi Romanæ summa diligentia pendenda esse compromiserit; cum Procuratori isti iniungatur, ut antequam dies præscriptus venerit solvendi, Quindennia Rectores Collegiorum, ad quos Uniones beneficiorum pertinent, diligenter admoneat, opportuno tempore pecunias Romam mittant.
units.tr: That these words, "the institute of the Society", are repeated so often and with such commendation in this book is not without some great mystery, and undoubtedly they contain something monstrous. This appears in the rules of the Procurator General, where the Society has pledged that the great tributes to the Roman See are to be paid with the utmost diligence; for this Procurator is charged that, before the prescribed day for payment arrives, he should diligently warn the Rectors of the Colleges, to whom the unions of benefices belong, to send the money to Rome at a suitable time.

units.la: Bullæ de Cœna Domini observatio, eiusque quod in ea mutatur vel additur diligentissime Procuratori Generali commendatur, ut & motus proprij Pontificis: adeo ut si motu proprio excommunicet Reges & Principes, eosque privet suis regnis & principatibus, vel quid sceleratius motu proprio statuat, monet ut conscio Præposito Generali Provincialibus omnibus id mittat, ut illi secundum ea Pontifici cæcâ obedientiâ pareant, & subditos contra Reges & Principes ad factiones & rebelliones suscitent.
units.tr: The observance of the Bull concerning the Lord's Supper, and whatever is changed or added in it, is most carefully commended to the Procurator General, as are the motu proprio decrees of the Pope; so that if by a motu proprio he excommunicates kings and princes and deprives them of their kingdoms and principalities, or decrees anything more wicked by motu proprio, he is charged, with the Provost General's knowledge, to send it to all the Provincials, so that they may obey the Pope in blind obedience according to these decrees, and stir up the subjects to factions and rebellions against kings and princes.

units.la: Pro Colophone Iesuitarum adjicitur epistola Ignatij de virtute obedientiæ ex cuius contextu non difficile erit dijudicare; epistolam eam per Ignatium ductu spiritus contradictionis congestam esse, quia non tantum contradictoria non pauca in ea videntur offendi posse; sed contra sententiam Spiritus Sancti Ignatium; adinstar spiritus infernalis, multa loca sacræ Scripturæ ad impijsimam suam de obedientia Iesuitica doctrinam blasphemè detorsisse; unde epistola illa exactissime & velut fundamentum viperinæ illius Societatis examinanda est; ac demonstrandum, Societatem illo suæ tyrannidis promovendæ studio, non quærere salutem, magnitudinem & libertatem Regum ac Principum, sed ut eos suis tyrannicis præceptis subjiciant, deque foliis suis deturbent, ac Reges ipsos, coronas & sceptra eorum ad pedes Pontificum abjiciant; sicuti hoc nuper Pontifex Rom. petiit à Legatis Henrici IV. Galliæ & Navarræ Regis. Verba relationis talia sunt: O'ultre que dessus, on a fait fonder vive voix par diverses personnes lesd. procureurs (nota hæc verba, non enim Legatorum honore dignatur, sed Procuratorum vili nomine superbe dehonestat Regios Legatos) si en faisant l'abiuration ils ne vouldroyent point au nom du Roy depoter aux pieds du Pape par signe d'une Couronne le royaume de France, qu'il auroit occupé de fait, foy disant Roy, combien que led. Siege l'eust priue du droit fuesiff & du tont aultre, qu'il eust pen pretendre a la Couronne de France, que sa Sainteté apres ceste submission la remettroit sur la teste desd. Procureurs. En præclarum, recentissimum atque indubitabile exemplum obedientiæ, quam cæco impetu cuivis Superiori præstandam esse docent: nonne digni, qui à Regibus & Principibus, omni suppliciorum genere in puteum abyssi proflgentur, &c.
units.tr: The Jesuits' colophon adds Ignatius's letter on the virtue of obedience. From its wording it will not be hard to judge that Ignatius composed this letter under the impulse of the spirit of contradiction. Many of its statements seem to contradict one another, and it runs against the mind of the Holy Spirit. Like an infernal spirit, Ignatius has blasphemously twisted many passages of Holy Scripture to support the Jesuits' most impious doctrine of obedience. For this reason the letter must be examined with the greatest exactness, as the foundation of that viperous Society, and it must be shown that the Society, in its eagerness to advance its tyranny, does not seek the safety, greatness and liberty of kings and princes. It seeks instead to bring them under its tyrannical commands, to thrust them from their thrones, and to cast the kings themselves, with their crowns and sceptres, at the feet of the popes. The Roman pontiff recently did exactly this when he demanded it of the envoys of Henry IV, King of France and Navarre. The words of the report are these: "Besides what has been said above, the said procurators were sounded out by word of mouth by various persons (note these words: he does not honour them with the title of envoys, but proudly disgraces the royal envoys with the base name of procurators), to see whether, in making their abjuration, they would not be willing, in the King's name, to lay at the Pope's feet, as a sign of the crown, the kingdom of France, which he had seized in fact while calling himself king, although the said See had deprived him of every right of succession and of every other claim he could make to the crown of France; and that His Holiness, after this submission, would place it again upon the head of the said procurators." What a remarkable, very recent and unmistakable example of the obedience which they teach must be rendered to any superior with blind zeal! Are they not worthy to be cast by kings and princes, through every kind of punishment, into the pit of the abyss, and so on?

units.la: Iudicium de epistola Ignatij de virtute obedientiæ.
units.tr: Judgment on Ignatius's letter on the virtue of obedience

units.la: NOTAE ET ANIMADVERSIONES A- LIAE AD QVASDAM SVMMARII IESVITA- RVM CONSTITVTIONES.
units.tr: NOTES AND OBSERVATIONS ON CERTAIN CONSTITUTIONS OF THE JESUITS IN THE SUMMARY

units.la: IN Summario Constitutionum lex vel regula octava sic habet: Vnusquisque eorum, qui Societatem ingrediuntur, consilium illud Christi sequendo, Qui dimiserit patrem, matrem, fratres & Sorores, & quicquid in mundo habet, relinquendum: imo sibi dictum existimet verbum illud: Qui non odit patrem, & matrem, insuper & animam suam, non potest meus esse discipulus. Et ita curandum ei est, ut omnem carnis affectum erga sanguine junctos exuat.
units.tr: In the Summary of the Constitutions, the eighth law or rule reads as follows: Each one of those who enter the Society, following that counsel of Christ, "Whoever has left father, mother, brothers and sisters, and whatever he has in the world," should consider that word said to himself: "Whoever does not hate father and mother, and even his own soul, cannot be my disciple." And he is to take care to strip off every affection of the flesh towards those joined to him by blood.

units.la: Exemplum Constitutionis seu regulae huius habemus apud Hasenmullerum: Erat Landspergae, inquit, Novitius, nomine Iohannes, artificio sartor: hic cum aliquis Novitiis animi gratia in campum procedit. Obviam fit illi pater senio confectus, ut filium, quem annum fere non viderat, alloqui & salutare cupit. Filius autem faciem vertit tanquam ad horrendi monstri occursum, & ne patrem audire & cum ipso loqui cogatur, auffugit. Pater senex filium inclamat: hocine est mihi nutricationis gratiam reddere? at ille surdus & mutus pergit: Pater, faxit Deus, inquit, ita fugias, ut nunquam videas: & reliquis Iesuitis silentibus, Haec, ait, est pietas quam Iesuitae suos docent? Pereat igitur in malam crucem degener iste filius, qui non se gerit ut Christianum decet. Ubi domum deventum est, Rector re audita factum Iohannis maxime probans; Macte virtute fili mi, inquit, qui patre tibi elegisti Patres Societatis nostrae, quos te magis quam patrem tuum amare oportet; eo quod hic secularis sit, illi spirituales. Factum hoc insuper ipso Hieronymi (per calcatum patrem perge ad Christum) confirmare conatus est, & cuiusdam Parisiensis Novitii exemplo, qui ne quidem matris lachrymis permoveri potuerit, ut ex coenobio pedem moveret. Addebat denique, parentibus, si eos a Societate Iesuitarum abstrahere conarentur; dicendum & scribendum esse: Vade post me Satana: quod non parentibus naturalibus, sed Societatis Patribus obedientiam absolutam voverint.
units.tr: We have an example of this constitution or rule in Hasenmüller: There was at Landsberg, he says, a novice named John, by trade a tailor. One day, when a certain novice went out into the fields for recreation, his father, worn out with age, met him, wishing to speak to and greet the son whom he had scarcely seen for a year. The son, however, turned his face away as if at the sight of some dreadful monster, and fled so as not to be forced to hear his father or speak with him. The old man called after his son: "Is this how you repay me for raising you?" But the son, deaf and mute, kept going: "Father, may God grant that you flee so that you never see me." And while the other Jesuits stayed silent, he said: "Is this the piety that the Jesuits teach their own?" Let this degenerate son, then, go to the devil, since he does not conduct himself as a Christian should. When they got back to the house, the Rector, having heard the matter, greatly approved John's deed: Well done, my son, he said, you have chosen as your father the Fathers of our Society, whom you ought to love more than your own father, because the latter is worldly and they are spiritual. He tried to confirm this deed by the example of Jerome himself ("go on to Christ over your trampled father"), and by the example of a certain Parisian novice, who could not be moved even by his mother's tears to leave the monastery. He added finally that if parents tried to draw their children away from the Society of Jesus, they should be told, and written to, "Get behind me, Satan," because they had vowed absolute obedience not to their natural parents but to the Fathers of the Society.

units.la: Iacob Crusius Iesuita Novitium quendam de Iesuitismo deserendo, & ad suos redire cogitantem, huiusmodi verbis compellavit: Quid tibi cura sunt parentes? Audi Christum & Ignatium. Hic monet ut naturalem seu carnalem authorem in spiritualem convertamus: hoc est, omnem storgen & dilectionem in Patres Societatis transfundamus: Ille vero dicit, Qui non odit patrem & matrem suam, non me est dignus. Hoc est, Si vis in Societate vivere, necesse est, ut parentes tuos, te ad seculum retrahere conantes, tanquam capitales hostes oderis & fugias, & Societatis amorem parentum dilectioni longe praeferas. Hoc est enim naturalem erga parentes affectum in spiritualem convertere, ut sanctus Pater noster Ignatius docuit. Quid tibi cum patre tuo? En pro patre seculari, recepisti aliquot mille spirituales Patres. Quid tibi cum matre tua? En mater tibi est Ecclesia Romana & Maria. Quid tibi cum fratribus? En pro uno atque altero fratre carnali tot abes fratres spirituales, quot sunt Iesuitae. Quid tum sororibus? Tot sunt tibi sorores, quot in Romana Ecclesia virgines. Quid cum tuis opibus & domibus? En pro una domo tot pulchra Collegia, tot amplas domos, atque tot redditus. Quid cum amicis? Iam tibi sunt amici Papa Dei Vicarius, Cardinales, Episcopi, Imperator, multi Reges & Principes, & omnes Catholici. Noli ergo Satanam audire, dientem, Redi ad tuos, contrahe matrimonium, &c.
units.tr: The Jesuit James Crusius addressed in such words a certain novice who was thinking of leaving the Jesuits and returning to his own people: What are your parents to you? Listen to Christ and Ignatius. He advises us to turn our natural or carnal father into a spiritual one, that is, to transfer all our storge and love to the Fathers of the Society. But he says, "Whoever does not hate his father and mother is not worthy of me." That is to say: if you want to live in the Society, you must hate and flee your parents, who try to draw you back to the world, as if they were your deadly enemies, and you must prefer love for the Society far above love for your parents. For this is how one turns natural affection for parents into spiritual affection, as our holy father Ignatius taught. What have you to do with your father? Behold, in place of a worldly father you have received several thousand spiritual fathers. What have you to do with your mother? Behold, the Roman Church and Mary are your mother. What have you to do with your brothers? Behold, in place of one or two carnal brothers you have as many spiritual brothers as there are Jesuits. What of your sisters? You have as many sisters as there are virgins in the Roman Church. What of your wealth and houses? Behold, in place of one house you have so many fine colleges, so many spacious houses, and so much income. What of your friends? You now have as friends the Pope, God's Vicar, the Cardinals, the Bishops, the Emperor, many Kings and Princes, and all Catholics. Do not listen, then, to Satan, who says: "Return to your own people, marry," and so on.

units.la: Respondebo autem non pro Ignatio Loyola, sed pro Christo: Is nihil tale his verbis, ut Iesuitae putant, docere voluit: nimirum, deserere, vel etiam odio abere parentes, ac Iesuiticam agere vitam, esse Christum plus quam patrem vel matrem amare: sed hoc potius, ut ipsum omnibus, etiam qui nobis coniunctissimi sunt, quaeque naturae legibus nobis commendantur praeferamus, imo tantum non odio habeamus, si quando res eo deveniat, ut aut ipsum abnegare, aut ab ipsis divelli oporteat. Per comparationem igitur dicuntur ista, ut neminem nobis tam charum aut amicum habeamus, ut in eius gratiam a Christo deficere velimus. Deinde hoc quoque vult, ut eos affectus, qui per se etiam laude digni sunt, in officio contineamus, ne nos a fide & pietate, quam ipsi debemus, transversum abripiant. Unde dicit, Qui amat patrem & matrem, &c. SVPRA ME, aut PLVS QVAM ME, non est me dignus. Nihil igitur haec pro stabilienda Iesuitica ἀσοφία faciunt. Damnantur etiam tales, qui hoc faciunt, Gangrensis Synodi Canone 16, qui sic habet: Quicunque filii a parentibus, praetextu divini cultus, abscedunt, nec debitam reverentiam & honorem illis dependunt, anathema sint.
units.tr: I shall answer, however, not for Ignatius of Loyola but for Christ. He did not intend by these words what the Jesuits suppose: namely, that we should desert or even hate our parents, and lead a Jesuitical life, and that loving Christ is more than loving father or mother. Rather, he meant this: that we should prefer him to all, even to those who are closest to us and who are commended to us by the laws of nature, indeed that we should hold them in something not far from hatred, if the situation should ever come to the point where we must either deny him or be torn away from them. These words, therefore, are spoken by way of comparison, so that we hold no one so dear or so friendly to us that we would want to fall away from Christ for their sake. Furthermore, he also wants us to keep in check those affections which in themselves deserve praise, lest they carry us off sideways from the faith and piety which we owe him. Hence he says, He who loves father and mother, etc., ABOVE ME, or MORE THAN ME, is not worthy of me. These things, therefore, do nothing to establish Jesuitical folly [ἀσοφία]. Those who do this are also condemned by Canon 16 of the Synod of Gangra, which reads: Whoever sons withdraw from their parents, under the pretext of divine worship, and do not render them the due reverence and honour, let them be anathema.

units.la: Constitutio 27 praecipit, Ut omnes, qui sub obedientia sint Societatis, meminerint se gratis dare debere, quae gratis acceperunt, nec postulando, nec admittendo stipendium, vel eleemosynas ullas, quibus Missae, vel Confessiones, vel praedicationes, vel quodvis aliud officium ex iis, quae Societas juxta suum institutum exercere potest, compensari videatur.
units.tr: Constitution 27 commands: That all who are under the obedience of the Society remember that they must give freely what they have received freely, neither asking for nor accepting any stipend or alms by which Masses, confessions, sermons, or any other office which the Society may perform according to its institute, might seem to be paid for.

units.la: Quis hic non merito exclamet, o leges & constitutiones prodigiose violatas, eversas & conculcatas. Cum Canonici Augustani & alii Gregorio Rosepho Iesuitarum Augustae Rectori, & in primario urbis templo concionatori 500 florenos in singulos annos offerret, respondit quidem, sibi propter legem hanc eos recipere non licere, ut quae gratis acceperit, gratis communicet: possint tamen loco eleemosynae quicquid voluerint ad Collegium Iesuitarum mittere, sibi enim licere eleemosynas, non autem mercedem accipere. Itaque quotannis die Nativitatis Christi ad Iesuitarum Collegium deferuntur 500 floreni, quos isti gratis scilicet, pro Rosephi concionibus accipiunt.
units.tr: Who here would not rightly cry out: "O laws and constitutions, shamelessly violated, overthrown and trampled underfoot!" When the canons of Augsburg and others offered Gregory Rosephus, Rector of the Jesuits at Augsburg and preacher in the city's principal church, 500 florins a year, he replied that because of this law he might not accept them, since he had received freely and must give freely; but they could send whatever they wished to the Jesuit College in place of alms, for it was lawful for him to accept alms but not wages. And so every year on the day of Christ's Nativity, 500 florins are carried to the Jesuit College, which they receive, of course, freely, for Rosephus's sermons.

units.la: Constitutione 43 praecipitur, Ut in Societate hac, nec fiat, nec sentiatur animorum propensio ad partem alterutram factionis, quae est inter Principes & Dominos Christianos: sed sit potius quidam universalis amor, qui partes omnes, licet sibi invicem contrariae sint, in Domino amplectatur. O Constitutionem prodigiose violatam quoque.
units.tr: Constitution 43 commands: That in this Society there should neither arise nor be perceived any inclination of minds towards either side of the faction which exists between Christian Princes and Lords; but rather there should be a certain universal love which embraces all sides in the Lord, though they may be opposed to one another. O Constitution, also shamelessly violated!

units.la: Constiturione 45 sancitur, quo plenius possit Societas rebus spiritualibus juxta suum institutum vacare, ut a negotiis saecularibus abstineat, nec ea ullis precibus adduci obeunda suscipiant, vel in illis se occupari sinant. At contra Iesuitae hodie in Curia Senatorum, ut supra diximus, & Principum versantur, a lateribus eorum numquam discedunt, consiliis eorum se ingerunt, in castris quoque & inter arma torum acies circumvolitant, & in ipsa quoque gynaecea ac penetralia mulierum usque perreptant, & nihil in saecularibus intentatum reliquuerunt. In Gallia visi sunt Iesuitae multi in Parmensi exercitu, quorum nonnunquam currus ornati & bene ornati intercipiebantur, cum insignibus nominis IESV, quae more Principum curribus suis infigebant. Ante hunc Principem nunquam visi fuerunt militiam sequi: imo solebant alios monachos, inter milites versantes, reprehendere ac damnare.
units.tr: Constitution 45 sanctions: So that the Society may more fully devote itself to spiritual things according to its institute, it should abstain from secular business, and not allow itself to be drawn by any entreaties to undertake such duties or to be occupied in them. But on the contrary, the Jesuits today, as we said above, are busy at the courts of Senators and Princes, never leave their sides, thrust themselves into their counsels, flit about the camps and among the lines of armed men, and creep even into the women's apartments and inner chambers, and they have left nothing in secular affairs untried. In France many Jesuits were seen in the Parma army, whose carriages, often richly adorned, were intercepted, bearing with them the emblems of the name of JESUS, which they fixed on their carriages in the manner of Princes. Before this Prince no Jesuits were ever seen following an army; indeed they used to rebuke and condemn other monks who lived among soldiers.

units.la: Ex instituto etiam suo iuramento sancte profitentur, se dignitates Ecclesiasticas non acceptaturos aut procuraturos, quod non conveniant religiosae humilitati. Sed callidam & deceptoriam hanc reiectionem iudicandam, per opera eidem contraria probari potest. Nam dignitates illas & captant & acceptant, praesertim si ignes & pingues sint. Unde nonnulli ex Pontificiis dixerunt, Captari ab ipsis dignitates amplas, paupertatis simulatae & humilitatis quasi esca.
units.tr: By their institute also, they solemnly profess under oath that they will not accept or seek ecclesiastical dignities, since these do not agree with religious humility. But this crafty and deceptive refusal may be judged and proved by actions contrary to it. For they both pursue and accept those dignities, especially when they are rich and fat. Whence some of the Papists have said: That lofty dignities are sought after by them, as bait for feigned poverty and a kind of humility.

units.la: Anno enim Domini 1593 Franciscus Toletus licet etiam ipse cum alii Cardinalitiam & Episcopalem dignitatem abiurarit, a Clemente VIII in Cardinalium Collegium cooptatus, & ad summam, excepto Pontificatu, Ecclesiasticam dignitatem evectus est. Ac licet finxerint, se cunctari & dubitare, acceptavit tamen, & placuit Reverendissimus & Illustrissimus appellari. Triennium autem tantummodo superyixit.
units.tr: For in the year of the Lord 1593, Francisco Toledo, although he too, like others, had renounced the cardinalate and episcopal dignity, was co-opted by Clement VIII into the College of Cardinals and raised to the highest ecclesiastical dignity, apart from the papacy. And although they pretended to hesitate and be reluctant, he accepted it, and was pleased to be called Most Reverend and Most Illustrious. He survived only three years.

units.la: Fingit tamen Ribadeneira in Catalogo Scriptorum Iesuiticorum, hoc factum esse magno cum moerore Societatis, paulo tamen post, videlicet anno 1598, die
units.tr: Ribadeneira, however, feigns in his Catalogue of Jesuit Writers that this happened with great grief to the Society, though a little afterwards, namely in the year 1598, on the day

units.la: Iesuitae nihil gratis dant.
units.tr: The Jesuits give nothing for free.

units.la: Iesuitae non sunt neutrales.
units.tr: The Jesuits are not neutral.

units.la: Iesuitae saecularibus negotiis se immiscent.
units.tr: The Jesuits meddle in secular affairs.

units.la: Iesuitae dignitates Ecclesiasticas captant. mênsis Martij, idem Pontifex Robertum Bellarminum in eundem dignitatis gradum ascivit. Et mox sequentur plures alij: nec cessabunt ambitiosissimi homines, donec Pontificiam sellam occupárint.
units.tr: The Jesuits seek ecclesiastical dignities. of March, the same Pontiff admitted Robert Bellarmine to the same rank of dignity. And soon many others followed; nor will the most ambitious men cease until they have seized the Papal chair.

units.la: Excusat tamen eos Gretserus de hac Cardinalitia dignitate contra leges Ordinis assumpta: quod nimirum Pontifex eos cogere, ijsque imperare possit sub peccati mortalis periculo. Exigit etiam hoc ipsorum iuramenti formula: Mandata Apostolica totis viribus observabo. Scilicet.
units.tr: Yet Gretser excuses them for having assumed this cardinalate dignity against the laws of the Order, namely that the Pontiff can compel them and command them under the danger of mortal sin. Their oath formula also requires this: I will observe apostolic mandates with all my strength. Clearly.

units.la: NOTAE ET ANIMADVERSIONES ALIQVOT AD BVL- LAS AC PRIVILEGIA A PONTIFICIB. ROM. IESVITIS DATA, EX HELIA HAFENMULLERO.
units.tr: NOTES AND REMARKS ON SOME BULLS AND PRIVILEGES GRANTED TO THE JESUITS BY ROMAN POPES, FROM ELIAS HAFENMÜLLER.

units.la: IN Bulla prima Pauli 3. Papae, conceditur Iesuitis potestas condendi tot Regulas & Constitutiones quot volunt, pro libitu & arbitrio, in Societatis suae usum & incrementum: hac tamen conditione, ut illarum scopus ac finis sit Rom. Sedis conservatio. Quid autem opus est ad Christiana perfectione tot, & talib. quidè Regulis, quae nihil sunt quàm superstitiosorum hominum figmenta & placita? Unica nostra regula & via ad salutem est Christus. Is in Decalogo & Evangelio plenè nobis praescripsit, qualiter vitam nostram instituere debeamus, si perfecti esse velimus. Et quicunque iuxta hanc Regulam incedent, pax super eos erit & misericordia. Gal. 6. Et quid de huiusmodi Regulis & Constitutionib. senserit primus Eremita Anton. hinc apparet, quod Petrus Parisiensis Cantor testatur, eu quibusdam Monachis, petentibus regulam seu normam piae vitae, Evangeliorum codicem obtulisse: quo ille nimirum indicare voluit, omnia ad pietatem necessaria abundè in sacris literis comprehensa esse, nec esse ullis novis Regulis, Canonibus aut normis opus.
units.tr: In the first Bull of Pope Paul III, the Jesuits are granted power to make as many rules and constitutions as they wish, at their pleasure and discretion, for the use and growth of their Society, on this condition only: that their aim and purpose be the preservation of the Roman See. But what need is there for so many and such rules for Christian perfection, which are nothing but the figments and opinions of superstitious men? Our one rule and way to salvation is Christ. In the Decalogue and the Gospel he has fully prescribed to us how we ought to order our lives if we wish to be perfect. And whoever walk according to this rule, peace and mercy shall be upon them (Gal. 6). What the first hermit Anthony thought of such rules and constitutions appears from this: Peter the Chanter of Paris relates that when certain monks asked him for a rule or norm of pious life, he offered them the codex of the Gospels. By this he clearly wished to show that everything necessary for piety is abundantly contained in the sacred letters, and that there is no need of any new rules, canons or norms.

units.la: In secunda Bulla tribuit illis divini nominis laude, quod sint in Theologia exercitati, Lutetiae graduati, & Spiritu sancto afflati, Christo & Papae dicati, ac speciali voto Pontifici Rom. obligati. Quae autem est communio lucis cum tenebris? quae cocordia Christo cum Belial? Hosine Spiritu sancto afflatos existimabimus, qui se Antichristo speciali voto obstrinxerunt, & in hoc coniurarunt, quod velint orthodoxa doctrina evertere, & Pontificias superstitiones stabilire? Et quis hos Theologos esse putabit, qui Dei verbum cereum esse nasum, materiam litis & haereticorum librum calumniantur, & in eius locum Paparum placita, Conciliorum decreta, humanas traditiones & Monachorum somnia substituunt? Dicit etiam Bulla, eos esse animarum zelantes: concedo eos zelum habere, sed qualem lupi ovium, & vulpes anserum.
units.tr: In the second Bull they are praised with the name of divine honour: that they are exercised in theology, graduated at Paris, inspired by the Holy Spirit, dedicated to Christ and to the Pope, and bound to the Roman Pontiff by a special vow. But what fellowship has light with darkness, or what concord has Christ with Belial? Are we to think them inspired by the Holy Spirit, who have bound themselves by special vow to Antichrist, and have conspired in this, that they wish to overthrow orthodox doctrine and establish Papist superstitions? And who would think those theologians, who slander the Word of God as a waxen nose, a matter of strife, and a heretics' book, and in its place substitute the decrees of popes, the decisions of councils, human traditions and the dreams of monks? The Bull also says that they are zealous for souls. I grant that they have zeal, but such as wolves have for sheep, and foxes for geese.

units.la: In tertia bulla datur Iesuitis potestas concionandi, sed non Dei verbum, sed humanas traditiones, quales sunt, statuta festa a Pontificib. Rom. instituta servare: omnib. diebus feriatis Missa audire; in quadragesima, quatuor item temporibus, Veneris quoque & Saturni diebus ieiunare, & a carnib. caseo, lacte, &c. abstinere; semel in anno peccata sua confiteri, circa festum Paschatis Sacramentum altaris sub una tantum specie sumere; diebus prohibitis a nuptiis abstinere, &c.
units.tr: In the third Bull the Jesuits are given power to preach, not God's Word, but human traditions, such as keeping the feast days instituted by the Roman pontiffs; hearing Mass on all holidays; fasting in Lent, likewise on the Ember days, and on Fridays and Saturdays, and abstaining from meat, cheese, milk, etc.; confessing their sins once a year; receiving the Sacrament of the altar under one kind only, around the feast of Easter; and abstaining from marriage on prohibited days, etc.

units.la: In eadem Bulla datur Iesuitis licentia audiendi Confessiones. Intelligitur autem plenaria omnium peccatorum enumeratio: ita ut nec secreta conscientiarum, nec intima penetralia cordium, nec cogitationes ullae Confessarium lateant.
units.tr: The same Bull gives the Jesuits licence to hear confessions. This is understood to mean a full enumeration of all sins, so that neither the secrets of consciences, nor the innermost recesses of hearts, nor any thoughts remain hidden from the confessor.

units.la: Tertio datur in hac Bulla quoque ipsis potestas commutandi vota. Vovet autem Iesuitae paupertate, castitate & obedientia. Constat vero omnib. eos opes quibuscunque possint artibus, seu, ut illorum verbis utar, pijs fraudibus, corradere. Sic si non possunt continere, sequuntur decretum: Si non caste, tamen caute. Eodem modo soli Papae & Generali suo infidei rebus vovent obedientia: ea non praestita, inobedientia suam flagellis, cilicijs, & aliqua abstinentia eos luere & expiare oportet.
units.tr: Thirdly, this Bull also gives them power to commute vows. The Jesuits vow poverty, chastity and obedience. Yet it is certain that they gather wealth by whatever arts they can, or, to use their own words, by pious frauds. So if they cannot contain themselves, they follow the decree: If not chastely, yet cautiously. In the same way they vow obedience to the Pope alone and to their General in matters of faith; and if this obedience is not rendered, they must atone for their disobedience by flogging, hair shirts and some abstinence.

units.la: Quarto Bulla haec potestatem dat Iesuitis audiendi Confessiones, & absolvendi ab omnibus casibus, etiam ijs, qui non sunt in Bulla Coenae Dominicae comprehensi, & ab ijs quoq; qui Apostolicæ Sedi reservati sunt. Hac vero potestate contra multos, tum vero vel maxime ad concitationem Ligæ seu Conspirationis illius Gallicanæ adversus Henricum III. Regem, quum præsertim anno 1585. valide emergeret, ita sunt uli Iesuitæ, ut nullum absolutione dignarentur, qui ad propositta eatenus interrogatoria se fidelem Regis subditum ac ministrum obsequentem esse profiteri fuisset ausus. Interea vero numerus eorum, qui confitebantur ipsis, adeo crescebat & adaugebatur, ut paulo post, anno videlicet 1587. in annuis illis Romæ impressis Epistolis ad Generalem suum Aquavivam de Collegio Parisiensi suo scribere non sint veriti: Confessiones auditæ, & quidem universæ vitæ, quam plurimæ. Hæc est enim communis fere omnium opinio, tum demum eorum satisfieri Conscientiæ, quum apud nos confitentur: ideoque nonnullus sexaginta millia rum confecit viam, ut a nostris audiretur. Et rursus, anno 1589. Totius vitæ confessiones auditæ trecentæ. Quicumque enim iuramenta Regi præstita & debita exinde obsequia seposuerant, eoque perfidiosi fuerant facti, & quos a peccatulis (uti loquuntur) istis Pastores ac Sacerdotes alij non ita leviter aut temere volebant absolvere; ij Iesuitis erant usquequaque acceptissimi; & indulgentissimam non tantum absolutionem, sed & amplissimam promissionem æternæ retributionis in de consequebantur; modo in rebellione ista sua fortiter perfisterent gnaviterque pergerent. Vnde passim in absolutionibus modum hunc observarunt talem; ut nimirum ad inserta Breviariis suis Evangelia iurare tenerentur omnes; quod neque tum temporis regnantem adhuc Regem, nec si forte sic caderet, eius successorem Navarræum pro legitimo vellent agnoscere Domino. Id quod a multis appendicem eam haud admittentibus, eoque sine absolutione dimissis, constanter adfirmatum postea & contestatum fuit. Caeterumquin æstimare facile licet efficacissimam, quantumvis occultam subfuisse causam; quia Ligæ seu conspiratio illa ab exiguis sane primordijs tam exiguo temporis spacio ad tantum flagitium evecta, tantusque non personarum solummodo, sed urbium quoque, nec non Provinciarum integrarum adversus regnantem tum, sed & residentem inibidem Regem numerus concitatus, ac conspiratione facta exarmatus fuit.
units.tr: Fourthly, this Bull gives the Jesuits power to hear confessions and to absolve from all cases, even those not included in the Bull of the Lord's Supper, and also from those reserved to the Apostolic See. With this power they dealt with many people, and above all to stir up the French League or conspiracy against King Henry III, especially when it broke out strongly in 1585. They so used it that they deigned to absolve no one who had dared to profess, in answer to their set questions, that he was a faithful subject and obedient minister of the King. Meanwhile the number of those who confessed to them grew and increased so much that shortly afterwards, in 1587, in the annual letters printed at Rome to their General Aquaviva about their Paris college, they did not hesitate to write: confessions heard, and indeed of whole lives, very many. For this is almost the common opinion of all, that their conscience is only satisfied when they confess to us; and therefore some travelled sixty thousand miles to be heard by ours. And again, in 1589: confessions of whole lives heard, three hundred. Whoever had set aside the oaths sworn to the King and the obedience owed him, and had thereby become faithless, and those whom other pastors and priests were unwilling to absolve lightly or rashly from such (as they call them) little sins: these were most welcome to the Jesuits in every way, and they obtained not only the most indulgent absolution but also a most ample promise of eternal reward besides, provided they persisted stoutly in this rebellion and pressed on vigorously. Hence in absolutions they everywhere observed this method: all were bound to swear, on the Gospels inserted in their breviaries, that they would not acknowledge as lawful lord the King then reigning, nor, should he fall, his successor, the Navarrese. Many who would not admit this appendix, and so were dismissed without absolution, afterwards constantly affirmed and attested it. Otherwise it is easy to judge that a most effective, though hidden, cause lay behind this; for that league or conspiracy, from very small beginnings, rose to such a crime in so short a time, and so great a number, not only of persons but of cities and whole provinces, was stirred up against the King then reigning and residing there, and was disarmed once the conspiracy was made.

units.la: Quinto Iesuitis concedit Bulla, peregrinationes, vota, &c. pro tempore commutandi; Missam ante diei exortum, & post meridiem celebrandi; Ecclesiastica Sacramenta administrandi; officium Romanum novum, non ex præcepto, sed ex libertate dicendi. Mandatur insuper, ut Assistentes sint & Cardinales, qui resistentes Iesuitis compescant, & rebelles in eos tollant. Sunt quidem hæc satis magna privilegia, quæque Iesuitis in illis conceduntur: sed hoc illud ipsum est, quod Daniel prædixit, Antichristum maximis beneficijs remuneraturum esse, quicunque suum illum Deum Mayzim colere, venerari & agnoscere dignentur.
units.tr: Fifthly, the Bull grants the Jesuits power to change pilgrimages, vows, etc. as the time requires; to celebrate Mass before sunrise and after noon; to administer the ecclesiastical sacraments; and to say the new Roman office not by precept but at their liberty. It is moreover commanded that there be assistants, and cardinals too, who are to restrain those who resist the Jesuits and to remove rebels against them. These are indeed quite great privileges granted to the Jesuits in these Bulls; but this is precisely what Daniel foretold, that Antichrist would reward most richly those who deigned to worship, venerate and acknowledge that god of his, Mayzim.

units.la: In quinta Bulla permittit Papa, ut quicunque velint, neglecto suo parocho Iesuitarum Missas audire, aliaque Sacramenta ab ipsis sumere possint, nec ad proprias parochias accedere opus habeant. Alias vero coguntur in Patratu omnes & singuli, ut intra parochiæ suæ septa maneant, Missas audiant, & ordinario suo Sacerdoti in anno semel confiteantur. Hæc autem libertas Iesuitis concessa ipsis quæstui inseruit vel maxime. Nummus enim confessionalis, qui hactenus sacrificulis cesserat, nunc Iesuitis cedit. Excusant quidem se Iesuitæ apud seculares Sacerdotes, quod Confessionis nummum non recipiant, & nullam mercedem propter Missas postulent. Ita quidem illi, dum in templis sedent, propter Confessionem nihil exigunt: si quis autem pecuniam super altare ponit, tacent, eamque hominibus absentibus, auferunt. Item, Si quis propter consessionem illis pecuniam vult dare, eam illi quidem in manus recipere nolunt: dicunt licunt autem, si quid nobis communicare vultis, illud ad Collegij nostri portas nittite, nobis enim non licet quicquam in templo recipere.
units.tr: In the fifth Bull the Pope permits whoever wishes, neglecting their own parish priest, to hear Masses of the Jesuits and to receive other sacraments from them, without needing to go to their own parishes. Otherwise all and each are compelled to remain within the bounds of their parish, to hear Mass there, and to confess once a year to their ordinary priest. This liberty granted to the Jesuits contributed greatly to their profit: the confession fee, which had hitherto gone to the lesser priests, now goes to the Jesuits. The Jesuits, indeed, excuse themselves before the secular priests, saying that they do not accept a confession fee and demand no payment for Masses. So while they sit in churches they demand nothing for confession; but if anyone places money on the altar, they keep silent and, when people are absent, take it away. Likewise, if anyone wishes to give them money on account of confession, they refuse to receive it into their hands, saying: if you wish to give us anything, bring it to the gates of our college, for it is not lawful for us to receive anything in the church.

units.la: Secundo, in hac Bulla mandatur, Iesuitas ab omni visitatione & cura Monialium, vel aliarum religiosarum personarum liberos & immunes esse debere. Ignatius autem Loyola tanta cura Moniales est complexus, ut etiam publica corta, propriis in domibus laute foveri & alí curaverít. Hodie quoque, inquit Hamnullerus, non quidem visitatores illarum agunt: sed tamen in peregrinationibus suis Monialium Caenobia libentissime divertunt, Missas in illis celebrant, & Confessiones illarum audiunt. Si tamen aliqui delectatione capiuntur Monialium agendi curam, eam, iuxta Bullam, facile vel ab illorum Generali vel a Papa consequi possunt.
units.tr: Secondly, this Bull orders that the Jesuits should be free and exempt from all visitation and care of nuns or other religious persons. Yet Ignatius Loyola embraced the care of nuns so thoroughly that he even had public prostitutes kept and fed in his own house with great lavishness. Even today, says Hafenmüller, they do not indeed act as visitors of these women; yet in their journeys they most gladly lodge in the convents of nuns, celebrate Masses in them, and hear their confessions. If, however, some are seized with a delight in taking up the care of nuns, they can easily obtain it, according to the Bull, either from their General or from the Pope.

units.la: Tertio, a Decimis, & ab omni contributione Iesuitarum bona Papalis hæc Bulla exímit, etiamsi prius sub censu fuerint. A reliquo vero clero maximos reditus censusque amplissimos singulis annis collígit Papa, omniaque illorum bona tributaria habet. Non tenentur, inquit Bulla, sol vere bonorum suorum decimam, vel aliam dare contributionem, seu procurationem, nec Papalem, nec Canonicam portionem: etiamsi prius fuere illa bona sub censu: nisi fit specifice & expresse in literis Apostolicis. Mirum ergo non est, Iesuitas tam brevi temporis spacio tam facile tot tantasque opes collegisse. Papa enim reliquam suam turbam miris artibus expilat; Iesuitis autem pilos aliis evulsos addit: quin cogit Episcopos, Abbates & alios praelatos Iesuitis de suis bonis & redditibus largiter dare, ut Monachi, Fuldae & aliis locis factum est.
units.tr: Thirdly, this Apostolic Bull exempts the Jesuits' goods from tithes and from every contribution, even if they were previously under tax. Yet from the rest of the clergy the Pope gathers very large revenues and very ample taxes every year, and holds all their goods as tributary. They are not bound, says the Bull, to give a tithe of their goods, or any other contribution or procuration, neither the papal nor the canonical portion, even if those goods were previously under tax, unless it is specifically and expressly stated in the Apostolic letters. It is no wonder, therefore, that the Jesuits have gathered together so easily such great wealth in so short a time. For the Pope plunders his other flock by wonderful arts, and adds to the Jesuits the wool plucked from others; indeed he compels bishops, abbots and other prelates to give generously to the Jesuits out of their goods and revenues, as has been done at Fulda and in other places.

units.la: Quarto, dicit Bulla, eum qui Iesuitarum aliquam Ecclesiam, vel alium pium eorum locum, a Praeposito signatum, semel in anno visitarit, indulgentiam plenariam omnium peccatorum consequi. Aliter vero loquitur Scriptura: Sanguis Iesu Christi, inquit Ioannes, emundat nos ab omni peccato. Item, remissa vobis sunt peccata propter nomen eius: Non dicit, propter visitationem Iesuiticorum templorum. Et Paulus dicit, In Christo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem eius.
units.tr: Fourthly, the Bull says that whoever has visited any church of the Jesuits, or another of their pious places, marked by the Provost, once in the year, obtains a plenary indulgence of all sins. But Scripture speaks otherwise: The blood of Jesus Christ, says John, cleanses us from all sin. Likewise: Your sins are forgiven you for his name's sake. It does not say: for the sake of visiting the Jesuit churches. And Paul says: In Christ we have redemption through his blood.

units.la: Iulius III. Papa in prima sua Bulla confirmat omnia praedecessoris sui Pauli III. Iesuitis data privilegia. In secunda vero, quae ordine est septima, die 22. Octob. Anno 1552. nova insuper addit, nimirum, Professis licere circa ieiunia & cibos prohibitos dispensare. Si Sacerdos alius vel Monachus, & Secularis etiam, ex speciali permissione Sacerdotis, talem permissionem habentis, qualiscunque ille esset, ieiunij tempore cibis prohibitis uteretur, videlicet carnibus, lacte, ovis, butyro & caseo, excommunicaretur, vel aliqua pecuniae summa multaretur. Iesuitarum autem Professis, qui quadruplici voto Papae obligati sunt, liset permittere sibi & aliis libertatem cibis quibuslibet vescendi; non quia Deus liberum eorum ciborum usum hominibus concessit, sed quia Papa illis hanc dispensandi facultatem dedit.
units.tr: Pope Julius III, in his first Bull, confirmed all the privileges given to the Jesuits by his predecessor Paul III. In the second, which is in order the seventh, dated 22 October 1552, he added new ones, namely that it is lawful for the professed to dispense with fasts and forbidden foods. If another priest or monk, or even a layman, by special permission of a priest holding such permission, whatever he might be, used forbidden foods during a time of fasting, namely meats, milk, eggs, butter and cheese, he would be excommunicated or fined some sum of money. But the professed of the Jesuits, who are bound to the Pope by a fourfold vow, may permit themselves and others the freedom to eat any foods whatever; not because God has granted men the free use of those foods, but because the Pope has given them this power of dispensing.

units.la: Secundo concessit etiam Iesuitis haereticos quoque absolvere, hoc est, ex Evangelico Pontificium, ex Christiano Antichristianum, ex filio Dei filium Satanae, liceat duplice gehennae filium facere. Haec autem potestas Iesuitis data est, ut commodiorem cum Evangelicis agendi occasionem habeant. Dicunt enim iis, Non est quod mali aliquid de nobis suspiceris; non enim nos solemus, ut reliqui Clerici, quenquam Inquisitioni prodere: ideo coram nobis profitere: est enim concessa nobis potestas te absolvendi, & in gremium Romanae Ecclesiae recipiendi, modo revoces; & te in omnibus adiuvabimus. In vero alios accesseris, consulere quidem eos poteris, sed non abiis absolvi, nisi ex gratia Papae, non aliis licet. In hoc conscientiae foro multorum nimos misere torquent.
units.tr: Secondly, he also granted the Jesuits the power to absolve heretics as well, that is, to make the Evangelical a Papist, the Christian an Antichristian, and the son of God a son of Satan, a son of double Gehenna. This power was given to the Jesuits so that they might have a more convenient opportunity of dealing with Evangelicals. For they say to them: "There is no need for you to suspect anything bad of us; for we, unlike other clergy, are not accustomed to betray anyone to the Inquisition. Therefore confess before us; for we have been granted the power of absolving you and receiving you into the bosom of the Roman Church, provided you recant; and we will help you in all things. But if you go to others, you may indeed consult them, but you cannot be absolved by them, except by the grace of the Pope; others are not permitted to do so." In this court of conscience they miserably torment the minds of many.

units.la: Tertio obtinuerunt a Papa etiam hoc privilegium, ut intra domorum & collegiorum suorum privatos parietes, suos ad quoscunque volunt gradus promovere possint. Ne tamen Academiarum legibus derogâsse videantur, ubi suos examinârunt, ad promotionis diem Rectorem & Cancellarium Academiæ vocare solent, qui licentiam promovendi illis dare coguntur, & ne in minimo quidem eis contradicere audeant, & sufficit illis hæc gratia; quòd ad prandium vel cœnam vocantur & admittuntur. Ne quis autem taliter examinatos & promotos contemnat, ut qui publica examina subire non aûsi fuerint, præcepit Papa, ut tales Socij graduati, qualificati & formati, quasi in publico id factum esset, in honore habeantur. Concedit etiam iis eadem privilegia, quæ habent ij, qui legitimè promoti sunt. In quo Papa quæstûs gratiâ, idem facit, quod illi, qui spurios, pro legitimis & honestè natis pronunciant.
units.tr: Thirdly, they have also obtained from the Pope this privilege: that within the private walls of their houses and colleges they may promote their own men to whatever degrees they wish. Lest, however, they seem to have derogated from the laws of the universities, where they have examined their own men, they are wont to summon the Rector and the Chancellor of the university to the day of promotion, who are compelled to give them licence to promote, and do not dare to contradict them even in the smallest matter; and this favour is enough for them, that they are invited and admitted to dinner or supper. Lest anyone, however, despise men examined and promoted in this way, as if they had not dared to undergo public examinations, the Pope has ordered that such graduated, qualified and formed Fellows be held in honour, as if this had been done in public. He also grants them the same privileges as those who have been lawfully promoted. In this the Pope, for the sake of gain, does the same as those who pronounce bastards to be legitimate and honourably born.

units.la: Pius IV. anno 1561. April. 13. die, in prima Bulla concedit Iesuitis potestatem ædificandi Collegia ubicunque velint; licetid seculares & Ecclesiastici prohibere conentur. Imò mandat, ut in huiusmodi conatibus Iesuitas, parochi, Prælati & Episcopi iuvent, & contradicentes vel impedientes coerceant. Felix sanè Iesuitarum conditio, qui nullis supplices fieri tenentur, ut recipiantur; sed ad quoscunque à Papa missi venerint, eos non modò hospitio excipere, gratis alere, sed etiam Collegia, domus, templa & scholas ædificare coguntur, quin etiam propriis possessionibus & hortis cedere; eâque in usum & dominium Iesuitarum tradere.
units.tr: Pius IV, in his first Bull, dated 13 April 1561, grants the Jesuits the power of building colleges wherever they wish, even if secular and ecclesiastical persons try to forbid it. Indeed he orders that parish priests, prelates and bishops help the Jesuits in such attempts, and restrain those who oppose or hinder them. Truly a happy condition for the Jesuits, who are not bound to beg anyone to receive them; but wherever they have come, sent by the Pope, they are compelled not only to be received as guests and fed free of charge, but also to build colleges, houses, churches and schools, and even to yield up their own possessions and gardens, and hand them over for the use and ownership of the Jesuits.

units.la: In altera Bulla die 19. Augusti. Anno 1561. edita, ad imitationem Iulij III. hos suos Socios ab omnibus oneribus & gravaminibus tum Ecclesiæ, tum Reipubl. eximit. Nam præcipit, ut & ipsi, & Collegia, & bona ipsorum omnia, perpetuâ libertate, sine ullo iuramento, excepto eo quo Papæ devincti sunt; sine omni ulla sura, fœnore, censura, decimis & exactionibus liberi relinquantur; tam in iis quæ iam possident, quàm quæ in illorum usum futuris temporibus ventura sint; tam in domibus & Collegiis, quàm in Civitatibus & Academiis; nullum tributum, nullum censum, nullas decimas, de domibus, Collegiis & feudis solvant, sed sua ab omni solutione exempta & libera possideant. Non immerito autem tam munifici sunt Papæ erga Iesuitas, quia præ reliquis Clericis & Monachis Paparum res augere & propagare norunt.
units.tr: In another Bull, issued on 19 August 1561, following the example of Julius III, he exempts these his Fellows from all burdens and grievances, both of the Church and of the commonwealth. For he commands that they themselves, their colleges, and all their goods be left free in perpetual liberty, without any oath, except the one by which they are bound to the Pope; free from every usury, interest, levy, tithes and exactions; both in those things they now possess and in those which will come to their use in future times; both in houses and colleges and in cities and universities; that they pay no tribute, no tax, no tithes on houses, colleges or fiefs, but possess their property free and exempt from every payment. Nor without reason are the Popes so generous towards the Jesuits, because they know how to increase and spread the Pope's wealth more than the other clergy and monks.

units.la: Pius V. Anno 1565. Calend. 16. Febr. ne Iesuitæ aliorum etiam Ordinum privilegiis destituantur, concessit illis omnia privilegia, quæ Mendicantibus Monachis concessa sunt; ut sic ubique & quocunque venerint, sua possint habere diversoria, & Socios habeant, qui illos in procurandis ac promovendis rebus Pontificijs adiuvent; adeòque prætextum aliquem paupertatis habeant; dum opulenti Mendicantibus annumerantur. Hoc etiam ideo à Papa illis concessum est, ut ficte clam in Monachorum res, opes, vitâ & doctrinam inquirere, illos Papæ deferre, & tandem illorum monasteria ac bona invadere possint: ob quem dolum etiam cane & angue peius Monachi illos oderunt.
units.tr: Pius V, in the year 1565, on 16 February, so that the Jesuits should not be deprived of the privileges of the other orders too, granted them all the privileges that have been given to the mendicant monks; so that wherever and whenever they come they may have their own lodgings, and have companions who may help them in managing and advancing papal affairs; and so that they may have some pretext of poverty, while being numbered among the mendicants though rich. This too was granted to them by the Pope so that, under this pretence, they might secretly inquire into the affairs, resources, life and teaching of the monks, report them to the Pope, and at last be able to invade their monasteries and goods; on account of this deceit the monks hate them even worse than dog and snake.

units.la: Gregorius XIII. non contentus Iesuitas cinctos esse sua; Cardinalium, Episcoporum auctoritate, dedit insuper facultatem illis anno 1573. Conservatores, Iudices & Advocatos assumendi in quibusvis causis. Illos autem iuvare renuentes, excommunicari iubet; sic ut & sub Ecclesiæ Romanæ custodia, & pollicitorum tutela licitè, liberèque, sine omni impedimento res Papæ exequi possint. Præcipit etiam, ut Archiepiscopi & reliqui Clerici Iesuitas laborantes vel periclitantes; cum potentiâ, tum opibus iuvent, neque permittant, ut vel impediatur, vel ulla ratione molestentur, vel expellatur, vel bonis suis cedere cogantur. Hinc tantis supercilijs, tantaque licentiâ omnibus insultant, & impune quidlibet agunt: sicut iam apud ipsos Pontificios in proverbium abiêrit, ut si quando ob scelera aliquis plectitur, dicant ei: Si Iesuita esses, impune fecisses. Alijs, quos noverunt in favore Papæ esse, dicunt: Propitium habes Pontificem; sed cura ne offendas. ndas Iesuitas, quibus iratus, Papæ clementia in furorem vertitur. Alij in causis mas aperte dicunt: Si mihi coram Papa causa agenda esset, mallem à meis partibus Iesuis, quàm Christum habere. Illi enim plus, quàm Christus, authoritatis & gratiæ in Papæ ulus obtinent.
units.tr: Gregory XIII, not content that the Jesuits were surrounded by their own cardinals and bishops, in the year 1573 also gave them the power to take up conservators, judges and advocates in any cases whatever. He orders that those who refuse to help them be excommunicated; so that under the custody of the Roman Church and the protection of its promises they may carry out the Pope's business lawfully and freely, without any hindrance. He also commands that archbishops and the rest of the clergy help the Jesuits who are in trouble or in danger, both with power and with resources, and not allow them to be hindered, or harassed in any way, or expelled, or forced to yield up their goods. Hence they insult everyone with such haughtiness and such licence, and do whatever they like with impunity; as it has already become a proverb among the Papists themselves, that if anyone is punished for crimes they say to him: If you had been a Jesuit, you would have done it with impunity. To others whom they know to be in the Pope's favour they say: You have a gracious Pontiff; but take care not to offend. ... the Jesuits, by whom, when angered, the Pope's clemency turns into fury. Others in cases speak more openly: If I had to plead my cause before the Pope, I would rather have the Jesuits on my side than have Christ. For they have more authority and favour with the Pope than Christ does.

units.la: Anno 1575. facultatem illis tribuit, in libris editis quicquid libuerit mutas, detruncare, adulterare & corrumpere. Hinc fit, quod Iesuitæ, terras mariaue peragrantes, & Bibliothecas perlustrantes, Patrum & Historicorum tum eterum tum recentiorum scripta eis repugnantia, interpolant; voces, sentenas, quin integras paginas addunt, assuunt, detrahunt, mutant, mutilant & orrumpunt, pro arbitratu seu libidine sua, quod isti honesto, scilicet, titulo; si ijs placet, Libros repurgare vocant. Hoc iuris autem nullus unquam bonus ir sibi sumpsit: tentarunt autem idem saepe Ariani, aliique impudentissimi & auacissimi haeretici, quo facilius portetosa sua dogmata contra orthodoxos tuepossent. Expergescimini igitur, qui ad clavum Ecclesiarum & Scholarum seetis, & hoc audax facinus diligenter attendite, ne quid detrimenti Ecclesiæ & cholæ vestræ fidei commissæ, inde accipiant.
units.tr: In 1575 he granted them the faculty to change, cut down, adulterate and corrupt whatever they liked in books they publish. Hence the Jesuits, roaming over land and sea and rummaging through libraries, falsify the writings of the Fathers and historians, both ancient and recent, whenever those writings oppose them. They add, insert, remove, alter, mutilate and corrupt words, sentences and even whole pages, as they please and at their own discretion. They call this, under an honourable title, "purging books," if they like the word. No good man has ever claimed this right for himself. The Arians and other most shameless and reckless heretics have often tried the same, so that they might more easily defend their pernicious doctrines against the orthodox. Wake up, then, you who sit at the helm of Churches and schools, and pay close attention to this bold outrage, lest your Churches and schools, entrusted to you, suffer any harm from it.

units.la: Anno 1576. die 16. Febr. concedit Gregorius Papa Iesuitis etiam medeni facultatem, qua liceat ipsis, exceptà ustione, medicos & chirurgos agere, & ræcipit, ne quis vel medicorum, vel chirurgorum eos impediat. Hoc privigium extorsit avaritia Iesuitarum, ne cogerentur vel ipsi infirmi sumptus leitimis & ordinariis Medicis solvere, vel potius nefandos suos morbos aliis reelare. Ideo propriōs habent medicos, tonsores & pharmacopolia, ut sic ubique in omnibus quaestum facere possint.
