units.la: Sub finem autem anni 1594 opportune prioribus gravissimis iustificationibus accusationibus accessit horrendum parricidium Ioannis Castellij octodecim annorum adolescentis, & Collegij Iesuitarum, cui nomen est Clarmontium Lutetiae alumni, qui Regem Henricum IV. e medio tollere voluit. Crimine igitur sententia Castellione hoc ad mortem damnato a Parlamento, suo premio Regio Consilio, decernitur simul eadem sententia, Ut omnes Sacerdotes Clarmontij Collegij, & omnes Iesuitica Societati addicti, tanquam corruptores iuventutis, pertur-batores publicae tranquillitatis, inimici Regis & Regni, infra tres dies post promulgationem editi, Lutetiae, & aliis urbibus atque locis, ubi sua habeant Collegia, discedant, & infra quindecim subsequentes dies toto Regno exeant, ut inferius ex ipso edicto Lector plenius intelliget.
units.tr: Towards the end of the year 1594, at a fitting moment, there was added to the earlier very grave charges and accusations the horrible parricide of John Chastel, an eighteen-year-old youth and a pupil of the Jesuit college called Clermont at Paris, who wished to remove King Henry IV from the midst. Therefore, Chastel having been condemned to death by Parliament for this crime, the Royal Council decrees at the same time the following sentence: that all priests of the Clermont college and all who are attached to the Jesuit Society, as corruptors of youth, disturbers of public tranquillity, and enemies of King and kingdom, shall depart from Paris and the other cities and places where they have their colleges within three days after the edict is published, and shall leave the whole kingdom within the fifteen days following. The reader will understand this more fully from the edict itself, below.

units.la: Quamvis autem multa Iesuitae opponerent, ac scriptis etiam apud Regem causam suam agere ac defendere niterentur, tamen ut admitteretur iterum impetrare non potuerunt, sed solum vertere cogebantur.
units.tr: Although the Jesuits objected much and tried to plead and defend their cause also in writing before the King, they could not obtain readmission, but were compelled only to depart.

units.la: Qui igitur Lutetiæ erant Iesuitæ, earumque asseclæ omnes, portâ Antoniâ emissi, comitantibus lugentibusque discipulis, alii Virodunum, alii in Lotharingiam & Germaniam, alii in Belgium præsertim Antuerpiam, sese receperunt. Quotquot etiam in finibus Parisiensis Curiæ, ut Auarici Biturigum, Nouioduni ad Ligerim & Ludouni habitárunt, coacto coetu, evectisque carris Rhodano Auenionem devehuntur. Qui Rotomagi Scholas habuerunt, quamquam Lutetiano foro exempti essent, tamen odio vulgi alio penates suos efferre coguntur. Vsque adeo tædebat omnes tentati parricidii, ut vel ad fontes obiurgatio, querimonia, & ipsa ultio redire. Qui enim in Scholis Iesuitarum tyrocinium egerant, torve adspiciebantur; pro hæretico, iamque ad publicam pyram deducendus existimabatur, qui vel verbo á Iesuitis parricidium Castelli depellere voluisset.
units.tr: Those who were Jesuits at Paris, together with all their adherents, were sent out through the Porte Antoine, accompanied and mourned by their pupils. Some withdrew to Verdun, some to Lorraine and Germany, and others especially to Belgium, to Antwerp. Likewise all those who lived in the districts of the Parisian court, as at Bourges, at Nevers on the Loire, and at Lyons, having gathered their company and loaded their carts, were carried down the Rhône to Avignon. Those who kept schools at Rouen, although exempt from the jurisdiction of Paris, were nevertheless forced by popular hatred to carry their household gods elsewhere. So much did everyone loathe the attempted parricide that reproach, complaint and vengeance itself flowed back to their very sources. Those who had served their apprenticeship in the Jesuit schools were looked at askance, and anyone who had even tried to turn aside Chastel's parricide with a word in the Jesuits' defence was thought a heretic, ready to be led to the public pyre.

units.la: Eiectis ex Gallia Iesuitis, quia Petrus Castellus, supra dicti Ioannis Castelli pater, filii sui parricidiale contra Regem propositum, ab ipsomet intellectum erat, & nihilominus occultaverat apud se ac reticuerat, á Parlamento iudicatum fuit, ut quæ erat eius ante Prætoriam Portam Palatii domus, funditus destrueretur, publicaretur, & nunquam in posterum reædificaretur; sed in eius area, ad perenne monumentum immortalis flagitii pyramis seu columna erigeretur, quæ literato marmore Senatusconsultum publice testaretur: atque in eius vertice crux aurea fastigietur; quaternisque angulis totidem insideant virginei virtutes, quas Cardinales vocant, quadrifariam adglutinatæ marmoreis tabulis, in quibus Senatus consultum literis aureis scriptum esset, & parricidium Castelli, adeoque causa, ob quam Iesuitæ in exilium relegati, unà cum Gallia exturbati sint, sequentem in modum.
units.tr: After the Jesuits had been expelled from France, because Peter Chastel, father of the aforesaid John Chastel, had learned of his son's parricidal plot against the King from the son himself and nevertheless had concealed it and kept silent, Parliament adjudged that his house, which stood before the Palace gate, should be utterly destroyed and confiscated, and never rebuilt in future. On its site a pyramid or column was to be erected as a lasting monument of the immortal crime, publicly attesting the decree of the Senate in lettered marble. On its summit a golden cross was to be set, and at its four corners four virtues, which they call cardinal, were to sit, fastened fourfold to marble tablets on which the decree of the Senate would be written in golden letters, together with the parricide of Chastel, and thus the cause for which the Jesuits were banished into exile and driven out along with France, in the following manner.

units.la: ARRESTVM CVRIAE, VT ET VERSVS, ET T- RACTATVS LATINI NIGRO MARMORI LITERIS AUREIS INSCRI- PTI IN QVATUOR FACIEBVS BASEOS PYRAMIDIS, ANTE PALATII PORTAM PARISIIS EXTRVCTAE.
units.tr: The Decree of the Court, as well as the Verses and the Latin Treatise, Inscribed in Gold Letters on Black Marble on the Four Faces of the Base of the Pyramid Erected Before the Gate of the Palace at Paris.

units.la: Visso per curiam, magna Camera & Tornellis in unum coactis, criminali processu per præfectum Palatii Regii incepto, & postea in eadem peracto, ad petitionem procuratoris generalis Regii actoris & accusatoris adversus Iohannem Chastellium, Parisiorum, & studiosum, qui studiorum cursum in collegio Claromontano absolvit, captum in Palatii carcere detentum ob maximè execrandum & abominandum parricidium in Regis personam intentatum: Quæstionibus & confessionibus eiusdem Iohannis Chastel auditi & interrogati in eadem Curia super eiusdem parricidii negotio: Auditis itidem eodem loco Iohanne Gueret presbytero, qui se de congregatione & Societate Iesus affirmabat esse, eodem in collegio agente & antehac eiusdem Iohannis Chastel præceptore: Petro Chastel & Dionysia Hazart parentibus præfati Iohannis: Conclusionibus Generalis procuratoris Regii & rebus omnibus perpensis.
units.tr: Having been seen through the Court, the Great Chamber and the Tournelle being brought together into one body; the criminal process having been begun by the prefect of the Royal Palace and afterwards completed in the same; at the petition of the Procurator General of the King, as plaintiff and accuser, against Jean Chastel, a Parisian and a student who completed his course of studies in the Clermont college; who was seized, and held in the prison of the Palace, on account of the most execrable and abominable parricide attempted against the person of the King; having heard the examinations and confessions of the same Jean Chastel, questioned and interrogated in the same Court concerning the matter of that parricide; having likewise heard, in the same place, Jean Guéret, a priest, who affirmed that he was of the congregation and Society of Jesus, working in the same college and formerly the tutor of the said Jean Chastel; Pierre Chastel and Dionysia Hazart, the parents of the aforesaid Jean; the conclusions of the Procurator General of the King; and all matters having been weighed carefully.

units.la: Dicetur eandem curiam pronunciasse & pronunciare præfatum Iohannem Chastel convictum criminis læsæ Majestatis divinæ & humanæ in primo capite, ob maximè impium & maximè detestandum parricidium in Regis personam intentatum: In cuius criminis reparationem præfatum Iohannem Chastel in multam honorariam adjudicavit & condemnavit, ut ante summas valvas templi Parisiani nudus, solo opertus indumento, cum face cerea ponderis duarum librarum manibus gestâ, eaque ardente, flexis genibus licat & pronunciet se iniquissimè inhumanum, & maximè abominandum parricidium ausceptisse, & Regem in facie cultro laesisse: seque falsa & damnanda institutione indultum in suo processu dixisse, Licere Reges occidere, & Regem Henricum quartum nunc regnantem, non esse in Ecclesia usque quò à Pontifice approbatus fuerit: eorumque omnium poenitentia duci, & veniam petere à Deo, à Rege, & à Magistratu. Hisque peractis, ut plaustro in locum Grevianum deducatur, ibique brachijs & foemoribus candentibus forcipibus inuratur, & manus dextra, cultrum, quo praedictum parricidium perpetrare ejus adnixus, gerens, abscindatur, deinde ipsius corpus quatuor equis discerpatur, membra & corpus discerpta in ignem conijciantur, & in cineres redacta in ventos projciantur. Pronunciavit eadem Curia & pronunciat universa & singula eius bona Regi acquisita. Ante quam executionem quaestioni ordinariae & extraordinariae idem Iohannes Chastel applicabitur, ut flagitij sociorum, & aliarum quarundam rerum, quae ex eiusdem processu resultant, veritas innotescere possit: Inhibuit omnibus, cuiuscunque qualitatis aut conditionis demum sint, sub poena criminis laesae Majestatis, ne dicant aut proferant in ullo loco publico, aut privato praedicta verba, quae eadem Curia pronunciavit et pronunciat scandalosa, seditiosa, verbo Dei contraria, & sacris decretis ut haeretica condemnata.
units.tr: It is declared that the same Court pronounced, and does pronounce, that the aforesaid Jean Chastel is convicted of the crime of high treason against divine and human majesty in the first degree, on account of the most impious and most detestable parricide attempted against the person of the King. In reparation of this crime, the Court has adjudged and condemned the aforesaid Jean Chastel to an honorary amend: that before the great doors of the Parisian church he is to be led naked, clothed only in a shirt, carrying in his hands a wax torch weighing two pounds, and burning; and kneeling, he shall declare and proclaim that he has undertaken a most iniquitous, inhuman and most abominable parricide, and has wounded the King in the face with a knife; and that, having been imbued with a false and damnable teaching, he said in his trial that it is lawful to kill kings, and that King Henry IV, now reigning, is not in the Church until he shall have been approved by the Pope; and that he is to be brought to repentance for all these things, and to ask pardon of God, of the King, and of the magistrate. When these things are done, he is to be drawn on a cart to the Place de Grève, and there his arms and thighs are to be branded with red-hot pincers, and his right hand, which holds the knife with which he committed the aforesaid parricide, is to be cut off; then his body is to be torn apart by four horses, and the dismembered limbs and body thrown into the fire, and reduced to ashes and cast to the winds. The same Court has pronounced, and does pronounce, that all and singular his goods are forfeit to the King. Before this execution, the same Jean Chastel is to be subjected to ordinary and extraordinary questioning, so that the truth about the accomplices of his crime and other matters arising from his trial may become known. It forbids everyone, of whatever quality or condition they may be, under penalty of the crime of high treason, to say or utter in any public or private place the aforesaid words, which the same Court has pronounced and does pronounce to be scandalous, seditious, contrary to the Word of God, and condemned as heretical by the sacred decrees.

units.la: Statuit ut presbyteri & studiosi collegij Claromontani, & reliqui omnes qui se eiusdem esse Societatis profitentur, tanquam corruptores juventutis, publicae tranquillitatis perturbatores, Regis hostes & regni, Urbe Parisiana intra tres dies post praesentis Arresti significationem excedant, ut & alijs urbibus & locis, ubi eorum habentur collegia; & quindecim post diebus, toto regno, sub comminatione, si ibidem post id tempori deprehensi fuerint, futurum esse ut puniantur tamquam facinorosi & rei eiusdem criminis laesae Majestatis. Omniaque ipsorum bona tum mobilia, tum immobilia operibus pijs applicabuntur, & quomodo ab ipsa Curia fuerit constitutum. Praeterea inhibet omnibus Regis subditis, ne studiosos in praedicta Societatis collegia quae extra regnum sunt immittant, ut ibidem instituantur, sub pari poena laesae Majestatis.
units.tr: It is ordered that the priests and students of the Clermont college, and all the rest who profess themselves to belong to the same Society, as corruptors of youth, disturbers of public tranquillity, enemies of the King and of the kingdom, shall leave the city of Paris within three days after the signification of the present Decree, and likewise the other towns and places where they have colleges; and that, fifteen days after that, throughout the whole kingdom, under threat that, if they are found there after that time, they will be punished as criminals and guilty of the same crime of high treason. All their goods, both movable and immovable, are to be applied to pious works, and in the manner decided by the Court itself. Moreover, it forbids all the King's subjects to send students to the colleges of the aforesaid Society which are outside the kingdom, to be educated there, under the same penalty of high treason.

units.la: Statuit eadem Curia, ut copia praesentis Arresti, ad praefecturas provinciarum huius ce iudicatus emittatur, ut ibi hic executioni secundum eius formam & tenorem mandetur. Mandat praefectis, eorum locum tenentibus generalibus & particularibus, ut id executioni mandent intra terminum in eo contentum: et Procuratoris generalis substitutis, ut manum teneant ad hoc ut fiat executio, & in delinquentes inquirant Curiam, qui doceant de sua diligentia intra mensem, sub poena privationis officiorum.
units.tr: The same Court ordains that a copy of the present Decree be sent to the prefectures of the provinces of this realm, so that it may be carried into execution there according to its form and tenor. It orders the prefects, and their lieutenants general and particular, to carry it into execution within the term contained in it; and it charges the substitutes of the Procurator General to take care that the execution is made, and to inquire into the offenders, and to report to the Court within a month of their diligence, under penalty of deprivation of their offices.

units.la: SIGNATVM. TILLET.
units.tr: SIGNED. TILLET.

units.la: Pronunciatum ipsi Iohanni Chastel, & executioni mandatum die Iovis vigesimo nono Decembris, Anni 1594.
units.tr: Pronounced to Jean Chastel himself, and ordered into execution on Thursday, the twenty-ninth day of December, in the year 1594.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: QVOD SACRVM VOTVMQVE SIT MEMORIAE, PERENNITATI, LONGAEVITATI, SALVTIQVE MAXI- MI, FORTISS. ET CLEMENTISS. PRINCIPIS HENRICI IV. GALLIAE ET NAVARRAE REGIS CHRISTIANISS.
units.tr: That this is a sacred vow to the memory, perpetuity, long life and safety of the greatest, bravest and most merciful prince Henry IV, Most Christian King of France and Navarre.

units.la: Advi viator, sive es extraneus Sive incola urbis, quoi Paris nomen dedit. Hic alta quae sto pyramis, domus fui Castella, sed quam deruendam funditus Frequens Senatus crimen ultus censuit. Huc me redegit tandem herilis filius, Malis magistris usus & schola impia: Soteri cum, eheu i nomen usurpantibus: Incestus, & mox parricida in Principem, Qui nuper urbem perditam servaverat, Et qui favente saepe victor Numine Deflexit ictum audaculi sicarij, Punctusque tantum est dentium sepio-tenus. Abi Viator, plura me vetat loqui Nostra stupendum civitatis decus.
units.tr: Stop, traveller, whether you are a stranger or a resident of the city that bears the name of Paris. Here stands a lofty pyramid. It was once the house of Castel, but the Senate, often assembled, judged that it should be razed to the ground as punishment for its crime. To this place at last my master's son brought me, having been trained by wicked teachers and an impure school. Alas, he took the name of Saviour, yet he was incestuous and soon became a parricide against the Prince who had lately saved the ruined city, and who, often victorious by the favour of God, turned aside the blow of a daring assassin, who pricked him only as far as the gums. Go, traveller; our city's wondrous ornament forbids me to say more.

units.la: IN PYRAMIDEM EANDEM.
units.tr: On the same pyramid.

units.la: Quae trahit a puro sua nomina Pyramis igne, Ardua barbaricas olim decoraverat urbes: Nunc decori non est, sed criminis arapiatrix: Omnia nam flammis pariter purgantur & undis. Hic tamen esse pius monimentum insigne Senatus, Principis incolumis statuit, quo sospite, casum Nec metuet pietas, nec Res grave publica damnum.
units.tr: The pyramid, which takes its name from pure fire, once adorned the barbarian cities with its height. Now it is no ornament but an avenger of crime, for all things are purged alike by flames and waters. Yet here the Senate has resolved to set up a pious and distinguished monument while the Prince is safe. While he is safe, piety will fear no disaster, nor will the commonwealth fear grave loss.

units.la: III. D. O. M.
units.tr: III. To God, Best and Greatest (D. O. M.)

units.la: Pro salute Henrici IV. Clementiss. ac fortiss. Regis, quem nefandus parricida periciosiss. factionis haeresi pestifera imbutus, quae nuper abominandis sceleribus pietatis non obtendens, unctos Domini vivas, Majestatis ipsius imagines occidere populariter donat, dum confodere tentat, caelesti numine sceleslam manum inhibente, cultro in labrum superius delato, & dentium occursu feliciter retuso, violare ausus est. Ordo amplissimus, ut vel conatus tam nefarij poenae terror, simul & praesentissimi in Opt. Principem ac gnum, cuius salus in eius salute posita est, divini favoris apud posteros memoria extaret, onstro illo admissus equis membratim discerpto, & flammis ultricibus consumpto: Aedes iam unde prodierat, hoc sitas funditus everti, & in earum locum, salutis omnium ac gloriae signum erigi decrevit. IIII. Non. Jan. Ann. prox. 1595.
units.tr: For the safety of Henry IV, the most merciful and most brave King, whom a wicked parricide, imbued with the pestilent heresy of a most dangerous faction, which lately, under the pretext of piety, dared with abominable crimes to kill the living anointed of the Lord, the very images of his majesty, ventured to violate when he tried to stab him. By heavenly power the criminal hand was restrained: the knife, driven to the upper lip, was happily blunted by the meeting of the teeth. The most august Order decreed that, so that the terror of punishment for so nefarious an attempt, and at the same time the memory of the most manifest divine favour toward the best Prince and kingdom, whose safety rests on his safety, might endure among posterity, the monster, having been torn limb from limb by horses and consumed by avenging flames, should have the house from which he had come razed to the ground on this site, and that in its place a sign of the safety and glory of all should be erected. IIII Non. Jan. in the year next following, 1595.

units.la: EX. S. C.
units.tr: BY DECREE OF THE SENATE

units.la: Heic domus immani quondam fuit hospita monstro, Crux ubi nunc caelsum tollit in astra caput. Sancijt in miseros poenam hanc sacer Ordo Penates, Regibus ut scires sanctius esse nihil.
units.tr: Here once a house was host to a monstrous beast; where the cross now lifts its head high toward the stars. The sacred Order decreed this punishment for the wretched household, so that kings might learn that nothing is more sacred.

units.la: IV. D. O. M. SACRVM.
units.tr: IV. To God, Best and Greatest, sacred.

units.la: Quum Henricus Christianissimus Francorum & Navarrorum Rex bono Reipubl. ...utus, inter cetera victoriarum exempla, quibus tam de Tyrannide Hispanica, quam de ...us factione prisca m regni huius Majestatem justis ultus est armis, etiam hanc urbem & re-quas regni huius pene omnes recepisset, ac denique felicitate eius intestinorum Franciae nominis hostium furorem provocante, Ioannes Petri F. Castellus ab illis submissus, sacrum Regis Caput cultro petere ausus esset, praesentiore temeritate, quàm feliciore sceleris successu: Ob eam rem ex ampliss. ordinis consulto, vindicato perduellione, diruta Petri Castelli domo, in qua Ioannes eius F. inexpiabile nefas designatum patri communicaverat, in area aequata hoc perenne monumentum erectum est, in memoriam eius diei, in quo facili felicitas inter vota & metus urbis, liberatorem regni, fundatoremque publicae quietis à temeratoris infando incepto, regni autem huius opes attritas ab extremo interitu vindicavit, pulso praeterea tota Gallia hominum genere nova ac malefica superstitionis, qui Remp. turbabant, quorum instinctu piacularis adolescens dirum facinus instituerat.
units.tr: When Henry, most Christian King of the French and Navarrese, for the good of the Republic, among his other victories, by which he avenged the majesty of this kingdom with just arms, both against Spanish tyranny and against the ancient faction of ..., had recovered this city and almost all the cities of this kingdom, and finally, when his good fortune had provoked the fury of the enemies of the French name within the realm, John Castel, son of Peter, sent by them, dared to aim a knife at the sacred head of the King, showing more rashness than success in his crime: for this reason, by decree of the most distinguished order, the treason having been avenged, the house of Peter Castel, in which his son John had communicated the unspeakable crime he had planned to his father, was razed, and on the leveled site this everlasting monument was erected, in memory of that day on which happiness, between the prayers and fears of the city, freed the kingdom's liberator and founder of public peace from the unspeakable undertaking of the violator, and rescued the wasted resources of this kingdom from utter ruin, and, moreover, with all of France having driven out the new and harmful class of men who were disturbing the Republic, at whose instigation the guilty young man had undertaken his dreadful deed, of a superstition.

units.la: S. P. Q. P.
units.tr: The Senate and People of Paris.

units.la: Extinctori pestiferae factionis Hispanicae, incolumitate eius & vindictae parricidij lati Majestatisque eius devotiff. Duplex potestas ista fatorum fuit, Gallis saluti quod foret, Gallis dare: Servare Gallus, quod dedissent optimum.
units.tr: To the extinguisher of the pestilent Spanish faction, to his safety and to the avenger of the parricide planned against his majesty, his most devoted. This double power of the fates was to give whatever would be salvation to the Gauls: the Gauls were to preserve the best thing they had been given.

units.la: Post aliquod tempus multi Iesuitarum, qui e Regno Galliae relegati erant, in id rursus se intrudere conabantur. Alii igitur mutarunt sua nomina & vestes; alii simularunt se Ordinem ac sectam Iesuiticam abiurâsse, petere igitur ut rursus recipiantur constituendarum Scholarum vel praedicandi causa. Horum subdolorum conatuum Curia Parlamenti Parisiensis certiorfacta, Arresto omnibus subditis totius Regni prohibuit, ne Iesuitas in hos usus vel publice vel privatim recipiant. Arrestum de verbo ad verbum sic habet.
units.tr: Some time later, many Jesuits who had been banished from the kingdom of France again tried to force their way back in. Some therefore changed their names and their clothes; others pretended that they had renounced the Jesuit order and sect, and so asked to be received again, either to set up schools or for the purpose of preaching. The Parlement of Paris, having been informed of these deceitful attempts, forbade by an Arrest all subjects of the whole kingdom to receive the Jesuits for these purposes, either publicly or privately. The Arrest reads word for word as follows.

units.la: EXTRACTVM EX REGVLIS PARLAMENTI.
units.tr: EXTRACT FROM THE REGISTERS OF THE PARLIAMENT.

units.la: Postquam Procurator Regis Generalis ostendit ac demonstravit, se certiorem esse factum, quod quidam eorum, qui antehac e Societate illa de nomine Iesu dicta, tam in Collegio Claremontano huius urbis Parisiensis, quàm in aliis huius Regni locis fuerunt, in plures urbes, praesertim limitaneas, redivissent, ubi constituendarum Scholarum, & praedicandi causa, sub pretextu, quòd pristinam, ut praeferrent, pratensi Ordinis & fectae illius Societatis professionem abjurassent, recepti erant: Ex quo periculum foret, ne juventus per pravarum doctrinarum blanditias & illecebras corrumperetur, & populus falsis praedicationibus circumveniretur: quodque, si toleraretur, Arresto Curiae 29. Decemb. Anno 1594. declaratum, contemptui & illusioni exponeretur: ea de causa requisivit, ut omnibus personis, corporibus & communitatibus, officialibus & privatis, cujuscunque sint qualitatis, aut conditionis, mandaretur, ne quenquam eorum, qui de dicta nomine Iesu Societate se dicunt, sub pretextu cujuscunque abjurationus, quam fecissent, aut facere possent, sive scholarum vel publice vel privatim constituendarum, sive in Ecclesiis praedicandi, sive quacunque alia de causa reciperent, aut recipi paterentur, ijs qui illos receperunt, recipient, aut tolerabunt, quòd laesae Majestatis rei & convitii declarandi sint, poena indicta: Iesuitis etiam, ijs, quae in dicto Arresto continentur, supplicijs propositis. Dicta curia, deliberatione, super hac materia habita, decrevit ac decernit, ut dictum Arrestum 29. Decembris, Anno 1594. promulgatum, secundum formam, & tenorem suum executioni mandetur, & juxta illud mandavit, & mandat omnibus personis, corporibus & communitatibus civitatum, officiarijs & privatis, cujuscunque sint qualitatis aut conditionis, ne quenquam Presbyterorum, aut scholarium de Societate nominis Iesu se dicentium, quamvis etiam pristinum Professionis suae votum abjurârint, eique renunciârint, sive Scholarum publice privatimve constituendarum, sive quacunque alia de causa recipiant, aut recipi patiantur: ijs, qui secus facient, quòd laesae Majestatis rei, & convitii declarari, clarari debent poenâ indicta. Injunxit & inungit Diœcesis & Præfectis, aut ipsorum cum tenentibus, ut executioni præsens hoc Arrestum mandari faciant; Gubernatoribus earum, ut manum huic rei admoveant: & substitutis dicti Procuratoris Generalis, ut diligentiam in his adhibeat, & Curiam intra 15. diem certiorem reddant, pœnâ proprio nomine respondendi propositâ. Factum in Curia 21. Augusti. Anno 1597.
units.tr: Whereas the King's Procurator General has shown and demonstrated that he has been informed that some of those who formerly belonged to the Society called by the name of Jesus, both in the College of Clermont in this city of Paris and in other places in this kingdom, have returned to many towns, especially those on the frontiers, where they have been received, under the pretext that they have renounced the former profession of that Order and Society (as they put it), for the purpose of founding schools and preaching. From this there is danger that the young may be corrupted by the enticements and allurements of perverse doctrines, and the people deceived by false preaching; and that, if this were tolerated, the Arrest of the Court of 29 December 1594 would be exposed to contempt and mockery. For this reason he asked that it be ordered to all persons, bodies and communities, officials and private individuals, of whatever quality or condition, that they should not receive, nor allow to be received, any of those who call themselves of the Society of the name of Jesus, under the pretext of any renunciation which they have made or might make, whether for the founding of schools, publicly or privately, or for preaching in churches, or for any other cause; and that those who receive, will receive, or tolerate them shall be declared guilty of treason against majesty and of insult, with the penalty imposed; the Jesuits also to suffer the punishments set out in the said Arrest. The said Court, after deliberation on this matter, has decreed and decrees that the said Arrest, promulgated on 29 December 1594, be carried into execution according to its form and tenor; and in accordance with it has commanded and commands all persons, bodies and communities of the towns, officials and private individuals, of whatever quality or condition, that they shall not receive, nor allow to be received, any of the priests or scholars who call themselves of the Society of the name of Jesus, even though they have abjured the former vow of their profession and renounced it, whether for the founding of schools publicly or privately, or for any other cause; those who act otherwise shall be declared guilty of treason against majesty and of insult, and shall be punished with the penalty imposed. It enjoins and charges the Bailiffs and Prefects, or their lieutenants, to cause the present Arrest to be carried into execution; the Governors of the provinces to lend their hand to this matter; and the deputies of the said Procurator General to take care in these matters and to report to the Court within fifteen days, under penalty of answering in their own name. Done in the Court, 21 August 1597.

units.la: Signatum Bodin.
units.tr: Signed: Bodin.

units.la: ARRESTVM CVRIAE PARISIENSIS CONTRA IESVITAS LVGDVNENSES, NE IBI SCHOLAS INSTI- TVANT, AVT CONCIONES HABEANT; EXTRA- CTVM EX REGISTRO PAR- LAMENTI.
units.tr: A DECREE OF THE PARIS COURT AGAINST THE JESUITS OF LYONS, THAT THEY MAY NOT ESTABLISH SCHOOLS THERE OR HOLD SERMONS; EXTRACTED FROM THE REGISTER OF THE PARLIAMENT.

units.la: DIe Iovis, 16. Octob. Anno 1597. quum Mario loco Procuratoris Generalis Regis in Camera Vacationum dixisset, quod juxta illius decretum ipsi in manus Balonij Procuratoris in Parlamento, & Procuratoris Præfectorum Mercatorum, & Bulentarum civitatis Lugdunensis obtestationes illas tradidisset, quæ in conventu generali in Curia municipali dictæ urbis Lugdunensis 20. Septembris proximi habita recitatæ, & per illos dicto Procuratori generali transmissæ fuerunt, super executione Arresti 21. Augusti proximi die decreto, per quod omnibus personis, corporibus & communitatibus, quenquam præsbyterorum & cholarium de Societate nominis Iesu se dicentium recipere prohibitum fuit, licet etiam triennio professionis suæ voto renunciassent, illudque abjurassent, sub pœnis in eo contentis.
units.tr: On Thursday, 16 October 1597. When Mario, in place of the King's Procurator General, had said in the Chamber of Vacations that, in accordance with its decree, he had handed over to Balonius, Procurator in Parliament, and to the Procurator of the Prefects of the Merchants and of the Bulentae of the city of Lyons, those objections which had been read out at the general assembly held in the municipal court of the said city of Lyons on 20 September last, and had been sent through them to the said Procurator General, concerning the execution of the decree of 21 August last, by which it was forbidden for all persons, bodies and communities to receive any priests or scholars calling themselves of the Society of the name of Jesus, even if they had renounced the vow of their profession after three years and abjured it, under the penalties contained in that decree.

units.la: Ut etiam Ballonio proximo die Martis injunctum fuisset, ut consilium dictorum Præfectorum, Mercatorum, & Bulentarum certius faceret, & hoc mane adesset: Ballonius ipse de re in dicta Camera auditus fuit, qui dixit, se hoc decretum M. Bartholomæo Thomæ dictæ Civitatis Lugdunensis Secretario in hac urbe jam præsenti notum fecisse, qui se nulla memorialia & instructiones ea de re habere sibi respondisset. Et cum dictus Ballonius juxta dictæ Cameræ illas obtestationes prælegisset, & Mario, loco Procuratoris generalis, is propter rationes, ab ipso deductas nulla consideratione dignas esse dixisset: Requirens mul, ut, ijs non obstantibus, dictum Arrestum 21. Augusti declaratum in urbe Lugdunensi executioni mandaretur, præsertim quantum id Porsanum in dictis obtestationibus denominatum attineret. Et ut nihilominus Porsanus ille, antequam cum executione contra ipsum procederetur, captivus in custodias Palatij duceretur, juxta Arrestum de ipso in vincula conij ciendo per dictam Cameram decretum, quo juxta crimina, & informationes contra ipsum facti processus adversus eum formaretur, & perficeretur: mandato simul substituto Procuratoris generalis ijs in locis dato, ut omnem diligentiam adhiberet: ac præter auxilio Præfectis Mercatorum, & Buteutarum ad Principalem & Regentem Catholicum dolum, & virtutibus præditum, Institutionijuventutis in dicta urbe Lugdunensi inveniendum, oblato. Illis digressis, re in deliberationem sumpta:
units.tr: Likewise, it had been enjoined on Balonius the following Tuesday that he should make the counsel of the said Prefects, Merchants and Bulentae more certain, and be present this morning. Balonius himself was heard in the said Chamber on the matter, and he said that he had made this decree known to M. Bartholomew Thomas, Secretary of the said city of Lyons, who was now present in this city, and that he had replied that he had no memorials or instructions on this matter. And when the said Balonius had read aloud those objections before the said Chamber, and Mario, in place of the Procurator General, had said that the reasons advanced by him were not worthy of any consideration, he nevertheless demanded that, notwithstanding these, the said decree of 21 August, as declared, be carried into execution in the city of Lyons, especially as far as that Porsanus named in the said objections is concerned. And that, nevertheless, before proceedings were taken against him by execution, that Porsanus be led away a prisoner into the custody of the Palace, according to the decree of the said Chamber for casting him into chains, so that a legal process be formed and completed against him in accordance with the crimes and informations made against him; with a deputy of the Procurator General being appointed in those places to use all diligence; and besides, that aid be offered to the Prefects of the Merchants and Bulentae for finding a Principal and a Catholic Regent endowed with learning and virtues for the instruction of youth in the said city of Lyons. When they had withdrawn, the matter was taken into deliberation.

units.la: Dicta Camera, nullo dictarum obtestationem habito respectu, decrevit & decernit, ut dictum Arrestum 21. Aug. proximi declaratum juxta formam & tenorem suum, in urbe Lugdunensi executioni mandetur: præsertim quantum ad dictum Porsanum attinet, quæ in isto comprendendi declaravit & declarat. Et nihilominus, juxta Arrestum 25. Sept. statuit, ut Porsanus ille capiatur, & captivus in custodias Palatij ducatur: quo de ijs, quæ in informationib. ante ac factis continentur, interrogetur & audiatur, & contra eum, pro ut ratio postulabit, procedatur: Injunxit & injungit substituto dicti Procuratoris generalis in Municipio, & sedeæ præsidiali Lugdunensi, ut Arrestum hoc præsens executioni mandari faciat; & Curiæ Parlamenti de sua diligentia intra mensem certiorem reddat. Et quantum ad administrationem & directionem Collegij dictæ urbis Lugdunensis attinet, ei de principali, Rectore & aliis personis idoneis & capacibus, pro ut ratio postulabit, prospicietur. Et præsens hoc Arrestum ex vi Extracti illius exsecutioni mandabitur. Signatum: Tillet.
units.tr: The said Chamber, with no regard had to the said objections, decreed and decrees that the said decree of 21 August last, as declared, be carried into execution in the city of Lyons according to its form and tenor, especially as far as the said Porsanus is concerned, whom it declared and declares to be included in it. And nevertheless, according to the decree of 25 September, it ordered that the said Porsanus be seized and led away a prisoner into the custody of the Palace, where he is to be questioned and heard on those matters contained in the informations made before and against him, and that proceedings be taken against him as the case shall require. It enjoined and enjoins the deputy of the said Procurator General in the municipality and presidial seat of Lyons that he cause this present decree to be carried into execution, and that he report to the Court of Parliament within a month on his diligence. And as far as the administration and direction of the College of the said city of Lyons is concerned, provision shall be made for it, with a principal, rector and other suitable and capable persons, as the case shall require. And this present decree shall be carried into execution by virtue of its extract. Signed: Tillet.

units.la: DE PROPAGATIONE
units.tr: On the Propagation

units.la: Ex his intelligitur Arresta & decreta haec non levi animorum motu, sed matura deliberatione praehabita, prolata fuisse. Id etiam testatur Arrestum Parlamenti Parisiensis 18. Augusti, Anno 1598, contra Dominum Touronensem, Iesuitas in suo territorio defendentem, integro anno evoluto, quo prohibetur omnibus cuiuscunque sint status aut conditionis, liberos ad Collegia Iesuitarum quocunque sint in loco, literarum causa mittere. Id enim sic de verbo ad verbum habet.
units.tr: From these things it is clear that these decrees and judgments were issued not out of a passing burst of feeling but after mature deliberation. The judgment of the Parlement of Paris of 18 August 1598 also bears witness to this, against the Lord of Tours, who defended the Jesuits in his territory. It forbids, for a full year, that anyone of whatever rank or condition send children to Jesuit colleges, wherever they may be, for the sake of their studies. For it reads word for word as follows:

units.la: Henricus, Gratia Dei, Galliae & Navarrae Rex, omnibus, qui literas praesentes viderint, salutem. Notum facimus, quod super iis, quae Procurator noster generalis, a Magistro Ludovico Servino, & Simone Marione Advocatis nostris adjutus, Curiae nostri Parlamenti per dictum Servinum ostendit, quod scilicet per Arrestum 1. Octob. superiori die publicatum Dominus Touronensis condemnatus fuisset, ut Presbyteros & Scholares de Societate nominis Iesu se dicentes, intra duos menses, pro ultima dilatione ipsi a significatione praefixos, e finibus & limitibus urbis & Dominij Touronensis discedere & abire faceret, & uno mense post subpoenis ibi constitutis, dictam nostram Curiam certiorem redderet: quod id Arrestum dicto Touronensi in hac urbe Parisiensi undecimo dicti mensis Octobris personaliter significatum fuisset: & ille tamen nihilominus non satisfecisset, neque obedivisset.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God King of France and Navarre, to all who shall see these present letters, greeting. We make known that concerning those matters which our Procurator General, aided by our advocates Master Louis Servin and Simon Marion, laid before our Court of Parliament through the said Servin: namely, that by the decree published the previous day, on 1 October, the Lord of Tours had been condemned to cause the priests and scholars who call themselves of the Society of the name of Jesus to depart and withdraw from the boundaries and territory of the city and lordship of Tours within two months, the last extension granted to him from the date of notification; and that one month after that, he was to inform our said Court, through the summonses issued there, of his compliance; that this decree had been served personally on the said Lord of Tours in this city of Paris on the eleventh day of the said month of October; and yet he had nonetheless not complied and had not obeyed.

units.la: Quod etiam ipse, dictus noster Procurator generalis, certior factus esset, multos subditorum nostrorum, contra inhibitiones per Arrestum 29. Decembris, Anno 1594 promulgatas, liberos suos in dictam urbem Touronensem & Pontamoufonium & in alias regiones & loca tam intra quam extra Regnum, ad Collegia dicta praetensa Societatis nominis Iesu, studiorum & institutionis causa emisisse.
units.tr: Our said Procurator General also was informed that many of our subjects, contrary to the prohibitions published by the decree of 29 December 1594, had sent their children to the said city of Tours and to Pont-à-Mousson, and to other regions and places both within and outside the kingdom, to the colleges of the so-called Society of the name of Jesus, for the sake of study and instruction.

units.la: DICTA NOSTRA CVRIA
units.tr: OUR SAID COURT

units.la: conclusionibus Procuratoris nostri generalis confideratis per Arrestum suum dictum Touronensem poenas in dicto primi Octobris Arresto constitutas incurrisse declaravit & declarat: Decrevit & decernit, ut omnia ipsius bona occupentur, & in nostram potestatem redigantur: Injunxit & injungit nostri Dominij Quaestoribus, singulis in eo, quod sui est officij, ut fructus & proventus recipiant, & de iis, & de aliis acceptorum suorum pecuniis, rationem reddant, juxta designationes, quae penes Thesaurarios Galliae fient, & quas illi in manus dictorum Quaestorum tradent. um declaravit, & declarat. Mandavit & mandat Vicarijs & Officialibus dictæ præsturæ, ne ipsis ullum ingressum aut dignitatem in suis sedibus permittant: & omnibus stris subditis, ut ipsum pro tali agnoscant: Notarijs, ne ullas commissiones, sententias, alias actiones in ipsius nomine amplius concipiant: Omnibus Rationalibus, ne ipsi ulstipendia, aut jura propter dictum officium solvant: omnia sub pœna repetendorum storum stipendiorum & jurium privationis officij, amendarum arbitriarum, & aliaum majorum multarum, si secus actum fuerit. Et præterea mandavit, ac præcepit, addat & præcipit omnibus personis, ne scholasticos ad Collegia dictæ prætensæ Societis, quocunque tandem in loco & regione sint, studiorum causa emittant: pœnis, quæ dictis Arrestis continentur, indictis, quæ denuo locis & regionibus consuetis publicantur, quo omnibus innotescant. Et dicto nostro Procuratori generali negotium in ea, ut secus agentur inquirendi committetur, ut informationibus in dicta Curia nostra faris, per eandem adversus contravenientes, prout ratio postulabit, procedatur. Et de asenti decrevit, & decernit, ut omnes nostri subditi, qui in Collegijs dictæ prætensæ Societatis, vel intra vel extra Regnum post Arrestum vigesimo nono Decembris, Anno illesimo quingentesimo nonagesimo quarto decretum, informati, aut instituti fuerunt, nul- lis privilegijs Academicis, tanquam graduum incapaces, fruantur. Gradus etiam, quos m obtinuerunt, aut in posterum in quacunque Academia obtinebunt, nullos, nullius omenti & valoris declaramus, ut ratione eorum nec docere, nec officijs ornari, nec neficijs gradum assici, nec in dicta Curia nostra, aut alijs quibuscunque locis pro Adocatus recipi, nec ullis juribus, prærogativis & præeminentijs, fructibus, commodis, aut olumentis dictorum graduum frui possint. Decernit dicta nostra Curia, ut præsens Arstum in omnibus municipijs & præfecturis promulgetur: injungit substitutis dicti Proratoris nostri generalis, ut executionem eius persequantur, & dictam Curiam certiorem ddant de ijs, quæ contra dictum vigesimi noni Decembris, anni millesimi quingentesimi nagefimi quarti, Arrestum agentur, sese informent: & informationes intra duos menses d Grapheum mittant, pœna illis proprio & privato nomine respondendi proposita. Sic : Decreto dicta nostra Curia mandamus omnibus Dioecetis, præfestis, aut ipsorum lom tenentibus, singulis in sua Dioecesi & præfectura, & suo loco, ad quos hoc pertinebit, præsens Arrestum, juxta formam & tenorem suum debita & integræ executioni mannt: omnes eos, qui ad hoc cogendi sunt, modis & medijs debitis & æquis cogentes. Mandamus omnibus, ut hisce sicuti decebit, obediant. Datum Parisijs in Parlamento stro, decimo octavo die Augusti, Anno gratiæ millesimo quingentisimo nonagesimo octao, Regni nostri decimo.
units.tr: Having considered the submissions of our Procurator General, our said Court has declared, and by this judgment declares, that the said lord of Tours has incurred the penalties laid down in the judgment of 1 October. It has decreed, and by this decree decrees, that all his goods be seized and brought into our possession. It has enjoined, and by this order enjoins, our treasurers of our domain, each within the scope of his office, to collect the revenues and proceeds and to render account of them and of the other sums they receive, according to the schedules to be drawn up before the Treasurers of France, which they shall hand over to the said treasurers. It has declared, and declares, the said lord of tours' office forfeit. It has ordered, and orders, the vicars and officials of the said provostship not to allow him any entry or dignity in their seats, and all our subjects to acknowledge him as such no longer. It orders the notaries not to draw up any further commissions, sentences or other acts in his name; and all accountants not to pay him any salaries or fees on account of the said office. All this is under penalty of repaying the salaries and fees received, deprivation of office, arbitrary fines, and other greater penalties if anything is done otherwise. Moreover, it has commanded and ordered, and now commands and orders all persons not to send scholars to the colleges of the so-called Society, wherever in any place or region they may be, for the sake of study, under the penalties laid down in the said judgments, which are again to be published in the usual places and regions so that all may know them. And our said Procurator General is charged with inquiring into the matter, so that if others act otherwise, proceedings may be taken against the offenders in our said Court by means of informations, as the case requires. And with the advice of our council it has decreed, and decrees, that all our subjects who have been educated or instructed in the colleges of the so-called Society, whether within or beyond the Kingdom, after the judgment of 29 December 1594, shall enjoy no academic privileges, as incapable of degrees. Likewise we declare null and of no force or value any degrees they have obtained or will obtain in future in any university, so that by reason of them they may neither teach, nor be adorned with offices, nor be promoted to benefices, nor be admitted as advocates in our said Court or in any other place, nor enjoy any rights, prerogatives and pre-eminences, fruits, advantages or emoluments of the said degrees. Our said Court orders that this present judgment be published in all towns and prefectures. It enjoins the deputies of our said Procurator General to pursue its execution and to inform themselves of what is done against the said judgment of 29 December 1594, and to send their information to the Registry within two months, under penalty of answering for it in their own name and at their own risk. Thus by decree our said Court commands all bailiffs, seneschals, or their lieutenants, each within his own diocese and prefecture and place, to whom this shall pertain, to carry out this present judgment in full and due execution according to its form and tenor, compelling all those who are to be compelled by due and fair means. We command all to obey these things as is fitting. Given at Paris in our Parlement, on the eighteenth day of August, in the year of grace 1598, the tenth of our reign.

units.la: Signatum per Cameram.
units.tr: Signed by the Chamber.

units.la: Exasto iam fere decennio a Iesuitarum ex Gallia eiectione, anno videlicet soi, totis viribus, conatibus ac modis variis, imprimisq; Apologijs, & supplicibus libellis apud Regem tentarunt, ut reciperentur in Regnum denuo.
units.tr: Almost ten years after the expulsion of the Jesuits from France, namely in the year 1603, they tried with all their strength, by every means and in various ways, and above all by apologies and humble petitions, to be received back into the kingdom.

units.la: Sed tunc quidem adhuc temporis tale Responsum a Rege acceperunt. Perlegi go, Sacerdotales, Apologiam vestram, satis verbosam, ac diligenter mecum perpendi omnia, quæ itis scite innocentiæ vestræ gratia collegistis. Quia vero negotiū arduum est, nec res dijudita temere rescindeda, breviter, & ut Regem decet, quid faciendum statua, expona. Totus ja n hoc sum, ut regnū meū bellis civilib. attritū & viribus opibusq; exhaustū, recens cū Hiano pace inita pristino nitori restituam, legibus firmēm, humanitate recreēm. Id quando lia ratione fieri non potest, nisi ut æqualiiure & benevolentia Catholicos & Huguenotas opellatos complettar, tum in Ecclesasticis tum in policiis: accurate mihi de vobis revocanis cogitandum esse video. Novi ego vos viros doctos & discitos; novi zelo Catholica & omana doctrinæ inflammatos; novi vos acerrimo Huguenotarū flagrare odio: novi vos nctorum reliquias, cereos divini Agni orbiculos, Deiparæ Virginis numismata, Rosaria vel aliud quidpiam à Pontifice consecratum, devotè venerari; quæ Huguenotæ ut ridicula aspernantur, ut Idololatrica execrantur. Metuo igitur, ne vehementia, quâ in coronando uti soleris, & condemnationum, quas scribendo iteratis, acerbitate, multorum animos, nunc prorsus pacatos, denuò irritetis, atque ita etiam imprudentes turbarum ac flores sitis. Iam, res ut sunt humanæ, levi aliqua occasione fieri posset (quod tamen nolim) ut bellum inter me & Hispanum recrudescat. Quid tum animi mihi futurum sit, malim vos cogitare, quam me dicere. Quid autem ante quadriennium admissum fuerit, Regi non est, vel vobis vel aliis objectare. Sententiam igitur semel latam non muto. Vos si vere Galli estis, magis totius tranquillitati Regni, quàm vestræ utilitati consulatis. Dixi quæ volui. Abite & valete.
units.tr: At that time they received this reply from the King: "Priests, I have read through your Apology, which is rather wordy, and I have weighed carefully everything you have cleverly gathered in the cause of your innocence. Since the matter is difficult, and a settled question should not be rashly reopened, I will state briefly, as befits a king, what I intend to do. I am wholly intent on this, that my kingdom, worn down by civil wars and drained of its strength and resources, should be restored to its former lustre now that peace has recently been made with Spain, strengthened by laws and refreshed by kindness. If this cannot be done in any other way than by embracing both Catholics and so-called Huguenots with equal right and goodwill, in church matters as in civil ones, then I see that I must think carefully about how you are to be recalled. I know you to be learned and disciplined men. I know you to be inflamed with Catholic zeal and with all learning. I know you to burn with the fiercest hatred of the Huguenots. I know you to venerate devoutly the relics of the saints, the candles of the divine Lamb, the medals of the Virgin Mother of God, rosaries, and whatever else has been consecrated by the Pope, things which the Huguenots scorn as ridiculous and denounce as idolatrous. I fear, therefore, that by the vehemence with which you are wont to preach, and by the bitterness of the condemnations you repeat in your writings, you will stir up again the minds of many who are now thoroughly calm, and so become, without meaning to, the makers of disturbances and tumults. As human affairs stand, it could happen through some slight occasion (though I would not wish it) that war between me and the Spaniard should break out again. What I would then feel, I would rather you consider than that I should say. What was admitted four years ago, however, it is not for the King to throw in your face or in that of others. I do not change a sentence once pronounced. If you are truly Frenchmen, you will look to the tranquillity of the whole kingdom rather than to your own advantage. I have said what I wished. Go, and farewell."

units.la: Non tamen quiescere statuerunt irrequieti homines, sed post hæc omnia varia rursus inierunt consilia, quibus tandem machinis Regis obstirmatum animum expugnare possent: Pontificis quoque, Reginæ & multorum Principum auxilium opemque implorarunt. Eóque rem deduxerunt, ut rex tandem expugnatus & victus de receptione eorum cogitare inciperet. Amplissimus Curiæ Parlamenti Parisiensis Senatus, cum hoc resciviisset, imprimis quod Pontifex Romanus per Legatos & Nuncios Iesuiticæ sectæ restitutionem per universam Galliam urgeret, nervosâ & verissimâ Oratione 24. Decemb. Anno 1603, a hoc proposito Regem avertere conatus est. In hac Oratione nihil à Parlamenti Parisiensi Regi in memoriam revocatur, quod non Acta ipsissima antecedentia & sequentia evidentissima veritate niti ostendant. Verba autem Orationis illius ex Gallico in Latinum fideliter translata, hæc sunt.
units.tr: Yet these restless men decided not to be quiet. After all this they again adopted various plans, by which at last they might overcome the King's obstinate mind by contrivances. They also implored the help and assistance of the Pope, the Queen and many princes. And they so managed the affair that the King, at last overcome and conquered, began to consider their readmission. When the most distinguished Senate of the Parlement of Paris learned of this, chiefly because the Roman Pontiff was urging, through legates and nuncios, the restoration of the Jesuit sect throughout all France, it sought to turn the King from this purpose by a vigorous and most true Oration, delivered on 24 December 1603. In this Oration nothing is recalled to the King's memory by the Parlement of Paris that the very records before and after do not show to rest on the clearest truth. The words of that Oration, faithfully translated from French into Latin, are these.

units.la: ORATIO PARLAMENTI PARISIEN. CON- TRA IESVITARVM RESTITVTIONEM COMMINATI- ONIBVS PONTIFICIS ROM. PETITAM CORAM REGE HENRICO QVARTO RECITATA.
units.tr: Speech of the Parisian Parliament against the restoration of the Jesuits, sought under threats from the Roman Pontiff, delivered before King Henry IV.

units.la: Parlamenti vestri Curia instituta deliberatione super literis vestris patentibus, deprædyterorum & Scholarium Collegij Claromontani (qui Iesuitarum sibi nomen indiderunt) in quibusdam huius jurisdictionis locis restauratione, decrevit: ut humilimæ obtestationes vestræ Majestati fierent, ac nobis mandavit, ut quædam vobis puncta repræsentaremus, quæ ad rerum vestrarum bonum & ad salutem publicam, quæ à vestri conservatione dependet, multum conferre judicavimus, quæ etiam nos retinuerunt, ne ad earum approbationem continuò procederemus.
units.tr: Your Parliament's court, after deliberating on your letters patent concerning the restoration of the priests and scholars of the Clermont College (who have given themselves the name of Jesuits) in certain places within this jurisdiction, decided that most humble entreaties be made to Your Majesty. It commanded us to set before you certain points which we judged to contribute greatly to the welfare of your affairs and to the public safety, which depends on your preservation. These same points also held us back from proceeding straight away to approve the restoration.

units.la: Et priusquam ad singula proponenda accederemus, ut vobis humilime gratias pro honore ageremus, quo nos afficere placet, quod videlicet gratum vobis sit, ut viva voce hobtestationes faciamus, quo ostenditis vestram erga nos indulgentiam ac benignitatem tanto majore laude dignam, quanto longius à primorum Imperatorum Romanorum auctoritate abest, qui subditis accedendi sui copiam non faciebant, sed cunctas petitiones & supplicationes codicillis sibi exhiberi volebant.
units.tr: Before we came to set out the individual points, we wish first to thank you most humbly for the honour you are pleased to show us, namely that you are willing for us to make these entreaties by living voice. This shows your indulgence and kindness towards us, all the more worthy of praise the further it is from the practice of the earliest Roman emperors, who did not allow subjects access to them but wanted all petitions and supplications presented to them in writing.

units.la: Ordinis huius, qui se Iesuitas dicunt, in hoc Regno institutio, huic statui tam perniciosa judicata fuit, ut se omnes Ordines Ecclesiastici ipsorum admissioni opposuerint, ideoque Collegium Sorbonianum decreverit, quod ista Societas non ad aedificationem, sed ad destructionem inventa esset. Illa quidem in Synodo Ecclesiasticorum Anno 1551. mense Septemb. habita, cui Archiepiscopi & Episcopi interfuerant, & Cardinalis Turonensis præsidebat, approbata fuit, verum tam multis cum clausulis & restrictionibus, ut si Iesuitæ eas observare debuissent, verisimile fuerit, quod locum citò mutaturi fuissent.
units.tr: The establishment of this order, which calls itself the Society of Jesus, in this kingdom was judged so harmful to the state that all the ecclesiastical orders opposed their admission. For this reason the Sorbonne College decreed that this society had been devised not for building up but for destruction. It was indeed approved in the synod of the clergy held in September 1551, at which archbishops and bishops were present and the Cardinal of Tours presided. But it was approved with so many clauses and restrictions that, if the Jesuits had been obliged to observe them, it would have been likely that they would soon have changed their place.

units.la: Nec fuerunt admissi nisi per provisionem, ipsíque Iesuitarum ac Societatis Iesu mentem per Arrestum Anni 1564. assumere prohibitum fuit: quo tamen non obstante, nomen illicitum
units.tr: Nor were they admitted except provisionally, and by a decree of 1564 they were forbidden to assume the mind and character of the Society of Jesus. Nevertheless, in spite of this, they took up the unlawful name

units.la: Rex Galliæ expugnatis, de lestitutione deliberat multi vero à Proposito cum destantur. icitū usurpare, ac fe insuper omni potestati tā seculari, quā Ecclesiasticę eximcvoluerunt. Vos aūt, illos nunc restaurādo, maiori eos auctoritate ornabitis, & ipsorum coditione melio rem, quam unquam fuit reddetis. Dignius itaq; à vestri Parlamenti Senatu iudicatū fuit, imò Procuratores & Advocati, omnesq; Ordines vestri necessariū existimāt, istos homines continere talib^cautionibus, quibus ipsorum licentia, quæ alias in ipsorū actionibus nimis soluta est, cuius quoq; crementum publico bono summe perniciosum esset futurum, impediatur. In otione Advocatorum vestrorum, qui ipsis non patrocinantur, præmonitio est ilde expressa, quod necessariū sit, ut huic rei providearur, ne eo quod iam erspiciunt, peius aliquid inde proveniat.
units.tr: ...and moreover wished to exempt themselves from every power, both secular and ecclesiastical. You, however, by restoring them now, will adorn them with greater authority and will make their condition better than it has ever been. It has therefore been judged more fitting by the Senate of your Parliament, and indeed the procurators, advocates and all your orders think it necessary, that these men be restrained by such safeguards that their licence, which in their actions is otherwise too unrestrained, and whose growth would be most harmful to the public good, be checked. In the speech of your advocates who do not defend them there is a clear warning that this matter must be provided for, lest something worse come of what is already visible.

units.la: Et quemadmodum huius Societatis nome & votum Vniversale est, sic etiam axioma- doctrinæ ipsorum uniformia sunt, quod videlicet Superiorem non agnoscant, nisi S. Patrem nostrum, cui juramentum fidelitatis & obedientiæ in omnibus rebus præstant, & pro regulâ indubitatâ habent, quod ille excommunicandorum Regum potestatem habeat: quod ex excommunicatus nihil sit, aliud quam Tyrannus, cui populus rebellare possit. Quod omnes Regnicolæ, qui minimum in Ecclesia ordinem habent, si quodcunq; crimen committent, illud pro læsæ Majestatis crimine haberi non possit, propterea quod Regum subditi non sunt, nec ad eorum jurisdictionem pertineant: sic ut omnes Ecclesiasticos, & per consequens ipsos à potestate seculari exemptos esse, & impune sanguinarias suas manus sacrasimus Regum personis inijcere posse dicant. Hoc est quod in concionibus apud alios docet, & est, quod scribunt, impugnantes sententias eorum, qui propositiones contrarias tuentur.
units.tr: And just as the name and the vow of this Society is universal, so too their doctrines are uniform: namely, that they acknowledge no superior except our Holy Father, to whom they swear an oath of fidelity and obedience in all things, and they hold as an indubitable rule that he has the power to excommunicate kings, and that an excommunicated king is nothing but a tyrant against whom the people may rebel. From this it follows that all subjects of the kingdom who hold even the lowest rank in the Church, if they commit any crime whatever, cannot be held guilty of treason, because they are not subjects of kings and do not come under their jurisdiction. Thus they say that all ecclesiastics, and consequently they themselves, are exempt from secular power and may with impunity lay their bloody hands on the sacred persons of kings. This is what they teach in sermons elsewhere, and what they write when attacking the opinions of those who uphold contrary propositions.

units.la: Duo juris Doctores Hispani, cum Clericos Regum & Principum potestati subjectos esse adidissent, aliquis ex huius Societatis præcipuis contra eos scripsit, inter cæteras rationes serens, quod sicuti Levitæ in V. T. ab omni potestate seculari exempti fuissent, sic etiam clerici ab eâdē potestate per novum Testamentum immunes & liberi sint, Regesq;& Monarchæ nullam in eos jurisdictionem habeant.
units.tr: Two Spanish doctors of law, having asserted that clergy are subject to the power of kings and princes, were written against by one of the chief men of this Society. Among other arguments he contended that just as the Levites in the Old Testament were exempt from all secular power, so too clerics are, by the New Testament, free and immune from the same power, and that kings and monarchs have no jurisdiction over them.

units.la: Has Regulas, ut nimis falsas, ac erroribus plenissimas, Majestas vestra non approbabit. Oportet igitur, ut illi, qui tenent, & in regno vestro manere volunt, eas publicè in suis collegijs abjurent: Hoc si facere noluerint, permittetisne vos, ut illi hic permaneat & fundamenta potestatis, & auctoritatis vestræ Regiæ subvertat? Sed si id faciant, creditisne vos, quod possint habere aliquam doctrinam, quæ Religionis suæ pars est Romæ; Hispaniæ & ijs omnibus salutarem, quæ eadem & Galliæ talis esse possit: cum illa, quæ alij acceptant, ijciat? & quod de loco in locum commeantes, remeantesq; illam & deponere & recipere sint? Quod si dixerint, se hoc per aliquam dissimulationem secretam posse: quam quaso curitatem vos in ijs ingeniis habebitis, qui in ea professione fuere enutriti, quæ per adversatem & mutationem locorum se bonam & malam reddit?
units.tr: Your Majesty will not approve these rules, as being far too false and full of errors. It is necessary, therefore, that those who hold them, and wish to remain in your kingdom, publicly abjure them in their colleges. If they refuse to do this, will you permit them to remain here and undermine the foundations of your power and royal authority? But if they do so, do you believe they can hold a doctrine which is part of their religion at Rome and in Spain, and which is salutary for all those others, and which could be equally so in France, when it rejects what others accept? And that they can both lay down and take up this doctrine as they travel from place to place and back again? But if they say they can do this by some secret dissimulation, what sincerity, I pray, will you find in those minds which have been nurtured in a profession that makes itself good or bad by changes of circumstance and place?

units.la: Illa doctrina omnibus, quacunque orbis sint plagâ, communis est, & tantas vires in regno vestro assumit, ut si illi restaurati fuerint, tandem in Collegia etiam moderatissima sit reptura. Antehac majorem Adversarium, quam Collegium Sorbonianum non habebant, nec illud ipsum ijs favet, propterea quod in eorum Collegijs quidam Iuniorum Theolorum literis operam dederunt: reliqui idem facient, ad altiora contendent, ac ad prima Parlamentis vestris officia admitti potuerunt, & servantes eandem doctrinam se postati vestræ subducent, cunctaDiadematis vestri jura & Ecclesiæ Gallicanæ libertates persioni relinquentes: ac nullum crimen læsæ Majestatis, quasi per Ecclesiasticum commissum, puniendum censentes. Imò hoc jam fraude suâ effecerunt Iesuitæ, ut continuò Regorum domesticorum vel præcipuorum ministrorum 24. liberi in novo Flesiaco Collegio suitici præceptis imbuantur, & exillis singulis annis ita Regijs officijs præficiantur, ais sex in eorum locum in illud summissus: & sic hisce cuniculis intra paucos annos Iefuitotum illud regnum sub Pontificis & suam tyrannidem adigent.
units.tr: That doctrine is common to every part of the world, and it assumes such strength in your kingdom that, if they are restored, it will in the end creep even into the most moderate colleges. Hitherto they have had no greater adversary than the Sorbonne College, nor does that college favour them, because some young theologians in their colleges have devoted themselves to letters. The rest will do the same, will strive for higher things, and once they can be admitted to the first offices of your Parliaments, holding the same doctrine they will withdraw from the authority of your crown, leaving all the rights of your diadem and the liberties of the Gallican Church to the Pope, and judging that no crime of treason committed by an ecclesiastic should be punished. Indeed, the Jesuits have already achieved this by their craft: the sons of the royal household and of the chief royal ministers, twenty-four of them, are being imbued with Jesuit precepts in the new college at La Flèche, and each year some of them are appointed to royal offices, six being sent in their place to that college. And so, by these underground channels, within a few years they will bring that kingdom under the tyranny of the Pope and of themselves.

units.la: Atque nos adeo in hac nostra vita infelices sumus, ut etiam detestabilia effecta ex
units.tr: And we are so unhappy in this our life that even detestable effects arising from

units.la: DE PROPAGATIONE
units.tr: On the Propagation

units.la: ipsorum institutionibus prodeuntia, in propria vestra sacratissima persona consp exerimu Barrierius (horrescit animus adrei commemorationem) instructus per Varadem fuit, confessus est, se juramento inter ipsius manus in necem vestram facto, Sacramenti communi nem percepisse; sed cum scelus peragere nequivissei; alij animum addiderunt huic prav vipera, qui ex parte peregit, quod conjuraverat. Guignardus libros suos propria sua man scriptos habebat, asserens parricidium in Regem Antecessorem vestrum justissime commi sum esse, confirmando propositionem in Concilio Constantiensi damnatam. Et quid nos, r cordantes pessima ac perfidissima ipsorum acta, quae facile renovari possunt, timendu non habemus?
units.tr: Their teachings led to deeds which were carried out against your most sacred person. Barrière (my mind shudders at the recollection) was instructed by Varade. He confessed that he had received the Sacrament with an oath, made in their hands, to murder you. Since he could not carry out the crime, others encouraged this wicked viper, and he partly did what he had conspired to do. Guignard had his books written in his own hand, asserting that the parricide against your predecessor, the King, was most justly committed, and confirming a proposition condemned by the Council of Constance. And what have we to fear, when we recall their most wicked and treacherous deeds, which can easily be renewed?

units.la: Si nos, vestram vitam in periculo cernentes, dies nostros, in perpetuo metu transige oportebit, quam tranquillitatem nostris procurabimus? Nonne summa haec impietas f ret, praevidere periculum malumq, ac, ut tam prope ad vos accedat, permittere? Nonne h esset se in profundissimam miseriam praecipitem dare, si quis huius Regni exitio, & ruin superviavere vellet? quae, ut aliquoties vobis demonstravimus, non ulterius, quam vitae v litra longitudine a nobis abest? Deo, propter mutuam inter vos, & sanctum Patrem nostru bene volentiam, sit gloria. Deus vobis, vestrum Diadema; & ipsam sanctam Sedem longi sime conservet; verum si seneus aut valetudo dies ipsius praecideret, ac successor ipsi malo animo, gladium suu spiritualem contra vos stringeret, queadmodum Antecessores ipsius in vestros Reges Franciae & Navarrae, idem fecerunt, quantus quaeso dolor ful ditos vestros occuparet, si tot huius Regni hostes, & contra Majestatem vestram conj ratos, in ipsius vi seribus viderent, quot contra superiorem Regem felicis. memoriae vid runt? cum praecipui Rebellionis auctores & ministri, neq; etiam parricidij in ipsum patri ti insontes, ex proprio ipsius Regno fuerint?
units.tr: If we, seeing your life in danger, must spend our days in constant fear, what tranquillity shall we secure for ourselves? Would this not be the height of impiety, to foresee the danger and the evil, and to allow it to come so near to you? Would it not be to plunge oneself into the deepest misery, if anyone wished to survive the ruin and destruction of this kingdom? As we have shown you several times, that ruin is no further from us than the length of your life. God be praised for the mutual goodwill between you and our holy Father. May God preserve you and your Diadem, and the holy See itself, for a very long time. But if old age or illness should cut short his days, and a successor with ill will should draw his spiritual sword against you, as his predecessors did against your kings of France and Navarre, how great, I ask, would be the grief that seized your subjects, if they saw in his ranks so many enemies of this kingdom, and so many conspirators against your Majesty, as they once saw against the former king of happy memory? Were not the chief authors and ministers of the rebellion, and those not innocent of parricide against that very father, from his own kingdom?

units.la: Scelera sua antea acta non magis, quam reliquorum Ordinum & societatum omnium, q non minus quam ipsi erraverint, illi notari aut exaggerari debere ajunt. Fortasis in pr judicium ipsorum dictum fuerit, quod etiam si in omnibus reliquis Ordinibus, & Societat bus vitia deprehendantur, illa tamen non universa alia fuerint. Societates erant diverse, mnes vero illi, qui earundem uni adhaerebant, se obedientiae Majestati vestrae debitae non ful duxerunt: sed qui de ipsorum sunt Societate, unitissime ac pervicacissime in rebellione fi perstiterunt, ac non solum nullus ipsorum partes vestras est secutus, verum e contrario vterum Regni hostium partibus prae caeteris deditissimi fuere; ac cum tales essent, Odo, un ex ipsorum Societate per sedecim illos conjuratos proprincipe electus fuit. Et si exemplu aliquod externum nostris interi cere fas est, miserandum aliquod ex Historia Lusitaniae r feremus. Cum Rex Hispaniae animum ad Regni Lusitanici usurpatione applicasset, omn Religiosorum Ordines constantes in fidelitate Regi suo debita permansere: soli ipsi, ut De minatione Hispanicam adjuvarent, desertores fuere: ex quo etiam factum est, ut plus qu duo millia ta religiosorum, quam caeterorum Ecclesiasticorum miserrime perierint: ad quo expiandum Bulla absolutionis concessa fuit. Ipsorum doctrina, & anteriora gesta ca fa fuere, ut, cum Castellus adversum vos insurrexisset, Arrestum tam contra ipsum, qua contra omnes ius Societatis participes, per os vestrum proprium damnatos; secutu fit; Quod Arrestum nos, velut felicissimum nostri temporis miraculum, & memoriae conf cravimus; Indicantes tunc, quo si juventutem malitiosa & execranda illa doctrina in imbuere pergerent, nihil securitatis vestra vita habitura esset. Quae etiam causa idoneaji dicata fuit, quod nos formulas quasdam transfiliebamus, quibus adstringebamur ad judicandum cum causae cognitione de instantijs formatis; quae saluti publicae postpon bantur.
units.tr: They say that their past crimes should be noted and magnified no more than those of all the other orders and societies, which have erred no less than they have. It may perhaps be objected against them that, even if faults are found in all the other orders and societies, those faults were not universal among them. The societies were various, but not all who adhered to any one of them thought themselves exempt from the obedience owed to your Majesty. Those of their Society, however, persisted most unitedly and obstinately in rebellion. Not only did none of them follow your side, but on the contrary they were more devoted than all others to the side of the enemies of the kingdom. Since they were such men, Odo, one of their Society, was chosen as prince by the sixteen conspirators. And if it is permitted to bring forward a foreign example alongside our own, we shall cite a pitiable one from the history of Portugal. When the King of Spain had set his mind on usurping the kingdom of Portugal, all the religious orders remained constant in the fidelity owed to their king; only they, in order to help the Spanish domination, became deserters. As a result, more than two thousand of these religious perished, most miserably, more than the other ecclesiastics did; and for the expiation of this a bull of absolution was granted. Their doctrine and their past deeds were the cause that, when Castel rose against you, an arrest was made, condemning him and all sharers in the Society's teaching, by your own mouth. We have treasured this arrest in memory as the most fortunate miracle of our time, recognising at the time that if they continued to imbue youth with that malicious and execrable doctrine, your life would have no security. This was also rightly given as the reason why we passed over certain formulas by which we were bound to judge, with knowledge of the case, the instances that had been formed, which were put after public safety.

units.la: Nulla nos invidia, odio, aut malevolentia, neque generatim neque speciatim cont ipsos laboramus; si laborassemus, Deus nos punivisset, quod nihilominus ipsorum judic esse voluissemus. Nihil nisi atrocitas criminis, & affectus ille, quo Majestatis vestrae con servatione in posterum quoq; prosequimur, ad illud Arrestum incitavit, quod in Parlam ti Rothomagensis, Diviodunensis jurisdictione executioni mandatum fuit, & quide ad vestru d vestrum proprium mandatum, idq; idem etiam in alijs omnibus factum fuisset, nisi illi qui ndum obedientiæ vestræ sese subjecerant, restitissent: quiq; etiam à proposito suo, nisi cum imis magno malæ suæ voluntatis supplicio, recedere poterant.
units.tr: We bear no envy, hatred or ill will against them, either in general or in particular. If we did, God would punish us, since we would nevertheless wish to be their judges. Nothing but the atrocity of the crime, and that affection with which we also pursue the preservation of your Majesty in the future, prompted that arrest, which was put into execution in the Parlement of Rouen and in the jurisdiction of Dijon, and indeed by your own command. The same would have been done in all the others, had not those who had submitted to your obedience resisted; and they could have withdrawn from their purpose only under the threat of great punishment for their wicked will.

units.la: Conqueruntur in scriptis suis, quod tota Societas propter delicta trium aut quatuor on debeat puniri. Verum etsi ad Fratrum Humiliatorum conditionem redacti fuissent, ccasionem conquerendi nullam haberent: cum ob eadem in Cardinalem Borromeum per regiofum unum tantum ex ordine Fratrum Humiliatorum patratam (quod annis abhinc rè triginta accidit) totus Ordo per Pium V. Pontificem juxta resolutionem in convenCardinalium factam, spreta etiam Regis Hispaniæ deprecatione, abolitus fuerit. Nostrum dicium non est tam severum. Si dixerint, Humiliatorum cum suo Ordine, qui longè major fit, nullam esse comparationem: Nos ipsis dicemus, multò minorem esse comparationem cardinalis, cum potentissimo Mundi Rege, qui dignitate Cardinalem longius, quam ipsorum Ordo etiam minimum, superet: Fratres etiam Humiliatos minùs peccâsse, quàm ipsos: Iam eorum unius tantum cædis in Cardinalem patrata author fuit, at ipsi omnes parriciij in vos tentati propter institutionem suam rei sunt.
units.tr: They complain in their writings that the whole Society should not be punished for the crimes of three or four men. But even if they had been reduced to the condition of the Humiliati, they would have no cause for complaint. For the same offence, committed against Cardinal Borromeo by only one man of the Order of the Humiliati (which happened some thirty years ago), led Pope Pius V, in accordance with a resolution made in an assembly of the cardinals, to abolish the whole Order, disregarding even the entreaty of the King of Spain. Our judgment is not so severe. If they say there is no comparison between the Humiliati and their Order, which is far larger, we shall reply that there is much less comparison between a cardinal and the most powerful king in the world, who surpasses a cardinal in dignity far more than their Order surpasses even the smallest. The Humiliati also sinned less than they did: the author of the murder of the cardinal was one man alone, whereas all of them are guilty of parricides attempted against you, on account of their very institution.

units.la: Supplices vos rogamus, ut, quemadmodum gratum habuistis Arrestum justissimè faum, & tum temporis ad deterrendos tam multos, ne contra vos conspirarent, proditores, cessarium: sic etiam illud conservare, & nobis præmonitionem illius periculi, in quo tum amus, cùm nimirùm communi nostro Parenti, cujus vita nobis propria vita charior est, interitum parari videremus, condonare dignemini. Ac certè summum etiam infidelitatis, ingratitudinis vitium existimaremus, si illius perpetuam curam non ageremus: quanoquidem vos nostram vitam, nostram tranquillitatem, & nostra bona nobis reddidistis. Memoria præteritorum cautioni nobis esse debet, ut prosideamus, ne per incuriam in abyssecundi naufragij sepulti maneamus.
units.tr: We beg you as suppliants: just as you found the arrest most justly made to be welcome, and at that time necessary to deter so many traitors from conspiring against you, so may you deign to keep it in force, and to pardon us for giving warning of the danger in which we stand, when we see destruction being prepared for our common Father, whose life is dearer to us than our own. Indeed we would judge it the greatest vice of disloyalty and ingratitude if we did not take perpetual care of his safety, since you have restored to us our life, our tranquillity and our goods. The memory of the past ought to be a warning to us, so that we may take precautions, lest through carelessness we remain buried in the abyss of a second shipwreck.
