For who would believe that, if all the French had been expelled from the kingdom and you had been allowed to bring in Spaniards, you could have dared anything more than to remove the monument of the condemnation and sentence passed upon you? But I would have you persuaded that you have gained nothing by this method. For in place of the one desolated and overturned pyramid, which could be rebuilt only in one place, it has roused several thousand men who proclaim throughout the world and openly profess that you were declared and pronounced, by distinct and lawful judgments, corrupters of French youth, disturbers of public peace and tranquillity, betrayers of the King, and destroyers of your fatherland, and so on.

units.la: Alius etiam in Pyramidis huius destructionem hæc scripsit: At vos ô Socij, quid vasta ruina juvabit? Pyramidis læsæ marmora muta jacent: Marmora muta jacent, sed factà nefaria dum Sol Fulgebit cœlo, fama loquetur anus Vel, si comprimet hanc metus ingens forte periclï, Contemptrix hujus charta loquetur anus.
units.tr: But you, O Companions, what good will vast ruin do? The marbles of the wounded pyramid lie mute. The marbles lie mute, but while the Sun shines in heaven, the old woman Fame will tell of the impious deed. Or, if great fear of danger restrains her, the old woman Paper, scorner of this, will tell of it.

units.la: Exaravit etiam alius Epigramma ad Regem Christianissimum Henricum 4. super restitutione Iesuitarum. Sic autem habet.
units.tr: Another man also wrote an epigram to the Most Christian King Henry IV concerning the restoration of the Jesuits. It runs thus.

units.la: Francorum
units.tr: Of the French

units.la: Epigramma super restitutione Iesuitarum in Gallia.
units.tr: Epigram on the restoration of the Jesuits in France.

units.la: Francorum summas qui nunc moderaris habenas,
units.tr: You who now guide the highest reins of the Franks,

units.la: Juraq; Francigenis summa cum laude ministras
units.tr: And administer the law to the French with the highest praise,

units.la: Inclyte REX, sit pace tua mihi pauca referre
units.tr: Renowned KING, let it be granted to me to say a few words with your leave,

units.la: Concessum, facilisq; animo mea dicta reconde,
units.tr: And kindly store my words in your mind,

units.la: Vera canam, liceat tantum mihi dicere vera.
units.tr: I will sing the truth; let me only be allowed to speak the truth.

units.la: Tertius HENRICVS, cujus nunc sceptra tueris,
units.tr: Third HENRY, whose sceptre you now hold,

units.la: AVGERIVM coluit Patris instar, eiq; salutem
units.tr: Cherished Auger like a father, and trusted him with your safety,

units.la: Credidit, & summo semper dignatus honore est,
units.tr: And always deemed him worthy of the highest honour,

units.la: Ignorans quod CHRISTE tuum qui nomen ubiq;
units.tr: Not knowing that those who everywhere boast of your name, O CHRIST,

units.la: Et vitam iactent, studia in contraria currant;
units.tr: And of their life, run their studies in opposite directions.

units.la: Tantum saepe valet sanctae simulatio vitae.
units.tr: So often does the pretence of a holy life avail.

units.la: Sed postquam sese falsa sub imagine vitii,
units.tr: But after he had perceived himself deceived under the false image of virtue,

units.la: Mendaciq; diu pietatis fallier umbra
units.tr: And long deceived by the shadow of lying piety,

units.la: Sensisset, moresq; tuos IESVITA notâsset,
units.tr: And had noted your manners, JESUIT,

units.la: Tandem poenituit: Quis enim modo crederet illis
units.tr: At last he repented. For who would now believe those

units.la: Qui Christum simulant & latrocinia vivunt,
units.tr: Who feign Christ and live by robbery,

units.la: Queis magis in votis nihil est, quàm nomine SANCTI
units.tr: To whom nothing is more desirable than, in the name of the HOLY

units.la: FOEDERIS, è solijs Dominos depellere avitis,
units.tr: COVENANT, to drive lords from their ancestral thrones,

units.la: Et Reges jugulare pios, populumq; fidelem
units.tr: And to slay pious kings, and to rouse the faithful people

units.la: In proprios animare Duces & ad arma ciere,
units.tr: Against their own leaders and call them to arms,

units.la: Sceptraq; FRANCORVM raptori tradere Ibero,
units.tr: And to hand the sceptres of the FRANKS over to an Iberian robber,

units.la: Cunctaq; terrarum Papae submittere habenis.
units.tr: And to submit all lands to the reins of the Pope?

units.la: Nec satis impune est scelera haec committere, ipso
units.tr: Nor is it enough to commit these crimes with impunity,

units.la: Instinctore Deo fieri, numenq; supernum
units.tr: As if God himself were the instigator, and the heavenly power

units.la: Iratum posse haud alia ratione moveri,
units.tr: Could be moved to anger in no other way,

units.la: Unanimes uno ore canunt, scelerumq; magistros,
units.tr: They sing with one voice, and call the masters of crimes

units.la: Et percussores Regum, caelumq; mereri
units.tr: And murderers of kings deserving of heaven,

units.la: Deberiq; Deo, toties repetunt q; docentq;
units.tr: And owed to God; they repeat this so often and teach it,

units.la: Indigetesq; vocant Regumq; Ducumq; latrones.
units.tr: And call them the deified heroes, and the robbers of kings and leaders.

units.la: Quàm sint vera equidem nosti Rex maxime, nosti,
units.tr: How true these things are, you know, most mighty King, you know,

units.la: Si meminisse voles, neq; longè exempla petenda,
units.tr: If you care to remember; nor need examples be sought from afar.

units.la: Intus habes, nam tu, vel nemo, conscius horum
units.tr: You have them within yourself, for you, or no one, can be witness to these things,

units.la: Esse potes, si vel dentis, vel cætera vitae
units.tr: If you weigh the times of your life, both the early and the rest,

units.la: Tempora perpendas, vix, nec vix tutus in aulâ
units.tr: Scarcely, and scarcely safe, in the court

units.la: Nunc hodie es, licet ipse sacros ampletere PAPAS
units.tr: You are today, though you embrace the holy POPES,

units.la: Et veluti primus dicaris filius esse.
units.tr: And are called as if the first son.

units.la: Praeteriti memor esto, animoq; futura revolve
units.tr: Be mindful of the past, and turn over the future in your mind,

units.la: Si potes, & tibi sit Rex Lusitanicus, & tu
units.tr: If you can, and let the King of Portugal be a perpetual example to you.

units.la: Perpetuo exemplo: Quis enim majore adamavit
units.tr: For who has loved this breed with greater zeal,

units.la: Progeniem hanc zelo, similiq; affecit honore?
units.tr: And regarded it with a similar honour?

units.la: Quâ mercede? jacet Regno spoliatus avito,
units.tr: And for what reward? He lies stripped of his ancestral kingdom,

units.la: Et procul à Patria peregrinis caesus in oris,
units.tr: And slain far from his fatherland on foreign shores,

units.la: Consilio Iesuita tuo delusus & arte:
units.tr: Deluded by your Jesuit counsel and craft.

units.la: Hoc meruit probitate suâ, eximioq; favore,
units.tr: He earned this by his integrity and that singular favour

units.la: Quo te dira lues, quo te furialis Erinnys
units.tr: With which the dire pestilence, with which the furious Erinys,

units.la: Plus justo affecit; sed quemnam servit in usum
units.tr: Has afflicted you more than was just. But to what use is it

units.la: Haec dixisse tibi toties, eademq; referre,
units.tr: To have said these things to you so often and to repeat the same,

units.la: Si mens certa manet, saevas revocare locustas,
units.tr: If your mind remains fixed, to recall the savage locusts,

units.la: Harpyiasq; animarum antiquas reddere sedes
units.tr: And restore the Harpies of souls to their ancient seats,

units.la: Et denuò innumeris Regnum objectare periclis?
units.tr: And again expose the kingdom to countless perils?

units.la: Quid juvat ad surdas facere irrita verba procellas,
units.tr: What good is it to speak empty words to deaf storms?

units.la: DE PROPAGATIONE
units.tr: On the Propagation

units.la: Et frustrà infandum toties iterare dolorem? Sæpè adimit mentem summi Regnator Olympi Principibus, meritis statuit cum plectere pœnis Et Regem Populumq; suum non æqua ferentes.
units.tr: And why do I vainly repeat so often this unspeakable grief? The Ruler of high Olympus often takes away the wits of princes, when He resolves to punish them with deserved penalties, those who do not bear with an even mind both their King and their people.

units.la: Si te forte putas hinc terq; quaterq; beatum, Induperatorem quia te Iesuita salutat, Quodq; tuas vires latéq; patentia sceptra Prædicet, atq; tuas in laudes ora resolvat; Falleris ô Princeps scelerati fraude COTONIS, Cantando pariter teq; & tua perdere Regna Iam dudum ille parat, nec enim nova crimina tentat Antiquus scelerum strustor, Magiaq; sacerdos.
units.tr: If perhaps you think yourself thrice and four times blessed, because the Jesuit greets you as Emperor, and proclaims your power and your far-reaching sceptre, and opens his mouth in praise of you, you are deceived, O Prince, by the fraud of Coton. That ancient plotter of crimes and priest of magic has long been preparing, while singing your praises, to destroy you and your kingdom alike; nor does he attempt new crimes.

units.la: Nonne vides nil posse prius neque sanctius esse Mancipijs Papæ, stygij quàm jussa Parentis: Fraude dolog; pari ad decretum ducere finem? Respice quid statuant, te solo nomine Regem, Et titulo tenus, at proprio nil jure posse A Patre latronum nisi sit concessa potestas, Quem penes arbitrium faciunt Regniq; tuiq;.
units.tr: Do you not see that nothing can be more holy for the slaves of the Pope than the commands of the infernal Father, to bring the matter to an end by equal fraud and guile? Consider what they decree: that you are King in name only and merely by title, and that you can have no real right without the Father of thieves, unless power is granted to you, in whose hands they place the judgment of your kingdom and of you.

units.la: Sic te, quem Regem & Dominum Rex maximus unxit, Hac lege agnoscunt, Papæ si jussa ministres, Quo sine nulla tuis reverentia debita sceptris, Qui (modò sic libeat) peregrino tradere Regna Vestra potest, Dominoq; alij committere habenda.
units.tr: Thus they acknowledge you, whom the greatest King anointed as King and Lord, on this condition: that you serve the commands of the Pope. Without this, no due reverence is owed to your sceptre. Whoever (provided it so pleases him) can hand over your kingdom to a foreigner, and entrust it to another lord to hold.

units.la: I nunc, rursum illas recipe in tua regna Cicadas, Materiamq; novam Vertumnus trade nocendi; Sanguinis effusum haud satis est, si forte furores Et rabiem illorum validis compescere frenis Fixum animo teneas, specie laetaris inani, Nequicquam q; tui prætendis commoda regni, Nil prodesse queunt Regalia sceptra, tuorumq; Auxilia Heroum fortesq; in prælia dextræ: Obstrictti remanent specialis nomine voti, Quod violare nefas vel cum discrimine vitæ Iusjurandum ipsum, si voto forte repugnat; Servandum esse negant; Quid enim magis esse profanum, Aut magè turpe potest, quàm sacris ludere pactis Vinclaq; divini violare sacerrima juris? Tantáne & Impietas à tanto Rege ferenda est?
units.tr: Go now, and receive back into your realm those cicadas, and give new material for harm to Vertumnus. Shedding blood is not enough, if perhaps you hold fixed in your mind to curb their fury and madness with strong bridles, and you rejoice in an empty show, and you vainly put forward the advantages of your kingdom. Royal sceptres cannot avail, nor the help of your heroes and brave right hands in battle. They remain bound by the special name of a vow, which they deny must be kept, since it is a crime to violate even an oath itself, even at the risk of life, if perhaps it conflicts with the vow. For what can be more profane, or more shameful, than to trifle with sacred pacts and to violate the most sacred bonds of divine right? Must such impiety be borne from so great a King?

units.la: Scrutare ipse, licet (nec enim nisi justa requiro) Quid Iesuita paret, penitusq; introspice, & omnes Doctrinæ partes vitaq; evolvere recessus; Aspicies, nitidâ veluti depicta tabellâ, Inclyta gesta Patrum, (qui falso nomen Iesu) Præfigunt fronti, titulisq; illustribus ornant; Quo mage dira cohors, imageq; scelerata propago, Occultis studijs, & multâ callida fraude, Præluceré alijs, vulgoq; imponere possit) Et quæ præterea non nullis cognita sædis Occurrent Rex magne tibi, & mea dicta probabunt.
units.tr: Search it out yourself, if you will (for I ask only what is just), what the Jesuit is preparing, and look deep within, and unroll all the parts of his teaching and the recesses of his life. You will see, as if painted on a bright tablet, the famous deeds of the Fathers (who falsely bear the name of Jesus), which they set before their brow and adorn with illustrious titles, so that the dreadful cohort and the wicked offspring of that image may, by hidden studies and much cunning fraud, be able to shine before others and impose upon the common people. And what else, known to some, is shameful, will meet you, great King, and will prove my words.

units.la: Nullum unquam in terris magis execrabile monstrum
units.tr: Never before on earth has there arisen a more execrable monster.

units.la: Exstitit, ô superi! non peste saevior ullaChristiadum terras corrupit & infestavit.
units.tr: O gods above, no plague more savage than this has corrupted and infested the lands of the Christians.

units.la: Non scelus admissum est Iesuitis inde remotis. Singula quid referam? nil non damnabile praestant,
units.tr: No crime has been committed that the Jesuits have not been involved in. Why should I recount each one? They perform nothing that is not damnable.

units.la: Immunes operum, contemtoresque sacrorum, Impuri, immites, scelerati, & dira luporum
units.tr: Free from works, scorners of sacred things, impure, merciless, wicked, and the dreadful

units.la: Semina, celantes agni sub vellere virusEt Stygijs genitore fati qui praesidet umbris.
units.tr: seeds of wolves, concealing their poison under a lamb's fleece, and such as are ruled by the father of fate in the Stygian shades.

units.la: Certior est aliunde fides: propria inspice tantumScripta Patrum, arbitrio stabit sententia vestro,
units.tr: Trust is more certain from elsewhere: look only at the writings of the Fathers themselves; the verdict will stand by your own judgment.

units.la: Ipsa licet volvas sinuosa volumina magniRichonij, solus Iesuitarum esse Patronus
units.tr: Even if you unroll the winding volumes of the great Richeome, you will find him the sole patron of the Jesuits.

units.la: Qui modo sustinuit multis e millibus unus, Atque illi comitem adjungas sociumque COTONEM,
units.tr: He alone, of many thousands, has lately held up this cause, and if you join to him as companion and partner Coton,

units.la: Omnia cognoscens, proprijsque docebere libris.
units.tr: you will be taught, knowing all things, from their own books.

units.la: Insuper ah faciet miseranda Ecclesia cunctisGallica nostra fidem, quo nunc sub pondere vasto
units.tr: Moreover, our Gallican Church, wretched in every way, will bring faith to nothing, now that it can barely draw breath under that vast weight.

units.la: Vix animam trahit immuneris oppressa statutis, Servitiumque tuosque Esavita exosa furores,
units.tr: Oppressed by harsh decrees, it hardly draws breath, and it hates the slavery and the furies of the Esauite (Jesuit) tyrants.

units.la: Antiquae deflet proh Libertatis honorem.
units.tr: Alas, it mourns the honour of ancient Liberty.

units.la: Aurea Libertas sic, sic calcabere, sicneIlla tibi frenum injiciet Iesuitica pestis?
units.tr: Will golden Liberty thus, thus be trampled? Will that Jesuit plague put a bridle upon you?

units.la: Ultima fax hominum Sathanaeq; excrementum, Quo nil terra tulit peius nec faedius unquam.
units.tr: Ultimate torch of men and excrement of Satan, than which the earth has never produced anything worse or more foul.

units.la: Ergone Libertas, quam tu LVDOICE tuorumVirtute, & proprio peperisti sanguine nobis
units.tr: Is Liberty, which you, Louis, won for us by the valour of your ancestors and by your own blood, now to be given up for seizure?

units.la: Eripienda data est? Ergo hac tibi lege relictum estAProavis tritaqueq; tuis BORBONICA proles
units.tr: Is it thus, by this law, that the Bourbon offspring is left to you, worn by your ancestors,

units.la: Francorum Imperium, tandem circumspice, tandem
units.tr: O Empire of the French? At last look around, at last

units.la: Erige te, rursumq; antiqua imitare tuorumGesta Patrum, priscosq; atavorum respice honores.
units.tr: raise yourself up, and imitate again the deeds of your ancestors, and look upon the honours of your forefathers of old.

units.la: Cessatum satis est, sanam semel arripe mentem, Atque animo perpende tuo, tecumq; revolve,
units.tr: There has been enough delay. Seize at last a sound mind, weigh it in your own spirit, and turn it over with yourself,

units.la: Officium praestare pium, civemq; vocari, Qui, quantum in se est, pro Libertate tuenda
units.tr: to render the dutiful service and be called a citizen, who, as far as in him lies, for the defence of Liberty,

units.la: Prospicit imperio, & Regi sua jura reservatIntegra, quiq; cavet ne quid Respublica damni
units.tr: looks out for the empire, and keeps the King's rights whole, and takes care that the commonwealth suffers no loss,

units.la: Accipiat, priscoque suo videtur honore.
units.tr: and seems to keep its ancient honour.

units.la: Contra etiam vestrum esse puta curare subinde, Ne quid forte novi perturbet publica rerum
units.tr: Consider it also your task, on the contrary, to take care from time to time that no novelty disturbs public affairs,

units.la: Commodaq; civilesq; ciat mala factio motus, Sic poteris Rex esse diu, populoq; praeesse,
units.tr: and that a seditious faction does not stir up troubles hostile to the public good and to civil peace. So you will be able to be King for long and to rule the people

units.la: Quem divina tibi commisit cura regendum.
units.tr: which divine care has entrusted to you to govern.

units.la: Ergo si quis amor, sive quae cura fatigetImperij, Populiq; tui, propriaeq; salutis,
units.tr: Therefore, if any love, or any care, troubles you for the empire, your people, and your own safety,

units.la: Ne temere admittas inferno Acheronte remensamProgeniem, denuoq; caput, Regnumq; tuosq;
units.tr: do not rashly admit to the Acheron of hell a progeny that has returned, and again the head, and your kingdom and yourself

units.la: Objice mille malis, quibus haud virtute resisti,Nec telis armisve potest, sat viximus ehen
units.tr: expose to a thousand evils, which cannot be resisted by virtue, nor by weapons or arms. Alas, we have lived long enough,

units.la: Pestiferis agitati odijs: scelerumq; referti,Tu opus est aliunde novis accersere terris
units.tr: harassed by pestilent hatreds, and filled with crimes. You must summon new lands from elsewhere.

units.la: DE PROPAGATIONE
units.tr: On the Propagation

units.la: Fœdifragos, tenerœ deceptoresq; juventa: Sat natura mali per se corrupta ministrat.
units.tr: Breakers of faith and deceivers of tender youth: nature, already corrupt of itself, supplies evil enough.

units.la: Cuinam hominum ignotum est Iesuitas nocte die’ Nil meditari aliud, quam qua ratione modo ve Prisca statuta queant, patrias’q; evertere leges, In’q; locum, antiquis totum in contraria, nobis Iura dare, & sanctos privata ad commoda ritus Flectere, nulli unquam quod post mutare licebit, Ut te dein placitis cogant subscribere, teq; Pro libitu ad nutum ducant, decretaq; condant Duratura magis quam quae sculpuntur in aere, Aut quae Dalmatico fulgent incisa metallo.
units.tr: Who among men does not know that the Jesuits, night and day, think of nothing but by what method they might overturn the ancient statutes and the laws of the fatherland; that they aim to set up laws for us in place of the old ones, wholly contrary to them, and to bend holy rites to private advantage, so that nothing once done may ever be changed afterwards; that they mean to compel you to subscribe to their decrees, to lead you about at their nod and at their pleasure, and to establish decrees that will last longer than what is carved in bronze or what gleams engraved on Dalmatian metal?

units.la: Det Deus Omnipotens, penes est quem summa potestas, Inclyte Rex, ne tu deceptus fraude COTONIS Melliti alloquio capiare; aquamq; remittas Iram, animumq; tuum, justas qui exarsit in iras, Et poenas merito scelerata a gente poposcit; Sufficiat lacrymasse tuos, poenasq; dedisse Francigenas toties, metuo ne deniq; nobis Plura ferenda manent mala quam quae sensim ut oli n, Auctores scelerum denuo si in viscera Regni Admittas, facilisq; illorum audire querelas, Ut fert fama, paras, prisco’ in honore locare.
units.tr: May Almighty God, in whose hands lies supreme power, keep you, illustrious King, from being deceived by the fraud of Cotton and from being taken in by the honeyed address of Cotton's kind. May you lay aside the anger that flared up in just wrath and rightly demanded punishment from that wicked people. Let it suffice that you have wept and that the French have so often been punished. I fear that more evils remain for us to bear than those we once endured, if you again admit the authors of crimes into the very heart of the kingdom, and, as rumour has it, are preparing to readily hear their complaints and restore them to their former honour.

units.la: Parce tibi, nobisq; simul, communia uti os’q; Fata manent, prohibe instantem subitamq; ruinam A Regnis populisq; tuis, nam te sine Ranus Permissum nihil; At crimen fautore levatur. Quid juvat a vitijs Regnum purgasse, suaq; E ditione omnes scelerats inde potenti Ejecisse manu, propria si deniq; culpa Restaurentur, & in multo majore habeantur Respectu? e quibus heu lateri constanter adhæret Alter, ita ex cultus magicis virtutibus: ut se Scire canat quae vos semper fortuna manebit, Sic mentem atque oculos objectis fascinat umbris, Viribus inferni pollens & fraude parentis. Alter ita est fidens tantumq; pudore remotus, Defunctum ut Regem, Serpente nocentior omni, Non dubitet scriptis proscindere, & interea illi Hoc impune licet, nullo prohibente furores. Quo tandem erumpet monstrosa licentia? Reges Sic ne licet lacerare sacros, odijs’q; agitare?
units.tr: Spare yourself and us together; our fates are shared, and the imminent and sudden ruin of your realms and peoples must be prevented. Without you, Ranus permits nothing, yet the crime is lightened by a patron. What good is it to have purged the kingdom of vices, and to have driven every wicked man out of your dominion with a strong hand, if through their own fault they are restored and held in much greater regard? Of these, alas, one constantly clings to your side. By the magic powers of his rites he sings that he knows what fortune will always await you, and so he bewitches mind and eyes with empty shadows, mighty in the powers of hell and in the fraud of his father. Another is so bold and so far removed from shame that, more harmful than any serpent, he does not hesitate to tear the dead king to pieces in his writings, and meanwhile he is allowed to do so with impunity, no one restraining his frenzies. To what end will this monstrous licence break out? Is it lawful to mangle sacred kings in this way and to harass them with hatred?

units.la: Iam, jam tempus erit Regum Rex maxime, mentem Dirigere hue populumq; tuum Regnumq; tueri: Quo res nostra loco, quae sit fortuna videmus; Vester honos agitur, Mundi pulcerrima tellus Opprobrijs vexata jacet, reliquisq; pudori Gentibus est, miserere tui, miserere tuorum; Iura patrum, ritusq; sacros, leges’q; atavorum Restitue, afflictae sua da medicamina genti, Non indigna peto, propriam quoque respice famam, Et nomen Regale tuum, titulosque decoros. Ne tua, Roma salax, manibus post terga revinctis. Colla premat, prisco{q;} tuo te fraudet honore.
units.tr: Now, now the time will come, greatest of kings, to direct your mind to this matter and to protect your people and your kingdom. We see where our affair stands and what its fortune is. Your honour is at stake. The most beautiful land in the world lies battered by reproaches and is left to the shame of other nations. Have pity on yourself, have pity on your own. Restore the laws of the fathers, the sacred rites and the laws of our ancestors; give remedies to the afflicted nation. I ask for nothing unworthy. Look also to your own reputation, your royal name and your fair titles, lest Rome, lascivious, with your hands bound behind your back, press upon your neck and cheat you of your ancient honour.

units.la: Perpetuum Imperium, longaevos Nestoris annos, Deniq; caelestem requiem tibi quisq; precatur, Inclyte Rex, & ne videar mutescere solus, Haec eadem tibi vota fero, & quia dicere coram Non mihi concessum est, fungatur epistola nostra Officio, & tutum teneant mea carbasa portum. Praeterea haec nostris accedunt vota tabellis, Finibus ut Patriae Iesuitas pellere Christi Nomine digneris, regnisq; avertere pestem, Quam vestro, & populi capiti impendere videmus. Haud incerta queror, nec quae ventosa per orbem Ventilat, indignis pascens rumoribus aures, Fama, tibi obtrudo, sed cunctis obvia, quae non Immerito iniiciant Regi populoq; pudorem.
units.tr: Perpetual empire, the years of Nestor, and at last heavenly rest: everyone prays these things for you, illustrious King. And lest I seem to be the only one to keep silent, I offer these same vows to you. Since it is not granted me to speak to you in person, let this letter perform its office, and may my sails find a safe harbour. Besides, these prayers are added to my tablets: that you may deign, in the name of Christ, to drive the Jesuits from the borders of the fatherland, and to turn away from your kingdoms the plague which we see hanging over your head and the head of your people. I complain of nothing uncertain, nor do I press upon you the rumour that blows about the world, feeding ears with unworthy gossip; rather, these are things that lie open to all, and that cannot fail to bring shame upon king and people.

units.la: Non latet hoc quemquam, quantum Iesuitica turba Afferat imperiis tandem populisq; malorum, Quo semel illa pedem fixit, torrentis ad instar Cuncta rapit, viduasq; opibus, domibusq; potentes Exuit, & fama, & titulis defraudat avitis. Nec satis hoc, Regna evertit, penitusq; superbis Deiicit e solijs Reges, quis talia demens Ulterius perferre queat? si exempla petantur, Scilicet haud opus est peregrinos volvere fastos, Scriptasq; maiorum impigre scrutarier; ipsa Tempora nostra dabunt quae nos meminisse pudebit; Si pudor ullus inest, quid enim vel ante malorum Perpessi fumus? ah! quos non fecdata vimus amnes Sanguine? & infestos miserè satiavimus hostes?
units.tr: It is not hidden from anyone how much evil the Jesuit crowd brings to empires and peoples. Once it has planted its foot somewhere, it seizes everything like a torrent, strips the powerful of their wealth and houses, leaves them widowed, and defrauds them of reputation and hereditary titles. Nor is this enough: it overthrows kingdoms and casts kings down from their proud thrones. Who, being mad, could endure such things any longer? If examples are sought, there is surely no need to unroll foreign annals or diligently search the written records of our forefathers; our own times will supply things that we shall be ashamed to remember. If any shame is left in us, for what have we not suffered before now? Ah! What rivers have we not seen defiled with blood, and what hostile enemies have we not wretchedly glutted?

units.la: Impius interea grassatur Barbarus, & nos Turca ferox ridet, miseranda Ecclesia justas Vix lacrymas cohibere poterit, heu ubi prisca Religio, sanctiq; Patres, atq; inclyta Regum Gloria? quo tandem miseri pervenimus! ah quae! Quae non pertulimus! quae non ventura timemus!
units.tr: Meanwhile the impious barbarian rages, and fierce Turk laughs at us, and the pitiable Church can scarcely hold back her just tears. Alas, where is the ancient religion, the holy Fathers, and the illustrious glory of kings? To what wretched state have we come! Ah, what have we not suffered! What do we not fear is yet to come!

units.la: Serius hoc vidit, vidit tamen ultimus HEROS VALLESIAE stirpis, qui quamvis se esse putaret Delitias Papae, primaq; in amore tenere, Nil minus interijt sica intereremus iniqua.
units.tr: He saw this too late, yet the last hero of the Valois line saw it. Although he thought himself the darling of the Pope and held first place in his affection, he nonetheless perished by a wicked blade, no less than we too might have perished by an unjust dagger.

units.la: Qui semel evasit scopulos, scyllamq; voracem, Neptuno monstrante viam ventisq; secundis: Naufragus immerito fluctus incusat & imbres Immitesq; Deos Pelagi, saevamq; Charybdim, Neglecto custode Deo, si incauta carina Obruitur, tandem & sterili sepelitur arena.
units.tr: He who has once escaped the rocks and the voracious Scylla, with Neptune showing the way and the winds in his favour, is shipwrecked and wrongly blames the waves, the rains, the cruel gods of the sea and savage Charybdis. He has neglected God as his guardian, and if his unwary keel is overwhelmed, he is at last buried in barren sand.

units.la: Stabat Roma potens, & adhuc cum laude superbis Ius dabat imperiis, cum prudentissimus Heros Occasum interitumq; CATO praediceret, heu! Det Deus o Princeps similis quandoq; ruina
units.tr: Rome stood powerful, and still with praise gave law to her proud empires, when the most prudent hero Cato foretold her decline and ruin. Alas! May God grant, O Prince, that some similar ruin

units.la: DE PROPAGATIONE
units.tr: On the Propagation

units.la: Ne subeunda siet Regi, miseroque popello Insidijsque dolisque & iniqui fraude COTONIS. Hic sermo mellitus, & haec dulcissima verba, Ille quibus vestras, Rex maxime, detinet aures. Incantator atrox, magico sunt plena veneno, Permittente Deo, qui quando imponere finem Imperijs statuit, meritasque exposcere pœnas, Iudicio sensuque omni regesque Ducesque Exuit, & tandem populum cum Rege relinquit.
units.tr: Lest the King should be exposed to these things, and the wretched people to the snares and tricks and unjust deceit of Coton. This is the honeyed speech and these the sweetest words by which he holds your ears, greatest King. He is a cruel enchanter, full of magic poison; God permitting, when He resolves to set an end to empires and to demand deserved punishments, He strips kings and leaders of judgement and every sense, and at last leaves the people behind with the King.

units.la: Iesuitæ autem immemores tanti beneficij Regis, & conditionum quibus rursus in Gallia admissi ac recepti fuerunt, post transactionem Henrici IV. Regis cum Duce Bulioneo anno 1606. factam, cum Rex Lutetiam redijsset, suplici libello eum exceperunt, post gratulationem de successu, quo prospero in hac expeditione usus esset, & simul Scholam ut sibi Sedanī aperire liceret petierunt. Rex autem respondit, se quidem assensum suum daturum facile, modo id a Duce obtinere possint: conatu igitur irrito discesserunt.
units.tr: The Jesuits, however, forgetful of so great a kindness from the King, and of the conditions on which they were again admitted and received in France, after the agreement made in 1606 between King Henry IV and the Duke of Bouillon, when the King had returned to Paris, presented him with a petition. After congratulating him on the success he had enjoyed in this campaign, they also asked that they might be allowed to open a school for themselves at Sedan. The King replied that he would readily give his assent, provided they could obtain it from the Duke. They therefore withdrew, their effort having come to nothing.

units.la: Iesuitæ etiam ex Societate sua miserunt aliquem Aurelias Quadragesimali tempore, ut ibi concionaretur, confessiones audiret & Missam celebraret, se factum hoc magna cum civium indignatione. Nam neglecto hoc suo officio in id solum totus incubuit, ut superioris temporis Ligistas in suas partes pertrahere posset. Hoc cum ex animi sui sententia successisset, rumorem ipse & adhærentes in urbe sparserunt, Regem omnino velle atque iubere ut Iesuitæ in urbem recipiantur. Regi contra persuaserunt, Aureliānēnses nihil magis cupere & exoptare, quam ut Iesuitæ in urbem introinittantur. Rex annuit illis benigne, & concessit ut Collegium in hac urbe extruant, modo id cum licentia Senatus consensu civium fiat. Hoc vero quum primum cives resciverunt, in unum convenerunt, ibique Tourvilleus Advocatus urbis, multis gravibusque argumentis in medium adductis, probavit, non sine ingenti damno & periculo Iesuitas, irrequietum, superbum & arrogans hominum genus, in urbem recipi posse. Placuit hoc consilium præcipuis Senatoribus & civibus, decreveruntque unanimiter, non recipiendos esse.
units.tr: The Jesuits also sent one of their Society to Orléans during Lent, so that he might preach there, hear confessions and celebrate Mass. This was done with great indignation among the citizens. For, neglecting this duty, he devoted himself wholly to one end: to draw the former Leaguers over to their side. When this had succeeded according to his own wish, he and his adherents spread a rumour in the city that the King wholly wished and commanded that the Jesuits be received into the city. They also persuaded the King that the people of Orléans desired and longed for nothing more than that the Jesuits be admitted into the city. The King graciously assented to them and allowed them to build a college in this city, provided this was done with the permission of the Senate and the consent of the citizens. As soon as the citizens learned of this, they gathered together, and there Tourville, the advocate of the city, set out many weighty arguments and proved that the Jesuits, a restless, proud and arrogant breed of men, could not be received into the city without great loss and danger. This plan pleased the leading senators and citizens, and they unanimously resolved that they were not to be received.

units.la: Hæc breviter de aureliensibus: de Trecensibus, in gratiam Germanorum & Helvetiorum meorum, ut est ex Gallica in Germanicam linguam translatum, bona fide integrum adscribam.
units.tr: These things concerning the people of Orléans are briefly set out. Concerning Troyes, for the sake of my Germans and Swiss, I shall faithfully and in full copy out what has been translated from French into German.

units.la: Warhafftiger bericht/ was sich inn der Statt Troyen in Franckreich / bey dero von den Jesuiten daselbst gesúchter einkommung/ vom jahr 1603. biß auff den Monat Julium 1611. zu getragen.
units.tr: A True Report of What Took Place in the Town of Troyes in France, During the Attempted Readmission of the Jesuits There, from the Year 1603 until July 1611.

units.la: Ach dem die Jesuiten / krafft deß zu Pariß im September Anno 1603. außgangenen Edicts/ wider in Franckreich einkommen: haben sie sich/ durch ihr geschwinde Räncke/ deren sie / ihr furnemmen ins werck zu richten / sich zugebrauchen pflegen/ inn die vornembste Stätte deß Königreichs einzuschleichen / vnderstanden. Man hat gewisse nachrichtung/ daß die Obersten in ihrer Societet einmütig beschlossen gehabt/ im Collegio zu Pariß nicht hart auff die schulaltung zu dringen/ damit sie desto leichtlicher in allen Provintzen vnd vornemmen Stätten in Franckreich einen freyen eingang hetten.
units.tr: After the Jesuits, by virtue of the edict issued at Paris in September 1603, had returned to France, they set about, by their usual swift tricks, to slip into the most important towns of the kingdom. Reliable information has it that the superiors of their Society had unanimously resolved not to press hard for the teaching arrangements at the College in Paris, so that they could more easily gain free entry into all the provinces and leading towns of France.

units.la: Hierzu zu gelangen/ vnd damit der König ihr fürhaben desto weniger mercken solte/ habe a sie Ihr Mayt. durch etliche ihrer vertrawten zu verstehen gegeben / daß weil ihre Mayestet gleichfalls aller Vatter inn diesem grossen Königreich were/ dieselbe ebener massen/ wie sie ihren Vndertha nen den Frieden zu wegen gebracht/ auch die lehr vnd vnderweisung ihnen ins gemein widerertatten wolte/ vnd das sichs nicht gebürte/ daß die Statt Pariß allein / einer so lieblichen vnd angenehmen Frucht genießen solte : dardurch wurde Ihre Mayestet bey den Vndertha nen desto mehr gehrt vnd geliebt werden. Auff diß scheinbarlich anbringen / hat der König ihnen erlaubt/ sich allenthalben in Franckreich/ da es ihnen anstehen wurde/ niederzulassen.
units.tr: To achieve this, and so that the King would notice their purpose less, they gave His Majesty to understand, through some of their trusted associates, that since His Majesty was likewise the father of all in this great kingdom, he should, just as he had brought peace to his subjects, also restore instruction and teaching to them generally. It was not fitting, they said, that the city of Paris alone should enjoy so lovely and pleasant a fruit; by this means His Majesty would be all the more honoured and loved by his subjects. On the strength of this plausible proposal, the King permitted them to settle wherever in France it suited them.

units.la: In der Provintzen Champagnien haben sie auß ursachen / die hernach sollen gemeldet werden / ihre augen vnd gemüth sonderlich auff die Statt Troyen gerichtet. Zum anfang ist es ihnen zimlich gelungen / dieweil sie drey vornemme Personen/die ihnen vber die maß gewogen vnd zugethan waren/ angetroffen haben/ nemlich den Herren Bischoff/ den Præsidenten vnd General Leutenant/ vnd den Schultessen in der Statt / welche auß vnderschiedlichen vnd sonderbaren vrsachen / die hernach in diesem bericht erklärt werden sollen/ ihr eusserstes gethan haben/ die Jesuiten in der Statt Troyen zu installiren. M. Iacob Nivelle, der fast zwantzig Jar lang / ein Jesuit von gelübd vnd profession gewesen/ vnd noch einer im herzen vnd gemüth ist/ hat auch nicht wenig darzu geholffen.
units.tr: In the province of Champagne they have, for reasons that will be set out later, directed their eyes and minds especially to the town of Troyes. At first they had considerable success, for they found three prominent persons who were exceedingly well disposed and attached to them: namely the Lord Bishop, the President and Lieutenant-General, and the bailiff of the town. For various particular reasons, which will be explained later in this report, these men did their utmost to install the Jesuits in the town of Troyes. Master Jacob Nivelle, who had been a Jesuit by vow and profession for nearly twenty years, and who is still one at heart and in mind, also helped them not a little.

units.la: Als die Jesuiten vmb bekräfftigung ihrer widereinkommung zu Troyen anhielten / ist der Herr Johann Dautruy Schultes daselbst/ welcher etlicher gemeinen geschäfften halben gen Pariß kommen war/ in eine Herberg/ da Herr Vestier, Dechant der Thumkirche / vnnd einer seiner Brüder/ der Statt Rath/ auch lagen/ eingekehrt. Auff einen Feyertag fragt er sie/ ob sie wolten den König sehen zu mittag essen: welches sie verwilligt/ vnnd sich mit ihm dahin verfügt haben / wußten aber nicht/ was er vorhatte/ vnd machten ihnen keine gedancken/ daß er sie verörtheilen/ vnnd ihrer gegenwart zur verrichtung dessen/ darvon hernach/ mißbrauchen wolte.
units.tr: When the Jesuits sought confirmation of their return to Troyes, the Lord Johann Dautruy, bailiff there, who had come to Paris on some public business, lodged at an inn where Lord Vestier, dean of the cathedral, and one of his brothers, a member of the town council, were also staying. On a feast day he asked them whether they would like to see the King and dine with him. They agreed and went there with him, but they did not know what he intended, and had no suspicion that he meant to condemn them, or to misuse their presence for a purpose that would become clear later.

units.la: Dautruy gehet in deß Königs Kammer hinein/ vnd redet heimlich mit einem seines anhangs/ Mr. René Breslé genandt/ welcher der Kön. May. Almosenpfleger/ vnd zu einem Bischoff gen Troyen fürgeschlagen war.
units.tr: Dautruy went into the King's chamber and spoke secretly with one of his supporters, called Master René Breslé, who was the King's almoner and had been proposed to be bishop of Troyes.

units.la: Wie nun der König nach eingenommener Mahlzeit sich wider in sein Gemach verfügen wolte / vnnd die Königin bey der hand führte / hat jhm Dautruy an dem Ort / da er furuber gehen solte / einen fußfall gethan / welches der Herr Vestier vnnd sein Bruder ebener massen auch gethan / dieweil sie meinten / daß Dautruy, welcher Schultes war / etwas / daß die gemeine Statt angieng / dem König fürzubringen hette. Da thet Bresle das wort / vnnd sprach zum König: Es seynd / Herr König / der Schultes vnd die Einwohner der Statt Troyen / die Ewer May. vnderthenigist ersuchen / daß sie ein Jesuiter Collegium bey jhnen haben mögen. Der König gab dem Bresle kein antwort / sonder sagte stracks zur Königin / Diser ist meiner Almosen pfleger einer / vnd ist allein zu Bischoff gen Troyen fürgeschlagen worden / gleichwol wil er schon albereit die Jesuiten daselbst einführen. Der Herr Dechant / Vestier, vnd sein Bruder / kundten sich nicht gnügsam über der behenden antwort deß Königs verwundern: gleichwol kame jhnen deß Schultessen kühne that vnd fürnemen noch viel seltsamer vor / daß er also für sich selbst / auß eignem trieb / vnnd ohne vorwissen der anderen Stände in der Statt / umb die Jesuiten anhalten dorffte. Vnd that jhnen sonderlich wehe / daß sie ins Königliche Schloß vnder dem schein / als solten sie den König sehen essen / in der that aber / damit ein so betrieglicher bitt durch jhre gegenwart desto mehr krafft vnd ansehens hette / waren geführt worden. Darüber sie in eine verbitterung wider den Dautruy geraten / vnd jhme seine vntrew vnd gewalt / den er zur zeit der Liga wider seine Mitburger geübt / verwiesen haben. Der Bresle, welcher damit umbgieng / daß er jhm die Jesuiten verpflichtete / vnnd durch jhre fürbitt seine Bullen beym Bapst umb sonst bekommen möchte / hat diese sach beym König zutreiben auff sich genommen / vnd dermassen angehalten / daß nach dem er Ihre May. vberedt / als solte die Bitt / die Dautruy der Jesuiten halben gethan hatte / mit bewilligung aller Einwohner geschehen seyn / er ein schreiben dato deß Februarij 1604. deß innhalts / wie hernach folgt / erlangt hat.
units.tr: When the King, after the meal, was about to withdraw to his chamber and was leading the Queen by the hand, Dautruy knelt before him at the place where he was to pass. Vestier and his brother likewise knelt, since they supposed that Dautruy, being bailiff, had some matter concerning the town as a whole to put before the King. Then Bresle took up the word and said to the King: "Sire, it is the bailiff and the inhabitants of the town of Troyes who humbly beg Your Majesty that they may have a Jesuit college among them." The King gave Bresle no answer, but at once said to the Queen: "This man is one of my almoners, and has been proposed as bishop of Troyes only; nevertheless he is already seeking to introduce the Jesuits there." The Lord Dean Vestier and his brother could not sufficiently marvel at the King's quick reply. Yet the bailiff's bold conduct and purpose seemed even stranger to them, that he should thus, on his own initiative and without the knowledge of the other estates of the town, dare to request the Jesuits. What especially grieved them was that they had been brought into the royal palace under the pretence of seeing the King dine, but in fact so that the presence of such men would give greater force and authority to a deceitful petition. Angered at this, they turned in bitterness against Dautruy and reproached him for his faithlessness and for the violence he had practised against his fellow citizens in the time of the League. Bresle, who intended to bind the Jesuits to himself and, through their intercession, to obtain his bulls from the Pope without cost, undertook to press this matter with the King, and pursued it so vigorously that, having persuaded His Majesty that the petition Dautruy had made on behalf of the Jesuits had been granted with the consent of all the inhabitants, he obtained a letter dated February 1604, with the following content.

units.la: Demnach wir uns gegen unsern lieben getrewen / die Einwohner unser Statt Troyen / in allem / was uns müglich / gnedig vnd günstig zuerzeigen willens seyn: Als haben wir auff des inständige anhalten vnd suppliciren, so uns von unsern auch lieben getrewen René Bresle, unserm Rath vnnd verordneten Almusenpfleger / den wir zugleich zum Bischoff gen Troyen ernannt haben / wie auch obgedachten Einwohnern geschehen / zugelassen, &c. Dieser Brieff hat auch eine besondere clausul / den Jesuiten zum vortheil: Das alles / was jhnen so wol von gemeiner Statt / als von einem jeden insonderheit / wurde gestifftet werden / es weren gleich fahrende oder liegende güter / solte angenommen werden vnd gültig seyn.
units.tr: Since We are minded to show Our dear and faithful inhabitants of Our town of Troyes every kindness and favour in all that is possible for Us: We have, upon the earnest request and supplication made to Us by Our dear and faithful René Bresle, Our councillor and appointed almoner, whom We have also named bishop of Troyes, and likewise by the aforesaid inhabitants, granted, etc. This letter also contains a special clause to the advantage of the Jesuits: that everything which should be founded for them, whether by the town as a whole or by any individual in particular, whether movable or immovable goods, shall be accepted and be valid.

units.la: Als diß Patent vom Schultessen Dautruy auff dem Rathhauß eingeliefert vnd abgelesen worden / gabes bey allen / die zugegen waren / ein groß stillschweigen vnnd verwundern / vnnd hielte ein jeder darfür / daß es nun mit jhrer freyheit auß were / dieweil man Jesuiter bey jhnen einlosieren wolte / vnd das fälschlich fürgeben wurde / als solten sie dieselbe begert haben / da sie doch niemals das geringste wort davon geredt hatten: vnd gieng die gemeine rede dahin / das Dautruy, der mehr auff sein privat nutz als auff gemeiner Statt wolfahrt sehen thete / solches hinder jhnen erprac-ticirt hette. Dieweil aber Dautruy die Gemüter der Einwohner durch diß erst schreiben zu seinem willen nicht lencken können / hat er dem Bresle wider zugeschriben / der ein anderes dato 18. Maij 1604. außgebracht / darinn diese wort stünden: Daß Ihre May. die einnemmung der Jesuiten in der Statt Troyen höchlich begerte / vnd daß Ihr dieselbig zu sonderem gefallen gereichen wurde. Da diß ander schreiben nicht mehr wircken wolte / als das erste / kam ein drittes den 29. Iunij nechst folgend / in welchem dem obersten Supplicationmeister / Ampemann zu Troyen / oder seinem Leutenannt / das jenige so im schreiben befohlen worden / zu vollziehen aufferlegt werden. In diesem schreiben geschach kein fernere meldung der fürgewandten supplication deren von Troyen umb ein Jesuiter Collegium: Da war nun ein ernstes geboth ttan die Einwohner: ihre Freyheit ward in eine noth zugeschochen verwandelt: an vnderstünd sich/ durch deß Königs befelch durchzübringen/ das erstlich den nachen hatte/ als hetten sie es selbsten gesücht.
units.tr: When this patent had been delivered by the bailiff Dautruy at the town hall and read aloud, there was a great silence and wonder among all who were present, and each one held that their liberty was now at an end, since Jesuits were to be quartered upon them; and it was falsely given out that they had asked for them, although they had never said the least word about it. The common talk ran that Dautruy, who looked more to his own private advantage than to the welfare of the town, had contrived this behind their backs. But since Dautruy could not turn the minds of the inhabitants to his will by this first letter, he wrote again to Bresle, who obtained another letter dated 18 May 1604, in which these words stood: that His Majesty earnestly desired the admission of the Jesuits into the town of Troyes, and that it would be a special pleasure to Him. When this second letter was no more effective than the first, a third came on 29 June following, in which the chief supplication-master, the bailiff of Troyes, or his lieutenant, was charged to carry out what was ordered in the letter. This letter made no further mention of the petition put forward by the people of Troyes for a Jesuit college. There was now a stern command laid upon the inhabitants; their liberty was turned into a forced necessity; and an attempt was made to carry through, by the King's order, what at first had been done under the pretence that they had themselves sought it.

units.la: Inzwischen lest man einen Provincial Jesuiten sampt etlichen seiner Mitbrüder gen Troyen kommen/ welche anzeigten/ daß sie auß sonderlichem befelch Ihrer Königl. May. nit aber auff das ansüchen der Einwohner kommen weren. Für das ehrgelt/ so ihnen auff der Reyß aufgangen/ sind ihnen auß der Statt Rechen immer zweyhundert vnnd zwentzig Cronen vnnd sechs schilling gereicht vnnd geget worden. Da sie nun in der Statt seyn/ besichtigen sie mit fleiß alle gelegenheit darinnen/ damit sie ihnen bequämen Platz zu einem newen Collegio erwehlen: dann sie fürgaben/ das alte/ welches mehr dann zehen tausend Cronen gekostet/ were zu klein für sie. Nach dem sie alles wol durchsehen vnnd erwogen/ so forderten sie endtlich tausent siebenhundert Cronen Järlichen rennten/ die zweyhundert Cronen/ die ihnen für einmal zu erweiterung ihres Collegij gereichet worden/ sie auch eine andere ansehenliche summ/ die sie ihre Bibliothec mit Büchern/ vnnd ihre Wohnung mit Haußrath zu versehen/ empfangen hatten/ nicht mit eingerechnet. Auff dieß vbermäßiges begehren sind etliche von den Einwohneren heffig erzürnet worden/ andere haben nur ihr gespött darmit getrieben/ vnnd gesagt/ es liesse sich ansehen/ als wann diese gute Patres zum raub vnnd plünderung einer eroberten Stadt kommen weren: zugeschweigen/ daß die Statt durch die letzte Kriege dermaßen erschöpfft vnnd zu ruck gesetzt worden/ daß sie auff die achtzig oder hundert tausent Cronen schuldig were: Belieffe also das jenige/ daß die Jesuiten zu ihrem vnderhalt begerten/ nicht viel weniger als den halben theil dieser Summen: und were das ein feiner weg/ der Statt baldt auß ihren schulden zu helffen. Endtlich geben die Einwohner diese Antwort/ daß wann es je deß Königs wille seye/ daß die Jesuiter einnemmen solten/ seyen sie erbietig zu gehorchen/ doch daß Seine Majestet geruhe/ ihnen gnügsamen vnderhalt vnnd einkommen zu verschaffen. Etliche von denen/ die den Jesuiten zugethan waren/ baten sie/ solches bey dem König selbsten anzubringen. Also zog der Provincial vnnd seine Mitbrüder wider von dannen/ vnnd hatten weiters nichts außgerichtet/ dann daß sie den Orth besichtigt/ auff der Statt vnkosten wolgelebt/ vnnd etliche vrsachen ihrer vermeinten Visitation auffs Papier gebracht haben: darin sie getruckt was ihnen gefallen/ mit namen/ daß man ihnen viel angebotten hette: welches ob es wol ein lauter gedicht gewesen/ jedoch haben sie sich hernach darauff wider die Einwohner gründen wollen.
units.tr: Meanwhile a provincial of the Jesuits came to Troyes with several of his brothers. They declared that they had come by special order of His Royal Majesty, and not at the request of the inhabitants. For the travelling expenses they had incurred on the journey, the town treasury paid them two hundred and twenty crowns and six shillings. Once they were in the town, they inspected every possible site there with care, to choose a suitable place for a new college, since they claimed the old one, which had cost more than ten thousand crowns, was too small for them. After they had looked over and weighed everything carefully, they finally demanded an annual income of one thousand seven hundred crowns. This was in addition to the two hundred crowns already given them once for enlarging their college, and to another considerable sum they had received for stocking their library with books and furnishing their residence. Some of the inhabitants were violently angered by this excessive demand, while others only mocked it, saying it looked as if these good Fathers had come to plunder a conquered city. Quite apart from that, the town had been so exhausted and set back by the recent wars that it owed eighty or a hundred thousand crowns. So what the Jesuits asked for their upkeep was not much less than half of these sums, and this would be a fine way of helping the town out of its debts. In the end the inhabitants gave this answer: if it were indeed the king's will that the Jesuits should be admitted, they were ready to obey, provided His Majesty would see to it that they had adequate support and income. Some of those who favoured the Jesuits asked them to put this to the king himself. So the provincial and his brothers withdrew, having achieved nothing beyond inspecting the site, living well at the town's expense, and setting down on paper several reasons for their supposed visitation. In these they printed whatever pleased them, namely that a great many things had been offered to them. Although this was pure invention, they afterwards tried to build on it against the inhabitants.

units.la: Man hat von etlichen ihrer vertrawten verstanden/ daß sie vnder allen Stätten inn Champagnien fürnemblich nach der Statt Troyen trachten/ vier vrsachen halben/ die wol zu mercken. Die erste ist/ die schönheit vnnd gelegenheit der Statt vnnd daß man wegen deß Passes vnnd gemeiner Landtstraßen/ leichtlich auff Paris/ Lotringen/ Burgund/ Flandern/ Teutschland/ Brieff bestellen/ vnd von dannen wider bekommen kan. Die andere/ daß sie ihnen gewisse hoffnung gemacht/ daselbst mit der zeit zwey Häuser auffzurichten/ Nemblich ein Profession Hauß im Spital zur Dreyfaltigkeit/ welches am schönsten Orth in der Statt ligt/ nahe bey dem Korn vnnd Weinmarck/ wie auch dem Wechssel: Darnach ein Collegium, da das jetzige stehet/ welliches sie für hatten vmb ein gutes zu weitteren/ vnnd mit Wohnungen zuvermehren. Die dritte war wegen der Erbschafft P. Merat, der deß Herren von Drou eltester Sohn war/ vnnd den sie im siebenzehenden Jahr seines alters entführet/ vnnd im Jahr 1585. von Paris weggenommen haben/ dahin ihn sein Vatter/ nach dem er ihn von Pantamoussò gefordert/ zu studieren gesandt hatte. Diese gute Patres bildeten ihnen ein/ daß wann sie zu Troyen ihren fuß würden gesetzt haben/ sie würden ihre sache leichtlich wider deß von Drouerben außführen. Es seynd jhrer viel/ die von jhnen gehört ha-ben/ daß das jenige/ so dem P. Merat für sein theil zugefallen/ mehr dann dreyßig tausend Cronen werth sey/ vnd daß sie solches zu auffrichtung eines Collegij zu Troyen verordnet haben. Zum vierdten/ so hatten sie bey den letzten Kriegsemporungen der Liga erfahren/ daß kein Volck in ganß Franckreich sich leichtlicher vnder dem schein der Religion auffwickeln lasse/ als die zu Troyen: vnnd daß ihnen diß ein gewisses mittel sein würde/ das Regiment der ganzen Statt an sich zubringen/ wann sie nur zwo oder drey Personen genommen hetten/ die sie schon zu jrem willen hatten/ nemlich den Herren Bischoff/ den Präsidenten vnd den Schultessen. Vmb welcher vorhabenden sachen willen sie sich mit aller macht bemühet/ in Troyen einzunisten/ vnnd ist der verzug/ den die von der Statt gegen ihnen eingeworffen/ dem obersten jhrer Societet ganß hinderlich vnd beschwerlich gefallen/ wie solches abzunehmen auß dem register der fragen/ die P. Cotton dem Teuffel/ welcher Adrianam du Fresne besessen/ vorgehalten hat/ da vnder vielen andern/ die deß Königs Person/ vnnd die heimlichste vnd wichtigste sachen deß Reichs betreffen/ diese mit namen auffgezeichnet seyn: Quis Ambianensie Collegium impediat, quid Trecenses, das ist/ was die auffrichtung deß Collegij zu Amiens vnd zu Troyen verhindere? Zwar ob wol die Jesuiten in allen jren händlen/ die sie fürnemlich/ sich ganz embsich vnd vngestüm erzeigen: jedoch spüret man nicht/ daß sie sich hefftiger bearbeitet/ irgend einen sitz zu haben/ als in der Statt Troyen/ vnd dieweil sie gesehen/ daß man jhnen nichts geben wolte/ haben sie sich erbotten/ damit zu frieden seyn/ daß sie allein daselbst jren vnderschleiff haben möchten: welches bey vielen frommen leuten jhr suchen sehr verdächtig gemacht hat.
units.tr: From some of their confidants it was learned that among all the towns in Champagne they aim chiefly at Troyes, for four reasons which are worth noting. The first is the beauty and convenient location of the town, and that because of its passes and the common highways, letters can easily be sent from there to Paris, Lorraine, Burgundy, Flanders and Germany, and received back again. The second is that they had given the town firm hopes of eventually establishing two houses there: namely, a professed house in the Hospital of the Holy Trinity, which lies in the most beautiful spot in the town, near the grain and wine markets as well as the exchange; and then a college on the site where the present one stands, which they hoped to acquire by some good means and enlarge with residences. The third concerned the inheritance of Father Merat, who was the eldest son of the Lord of Drou, and whom they had lured away at the age of seventeen and taken from Paris in the year 1585, where his father had sent him to study after recalling him from Pont-à-Mousson. These good Fathers persuaded themselves that once they had set foot in Troyes they would easily carry their claim against the heir of Drou. Many people have heard from them that the share which fell to Father Merat is worth more than thirty thousand crowns, and that they have destined it for the founding of a college at Troyes. Fourthly, during the recent uprisings of the League they had found that no people in all France could be more easily stirred up under the guise of religion than those of Troyes. They thought this would be a sure means of seizing control of the whole town, once they had taken two or three persons who were already at their disposal, namely the bishop, the president and the mayor. For the sake of these plans they had exerted every effort to settle in Troyes, and the delay which the townspeople put in their way has greatly hindered and troubled the head of their Society. This may be gathered from the register of questions which Father Cotton put to the devil who possessed Adriana du Fresne. Among many others, which concern the person of the king and the most secret and important affairs of the realm, this one is recorded: What hinders the college at Amiens, and what hinders the college at Troyes? Indeed, although the Jesuits show themselves most eager and forceful in all their business, one does not find that they have worked harder to gain a foothold anywhere than in the town of Troyes. And since they saw that nothing would be granted them there, they offered to be content if they might at least have a private school of their own. This made their pursuit very suspicious to many devout people.

units.la: Die in der Statt/ die jhnen jhre einkommung liessen angelegen seyn/ nach der sie vermerckt/ daß es an nichts anders mangel/ die erwünschten zweck zu erreichen/ dann daß man jhnen ein reiches einkommen verordnen könte: haben sie alles anhalten so lang anstehen lassen/ biß der new Bischoff Herr Bresle bestetiget worden/ vnd angekommen ist: welcher da er auffgezogen/ als bald alle stånd/ die in der Statt wohnen/ zu sich in sein Hauß berüffen hett. Herr Ludwig Bobusse von Blois bürtig Leutenant deß Gerichts zu Troyen/ wurd von wegen deß Gerichts dahin verordnet/ und mit jhm Herr Dionysius Gombault Präsidentsrath. Aber dieweil der Bischoff die deputierte, in den Bischofflichen Hoff berüffen hatte/ sagte Herr Bobusse, er könte nicht daselbst erscheinen/ dieweil er auff das Rathhauß/ und nicht auff deß Bischofs Hof bestelt were: Gleichwol sind die andere deputirte dahin gangen: da hat jhnen der Bischoff einen brieff/ mit anhangendem sigel verlesen/ deß inhalts/ Der König hette verstanden/ welcher massen die Einwohner zu Troyen noch jmmer vmb ein Jesuiter Collegium ansüchten: Derhalben wolle er/ daß sie daselbsten solten eingenommen werden/ &c. Hieraus nam er anlaß fürzubringen/ wie die Jesuiten wolten kenneten/ daß der schwere schuldenlast/ mit welchem die Statt beladen/ nicht gestatten wolte/ jhnen ersten forderungen einen genügen zuthun/ sie wolten sich aber damit an vernügen/ daß man jhnen zwey tausent pfund oder francken jährlichen einkommens verordnet: derwegen vermahnet er sie/ sie wolten auff mittel vnd weg bedacht seyn/ woher solche summ zunemmen. Die deputirten antworteten alle einmütiglich/ daß die Statt keine mittel wüßte/ vnd daß sie viel zu tieff in schulden steckte/ darumb könte sie nichts geben. Vil sagten weiters/ die Statt köndte der Jesuiter wol entraten/ vnd daß sie schon zu vor ein Collegium hetten/ welches jhren vorfahren gut gewesen were: Im fall der König kurtzumb haben wolte/ daß sie sie einnemmen solten/ vnd Er jhnen nothwendige renten stifften würde/ so müßten sie es geschehen lassen: Aber wanns Ihrer Maj. belieben solte/ diese sach der Einwohnern gütacht heimzustellen/ so könten sie inn solche newerungen nicht einwilligen. Da sagte Herr Dionysius Gombault, er hette von den Präsidentherren befehl gehabt/ vmb
units.tr: Those in the town who had their settlement at heart, having noticed that nothing else stood in the way of achieving their desired end except that a rich income should be assigned to them, let all their petitions wait until the new bishop, Lord Bresle, had been confirmed and had arrived. When he had made his entry, he at once summoned all the estates living in the town to his house. Lord Ludwig Bobusse of Blois, lieutenant of the court at Troyes, was appointed there on behalf of the court, and with him Lord Dionysius Gombault, presidential councillor. But since the bishop had summoned the deputierte to the episcopal court, Lord Bobusse said he could not appear there, since he had been assigned to the town hall and not to the bishop's court. Nevertheless the other deputirte went there. The bishop then read them a letter with an attached seal, the content of which was that the king had understood how the inhabitants of Troyes still continually petitioned for a Jesuit Collegium; therefore he wished that they be received there, etc. From this he took occasion to say that the Jesuits recognised that the heavy burden of debt with which the town was laden did not allow it to satisfy their first demands; they would, however, be content if an income of two thousand pounds or francs a year were assigned to them. Accordingly he admonished the deputirten to consider means and ways of raising such a sum. The deputies all answered unanimously that the town knew of no means and was sunk too deep in debt, so it could give nothing. Many further said that the town could well do without Jesuits, and that it already had a Collegium, which had served its forefathers well: if the king wished outright that they be received, and he endowed them with necessary revenues, they would have to allow it; but if it pleased His Majesty to leave the matter to the goodwill of the inhabitants, they could not consent to such innovations. Then Lord Dionysius Gombault said he had received an order from the presidents to petition, on their behalf, for

units.la: Jesuiten esuiten anzuhalten: welchem aber seine Collegæ widersprochen: vnd ist solches wi-dersprechen ins Stattbuch eingeschriben worden.
units.tr: to apply on behalf of the Jesuits. But his fellow Collegæ Collegæ objected, and this objection was entered in the town register.

units.la: Als nun der Bischoff die sach der gestalt auff die bahn gebracht/ sind die jenige die n Jesuiten gewogen waren/ bewegt worden/ mittel vnd weg zu erdencken/ wie man das Collegium mit notwendige einkommen versehen möchte/ vnd habe vnder andern disen rschlag gethan/ daß man eine ansehnliche summa von der Clerisey derselbe Provintz heben/ vnd einen besondern stand gewisser personen vndern namen eines amptes richten/ hinder welchen die güter/ so das gericht zu iren händen gezogen/ zuverwaen gelegt wurden/ vnd daß man jnen einen schilling von eine jeden pfund oder franen aller fahrnuß/ die sie in irer verwarung gehabt hetten/ verordnen solte. Weil n a- r darfür gehalte worden/ daß auß disen benden fürschlägen ein sorgliche consequenz stehn möchte/ hat man für gut angesehen/ ein gewisse geltsumm für arme/ schwae vnd dürfftige fürzuschlagen/ vber welche der Herr Præsident Angenoust die articln gestelt/ vnd gesagt/ man wurde zur versicherung derselben etliche/ die wol gesef- n vnd zweyhundert tausent Cronen in vermögen hetten/ darzu benennen. Es ward ch dessen gedacht/ daß man das siechenhauß/ welches in der vorstatt Breviande ge- gen/ zu diesem Collegio ziehen könte. Vnd dieweil der Schultess vnd Schöpffen in r statt/ dasselbe allzeit von vndenckliche jaren her/ in irer verwaltung gehabt/ vnd s einkommen sich auff ein tausend oder zwölffhundert pfund erstrecken thut: so ha- n die/ welche den Jesuite zugethan waren/ fürgeben/ der Schultes vñ die Schöpfn kønten nit mit gütem gewissen/ vnd ohne simonej/ die verwaltung gedachtes sieenhauß behalten. Aber die einwohner wolten solche fürschlag nit eingehn/ noch ihn gefallen lassen/ was man auch für farben denselben anstriche/ vnd wurd offent- h gesagt/ daß es am rathsamsten were/ keine newrung zu machen/ sonder alles in n tand zulassen/ in welchem man es gefunden hette.
units.tr: When the bishop had raised the matter in this way, those who favoured the Jesuits were moved to devise means and ways of providing the Collegium with adequate income. Among other proposals, one was that a considerable sum be levied from the clergy of that province, and that a special body of certain persons be set up under the name of an office, into whose hands the goods that the court had taken over would be placed for safekeeping; and that they be assigned a shilling from every pound or franc of movable property that they held in custody. But since it was judged that a worrying consequenz might follow from these two proposals, it was thought advisable to propose a fixed sum of money for the poor, the weak and the needy. On these terms, President Angenoust drew up the articles, and said that to guarantee them some persons who were well off and had two hundred thousand crowns in property would be named. It was also mentioned that the hospital for the sick, which stood in the suburb of Breviande, could be transferred to this Collegio. And since the sheriff and aldermen of the town had always, from time immemorial, administered that hospital, and its income amounted to a thousand or twelve hundred pounds, those who were devoted to the Jesuits argued that the sheriff and aldermen could not in good conscience, and without simony, keep the administration of that hospital. But the citizens would not agree to these proposals nor accept them, whatever colours were painted on them; and it was openly said that it was most advisable to make no innovation at all, but to leave everything in the state in which it had been found.

units.la: Das ist also in einer summ der gantze verlauff/ was sich wegen einkommung der Jeit in der statt Tropen vom jar 1603. biß euff gegenwirtiges 1611. zu getragen: Da daß cob Nivelle Rector im Collegio, als er gesehen/ daß die zeit seiner bedienung bald rslossen/ vnd man jhm zu verstehen geben/ daß man jhn nit lenger im Collegio wer für einen Schülmeister noch Rectorem leiden wolte/ sich verneinen lassen/ er were schlossen/ von dannen zu weichen: vnd dieweil er damit vmbgieng/ daß er durch nen abzug den Jesuiten plaß machte (umb welches willen er etliche jar ganz fahr- sig gewesen/ vnd die vbungen deß Collegij hatte fallen lassen) ließer durch die/ wele es mit den Jesuiten hielten/ außgeben/ daß es der gantzen Provinz vnd sonderh der Statt sehr damit wurde gedient seyn/ wann man jhnen das Regiment vber s Collegium vertrawte/ vnd daß sie anders nichts/ dann das Collegium, begerten: r für sein theil/ wegen der sonderlichen affection, die er zu seinem Vatterland trûg/ bietig were/ von dem seinen 14000. pfundt zu ihrer vnderhalt zugeben. Man hiele rfür/ daß es mit dem Nivelle nur ein angelegt werck gewesen/ vnd daß das Gelt/ sches er darzu schiessen wolte/ von den Jesuiten herkommen/ die ohne das im brauch iben/ vnder eines andern namen güter an sich zu bringen. Vnd ist die vermütung her desto stärcker/ daß man wol weiß/ was Nivelle für ein geizhals ist/ der jhm selr von dem/ daß jhm Gott beschéret/ nichts güts anthut/ sonder rewt jhn auch deß ssers/ damit er seine hände wäschet. Daß dem also sey/ erscheint auch auß dem/ daß s er die Jesuiten diß letzte mal/ da sie bey der Statt angehalten in seins Canonicats hausung geherbergt/ vnd gesehen/ daß die sache solchen außgang/ wie sie gehoffet/ t gewinnen wolte/ vnd sie gleichwol stets bey jhm in der herberg blieben/ hat er sich laqt/ daß sie jhm sein leinwad zu schanden machten/ vnd solches grossen vnleidlien schadens halben hat er sie fein höflich abgewiesen/ vnd eine andere herberg zufuen genöitiget. Ein ander merckliche Exempel seines geistes ist dieses/ da er ins Colle- um, als oberster schülmeister kommen/ er eine Taffel von geringem werth in der Capellen hatte anheffen lassen/ den Altar daselbst damit zu zieren/ gleich ob sie stets da bleiben solte; gleichwol/ als er auß dem Collegio geschieden / hat er dieselbig wider ab- brechen und wegführen lassen / ohnangesehen er seinen nutzen daselbst sehr wol geschaffet hatte. Der Herr Bischoff und Præsident Angenoust, welche auch ihr bestes thaten / damit durch den abzug deß Nivelle die Jesuiter möchten eingelassen werden/ liessen außsagen/ der Nivelle wolte das Collegium verlassen/ und daß sie viel zu thun hetten/ ihn davon abzuhalten: neben dem aber schrieben sie den Jesuiten zu Paris zu/ was sich verlieff/ mit vermahnen/ daß sie solche gelegenheit nicht versaumen/ sondern der jemand von den ihrigen schicken wolten/ der das volck gewinnen/ und bey ihnen einen lust und begierd zu ihrer Societet erwecken köndte. Hierzu nimpt man den Pater Binet, als welcher durch seine geberden/ die sich mehr auff einem schawplatz / als auff der Cantzel/ da die warheit gepredigt wird/ reimen/ die gemüter deß gemeinen manns wol wurde wissen zu bewegen. Dieser kompt gen Troyen gegen dem anfang deß monats Maii/ und thût seine erste predig den Auffartsabend/ den 11. Maii/ in der kirchen zu S. Magdalene/ welche predig/ der gemeine mann/ vom gefalßnen fleisch zu nennen pflegt. Allda er einer der burger einrede zubegegnen/ als weil kein Hugenotten bey ihnen/ bedörfften sie der Jesuiter nicht: Hierauff sagte er/ daß sie zwar keine Hugenotten hetten/ aber dargegen were die Stat voll Atheisten/ Libertiner und grober Catholischen/ Das Agar und ihr Sohn Ismael sich unterstanden hetten ein trennung zwischen Abraham und seine ehliche hausfrawen Saram/ zu machen. Hette der Haußvatter wollen frieden haben in seinem hauß/ welches ein fürbild der kirchen gewesen/ so hette er müssen eijcere ancillam & filium eius. Was er aber durch die gleich nuß andeuten wöllen/ hat er mit fleiß verschwiegen/ nemlich diß/ daß die Ca- tholischen/ welche er Libertiner und Atheisten nennet/ so durch den Ismael zu verste- hen/ eben so wol/ als Hugenotten/ welche durch Agar bedeutet werden/ auß der Stat gejagt werden solten / und daß weder der eine noch der ander hauff darinnen zu du[l]den: welche rede zu einer offentlichen Auffrühr gerichtet war. Darnach predigte er noch einmal in derselben Kirchen auff den Geburtstag unser lieben Frawen/ und bracht für/ wie S. Dominicus im traum gesehen hette/ Gott den Vatter die augen im Haupt herumb drehen/ mit einem fewrigen Gesicht/ und daß ihm der Mund von zorn schaumte. Diß waren seine eigne wort/ ab welchen die zuhörer sich dermassen ärgerten/ daß viel offentlich sagten/ solche wort weren voll Gotteslästerung/ und solte man nit gestatten/ dergleichen außzugiessen. Nach dem er aber vernossen/ daß sein vorgeben von groben Catholischen/ Libertinern und Atheisten/ fehr vil auch under denen/ die ihrer Societet gewogen waren/ für den kopff gestossen: hat er in einer andern predigt solchen fehler verbessern wöllen/ lobte derwegen die Einwohner zu Troyen über diemassen/ und striche ine den fuchs-schwanz meisterlich/ sagend/ daß wann er die laster straffte/ er sie nicht meinte/ sondern die Türcken/ Persianer und andere Barbarische völcker. Den 14. Maij bey der begängnuß/ die de letsten verstorbnen König auf den tag/ er umbkommen/ zu ehren geschehen/ thet er eine Leichpredig in der Thumkirchen/ beyseyn Herren von Praslain, Oberamptmans daselbst/ und aller ständ der stat. Da nam er anlaß zu reden von der liebe/ trew und gehorsam/ die seine gesellē dē König und Franckreich gelobt hetten. Und dieweil er sich beforgte / man möchte denken/ daß er æquivociren und außflüchte gebrauchen wolte / hat er zum höchsten protestiret und geschworen/ der donner solte ihn eben an dem ort erschlagen und zu äschen verbrennen/ wann daß/ so er sagte/ nit war were. Sagte darbey/ daß seine Societet sich keines wegs in Reichshändel einmengten/ daß sie auch keine Spanier/ sondern gut und geborne Franzosen weren. Diese seine Leichpredig ist hernach in truck außgangen: aber er hat sich wol darfür gehütet/ daß er die protestationes und verflüchungen/ die ihm in der predigt entfaren/ hinein getruckt hette. Da nun die predigten dises Jesuiten den leuten je lenger je mehr mißfielen/so hat an bestelt/daß jm auff den 8. tag nach dem 13. Sacrament alle fürneme Pfarrkir en verjagt vnd versagt wurden/also daß der Bischoff/der sonst nit wußte/wo er it jhm hi nauß solte/ihn zu S. Nicier predigen ließ/welches ein kleine Pfarrkirch am ende der Statt: da er noch besser herauß führ/als noch jemals/vnd sagte/daß ein die grobe Catholische/Atheisten vnd Libertiner jhnen im weg stünden/daß sie Troyen nit eingenomen wurden: daß alle andere Priester vngeschickte tölpel we/vnd daß innerhalb zehen/zwanzig vnd auch wol dreißig jaren/kaum einiger vil cht gewesen/der recht/vnd wie sichs gebürt/gebeicht hette. Solche kühne reden erreg bey etlichen einen verdacht/bey andern eingetümel/vnd verursachten/daß viel biß daher in dieser sach/der Jesuiten einnemmung betreffend/neutral gewesen/die gen begunden auf zuthun/vnd diese Societet für sehr gefährlich vnd auffrührisch halten. Vnd waren diß gemeine reden der fürnembsten vnd ansehenlichsten bür r in auß allen Ständen in der Statt.
units.tr: That, in summary, is the whole course of events concerning the acquisition of the Collegium in the town of Troyes from the year 1603 until the present 1611. When the man called Nivelle Rector in the Collegio saw that his term of office was soon ending, and that he had been given to understand that the Collegio would no longer tolerate him either as a schoolmaster or as Rectorem, he had himself excused, saying he had decided to withdraw from there. And since he was minded, by his departure, to make room for the Jesuits (for the sake of which he had for several years been completely idle and had let the exercises of the Collegium lapse), he let it be given out through those who sided with the Jesuits that the whole province, and the town in particular, would be greatly served if the government of the Collegium were entrusted to them, and that they desired nothing other than the Collegium. For his own part, out of his particular affection for his native land, he was ready to contribute 14,000 pounds from his own means towards their maintenance. It was thought that this had been an arranged scheme with Nivelle only, and that the money he was prepared to put up came from the Jesuits, who in any case were in the habit of acquiring property under another's name. This suspicion is all the stronger because people well know what a miser Nivelle is, who does himself no good from what God has granted him, but even grudges himself the soap with which he washes his hands. That this is so also appears from the following: when the Jesuits last applied to the town, he had lodged them in the house of his canonry, and, seeing that the affair was not turning out as they hoped, and that they nevertheless stayed on as his guests, he complained that they were ruining his linen, and, because of this great and intolerable damage, he politely dismissed them and forced them to seek other lodging. Another notable example of his spirit is this: when he came to the Collegium as chief schoolmaster, he had a picture of little value hung in the chapel to adorn the altar there, as if it were to remain there for ever; yet when he left the Collegium, he had it taken down again and carried away, although he had done very well out of his position there. The Lord Bishop and President Angenoust, who also did their best so that through Nivelle's departure the Jesuits might be admitted, let it be said that Nivelle wished to leave the Collegium, and that they had much to do to dissuade him from it. Besides this, they wrote to the Jesuits in Paris about what was happening, urging them not to let this opportunity slip, but to send one of their men who could win over the people and awaken in them a desire and inclination for their Societet. For this task they chose Father Binet, since by his gestures, which suit a stage rather than the pulpit where the truth is preached, he would know how to stir the feelings of the common man. He came to Troyes at the beginning of May and preached his first sermon on the vigil of the Ascension, 11 May, in the church of St Magdalene; this is the sermon which common people are accustomed to call the sermon of the fleshpots. There he undertook to answer a remark of the citizens that, since there were no Huguenots among them, they had no need of Jesuits. To this he replied that, to be sure, they had no Huguenots, but on the other hand the town was full of atheists, libertines and gross Catholics, who were like Hagar and her son Ishmael, who had presumed to make a separation between Abraham and his lawful wife Sarah. If the householder had wished to have peace in his house, which was a figure of the Church, he would have had to eijcere ancillam & filium eius [cast out the bondwoman and her son]. But what he meant to suggest by this comparison he carefully kept silent, namely this: that the Catholics whom he called libertines and atheists, who were to be understood by Ishmael, just as much as the Huguenots, who were signified by Hagar, were to be driven out of the town, and that neither the one party nor the other was to be tolerated there. This speech was aimed at open sedition. Afterwards he preached again in the same church on the feast of the Nativity of Our Lady, and related how St Dominic had seen in a dream God the Father turning the eyes in his head about, with a fiery countenance, and his mouth foaming with anger. These were his own words, and the hearers were so offended by them that many said openly that such words were full of blasphemy, and that such things should not be allowed to be poured out.
