units.la: Quatuor libros contra vel titulum, vel personam Regis Angliæ scripserunt, aut saltem primi fecerunt. In eorum uno Natalitia Regis taxatur, ut Mater infamaretur, & Rex minus quàm Elisabetha contra religionem perpetuò irritaretur.
units.tr: They wrote four books against either the title or the person of the King of England, or at least were the first to do so. In one of them the King's birthday is censured, so that the Mother might be defamed, and the King might be continually provoked against religion, though less than Elizabeth.

units.la: Cùm Oglebein quidam missus fuisset in Hispaniam, tractaturus de fœdere inter Hispa- nam & Scotum, articulos indignissimos, & planè infames contra Regem Scotiæ exhiberi curârunt, ne cum Rege Hispaniarum, fœdus iceretur.
units.tr: When a certain Ogilvie had been sent to Spain to treat of an alliance between Spain and the Scot, they took care that the most unworthy and utterly infamous articles against the King of Scots were put forward, so that no treaty would be struck with the King of Spain.

units.la: In prima invasione Angliæ ab Hispanis factâ anno 1588. notum est, quæ eorum creaturas, ab illis subornatæ, Regem Hispaniæ commoverint.
units.tr: In the first invasion of England by the Spaniards, made in 1588, it is well known which of their creatures, suborned by them, stirred up the King of Spain.

units.la: In invasione anni 1596. præter secretiora auxilia sua, promiserunt Regi Hispaniarum cum classe Sacerdotes etiam Anglos missuros, qui causam Hispanicam apud Anglos procederent. Multi autem ex Sacerdotibus Anglis, quòd hoc recusarent, multas indignitates à Iesuitis passi sunt.
units.tr: In the invasion of 1596, besides their more secret aid, they promised the King of Spain that they would send English priests with the fleet as well, who would press the Spanish cause among the English. Many of the English priests, because they refused this, suffered many indignities at the hands of the Jesuits.

units.la: Ad invasionem anni 1597. varias fraudes excogitârunt, ut Regem Hispaniæ permoverent. Una erat; Robertus quidâ Eliotus Anglus in Hispaniam cum navi propria multis remigibus, aliisq; militibus, illi pro tempore servientibus, appulit. Industus est à Iesuitis, se Comitem Angliæ esse singeret, ab aliis proceribus missum, ad persuadendum Regi Hispaniæ expeditionem Anglicanam. Id quod præstitit, paratissima Anglorum auxilia promittes, deductus ad Regem à Tancredo quodam Iesuita Anglo, à quo sociisq; aliis ad istam posturam efformatus erat.
units.tr: For the invasion of 1597 they devised various frauds to move the King of Spain. One was this: a certain Robert Eliot, an Englishman, put in to Spain with his own ship, with many rowers and other soldiers serving him for the occasion. He was instructed by the Jesuits to pretend that he was the Earl of England, sent by other nobles to persuade the King of Spain to an English expedition. This he accomplished, promising the most ready English aid, and he was brought to the King by one Tancred, an English Jesuit, by whom he and his companions had been shaped for this part.

units.la: In Scotiâ proceret quosdam, Huntleium, Arrolium, Angufiu & alios, tanto odio Calnismi ibi devastantes omnia, percitos invenerunt, ut ad Iesuitarum imperium, chartas subsignatas in Hispaniam mittere non vererentur, ne ex parte Scotorum aliquid deet ad Calvinismum evertendum. Permisit Deus (ad castigandum forte Iesuitarum subiam) chartas albas intercipi: unde Bringthonio latori mors consequuta est, proceribus exilium, Catholicis periculum, hæreticis insultatio, Regi Scotiæ suspicio, & arctior cum Anglia conjunctio.
units.tr: They found certain nobles in Scotland, Huntly, Errol, Angus and others, so inflamed with hatred of Calvinism, which was laying waste everything there, that they did not shrink from sending blank signed charters to Spain at the Jesuits' command, so that nothing might be lacking on the Scots' side for overthrowing Calvinism. God permitted (perhaps to punish the Jesuits' cunning) the blank charters to be intercepted. From this came death for the bearer Bringthon, exile for the nobles, danger for the Catholics, mockery from the heretics, suspicion for the King of Scots, and a closer union with England.

units.la: Proceres exules, quia consensum suum recusaverant, ut redditus monasteriorum in totia Iesuitis permitterent, responsum acceperunt, nihil illis subsidij expectandum esse, si Infantam contra proprium Regem ad Regnū Angliæ capessendum, adjuvare fidem darent. Inde in Scotiam commeare coacti sunt, & cum proprio Rege incolumitatem, ut potuerint, pacifici.
units.tr: The exiled nobles, because they had refused their consent to hand over the revenues of the monasteries entirely to the Jesuits, received the answer that they could expect no aid unless they pledged their faith to help the Infanta seize the kingdom of England against their own king. Thereafter they were compelled to return to Scotland and, as best they could, to make peace with their own king.

units.la: In invasionibus Hybernis ab Hispano factis, si Iesuitæ negare vellent, eorum manus isse præcipuas in instigando Hispanos, præter alia argumenta benè nota Regi Britanniæ, Eduvici Mansonis Iesuitæ in Nunciaturam Apostolicam evestio testabitur.
units.tr: In the invasions of Ireland made by the Spaniard, should the Jesuits wish to deny that their hands were chief in instigating the Spaniards, the removal of the Jesuit Edward Mason into the Apostolic Nunciature will bear witness, besides other arguments well known to the King of Britain.

units.la: Sacerdotibus ex Anglia Romam missis, & in Collegio Anglicano incarceratis, ut a à Scoto faveando terrore detinerentur, pro crimine objectum est piaculari, & in quo dalia solverentur, quòd Scotisticæ planè essent factionis. Sic loqui & sic scribere visum est Iesuitis. Idem postea Sacerdotibus alijs in Belgium venientibus, nec pro levi peccato, nec mi levi periculo objectum est.
units.tr: When priests from England were sent to Rome and imprisoned in the English College, so that they might be kept from favouring the Scot through fear, it was objected against them as a crime deserving expiation, by which other faults would be paid for, that they were wholly of the Scottish faction. This is how the Jesuits thought fit to speak and to write. The same charge was later brought against other priests coming into Belgium, and it was brought not for a slight sin nor for a slight danger.

units.la: Vt Anglos Catholicos in speciem Hispanis, revera autem sibiipsis obnoxios tenent, à multis jam annis de tempore in tempus invasionem Hispanicam promiserunt. Onnullos subornârunt, qui de expeditus Classibus, militibus, apparatibus, mendacia lendida solenni more disseminârent. Notæ sunt litteræ, & in manibus Senatus Anglicani unius Iesuitæ ad alium teruntur, suadentis in illis, ut rumores invasionis turæ non intermittendo omnem operam navaret. Istâ fraude detectâ & explosâ, sinuarunt subdolè, Elisabetham Angliæ secretum fœdus cum Infanta icisse, eamne in successionem Angliæ destinâsse. Addunt, & idin toto orbe proclamant, eorum
units.tr: So that they might keep the English Catholics in appearance for the Spaniards, but in truth bound to themselves, they have for many years, from time to time, promised a Spanish invasion. They suborned some who spread lying rumours in the customary manner about the fleets, soldiers and preparations. Letters survive, and are in the hands of the English Senate, in which one Jesuit writes to another, urging that the rumours of the coming invasion not be allowed to cease, and that he exert every effort. This fraud being detected and exploded, they slyly whispered that Elizabeth had made a secret treaty with the Infanta, and had destined her for the succession to England. They add, and proclaim throughout the whole world, that

units.la: operâ factum esse, ut Hispanus cum Angliae Principe nullam confœderationem inire vellet, nisi cum expresso articulo religionis Catholicae in Anglia liberae. Eventu ipso hac techna etiam dissipata, adhuc Catholicis persuadere conantur, multa millia aureorum à Rege Catholico designari, quae illis distribuantur; cuius rumoris vanitas, ut & aliorum, lippis [illegible, ~10 letters]
units.tr: by their work it came about that the Spaniard would not enter any alliance with the Prince of England except on an express article that the Catholic religion be free in England. This device too having been dissipated by the outcome, they still try to persuade the Catholics that many thousands of gold pieces are being set aside by the Catholic King to be distributed among them. The vanity of this rumour, like that of others, [illegible]

units.la: Interea ut à quo, & cuius pisicatores constituti essent, clarere inciperet, Iesuitam ali[illegible, ~10 letters] quem Cardinalem creandum esse decernunt. Emendicatis, vel mentitis suffragijs aliquorum Sacerdotum (magnam & tantum non magicam vim tribuunt subscriptionum Catalogus) adjungunt nomina Scholarium, militum, lotricum, quibus magno quasi consensu gentis Anglicanae Robertus Persionius Regi Hispaniarum commendatur eius auspicijs promovendus. Non facile ratio reddi potest, cur is reliquis Iesuitis Britannicis praeferretur longè illo hac dignitate dignioribus, qui non infames erant propter mores, qui doctrinâ competenti imbuti, non necesse habebant ut doúti viderentur, aliorum libros uti proprios edere: qui non formidine & aversione Catholicorum coacti fuerant à Britannia aufugere. Sed cùm famâ, doctrinâ, animoq; careret, Spiritu tamen turbulentissimo non carebat, propter quem sciebant, eum Regi Britanniae, cui semper opponebatur, merito odiosissimum esse.
units.tr: Meanwhile, so that it might begin to be clear by whom and whose fishermen they had been appointed, they decree that a Jesuit [illegible] is to be created Cardinal. With begged or feigned votes of some priests (they attribute a great and almost magical power to the catalogue of signatures), they add the names of scholars, soldiers and laundresses. By the great, almost unanimous consent of the English nation, Robert Persons is commended to the King of Spain, to be promoted under his auspices. It is not easy to give a reason why he was preferred to the other British Jesuits, who were far more worthy of this dignity: men who were not infamous for their morals, who, being imbued with sufficient learning, had no need to seem learned by publishing others' books as their own, and who had not been forced by the fear and aversion of Catholics to flee from Britain. But since he lacked reputation, learning and character, he did not lack a most turbulent spirit, on account of which they knew he would rightly be most hateful to the King of Britain, to whom he was always opposed.

units.la: Propter Cardinalatus Persioniani sollicitudinem Vuorthingthonius praecipuus aulicus, praesidentiâ Duacensis Collegij, sed à triennio in triennium, ut à Iesuitis pendeat totus, rursus muneratus est. Is, ut fidem Roberto Personio praestitam exsolveret, cuius sollicitudinem & studium in Cardinalatu ambiendo intimè noverat, audiens Elisabetham Angliae morituam esse, vel morti vicinam, Anglos convocat, longaque habita contra Regem Scotiae invectiva, docet, quàm intolerandum esset, eum sustinere Regem Angliae, & ut ne fieret orare serio admonebat. Rex Scotiae declaratus tamen fuerat Rex Angliae, & forte Dominus Vuorthingthonius audierat, sed non credebat, quia non volebat. Ex Senatoribus Anglicanis sunt, qui Sacerdotes admonebat, ne à Duaco in Angliam ordinati mitterentur, quod id Regi futurum esset valde exosum propter ipsius Vuorthingthonij nomen.
units.tr: On account of the anxiety over Persons' cardinalate, Worthington, the chief courtier, was again installed as president of the Douai College, though only for three-year terms, so that he depends wholly on the Jesuits. He, in order to fulfil the promise made to Robert Persons, whose anxiety and zeal in canvassing for the cardinalate he knew intimately, heard that Elizabeth was about to die or near death. He convened the English and, after a long invective against the King of Scots, taught how intolerable it would be to endure him as King of England, and warned them to pray earnestly that it not happen. The King of Scots had indeed been declared King of England, and perhaps Worthington had heard this, but he did not believe it, because he did not want to. Among the English senators there were some who warned priests not to be sent into England ordained from Douai, because that would be very hateful to the King on account of Worthington's own name.

units.la: Nec humanis tantum rationibus niti voluerunt Iesuitae Hispanorum in Anglia victoriam, sed excogitatis etiam revelationibus. Inter alias magnâ gravitate asseverabant S. Iacobum navi lapideâ in Hispaniam vectum, illi genti victoriam contra Anglos promi-sisse. Nec desunt fide digni homines, qui Iesuitas faciunt authores Indulgentiarum concessarum illis, qui titulum Hispanicum ad Regnum Angliae promoverent.
units.tr: The Jesuits did not want the Spanish victory in England to rest on human reasons alone; they also devised revelations. Among others, they asserted with great seriousness that St James had sailed to Spain in a stone ship and had promised that nation victory over the English. Nor are there lacking trustworthy men who make the Jesuits the authors of the indulgences granted to those who advanced the Spanish claim to the Kingdom of England.

units.la: AN RELIGIO CATHOLICA PROMOTA PER ANGLO-IESVITAS IN BRI- TANNIA.
units.tr: WHETHER THE CATHOLIC RELIGION WAS PROMOTED IN BRITAIN BY THE ANGLO-JESUITS.

units.la: Cotorum Seminaria per viginti annos Iesuitis subfuerunt. Laudi illis esset, si viginti tantum Sacerdotes idoneos ex illis prodijsse ostenderent. Imò viros aliquot Scotiae nationis eximios, & optimè de Ecclesia meritos, pessimè exagitarunt, eorumq; conatus quo modo impedierunt.
units.tr: The seminaries of the Scots were under the Jesuits' control for twenty years. It would be to their credit if they could show that only twenty suitable priests had come out of them. Instead, they harassed severely several outstanding men of the Scottish nation, who had deserved very well of the Church, and they hindered their efforts in every way.

units.la: Quàm parvos Iesuitae in Scotia fructus fecerint, utinam non lamentabilis Regni illius facies toti orbi testaretur, quàm vix nova Arithmetica, vix, aut ne vix quidem triginta Catholicos, ad triginta millia in suis Relationibus multiplicarint.
units.tr: How small the fruits the Jesuits produced in Scotland were, the wretched face of that kingdom would that it did not testify to the whole world: how a new arithmetic, hardly, or not even hardly, thirty Catholics, they multiplied in their reports to thirty thousand.

units.la: In Angliae negotijs, si religionem Iesuitae dicant omnium suarum actionum Regulam fuisse, fateor ignorantiam meam, & probationem desidero.
units.tr: In the affairs of England, if the Jesuits say that religion was the rule of all their actions, I confess my ignorance and I want proof.

units.la: Num religio fecit, ut defectus professionis Catholicae non esset impedimentum in successione Galliae Navarraeo (sic scribunt in uno ex plurimis suis libello famoso contra Lestrium) esset vero impedimentum Scoto in successione Angliae?
units.tr: Did religion bring it about that the defect of Catholic profession was no hindrance to Navarre's succession to France (so they write in one of the many libels they published against Lestrius), but was a hindrance to the Scot's succession to England?

units.la: Num religio fecit, ut praeter clancularias omnium officiorum promissiones, Elisabetha Angliae, justissimae, simul & misericordissimae Principi vitam optarent diuturnam eo quo-[illegible, ~3 letters] quod parem (ut in Apologia quadam typis evulgata loquuntur) successorem non sperent.
units.tr: Did religion bring it about that, apart from their secret promises of every kind of service, they wished Elizabeth of England, the most just and at the same time most merciful prince, a long life, for the reason that (as they say in a certain published Apology) they do not hope for an equal successor?

units.la: Num religio fecit, ut Angliae titulus ab illis prostitueretur, non modò Catholicis Principibus in mutuam eorum perniciem, sed etiam quibusdam non-Catholicis, ut Ferdinando Herbiensi Comiti, & aliis propter justas causas reticendis?
units.tr: Did religion bring it about that they prostituted the title of England, not only to Catholic princes for their mutual destruction, but also to some non-Catholics, such as the Earl of Herbiers Ferdinand and others whom I pass over for just reasons?

units.la: Num religio fecit, ut Mariam Scotiae prae omnibus mortalibus tractarent indignissime, cui prae omnibus mortalibus Angli debebant obedire, ut Principi; compassionem, ut iptiva; venerationem, ut martyri.
units.tr: Did religion bring it about that they treated Mary of Scotland most unworthily, beyond all mortals, to whom the English ought to have owed obedience beyond all mortals as to a prince; compassion as to one who was ill-used; veneration as to a martyr?

units.la: Num religio fecit, ut pro atheistis infamarentur à Iesuitis, qui Scotico titulo favent, nec Archiepiscopo Glasgoniensi, nec Episcopo Dumblamensi, viris honorandissimis, ceptis, nec ipso Guilelmo Reinoldo, singulari huius aetatis ornamento, qui in libro contra Brafum edito, anno 1593. impressio, & Regi dedicato, eum legitimum Regni Anglicani sacredem appellare non vererétur?
units.tr: Did religion bring it about that men who favour the Scottish title were slandered by the Jesuits as atheists, and that they did not hesitate to call the Archbishop of Glasgow and the Bishop of Dumblane, most honourable men, and the famous William Reynolds, a singular ornament of this age, who in his book against Brafus, published in 1593 and dedicated to the King, did not shrink from calling him the lawful heir of the Kingdom of England, the lawful heir?

units.la: Num religio fecit, ut Vuestmarlandius Comes, Regulus Pagettus, & alij ex Anglicana nobilitate, pro fide exules propter odium Scotici tituli Iesuitis insitum, perpetuis ditionibus exagitarentur, Generali Iesuitarum per eorum literas incassum pro remedijs interpellato?
units.tr: Did religion bring it about that the Earl of Westmorland, Regulus Paget, and others of the English nobility, exiles for the faith, were harassed with perpetual proscriptions because of the hatred of the Scottish title implanted in the Jesuits, though they had appealed to the General of the Jesuits by their letters for remedies, to no avail?

units.la: Num religio fecit, ut tot seditiosorum libellorum, assassinatuum artifices à Iesuitis subornati, laudem mererentur: Catholici vero quidam, Rabinghtonius, Filneius, Satisirius & alij, quibus Sol nihil videt illustrius, eo quod de liberanda persona Reginae Scotiae deliberassent, vel nebulones quosdam exploratores ad eam deliberationem subornas audivissent, potius in libello Apologetico Iesuitarum pro perduellibus damnarentur; ccerfito illis Sacerdote quodam nomine Vuallardo, qui supra nongentos Catholicae reli- gioni reconciliaverat?
units.tr: Did religion bring it about that the makers of so many seditious pamphlets and the assassins suborned by the Jesuits deserved praise, while certain Catholics, Rabinghton, Filney, Satisirius and others, than whom the sun sees nothing more illustrious, because they had deliberated about freeing the person of the Queen of Scots, or because they had heard that certain scoundrels had been suborned as spies for that deliberation, were rather condemned as traitors in the Jesuits' apologetic pamphlet, passing over the priest named Wallard, who had reconciled more than nine hundred to the Catholic religion?

units.la: Num religio fecit, ut Mariae Scotiae Reginae injustissima mors patronum inveret Iesuitam? Praeterea lex in praeteritis Comitijs Anglorum fertur, ut si persona quaeam in mortem Elisabethae conspiraret, & illa persona, & omnes ab illa jus Regni Anglicani praetendentes, ut perduelles successione in Regnum privarentur. Haec lex urgeri on potuit à Christiano quovis, ut dum per Matrem impetitur filius, illius martyrium in ibium & in crimen vocetur, imò & damnetur plane, cui similis foemina, tantae celsitudinis, ut ait Bosius in libro de signis Ecclesiae, pro nulla unquam secta aut professione, à mundo indito, mortem oppetijt. Vrgetur tamen haec lex contra Regem Scotiae à Iesuita authore bri Titulorum.
units.tr: Did religion bring it about that the most unjust death of Mary, Queen of Scots, found a Jesuit as its defender? Moreover, a law was passed in the recent English Parliament that if any person conspired against the life of Elizabeth, that person and all who claimed the right to the Kingdom of England through her should be deprived of succession to the kingdom as traitors. No Christian could press this law so that, while a son is attacked through his mother, the son's martyrdom is called in question and made a crime; indeed, a woman of such high rank, who, as Bosius says in his book on the marks of the Church, never died for any sect or profession since the world was founded, is plainly to be condemned. Yet this law is pressed against the King of Scots by a Jesuit, the author of the Titles.

units.la: Num religio fecit, ut Anglia, dum in ea Cardinalitus pileus Roberto Personio, vel ex implicibus alicui sanguine martyrum rubricaretur, & Vtopianum, fere, Anabaptisticum d reformandam Ecclesiam instituatur Consistorium, fiat tragicum omnium miseriarum eatrum?
units.tr: Did religion bring it about that England, while a cardinal's hat was given to Robert Persons, or was coloured with the blood of martyrs by someone implicated in it, and a Utopian, almost Anabaptist, consistory was set up to reform the Church, became the tragic theatre of all miseries?

units.la: Vnica solutio est, quam in recenti Iesuitarum Theologia reperimus in Anglia, ilicet Catholicum & Hispanicum esse synonyma. Imò eò usque progressi sunt, ut in sponso quodam ad editum Elisabethae quoddam afferant plane, florentem statum Regis Hispanicae fis esse conjunctum cum statu Ecclesiae, ut illo sublato, hic subsistere nequeat. Monarchiae Hispanicae in tota Europa necessitatem persuadere conantur Iesuitae, sedum magno praejudicio, & nota ingratitudinis erga alias Monarchas & Principes, ibus multum debent; cum suspicione perfidae adulationis Regi Britanniae injectâ, em jam ad regna evectum ad astra usque laudibus evehunt. Iudiciorum Dei inscrubilis abyssus est, propterea omnes à Iesuitis instigatos conatus contra Angliam subsan- avit.
units.tr: There is one solution, which we find in the recent Jesuit theology in England, namely that Catholic and Spanish are synonyms. Indeed, they have gone so far as to assert plainly, in a certain sponsio on Elizabeth's edict, that the flourishing state of the Spanish King is so bound up with the state of the Church that the one cannot survive if the other is removed. The Jesuits try to persuade all Europe of the necessity of a Spanish monarchy, but with great prejudice and a mark of ingratitude towards other monarchs and princes, to whom they owe much; and, with suspicion of treacherous flattery cast upon the King of Britain, whom they now raise to the stars with praises, they carry him up to the heavens. The abyss of God's judgments is unsearchable; therefore He has frustrated all the attempts instigated by the Jesuits against England.

units.la: Serio autem perpendant Iesuitae, an illi novi Apostoli id imitentur quod dicit Pau- lus 2. Corinth. 1. Gloria nostra haec est, testimonium conscientiae nostrae, quod in simplicitate cordis, & sinceritate Dei, & non in sapientia carnali, sed cum gratia Dei conversati sumus in mundo: cuius indicium & quasi probatio sequitur; Fidelis est Deus, quia sermo noster, qui fuit apud vos, non fuit etiam & non, sed etiā per se ipsum fuit. Huic Apostolicæ regulæ, num Iesuitæ se conformaverint ab initio quasi renascentis Ecclesiæ Anglicanæ videndum est: Hispanis relictâ discussione, an illorum sermo de Monarchia Hispanica fuerit etiam & non.
units.tr: But let the Jesuits seriously consider whether those new apostles imitate what Paul says in 2 Corinthians 1: "Our glory is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity of heart and sincerity of God, not in carnal wisdom but in the grace of God, we have conducted ourselves in the world; and of this comes the sign and, as it were, the proof: God is faithful, because our word, which was among you, was not yes and no, but in Him it was yes." We must see whether the Jesuits conformed themselves to this apostolic rule from the beginning of the newly reborn English Church, leaving aside for the Spaniards the examination of whether their talk about a Spanish monarchy was yes and no.

units.la: DE IESVITARVM MODO PROCEDEN- DI IN REBVS ECCLESIAE ANGLICANAE TRACTANDIS.
units.tr: ON THE MANNER IN WHICH THE JESUITS PROCEEDED IN DEALING WITH THE AFFAIRS OF THE ENGLISH CHURCH.

units.la: Propter seminaria omnibus Catholicis obvia, magno Anglorum in partes transmarinas confluente numero, anno 1580. Collegium Anglorum, quod per 800. annos Romæ tenuerunt, in novam faciem mutatum est, magna Iesuitarum Calliditate, qui dissidium inter Anglos, & Cambobritannos seredo, sese insinuantes, viros graves excludendo, juniores varijs prætextibus eludendo, omnia ad se revocare conabantur.
units.tr: Because seminaries were open to all Catholics, and a great number of English were flocking to the lands beyond the sea, the English College, which they had held at Rome for 800 years, was changed into a new form in 1580 by the great cunning of the Jesuits. Insinuating themselves, they sowed discord between the English and the Welsh. They excluded the grave men, eluded the younger ones with various pretexts, and tried to draw everything to themselves.

units.la: In Collegio Anglo-Romano pede fixo anno 1580. in Angliam admissi, pro more gentis nostræ cum omni humanitate excipiebantur, præsertim cum in aliis regnis, plurimum cautum sam Catholicorum promoturos se sanctissime promisissent.
units.tr: Those admitted into England from the English-Roman College, established in 1580, were received with all courtesy, in the manner of our nation, especially since they had most solemnly promised that in England they would promote the cause of the Catholics with far more caution than in other kingdoms.

units.la: Robertus Personius, & Edmundus Campianus primi Angliā ingressuri, secum Rhemos usque in Gallijs adduxerunt Episcopum Asaphensem Anglum tanquam Patronum, cui auxiliari debebant, & spoponderant.
units.tr: Robert Persons and Edmund Campion, the first to enter England, brought with them to Rheims, even into France, the English Bishop of St Asaph as a patron, whom they were bound to assist and had promised to serve.

units.la: In Anglia sacramenta administrare nolebant sine licentia sacerdotum, in quorum quasi residentia, in privatis Catholicorum ædibus erant: à Sacerdotibus enim, qui jam onus Dei portaverant, in adjutorium non necessario petebantur, & ad messem veriùs, quàm ad sementem admittebantur.
units.tr: In England they were unwilling to administer the sacraments without the permission of the priests in whose district, so to speak, they were staying, in the private houses of Catholics. For they did not need to ask for help from priests who had already borne the burden of God; they were admitted to the harvest rather than to the sowing.

units.la: In publicis scriptis, & colloquijs privatis, fidem dabant Catholicis laicis, se nihil nisi spiritualia tractaturos, sub ea conditione, non alios in eorum domibus excipiendi, & ista conditione violata (quod postea in Roberto Personio contigit) eij ciendi.
units.tr: In public writings and private conversations they gave the Catholic laity their word that they would deal only with spiritual matters, on the condition that they would not receive others into their houses. When this condition was violated (as later happened with Robert Persons), they expelled them.

units.la: Paupertatis & humilitatis professionem faciebat. Propter istas virtutum species, reliqua nova admirationem, & alias artes, multi in Societatem Iesuitarum, omnes in bonam de illis opinionem adducti sunt.
units.tr: They professed poverty and humility. Because of these outward shows of virtue and their other new arts, many were drawn into the Society of Jesus, and all were brought to a good opinion of them.

units.la: Collegij Romani Anglorum administratio cum reditibus illis cedebat. Pecuniarum distributio paulatim in Anglia Iesuitis commissa est, præsertim cum sacerdotes seculares tam fuerint rerum temporalium negligentes, ut ordo eorum universus, nec censum, nec domum, nec hortū usquam haberet, id quod strictissimam nuditatem cuiuscunq; ordinis superat. Pecuniarum collectionem, licet magnum onus, Iesuitæ tamen ex charitate ferre didicerant.
units.tr: The administration of the English-Roman College was passing to them along with its revenues. Gradually the distribution of money in England was committed to the Jesuits, especially since the secular priests were so negligent of temporal affairs that their whole order had no endowment, no house, and no garden anywhere, a poverty that surpasses the strictest nakedness of any order. The collection of money, though a great burden, the Jesuits had learned to bear out of charity.

units.la: Interea Iesuitæ, ut paulatim omnia sua efficerent, omnes in Collegio Romano, obedientiæ merito prætenso, juramento sibi obstrictos habere procurârunt, ut ad Iesuitarum libitum fierent Sacerdotes, vel non; & in Angliam proficiscerentur, vel non. Hoc stratagema glorianter sibi tribuit Robertus Personius, quod sciret Iesuitarum equum Troianum esse.
units.tr: Meanwhile, so that they might gradually bring all their plans to pass, the Jesuits took care to have everyone in the Roman College bound to them by oath, on the pretext of the merit of obedience, so that they would become priests, or not, at the Jesuits' pleasure, and would go to England, or not. Robert Persons proudly claimed this stratagem for himself, since he knew that the Jesuits' horse was a Trojan one.

units.la: Sub specie regularium in Collegio Anglo-Romano observandarum, omnes omnium litera illis aperiendæ veniebant, comprehensis etiam in praxi Anglis extra Collegium degentibus, ut sic nihil ad Angliam spectans tractari posset Romæ, vel cum ipso Pontifice, nisi per Iesuitas.
units.tr: Under the pretext of rules to be observed in the English-Roman College, the letters of all men were brought to them to be opened, including those of Englishmen living outside the College, so that nothing concerning England could be dealt with at Rome, or with the Pope himself, except through the Jesuits.

units.la: Mortuo Cardinale Moroño protectore Anglorum, cujus prudentia effecit, ne in aqua turbata piscari possent, subrogandum ei curârunt Cardinalem Boncompagnum, repudiato Farnesio verę nobilitatis Cardinale, qui propter avitam cum Polo amicitiam, & multa erga Anglos amoris indicia Protectoris munus, quod verè præstitisset, meritò expectavit.
units.tr: When Cardinal Morone, the protector of the English, died, his prudence had prevented them from fishing in troubled waters. They then took care that Cardinal Boncompagni be substituted for him, and Farnese, a cardinal of true nobility, was passed over. Because of his ancestral friendship with Pole and his many signs of affection toward the English, Farnese had rightly expected the office of protector, which he had indeed performed.

units.la: Et ut seipsos ad omnem evētum pro Protectoribus venditarent, jactabant se facultatem habere, abere, Anglum, quemcunq; vellent, constituendi Cardinalem, unde facile omnes ex se dependentes habere possent: id quod postea attentarunt, facto per ipsos, ut dicunt ipsi, Alano Cardinale.
units.tr: In order to peddle themselves as protectors for every eventuality, they boasted that they had the power to appoint whichever Englishman they wished as cardinal, so that they could easily have everyone dependent on themselves. This they later attempted, the thing being done by them, as they themselves say, for Cardinal Allen.

units.la: Nec cessabant interim seditionibus, detractionibusque artificiosissime superseminatis, omnes impetere, quos metuebant impediturros, ne pervenirent Iesuitae ad metam, ad quam ollimabant. In eo numero omnes viros eminentiores comprehendebant; quantumcunque e causa Dei, & illis etiam ipsis optime meritos. Pro reliquis exemplo fit Episcopus Caffanensis. Is Iesuitas in Anglorum Collegium Romae introduxit, invito Cardinale Morono, et introductos continuis bonis officiis prosequutus est. Notum est quid Romae in eorum gratiam fecerit, cum esset ibi religiosorum Visitator. Septimana tim ad extremum usque spiritum aliquid Casae professae contulit. Inter istum tamen & Alanum discordias severunt maximas, quibus paulo ante mortem finem impo fuit Alanus, dicens, Non esse aequum, ut pro ter greges vel pastores, Abraham & Loth discordarent. Mortuo vero Alano, oculos in Caffanensem conjiciebant Angli, tanquam notum illis, & illos noscentem, ideoque petebant, ut Alani authoritas in Caffanensi resideret.
units.tr: Meanwhile they did not cease, with sedition and detraction most artfully sown, to attack all whom they feared would hinder the Jesuits from reaching the goal they aimed at. In that number they included all the more eminent men, however well they had deserved of the cause of God and of the Jesuits themselves. As an example for the rest, there is the Bishop of Cassano. He introduced the Jesuits into the English College at Rome, against the wishes of Cardinal Morone, and continually supported them with good offices. It is well known what he did at Rome in their favour, when he was Visitor of the religious there. Almost to his last breath he contributed something to the professed house. Yet between him and Allen they sowed the greatest discords, which Allen ended shortly before his death, saying it was not fair that Abraham and Lot should quarrel over their herdsmen. After Allen's death, the English fixed their eyes on the Bishop of Cassano, as one known to them and knowing them, and therefore they asked that Allen's authority should rest in the Bishop of Cassano.

units.la: Petitioni tanquam justissimae Iesuitae se primo affirmabant concursuros. Cardinali Cajetano clanculariè persuadebant, ut se Caffanensi, tanquam Protectoratus Anglicani aemulo (quod & fecit) & Anglis petitionem suam Pontifici exhibentibus, opponeret. Hinc magna Anglicani fundi calamitas, & perpetua contra Caffanensem oppositio. Is tamen moriturus adversariis suis ignovit, & in eius rei signum jussit comburi Iesuitae cujusdam literas, in quibus de Caffanensi scripserat, Aut Deus, aut daemon, aut Turca eripiat eum.
units.tr: The Jesuits first declared that they would join in this petition, as most just. They secretly persuaded Cardinal Caetani to oppose Cassano, as a rival to the English protectorate (which he did), while the English presented their petition to the Pope. Hence came a great calamity to the English cause and perpetual opposition to Cassano. He, however, when dying, forgave his adversaries, and as a sign of this he ordered the burning of the letters of a certain Jesuit, in which that man had written about him: "May God, or the devil, or the Turk, deliver him."

units.la: In Anglia erant adhuc veteris Cleri reliquiae a tempore Mariae Reginae superstites. Inter hos erant viri omni exceptione majores: sed quia a Iesuitis, recenter appulsis, dependere merito dedignabantur, cum his idcirco contentiones honesto praetextu exercendae erant: rum jurisdictio a Iesuitis in dubium vocatur, licet a Pio V. concessa, & a Legato eius Episcopo Sincolnien. adhuc vivo confirmata, qui postea in carcere profide obiit.
units.tr: In England there still survived, from the time of Queen Mary, remnants of the old clergy. Among these were men of every distinction. But because they rightly disdained to depend on the Jesuits, who had recently arrived, disputes had therefore to be waged with them under a respectable pretext. Their jurisdiction is called into doubt by the Jesuits, although it was granted by Pius V and confirmed by his legate, the Bishop of Lincoln, while he was still alive; he afterwards died in prison for the faith.

units.la: Inter alios aliis intentatos abusus, unius nomine, qui Dolmannus vocabatur, procudit librum Titulorum ad Regnum Angliae supradictu, magno cum Dolmanni periculo. Huic maxime infensi erant Iesuitae, quod ei, utpote perspectissimae integritatis viro, maximae pecuniarum summae in suos usus distribuendae, committerentur.
units.tr: Among other abuses attacked by others, one man named Dolman published a book of titles to the aforementioned kingdom of England, at great risk to Dolman himself. The Jesuits were especially hostile to him, because, as a man of the most perfect integrity, he had been entrusted with the largest sums of money to distribute for their uses.

units.la: Via hoc modo Iesuitis patefacta, proclamant statim, se habere facultatem illis plenam indulgentiam concedendi, pro prima vice, qui peccata Iesuitis confiterentur, & ad iam facultatem intimandam, ex suis devotis, quorum jam numerus accreverat, emissarios dornant. Inde facillime aliorum poenitentes ad se alliciebant, & fecerunt filios sibi, quos ipsi non genuerunt. Generales etiam esse volunt confessiones, ut omnia omnium negotia pateant. Facultates alias promunt, quibus nervis belli contra saeculare clerum intenti, ut impatet, pecunia comparatur: Una, ut in incertis restitutionib. aliquid donetur Iesuitis, & fiat: alia dispensandi, ne bona haereticis debita, haereticis restituantur, sed Iesuitis: alia dispensandi de rebus ad Ecclesiam pertinentibus: aliam permittendi Patronis, ut beneficia vendant Hugonoticis Ministris, temporalia beneficia a spiritualibus separando: Hispanicis viribus se interim sustentatos plenis buccis ostentabant.
units.tr: With the way thus opened to the Jesuits, they at once proclaimed that they had full power to grant a plenary indulgence, for the first time, to those who confessed their sins to the Jesuits. To make this faculty known, they sent emissaries from among their devotees, whose number had already grown. From there they very easily drew others' penitents to themselves, and made sons for themselves whom they had not begotten. They also wish confessions to be general, so that the affairs of everyone may lie open to them. They put forward other faculties, by which money is obtained for the war against the secular clergy, as is evident: (1) that something be given to the Jesuits in uncertain restitutions, and that it be done; (2) of dispensing, so that goods owed to heretics be restored not to the heretics but to the Jesuits; (3) of dispensing with things pertaining to the Church; (4) of permitting patrons to sell benefices to Huguenot ministers, separating temporal benefices from spiritual ones. Meanwhile they boasted, with full cheeks, that they were sustained by Spanish forces.

units.la: Ex Collegiis transmarinis per hoc tempus fecerant fere monopolia. His initiis & incrementis, Iesuitica m se fabricam Anglia Catholica miratur & ingemiscit.
units.tr: By this time the overseas Colleges had become almost monopolies. Through these beginnings and this growth, Catholic England marvels at and groans over the Jesuitical edifice itself.

units.la: Neque tamen aliis artificiis Iesuitae vel hilum profecissent, si ad sedem Apostolicam pervius accessus fuisset. Omnes itaque viae ad illam obsepiendae erant. Surreptionibus omnino aures Pontificis praeoccupandae, quem eo potius nomine novam istam congregationem instituisse credendum est.
units.tr: Nor would the Jesuits have gained the slightest advantage by other tricks, had access to the Apostolic See been open. Therefore every way to it had to be blocked, and the ears of the Pope had to be forestalled by surreptitious means. It must be believed that for this very reason they set up that new congregation.

units.la: DE NEFARIIS FACINORIBVS DE AVTHORITATE SVMMI PONTIFI- CIS à IESVITIS AD SVAS MACHINATIO- NES DETORTA.
units.tr: Of the Heinous Crimes by Which the Jesuits Twisted the Authority of the Supreme Pontiff to Their Own Schemes.

units.la: Multa perperam facta fuisse, Apostolicæ sedis authoritate prætensâ, eoque dignitatis imminutâ, dolendum est, negandum non est. Ne aliquis dubitandi scrupulus Anglis inesset, quinam sint, qui malis informationibus de absentibus uti fuerintausi, inter plurima argumenta, divina providentia, quæ illi sedi assistit, effecit, ut male informato Pontifici aliqui Anglorum præsentes essent.
units.tr: It must be lamented, and cannot be denied, that many things have been done wrongly under the pretended authority of the Apostolic See, and so its dignity has been diminished. Lest any scruple of doubt remain among the English about who it is that has used misinformation about those who are absent, divine providence, which watches over that See among many other arguments, has ensured that some Englishmen were present when the Pontiff was misinformed.

units.la: Quinque Sacerdotibus uno tempore in Angliam profecturis, Dn. Barnabeo, D. Marloo, D. Henfleo, alijfq; duobus, & ad Sanctissimum Dominum nostrum Clementem VIII pro benedictione impetranda adductis, sua sanctitas quæsivit Italicè, an omnes illi quinque cursum studiorum in Seminario absolvissent? Robertus Parsonius Iesuita præsens respondit, absolvisse. Sua sanctitas (mirum dictu) idem petiit Latinè. Ille iterum sine verecundia respondit, omnes absolvisse, idq; Latinè. Ex omnibus autem quinque illis ne unus quidem cursum studiorum absolverat. Sed quid faciendum Sacerdotibus illis, qui modestiæ causa tacendum putabant, & nihil forte expectabant magis, quàm ut ab eo Collegio dimitterentur, in quo diu detenti & vexati fuerant.
units.tr: Five priests were about to set out for England at the same time: Master Barnabeus, Master Marlow, Master Henfield, and two others. They were brought before our Most Holy Lord Clement VIII to obtain his blessing. His Holiness asked in Italian whether all five had completed the course of studies in the Seminary. Robert Parsons the Jesuit, who was present, replied that they had. His Holiness (strange to say) asked the same question in Latin. Parsons again answered without shame that all had completed it, and he answered in Latin. Yet of those five not one had completed the course of studies. What were those priests to do, who thought it fitting, out of modesty, to keep silent, and who perhaps hoped for nothing more than to be dismissed from that college, where they had been long detained and harassed?

units.la: Nec expectadum est, ut ex illo Collegio Anglo-Romano aliquis audeat, aut valeat si auderet, vere Pontificem, aut institutam ab eo congregationem informare; ubi quisq; peius quàm in carcere, secreta custodia mancipatur, non collocuturus cum aliquo secundo, nisi in præsentia tertij exploratoris.
units.tr: Nor is it to be expected that anyone from that Anglo-Roman College would dare, or, if he dared, would be able to, truly inform the Pontiff or the congregation instituted by him. There, each man is held in secret custody, worse than in prison, and will not speak with any second person except in the presence of a third, a spy.

units.la: Qui e Collegio dimittuntur pauci sunt, qui neq; adulationibus, neq; minis credunt. De quibus dubitatur, illi uno vel alio modo præveniuntur. Inter alios D. Tempertus, D. Bennonus, D. Hillus, Româ honorificè dimissi in Belgium venientes, inauditi, & causâ in hunc diem incognitâ, facultatibus à Iesuitis privantur, sic ut nec redire, nec manere, viatico consumpto, nisi mendicando, possent, nec ad munia sacerdotalia, ex quibus etiam vivendum esset, in Angliam proficisci; in quam tamen venientes, capti, & pro fide incarcerati, omnes tres illustres confessores evaserunt.
units.tr: Few of those dismissed from the College are such that they believe neither flattery nor threats. Concerning those who are doubtful, they are forestalled in one way or another. Among others, Master Tempest, Master Bennet and Master Hill, who were honourably dismissed from Rome and were coming to Belgium, were deprived of their faculties by the Jesuits without being heard, and the cause remains unknown to this day. So they could neither return nor remain, their travelling money being spent, except by begging, nor could they set out for England to take up priestly duties, by which they would have had to live. Yet when they came to England, they were seized and imprisoned for the faith, and all three illustrious confessors came through.

units.la: Neminem Româ residere, qui Cleri secularis Anglicani causam apud sedem Apostolicam agat, passi sunt Iesuitæ, cum tamen hospitium Anglis, ab Anglorum Regibus ante 800. annos paratum, detineant.
units.tr: The Jesuits have allowed no one to reside at Rome to conduct the business of the English secular clergy before the Apostolic See, although they keep in their hands the lodging for the English, which the kings of England prepared more than 800 years ago.

units.la: Anglorum extra Angliam, quantum in ijs erat, sustentationem & æstimationem semper Iesuitæ impedierunt, bullam quandam urgentes, ne quis ad Rectoratu promoveretur, veros gradus impediedo pro ijs, qui Pontificis dignitatem tuentur, quem sciunt ab ijs impugnari, qui gradus ut cunq; suscepftos prætendunt, & eò magis, quo gradum altiorem ostentant. Hoc Pontificem bene informatum quis laturum suspicetur? Sed quæ informatio ab hominibus dignitate & sustentatione privatis expectari potest?
units.tr: Outside England, as far as lay in their power, the Jesuits have always hindered the support and esteem of the English, insisting on a certain bull that no one should be promoted to the rectorate, thus blocking genuine degrees for those who defend the dignity of the Pontiff, whom they know to be attacked by those who claim degrees, however obtained, and all the more the higher the degree they display. Who would suppose that the Pontiff, so informed, would bear this? But what information can be expected from men deprived of dignity and support?

units.la: Ex Anglia literæ ad Pontificem difficillime mittuntur, propter agniti primarius Pontificis periculu, præsertim à Sacerdotibus in angulis ædium privatarum, vel carcerum latentibus, afflictis, angustiatis, quibus etiam nuciorum penuria, & portuum observatio bene nota est. Quanta ergo afflictis Sacerdotibus addita afflictio est, quanta injuria sedi Apostolicæ inusta est, quòd literæ à Sacerdotibus Anglis propter eorum negotia urgentissima ad suam sanctitatem, interceptæ non modò fuerint, sed & impune? Quid dico impune? imò, ut ajunt, Pontifice sciente, volente, decernente, imò & latore literarum in Collegio Anglicano, sicut ipsemet refert, sed penes eum fides esse debet, incarcerato, quem etiam Iesuitæ facibus ardentibus adductis torquere minitabantur, nisi narrationibus quibusdà, à Iesuitis confictis, satisfacere subscriberet.
units.tr: Letters from England to the Pontiff are sent with the greatest difficulty, owing to the well-known danger to the Pontiff's own person, especially since the priests, afflicted, distressed and hard pressed, lie hidden in corners of private houses or in prisons, and they are well aware of the shortage of messengers and the watching of the ports. How great, then, was the additional affliction to the afflicted priests, and how great the injury done to the Apostolic See, that letters written by the English priests to His Holiness on their most urgent business were intercepted, and not only intercepted but intercepted with impunity? Why do I say with impunity? Indeed, as they say, with the Pontiff knowing, willing and decreeing it, and even with the bearer of the letters imprisoned in the English College, as he himself reports (but his word must be trusted), and the Jesuits threatened to torture him with blazing torches unless he agreed to satisfy them by signing certain narratives invented by the Jesuits.

units.la: In illis literis significati sunt abusus multi, qui Alano & Caffanenfe mortuis, in Ecclesiam Anglicanam irripere cœperunt. Inter alios recensebantur insolentissimæ quædam propositiones à devotis Iesuitarum absordè probatæ, & postea à Iesuitis absurdus (quod in factionib. eorum usitatum est) defensitatæ. Una erat, prostibula Româ æquè licita esse atq; ipsum Pontificem; alia erat, Sixtum 5. fuisse lupum; in cuius odium priorem forte effuderant. Obiectorum in illis literis, aliisque criminum exemplar Iesuitae in Angliam remittunt, et memoriale Pontifici exhibitum appellarunt. Iesuitarum in Anglia Provincialis Henricus Garnetus in illis literis nec micam veritatis inesse solenniter in literis ad omnes Sacerdotes Anglicanos, protestatus, ut contra illud memoriale manibus subscriptis ferant, rogat, idque ex ordine ab ipso Pontifice, ut scribit, praescripto. Tres formas subscriptionum praefixit: Primam, omnia in memoriali scio falsa esse: Secundam, omnia in memoriali puro falsa esse: Tertiam, omnia in memoriali sunt ab illis, non a me suae sanctitati exhibita. A Sacerdotibus seorsim viventibus, difficillime convenientibus, persecutione horum qui sunt extra Ecclesiam, sed magis tyrannide eorum, qui sunt intra Ecclesiam, ut verela eorum testantur, oppressis; facile erat, aliquas subscriptiones extorquere, quas tamen multi recusarunt. Hoc in lucrum Iesuitis cedebat, quod devotos ab adversariis aeternos farent, et ad omnem eventum subscriptiones extortas, vel ementitas haberent patitas. Nec quemquam verisimile erat postea Pontificem missurum, cum nihil Romae initiatum Iesuitas latere posset.
units.tr: In those letters many abuses were pointed out, which began to creep into the English Church after the deaths of Allen and Caffarensis. Among others were listed some most insolent propositions, absurdly approved by the Jesuits' devoted followers and afterwards defended by the Jesuits (a common practice in their factions). One was that prostitution at Rome is as lawful as the Pontiff himself; another was that Sixtus V was a wolf, against whom they had perhaps poured out their hatred earlier. The Jesuits sent back to England a copy of the charges contained in those letters and of other crimes, and called it a memorial presented to the Pontiff. Henry Garnet, the Jesuit Provincial in England, solemnly declared in letters to all the English priests that there was not a crumb of truth in those letters, and he asks them to bring forward signatures against that memorial, which he says was prescribed to him by the Pontiff himself. He prefixed three forms of signature: the first, I know that everything in the memorial is false; the second, I know that everything in the memorial is purely false; the third, everything in the memorial was presented to His Holiness by them, not by me. The priests lived apart and could meet only with great difficulty, and they were oppressed not so much by the persecution of those outside the Church as by the tyranny of those within it, as their own letters testify. So it was easy to extort some signatures, though many refused. This profited the Jesuits, for they made their devoted followers eternal enemies of their opponents, and so they had, for every outcome, signatures either extorted or falsely obtained. Nor was it likely that the Pontiff would afterwards send anyone, since the Jesuits could not be kept in the dark about anything begun at Rome.

units.la: Quid jam mirabimur, Iesuitas in Anglia Sacerdotibus ad Pontificem missis, praedixisse, exceptionem Romae illos habituros, longe ab illa dissimilem, qua Istrianos schismaticos tractandos censuit noster Apostolus Gregorius Papa.
units.tr: Why should we now be surprised that the Jesuits, when the priests were sent to the Pontiff in England, foretold that they would receive at Rome a reception very unlike that which our Apostle, Pope Gregory, judged should be given to the schismatic Istrians?

units.la: Quid jam mirabimur, temporalia subsidia, gratias spirituales, hierarchiam, et illam consequentia, sacramenta, sacramentaliaque, ipsius denique appellationis beneficia, Ecclesiae Anglicanae denegata? et clero olim tam nobili, et jam tam bene de fide Apostolica merito, infimum quasi gradum Archipresbyteratus, infimo homini (ut nihil gravius dicitur) per surreptionem collatum, praeponi?
units.tr: Why should we now be surprised that temporal aid, spiritual graces, the hierarchy and the things that follow from it, the sacraments and sacramentals, and finally the benefits of appeal itself have been denied to the English Church, and that the lowest step of the archpresbyterate, granted by surreptitious means to the lowest of men (to say nothing more severe), has been placed over a clergy once so noble and so deservedly good for the Apostolic faith?

units.la: Iesuitae in castello de Vuisbich, ut Iesuitae cuidam Guilelmo Vuestono, primatum in clero Anglicano comparant, novum ordinem melioris (si Deo placet) disciplinae inceperunt. Ille novus Ordo inter infinitas scandalosissimas absurditates, quia carebat authoritate Pontificis, a clero reiectus, caussam et praetextum dedit Iesuitis, nihilominus sepationem a Sacerdotibus (quae sub meliori judicio verum schisma putatur) faciendi. Non debebatur postea expediens, ut Iesuitae non larvati primatus ambiretur, clanculariis Iesuitis promovendus erat, et quidem Georgius Balcuuillius aptissimus inventus est. Ex eo tales, et ob quae merita a Iesuitis promoveantur, apparebit.
units.tr: The Jesuits at the castle of Wisbech began a new order of (God willing) better discipline, aiming to secure the primacy among the English clergy for a certain Jesuit, William Weston. That new order, among countless most scandalous absurdities, since it lacked the authority of the Pontiff, was rejected by the clergy; yet it gave the Jesuits a cause and pretext for making a separation from the priests (which on better judgement is regarded as true schism). It was then thought necessary that a non-disguised primacy should be sought, to be secretly promoted by the Jesuits, and George Blackwell was found most suitable for it. From this one may see what kind of men, and for what merits, are promoted by the Jesuits.

units.la: Inter alia multa similia sui Novitiatus exercitia, fecerunt, ut scriberet ad Cardinalem Cajetanum literas, jam cum refutatione impressas. Earum summa erat, Iesuitas in Anglia et alibi male audire, idque verissimum est. Quae sequuntur, in Lucianicas narrationes poni deberent, non esse videlicet Iesuitarum demeritum aliquod, quin potius omnibus illis virtutibus praelucere: aliquam tamen illis invidiam, vel aemulationem conflatam esse, quod valde nobiles essent, et divenditis amplissimis suis patrimoniis, pauperes omnes, inveteratos praecipue, sustentarent, cum tamen per quam exiguum ab illis in pios usus converetur.
units.tr: Among many other similar exercises of their novitiate, they had him write letters to Cardinal Cajetan, already printed with a refutation. The sum of them was that the Jesuits were ill spoken of in England and elsewhere, and this is most true. What follows ought to be placed among the Lucianic narratives: that the Jesuits had no particular demerit, but on the contrary shone with all virtues; yet some envy or rivalry had been stirred against them, because they were very noble, and, having sold their very ample patrimonies, supported all the poor, especially the long-term poor, though very little was turned from them to pious uses.

units.la: Archipresbytero taliter per Cardinalem Cajetanum, sed nomine Pontificis, creato, qui praesum Pontificis consensum expectandum censuerunt, et bullam authenticam in re tanti momenti plus quam necessariam, schismatis postulantur. Ab illis Iesuitae secundam ciunt separationem, vel potius schisma.
units.tr: When an archpriest had been created in this way by Cardinal Cajetan, but in the name of the Pontiff, the Jesuits demanded that the priests, who thought the Pontiff's consent should be awaited, and that an authentic bull in a matter of such importance was more than necessary, were to be treated as schismatics. Against them the Jesuits made a second separation, or rather a schism.

units.la: Archipresbyter post undecim menses per Bullam Pontificis confirmatus, in causa sua cit se esse debere judicem: decrevit dilationem obedientiae illi fiendae ante bullam Pontificis fuisse schismatica. Libellos Iesuitarum, qui Sacerdotes schismaticos esse affirmabat, omnibus convitiis proscindebant, plus quam Pontificia authoritate confirmat: prohibet, ne quis innocentiam suam tueatur, aut Academia Parisiensis decretum defendat, quo expectantes Bullam Pontificiam immunes a schismate declarabantur, authoritatem edi orum, ut Principes, vel canonum, ut Papa, condendorum usurpat. Edicit, ne Sacerdotes inter se de aliqua re, eo inconsulto, tractent, ne dent, vel accipiant suffragia pro ua re, ne veniant, aut scribant ad partes transmarinas. Aperte adhuc non ausus est dicere, Nulli Pontifici, aut Principi, præter Archipresbyterum, obtemperetis. Quid enim secutum est? Sacerdotes propter istas male fani cerebri insolentias, appellationem ad summum Pontificem fecerunt. Exclamant Jesuitæ, Sacerdotes per fubfcriptionem appellationis Archipresbyteri edictum de non dandis vel accipiendis suffragijs, violaffe, non esse dignos, qui ad altare admittantur, non qui domibus excipiantur, imo fame tollendos esse, expressis verbis per totam Angliam inter Catholicos urgebant: hinc tertiam separationem, vel potius schisma à Sacerdotibus fecerunt.
units.tr: The archpriest, confirmed after eleven months by a bull of the Pontiff, claimed that he himself ought to be judge in his own cause, and decreed that the delay in rendering obedience to him before the Pontiff's bull had been schismatic. He had the Jesuits' libels, which declared the priests to be schismatics, torn to pieces with every insult, more than the Pontifical authority would confirm; he forbade anyone to defend his own innocence or to uphold the decree of the University of Paris, by which those awaiting the Pontifical bull were declared free from schism; he usurped the authority of issuing edicts as a prince does, or of enacting canons as the Pope does. He issued an edict that the priests should not discuss any matter among themselves without his consent, nor give or accept votes on any such matter, nor come or write to parts beyond the sea. He has not yet openly dared to say, You are to obey no Pontiff or prince except the archpriest. What followed? Because of these insolences of men of disordered mind, the priests appealed to the Supreme Pontiff. The Jesuits cried out that the priests, by subscribing to the appeal, had violated the archpriest's edict forbidding the giving or accepting of votes, that they were not worthy to be admitted to the altar, nor to be received into houses, and indeed that they should be starved; and they pressed this in express words throughout England among the Catholics. Hence they made a third separation, or rather schism, from the priests.

units.la: Quis crederet eos, qui speciali voto obedire Pontifici tenentur, tria dissidia tam intempestiva, tam illicita, tam supra fidem scandalosa contra illos facturos, quos omni modo adjuvare tenebantur, ea vero de causa utcumque fucata, quod ad authoritatem summi Pontificis in omnibus negotijs Ecclesiasticis, tanquam ad sacram anchoram recurrendum decreverant?
units.tr: Who would believe that those who are bound by a special vow to obey the Pontiff would make three such ill-timed and unlawful divisions, so scandalous to the faith, against those whom they were bound to help in every way, and that they did so for a cause, however specious, that they had resolved to flee to the authority of the supreme Pontiff in all ecclesiastical affairs as to a sacred anchor?

units.la: Sequitur, ut Jesuitarum in Anglia & Scotia molitionum particulares effectus recensentur, & quæ pro incommodis graviter prementibus expectanda remedia.
units.tr: What follows is an account of the particular effects of the Jesuits' machinations in England and Scotland, and of the remedies to be expected for the grievous inconveniences that press upon us.

units.la: DE REGE BRITANNIÆ.
units.tr: ON THE KING OF BRITAIN.

units.la: Rex merito, ut sibi videtur, contra Catholicos nonnullos irritatus, bonis omnibus officijs promerendus est. Libellis, rumoribus, molitionibus seditiosis status temporalis, nullo modo, quod Jesuitæ faciunt, contra religionem irritandus est. Veritatem partim expressam, partim intellectam, magistratus genus quoddam artificiosum mendacij arbitrantur. Illo se deludi in rebus temporalib. ægerrimè ferētes, vix alicui Catholico credendū censent, cum fidelitatē erga Principem profiteatur, vel juramento etiam confirmet. Pecuniam in magna quantitate in alias regiones à Jesuitis transportatam, fisco interceptæ cesserunt, semper, nisi justissima causa appareat, suspiciones dat, authores innaturalia esse Reipub. membra.
units.tr: The King, as he himself thinks, has been justly provoked against some Catholics, and he deserves to be won over by every good office. He must not be provoked against religion in the way the Jesuits provoke him, by libels, rumours and seditious schemes against the temporal state. The magistrates consider that partly expressed and partly understood truth is a certain artful kind of lying. Bitterly resenting that they have been deceived in temporal matters, they think hardly any Catholic should be believed, even when he professes loyalty to the Prince and confirms it with an oath. Whenever large sums of money transported by the Jesuits into other countries have been intercepted by the treasury, they have always, unless the most just cause appears, given cause for suspicion that the authors are unnatural members of the commonwealth.

units.la: DE SEMINARIIS.
units.tr: ON THE SEMINARIES.

units.la: Seminaria Anglicana olim numerosa fuere & florentia: unicum Rhemense uno tempore supra 400. aluit, uno die 80. ad sacros ordines promovit. Libera erat omnium commendatorum admissio, & dispositioni synceritatis Anglicanæ congrua educatio, quæ quales viros ex Anglia Catholica protulerit, Alanus, Saderus, Hardingus, Stapletonus, Martinus & infiniti alij testantur. Multi sub Alano fuere Rectores, viri maturi ex Academiarum spaciis, & Juristarum municipalium hospitijs prodeuntes, benignè excepti & frequenter excitati. Lectiones frequentes erant & doctæ: omnes Christiano zelo ita ad Anglicanam messem anhelabant, ut difficillimè aliqui ad scribendum contra hæreticos, vel legendum, vel confitendum detinerentur.
units.tr: The English seminaries were once numerous and flourishing. The one at Reims alone once supported more than 400 students, and on a single day it promoted 80 to holy orders. Admission was open to all recommended persons, and their education was suited to the sincerity of the English character. What men Catholic England produced from it, Allen, Saunders, Harding, Stapleton, Martin and countless others bear witness. Many under Allen were rectors, mature men who came out of the precincts of the universities and the lodgings of the municipal lawyers, kindly received and frequently stirred up. The lectures were frequent and learned. All burned with Christian zeal for the English harvest, so that it was very hard to keep any of them from writing against the heretics, or from reading or hearing confessions.

units.la: Seminaria, ut nunc sunt sub Jesuitis, vel eorum devotis, nec numerum habent competentem, nec Doctores, nec lectores, nec confessarios ex sæculari clero: viri meliorum notæ, præcipuè in Academijs enutriti, non admittuntur. Qui pueri veniunt, in Seminarijs cursum Solis (ut appellant) studiorum absolventes, non possunt evadere viri maturi, & profligandis hæresibus pares. Scripturas non exactè callent: Patres non versant. ant, antiquitatis monimenta non terunt: linguarum sufficientem cognitionem non adiifcuntur: varia lectio scriptoribus & concionatoribus, quorum magna simul est penuia, & lectoribus necessaria, non attingitur: haeresis ipsa, nova quasi hydra capita indies emittens non exploratur: tempus deest eis studijs: mutuis explorationibus, fufurationibus, factionibus optima ingenia franguntur: nec inter istas incommoditates, forte unus ex clero seculari assignari poterit, qui cursum studiorum jam per viginti annorum spatium absolvit.
units.tr: Seminaries as they now are, under the Jesuits or their dependants, have neither a suitable number of students nor teachers, lecturers or confessors drawn from the secular clergy. Men of better reputation, especially those brought up in the universities, are not admitted. The boys who come in, finishing the course of studies they call the Sol in the seminaries, cannot grow into mature men equal to crushing heresies. They do not thoroughly master the Scriptures; they do not engage with the Fathers; they do not wear down the records of antiquity; they do not acquire a sufficient knowledge of languages; the varied reading that writers and preachers need, and of which there is great scarcity, is not attained by the readers; heresy itself, sending out new heads like a hydra every day, is not investigated; there is no time for these studies; the finest talents are broken by mutual spying, whispering and factions. And among these disadvantages one could hardly point to a single man from the secular clergy who has now completed the course of studies over a span of twenty years.

units.la: In Collegio Romano decem fuerunt sub Iesuitis scandalosissimi tumultus. Ex eo collegio litera ad Pontificem missae sunt a studentibus in haec verba: Collegium nostrum astrum foris, carcer intus, &c. Ex eo Collegio Sacerdotes Dei vincti fuerunt in plateis Romanis. Ex eo Collegio non nominanda infamia sub educatione Iesuitica, in gentem Anglicanam, in sacerdotalem ordinem, adeoque in ipsum nomen Christianum redundavit. Ex hoc Collegio & alijs sub Iesuitis, proditiones, delationes, sycophantia, adulationes in pueris inceptae, ad omnes Angliae partes permanarunt. Nemo insignis explorator & peruitiosus, qui non fuerit sub Iesuitis educatus. Ante venientem & praevalentem Iesuitarum coetum, non audita fuerunt in Anglia libellorum famosorum, seditionum, infidiorum, detractionum nomina: nemo nisi post eos sacerdotium suum inficiatus est, e arcere contra datam fidem aufugit, mendacij publice convictus est, aut a religione publice postatavit.
units.tr: In the Roman College there were ten scandalous uproars under the Jesuits. From that college a letter was sent to the Pope by the students, in these words: "Our college is a star outside, a prison within," and so on. From that college priests of God were bound and paraded through the streets of Rome. From that college, and from others under the Jesuits, came an infamy not to be named, which rebounded upon the English nation, upon the priestly order, and so upon the very name of Christian. From this college and the others under the Jesuits, betrayals, informing, sycophancy and flattery, begun in boys, spread through every part of England. There is no notorious and pernicious spy who was not educated under the Jesuits. Before the Jesuit company came in and gained the upper hand, the names of defamatory libels, sedition, treachery and slander were unheard of in England. No one, except after their coming, has defiled his priesthood, fled from the stronghold against the faith given to him, been publicly convicted of lying, or publicly apostatised from religion.

units.la: In Seminarijs Hispanicis, omnes honestioris vitae, & melioris judicij ad ordinem santi Benedicti fere transierunt, non obstantibus infinitis calumnijs contra illum ordinem, & alios omnes in Ecclesia approbatos, praeter suum, a Iesuitis insusurratis.
units.tr: In the Spanish seminaries, almost all men of more honourable life and better judgement have passed over to the order of St Benedict, despite the endless slanders against that order and all the others approved in the Church, whispered in by the Jesuits, apart from their own.

units.la: Duacense seminarium multis in Anglia Scholis Grammaticalibus splendore, doctrina & actionum morali bonitate cedet. Per factionem admissi, blanditijs, fastoribus, minis ad Iesuiticum alliciuntur, si consenserint, extrema indignissima paralitate foventur, donec tandem inferuescente juvenili impetu Iesuitismi poeniteat. Qui aperte nolunt ad Iesuiticum transire, ergastula potius, quam Collegia expeuntur.
units.tr: The seminary at Douai yields to none of the English grammar schools in splendour, learning and moral goodness of conduct. Those admitted through faction are enticed to Jesuitism by flattery, flatteries and threats; if they consent, they are cherished with the most unworthy and extreme indulgence, until at last, when youthful zeal cools, they regret their Jesuitism. Those who openly refuse to pass over to Jesuitism are thrust out into prisons rather than colleges.

units.la: Restituantur necesse est Seminarijs, si inde conversio Britanniae expectetur, doctrina & morum maturitas. Viri apti scribendo contra haereticos, & docendo aos, si inveniri possunt, destinentur. Academici, & melioris educationis viri, non modo syncera humanitate in seminarijs excipiendi sunt, si veniant, sed ut veniant, sunt provocandi. Quod non nisi per Academicos mutua familiaritate notos sibimet fieri oteft, ut sub Alano experientia docuit. Iesuitis non amotis e Collegijs, nihil boni sperandum est, &c. Haec omnia Monachi & Cleri Anglicani de Iesuitis.
units.tr: If a conversion of Britain is to be looked for, the seminaries must necessarily be restored to doctrine and maturity of character. Men fit to write against heretics and to teach the young should be sent there, if they can be found. Scholars and men of better education should not only be received into the seminaries with sincere kindness, if they come, but should be urged to come. This can be done only through the scholars who are known to one another through mutual familiarity, as experience taught under Allen. Unless the Jesuits are removed from the colleges, nothing good is to be hoped for, and so on. All these things the monks and the English clergy say of the Jesuits.

units.la: IN SCOTIA QVID ACTVM à IESVITIS.
units.tr: In Scotland, what the Jesuits did there.

units.la: REx Hispaniarum haud diu post mortem Mariae Reginae Scotiae Parmensi Gubernatori in Belgio mandarat, suo nomine Regi Scotiae pecunias & exercitum adversus Reginam Angliae promitteret, ut eo facilius matris mortem ulcisci posset. Ea de causa Parmesis nobilem Scotum, Robertum de Brusse, qui iuventute apud Iesuitas educatus fuerat, in Scotiam multa cum pecunia ablegavit. Eodem tempore advenit etiam in Scotiam iussu Sixti 5. Pont. Rom. Dublain Episcopus, qui Infatam Hispanicam Scotiae Regi in matrimonium offerret, sed ea conditione, ut Romanam Religionem amplecti vellet. In huius Episcopi comitatu fuit etiam Guilelmus Creichton, qui Lugduni aliquandiu Rector in Iesuitarum Collegio fuerat. Repulsam autem passus Episcopus consilio, virtute & fidelitate Iohannis Metelani Magni Cancellarij Scotiae, qui Regi suadebat, sibi ab huiusmodi dolis & fallacibus promissis caveret, domum reversus est. Mansit autem in Scotia Creichtonus Iesuita, & Bruffeo sese iunxit, eique persuadere conatus est, ut Cancellarium obtruncaret, quod molitionibus Iesuiticis, eorumque parricidijs vel solus resisteret. Ad quae Bruffeus totus exhorruit, eiusque postulatis iniquis & crudelibus prorsus consentire noluit. Hortatur igitur Iesuita Bruffeum, det ergo 1500. coronatos, quos a Parmensi accepisset, tribus nobilibus, qui in necem Cancellarij coniurarint. Sed nec hoc quidem persuadere ei potuit, inquiens, unum & idem esse, sive quis sua manu interficiat aliquem, sive pecunia conducat alium ad caedem faciendam. Cum ergo nullis rationibus expugnari posset, accusat eum Creichto Iesuita, apud Fuentem Parmensis successorem, quod pecunias a Parmensi acceptas dilapidasset, & in alios usus converterit. Comprehenditur miser Bruffeus, in carcerem coniicitur, & menses quatuordecim in eo detinetur, tandem liberatur, Iesuita autem impunitus evadit.
units.tr: Not long after the death of Queen Mary of Scotland, the King of Spain had instructed the Governor of Parma in Belgium to promise, in his name, money and an army to the King of Scotland against the Queen of England, so that he might more easily avenge his mother's death. For this reason Parma sent a noble Scot, Robert de Bruce, who had been educated among the Jesuits, into Scotland with a large sum of money. At the same time, by order of Pope Sixtus V, the Bishop of Dublin also came into Scotland, to offer the Spanish Infanta in marriage to the King of Scotland, but on the condition that he would embrace the Roman religion. In the bishop's company was also William Crichton, who had for some time been Rector of the Jesuit College at Lyons. The bishop, however, met with a rebuff, through the counsel, courage and loyalty of John Maitland, the Lord Chancellor of Scotland, who advised the King to beware of such deceits and treacherous promises; and so he returned home. Crichton the Jesuit, however, remained in Scotland, joined himself to Bruce, and tried to persuade him to cut down the Chancellor, since he alone stood in the way of the Jesuit schemes and their murders. At this Bruce shrank back in horror, and utterly refused to consent to their unjust and cruel demands. The Jesuit therefore urged Bruce to give the 1500 crowns which he had received from Parma to three noblemen who had conspired to kill the Chancellor. But he could not even persuade him to do this, the Jesuit saying that it made no difference whether someone killed a man with his own hand or hired another to do the slaying with money. Since he could therefore not be overcome by any arguments, the Jesuit Crichton accused him before Fuentes, Parma's successor, of having squandered the money received from Parma and of having turned it to other uses. The wretched Bruce was seized, thrown into prison, and kept there for fourteen months; at last he was released, but the Jesuit escaped unpunished.

units.la: DE TVRBIS IN PATAVINA ACADE- MIA, TVM INTER VENETOS ET PAVLVM V. PON- TIFICEM ROMANVM A IESVITIS EXCITATIS.
units.tr: ON THE DISTURBANCE IN THE PADUAN ACADEMY, WHEN THE JESUITS STIRRED UP A QUARREL BETWEEN THE VENETIANS AND POPE PAUL V

units.la: CVM Iesuitae Patavij, & alibi passim publicas in suis Collegijs Lectiones habere, & hoc modo studiosam iuventutem ad se pertrahere conarentur, gravis ea de causa inter ipsos & Academiam contentio exorta est. Tandem Academia illius loci de novatione ista apud Magistratum Venetum Anno 1591. admodum conquesta est, & per delegatum suum Caesarem Cremoninum haec talia proponi ipsi curavit; quod nimirum Iesuitae privata quadam authoritate, contra Academiae illius leges ac consuetudinem antiquam & approbatam, peculiare quodpiam Collegium seu Anticollegium potius occulto, sub Pontificiarum quarundam a Superioribus in Republ. Veneta, tanquam a Magistratu suo legitimo, nondum approbatarum seu confirmatarum Bullarum praetextu, introduxerint: unde contentiones inter studiosos per quam multas & varias excitarent; eoque non celeberrimae tantum Academiae despectus haud ferendus, sed ipsis etiam Iesuitarum discipulis illis putativis ab ineptis istis Praeceptoribus maius detrimentum, quam emolumentum accederet. Rogare itaque se, ut Anticollegium istud temerarie nec non clandestine contra leges institutum abrogetur. Ad quos Magistratus ille eiusdem Anni 1591. die Decemb. 23. rescripsit & decrevit ita: Nostra haec est sententia ac voluntas, ut Lectiones, nisi inter sese & apud aliquas classes sive loci suos, habeant omnino nullas; ut in ... tum ac Privilegijs Academiae Patavinae neutiquam adversentur.
units.tr: When the Jesuits at Padua, and in many other places, tried to give public lectures in their colleges and so draw the studious youth to themselves, a serious dispute arose on this account between them and the University. In 1591 the University of that place complained bitterly about this innovation before the Venetian magistrate, and through its delegate Caesar Cremoninus it had the following put to them: that the Jesuits, by a private authority of their own and contrary to the laws of that Academy and its old and approved custom, had secretly introduced a special college, or rather an anti-college, under the pretext of certain papal bulls sent by their superiors, which had not yet been approved or confirmed by the Venetian Republic, their lawful magistrate. From this, they said, arose very many and varied quarrels among the students; and so not only was contempt for this most famous Academy something not to be borne, but the so-called pupils of the Jesuits also suffered more harm than good from those inept teachers. They therefore asked that this anti-college, rashly and clandestinely set up against the laws, be abolished. To this the magistrate replied and decreed on 23 December of the same year 1591 as follows: This is our opinion and will, that they have no lectures at all, except among themselves and in certain classes or their own places; and that they in no way be adverse to ... and to the privileges of the Academy of Padua.

units.la: CONTROVERSIA INTER VENETOS ET PAVLVM V. EXORTA IESVITIS AVTHORIBVS.
units.tr: THE CONTROVERSY BETWEEN THE VENETIANS AND PAUL V, STIRRED UP BY THE JESUIT AUTHORS.

units.la: ANNO vero 1605. inter Venetos, & Paulum V. Pontificem Romanum gravissima & periculosissima intercessit Controversia, super Constitutionibus quibusdam, quarum renovandarum occasionem Senatui Veneto Iesuitarum artes & dolí testamentarij praebuerunt. Cùm enim Ecclesiastici, maximè verò Iesuitæ Venetiis hactenus multa aedificia, & bona alia mobilia, & immobilia, tam in urbe, quàm extra eam sita, ad sese sub titulo testamentorum, aliorumque gatorum, variis technis & molitionibus pertraxissent, & verò bonis spiritualibus adnumerata, ita iam possidere inciperent, ut tributi inde ad magistratum oliticum nihil amplius, vel parum admodum rediret, Magistratus Venetus, cum Reipubl. detrimento maximo ditescerent, lege cavendum & in eos maiore animadvertendum censuit.
units.tr: In the year 1605, however, a most grave and dangerous controversy arose between the Venetians and Paul V, the Roman Pontiff, concerning certain constitutions, the occasion of renewing which was furnished to the Venetian Senate by the arts and deceitful wiles of testators on the part of the Jesuits. For when the ecclesiastics, and most of all the Jesuits, had hitherto drawn to themselves, in Venice, many buildings and other movable and immovable goods, both within the city and situated outside it, under the title of wills and other gifts, by various devices and contrivances, and had counted them among spiritual goods, so that they began to possess them in such a way that little or nothing more came back from them in taxes to the civil magistrate, the Venetian magistrate, since they were growing rich to the very great detriment of the Commonwealth, judged that they must be checked by law and that severer measures must be taken against them.

units.la: Iuvat hoc loco non mea verba adscribere, sed Cl. V. Hieronymi Vendramini Sacerdotis & Theologi Veneti, pro Serenissima Venetorum Republ. ad Cardinalium Román. Collegium. Triginta decies, inquit, centena millia, & amplius Ecclesiasticorum bona ac facultates, aestimantur valere sub Venetae ditionis Imperio. Et quidem, quocumque te Venetiis, vel alibi in toto Veneto Dominio conferas, aedificia quae cumque, praedia, agros, domos & cetera huiusmodi meliora, pulchriora ac magnitudine conspexeris, illa Ecclesiasticorum esse certò scias.
