Quod si ex urbe Veneta solùm & agro extrahas templa, aedificia, bona, facultates Patriarcharum, Episcoporum, Abbatum, Archipresbyterorum, plebanorum, presbyterorum, Monasteriorum, Hospitalium, Ecclesiarum & caeterorum huiusmodi, quae temporibus, quibus Veneta Resp. coepta est, vel prorsus nulla extabant, vel certè admodum pauca, illaque omnia simul in unum locum conferas: ac seorsim quidem templa, domos, aedificia, & cetera huiusmodi opera ponas: seorsim verò praedia, agros, rura, hortos, & similia; quid obsecro Venetorum civitas ac dominium erunt cum his collata? Illa certè urbs maxima erunt, haec verò vicus & provincia per quam angusta apparent: & tamen Ecclesiastica illa omnia, vel plura certè Venetae Reip. subditorum erant, ac proinde Veneta: Principes enim in subditorum suorum bona jus aliquod habent. Necessario igitur Reip. Venetae Patribus his malis medendum, ac legibus cavendum fuit, ne contra itae suae rationem, & Christi Servatoris Domini institutum Ecclesiastici viri tandem omnia saecularia occupent, ac possideant. Hucusque Vendramenus.
units.tr: Here it is worth citing not my own words but those of the distinguished Hieronymus Vendramin, priest and theologian of Venice, written on behalf of the most serene Venetian Republic to the College of Roman Cardinals. "Three hundred and ten thousand, or more," he says, "is the estimated value of the goods and resources of the ecclesiastics under the rule of the Venetian dominion." And indeed, wherever you go in Venice or elsewhere in the whole Venetian territory, you may be certain that whatever buildings, estates, fields, houses and other such things of finer quality, beauty and size you see belong to the ecclesiastics. But if you take out of the city and countryside of Venice alone the churches, buildings, goods and resources of the patriarchs, bishops, abbots, archpriests, parish priests, presbyters, monasteries, hospitals, churches and all such things, which at the time the Venetian Commonwealth began either did not exist at all or were certainly very few, and gather all of them together into one place; and, setting apart the churches, houses, buildings and other such works, you set apart the estates, fields, farmland, gardens and the like; what, I ask you, will the city and dominion of Venice be when compared with these? Those would be a very great city, while these would appear as a village and a province, quite narrow. And yet all those ecclesiastical possessions, or at least most of them, belonged to subjects of the Venetian Commonwealth, and therefore were Venetian; for princes have some right over the goods of their subjects. Therefore the Fathers of the Venetian Commonwealth had necessarily to remedy these evils and provide by law, lest, contrary to the purpose of their state and the institution of Christ our Saviour and Lord, ecclesiastical men should at last occupy and possess all secular things. Thus far Vendramin.

units.la: Iesuitae verò hoc indignissime ferentes, totum hoc negotium Romam ad Paulum V. perscripserunt.
units.tr: The Jesuits, however, took this most indignantly and wrote the whole matter to Paul V at Rome.

units.la: Compellati igitur hoc nomine à Pontifice, Veneti iure suo cedere noluerunt, sed protestati sunt, sibi in ditione sua supremam iurisdictionem, & sic etiam legum ferendarum potestatem, non autem Pontifici competere, &c. Hoc responso accepto, Pontifex Excommunicationis fulmine eos territat.
units.tr: Accordingly, being called to account on this score by the Pontiff, the Venetians were unwilling to yield their right, but protested that supreme jurisdiction in their dominion, and thus also the power of enacting laws, belonged to themselves and not to the Pontiff, etc. On receiving this reply, the Pontiff terrified them with the thunderbolt of excommunication.

units.la: Vbi notanda summa iniquitas & iniustitia huius Pontificis: paulò ante illum Clemens 8. lege quoque cavit, ne Deiparae Lauretanae Domus, qua Papistis nihil toto terrarum orbe sanctius, valeat deinceps, aut emere, aut acquirere privatorum hominum agros vel bona, propter easdem causas, quae Venetos etiam ad idem statuendum impulerunt. Conciliari haec non possunt. Idem omnino statuunt & decernunt Veneti & Pont. Rom. Pontificis decreta sancta & inviolata: Venetorum autem blasphemiae & anathemata iudicantur.
units.tr: Here the great iniquity and injustice of this Pontiff is to be noted. Shortly before him Clement VIII also provided by law that the House of the Lauretan Mother of God, than which nothing is holier to the Papists anywhere in the world, should not henceforth be able either to buy or to acquire the fields or goods of private persons, for the same reasons which also moved the Venetians to decree the same thing. These cannot be reconciled. The Venetians and the Roman Pontiff decree exactly the same thing; the decrees of the Pontiff are holy and inviolable, but the Venetians' acts are judged blasphemies and anathemas.

units.la: Dux verò & Senatus contrá Excommunicationem illam decreto publico pro iniqua, iniusta & omnino nulla decrevit, quippe quae tanquam brutum aliquod ulmen, sine iure & legibus conceptum, aërem tantum feriat.
units.tr: The Doge and Senate, however, in response to that excommunication, by public decree declared it iniquitous, unjust and altogether null, since it was conceived, like some senseless elm, without right and laws, and strikes only the air.

units.la: Quia verò Decretum hoc dignum est, ut in rei huius sempiternam memoriam ad posteritatem transmittatur, id hoc loco ex Italico idiomate in Latinum fideliter translatum, adscribam, & de verbo ad verbum sic habet. LEONARDVS DONATVS, Dei gratia Dux Venetiarum, &c. Reverendissimis Patriarchis, Archiepiscopis, Episcopis totius Domini nostri Veneti: & Vicariis, Abbatibus, Prioribus, Rectoribus Ecclesiarum Parochialium, & aliis Prælatis Ecclesiasticis Salutem. Ad notitiam nostram pervenit, die 17. Aprilis nuper præteriti, de jussu & sententia Sanctissimi Patris Pauli Papæ V. publicatum & affixum fuisse Romæ BREVE quoddam fulminatum contra Nos, & Senatum ac Dominium nostrum, directum ad vos, eius tenoris & argumenti, quod in eo continetur.
units.tr: Since this decree is worthy of being handed down to posterity in perpetual memory of this affair, I shall here add it, faithfully translated from the Italian into Latin, and it reads word for word thus: LEONARDO DONATO, by the grace of God Doge of Venice, etc., to the most reverend Patriarchs, Archbishops, Bishops of our whole Venetian dominion, and to the Vicars, Abbots, Priors, Rectors of the parish churches, and other ecclesiastical prelates, greeting. It has come to our notice that on the 17th day of April last past, by the order and decision of the most holy Father Pope Paul V, there was published and posted at Rome a certain brief thundered against us, and against our Senate and dominion, addressed to you, of the tenor and purport contained in it.

units.la: Quapropter cum devinctos nos esse consideremus ad conservandum in quiete & tranquillitate statum nostrum nobis ad gubernandum a Deo datum, utque vindicemus & defendamus authoritatem Principis, qui in rebus temporalibus alium superiorem, præter Divinam Majestatem non agnoscit: præsentibus his nostris literis coram Deo & toto Mundo protestamur, nos non intermisisse omnibus possibilibus uti, quibus sanctitatem suam validissimam nostrarum & indissolubilium rationum capacem redderemus: & primum quidem per Oratorem nostrum apud S.S. residentem: postea vero per literas nostras responsorias ad Brevia ipsius nobis scripta: & tandem per Oratorem expressum, in hunc finem & missum.
units.tr: Wherefore, since we consider that we are bound to keep in peace and tranquillity the state which God has given us to govern, and to vindicate and defend the authority of a Prince who in temporal matters acknowledges no superior besides the Divine Majesty, by these our present letters we protest before God and the whole world that we have not ceased to use every possible means by which we might render His Holiness capable of our most valid and indissoluble reasons: first indeed through our Ambassador residing with His Holiness; afterwards through our letters in reply to his briefs written to us; and finally through an express ambassador sent for this very purpose.

units.la: Verum quum animad verterimus SS. aures occlusas, & Breve istud publicatum esse contra formam omnis rationis, & contra id, quod docet sacra Scriptura, doctrina Sanctorum Patrum, & sacri Canones, in præjudicium authoritatis secularis concessæ nobis a Deo, & libertatis status nostri, cum perturbatione possessionis quietæ, quam, per gratiam divinam, sub dominio nostro fideles nostri subditi possidet, bonorum, honoris, vitæ ipsorum, nec non cuiuscumque universali & gravissimo omnium hominum: idcirco nullo modo dubitamus prædictum Breve habere, ac censere non tantum pro injusto ac indebito, sed etiam pro nullo, & tali, quod sit pretij plane nullius, & ita pro invalido, irrito, & illegitime fulminato, ac de facto, nullo juris ordine servato, ut indignum atque inconveniens judicaverimus uti contra illud remedijs, quibus Majores nostri, & alij Principes supremi contra Pontifices usi sunt: qui dum potestate sua ipsis a Deo data uti deberent ad ædificationem, terminos transgressi sunt: maxime cum certissimus, illum a vobis & aliis nostris subditis fidelibus, adeoque mundo toto pro tali censeri & reputari: in certissimam spem venientes, fore, ut quemadmodum hactenus fidelem curam gesistis animarum subditorum nostrorum fidelium, & cultus divini, qui studio vestrum floret in hoc statu nostro, si quisquam alius, ita in posterum etiam officium illud pastorale continuetis: siquidem certo constituimus perseverare in sancta fide Catholica & Apostolica, inque observatione sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ, perinde ac Majores nostri a principio fundationis urbis huius ad præsens per divinam gratiam perseverarunt. Volumus autem, ut præsentes hæ literæ, quo ab unoquoque intelligantur, affigantur in locis publicis Civitatis huius nostræ & aliarum dominio nostro subditarum: sperantes, si tam publicationem adeo manifestam, perventuram ad aures omnium, qui prænominati Brevis cognitionem habuere, & perventuram etiam ad aures Sanctitatis suæ: cui, oramus, ut Dominus Deus noster inspiret gratiam, qua cognoscat Brevis iistius nullitatem & aliorum factorum contra Nos institutorum; & postquam justitiam causæ nostræ cognoverit nobis augeat animum ad præstandum reverentiam erga sanctam sedem Apostolicam: cuius Nos & antecessores nostri una cum hac Republ. semper fuimus & erimus devotissimi. Datum in Ducali nostro Palatio ad 6. diem Maij Indict. 4. Anno 1606.
units.tr: But since we have perceived that the ears of His Holiness were closed, and that this brief was published contrary to the form of all reason and contrary to what holy Scripture, the teaching of the holy Fathers and the sacred canons teach, to the prejudice of the secular authority granted to us by God and of the liberty of our state, with disturbance of the quiet possession which, by the grace of God, our faithful subjects enjoy under our dominion, of their goods, honour and lives, as well as of the universal and most grave interest of all men: therefore we by no means doubt that the said brief is to be held and judged not only unjust and undue, but also null, and of such a kind as to be of plainly no value, and thus invalid, void, and illegitimately thundered forth, and in fact, with no order of law observed; so that we have judged it unworthy and unsuitable to use against it those remedies which our forefathers and other supreme princes have used against Pontiffs, who, when they ought to use the power given them by God for building up, have overstepped the bounds. Especially since we come to the most certain hope that it will be regarded and reckoned by you and our other faithful subjects, and so by the whole world, as such; that just as hitherto you have carried on the faithful care of the souls of our faithful subjects and of divine worship, which flourishes in this our state through your zeal as much as anywhere else, so in future also you will continue that pastoral office; since we are firmly resolved to persevere in the holy Catholic and Apostolic faith and in observance of the holy Roman Church, just as our forefathers have persevered from the beginning of the founding of this city until the present, by divine grace. We wish, moreover, that these present letters be posted in public places of this our city and of the other places subject to our dominion, so that they may be understood by everyone; hoping that such a publication, so manifest, will reach the ears of all who have known of the aforesaid brief, and will also reach the ears of His Holiness; to whom we pray that our Lord God may inspire grace, by which he may recognise the nullity of this brief and of the other acts instituted against us; and that, having come to know the justice of our cause, he may increase our spirit to show reverence towards the holy Apostolic See, of which we and our predecessors, together with this Republic, have always been and shall be most devoted. Given in our Ducal Palace on the 6th day of May, Indiction 4, in the year 1606.

units.la: Iacobus Girardus Secret.
units.tr: Iacobus Girardus, Secretary.

units.la: Hoc decreto publicato, Serenissimus Dux & Senatus Clerum etiam suum convocant, & ius Reipubl. eidem exponunt, Pontificiæque Excommunicationis iniquitatem demonstrant, eumque pro authoritate hortantur, ut curato suo officio Excommunicationem Papalem pro nulla habeat, &c. Clerus antiquus adhæc unanimiter.
units.tr: After this decree was published, the Most Serene Doge and Senate also summoned their own clergy, expounded to them the rights of the Republic, and demonstrated the injustice of the Papal excommunication. They urged them, by their authority, to carry out their office and to regard the Papal excommunication as null, and so on. The old clergy unanimously agreed.

units.la: Decreto Reipub. Veneto unà cum Clero omnes subscribunt exceptis Jesuitis. ianimi consensu Reip. causam contra Pontificem probat, & de fide sua prolixé disputat. Hæc in luce libros præclarissimos ediderunt aliquot Clerici, in quibus partim Iesuitarum technæ & Sinonicæ artes detegūtur, & graphicè depingūntur, partim vero potestas Papæ in temporalibus solidè & sacris literis conuenienter impugnatur. Inter hos cumprimis egregiam operam studiumq; nauare doclissimus ille & omni literatura excultissimus ac expolitissimus P A V L V S V E N E T V S, quem honoris causa nomino, cuius Tractatus de Interdicto Papæ, & Considerationes seu animadversiones in Censuras Papales, & Apologia aduersus Bellarminum Principem obtinent; una cum Declaratione rationum, quibus permota Serenissima Resp. Papæ Paulo V. sese masculè oppo suit, & Antonio Quirino Senatore ibidem in lucem edita.
units.tr: All the clergy, except the Jesuits, subscribed to the decree of the Venetian Republic. With unanimous consent they approved the Republic's cause against the Pontiff and argued at length for their own faith. Several clergymen have since published most distinguished books, in which the artifices and Sinon-like tricks of the Jesuits are partly uncovered and vividly portrayed, and the power of the Pope in temporal matters is partly attacked solidly and fittingly from Holy Scripture. Among these, the most learned man, PAUL OF VENICE, who is cultured and polished in every branch of literature, whom I name out of respect, has devoted especial labour and zeal. His Treatise on the Papal Interdict, his Considerations or Animadversions on the Papal Censures, and his Apology against Cardinal Bellarmine are highly regarded, together with the Declaration of the reasons by which the Most Serene Republic, moved to resist, manfully opposed itself to Pope Paul V, which was published by the Senator Antonio Quirini.

units.la: Sed bonus Paulus pessimam hoc ipso a Iesuitis iniuriam gratiam, qui se ulciscí, & iurias suas, quas ita vocabant, modis omnibus persequi statuerunt. Conduxerunt igitur & pecunia corruperunt Ridolfum Pomam, & Michaelem Viti sacerdotem, cum duobus aliis Anconā & Florentinā oriundis, quorum alter Alexander, alter vero Iohannes vocabatur; hi adoriuntur 5. Octob. anno 1607 patrem Paulum Venetum, eumq; opprimere, Assassinorum more, in pōte de Ponte Forsca tentarunt, quod eorum conatibus vehementer resisteret, & parum abfuit, quin illum stiletis seu pugionibus suis interemisserunt; latrones autem fugā elapsi sunt.
units.tr: But good Paul suffered the worst injury from the Jesuits for this very reason. They resolved to take revenge and to pursue by every means what they called their wrongs. Therefore they hired and bribed Ridolfo Poma and Michele Viti, a priest, together with two others, natives of Ancona and Florence, named Alessandro and Giovanni. On 5 October 1607 these men set upon Father Paul of Venice and tried to crush him in the manner of assassins on the Ponte de Ponte Forsca. Since he resisted their attempts vigorously, they came very close to killing him with their stilettos or daggers. The villains, however, escaped by flight.

units.la: Recentiores vero Religiosi, nempe Iesuitæ, Capucini & Tolendini, quorum regulæ praesentis temporis conditioni accommodatae sunt, Reipub. causam damnant, & contra mandatum Senatus Ecclesiastica sua officia occlusis semper terris peragentes, varia molìri, & plebem ad seditionem excitare visi sunt. Fecerunt autem hoc Iesuitæ non aliam ob causam, quam quod viderent, se, stante & sensa Reipubl. Venetæ libertate, stantibusq; legibus, nec stare, nec instituti sinem obtinere posse.
units.tr: More recent religious orders, namely the Jesuits, the Capuchins and the Theatines, whose rules have been adapted to the present age, condemned the Republic's cause. Contrary to the Senate's order, they carried out their ecclesiastical duties with the doors always shut, and they were seen to be devising various schemes and stirring the common people to sedition. The Jesuits did this for no other reason than that they saw that, while the liberty of the Venetian Republic and its laws remained in force, they could neither stand nor achieve the end of their institute.

units.la: Dux itaque & Senatus Venetus ut malis omnibus mature obviam irent, Iesuitas omnes ex urbe & ditione sua tota dimittendos edicto nouo in æternum censuerunt, & spem omnem ipsis redeundi futuris temporibus præcidérunt; parentum quoq; omnium omnes omnino liberos, qui in ea ditione fuerunt, e Scholis & amplexibus Iesuiticis, ne diutius inficiantur, auulsos domum sudentissimè reuocarunt.
units.tr: Therefore the Doge and Senate of Venice, to meet all these evils promptly, decreed by a new edict that the Jesuits should be dismissed from the city and its whole territory for ever, and they cut off all hope of their return in future times. They also most earnestly recalled home all the children of all parents in that territory, who had been taken from the Jesuit schools and embraces, so that they might no longer be infected.

units.la: Maij igitur 1 o. anno 1606. Iesuitæ cum vestimentis, lectulisque & necessaria suppellectile, conscensis navigijs ex urbe Mediolanum versus discesserunt. Post illorum discessum, in Iesuitarum Collegium Canonici ad D. Marcum inducti sunt, Monachis, quos Reformatos vocant, aliorum Collegia occupantibus. Franciscani vero Monachi, quorum maxima ibi frequentia est, neque aliqua se Collegia sua deserturos, quod iustam Veneti aduersus Pontificem tuerentur causam, aperte professi sunt. Atq; ita Iesuitæ Papæ Excommunicationem & tyrannidem ipsi causæ æquitati prætulerunt.
units.tr: Therefore on 10 May 1606 the Jesuits, with their clothes, bedding and necessary household goods, went on board ships and departed from the city towards Milan. After their departure, canons were brought into the Jesuit college of St Mark, while monks whom they call Reformed occupied other colleges. The Franciscan monks, who are very numerous there, openly declared that they would not abandon their colleges, since they upheld the just cause of the Venetians against the Pontiff. And so the Jesuits preferred the Pope's excommunication and tyranny to the very justice of the cause.

units.la: Vt autem his quæ hucusque diximus deturbis a Iesuitis Venetijs excitatis aior fides habeatur, neve Iesuitæ aliquid in hac tota narratione fictum a me fe calumnientur, adscribam quaedam ex literis ad nos a viro graui & patriæ amatissimo ex Italia scriptis, in quibus superiora omnia, sed breviter confirmantur: Illa autem sic de verbo ad verbum habent.
units.tr: So that what we have said so far about the disturbances stirred up by the Jesuits at Venice may be believed, and lest the Jesuits accuse me of inventing anything in this whole account, I will add some passages from a letter written to us from Italy by a serious man who loves his country greatly. In it all the things above are confirmed, though briefly. The letter reads word for word as follows:

units.la: Postquam publicatum fuit interdictum Pont. Pauli V. contra urbem & statum Veneti huncfine, ut subditi si priuarentur exercitio religionis tumultus excitarent, & obid Ses itus ad ipsis gratificandū copellerētur: deliberatum fuit imperandū esse omni religiosis, in quacunq; Ecclesia continuaretur exercitium consuetum diuinum sine nouitate illa. Pro è obtemperatum fuit ab omnibus: & nominatim Iesuitæ responderunt, quod & ipsi diuinū cultum continuarent: verum interim per civitatem spargebant, quod publice Missam dicere abstineant. Hoc cum cognovissent Magistratus, ipsi ad diem 9. Maij, Anno 1606 accersiti fuerunt, ut certò ab ipsis cognosceretur, quidnam tandem animi ipsis esset: & admoniti, ut Principis mandatum in ministerio suo exequerentur: ipsi se missam posse dicere negabant promissioni quandoquidem hoc suae non adversetur. Missam enim sub nomine officiorum divinorum non comprehendi. Hoc cognito deliberatum fuit a Senatu, ut Patriarchalis Vicarius ablegaretur, qui res Ecclesiae ipsorum consignaret, & mandatum darent Iesuitis subito discedendi. Scriptum etiam fuit civitatum gubernatoribus, ut omni ex loco discessum illorum procurarent.
units.tr: After the interdict of Pope Paul V against the city and state of Venice was published, with the aim that the subjects, deprived of the exercise of religion, would stir up tumults and be compelled to give way to him, it was decided that an order should be issued to all religious that in every church the customary divine services should be continued without that novelty. All obeyed this, and the Jesuits in particular replied that they too would continue divine worship. Meanwhile, however, they spread through the city that they would abstain from saying Mass in public. When the magistrates learned of this, they summoned the Jesuits on 9 May 1606, so that it might be known for certain from them what their intention was. Being warned to carry out the Prince's command in their ministry, they said they could not say Mass, since this, as they claimed, did not conflict with their promise. For Mass, they said, was not included under the name of divine offices. When this was known, the Senate resolved that the Patriarchal Vicar should be sent to take charge of the Jesuits' church property, and that the Jesuits should be ordered to leave at once. Letters were also sent to the governors of the cities, to arrange their departure from every place.

units.la: Iesuitae intellecta intimatione tumultuarie ad Ecclesias convocarunt suas devotas, & ut postea compertum fuit, inde ingens auri & gemmarum pondus deprompserunt. Sub vesperam ministros publicos sibi dari petierunt securitatis suae causa: qui utique ipsis missi fuerunt. Discesserunt vesperi sub horam secundam noctis, singuli cum imagine Christi ad collum, ad ostendendum, Christum nunc secum pati: Sua Collegia quasi nuda reliquerunt, in quibus totam noctem & integrum diem reliquiae remanebant ignis: praesertim duobus in locis, ubi immensam copiam scriptorum suorum combusserunt, reliquis pluribus instrumentis, quibus funditur metallum. Quod cum per urbem increbuisset non sine scandalo, Patr. Possevinus paucis diebus post Ferrariam scripsit, & visa etiam fuit litera publice, instrumenta non fuisse, ut funderent aurum & argentum, sicuti calumniose traducerentur, sed ut concinnarent pileos suos sive baretas.
units.tr: On hearing the notice, the Jesuits tumultuously summoned their devout women to the churches, and, as was afterwards discovered, they brought out from there a great weight of gold and jewels. Towards evening they asked that public officers be assigned to them for their safety, and these were indeed sent. They left in the evening, about the second hour of the night, each with an image of Christ hung round his neck, to show that Christ now suffers with them. They left their colleges as if stripped bare. Remnants of fire remained in them through the whole night and the entire day, especially in two places where they burned an immense quantity of their writings, along with many other instruments by which metal is melted. When this had spread through the city, not without scandal, Father Possevino wrote a few days later from Ferrara, and a letter was also read publicly, saying that the instruments were not for melting gold and silver, as they were slanderously reported, but for making their caps or biretta.

units.la: Verum Patavij multa exempla remanebant scripti, quod octodecim continebat regulas cum hoc titulo: Regulae quaedam servandae, ut cum orthodoxa Ecclesia vel sentiamus. In harum 17. praecipitur praedicandam aut inculcandam nimis nor effegratiam De I. Et in 13. ordinatur, debere Ecclesiam Hierarchicam credere nigrum esse id, quod oculis videtur album. Quod scriptum ob ingentem numerum exemplorum eius uniformium, quae illic reperiebantur, perhibetur fuisse eo fine compositum ut quotidie distribueretur scholasticis, qui Venetias adventarent ad societatem se conferrent. Verba formalia capitis illius 13. haec sunt: Denique ut ipsi Ecclesiae Catholicae omnino unanimes, conformesque, si quid, quod oculis vestris apparet album, nigrum illa esse definierit, debemus idem, quod nigrum sit, pronunciare, &c. Capitis 18. verba formalia sunt ista: Nec idem praedicandae aut inculcandae gratiae De I adeo insistendum fuerit, ut serpere inde possit animis errorum lethalis negata liberi arbitrij nostri facultate.
units.tr: However, at Padua many copies of a writing remained, which contained eighteen rules under this title: Certain rules to be observed, so that we may feel with the orthodox Church. In the seventeenth it is commanded that the grace of God should not be preached or inculcated too insistently. In the thirteenth it is ordered that the hierarchical Church must believe black to be what the eyes see as white. Because a huge number of identical copies of this writing were found there, it is said to have been composed for this purpose: that it should be distributed every day to the students who came to Venice to join the Society. The formal words of that thirteenth chapter are these: Finally, that we may be wholly united and conformed to the Catholic Church itself, if it should define that what appears white to your eyes is black, we ought to pronounce that what is black, and so on. The formal words of the eighteenth chapter are these: Nor should we insist so much on preaching or inculcating the grace of God that the deadly error of denying the faculty of our free will may creep into men's minds from it.

units.la: Diebus sequentibus non tantum Iesuitae ex statu Veneto profecti, verum universa eorum societas in & extra Italiam disseminabant infinitas calumnias contra Rempublicam cum in privatis colloquijs, tum in praedicationibus publicis, & in dominio Reipubl cum literis ipsis adhaerentibus: Convocabant ad confinia suos devotos, ingrediebantur dominium habitu & personis dissimulatis: praedicabant varias indulgentias ijs, qui interdium observarent, aut alias ad id observandum, & causae Pontificis patrocinandum promoverent: fingebant literas falsas, quas sub nomine Reip. Genuensis scribebant Venetae & quas sub nomine civitatis Veronensis scribebant civitati Brixianae.
units.tr: In the following days, not only the Jesuits who had left the Venetian state but their whole society, in Italy and outside it, spread countless calumnies against the Republic, both in private conversations and in public sermons, and with letters attached to them within the Republic's territory. They summoned their devotees to the borders and entered the territory in disguise, with feigned dress and identities. They preached various indulgences to those who observed the interdict, or who otherwise promoted its observance and the defence of the Pontiff's cause. They forged false letters, which they wrote in the name of the Republic of Genoa to Venice, and in the name of the city of Verona to the city of Brescia.

units.la: Quae cum intolerabilia viderentur esse Venetis, in mandatis datum fuit a Senatu, ut seditiosarum actionum ipsorum novissimarum, ut & praecedentium aliarum formaretur processus. Et quoad ultimas quidem abunde compertum fuit, ipsos in concionibus suis invectos esse in Rempubl. appellando illam haereticam, Lutheranam, tyrannicam, & abominandam, & quae sunt innumerabilia huiusmodi epitheta: idque Ferrariae, Bononiae, Parmae, Mantuae, Palermi & alibi: opera etiam ipsorum atque instinctu omnia ista mala evenisse, quae evenerunt in Hispania, Bohemia, Gallia, Polonia & Anglia Legatis Venetis quod equidem literis Legatorum & ministrorum publicorum mmet, qui illis in regnis erant, & aliorum sermone, comprobatum fuit.
units.tr: Since these things seemed intolerable to the Venetians, the Senate ordered that a legal process be drawn up concerning the most recent seditious actions of the Jesuits, as well as earlier ones. As for the latest, it was amply established that they had inveighed against the Republic in their sermons, calling it heretical, Lutheran, tyrannical and abominable, with countless epithets of this kind; and this at Ferrara, Bologna, Parma, Mantua, Palermo and elsewhere. It was also proved, from the letters and reports of the Venetian ministers and public agents in those kingdoms and from the talk of others, that all those evils which befell Spain, Bohemia, France, Poland and England were brought about by their work and instigation.

units.la: Operam etiam dabant apud Principes Italiae, ut in provincijs ipsorum Reip. militem conscribendi licentia praecideretur: & cum hoc non succederet, vicatim euntes detestabantur omnem Venetū, anathema minati iis, qui in militiam ipsorum proficiscerentur. Seditiones, quas in Dominio excitabant partim literis, partim instructionib. & partim tractationibus clàm & oretenus cum subditis Venetijs, & inconsinijs cum Devotis suis, quos illuc acceperant, fuere innumerabiles. Compertum praeterea fuit, ipsos turbarum illarum fuisse architectos praecipuos, quas tum temporis concitaverunt apud quosdam, quibus spem secerunt, ut in administratione Reip. partem aliquam, locumq; obtinerent distractione excitata inter Senatores.
units.tr: They also worked upon the princes of Italy to have the Republic's power to raise soldiers in their provinces cut off. When this did not succeed, they went from village to village denouncing every Venetian and threatening with anathema those who enlisted in the Venetian service. The seditions they stirred up in the Venetian territory, partly by letters, partly by instructions, and partly by secret and oral dealings with Venetian subjects and with their own adherents whom they had gathered there, were innumerable. It was further established that they were the chief architects of those disturbances which they then stirred up among certain men, to whom they held out hope that, through the division aroused among the senators, they might obtain some part and place in the government of the Republic.

units.la: Quin etiam innotuit, quod cum Resp. à morte Henrici III. Christianissimum appellassent Henricum IV. Regem Galliae, ipsi Romam scriptis literis multis Senatoribus scrupulum injecerunt, qui propterea Venetijs discesserunt, quia Iesuitae absolutionem eis negabant, nisi reuocarent. Alia incommoda, quae inde sequebantur, transfeo. Pro diversis occasionibus monstrabant se fautores magnorum principum, in negotia illorum se ita intrudentes; Menstrua impendebant plures quam centum coronatos in curandis tantum literis, quod πολυπραγμοσύνω & correspondentiam illorum per omnia loca satis superque arguit. Detegebantur ultae insidiae eorum, quas struebant bonis & facultatibus suorum amicorum, & praesertim ultarum cum damno insigni familiarum.
units.tr: It also came to light that, when the Republic had called Henry IV, King of France, "most Christian" after the death of Henry III, the Jesuits wrote many letters to Rome and cast doubt upon this among several senators, who for that reason left Venice, because the Jesuits refused them absolution unless they recanted. I pass over the other troubles that followed from this. On various occasions they showed themselves to be patrons of great princes, thrusting themselves thus into the affairs of others. They spent more than a hundred gold crowns a month on the mere handling of letters, which amply proves their busybodying and their correspondence through every place. Their secret plots against the goods and property of their friends were also brought to light, especially those which caused serious loss to entire families.

units.la: Quo ad doctrinam ipsorum innotuit in rebus quidem politicis meliorem in modum ipsos extollere Monarchiam, & deprimere Aristocratiam, cum hypothesibus certis, quae instituerunt & administrationi Reip. sunt contrariae: unde apparuit Iesuitas authores & instrumenta fuisse omnium turbarum, confusionum, seditionum & damnorum nostris temporibus in omnibus regnis & provincijs mundi subortorum.
units.tr: As regards their teaching, it became known that in political matters they exalt monarchy and depress aristocracy in a most fawning manner, on the basis of certain assumptions which they laid down and which are contrary to the administration of the Republic. From this it appeared that the Jesuits were the authors and instruments of all the disturbances, confusions, seditions and losses that have arisen in our times in all the kingdoms and provinces of the world.

units.la: Quae omnia & singula cum ad d. 14. Iun. anno 1606. essent propositia, deliberatum & deretum fuit, quod cum Societas Iesuitarum Venetijs à primo tempore, quo recepta & bene habita fuit erga Rempub. se exhibuerit semper ingratam, inq; detrimentum potius quam emolumentum fuerit propensa, idemq; etiam nunc non sine intolerabili molestia & insolenti dicacitate continet, in aeternum illam amplius recipi in quemcunq; locum Dominij Veneti non posse nec debere.
units.tr: When all these things and each of them had been laid before the Senate on 14 June 1606, it was resolved and decreed that the Society of Jesus, which from the first time it was received and well treated by the Republic has always shown itself ungrateful, and has been inclined to bring harm rather than benefit, and which even now still persists in this with intolerable annoyance and insolent abuse, could not and should not ever again be admitted into any place in the Venetian dominion.

units.la: Et sane evidentissimum est argumentum enormitatis delicti eorum, quod in tanto numero Senatorum ne unus quidem ipsis patrocinabatur, & in scrutinio votorum secretorum exploratum fuit, omnia conformia esse, ut perpetua ipsorum proscriptio decerneretur.
units.tr: Indeed, the clearest proof of the enormity of their offence is that, among so great a number of senators, not one defended them, and in the secret ballot it was found that all were agreed that their perpetual banishment should be decreed.

units.la: Ad d. 18. ejusdem mensis deliberatum & conclusum fuit ab eodem Senatu ut publicaretur mandatum, Ne ullus cujuscunque conditionis & sexus sive Venetijs sive aliis in civitatibus Reipublicae recipere audeat Iesuitas, aut literas ad eorum Societates perferre, aut commercium ullum cum eis habere, sub poena irremissibili proscriptionis ex omnibus terris & locis Reipub. vel sub graviori poena, pro transgressionis & personarum qualitate: ut teneantur etiam omnes, qui liberos suos sub disciplina illorum habeant, eos ocyus & sine mora revocare, neque in perpetuum illos ad Collegia eorum remittere, sub isdem poenis.
units.tr: On 18 of the same month, the same Senate resolved and concluded that a mandate should be published: that no one of any rank or sex, whether in Venice or in other cities of the Republic, shall dare to receive the Jesuits, or carry letters to their Societies, or have any dealings with them, on pain of irrevocable banishment from all the lands and places of the Republic, or a heavier penalty according to the nature of the transgression and of the persons; and that all who have their children under the discipline of the Jesuits shall likewise be bound to recall them at once and without delay, and never again to send them back to their colleges, under the same penalties.

units.la: Quum suscipiueretur tractatio pacis inter Pontificem & Remp. Iesuitae sollicite instituerunt Romae, & in Hispania praesertim, ut & ipsi tractationi includerentur, in medium afferentes summa sua in Coronam merita, & quod exclusio ipsorum tum Papae, tum Hispaniarum Regi dedecus magnum fit allatura. Non dubitabat etiam Confessarius Regis e Societate unius palam dicere. Non à Rege tantum, sed à tota Curia controversiam illam componi bona cum conscientia non posse, nisi Iesuitae Venetijs restituantur in integrum.
units.tr: When the negotiation of peace between the Pope and the Republic was taken up, the Jesuits eagerly worked at Rome, and especially in Spain, to have themselves included in the negotiation, putting forward their great services to the Crown, and saying that their exclusion would bring great disgrace both to the Pope and to the King of Spain. The King's confessor, a member of the Society, did not hesitate to say openly that this controversy could not be settled with a good conscience, not only by the King but by the whole Curia, unless the Jesuits were restored to their full position at Venice.

units.la: Scriptum quoque sparserunt Romae Italice, & in Hispania Hispanice, quod oblatum est Pragae à Patrib. Societatis Iesu Nuncio Pontificis & Legato Hispanico residentibus apud Imperatorem anno 1607. Aprili mense, quando fuit nuncuatum
units.tr: They also circulated in Rome a writing in Italian, and in Spain one in Spanish, which was presented at Prague in April 1607 by the Fathers of the Society of Jesus, the Pope's nuncio and the Spanish legate, who were residing with the Emperor, when it was announced.

units.la: De Nefariis Facinoribus
units.tr: On the Nefarious Deeds

units.la: controversiam inter Paulum V. Papam & Serenissimam Rempub. Venetam composita esse, ita tamen, ut Iesuitae a Statu Veneto exterminati essent: in quo varia sed futiles ac vanae causae afferuntur, quibus probare conantur, non permittenda esse Venetis proscriptionem Iesuitarum ex ipsorum Statu. Id autem sic habet:
units.tr: The controversy between Pope Paul V and the Most Serene Republic of Venice was settled, but on the condition that the Jesuits be expelled from the Venetian State. Various reasons are put forward for this, though they are trivial and empty, by which they try to prove that the Venetians should not be allowed to banish the Jesuits from their own State. The passage reads as follows:

units.la: Quemadmodum Veneti tempore inobedientiae & schismatis declararunt, se comaculatos esse haereses: sic quum quaerunt hoc tempore, ut Iesuitae nunquam revertantur, satis eo ostendunt id, quod Demosthenes de lupis dicit, eos quum pacem inire vellent cum ovibus, petisse, ut exterminaretur canes, veluti eos qui distractionis fuerint authores. Quod si igitur hoc ipsi concedatur, malum in dies ingravescet, donec fiat immedicabile, & aperte bellum inde tandem enascatur. Hoc modo plus lucrabuntur, quam eo quod in principio praetendebant, nempe jurisdictione in bona & personas noxias, nunc vero captigandi & innocentes potestate constituti sequentur. Manifestissimum hoc erit signum, Regi & Papam manus dare, nec vires habere ad redigendum ipsos in ordine, sicut vitios esse, tam iniqua videlicet conditione: unde libertati Ecclesiasticae maius detrimentum oboriretur, sicut etiam authoritati Papae, quam cum omnibus iis legibus quae censurarum extiterunt causae.
units.tr: Just as the Venetians declared at the time of their disobedience and schism that they were stained with heresies, so now, when they ask that the Jesuits never return, they sufficiently show that what Demosthenes says of wolves applies to them. When the wolves wished to make peace with the sheep, they asked that the dogs be driven out, as the authors of the quarrel. If this were conceded to them, the evil would grow worse by the day until it became incurable, and open war would at last break out from it. In this way they will gain more than they claimed at the beginning, namely jurisdiction over guilty goods and persons; now, invested with power to ensnare the innocent too, they will go on to do so. This will be a most manifest sign that the King and the Pope have given way and lack the strength to bring them back into order, since they are vicious, on such an unfair condition. Whence greater harm would arise to ecclesiastical liberty, and also to the authority of the Pope, than from all those laws which were the causes of the censures.

units.la: Papa sibimet facit injuriam, permittendo, ut primi, qui ipsi obedierant, ob hanc causam confundantur in conspectu totius mundi inter Catholicos & haereticos, & castigentur proscriptione perpetua & suorum bonorum privatione. Hoc modo confirmabitur id, quod per totum annum publicarunt per mundum, nempe Interdictum & omnes actiones Papae contra Venetos nullas esse, neminemque eis debere obedire, quadoquidem praetendebant, atque etiam obtinebant eos, qui ipsi obedierant hunc in modum castigari.
units.tr: The Pope does an injury to himself by permitting those who first obeyed him to be confounded for this cause, in the sight of the whole world, among Catholics and heretics, and to be punished with perpetual banishment and the loss of their goods. In this way what the Venetians have published throughout the world for the whole year will be confirmed, namely that the Interdict and all the Pope's actions against the Venetians are null, and that no one ought to obey him, since they were claiming, and even obtaining, that those who had obeyed him be punished in this manner.

units.la: Ex altera causa etiam Papa praejudicat suae authoritati, quandoquidem deinceps non poterit amplius publicare interdictum, quod fit validum: nam cum videat eos, qui obediunt pro eo quod debent affici praemiis, adeo graviter puniri, nemo Ecclesiasticus amplius ipsi obediet, & ipsimet Iesuitae, qui hactenus in omnibus rebellionibus, quae in quacunque parte mundi contra sanctitatem eius & Regem nostrum fuerant excitatae, ad ipsis serviendum periculis expositi fuerunt facultates & vitas suas, tempore futuro perdet animam. Quod facturi sunt & caeteri omnes religiosi, cum videant se desertos esse, sicque male tractari eos, qui in hujusmodi occasionibus adeo bene se gesserunt.
units.tr: On the other hand, the Pope also prejudices his own authority, since from now on he will no longer be able to publish an interdict that is valid. For when churchmen see that those who obey, instead of being rewarded as they ought, are punished so severely, no churchman will obey him any more. The Jesuits themselves, who hitherto, in all the rebellions stirred up in whatever part of the world against his Holiness and our King, were exposed to dangers in serving him with their goods and lives, will in future lose their souls. All the other religious orders will do the same, when they see themselves deserted and those treated badly who behaved so well on such occasions.

units.la: Praeterea Sanctitas & Majestas sua dabunt maximum scandalum toti mundo, siquidem illud exemplum animum addet omnibus haereticis & politicis in quacunque parte: molientur enim quidvis contra Sanctitatem eius, quippe certi, se illud obtenturos, unde facile ipso exemplo se se justificabunt.
units.tr: Moreover, His Holiness and His Majesty will give the greatest scandal to the whole world, since that example will embolden all heretics and politicians in every part of it. For they will attempt anything against His Holiness, being certain of obtaining it, and so they will easily justify themselves by that very example.

units.la: Quod si forte existimetur id precario posse accommodari, sciendum illud ipsum in medium etiam propositum fuisse, cum tractaretur pax cum Anglia: nunc vero apparet quam fuerit id sine fundamento & ratione. Deinde, si consideretur obstinacia quam hactenus sunt professi, excutiendo poenas Ecclesiasticas, & minas bellicas, prudenter praesupponi nullo modo potest id ipsos facturos precario, postquam periculum evaserunt: Tertio, non excusabuntur propterea incommoda illa superiora: Quarto, etiamsi id facerent postea propria sua voluntate, ut satisfacerent Principi alicui id ab ipsis postulanti, dum consideran debet, quanta existimatione id lucrifaceret eiusmodi Princeps, & quantam inde jacturam faceret & ipsius Sanctitas & Majestas Catholica, cum ne quidem omnibus suis viribus & authoritate rem tam justam obtinere potuerint.
units.tr: But if perhaps it is thought that this could be granted as a favour, it should be known that this very proposal was also put forward when peace with England was being negotiated; now it appears how groundless and unreasoned it was. Next, if one considers the obstinacy they have hitherto professed, shaking off ecclesiastical penalties and threats of war, it cannot prudently be presupposed in any way that they will do it as a favour once they have escaped the danger. Third, those greater inconveniences mentioned above will not be excused on that account. Fourth, even if they were to do it afterwards of their own will, to satisfy some prince who asked it of them, one must consider how great an esteem such a prince would gain from it, and how great a loss would thereby fall on His Holiness and the Catholic Majesty, since they could not obtain a matter so just even with all their forces and authority.

units.la: Et si quis objiceret, necessario admittendam esse illam conditionem, ut non introducatur in Italiam bellum, quadoquidem ipsi volunt sine eo subiicere se Papae, primum quidem ista dissimulatio & major subinde propagatio haereseos in statu Veneto majoris & periculosioris belli causa erit: Secundo, evenient ex ista haereticorum & politicorum inventione, ut in conditione illa tanquam si essent minoris ponderis, exhibituri se sint obstinationes, utpote in qua, sicut apparet ex superioribus, cosistit omnis existimatio sive justitiae, sive injustitiae hujusce negotii, necnon ipsius Sanctitatis & Majestatis Catholicae: Tertio, Veneti ampliore habent occasione pertimescendi bellum in sua domo modo exiguo quem habent ad se defendendum, exigua securitate erga suos Vasallos in re tam pudenda & injusta, ut non debeant habere Papam vel Regem Dominum nostrum, qui inferant ipsis bellum ad redigendum eos in exitium, quod ocyus amplientur, si videant ex altera parte constantiam & resolutionem a ipsis conditio negatur tam indigna & intolerabilis.
units.tr: And if anyone should object that this condition must necessarily be admitted, so that war is not brought into Italy, since they wish to submit to the Pope on no other terms, then first, this dissimulation and the greater spread of heresy in the Venetian state will be the cause of a greater and more dangerous war. Second, from this invention of heretics and politicians it will come about that they will display their obstinacy as if that condition were of little weight, although, as appears from what was said above, all estimation of the justice or injustice of this business, and likewise of His Holiness and the Catholic Majesty, rests upon it. Third, the Venetians have a greater occasion to fear war in their own house, since they have little force with which to defend themselves, and little security towards their vassals in a matter so shameful and unjust, that they ought not to have the Pope or our Lord the King bringing war against them to bring them to ruin; and this will be enlarged all the more quickly if they see on the other side that constancy and resolution are refused to them in a condition so unworthy and intolerable.

units.la: DE TVRBIS ET VARIIS CALAMITATIBVS
units.tr: DE TVRBIS ET VARIIS CALAMITATIBVS

units.la: IN BOHEMIAE REGNO A IESVITIS EX- CITATIS.
units.tr: IN BOHEMIAE REGNO A IESVITIS EX- CITATIS.

units.la: ANno 1609. die 3. Augusti mensis Status Bohemici libello supplici Caesareae Maiestati oblato, graviter conqueruntur de Iesuitis, quod quum non ligenae, sed peregrini & advenae pleriq; sint, nihilominus agros & praedia ad se pertraxisse, & nec tributum de illis solvant, nec onera sustineant alia, multo minus autem contributionem, quam a subditis exigant ullam faciant; necessario igitur cogente, sese a Caesarea Maiestate petere, eo adigantur, ut a praedijs istis posterum abstineant, & nulla alia absq; consensu & peculiari indulto Caesaris coemant, vel ex testamentis, donationibus, vel alia quacunque ratione acquirant & ad se transferant. Sed parum impetrarunt.
units.tr: In the year 1609, on the 3rd day of August, the Bohemian Estates, having presented a humble petition to His Imperial Majesty, complained bitterly about the Jesuits: although they were mostly not native but foreign and alien men, they had nonetheless drawn fields and estates to themselves, and neither paid tax on them nor bore any other burdens, much less made any contribution such as the subjects are required to make. They therefore petitioned His Imperial Majesty that, since they were compelled by necessity, they might be obliged to refrain from these estates in future, and not to buy, or acquire and transfer to themselves by wills, gifts or any other means, anything else without the consent and special permission of the Emperor. But they gained little.

units.la: Ob quas causas autem Iesuitae ex Boemiae Regno Anno 1618. die 1. Iun. mensis proscripti tandem, & in aeternum inde eiecti sint, malo Statuum Boemorum urbis, quam meis referre. Prima est, quod a multo iam tempore fuerint VASTATORES publicae pacis & tranquillitatis huius Regni. Notum esse passim omnibus, qui in quantis inclytum Boemiae Regnum periculis per retro omnes annos, quo Iesuitica Secta idem Regnum fuit ingressa, versatum perpetuo fuerit, quam frequentes mutationum vicissitudines perturbationesque subierint; quae omnia Status ipsos, pariterque subditos eorum, & alios Regni incolas aegno suo incommodo persentiscere, eaque de causa bona capitaque exponere debuisse. Addunt, comperisse se ipso facto, eiusmodi aerumnarum nullos maiores authores esse, quam virulentae Religionis Iesuiticae homines: ut proinde quamdiu haec secta in Regno sit permansura, nunquam supradictis calamitatibus finis imponi, nec pax in Regno diuturna esse possit: sed tam ipsa Regia Maiestas, quam Status ipsi perpetuo de cervicibus & bonis omnibus sint periclitaturi. Secunda causa proscriptionis Iesuitarum ex Boemiae Regno est, quod idio stabiliendae Romanae Sedis, omnia regna, ac mundi huius terras iugo ac testatae eius subjicere unice adnitantur. Tertia, quod Magistratus politicos ios contra alios concitent, ac tam inter Status mutuo, praesertim Religionis offensione diversos, quam inter Magistratus ac subditos, dissensiones & dissidia citent: ipsosque subditos contra Reges conjuris, doctrina & pollicitationibus, etiam suis gloriae aeternae acquirendae, ac purgatorii ignis evadendi armant. Quarta, quod per confessiones arcana omnia rescire, atque ita conscientiis hominum dominantur, etiam ad illicita compellendo consuescant. Quinta, quod exemplo Templariorum cuti, insignia quaeque loca, suo usui vendicet. Sexta, quod administrationi securi in omnib. sese ingerant. Septima, quod omnes, qui Roman. Ecclesiae collegia sua subjicere & Papae parere nolunt, Haereticos proclament, eisque fidem habendam nullam palam doceant. Octava, quod eiusmodi crimina ac technae Societatis Iesuiticae testata reddantur etiam ab externis Regnis ac Provinciis: specialiter in Gallia, Anglia, Hungaria, Veneti, Belgio aliisque Sacri Romani Imperii Provinciis. Nono, quod non obstantibus Maiestatis literis, a gloriosae memoriae Rodolpho pro libero Exercitio Religionis concessis, nec non inita & iterata Caesarea Maiest. super eadem re cum caeteris Catholicis Statibus convenerit, parte sub Vtraque in concionibus & scriptis audacter sconatis proscindant, lacerent, verba earundem literarum partialiter, & contrarie explicent.
units.tr: As for the causes for which the Jesuits were at last proscribed and cast out forever from the Kingdom of Bohemia on the 1st day of June 1618, I prefer to report the grounds stated by the Estates of Bohemia rather than my own. (1) First, that for a long time they have been the DEVASTATORS of the public peace and tranquillity of this Kingdom. It is known to everyone everywhere what dangers the renowned Kingdom of Bohemia has been exposed to through all the years since the Jesuit sect entered that Kingdom, and what frequent upheavals and disturbances it has undergone; all of which the Estates themselves, and likewise their subjects and the other inhabitants of the Kingdom, have felt to their own great harm, and for which reason they ought to have exposed goods and lives. They add that they have found by experience that there are no greater authors of such calamities than the men of the virulent Jesuit religion, so that, as long as this sect remains in the Kingdom, no end can ever be put to the aforesaid calamities, nor can peace in the Kingdom be lasting; but both His Royal Majesty himself and the Estates will be perpetually in danger of their necks and all their goods. (2) The second cause for the proscription of the Jesuits from the Kingdom of Bohemia is that they strive solely to establish the Roman See and to subject all kingdoms and the lands of this world to its yoke and to its tested authority. (3) Third, that they stir up the political magistrates against one another, and arouse dissensions and quarrels both among the Estates themselves, especially those divided by offence in religion, and between the magistrates and their subjects; and that they arm the subjects against the kings by conspiracy, teaching and promises, even promising them eternal glory to be won and escape from the fire of purgatory. (4) Fourth, that they learn all secrets through confessions, and thus lord it over men's consciences, accustoming them, even by compulsion, to unlawful things. (5) Fifth, that in the manner of the Templars they claim for their own use whatever notable places they like. (6) Sixth, that they insinuate themselves into the administration of affairs in all matters. (7) Seventh, that they proclaim all who are unwilling to subject their colleges to the Roman Church and to obey the Pope to be heretics, and openly teach that no faith is to be kept with them. (8) Eighth, that such crimes and the treachery of the Jesuit Society are made known even by foreign kingdoms and provinces, especially in France, England, Hungary, Venice, Belgium and other provinces of the Holy Roman Empire. (9) Ninth, that, notwithstanding the letters of His Majesty granted for the free exercise of religion by Rudolf of glorious memory, and although His Imperial Majesty has agreed on the same matter, both once and repeatedly, with the other Catholic Estates, they boldly tear to pieces and rend, in sermons and writings, the party of the Utraquists, and explain the words of those same letters partially and contrary to their meaning.

units.la: DE NEFARIIS FACINORIBVS
units.tr: On the Nefarious Deeds

units.la: Decima, quòd in concessione Literarum Maiestatis Religionis Statum in Boemia concernentium, interponendam fuisse iudicent authoritatem Romani Pontificis, qui tamen nec in Status sub utraque, multò minus in Regem ullum ius habeat. Undecima, quòd Iesuitarum instinctu & consilio sub Vtraque subditi Regis, aliorumque Dominorum Papisticorum, carceribus, aliisque modis ad Romanam Religionem capessendam adacti fuerint, templaque & cultus divinus Vtraquistarum in eorundem Papistarum Dominorum quibusdam locis sublatus, omniaque officia praecipua, tam Regia, quam Regni & Civilia personis religionis sub Vnadistributa, Vtraquistae e contra, qui sese pro conscientiae debito interposuerint, officijs ac dignitatibus suis magno cum probro deiecti fuerint. Duodecima, quòd administris paucis Papistis quibusdam, perfidis patriae filijs, cum pene omnia Iesuitarum instinctu & nutu agerentur, totum Regnum, ac praecipue pars sub Vtraque ad extremum prope interitum esset adducta, nisi Deus ex mera charitate & misericordia sua sancta, quam erga Verbum suum & partem sub Vtraque gerere dignatur, malum praevenisset.
units.tr: Tenth, they judge that the authority of the Roman Pontiff ought to have been interposed in the granting of the Letter of Majesty concerning the state of religion in Bohemia, although he has no right at all over the estates under both kinds, far less over any king. Eleventh, that at the instigation and counsel of the Jesuits, subjects of the king under both kinds, and of other Papist lords, were driven by imprisonment and other means to embrace the Roman religion; that in some places of those same Papist lords the temples and divine worship of the Utraquists were abolished; and that all the principal offices, royal, provincial and civil, were distributed among persons of the Roman religion, while Utraquists who had stood up for the duty of conscience were thrown out of their offices and dignities with great disgrace. Twelfth, that since almost everything was done at the instigation and nod of the Jesuits, by a few Papists, faithless sons of the fatherland, in the administration, the whole kingdom, and especially the part under both kinds, had been brought almost to utter ruin, had not God, out of his pure charity and mercy, which he deigns to show toward his holy Word and the part under both kinds, forestalled the evil.

units.la: Haec est summa Decreti Statuum Boemiae contra Iesuitas: Ipsum verò Decretum de verbo ad verbum Latine fere habet: Omnibus tribus sub Vtraque Ordinib. satis cognitas quantis periculis & incommoditatibus regnum illud, à primo Sectae Iesuiticae in illud ingressu, expositum, quidque afflictionis & miseriarum experti oes fuerint. Harum incommoditatum causam unam & solam à Iesuitis dependere, reipsa Defensores cognovisse, qui id propositum sibi habeat ut Sedem Romanam firmare, & regna mundi totius omnia sub potestatem suam redigere possint.
units.tr: This is the substance of the Decree of the Estates of Bohemia against the Jesuits. The Decree itself, word for word, runs in Latin much as follows: Since all three orders under both kinds know well enough with what great dangers and inconveniences that kingdom was exposed from the first entry of the Jesuit sect into it, and what afflictions and miseries all have suffered, the defenders have recognised that the one and only cause of these inconveniences depends on the Jesuits, who have this purpose, to strengthen the Roman See and to bring all the kingdoms of the whole world under its power.

units.la: Nam ne Deum quidem reverentes, quae ad eam rem facere possint, sedulo facere, Principes adversus seipsos concitare inter Ordines regionum, diversam religionem fovendo, dissidia excitare, magistratus adversus subditos, & hos contra magistratus suos incitare, Reges ad nutum suum coponere, se nolentes, sicariorum libidini exponere, sceleratos quosque ad parricidia in Regibus perpetranda, salutis aeternae consequenda, & purgatorij evitandi promissione animare, amicos adversus invicem committere, in secreta omnia per auricularem confessionem inquirere, conscientijs hominum laqueum immittere, & eas ita constringere, ut fine consensu ipsorum, ne bonum quidem quod fit, facere audeat, quemadmodum etiam thesauros ingentes Teplariorum exemplo sibi coparârint, in politicam gubernationem se se immiscuerint, & ijs, qui Rom. religionem non amplectantur, fidem servandam nullam esse docuerint, haereticos eos proclamantes.
units.tr: For, not even reverencing God, they zealously do whatever can serve that end: they stir up princes against themselves; among the orders of the regions they foment diverse religions and excite dissensions; they incite magistrates against subjects and subjects against their magistrates; they bend kings to their nod, or, if unwilling, expose them to the lust of assassins; they encourage the most wicked men to commit parricide upon kings, with the promise of attaining eternal salvation and escaping purgatory; they set friends against one another; they inquire into all secrets through auricular confession; they cast a noose upon men's consciences and so bind them that, without their consent, they dare not even do a good deed. In the same way, after the example of the Templars, they have gathered vast treasures for themselves, have meddled in political government, and have taught that no faith is to be kept with those who do not embrace the Roman religion, proclaiming them heretics.

units.la: Testimonia huius rei satis manifesta & perspicua, Galliam, Angliam, Hungariam, Transylvaniam, Venetias, Belgium, & regna regionesque alias suppeditare. In hoc ipso Bohemiae regno, cum post perpessas, ex ipsorum instinctu, afflictiones varias, Regales a Caesare Rodolpho super exercitio religionis libero obtinuissent literas, & pacta cum illis sub Vna, de non vituperando, criminando, damnando se se invicem minisset, in tabulas publicas, maioris confirmationis ergo inferenda omnia ista curassent, veritos non fuisse, post habitis poenarum Maiestatis literis expressarum comminatione, Ordines sub Vtraque pro cocionibus suis calumniis proscindere, & tanquam haereticos condemnare, literas Maiestatis in alienum sensum trahere, eaque ad Caesaream Maiestatis Cameraque Regalis, Monasteriorum item, & Ecclesiasticorum, necnon Ordinum sub Vna subditos minimè pertinere distinguere, Regem Bohemiae non posse Maiestatis istas literas confirmare, & religionis libertatem fidelibus suis subditis sine Pontificis Romani consensu permittere: cum Papa tamen neque in Ordines Bohemiae, nec in Regem Dominum suum juris quicquam habeat, publice affirmare, Regis subditos ad Ecclesiasticam maxime juris dictionem pertinentes, à religione sua sub Vtraque ad ea sub Vna vel invitos trahere, templa ipsis praecludere, & aliquibus in locis solo aequare, religionis exercitii prohibere, officia Regis regniqueque primaria non nisi illis, qui sub Vna sunt, administranda permittere, eos verò, qui sub Vtraque sunt, ab officijs publicis nulla causa, quin imò conscientia ipsorum reclamante, cum dedecore, & ignominia removere. Hac ratione id tandem effecisse, ut paucis quibusdam sub Vna perfidis hominibus, patria totius administratio cederet, quorum opera patriae interitum, fidelibus verò sub rò sub utraq; Ordinibus extremam perniciem, & exterminatione acceleraret. Cùigitur omnium in regno auctores sint, indignos esse, qui in eo diutius vivant, & tolerentur. Defensores ergo animad vertentes, mala ista finem non habitura, nec pacem ineo constantem fieri posse, sed & Regem, & ordines omnes cum uxoribus liberisque, & bonis omnibus, in summo periculo versari oportere, quamdiu Secta isti perniciosissima locis aliquis in regno relinquatur, notum omnibus facere, quod deliberato consilio, & opinium Ordinum impetrato consensu, Iesuitas omnes ex oppidis Pragensibus, Crumanom, Comurtavio, Neuhusio, Glatsio, & locis aliis, in quibus Collegia sua habeant, quino ex toto Bohemiæ regno proscripserint, & præsentibus hisce literis in æternum profcriant, ita ut omnes regno quiete excedere, & nullo unquam tempore, ne sub alterius quidemdinis titulo redire in regnum istud debeant, ni incurrere in pœnam, de ipsis & omnibusexcipientibus fovent ibusque, certissime sumendam, & perniciem sibi, fautoribusque suis, quam Reipubl. turbatoribus, & manifestis hostibus, accersere ex regni constitutionelint. Nullum exim plane reditum ipsis in regnum istud, ne ad Romani quidem Pontifi- ci intercessionem, patere debere, nec si illud a quoquam expetatur, intercedere pro illis enquam ex Ordinibus debere, poena quietis publicæ turbatoribus debita, in eum, qui ia fact, constituta. Notum id literis publicis ad perpetuam memoriam fieri omnibus debeat. Illos tamen Ordines sub una in monasteriis viventes & alibi, dummodo quietos se gerant, a sua proscriptione, quæ Iesuitas solos, utpote ex regnis quibusdam etiam alijs jam pridem proscriptos, concernat, intelle&os, minime velle.
units.tr: The evidence of this is clear and manifest enough: France, England, Hungary, Transylvania, Venice, Belgium, and other kingdoms and regions supply it. In this very kingdom of Bohemia, after the various afflictions suffered at their instigation, the estates under both kinds obtained royal letters from the Emperor Rudolph concerning free exercise of religion, and made agreements with those under one kind that neither side would revile, accuse or condemn the other. They took care to have all this entered in the public records for greater confirmation. Yet they were not afraid, despite the threat of the penalties of Majesty expressly stated in the letters, to tear the estates under both kinds to pieces from their pulpits with calumnies and to condemn them as heretics; to twist the letters of Majesty to another sense; and to distinguish that they do not in any way pertain to the Emperor's Majesty, the Royal Chamber, the monasteries and ecclesiastics, or the estates under one kind. They claimed that the King of Bohemia could not confirm those letters of Majesty, nor grant freedom of religion to his faithful subjects, without the consent of the Roman Pontiff; yet they publicly affirmed that the Pope has no right whatever over the estates of Bohemia or over the King, their lord. They drag the King's subjects, who belong above all to the ecclesiastical jurisdiction, away from their religion under both kinds into that under one kind, whether they wish it or not; they close the temples against them and in some places raze them to the ground; they forbid the exercise of religion; they allow the chief offices of the King and of the kingdom to be administered only by those who are under one kind; and those who are under both kinds they remove from public offices for no cause, indeed against the protest of their own conscience, with dishonour and disgrace. By this method they at last brought it about that the whole administration of the fatherland passed to a few faithless men under one kind, by whose work the ruin of the fatherland, and extreme destruction for the faithful under both kinds, was hastened. Since, therefore, they are the authors of all the troubles in the kingdom, they are unworthy to live and be tolerated in it any longer. The defenders, therefore, perceiving that these evils would have no end, and that no lasting peace could be made in it, and that the King and all the orders, with their wives, children and all their goods, must be in the greatest danger as long as this most pernicious sect is left in any place in the kingdom, have made known to all that, by deliberate counsel and with the consent of the orders obtained by common agreement, they have banished all the Jesuits from the towns of Prague, Krumau, Komotau, Neuhaus, Glatz and other places where they have their colleges, and indeed from the whole kingdom of Bohemia; and by these present letters they banish them for ever, so that all must leave the kingdom quietly, and at no time, not even under the title of another dignity, ought they to return into that kingdom, unless they incur the penalty, to be most certainly exacted from them and from all their abettors and favourers, which the constitution of the kingdom prescribes for the disturbers of the commonwealth and manifest enemies, bringing ruin upon themselves and their supporters. For there ought to be no return for them at all into that kingdom, not even through the intercession of the Roman Pontiff; and if anyone should seek it for them, none of the orders ought to intercede for them, on pain of the penalty due to disturbers of public peace, established in the law for such a case. Let this be made known to all by public letters for perpetual remembrance. Yet they do not wish the orders under one kind who live in monasteries or elsewhere, provided they behave quietly, to be understood as included in this proscription, which concerns the Jesuits alone, since they had long ago been banished from certain other kingdoms as well.

units.la: Inhuius Decreti sententia Status Bohemici postea constanter perseverarunt mper: nempe, Ne Societas hæc in Regnum posthac unquam recipiatur: ut ab officijs & muneribus removeantur & excludantur, ac bona illorum in alios us s convertantur.
units.tr: In accordance with the sense of this Decree, the Estates of Bohemia afterwards persevered constantly in it: namely, that this Society should never again be received into the kingdom; that they should be removed and excluded from offices and functions; and that their goods should be turned to other uses.

units.la: Huic vero, quantumvis iustissimo Decreto ac sententiæ, hisque accusationis gravissimis capitibus, & causis æquissimis proscriptionis Iesuitarum ex Bœmiæ regno, quidam Anonymus Iesuita oppositus Apologiam pro Iesuitis, Viennæ Austriæ editam, in qua omnia simpliciter negat ac pernegat, quæ ipsis in Decreimpinguntur crimina, merasq; calumnias & criminationes esse dicit. 1. Negat ium primum ac tertium Accusationis caput, Quod Iesuitæ sint perturbatores publicæ tranquillitatis, dissensionesque, turbas & disiidia passim excitent, & c. ideoque subditis, vel alijs quibusvis potestatem tribuant Reges & Vnctos Domini invadendi, atque ad id faciunt perpetrandum animos eorum pollicitationeis vitæ æternæ acquirendæ, aut evitandi purgatorij accendant. Dicit hanc imam & blasphemam doctrinam, nunquam in Scholis Iesuiticis auditam, nunquam in scriptis eorum lectam, nunquam mente conceptam, sed paribus studijs animis a Iesuitis ubivis locorum damnatam esse: Addita hac elumbi exceptione, NISI IMPIE SIMVL AC IMPERITE Reges & Vnctos Domini in Tyrannos transformemus. 2. Negat Anonymus secundum ac septimum Accusationis caput; Quod Iesuitæ omnia Regna Mundi, Romanæ Sedi subiecre satagant, eidemq; non obtemperantes Hæreticos pronunciant, &c. Addit, Iesuitis manifestam iniuriam fieri, si dicatur, eos docere, Hereticis fidem nullam, neiuramentu quidem seruadum esse. 3. Negat quartum, undecimum & duodecimum Accusationis caput; Quod Iesuitæ conscientijs hominum dominari, eosq; ad illicita compellere omnia suo arbitratu confusueverint, &c. 4. Negat uintum ac sextum caput Accusationis; Quod Iesuitæ insignia quæq; bona ad trahere, & seculari administratione sese ingerere soleant. 5. Negat septimum Ac- usationis caput, Quod perversæ Iesuitarum technæ contexterae fiant externis tiam exèplis Galliæ, Angliæ, Hungariæ, Venetiarum, Belgij, &c. 6. Negat nonū c decimum Accusationis caput, quod literis Maiestatis suum pondus ac monentum, facto, interpretatione, a ciudicio adimere tentaverint, &c. Haec omnia Anonymus iste Iesuita negare nō erubescit, quae tamen lippis et tonsoribus, ut aiunt, ac tonsoribus sunt notissima, ut ex toto hoc opere nostro Lectore intelliget: & paulo infra exempla huius generis plura referemus, sub hoc titulo Iesuitae multa a se & aliis Papistis perpetrata, dicta & scripta impudenter negant iuxta illud Comici, Si fecisti, Nega. Hic enim illorum mos est, si quae refellere nequeant, ut ea simplici negatione satis refutata esse apud suos homines nimium credulos arbitrentur.
units.tr: Against this decree, however just it may be, and against these most grave heads of accusation and most equitable grounds for banishing the Jesuits from the kingdom of Bohemia, a certain anonymous Jesuit has set forth an Apology for the Jesuits, published at Vienna in Austria, in which he flatly and utterly denies all the crimes charged against them in the Decree, and says they are mere calumnies and slanders. (1) He denies the first and third heads of the accusation, that the Jesuits are disturbers of public tranquillity, who stir up dissensions, tumults and quarrels everywhere, and so on, and therefore give subjects, or any others, the power to attack kings and anointed lords, and kindle their minds to do so with promises of winning eternal life or escaping purgatory. He says this is an impious and blasphemous doctrine, never heard in Jesuit schools, never read in their writings, never conceived in their minds, but condemned by the Jesuits everywhere with equal zeal; adding this feeble exception: UNLESS WE IMPIOUSLY AND AT THE SAME TIME UNSKILFULLY TRANSFORM KINGS AND ANOINTED LORDS INTO TYRANTS. (2) The Anonymous denies the second and seventh heads of the accusation, that the Jesuits strive to bring all the kingdoms of the world under the Roman See, and pronounce those who do not obey it heretics, and so on. He adds that the Jesuits are manifestly wronged if it is said that they teach that no faith, not even an oath, is to be kept with heretics. (3) He denies the fourth, eleventh and twelfth heads of the accusation, that the Jesuits are accustomed to rule over men's consciences and compel them to illicit acts at their own pleasure, and so on. (4) He denies the fifth and sixth heads of the accusation, that the Jesuits are accustomed to draw to themselves all the outstanding goods and to meddle in secular administration. (5) He denies the seventh head of the accusation, that the perverse devices of the Jesuits are woven into the foreign examples of France, England, Hungary, Venice, Belgium, and so on. (6) He denies the ninth and tenth heads of the accusation, that they have tried by deed and interpretation to strip the letters of Majesty of their weight and authority, and so on. This Anonymous Jesuit is not ashamed to deny all these things, which are nonetheless as well known as anything to the bleary-eyed and to the barbers, as they say; as our reader will understand from the whole of this work of ours, and a little below we shall report many examples of this kind. Under this heading the Jesuits shamelessly deny many things done, said and written by themselves and other Papists, following that saying of the comic poet: If you did it, deny it. For it is their custom, if they cannot refute what is laid against them, to think that it has been sufficiently refuted by a simple denial among their too credulous people.

units.la: Sed concludam hunc locum: Aut mentiuntur Status Boëmici, qui talia conqueruntur in suo Edicto de Iesuitis: aut Anonymus noster, qui ea omnia negat simpliciter. Sed prius est falsum: quis enim tantos, tantaeque authoritatis, fidei & existimationis viros mendacij argueret? Ergo verum est posterius.
units.tr: But I will conclude this point: either the Bohemian Estates, who complain of such things in their Edict concerning the Jesuits, are lying, or our anonymous author, who simply denies all of them. But the former is false: for who could charge with lying men of such great standing, authority, trustworthiness and reputation? Therefore the latter is true.

units.la: Anno vero 1618. ex Moravia quoque sequuti Decreto proscripti & eiecti fuerunt.
units.tr: In the year 1618, moreover, they were also expelled and driven out of Moravia by a decree that followed.

units.la: Secret wider die Jesuiter in Mähren, den 6. Tag May, Anno 1619. ergangen.
units.tr: Decree against the Jesuits in Moravia, issued on the 6th day of May, 1619.

units.la: Wir N. N. N. die Herren, Ritterschafft, und Personen aus den Landen und Inwohnern des Marggrafthumbs Mähren, so der Evangelischen Religion zugethan, den Leib und Blut unsers Herren und Heylands Jesu Christi sub utraque empfahen, und an jetzo in der Statt Brinn versamblet seynd, thun kund und offenbar mit diesem brieff vor jedermänniglich, wo derselb gelesen oder gehört wird, und insonderheit wo es vonnöten, welcher massen uns von den Herren Ständen des Königreichs Böheim dises nit nur allein durch die in truck außgangne Apologia, sondern auch vil und mancherley schrifftē und beweiß zuerkennen geben worden, ja allberait zuvorhin weltkündig ist, was für gewaltige practike durch anstifftung der Jesuitischen Secte, wie in bemelte Königreich Böheim, also auch in andern Landern und Provinzen je und allwegen gestifftet worden: Also daß vil Potentaten ihr leib und leben gebracht, auch sie die Jesuiter grosser und gewaltiger kriegsempörungen und unschuldiges blütvergiessung in alweg ursächer gewesen. So werden wir gleichermassen berichtet, daß von jnen den Jesuiten zu disen jetzigen empörungen, durch welche das Marggrafthumb Mähren unser liebes Vatterland nit nur allein in gewaltige schuldeklaß gesetzt, sondern auch ins äusserste verderbe gebracht ist, ursach gebe worden sey. Dessen zû besserer vrkundt vnd beglaubung/ haben wir anfangs bemeldte Herren Ritterschafft vnd Abgesandte auß den Stätten vnsere Pitschafft an diese Pa-pier auffdrucken lassen. Geben in der Statt Brinn den 6. Maii/ Anno 1619.
units.tr: We, N. N. N., the lords, knighthood, and persons of the lands and inhabitants of the Margraviate of Moravia, who adhere to the Evangelical religion, receive the body and blood of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ under both kinds, and who are now assembled in the city of Brünn, make known and manifest by this letter to everyone whom it may concern, wherever it is read or heard, and particularly where it is needful, in what manner we have been informed by the lords Estates of the Kingdom of Bohemia, not only by the Apology published in print, but also by many writings and proofs. It is already known throughout the world what powerful intrigues have always and everywhere been set up by the instigation of the Jesuit sect, in the said Kingdom of Bohemia as well as in other lands and provinces. As a result, many potentates have lost their lives, and the Jesuits have in every way been the cause of great and violent wars, rebellions and the shedding of innocent blood. We are likewise informed that the present uprisings, by which the Margraviate of Moravia, our dear fatherland, has been not only plunged into grave debt but also brought to utter ruin, were occasioned by the Jesuits. To the better witness and confirmation of this, we, the aforementioned lords, knights and envoys from the towns, have had our seals impressed on this paper. Given in the city of Brünn, 6 May, in the year 1619.

units.la: Similiter Iesuitæ ex Hungaria quoq; ob easdem causas eiecti sunt anno 1619 ab Evangelicis Statibus seu Ordinibus hoc Decreto:
units.tr: Likewise, the Jesuits were also expelled from Hungary for the same reasons in the year 1619, by the Evangelical Estates or orders, by this decree:

units.la: Decret wegen der Jesuiten/ wie die selbigen auß dem Königreich Hungarn ewig verbannisiert/ vnd außgewiesen/ vom 16. Junij Anno 1619.
units.tr: Decree concerning the Jesuits, how they were banished forever and expelled from the Kingdom of Hungary, of 16 June 1619.
