You therefore now, my brother, consider what will become of our Poland, if all those things must be removed among us, as they certainly desire to remove the things by which the attainment of their end is hindered. So far concerning the end.

units.la: Videamus nunc Media sive praxin, per quam ad scopum illum perrumpere conantur, & hæc ex ijs, quæ jam dicta sunt, facilè intelliguntur. Hoc nimirum conjuncta operâ fervidissimè agunt, ut primum Reges Europæos, quotquot possunt uni cuidam Fœderi ilim ligent: Cujus Fœderis principem & directorem constituunt Hispaniarum regem, Aurei ipsius velleris possessorem & custodem. Ad cujus videlicet nutum reliqui se applicare coganitur, sub hac conditione, ut qui conatibus ejus quacunque ratione intercedit aut quam minimum adversatur, de hæresi suspectus sit, & prædicti velleris perisce-lidignus censeatur. Sed regnorum septentrionalium ea fere est ratio, ut ad Legum præscriptum, non autem ad absolutum Regum arbitrium regantur. Ideoque regiarum iarum Personarum confaderatio parum illis prodesse poterit, nisi etiam subjecta regi.s regna in eandem Vnionis nassam concludant. Atqui hoc opus hic labor est; Cum heic infinita, ut jam dictum est, difficultates obijciantur, quocirca etiam opera illorum heic ecipue enitet & omnium maximè conspicua est. Sic autem res suas hoc loco disponunt.
units.tr: Let us now look at the means, or practice, by which they strive to break through to that goal, and these are easily understood from what has already been said. They work with the greatest fervour and in concert to bind as many European kings as they can into one league. The prince and director of this league they set up as the King of Spain, the possessor and guardian of the Golden Fleece. To his nod, namely, the rest are compelled to submit, on this condition: that whoever in any way opposes his undertakings, or even resists them in the slightest, is to be suspected of heresy and judged unworthy of that Fleece. But the northern kingdoms are generally governed so that they are ruled by the prescription of laws, not by the absolute will of kings. Therefore a confederation of royal persons can do them little good, unless the subject kingdoms too are enclosed in the same net of union. But this is the hard task here. Since, as already said, infinite difficulties are thrown in the way here, their effort is especially eager here and most conspicuous. They arrange their affairs in this place as follows.

units.la: Primum omnium hoc seduló curant, ut in Aulis se insinuent. Hunc enim nidum hoc nus accipitrum sibi ubique praestruere inque eodem ova sua deponere solet, priusquam venatum evolent. Iesuita etiam ibi peregrinus sibi & exul, immò capite diminutus deretur, ubi ab Aula arceretur. Fixo heic pede, ulterius operam dant, ut clavum eipub. in suam potestatem redigant, id est, ut vel Regi Reginaeve ex suo corpore Confarium, vel saltem Haeredi regio Praeceptorem dent. Aut si hoc non semper succedit, il— dominentur, quorum in Reipub. administratione praecipuae partes sunt & vires. Vtque rum affectus, cupiditates & designationes penitissime cognita & perspecta habeant: a videlicet escaunus quisque alliciendus & captandus sit. Ad hoc autem felicius perfi— endum, Romana Aula, quicquid autoritate, quicquid opibus, quicquid artibus & consilio alet & poterit, Genti huic liberalissimae, ut jam dictum est, induiget. Adeò ut Iesuitarum commendationes Romae ad consequendas dignitates & praebendas plus valeant, quàm potentissimorum Regum intercessiones.
units.tr: First of all they take great care to insinuate themselves into the courts. For this is the nest in which this kind of hawk is wont to build for itself everywhere and lay its eggs before flying out to hunt. The Jesuit, too, is a stranger and an exile there, indeed deprived of his civil standing, and is driven off when he is shut out of the court. With his foot fixed here, they next work to bring the helm of the Commonwealth into their own power: that is, either to give the King or Queen a confessor from their own body, or at least to give the royal heir a tutor. Or if this does not always succeed, they seek to rule over those whose principal parts and strength lie in the administration of the Commonwealth. And so that they may know the affections, desires and designs of each most thoroughly, each man is to be enticed and caught. To carry this out more successfully, the Roman Court lavishes on this most generous people, as already said, whatever it can nourish with authority, wealth, arts and counsel. So much so that the recommendations of the Jesuits at Rome carry more weight for obtaining dignities and prebends than the intercessions of the most powerful kings.

units.la: Quae unica res, si catera abessent, ad corrumpendas omnes, OMNES dico, Europae aulas, abundè sufficeret, sicut eventus proh dolor testatur. Quam vis hoc etiam tibi advertendum est, Genio Iesuitico extra hoc quandam à natura occultam vim inesse, qua Ingenijs illicis imperat & dominatur.
units.tr: This single thing, even if the rest were absent, would be enough to corrupt all, ALL I say, the courts of Europe, as the outcome, alas, bears witness. Yet this must also be noted by you: that beyond this there is in the Jesuit genius a certain power hidden by nature, by which it commands and rules over enticed minds.

units.la: Vt autem de occultioribus Gentis hujus artibus, quas in praedictis politiarum officinis exercent, nil dicam: Duo sibi ibidem potissimum pacisci untur, Primum ut ipsorum mellificatio ex hac Reipub. Arce non impediatur, Vtq; deinceps adversarijs suis nullum eò refugium patet, illorumq; querelae, si quas eò deferent vel prorsus negligantur, vel quoquo modo eludantur. De his duobus quamprimum Iesuitae cautum est, ipse deinceps sibi ad reliqua perficienda sufficit.
units.tr: But I will say nothing of the more secret arts of this brotherhood, which they practise in the aforementioned workshops of the states. Above all they bargain for two things there: first, that their honey-making is not hindered from this citadel of the Commonwealth; and second, that henceforth no way of escape lies open to their adversaries there, and that their complaints, if they bring any there, are either altogether ignored or are somehow evaded. The Jesuits have taken care of these two matters as soon as possible; they themselves are thenceforth sufficient for accomplishing the rest.

units.la: Constructo & firmato hoc nido, pabulatores suos quaqua versum emittunt, suamq; venationem hac fere ratione instituunt: Primum operam dant, ut in primarijs Regni aut Provinciae Vrbibus Seminaria, collegia, templa quam plurima, tanquam instantis Messis suae horrea, exstruant. Per haec autem duo consequuntur, quae eis ad finem suum, de quo maximus, valdè proficua existunt Regnum primum universum his ceu unguibus apprehenduntur, & ita constringunt, ut ad suum nutum illud, quoties res ita postulat, cum singulis partibus circumagere queant. Quod ut facilius consequantur seminaria, sua in praedictis urbibus, ita plerunque construunt, ut suis aedificijs ipsa urbium moenia complectantur, eademq; sibi oftu diuq; pervia faciant. Vt in arcibus, quas Cracovia, Vilna, Calisij, Posnaniae, &c. habent, videre licet.
units.tr: Once this nest has been built and secured, they send out their foragers in every direction, and they conduct their hunting in roughly this way. First, they labour to build in the principal cities of the kingdom or province as many seminaries, colleges and churches as possible, as barns for their coming harvest. By these two means they gain what is most useful for their chief aim: first, the whole kingdom is seized by them as if with claws, and they so grip it that they can turn it, whenever the situation requires, at their nod, together with its individual parts. To achieve this more easily, they commonly build their seminaries in the said cities so that they enclose the city walls within their buildings, and make them open to themselves by gate and road. As may be seen in the citadels which they have at Cracow, Vilna, Kalisz, Posen and elsewhere.

units.la: Nec ego Gentis nostrae supinam negligentiam & incuriam satis hoc admirari, aut ro rei indignitate sufficienter detestari possum: Quod ad hujusmodi periculosa et Reipub. raejudiciales substructiones non solum connivimus: sed ad easdem materiem ceu propriis manibus congestimus. Cum sic existimem, si Rex aliquis tale quid machinaretur, universam Remp. contra eum insurrectionem. Et his exterorum Venatorum indagatoribus in no—stris nemoribus tantum licet?
units.tr: Nor can I sufficiently marvel at the supine negligence and carelessness of our nation in this matter, or adequately detest the unworthiness of the thing: that we not only tolerate such dangerous structures, prejudicial to the Commonwealth, but even heap up the materials for them with our own hands. Since I reckon that if any king were plotting something of this kind, the whole Commonwealth would rise in insurrection against him. And are these hunters of foreigners permitted so much in our woods?

units.la: Deinde eadem opera Iuventutem nostram, spem posteritatis, ad suum cerebrum, dispositis, & recoctis animis, regignunt, & sic inter nos Novi & Iesuitici Mundi sementem faciunt. Dum autem intra Regni urbes hoc ij agunt, qui ad haec donis idoneis sunt instructi, reliqui concionibus populalibus & audiendarum confessionum operosissimo simul & quaftuosissimo artificio pro virili studeant. Quarum artium effectus iterum duplex est: Plerumque enim primariam, ut ille loquitur, hac ratione paulatim suam faciunt, factionique vires adijciunt. Provisoribus deinceps qui Camerae sive Aerario praesunt, viam ubiq; muniunt, ut in omnia publica & privata bona aditus eis patefiat.
units.tr: Then, at the same time, they beget our youth, the hope of posterity, and bring them to their own brain, with minds disposed and softened, and so they sow the seed of a new and Jesuit world among us. While those who are suitably equipped with gifts for these tasks do this within the cities of the kingdom, the rest strive as best they can with popular sermons and the most laborious and at the same time most profitable craft of hearing confessions. The effect of these arts is again twofold: for most often, in that manner, they gradually make the chief men, as he puts it, their own and add strength to their faction. Then they pave the way everywhere for the treasurers who preside over the Chamber or treasury, so that access to all public and private goods lies open to them.

units.la: DE NEFARIIS FACINORIBVS
units.tr: On the Nefarious Crimes

units.la: Et hęc mihi latissima sermonis valva se aperiret, si aucupia illorum, quibus illi homines, Mulierculas præsertim, circumveniunt, explicare vellem. Cum vero instituti et occupationum mearum ratio mihi habenda sit: illud saltem præterire nolo, in quo etiam se hujus à reliquis Religiosorum ordinibus differentia aliqua perspicitur. Quod nempe Iesuitæ vulgaria illa munuscula, quæ vulgò in Religiosos erogari consueverunt, non curant, nec ea capiunt: Quod hoc eis sordidum et reliquo Ordinis splendori minus conveniens videatur. Aquila enim currucam non captat. Et ipsi alias, ut exercitati Practici bene norunt, Pecuniam in loco negligere maximum interdum lucrum esse. Nec vero egomet simulationem hanc aliquando eo usque processisse, ut oblatum 50. aureorum Vngaricorum precium repudiarint.
units.tr: And this would open for me the widest gate of my discourse, if I wished to explain the snares by which those men, especially the little women, entrap people. But since the plan of my work and my occupations must be taken into account, I do not want to pass over this one point, in which a certain difference between this Order and the other Religious Orders is seen. The Jesuits do not care for those common little gifts that are customarily offered to the Religious, and they do not accept them. This seems to them squalid and less fitting for the splendour of the Order. For the eagle does not catch flies. Moreover, as experienced practitioners know well, to neglect money in the right place is sometimes the greatest profit. Nor did I ever find this pretence go so far that they refused an offered sum of fifty Hungarian gold coins.

units.la: Hominum vero opulentorum testamentaria legata, et cum his integra prædia adeo non fastidiunt, ut eo potius fraudum exquisitissimarum artificio illa aucupentur, ut Polonia, in hac etiam publica morum corruptione, vix quicquam simile experta sit. Hinc ergo istis pecunię negleƈtoribus, qui suam gratuitam operam nobis tam officiose deferunt, illi regales inter nos Proventus, quos cum reliquis suis arcanis in Majore Polonia Calisiij, in Minore Cracoviæ, in Russia Lublini, Vilnæ in Lithuania, Poltoviij in Masovia, et Braunsbergæ in Borussia deponere et custodire dicuntur. Hæc inquam imperij Iesuitici inter nos æraria publica sunt et Chartophylacia, quæ si hoc tempore excuti deberent, Poloniam haud dubie destatus sui qualitate rectius instructura essent, quàm tot hactenus tumultuosa scrutinia præstare potuerunt. Et hæc de Praxi Iesuitica.
units.tr: Yet they do not disdain the legacies in wills of wealthy men, and whole estates along with them, and they pursue these with such exquisite artifice of deceit that Poland, even in this public corruption of morals, has hardly experienced anything similar. Hence, from these neglecters of money, who offer their free services to us so obligingly, come those royal revenues among us, which are said to be deposited and kept with their other secrets at Kalisz in Greater Poland, at Kraków in Lesser Poland, at Lublin in Russia, at Vilnius in Lithuania, at Płock in Masovia, and at Braunsberg in Prussia. I say these are the public treasuries and archives of the Jesuit empire among us. If they were ever to be searched in this age, they would undoubtedly furnish Poland with a truer understanding of its condition than all the tumultuous inquiries so far have been able to achieve. And this is enough on Jesuit practice.

units.la: Hæc itaque de primo designationis meæ capite, de politia nimirum Instituti Iesuitici pro tua instructione sufficiant. Tuum nunc erit cogitare, num is fallatur, qui Iesuitas Polonis, Reique eorum publicæ vehementer formidandos et sedulò cavendos censet. De narrationis autem mea veritate novi tibi melius, quàm mihi ipsi constare.
units.tr: So let these things about the first head of my plan, namely the polity of the Jesuit Institute, suffice for your instruction. It will now be your task to consider whether he is mistaken who judges the Jesuits to be dangerous to the Poles and to their public affairs, and to be carefully guarded against. As to the truth of my account, you know it better than I do myself.

units.la: Superest nunc, ut quæ in genere de gentis natura et moribus propositæ sunt, per particularia exempla comprobentur, adeoq; demonstretur, quàm periculosa harum rerum praxis Ordini Politico fuerit, quod secundum erat propositionis meæ caput. Hoc ipsum verò per domestica et nostræ experientiæ documenta satis copiosè explicari posset et demonstrari: spero tamen in exterorum historiarum magis conspicuam fore, quod illorum casus extra factionum affectus positi, et sic ad instruendum aptiores sunt. Ideòque exemplis eorum immorabor.
units.tr: It remains now that what has been set out in general about the nature and customs of the nation should be confirmed by particular examples, and so it may be shown how dangerous the practice of these things has been to the political order, which was the second head of my proposition. This could indeed be explained and demonstrated at sufficient length by domestic evidence from our own experience. Yet I hope that the foreign histories will be more striking in this matter, because their cases, lying outside the passions of factions, are more apt for instruction. Therefore I shall dwell on their examples.

units.la: Inter plurima verò documenta, vix quicquam illustrius est eo, quod historia ultimi tumultus Galliæ suppeditat: Ex quo nempe perspicitur, quantum Iesuitismi genius contra statum regium ad eius-que eversionem possit. Res sic habet: Regni Galliæ ea est conditio, ut à prudentiæ politicæ studiosis fere pro optimæ politiæ norma allegetur. Et quamvis in eo nobis cum ipsis non per omnia conveniat, certum tamen est, eam firmissimam esse. Siquidem ad absolutæ Monarchiæ formam quàm proximè accedit: Contra tyrannidem tamen, et seditionem ijs legibus, ea Parlamentorum auctoritate, illa demum sanguinis regij reverentia corroboratum et firmatum est, ut his solis rebus hactenus invictum perstiterit.
units.tr: Among very many proofs, hardly anything is more illustrious than what the history of the latest tumult in France supplies. From it clearly appears how much the spirit of Jesuitism can do against the royal state and toward its overthrow. The matter stands thus. The condition of the Kingdom of France is such that by those who study political prudence it is commonly cited as the norm of the best polity. And although we do not agree with them in every respect, it is certain that it is most firmly established. For it comes very near to the form of an absolute monarchy; yet against tyranny and sedition it has been strengthened and confirmed by its laws, by the authority of the Parlements, and finally by reverence for royal blood, so that by these means alone it has hitherto remained unconquered.

units.la: Et quantum ad sanguinis regij observantiam attinet, Galli vulgò aliquid præ reliquis Nationibus in hoc affectu putantur habere. Illorum sanè regia familia vetustior est quàm nulla Europæa. Contra hanc tamen firmissimam, ut Henrico 3. haud dubie videbatur, Arcem, Iesuitica impressionis cuneus tantum valuit, ut quod in Gallijs hactenus inauditum erat, Rege in ordinem redacto, Familiæ regiæ autoritatem itapenitus prostraverint, ut et Personam regiam neci dediderint, et infensissimæ Gallis nationi ad invadendum regnum viam longè lateq; complanaverint. Et nisi peculiaris et penè miraculosa Dei providentia conatibus eorum tam evidenter obstitisset, rem eò deducturi videbatur, ut Galli prodita regia familia, quæ inter eos per annos plus quàm 600. tam altas radices egit, ut omnes fere principes familias complexa sit, Gallici nominis perpetuum hostem et æmulum mulum sibi Regem ascivissent. Idque sane multo majori miraculo, quam si nobis antehac Demetrium suum Moscoviticum obtrusissent.
units.tr: And as far as reverence for royal blood is concerned, the French are commonly thought to have this feeling more than other nations. Their royal family is certainly older than any in Europe. Yet against this most firm stronghold, as surely seemed to Henry III, the wedge of Jesuit pressure prevailed so far that, something unheard of in France until then, they brought the King to heel and so utterly overthrew the authority of the royal family that they both delivered the royal person to death and levelled a road, broad and long, for the most hostile nation to the French to invade the kingdom. And unless a peculiar and almost miraculous providence of God had so clearly stood in the way of their efforts, they seemed likely to bring the matter to this point: that the French, having betrayed the royal family, which for more than 600 years had struck such deep roots among them that it had joined almost all the princely families, would have taken as king a perpetual enemy and rival of the French name. And this would have been by a far greater miracle than if they had foisted their Muscovite Demetrius upon us before this.

units.la: Heic autem ut magis perspicuum fiat, quomodo Instituti illius genius erga statum Politium sit affectus, ex tot illorum molitionibus, quibus Henricum illum subverterunt, unum sal-em, sed valde insigne illorum stratagema hic producam, cujus haec est ratio.
units.tr: Here, however, so that it may become clearer how the spirit of that Institute is disposed toward the political state, I shall bring forward from the many schemes by which they overthrew that king a single trick, but a very notable one of theirs, and its reasoning is as follows.

units.la: Sub initiu praedicti tumultus, quaestio illa in Gallijs agitari coepit, Num Pont. Rom. Galliae populum, a fidelitatis juramento, quo Regi suo obligatur in casu haeres absolvere possit? Ex hac oriebatur altera huic admodum affinis, Num cuilibet privato liceat Tyrannum propria authoritate occidere? Intelligis, opinor, quantum Regis statusque regij & universae Reipubl. in horum problematum decisione interfit. Et quid putas Apostolos dicturos fuisse, quando Hierosolymis primum Concilium sub praesidio Spiritus sancti celebrabant, si Religiosus aliquis cum hujusmodi quaestione comis eis apparuisset? Neque tamen in Gallijs controversiae istae novae erant. Ad priorem tum ventilandam Pontificum olim cum Galliae regibus perpetua litigia perennem materiam suppeditaverant.
units.tr: At the start of the said tumult, the question began to be debated in France: whether the Roman Pontiff can absolve the people of France from the oath of fidelity by which they are bound to their king, in the case of heresy? From this arose another question, closely related to it: whether any private person may, on his own authority, kill a tyrant? You understand, I think, how much the king, the royal state, and the whole commonwealth have at stake in the decision of these problems. And what do you suppose the Apostles would have said, when they held the first council at Jerusalem under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, if some Religious had appeared to them with a question of this kind? Yet these controversies were not new in France. The former of them, to be sure, had long furnished an everlasting matter for dispute between the Pontiffs and the kings of France.

units.la: Posterior vero ante annos plus minus 200. post caedem nempe Ludovici Aureliani in Corbonistarum collegio publice agitata & solenniter decisa erat. Utraque semper constantissime negata, adeo ut posterioris assertio & assertor Iohan. Pratus, ni fallor, in Concilio etiam constantiensi ex aequo damnati fuerint.
units.tr: The latter, however, had been publicly debated and solemnly decided in the College of the Sorbonne about 200 years before, namely after the murder of Louis of Orléans. Both propositions were always most firmly denied, so that the assertion and its author, Jean Prat (unless I am mistaken), were condemned alike, even at the Council of Constance.

units.la: Pro hac autem vice eaedem quaestiones Galliam ad eum modum immutatam invenerunt, ut bona pars Cleri & cum his totus Iesuitarum ordo utriusque assertionem probaverint, vocata & annihilata Majorum suorum perpetua sententia: non aliter, quam si novus terra Mundus successisset.
units.tr: On the present occasion, however, these same questions have been found in France so changed that a large part of the clergy, and with them the whole Jesuit Order, approved both assertions, the lasting judgment of their elders having been called back and annulled, as if a new world had arisen on the earth.

units.la: Hujus vero immutationis Iesuitas praecipuos authores extitisse ipsa Sarbona post res datas publice profesta est: Et Iesuitae idem non obscure agnoscunt, dum inter causas, propter quas olim Pontificia excommunicatio contra Galliae reges minus efficax fuerit, hanc minatim exprimunt, Quod Gallorum animi tum non sufficienter dispositi fuerint. Hoc est, quod tam acres seditionum concitatores non habebant, quales hodie Iesuitici ncionatores sunt & Confessarij.
units.tr: That the Jesuits were the chief authors of this change the Sorbonne itself has openly declared after the event. And the Jesuits do not obscurely acknowledge the same, when among the causes why the Pontifical excommunication was once less effective against the kings of France they hint at this one: that the minds of the French were then not sufficiently disposed. That is to say, they did not then have such fierce stirrers-up of sedition as the Jesuit preachers and confessors are today.

units.la: Hae cigitur Iesuitarum decisio (non tamen absque Deo) Henrico necem attulit, & conti Parricida absolvit, eumque Ehudo ipsi Israelitarum liberatori aequiparavit. Quale niin Christiani Orbis parte, inde a religionis incunabulis auditum, scriptumve est aut factum.
units.tr: Therefore this decision of the Jesuits (not, however, without God) brought death to Henry, and absolved the parricide, and likened him to Ehud, the liberator of Israel himself. Nothing like this has been heard or done in any part of the Christian world since the cradle of religion.

units.la: Ubi tu tamen, ut rei indignitatem melius perspicias, notare debes, Sectam hanc Tyranneus nempe, quem ab unoquoque privato impune occidi posse contendunt, definitionem sibi aequa discretioni referuasse. Secundum quam is nobis pro hujusmodi mactationis pecude habendus est, qui quacunque ratione in Romani Pontificis indignationem incidit, & ex Iesuitarum sensu excommunicatur. Id quod ideo heic addendum fuit, quod in alterius quaestionis formatione ab ipsis insidiose additur, in casu haeresis, ut hoc nempe fuco perstringerent: quam suam in supremum Magistratum incrustent. Cum constet Haereticos illos esse, non in pravas in religione opiniones sectantur: sed qui Iesuitarum artes quocunque modo impeunt, aut ipsis non per omnia obsequuntur.
units.tr: But here, so that you may better perceive the vileness of the matter, you must note that this sect has reserved for itself, as the one who may be killed with impunity by any private person, a definition of tyrant, which they insist is in their own discretion. According to it, he must be regarded by us as a beast fit for such slaughter who, for whatever reason, has fallen under the displeasure of the Roman Pontiff and is excommunicated in the Jesuits' judgment. This had to be added here because, in the formulation of the other question, they insidiously add the case of heresy, so that by this pretext they may bind fast those whom they wish to brand as enemies of the supreme magistrate. Since it is evident that those are heretics not who hold wrong opinions in religion, but who in any way attack the arts of the Jesuits or do not obey them in everything.

units.la: Sicut vel ex Venetorum exemplo intelligere possumus, quos haec secta per universam Italiam pro pestilentissimis Haereticis proclamare dicitur, ideo saltem, quod latis, seu potius novatis legibus Iesuitarum cupiditati frenum injecerunt.
units.tr: As we can understand even from the example of the Venetians, whom this sect is said to proclaim throughout all Italy as the most pestilent heretics, at least for this reason: that they imposed a curb on the Jesuits' greed by enacting, or rather renewing, laws.

units.la: De Henrico vero certum est, eum, dum vixit, nullius usquam erroris ab ullo Catholicominsimulatum esse. Constat etiam eum in Catholico-Romana communione usque ad extremum perstitisse. Furoris autem, quo eum persecuti sunt, haec vera causa fuit: Quod scerum regium non ei tradere volebat, quem sibi hi Socij, tanquam idoneum motionum suarum administrum, Galliae Regem destinaverant.
units.tr: Concerning Henry, however, it is certain that, while he lived, he was accused by no Catholic of any error whatever. It is also established that he persisted to the end in the Roman Catholic communion. The true cause of the fury with which they pursued him was this: he was unwilling to hand over the royal seal to the man whom these Fathers had designated for the King of France as a fit instrument of their schemes.

units.la: Tu ergo nunc iterum vide, Annon per hoc Iesuitarum decretum omnium Europaeorum Regum & quorumcunque Magistratuum Politicorum mors & vita ab arbitrij Iesuitici horoscopo suspendatur? Vt si hic illis dextrè ascendat, ipsi vivant & valeant, sin minus, pereant? Qua de re prædicta Venetorum calamitas, Regis Britanniæ perpetua pericula, & illorum omnium metus, qui hunc Ordinem sibi infestum sentiunt, abundè testantur. Venetorum tamen exemplum præcipuè conspicuum est, quod Respublica illa, ut dixi, Romano-Catholicam religionem hactenus, tanquam Imperij sui Palladium, accuratè observet & acerrimè tueatur.
units.tr: Now consider again: is not the life and death of all the kings of Europe and of whatever political magistrates there are made to hang on the Jesuit horoscope, so that if the stars rise favourably for them, they live and prosper, but if not, they perish? The aforementioned calamity of the Venetians, the perpetual dangers of the King of Britain, and the fears of all those who feel this Order to be hostile to them, bear abundant witness to this. Yet the example of the Venetians is especially conspicuous, since that Republic, as I said, has hitherto observed the Roman Catholic religion most carefully, as the palladium of its empire, and defends it most fiercely.

units.la: Quæ exempla quoties expendo, toties exhorresco, cum videam quam facilè sub præsenti rerum statu inter nos simile quiddam in alterutram partem accidere possit, postquam inprimis Gentis Iesuiticæ ad hujusmodi aliquem effectum tam pertinaces & fervidi conatus ab aliquot jam annis inter nos deprehenduntur.
units.tr: Whenever I weigh these examples, I shudder, since I see how easily something similar may happen among us in the present state of affairs, especially since such persistent and fervent efforts of the Jesuit tribe toward some such result have been detected among us for some years now.

units.la: Sed hoc fortasse dicere voles, Inter nos nihil ab hac parte esse periculi, quod Iesuitæ cum Rege nostro probè conveniat, &c. Mallem te dicere posse, Regi nostro cum Regni ordinibus & his cum regia Majestate probè convenire. Hoc enim ad Respubl. salutem aliquanto utilius, & ad securitatem nostram firmius & efficacius esset. Nunc autem hoc abs te vere dici agnosco, neque tamen hoc ipsum sollicitudinis meæ causam tollit, sed eandem potius auget. Equidem enim certò dicere poterit, quod hoc Regi nostro perpetuum futurum sit, ut Iesuitis tam propitijs utatur? Quid si is aliquando deprehensus illorum artibus, à quibus eum hactenus plerique nequiter circumventum existimant, animum mutet, & potiorem Resp. respectu habere incipiat, ecquid tu eum sperare jubebimus? Annon tepuisse fuit in Gallijs, quo Henricum III. ex Polonia redeuntem Natio hæc eo applausu excepiebat, ut laudum eius præconio exsatiari nequirent, dititates, Huic uni Individuo omnes Constantinos & Carolos Magnos, omnes Ludovicos, &c. inclusos esse. Hunc fortissimum, felicissimum, Christianissimum & invictissimum Christi athletam, Ecclesiæ Catholicæ protectorem, Hæreticorum malleum & pavorem à Deo Gallijs provisum.
units.tr: But perhaps you will want to say: among us there is no danger from this quarter, since the Jesuits agree well with our King, and so on. I would rather you could say that our King agrees well with the orders of the realm, and with them with the royal majesty. For that would be somewhat more useful for the safety of the commonwealth and more firm and effective for our security. As it is, I acknowledge that you speak truly in saying this, yet this does not remove the cause of my anxiety, but rather increases it. For can you certainly say that it will always be so for our King, that he will use the Jesuits so favourably? What if he someday, discovering their tricks, by which most people think he has hitherto been wickedly deceived, changes his mind and begins to regard the commonwealth more highly: would you bid us hope for that? Was it not in France that this nation received Henry III on his return from Poland with such applause that they could not be satiated with the praise of him, calling him the one individual in whom all the Constantines and Charlemagnes, all the Louises, and so on, were included; this most brave, most fortunate, most Christian and unconquered athlete of Christ, protector of the Catholic Church, hammer and terror of heretics, provided to the French by God?

units.la: Quid vero hæc omnia eum tandem juverunt? Cum hic projecta affectionis affectus paulo post ita prorsus in contrarium mutatus sit, ut eum non solum occiderint, sed occisi cadaver, quantum in ipsis fuit, sepultura prohibuerint: Ipsumque Parricidam in Divorum Catalogum retulerint.
units.tr: But what in the end did all these things help him? Since this sudden outpouring of affection soon changed so entirely to the opposite that they not only killed him but, as far as lay in their power, denied him burial after he was slain, and they enrolled the parricide himself in the catalogue of the saints.

units.la: Sed esto, inter nos tale nihil metuendum sit in præsentia, quis vero noverit, qualis in posterum Regum rerumque nostrarum status futurus sit? Nostrane itaque Matri ita confidemus, ut tam ambiguæ fructificationis semen scientes intra Respubl. vitæ cura foveamus & ad posteros propagemus? Quis, inquam, sanus nobis suadebit ut fortunas nostras tam ambigui eventus aleæ committamus? Vt nempe Respubl. non diutius salva sit, quam quousque Regi Reipublicæ cum Iesuitis probè convenit? Vt tunc demum nobis securis esse liceat, quando nihil inter nos est, quod sectæ huic offensionis causam præbere possit?
units.tr: But granted that nothing of the kind is to be feared among us at present, who knows what the future state of our kings and of our affairs will be? Shall we then trust our mother so far that, knowing the seed of so uncertain a harvest, we nurture it within the life of the commonwealth and pass it on to our descendants? Who, I ask, of sound mind will advise us to entrust our fortunes to the dice of so uncertain an outcome? Namely, that the commonwealth should not remain safe any longer than it suits the King of the commonwealth to agree well with the Jesuits? That we may only then be allowed to be secure when there is nothing among us that could give this sect a cause for offence?

units.la: Dixi quanta vis sit aculei Iesuitici contra Reges statumque regium, quoties hunc motum litionibus suis obstare intelligunt. Hoc autem te notare velim, eiusdem pestis non minorem efficaciam esse in oppugnanda & expugnanda Republ. atterendis legibus, quoties nemo pe sentiunt, se ab his in institutis suis venatione impediri. Et quod ad Leges attinet, hæ potiticæ tineæ illas præcipuè arrodere consueverunt & exedere, quibus jus successionis in regno continetur, libertasque, & pax publica firmatur.
units.tr: I have said how great is the force of the Jesuit sting against kings and the royal estate, whenever they perceive that this movement hinders their designs. But I would have you note that the same pest is no less effective in attacking and overthrowing the commonwealth and in wearing down its laws, whenever they perceive that they are hindered in their hunting by these institutions. And as regards the laws, these political moths are accustomed chiefly to gnaw and eat away those which contain the right of succession to the kingdom and by which public liberty and peace are secured.

units.la: Qualem in Gallijs præcipuè invenerunt legem illam Salicam Matriculam & fundamentum illius Regni, per quam stirpis regiæ malfcula proles, exclusis femellis, ad regnum sola admittitur. Cujus legis vigore successio Regni post interfectum Henricum III. ad Henricum IV. Regem tum Navarræ devolvebatur. Quod ipsum cum sæcta Iesuitica interpretaretur, tantum efficere potuit, ut Galli hoc Reipubl. suæ fundamentū ipsimet subruere conarentur, assuit contra hanc legem Philippi 2. Hispaniarum Regni filia, quam ex Henrici II. Galliarum Regis filia suscepérat, in regni sui hæredem. Operi totius promotoribus & internuntijs Iesuitis. Quod autem Gallis Lex Salica præstat, hoc Poloniæ adhuc Regum juramenta conferunt, per quæ hactenus Reip. liberæ electionis jus conservatur. Quam periculosè vero hoc etiam libertatis nostræ fulcimentum ab hisce tineis rosum sit, egomet dicere nolo, nec publicum dedecus ipsemet divulgabo. Eiusdem virtutis illustre specimen coram oculis nostris in vicina Hungaria, Austria, Styria, Carinthia, &c. ediderunt. Eo nimirum successu, ut obtritis legibus, quibus prædictarum nationum & provinciarum libertas nitebatur, partem earum penitus oppresserint, partem ad extremam desperationem adegerint. Hoc quidem rumor publicus hactenus constanter affirmat, in prædictis Provinciis alicubi illustribus & antiquissimæ nobilitatis familijs publice diem dictum esse, intra quem se aut coram Iesuitarum tribunali sistant, aut reliquis patriis sedibus alio migrent: quæ res fœtori isti male vertat.
units.tr: Such was the law they found especially in France: the Salic Law, the matrix and foundation of that kingdom, by which only the male offspring of the royal stock, the females being excluded, is admitted to the kingdom. By the force of this law the succession of the kingdom, after Henry III was killed, devolved upon Henry IV, then King of Navarre. When the Jesuit sect interpreted this, it was able to bring about so much that the French tried to undermine with their own hands this foundation of their commonwealth, while Philip II, King of Spain, daughter of Henry II, King of France, was set up as heir to his kingdom against this law, with the Jesuits as promoters and go-betweens of the whole enterprise. And what the Salic Law secures for the French, the oaths of the Kings of Poland still provide for Poland, by which the right of free election in the commonwealth has so far been preserved. How dangerously, however, this support of our liberty has been gnawed by these moths, I do not wish to say myself, nor will I publish the public disgrace. They have displayed a notable example of the same power before our eyes in neighbouring Hungary, Austria, Styria, Carinthia, and so on, with such success that, having crushed the laws on which the liberty of those nations and provinces rested, they have wholly oppressed part of them and driven part to utter despair. Public rumour has indeed constantly affirmed until now that in the aforesaid provinces, in some places, a day has been publicly appointed for the illustrious families of the most ancient nobility, within which they must either present themselves before the Jesuit tribunal or migrate elsewhere from their native seats: a thing that turns out badly for that stench.

units.la: Hæc ergo jam, mi frater, quæro, si forte res in eum casum deveniat, ut regiam Majestatem Iesuitæ inter nos vel nunc, vel posteris temporibus ita colant, ut eandem contra Remp. contra leges, & libertates nostras incitent: Ut quando hactenus coram moderna Regia Majestate, Pacem religionis, unicum illud furoris Iesuiticus repagulum, ita traducunt, ut eam Tartaricam & Mahometicam perfidiam nunc cupent, quam Regia Majestas citra æterna salutis suæ jacturam nec approbare possit, ne dum ut eandem tueri debeat, &c. quam inquam mihi spem facies?
units.tr: These things, then, my brother, I ask now: if perhaps it should come to that point, that the Jesuits cultivate the royal majesty among us, either now or in later times, in such a way that they stir it up against the commonwealth and against our laws and liberties; as hitherto, in the presence of the present royal majesty, they distort the peace of religion, the sole bulwark against Jesuit fury, so that they now wish for that Tartar and Mahometan perfidy which the royal majesty could not approve without the eternal loss of its own salvation, much less ought it to defend it, and so on: what hope, I ask, will you give me?

units.la: Novi tamen quid etiam hic nonnulli excipiant, Non esse videlicet tantopere admirandum, si Confœderatio illa fortasis non omnibus probetur, sub qua nimirum tot abominandæ res quotannis inter nos suppullulent, &c. Age itaque cedamus eis (quod tamen citra Reipub. præjudicium fiat) hoc jure, quid vero ad illud mihi respondebunt, quod in proximis Comitiis Versaviæ Dominica Misericordiæ Domini anno 1606. ex P. Scargæ ore audivimus, quando is conversus sermone ad Regem sic eum alloquebatur: Eheu Rex, quorsum iam nocis res tua intempestiva conniveнтia reciderunt? Reges olim Poloniæ de rebus ad Rempub. spectantibus cum solis Senatoribus deliberabant Nunciorum istorum errestrium, quos vocant, nullæ in hisce rebus partes erant, ut qui non ita dudum introducti sint. Nunc vero tua & quorundam Maiorum tuorum socordia res eo, proh dolor, deducta est, ut quia primum feroculus aliquis Domicellus, qui se pro Nuncio forte terrestri gerit, votum suum proponit, omnes ei protinus assurgere cogantur, &c. Tuum, tuum erat, o Rex, huiusmodi perversas quæ contra antiquos mores introduxerunt, consuetudines cohibere, &c. Ubi etiam manibus seu nutu indicavit, quid veri velit, Summa nimirum papavera demetienda esse.
units.tr: I know, however, what some here also object: that it is not so very surprising if that Confederation, under which so many abominable things sprout up among us every year, is perhaps not approved by all, and so on. Well then, let us yield them this right (which, however, is done without prejudice to the commonwealth). But what will they answer to that which we heard in the recent Diet at Warsaw, on the Sunday of Mercy of the Lord, in the year 1606, from the mouth of Father Skarga, when, turning to the King, he addressed him thus: "Alas, King, to what have your affairs been reduced by your untimely connivance? Formerly the Kings of Poland deliberated on matters pertaining to the commonwealth with the senators alone; the so-called envoys of the lesser nobility had no part in these matters, since they were introduced not so long ago. But now, by your sloth and that of some of your ancestors, the affair has been brought, alas, to such a point that when some fierce young nobleman, who perhaps acts as a land envoy, proposes his vote, all are forced to rise to their feet at once, and so on. It was your task, O King, to restrain these perverse customs which they have introduced against the ancient usages, and so on." Where he also indicated by his hands or nod what he truly wanted: namely, that the tallest poppies should be cut down.

units.la: Huncigitur Tubicinis istius aulici tenorem si reliqui tribules ita perseverentur, ut ad eorum consiliorum executionem operam & vires suas Regi aliquando in auxilium offerant, quid de nobis deque nostra illa hactenus illibata libertate futurum censes?
units.tr: Now if our fellow citizens continue in the tone of this courtier-trumpeter, so that they at some point offer their effort and strength to the King in carrying out these plans, what do you think will become of us, and of that liberty of ours, unimpaired until now?

units.la: Disputatur hodie inter nos de modo potestatis regiæ, itemque de Reip. in Rebus ad regni salutem spectantibus autoritate. De hac aut controversia quid Iesuitæ sentiant non est obscurum. Regi nempe regiaque Majestati quantum in conatibus ipsorum promovendis cofstanter nititur, tantum adiectum cupiunt, quantum Henrico 3. olim & eiusdem successori Henrico 4. propter oppositam rationem detraxerunt. Quomodo vero vice versa in Remp. animati sint, Scarga jam nos docuit, & tu nos adhuc dormire velles?
units.tr: Today we are debating among ourselves the manner of royal power, and likewise the authority of the Commonwealth in matters bearing on the safety of the realm. What the Jesuits think about this controversy is not unclear. They want the royal power and the royal Majesty to be increased exactly as much as they constantly strive to promote their own undertakings, just as they once took away from Henry III, and from his successor Henry IV, as much as their opposing reasoning required. How they are minded toward the Commonwealth in turn, Scarga has already taught us; and do you still want us to sleep on?

units.la: Hæc igitur et si palam inter nos practicentur itaut animi affectus citra rubore mipsimet publicum prodant, sunt tamen qui Iesuitarum inter nos patrocinium suscipiant, & omnia dulo coquirant, quibus hæc sub aliqua probabilitatis specie vel prorsus negari vel saltem illiari & excusari quocunque modo posse confidunt.
units.tr: These things, then, although they are openly carried on among us, so that their attitude betrays itself without any blush of shame, nevertheless there are those among us who take up the Jesuits' cause and search out every trick by which they trust these matters can be either wholly denied or at least softened and excused in some way under a semblance of probability.

units.la: His igitur deinceps nonnulla respondenda sunt: nam hoc tertium nobis designationis nostræ caput constitutum fuisse meminisfi.
units.tr: To these people some things must now be answered; for you will remember that this third head was set down as part of our purpose.

units.la: Qui itaque Iesuitas omnium fervidissimè propugnant, primo loco Catholicam religionem legare consueverunt, à cuius interitu sibi metuunt, si in Iesuitas gravius aliquid debeat statui. Estque hic defensionis Iesuiticæ longè splendidissimus & maximè plausibilis tentexus, ad quem amplificandum congeruntur Ordinis istius res gestæ Barbarorum
units.tr: Those who defend the Jesuits most ardently are accustomed, first of all, to put forward the Catholic religion, from whose ruin they fear for themselves if anything more severe should be decided against the Jesuits. And this is the most splendid and most plausible web of the Jesuit defence, and to enlarge it they heap together the deeds of this Order among the barbarians

units.la: NB. nimirum infidelium sub utroque Mundi axe, sicut & Haereticorum in hisce partibus plu- rimorum felicissima conversio. Quibus hodie inter nos adduntur divini illi & miraculosi gentis illius successus in Moscovia, & angusta spes, quam ex illo tractu & nobis & Romana Ecclesia ostentant, &c.
units.tr: NB. that is, the most fortunate conversion of unbelievers under both poles of the world, as well as of very many heretics in these parts. To these today are added among us that divine and miraculous success of the order in Muscovy, and the narrow hope which they hold out from that region both to us and to the Roman Church, and so on.

units.la: Ad haec igitur quid dicemus? Haec nempe, Primo heic admirari cogor, quibus ratio- nibus sibi persuaderi patiantur, Catholicam religionem citra Iesuitarum operam in Polonia consistere non posse, ij qui credunt, Rom. Catholicam religionem, qualis illa nunc est, paulo minus quam mille annos quingentos per Orbe durasse, antequam Ignatius Loyola in terris natus est: Ita videlicet ut in nostra etiam Polonia tot centenos annos egregie floruerit? Deinde dico, Christum & Apostolos inde ab initio non solum religionis propagationi, sed etiam aeternae eius conservationi per sufficientia media abunde prospexisse. Ut Ecclesia, quam diu in veritatis tramite simpliciter incedit, nullis novis & extraordinariis Mediis opus fit. Hi autem non Iesuitas, quod quidem ego sciam, sed Episcopos, Presbyteros, Doctores, Pastores, Diaconos, &c. ordinarunt: Iltorum vero officiorum cum non solum nomina, sed etiam personae inter nos superfuerint, quibus illorum cura demandata est, quis dubitet, quin hi, dummodo officium faciant, religionem recte sint curaturi, ut maxime Iesuitae in Polonia nulli sunt? Tertio ulterius sic dico, Religionis curam & propagationem Je- suitica designationis minimam partem esse: quam nimirum ipsi amplius non curant, quam quatenus praetextus illius eis ad principaliorem Instituti sui finem, de quo dictum est, viam munit. Id quod vel hinc apparet, quod inter eos partes docendi in Ecclesia inferiorib. fercommittuntur, ut primicerij huius ordinis & qui ingenio praestant, illis, quas diximus, sublimioribus artibus in Aulis liberius vacare queant. Quarto, experientia testatur, quod etiam virorum doctissimorum, quos vel Iesuitae ipsi pro Catholicis coguntur agnoscere, calculo confirmatur, Iesuitas religioni Romano-Catholicae intra Europam magis obstitisse, quam ut eandem promoverint. De quo aliquot inter nos praestantissimorum virorum, ex ipso etiam Ecclesiastico Ordine, querimonias me non semel audire memini.
units.tr: To these things, then, what shall we say? First, I am forced to wonder at those who believe that the Roman Catholic religion, as it now is, has lasted through the world for scarcely fifteen hundred years before Ignatius Loyola was born on earth, and who yet allow themselves to be persuaded that the Catholic religion cannot stand in Poland without the Jesuits' labour, as if it had flourished so splendidly in our Poland for so many hundreds of years. Next I say that Christ and the Apostles, from the very beginning, provided abundantly by sufficient means not only for the spread of religion but also for its eternal preservation. So that the Church, as long as it walks simply along the path of truth, has no need of any new and extraordinary means. Yet these men ordained not Jesuits (as far as I know), but bishops, elders, teachers, ministers, deacons, and so on. And since not only the names of those offices but also the persons to whom their care has been entrusted have survived among us, who can doubt that these, provided they do their duty, will tend religion rightly, just as the Jesuits, who are nowhere to be found in Poland, do not? Thirdly, I say further that the care and propagation of religion is the smallest part of the Jesuit design: which indeed they themselves no longer care for, except insofar as this pretext paves the way for them to their principal aim of their Institute, of which I have spoken. This is evident even from this: that among them the parts of teaching in the Church are committed to the lower men, so that the chiefs of this Order and those who excel in talent may be freer to devote themselves in the courts to those more lofty arts we have mentioned. Fourth, experience bears witness, and the reckoning confirms what even the most learned men, whom the Jesuits themselves are forced to acknowledge as Catholics, have said: that the Jesuits have hindered the Roman Catholic religion within Europe more than they have advanced it. Concerning this I remember hearing complaints not once from some of the most distinguished men among us, even from the ecclesiastical order itself.

units.la: Hoc ipsum vero cum multis prorsus incredibile videatur, his illud rationibus ulterius declaro: Ad experientiam quod attinet, negari non potest, solius Iesuitica bilis praefervidae astui imputandum esse, quod Romano-Catholica religio hodie in amplissimo Britanniae majoris regno tanto studio premitur & opprimitur, ut nunc etiam post exactos Jesuitas, Sacerdotum secularium usu penitus priventur, & sic Regis clementissimi beneficia gaudere nequeant. Eandem calamitatem Catholici ante annos non adeo multos in Scotia Iesuitarum culpa perpessi sunt. Cum enim illorum nonnulli in Regno illo Conjurationis cujusdam, quae contra Regem Scotiae in Hispania à P. Criechtonio Iesuita instituta erat, tabulas hinc inde inter Catholicos clanculum circumferrent, quibus illi subscribere debebant: Reprodita, Exprimaria Scotiae nobilitate complures, qui habebant ceu columnae religionis Romano-Catholicae in praedicto Regno fuerant, extremum vitae fortunarum omnium discrimen adierunt. Sed & reliqui Catholici omnes cum ipsa religione, cui Rex antehac non admodum adversari videbatur, in justissimum Regis odium incurrerunt: Ea ratione, ut in hunc usque diem miseri illi facinoris Iesuitici poenas luere cogantur. Et quid aliud Hungaros & Transylvanos non ita dudum ad eum modum exacerbavit, ut una cum Iesuitis omnes Catholicos Sacerdotes, quos nancisci potuerunt, male tractatos ex finibus suis expulerint, quam importunus ille Iesuitarum fervor? Dum hi supremi Magistratus authoritate & favore freti, praedictarum Provinciarum reliquas libertates tanto impetu invadunt, ut incolae, qui hactenus omnia pertulerant, has ultimas Iesuitarum injurias perferre nequiverint, & extrema potius remedia arripuerint: Ad quod eos haud dubie vicinarum Provinciarum perspecta calamitas animabat. Nec ego dubito, quin inter nos etiam rebus turbatis Catholici religioni magnum aliquod infortunium conflaturi sint, siquidem diutius inter nos conversari debeant. Cuius rei cum inter nos tum alibi haec abundantissima causa est, quod hic livor illa, quae nobis tantopere commendatur, docendi facultate non contentus, entus, machinationibus suis publicam Magistratus authoritatem praetendit. Quae res ut forte plebeculam territat, ita cordatiores quosq; vehementer offendit, studia eorum suspecta facit, & quod inquisitimum est, Magistratum, sicut & ipsum Clerum, publico odio exonit, eiusdemque authoritatem subditis contemptibilem reddit. Haec igitur Catholicae religionis damna si cum profectibus comparentur, quos Iesuitae intra Europam in eiusdem propagatione fecerunt, tantum fortasse vix superfuturum est, ut gloriabunda illorum jactantia respondeat.
units.tr: But since this may seem utterly incredible to many, I explain it further by these reasons. As for experience, it cannot be denied that it must be imputed to the fiery heat of Jesuit bile alone that the Roman Catholic religion today is pressed and oppressed with such zeal in the wide kingdom of Greater Britain that, even now after the Jesuits have been expelled, the Catholics are wholly deprived of the use of secular priests, and so cannot enjoy the benefits of the most merciful King. Not many years ago the Catholics in Scotland suffered the same calamity through the Jesuits' fault. For when some of them in that realm carried round, secretly among the Catholics, lists to which they were to subscribe, relating to a certain conspiracy against the King of Scotland which Father Crichton, a Jesuit, had set up in Spain, many of the foremost nobility of Scotland, who had been as pillars of the Roman Catholic religion in that kingdom, faced the last peril of life and fortune. And not only that, but all the other Catholics, together with the religion itself, which the King had until then not seemed greatly to oppose, incurred the most just hatred of the King, to such an extent that to this day those wretches are compelled to pay the penalties of the Jesuit crime. And what else, not so long ago, so exasperated the Hungarians and Transylvanians to such a degree that, together with the Jesuits, they expelled from their territories all the Catholic priests they could lay hands on, treating them badly, if not that troublesome zeal of the Jesuits? While these men, relying on the authority and favour of the supreme magistrate, assailed the remaining liberties of those provinces with such violence that the inhabitants, who until then had endured everything, could not bear these last injuries of the Jesuits, and seized rather the extreme remedies: to which the plainly visible calamity of the neighbouring provinces undoubtedly spurred them on. Nor do I doubt that among us too, once affairs are disturbed, the Catholics will bring some great misfortune upon their religion, if indeed they are to live among us for any length of time. The most abundant cause of this, both among us and elsewhere, is that this envy, which is so highly commended to us, not content with the faculty of teaching, lays claim by its machinations to the public authority of the magistrate. This, as it perhaps frightens the common folk, so it deeply offends the more thoughtful, makes their studies suspect, and, what is most to be feared, burdens the magistrate, as well as the clergy itself, with public hatred, and makes its authority contemptible to the subjects. If these losses to the Catholic religion are therefore weighed against the advances which the Jesuits have made in spreading it within Europe, there will perhaps hardly be enough left over to match their boastful bragging.

units.la: Veruntamen ut huius etiam infortunij culpam eis condonemus, si doctrinam Iesuiticam extra se & extra hos excessus afstimemus, in eadem nihil, quod tanto praeconio dignum sit, reprehendetur. Religio enim vel voce, vel honesta vita conservatione, vel scriptis propagatur & defenditur. Vocis ministerium Concíones & audiendarum confessionum artificium comprehendit. In concionibus Iesuitae ut plurimum subtiles, diserti, & in concitandis affectibus acres, vehementes & impetuosi esse consueverunt: ut imbecilles & incautos animos movere & percellere possint. Haec autem qualescunq; dotes, quae in sincera pietatis schola non perinde aestimandae sunt, corrumpit & cordatioribus suspectas facit, primum locutionis sive actionis (hanc quidam hypocrisin vocari dicunt) gesticulatoria levitas, nimiumq; fucandi sermonis studium, & qui sub hoc praelucet, ardentissimae ambitionis affectus. Quorum utrumq; nescio quid non Apostolicum sapit. Deinde deformat eas ista inexusta calumniandi & conviciandi libido, qua plurunq; in adversarios debacchantur. Idque ut plebis animos incendant, & exasperent: Cum interim adversarios, quos lucrari debebant, magis indurent. Me quidem haec ita offendunt, ut vilissimi pagi parochum in urbium concionantem audire malim, quam qui in universa Polonia inveniri queat, disertisimum Iesuitam.
units.tr: Yet, that we may pardon them even for this misfortune, if we judge their Jesuit doctrine apart from them and apart from these excesses, nothing in it will be found that deserves such great praise. For religion is propagated and defended by the voice, by the keeping of an honest life, or by writings. The office of the voice comprises sermons and the art of hearing confessions. In sermons the Jesuits are for the most part accustomed to be subtle, eloquent, and keen, vehement and impetuous in stirring the emotions, so that they can move and strike weak and unwary minds. But these gifts, whatever they are, which are not to be valued in the same way in the school of sincere piety, are corrupted and make them suspect to the more thoughtful: first, the gesturing levity of their speech or action (some call this hypocrisy), an excessive zeal for varnishing their speech, and the most ardent ambition that shines through it. Both of these have a flavour of something not apostolic. Next, that unrestrained lust for slandering and reviling, with which they very often rage against their adversaries, disfigures them. And they do this to inflame and exasperate the minds of the common people, while meanwhile they harden the adversaries whom they ought to have won. For my part, these things so offend me that I would rather hear the parson of the meanest village preach than the most eloquent Jesuit who can be found in all of Poland.

units.la: Ad confessionariorum artificium quod attinet, non inficias eo, hoc venationis Iesuiticae accipiuum instrumentum & per quam commodum rete esse. Neque tamen hoc ipsum cautè hactenus disponere potuerunt, ut illa omnium arcanorum perscrutatio, peccatorumque interdum non satis pudicum examen, cum satisfactionis illa insidiosa, multoties jam avara impositione non plurimos offenderit & à Catholica communione ita repulerit, ut ab eadem propter ipsos praecipue Iesuitas penitus abhorreant. Quantum ad vitae conservationem, eam quidem ita hactenus instituerunt, ut nimis conspicua illa vitiorum ulcera, quibus Clerus hactenus ad eum modum deformatus, Laicisq; exosus redditus fuit, fluose vitarint. Neq; tamen in hoc etiam propositio tam constantes aut circumspecti fuerunt, non in opposito arboris scientiae boni & mali fructus se in ijsde proderent. Dum enim ab una parte miraculosam quandam vitae continentiam, angelicam castitatem, religiosaq; pietatis devotum studium ostentant: ab altera parte profundae avaritiae tam diras lues & circumveniendarum nobilium Familiarum viduarumq; & orphanorum decipiendorum tam callidum artificium deprehenditur, ut hoc ipsum prudentioribus in hominibus tam religiosis summae admirationi fuerit. Ut interim superiorem artium Iesuiticarum chorum heic intactum reliquam, de quibus tam multa jam dicenda fuerunt.
units.tr: As for the art of the confessors, I do not deny that this is a very useful instrument and a quite convenient net for the Jesuit hunt. Yet they have not so far been able to manage it cautiously enough. That complete probing of every secret, and the sometimes not very modest examination of sins, together with that insidious imposition of satisfaction, which is often greedy, have offended not a few people and driven them so far from the Catholic communion that they shrink from it, chiefly because of the Jesuits themselves. As for the preservation of life, they have so far arranged it so that they have avoided those conspicuous ulcers of vice by which the clergy has hitherto been so disfigured and made hateful to the laity. Yet in this too they have not been so consistent or circumspect, and the fruits of good and evil of the tree of knowledge appear in them in the opposite way. For while on the one hand they display a kind of miraculous continence, angelic chastity and a devoted zeal for religious piety, on the other hand a dreadful plague of deep avarice is detected, and such a cunning craft of circumventing noble families, widows and orphans that this very thing has caused great astonishment even to the more prudent men among such religious people. Meanwhile I leave untouched here the rest of the Jesuit arts, about which so much had to be said.

units.la: Restat scriptio Iesuitica, in qua fere summus Instituti huius excellentiae gradus constituir, necid prorsus vanum censeri debet. Negari enim non potest, dictionis Iesuiticae charaterem per se tersum & argutum. Orationem etiam, si artificium flectes, floridam simul & rvofam esse. Quae scriptionis virtutes ad illeciendam & capiendam juventutem non iguam vim habent, quae etiam Iesuitas harum praecipue rerum admiratione suspicere & stari solet. Qui vero seriopietatis studio afficiuntur, haec tanto minus curant, quanto in sce rebus nimia Iesuitarum affectatio evidentior est: non aliter quam si omnibus veribus & recentibus Sophistis aut ipsis etiam rabulis palmam vellent praeripere. Veritatis item sermo simplex est & esse debet: Inprimis vero Christianae religionis tractatio huiusmodi fucata & colorata orationis lenocinia avertsatur & respuit, tanquam corruptarū urientium aurium non satis castum delinimentum. Prudentissimi denique, quique incorruptissime judicant, sic sentiunt Iesuitas suis hactenus argutijs & concitatis scriptis catenus saltem profecisse, ut Catholicos suos inflammatos concitaverint, partem vero adversariam acuerint & obfirmaverint: Ut sic bellum illud religiosum, quo ceu Causone quodam Europa adhuc amburitur, tanto periculosius exarserit. Quemadmodum nostris ipsimet oculis cernimus.
units.tr: There remains Jesuit writing, in which almost the highest degree of excellence of this Institute is thought to lie, and it should not be considered altogether worthless. For it cannot be denied that the Jesuit style is polished and witty in itself. The oratory too, if one looks at its art, is at once flowery and fluent. These qualities of writing have no small power to attract and capture the young, and they are accustomed to admire the Jesuits especially for these things. But those who are moved by a zeal for serious piety care for them the less, the more evident the excessive affectation of the Jesuits is in such matters. It is no different from wanting to snatch the palm from all the most skilled sophists, or even from mere wranglers. The speech of truth is simple, and ought to be. Above all, the treatment of the Christian religion shuns and rejects such painted and coloured embellishments of speech as an insufficiently chaste charm for ears that are corrupt and itching. Lastly, the most prudent and most impartial judges think that the Jesuits, with their clever and inflammatory writings, have so far achieved at least this: they have stirred up and inflamed their own Catholics, but have sharpened and hardened the opposing party. So that religious war, by which Europe is still burning as if by some fire, has flared up all the more dangerously, as we see with our own eyes.

units.la: Quod autem de barbarorum in utraque India conversione pro Iesuitis adducitur, illud ex ijs locis petitum est, ex quibus aliquis non solum verum dicere, sed etiam secure mentiri possit. In Polonia praesertim & in illa explorationis difficultate, postquam Caftilienfes & Lufitani nullum extraneum in illas regiones admittunt. Ideoque his nil aliud quam vulgatum illud respondeo: En Rhodus en saltus: De Haereticorum in his terris conversione rem non prorsus nego, ut de qua oculorum aspectus testetur. Opus tamen ipsum non tam doctrinae Iesuiticae extraordinariae virtuti, quam argumentorum aureorum & argenteorum ponderi asscribendum censeo, quibus utuntur, quorumque perennem copiam eis Ponti- ficis Romani favor Aulaeque Polonicae jucundus calor sufficit: Inter quae tamen heiinter nos quandoque vitrea concurrunt pro quibus alibi in vicinia, ferrea substituunt. Quod genus conversionis Paulus Apostolus haud dubie eversionem seu potius corruptionem dixisset.
units.tr: What is brought forward on behalf of the Jesuits concerning the conversion of barbarians in both Indies was taken from places where a man can not only tell the truth but also lie with impunity. This is especially so in Poland, given that difficulty of investigation, since the Castilians and Portuguese admit no foreigner into those regions. So to this I answer only with the well-known saying: Here is Rhodes, here jump! I do not altogether deny the conversion of heretics in these lands, since the sight of our eyes bears witness to it. Yet I think the work itself should be ascribed not so much to the extraordinary virtue of Jesuit doctrine as to the weight of the golden and silver arguments they use, whose perpetual supply is provided by the favour of the Roman Pontiff and the pleasant warmth of the Polish court. Among these arguments, however, glass sometimes clashes with us here, for which elsewhere in the neighbourhood they substitute iron. Such a kind of conversion the Apostle Paul would undoubtedly have called overthrow, or rather corruption.

units.la: Ad rerum Moscoviticarum successus quod attinet, illi revera nobis hactenus non cognita fastum ostentati sunt: quorum etiam praecox spes Gentem Iesuiticam ad eum modum inflavit, ut omnia sibi deinceps licere putaret. Qualia vero nunc ex ijs locis per repetitos nuncios constanter afferantur, te non ignorare credo. Iesuitas quidem audio narrationi huic acerrime contradicere, quod ipsum indicio est, rem ipsorum ubi agi, ut quicunque effectus (utinam bonus) secuturus sit, non alijs eum quam ipsis imputare possimus. Interim tamen nosti, quale meum ab initio, quam primum consiliorum istorum aliquid in vulgus emanavit, de molitionibus illis judicium fuerit. Ipsi nempe causae in genere melius fundamentum optabam. Deinde rem per se periculi plenam esse aperte profitebar. Meministi etiam me de his conatibus Horatianum illud usurpare: Nondum expiatis uncta cruoribus, Periculosae plenum opus aleae, Tractas, & incedis per ignes Suppositos cineri doloso.
units.tr: As for the successes in Muscovite affairs, indeed they have displayed a boastfulness hitherto unknown to us. Their premature hope of these things has so puffed up the Jesuit race that it thought everything henceforth was permitted to it. I believe you are not unaware what is now constantly reported from those places by repeated messengers. I hear that the Jesuits vigorously contradict this account, which is itself a sign that the matter is theirs. Whatever effect follows, (would that it were good), we can impute it to no one but them. Meanwhile you know what my judgment on those undertakings was from the beginning, as soon as something of these plans came out among the public. I had wished for a better foundation for the cause in general. Then I openly declared that the affair itself was full of danger. You also remember that I applied to these attempts that line of Horace: "Not yet cleansed from blood, you take up a work full of perilous hazard, and walk through fires laid beneath treacherous ashes."

units.la: Denique sic prae me semper suli, si Iesuitae negotio huic se immiscerent, nullum eius boni eventum expectandum, hos enim omnia turbaturos. Et si res felicissime cadat, Imperium illud ab ipsis perturbatum & motibus intestinis repletum iri, qui nobis tempore forsitan non aequissimo negocium facessere possent, quemadmodum in Suecia nobis non ita dudum accidit: Quam verus autem, & falsus in his omnibus fuerim, ipsum tempus revelabit, & tum nos etiam de Iesuitarum in convertendis barbaris studio rectius poterimus judicare.
units.tr: Finally, I always said openly that if the Jesuits mixed themselves into this business, no good outcome was to be expected, for they would disturb everything. Even if the affair turned out most happily, that empire would be thrown into confusion by them and filled with internal disturbances, which might cause us trouble at an inopportune time, as happened to us not long ago in Sweden. How true or false I have been in all this, time itself will reveal, and then we will be able to judge more rightly also of the Jesuits' zeal in converting barbarians.

units.la: Religionis Conservatrici propagationi subjungitur institutendae juventutis negotium, Iesuitarum opera carere nullo modo queat. Et hic praeteextus superioribus aestimationis pondere non multum cedit, cujus tamen vanitatem in omni disciplinarum genere exercitatissimi, qui Romano-Catholicam religionem publice profitentur & defendunt, jamdudum Orbi domonstrarunt. Rationibus firmissimis evidenter ostendentes: Iesuitas primum & Iesuitarum Institutum bonis literis & earum refloerescenti splendori plus offuisse quam eas demum promoverint. Ostendentes insuper, Disciplinam Iesuiticam meram corruptelam esse ingeniorum: quorum videlicet aciem retundat & pro eo quod illa liberali institutione informare, & excitare debebat, quendam potius enervem stuporem inducat.
units.tr: Attached to the propagation of the conserving religion is the business of educating youth, which cannot in any way do without the work of the Jesuits. This pretext does not yield much in weight of esteem to the earlier ones, but its emptiness has long since been shown to the world by those most practised in every kind of learning, who publicly profess and defend the Roman Catholic religion. They demonstrate with the firmest arguments that the Jesuits, and the Jesuit Institute, have harmed good letters and their flourishing splendour more than they have promoted them. They further show that Jesuit discipline is a pure corruption of minds: it blunts their edge, and instead of forming and stirring them by that liberal education which it ought to provide, it induces a kind of enervated stupor.

units.la: Qua de re aliquot inter nos praestantissimos non semel conquerentes audivi, qui hodie in praecipuis Reipubl. muneribus versantur, cum dicerent, se coactos esse Iesuitica institutione. iis vitia aut peregrinando corrigere, aut eadem postquam jam ad Remp. animum appliverant, ipso rerum usu dedisce re. Quorum judicio Experientia astipulatur, cum constet, er ipsos Haereticos, quos haec gens nempe pro talibus tractari vult & haberi, Viros iniri in omni disciplinarum genere exercitatos, qui ad omnia Reipub. munia idonei essent, i invidia eos premeret: etsi Iesuitica institutione nullo unquam tempore usi sint. Quomounque tamen haec se habeant, illud apud me fixum manet: Si, quae Iesuitis hac in parte ab quib. tribuuntur, omnia verissima essent, & ipsi in Poloniam nostram alteras Athenas portassent, illud tamen nimis vile pretium esse aestimandum, pro patria libertate, quam hac opera licitantur. Cum praesertim erudita doctrinae fructus aliunde non minus comde, quam a Iesuitis habere possimus.
units.tr: On this matter I have heard several of our most outstanding men, who today hold the chief offices in the Commonwealth, complaining more than once. They said that they had been compelled either to correct their vices by travelling abroad, or to unlearn them by the very practice of affairs, after they had applied their minds to public business. Experience agrees with their judgment, since it is established that the Heretics themselves, whom this race wants to be treated and regarded as such, men trained in every kind of learning and fit for all the offices of the Commonwealth, were oppressed by envy, although they never at any time used Jesuit instruction. However these things stand, this remains fixed with me: even if everything attributed to the Jesuits in this respect were most true, and they had brought another Athens to our Poland, still that would be reckoned too cheap a price for the liberty of the fatherland, which they bid for by this work. Especially since we can have the fruit of learned teaching from elsewhere no less conveniently than from the Jesuits.

units.la: His tertio loco a nonnullis subjungitur, Iesuitas tamen homines esse actuales; eorum in rebus arduis expediendis magna sit dexteritas, eximia fides, &c. ultis hoc in ore est, qui pro Iesuitis niuntur, quos equidem admirari soleo. Quod nempe ualitatem hanc Iesuitas ita tribuunt, ut propter illam eos laudent, eosdem propter eareendos, & fovendos statuant. Nimis enim mirabile mihi hoc in Religiosorum tam relifo Ordine epitheton videtur, cum hoc potius Davi alicujus Terentiani attributum sit, i sua veteratoria calliditate & panurgia omnia turbat & involvit. Ego itaque Poloniae lilites potius & Aulicos, mihi vero Servitores actuales, Ecclesiae autem Monachos & Religiosos pios, doctos, & devotos opto. Verum tamen si quod res est fateri volumus, Epitheton hoc Iesuitis nimis vere competit, de quo totus Orbis, inprimis tamen Europa adeo lulenter testatur. Et nos etiam hactenus actualitatem illorum ita sumus experti, ut si inter sad huc modum diu pergere debeat, de illis Comicum illud recte usurpaturi simus. Quod annitantur ex uniis nuptiis geminas nobis effecturi sint, duplicato nimirum quo praesentia urgemur, infortunio. Sed quid putabimus Augustinum reliquosque ipsorum temrum Patres de hujusmodi actualibus Monachis fuisse dicturos? Aut quis etiam in securibus negotiis tam demens fuit, ut in servo nequam veteratoriam calliditatem laudarit, ut exploratoris exteri solertiam ita commendarit, ut eum propterea sibi fovendum existiassei? Te igitur heic etiam scire velim, ingenio praestante & versatili nihil pernicious esse, si vires suas ad res malas applicet. Ideoque hanc ipsam Iesuitarum actualitatem egoet inter justissimas metus nostri causas refero, quae nobis veternum excutere, nosque ad seam rerum nostratium curam excitare deberet.
units.tr: In the third place, some add that the Jesuits are nevertheless active men, that their skill in dispatching difficult affairs is great, their fidelity outstanding, and so on. This is on the lips of all who press for the Jesuits, and I am accustomed indeed to wonder at it. For they attribute this ability to them in such a way that they praise them for it, and decide that they should be cherished and fostered because of it. This epithet seems to me far too strange for a religious Order so grave, since it is rather the attribute of some Davus from Terence, who throws everything into confusion and tangles it by his crafty cunning and knavery. I therefore wish the Polish nobles and courtiers to be active servants, but for the Church I wish monks and religious who are pious, learned and devout. Yet if we want to confess what is the case, this epithet fits the Jesuits all too truly, as the whole world, and Europe especially, bears witness so loudly. We too have so far experienced their activity in such a way that, if it must continue in this manner for long, we shall be about to use aptly that line of the comic poet about them: that they are going to bring us two misfortunes from one marriage, namely a doubling of the misfortune by which we are already pressed. But what do we think Augustine and the other Fathers of that time would have said of such active monks? Or who was so foolish, even in serious business, as to praise a bad servant for his crafty cunning, or to commend the skill of a foreign spy so highly that he thought he should therefore be cherished by himself? I should like you to know here too that nothing is more harmful than a gifted and versatile talent when it applies its strength to evil ends. Therefore I myself count this very activity of the Jesuits among our most just causes of fear, which ought to shake off our lethargy and rouse us to care for our own affairs.

units.la: Illud autem quod de expediendi dexteritate adjicitur, testimonio destituitur. Quid enim egregie natio haec inter nos praestitit, quid vel tam dextre expedivit, aut quod potius bonum on impedivit? Nisi forte amissam Sueciam, afflictam Galliam, tentatam Scotiam, Anlicas conspirationes & tot nobilium hominum tragicum interitum, Venetianas practicas, Moscovitias turbas, perturbata Vngariam, oppressam Styriam, Carinthia, Carniolam r quae hactenus in Polonia adiderunt aulica progymnasmata, pro Iesuitica dexteritatis veribus nobis sint habenda? Ad res quidem arduas aggrediendas & invadendas satis aduc audax est haec secta, audacia vero illius e vetus is hactenus ubique sequitur, ut turbae maimae ab illis excitentur: tales nimirum, quae citra infiniti fere sanguinis effusionem adhuc ec sisti nec sedari potuerunt. Quem igitur hae cagendi dexteritas delectat, is videat & proideat, ne quid Respub. Iesuitica detrimenti in Polonia capiat.
units.tr: It is also said that the Jesuits are skilful at extricating themselves from difficulties, but this claim has no evidence to support it. For what has this nation achieved among us so distinctly, what has it managed so adroitly, or rather, what good has it not hindered? Unless perhaps the lost Sweden, the afflicted France, the attacked Scotland, the English conspiracies and the tragic deaths of so many noble men, the Venetian intrigues, the Muscovite troubles, the disturbed Hungary, and the oppressed Styria, Carinthia and Carniola, which they have hitherto performed in Poland as courtly exercises, are to be counted for us as proofs of Jesuit skill? To undertake and attack great affairs this sect is certainly bold enough, and its boldness has hitherto everywhere been so successful that huge tumults have been stirred up by them, such as could not be checked or calmed without the shedding of almost infinite blood. Let him therefore who delights in this skill of stirring things up see to it and take care that the Jesuit commonwealth does not suffer harm in Poland.

units.la: Nec id quod de illorum eximia fide praedicatur, certioris fidei est: Quod tamen illis rite persuaderi poterit, qui vel Iesuitarum arcanas designationes prorsus ignorant, vel vibus illi os alias ita oblinunt, ut propter certas causas ad eorum palatum omnia dicant & faciant. Quod si tamen aliquis fidem Iesuiticam verbis extollere velit, dico eam, quana quanta est, totam exteris, & quidem citra ullum boni Polonici respectum, addictam esse & artissime obligatam. Hujusmodi inquam exteris, qui etsi corpore a nobis absunt, consilijs tamen & occultis machinationibus, nimium interdum familiariter inter nos conversantur. Cum hic ergo si forte aliqua nobis controversia incidat, ecquid illis nobis de Iesuitarum fide polliceri poterunt? Annon vero in Gallijs, Anglia, Scotia, Vngaria,
units.tr: Nor is what is claimed about their remarkable faithfulness any more trustworthy. Yet it can readily be persuaded to those who either are utterly ignorant of the Jesuits' secret designs, or who are otherwise so dazzled by them that for certain reasons they say and do everything to please their palate. But if anyone nonetheless wishes to extol Jesuit fidelity in words, I say that all of it, however great it is, is devoted and very tightly bound to foreigners, and indeed without any regard for the good of Poland. I mean foreigners who, though absent from us in body, nonetheless, through their counsels and secret machinations, sometimes associate very familiarly among us.
