If therefore some controversy arises between us here, what can they promise us about Jesuit fidelity? Have they not already, in France, England, Scotland, Hungary and Venice, published sufficiently clear proofs of their faithfulness, if we look at our own times? And why are words needed in a matter so manifest, when there is today no Christian European nation that does not complain of Jesuit treachery, or at least of the suggestion and execration of treachery, Spain alone excepted.

units.la: Kk Venetijs satis jam conspicua fidelitatis suæ documenta in publicum ediderunt, si ad nostra tempora respicimus: Et quid in re manifesta verbis opus est, cum nulla hodie Europæa Christiana natio sit, quæ non de Iesuitarum perfidia aut saltem perfidiæ suggestione et exsecratione conqueratur, si unam Hispaniam excipias.
units.tr: Venice has already published sufficiently conspicuous documents of their fidelity to the public, and why are words needed in a matter so manifest, when there is today no Christian European nation that does not complain of Jesuit treachery, or at least of the suggestion and execration of treachery, Spain alone excepted.

units.la: His denique à nonnullis additur, Inconveniens esse ut Iesuitas Poloni expellant, cum Galli, qui propter longe graviores causas eos eiecerunt, eosdem revocaverint, ubi etiam adhuc citra ullum Reipublicæ incommodum vivant, &c.
units.tr: Finally, some add that it is inconvenient for the Poles to expel the Jesuits, since the French, who expelled them for far more serious reasons, have recalled them, where even now they live without any inconvenience to the commonwealth, and so on.

units.la: Ego vero novi Iesuitas in Galliam reversos esse, sed quod à Gallis revocati fuerint, ne ipsi quidem, quamvis multa dicant, facile dicturi sunt. Interim vero artes, quibus se in Gallijs denuò insinuarunt, tales sunt, ut propter illas ipsas eiectionem eorum in ter nos maturandam existimem. Ex illis enim liquidissimè perspicitur, quantum hic Genius intra Europam in versando et circumagendo rerum cardine polleat.
units.tr: I know indeed that the Jesuits have returned to France, but why they were recalled by the French, not even they themselves, however much they may say, will readily explain. Meanwhile the arts by which they have again insinuated themselves into France are such that, because of those very arts, I think their expulsion from among us must be hastened. For from them it is most clearly seen how much this Genius within Europe prevails in turning and manipulating the hinge of affairs.

units.la: Sic enim nos fe debes, Iesuitas in Galliam non propter aliquem eorum usum, quo regnum illud carere non posset, receptos esse: sed ad vehementissimam Romani Pontificis instantiam, Quem videlicet Rex in tam infida cum vicino potentissimo pace offensum nolebat, Cum tamen serium Catholicismi studium vix probaturus erat, quamdiu Iesuitas regno arceret.
units.tr: For you must understand that the Jesuits were received into France not because of some use of theirs without which that kingdom could not manage, but at the most urgent insistence of the Roman Pontiff, whom the King, having taken offence at so faithless a peace with a very powerful neighbour, did not wish to offend. Yet he would scarcely approve of a serious zeal for Catholicism for as long as he kept the Jesuits out of the kingdom.

units.la: Interea ne illud quidem dubium est, eos qui Pontifici in restitutione illa promovenda operam suam apud Regem præstiterunt, majora præmia consecutos esse, quam omnes quicunque hactenus Reipublicæ vel inter nos vel alibi militarunt. Quamvis non desint, qui existimant, Henricum Quartum hac etiam ratione securitati suæ consulere voluisse, quod aliàs à Iesuitarum insidijs nunquam tutus esset futurus.
units.tr: Meanwhile there is no doubt that those who lent their efforts to the Pope in promoting that restoration with the King obtained greater rewards than all who have hitherto served the commonwealth, either among us or elsewhere. Yet there are not wanting those who think Henry IV also wished to provide for his own safety on this ground, since otherwise he would never have been safe from the ambushes of the Jesuits.

units.la: Quod autem hactenus pacatè dicuntur vivere, id si verum est, admirationem meretur: quantumvis causas gravissimas habeant, cur se in tam recente antea actorum memoria ad tempus cohibeant, sub illius præsertim Regis imperio, cuius authoritatem, quam sibi rebus gestis comparavit, non immeritò venerentur et metuunt. Quid autem futurum sit, si præsenti rerum Gallicarum capiti aliquid humani accideret, rerumque administratio, ut antehac factum meminimus, admodum norennes hæredes devolueretur, facile erit divinare. Cum verendum sit, Galliam tandem commisi in recipiendis Iesuitis erroris effectum suo magno malo sensuram.
units.tr: That they are said to live quietly until now, if it is true, deserves wonder, however grave the reasons they have for holding themselves back for a time, given how recent the memory of their past deeds is, especially under the rule of that king whose authority, which he won by his achievements, they rightly venerate and fear. What will happen if something human befell the present head of French affairs, and the administration of affairs fell, as we remember happened before, to very young heirs, will be easy to guess. Since it is to be feared that France, having at last committed the error of receiving the Jesuits, will feel the result to her great harm.

units.la: Non vero hactenus causa nulla, per Dei gratiam urget, ut Gallorum similes casus, tam ambiguos aleam subeamus.
units.tr: But thanks be to God, no cause yet urges us to undergo, with such uncertain dice, the fate of the French.

units.la: Hæc fere pro Iesuitis ab ijs afferuntur, qui persuasi sunt, nec Rempublicam, nec Ecclesiam gentis istius opera commodè carere posse. Præter quos etiam alij sunt, qui et Iesuitarum acta omnium minimè probent, in eosdem tamen nil gravius statui patiuntur, quòd hoc citra maxima Reipublicæ incommodante tentari quidem posse existiment.
units.tr: These are about all the arguments put forward for the Jesuits by those who are persuaded that neither the commonwealth nor the Church can conveniently do without the labour of that order. Besides these there are others who by no means approve of all the Jesuits' doings, yet they allow nothing more severe to be decided against them, because they think this can be done without the gravest harm to the commonwealth.

units.la: Itaque ergo Poloniæ res jam eò redierit, ut aut Iesuitæ et Iesuitismus nobis tolerandi, omnesque illorum machinationes cum tam præsenti Reipublicæ periculo perpetiendæ sint, aut extremum rerum discrimen adeundum? Ubi ergo tunc manebunt illa Ordinis istius elogia, quibus ab initio nobis commendati sunt? Quod homines sint inocentissimi, pacifici, quòd spiritualibus contemplationibus toti addicti, in quibus Poloni hujusmodi prorsus Clericos habituri sint, quales jam dudum desiderarint? Ab his ergo talibus ecquid nobis timendum erit?
units.tr: So has the situation in Poland come to this, that either we must tolerate the Jesuits and Jesuitism and endure all their machinations with such a present danger to the commonwealth, or face the extreme crisis? Where then will those praises of this Order remain, by which they were commended to us at the beginning? That these men are most innocent and peaceable, wholly devoted to spiritual contemplation, and that in them the Poles would at last have clergy of exactly the sort they have long desired? Then what shall we have to fear from such men?

units.la: Ego tamen jam dudum novi, Bilem hanc citra molestiam ex Reipub. corpore nunquam evacuatum iri, postquam jam nostra incuria ad viscera tam alte penetravit, ipsaque præcipue vitales partes tam arte obsedit. Existimo tamen periculum aliquanto minus futurum quàm pleriq; sibi imaginentur.
units.tr: I have however long known that this bile will never be drained from the body of the commonwealth without trouble, now that through our carelessness it has penetrated so deep into the vital organs and besieged especially the vital parts so skilfully. Yet I think the danger will be somewhat less than most people imagine.

units.la: Quæ enim incommoda nobis narrant, quæ Iesuitarum expulsionem secutura sint, Pontifex, inquiunt, et Hispanus gravissimè offendentur. Magna profecto numina, quorumque ira nobis haud leviter æstimanda est. Quid enim de Polonia futurum existimabis, si Saturnum, et Iovem Europæum tam male dispositos habeat? Ego vero hæc ferre illius Comici expostulatione uti possem, Possumne scire quot mihi hæc Domini perferenda rferendi sint? Ne tamen nimis alicui confidens & securus videar, de utroque alid dicendum erit. Ad Pontificis itaque offensionem quod attinet, de ea quidem nulsdubito, quin nimis certò secutura sit, agnosco etiam eam nobis formidandam esse. Sed vero a Iesuitis longe graviora cogamur metuere, existimo hanc indignationem Pontificis non nimium esse pertimescendam. Spero etiam ad eandem avertendam legitima remedia nobis non esse defutura. Pontifex enim aut bonus est & talis, qui memor sui officij, Regi Poloniae aeque ac omnium aliorum Christianorum regnorum optimum statum promotum & conservatum cupiat. Cum tali itaque sperandum esset nobis facileconturum: si nempe missis legatis ei ad oculum demonstraverimus, Regem Polonicam, nec cum Iesuitis, nec cum Iesuitarum hactenus usitatis artibus diutius consistere potuisse, &c. Nec dubito quin is tempori cessurus & indignationem, si quae oborta fuerit, Reipublicae facile remissurus sit.
units.tr: For what inconveniences they tell us will follow the expulsion of the Jesuits: the Pope, they say, and the Spaniard will be gravely offended. Great divinities indeed, whose anger we must by no means lightly reckon! For what do you think will become of Poland if it has Saturn and Jupiter of Europe so ill-disposed? I could indeed bear these things with that comic complaint: "Can I know how many of these masters' commands I must put up with?" Yet lest I seem too confident and carefree toward anyone, something must be said about both. As regards the Pope's offence, I certainly do not doubt that it will surely follow, and I acknowledge that we must fear it. But since we are forced to dread far graver things from the Jesuits, I think this indignation of the Pope is not to be feared too much. I also hope that legitimate remedies for averting it will not be lacking to us. For the Pope is either good, and such that, mindful of his office, he desires the best state of the Kingdom of Poland, as of all other Christian kingdoms, to be promoted and preserved. With such a man we ought to hope we would easily come to terms, if we sent envoys and plainly showed him that the King of Poland could not remain any longer with the Jesuits, nor with the arts of the Jesuits practised hitherto, and so on. Nor do I doubt that he will yield to the times and will readily remit any indignation that may have arisen against the commonwealth.

units.la: Aut idem malus talisque est, qui suae tantum libidini, citra ullum Reipublicae aut aequitatis respectum indulgeat, omniaque prius sursum deorsum ferri patiatur, quam ut od male ceptum est corrigi sustineat: Tum vero iram eius ne curandam quidem existimo. Neque enim ulla vel divina vel humana Lex Polonos obligat, ut aut summum ipsi periculum sibi scientes accersant, aut Romani P. injusta sibique praejudiciali voluntati se per omnia conforment.
units.tr: Or else he is such a bad man, who indulges only his own lust with no regard for the commonwealth or for justice, and would sooner allow everything to be turned upside down than suffer what has been begun amiss to be corrected. Then indeed I think his anger is not even worth caring about. For no divine or human law binds the Poles either to bring extreme danger upon themselves knowingly, or to conform themselves in everything to the unjust and prejudicial will of the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: Quare in re si meum tibi judicium suspectum esset, Majorum exemplis te patiaris erudiri ut cogites, quid ipsi in simili casu fecerint. Nosti etenim, quanta animorum contentione Romani Pontifices olim Crucigeros contra Regnum Poloniae defendendos suscepserint, amatrocia Regibus nostris plerunque minitati sint. Resque tandem eo processit, ut circa annum 1456. si Aeneae Sylvij epistolis credimus, Romae Excommunicatio contra Regem, quinque Poloniae decreta fuerit. Neque tamen hisce minis, quantum vis ipsius etiam imperatoris Friderici III. indignatio eas acueret, ad eum modum se perterreri passi sunt Majores nostri, ut non potiorem salutis Reipublicae, quam indignationis Pontificiae respectum habuerint. Ovum autem ovo tam simile nunquam esse poterit, quam bene Iesuitarum institutum, mores & actiones cum Crucigerorum ordine, rebusque gestis conveniunt.
units.tr: Therefore, if my judgment in this matter seems suspect to you, allow yourself to be instructed by the examples of our ancestors, and consider what they did in a similar case. You know with how much zeal the Roman Pontiffs once undertook to defend the Knights of the Cross against the Kingdom of Poland, and how often they threatened our kings with dreadful measures. The matter finally went so far that, around the year 1456, if we believe the letters of Aeneas Sylvius, an excommunication was issued at Rome against the King and the decrees of Poland. Yet our ancestors were not frightened by these threats, however much the indignation of the Emperor Frederick III himself sharpened them, and they did not let fear so move them that they had less regard for the safety of the Republic than for the Pope's displeasure. An egg could never be as like an egg as the Jesuit institute, its morals and actions agree with the order of the Knights of the Cross and with what they did.

units.la: Iam ortus ratio & occasio fere eadem utrobique fuit: Utrumque institutum ad unum eundemque finem per diversa saltem media fuit directum: Forma politica ex ceptis paucis circumstantiis eadem fuit: Utrque ordo progressus longe celerrimos fecit, dilatatâque per Christianae religionis & imperij laudem tulit: Uterque tandem à seipso ita degeneravit, ijs, pro quorum defensione instituti fuerant, graves & molesti esse ceperint. Differentia item in eo consistebat, quod Crucigeri professi Milites erant, remque apertis armis conabantur. Majores nostros gererent, quorum legitima remedia Polonis nunquam deerant: Hoc malum intra viscera nostra haerens ijs artibus nos oppugnat, quarum Poloniae anteprorsus imperita fuit. Quae res facit ut existimem, eos nova illius sectae institutum optimum rectissimè aestimare, qui Iesuitas Crucigerorum spurios dicunt. Cum itaque Majoribus nostris olim Pontificis nec indignatio nec authoritas obstiterit, quo minus Crucigerorum injurias acerrime vindicarent, regnumque tuerentur, cur in simili casu hujusmodi bello nos terreri patiamur?
units.tr: Indeed, the origin and occasion were nearly the same on both sides. Each institute was directed to one and the same end, though by different means at least. The political form was the same, apart from a few details. Each order made very rapid progress, spread widely, and won praise for the Christian religion and for its empire. And each in the end degenerated from itself, so that those for whose defence they had been founded began to find them burdensome and troublesome. The difference also lay in this: the Knights of the Cross were professed soldiers and tried to accomplish their aim with open arms, and our ancestors waged war against them, and lawful remedies were never lacking to the Poles. This evil, clinging to our vitals, attacks us with arts in which Poland was utterly inexperienced. This is why I think that those who call the Jesuits bastard Knights of the Cross judge this new sect's institute most rightly. Since, therefore, neither the Pope's displeasure nor his authority stood in the way of our ancestors when they most fiercely avenged the wrongs of the Knights of the Cross and defended the kingdom, why should we allow ourselves to be terrified by such a war in a similar case?

units.la: Sin tamen haec alicui forte nimis antiqua viderentur, illi recentius exemplum habent, ad Avorum memoria accidit.
units.tr: But if these examples seem to anyone too old, they have a more recent one, which happened within the memory of our grandfathers.

units.la: Sigismundus I. quem inter optimos suos Reges Poloniae non immerito recenset, quem Romana sedes adhuc pro genuino obedientiae filio agnoscit & praedicat, Albertum Brandeburgicum cum ditione Borussiaca in fidem & clientelam suam recepit; tum quanpropter abdicatum Crucigerorum ordinem & desertam religionem Romanam non solum a Pontifice, sed ad hujus institutum ab Imperio Romano sub potentissimo Imperatore Carolo Quinto Excommunicatus & proscriptus erat. Aula tamen praecipue Romana fremebat & indignabatur, quod tota Borussia hac ratione ab Ecclesia abalienaretur. Sic Sigismundo parsura fuisset, si Excommunicationis aliquem potentem executorem potuisset habere. Hic enim desiderabatur: quod tamen in susque deque tulit. Et quidem de Regibus nostris dico, cum nostra haec aetas eiusdem magnanimitatis & egregiae fidei in Rempublicam illustre exemplum in ipso Regni Primate habuerit? Fuit is Jacobus Vehanski, Archiepiscopus Gnesnensis, cui cum Romanus Pontifex Excommunicationis telum intentaret, quod animadverteret, eum in consiliis publicis majorem salutis Patriae, quam sedis Romanae respectum habere: Is se adeo non passus est a proposito dimoveri, ut Pontifici potius rescripserit, se si pergeret ei Reipublicae nomine molestiam exhibere, intentatam fulmen in ipsum retorsurum. Quo responso ictus Pontifex Archiepiscopum misit, ut qui nosset hoc ei in Polonia facilius factu quam dictu fuisse. Cujusmodi libertatis spiritum, si ex illius successoribus hodie, sub hac inquam Jesuitica animorum dispositione aliquis sibi usurpare praesumeret, ecquid tu de eo futurum praesagas? Annon ille quanto ocyus ad Patres ire cogeretur? Haec igitur masculae virtutis exempla quoties in Majoribus nostris considero, toties admirari cogor, quae res hodie nostratium Praelatorum animos ita immutarit, ut in multo leviori bus casibus tantas sibi difficultates imaginentur. Dum interdum Pontificis nescio quae Regalia allegant, quae inviolata retineri volunt, sed et Regem ita loqui docent: Non aliter quam si Polonia jam duos Reges haberet, unum Craconiae, alterum Romae. Dum etiam exterorum offensiones saepius ultra modum exaggerant, Reique publicae se tam difficiles praebent. Quem admodum jam aliquoties in deliberationibus de Moldavia, Valachia et tandem etiam Transylvania fieri vidimus. Ideoque sic tandem existimo, eos qui a Pontificis offensione sibi tantopere metuunt, siquidem Jesuitae paulo durius tractari deberent, eo ipso satis demonstrare, quam frigide erga Rempubl. affecti sint, et suspicionem de se non exiguam praebere, quod privata commoda illis Patriae salute potiora sint. Quales si Majores nostri suissent, Borussia nobis hodie carendum, et in hunc usque diem cum Crucigeris colluctandum esset. Sed et hanc scrupulosam in hoc ordine conscientiam nulli alii rei hodie, quam Jesuiticae, de qua dictum est, dispositioni debemus.
units.tr: Sigismund I, whom not undeservedly we count among the best kings of Poland, and whom the Roman See still acknowledges and proclaims as a genuine son of obedience, received Albert of Brandenburg with the Prussian territory into his faith and clientship. For this reason the Order of Knights, having been renounced and the Roman religion abandoned, was excommunicated and proscribed not only by the Pope but, at his instigation, by the Roman Empire under the most powerful Emperor Charles V. Yet the Roman court in particular raged and was indignant that all Prussia should be alienated from the Church in this way. Thus it would have spared Sigismund, had it been able to have some powerful executor of the excommunication. For this was what was lacking; yet he took it lightly. And indeed, do I speak of our kings, when this age of ours has had an illustrious example of the same magnanimity and excellent loyalty to the Republic in the Primate of the Kingdom himself? That was Jacob Uchański, Archbishop of Gniezno. When the Roman Pontiff aimed the weapon of excommunication at him, because he saw that in public counsels he had more regard for the safety of the homeland than for the Roman See, he was so far from allowing himself to be moved from his purpose that he replied to the Pope instead that, if he continued to cause trouble for him in the name of the Republic, he would hurl the thunderbolt aimed at himself back at him. Struck by this answer, the Pontiff sent the Archbishop a message, as one who knew that in Poland this was easier done than said. If someone among his successors today should presume to assume this spirit of liberty, I ask you, under this Jesuit disposition of minds, what do you foresee for him? Would he not be compelled as quickly as possible to go to the Fathers? Whenever I consider these examples of manly virtue in our ancestors, I am forced to marvel at what has so changed the minds of our prelates today that they imagine such great difficulties in much lighter cases. Sometimes they plead certain papal royal prerogatives which they want kept inviolate, and they teach the King to speak thus: "It is just as if Poland already had two kings, one at Kraków and the other at Rome." Sometimes, too, they exaggerate the offences of foreigners beyond measure and show themselves very difficult toward the public business of the Republic, as we have several times already seen in deliberations about Moldavia, Wallachia, and finally even Transylvania. And so I finally judge this: those who fear so greatly the Pope's displeasure, if the Jesuits ought to be treated a little more harshly, by that very fact sufficiently demonstrate how cold they are toward the Republic, and give no small grounds for suspicion about themselves, because their private advantages are dearer to them than the safety of the homeland. Had our ancestors been like this, we would today have to do without Prussia and wrestle with the Knights until this very day. But we owe this scrupulous conscience in this order today to no other cause than to the Jesuit disposition of which I have spoken.

units.la: Ubi tamen mirari cogor, quid hi, qui eis hac in parte eatenus astipulantur, ut Pontificem nulla in re offendi patiantur, posteritati aliquando responderi velint, si nempe illae ex nostrorum temporum historia rescisca, Rempub. Venetam propter improbatas quasdam non maximi momenti constitutiones, pro libertatis suae defensione, Jesuitas ex dominio suo universo expulisse, et intentatam propterea Pontificis excommunicationem, usque ad aperti belli periculum contempsisse: Cum interim Majores sui in Polonia libertatis alumni tam meticulosi fuerint?
units.tr: Yet here I am forced to wonder what those who support them in this respect, so that the Pope be allowed to be offended in no matter, wish to answer to posterity, if, that is, they learn from the history of our own times that the Venetian Republic, in defence of its liberty, expelled the Jesuits from its whole dominion over certain not very important constitutions which it disapproved, and on that account scorned an excommunication that had been threatened, even to the danger of open war. Meanwhile, are our ancestors, the nurslings of Polish liberty, to have been so timid?

units.la: Quod si etiam in his ce rebus nos ad eum modum a Pontificis arbitrio patiemur suspendi, Polonorum conditio multo deterior, adde et servilior futura erit, quam ipsorum Moscorum; qui in consiliis de Repub. nulla alia quam ipsius Principis Reipublicae Regalia respectant aut attendunt.
units.tr: But if we also allow ourselves, in these matters too, to be made dependent on the Pope's will in this way, the condition of the Poles will be far worse, and indeed more servile, than that of the Muscovites themselves, who in their counsels about the Republic consider and heed nothing but the royal prerogatives of their own Prince.

units.la: Ad Hispanum quod attinet, ego non video, quae ei justa offensionis causa a nobis praebeatur, si nos nostrae Reipublicae pro rerum nostrarum exigentia pro viribus studeamus consulere, citra ullum eius praejudicium? Cur etiam Regem illum potentissimum magis offendat, quod nos Jesuitas expellimus, quam nos haberemus offendit, quod ipse eos, ut sibi commendos tam indulgenter fovet? Quid si vero Rex Hispaniae, Rex Poloniae audire vellet (quod equidem quo minus ad libitum consequatur per Jesuitas non stabit) num ad cavendam eius indignationem hoc ei concedendum esset? Si denique eo nos demiserimus ut dominus nobis nihil agere aut tentare liceat, nisi quod aurei velleri probetur, ecquam Rempub. in Polonia habituri sumus?
units.tr: As for the Spaniard, I do not see what just cause of offence is given him by us, if we strive, as our needs demand, to look after our Republic to the best of our strength, without any prejudice to him. Why would that most powerful king be more offended that we expel the Jesuits than we would be offended that he so indulgently cherishes them as commended to himself? What if the King of Spain wished to hear the King of Poland (and whether he will not obtain this at his pleasure through the Jesuits, I for my part will not stand in the way), would this have to be granted him to avoid his indignation? And finally, if we were to lower ourselves to the point where it is permitted for our lord to do or attempt nothing unless it is approved by the Golden Fleece, what Republic would we have in Poland?

units.la: Verum hic nonnulli adhuc pergunt excipere, Etiam domi & intra parietes multos offensum iri. Cuialiqui adjiciunt, si Jesuitae extra regnum proscribi debeat, etiam alios & illos praecipue Evangelicorum ministros una exterminandos, &c.
units.tr: But here some still go on to object: that many will be offended even at home, within our own walls. Others add that if the Jesuits ought to be banished from the kingdom, then other ministers too, especially those of the Evangelicals, must be banished along with them, and so on.

units.la: Ad prius quod attinet de multorum intra domesticos parietes offensione, ego primum nescio scio, quinam illi multi futuri, sint quorum offensionem nobis tam periculosam imagiri debeamus si praesertim reliqui Cleri securitati caveretur? Cum enim hic nil aliud iam salus Reipublicae eiusque in longum propagatio quaeratur, nemo hinc tumultuanoccasionem habere poterit, nisi forte fortunas suas cum Iesuitis ita conjunxerit, ut cautibus illis ipse stare nequeat. Et hi vere illi sunt, qui eorum omnium molitionum & consiliorum, forte etiam contra regnum, sunt conscij: Et quamvis verendum sit, eorum ires esse, quam expediat, ne horum tamen offensio perinde nobis aestimanda est. Cum nedubitet, quin bonorum, qui Rempubl. salvam cupiunt, multo major pars in omnibus Republ. partibus futura sit.
units.tr: As to the first point, concerning the offence of many within the domestic walls: first, I do not know who these many would be whose offence we ought to imagine as so dangerous to us, especially if provision is made for the safety of the rest of the clergy. For since nothing else is now sought than the safety of the Republic and its long-term preservation, no one will have an occasion to stir up tumult from this, unless perhaps he has so bound his fortunes to the Jesuits that he cannot stand by those safeguards himself. And these are truly the men who are privy to all their plots and schemes, perhaps even against the kingdom. And although it is to be feared that their anger is greater than is expedient, nevertheless their offence is not to be reckoned as ours. For there is no doubt that the far greater part of the good men, who desire the Republic to be safe, will be on the side of all the parts of the Republic.

units.la: Sed esto, ut hei forte aliquid nobis molestiae suscipiendum esset; num propterea Medicinam respuemus? Quae purgatio aegroto unquam tam feliciter cessit, ut non aliquid ex illius eratione torminum senserit? Quod si Iesuitarum expulsione illos fatales tumultus ar-tere & praecavere possemus, qui hactenus plerasque Europaeas Provincias tam duriter afflixerunt, quo de egomet plane sum persuasus; Resne digna censebitur, propter quam etiam commodi aliquid patiamur? Si publicae libertati, si regno nihil periculi est, si privatorum corpora, & fortunae in tuto sunt, ecquid tumultamur? Cur exterorum insidias & conspirationes metuimus? Sin vero haec omnia nobis ita imminent, ut Iesuitas eorum, si non principales autores, perniciosos saltem actores, promotores, & internuncios noverimus, ut omnes praeferunt, ecquid amplius cunctabimur?
units.tr: But suppose we had to face some trouble from them: would we on that account reject the medicine? What purgative ever worked so happily that the patient felt none of its gripes? But if by expelling the Jesuits we could check and forestall those deadly tumults which have hitherto harshly afflicted most of the European provinces, as I myself am quite persuaded they could, will that be judged a thing not worth enduring some inconvenience for? If public liberty and the kingdom are in no danger, if the bodies and fortunes of private persons are safe, why do we make an uproar? Why do we fear the snares and conspiracies of foreigners? But if all these things threaten us in such a way that we know the Jesuits, if not as the principal authors, at least as the pernicious agents, promoters and go-betweens, as everyone declares, why shall we delay any longer?

units.la: Ad alios vero, Evangelicorum praesertim Ministros, quod attinet, si in eadem turbapacis & oppugnatae publicae libertatis culpa cum Iesuitis haerent, nil equidem causae dim, quo minus & illi & quicunq; criminis huic quocunq; modo affines deprehenduntur, cum expellantur. In suspicione enim turbatae Reipub. neminem quodcunq; vitae genus tueri teft, aut eidem patrocinari debet.
units.tr: As for the others, especially the ministers of the Evangelicals, if they are involved in the same fault of disturbing the peace and attacking public liberty along with the Jesuits, I see indeed no reason why they should not be expelled as well, whoever of them is found to be connected with that crime in any way. For under suspicion of a disturbed commonwealth, no one, whatever kind of life he leads, can be protected or ought to be defended.

units.la: Sed nunquid haec res cum re aut causa cum causa conferri poterit? Quemnam Pontifim aut Hispanum Ministri illi intra aut extra regnum habent, cui hunc agrum arent aut rant, aut ad quem eis, rebus hic perditis, perfugium pateat? Quales etiam in aula & cir-Reipub. clavum illorum partes sunt, aut in aeternum esse poterunt? Aut quae praedia hi in trimentum nobilitatis coemerunt, quasve immunitates in fraudem Reip. consecuti sunt? et quae etiam illorum vires sunt, propter quas Reipub. formidabiles aut saltem suspecti esse beant? Quorum divitiae fere omnes in lacera & detrita ut plurimum Reverenda, ut notes loquuntur, & Bibliorum, adde si res lauta est, Augustini codice, nudaq; & numerosa hole confiitit? Ipsi deniq; Evangelicorum Ministri annon uniuscujusq; paganii Praefecti su-prioritatem agnoscere eidemq; sefiftere coguntur? Collatio itaque haec prorsus inepta ad- & ridicula est.
units.tr: But can this matter be compared with that, or one cause with another? What Pontifical or Spanish patron do those ministers have inside or outside the kingdom, for whom they plough and sow this field, or to whom a refuge lies open once their affairs here are ruined? What part do they have, or could they ever have, in the court and in the council of the commonwealth? What estates have they bought to the detriment of the nobility, or what immunities have they obtained to the cheating of the Republic? And what powers do they have, by which they could be feared or at least suspected by the commonwealth? Are not their riches almost all in worn and tattered Bibles, "Reverend" as they say, and, if the household is well off, an Augustine codex, and a bare and numerous flock? Finally, are the Evangelical ministers not compelled to acknowledge the superiority of each village prefect and to submit to him? So this comparison is utterly absurd and ridiculous.

units.la: Sunt fortasse & alia quae pro Iesuitis ab illorum fautoribus nobis objici possent, sed ea ex majoris momenti erunt, quam quae hactenus allata sunt.
units.tr: There are perhaps other things which the Jesuits' supporters could throw at us in their favour, but these will be of greater weight than what has been advanced so far.

units.la: Ex his ergo, quae hactenus demonstrata sunt firmiter tandem concludo: Iis qui hoc temre Rempub. restitutam, sanatam & in posterum salvam cupiunt, si ordine procedere, si horum suorum fructum aliquem sibi polliceri volunt, ante omnia operam esse dandam, Iesuita extra regnum abigantur: sed ita ut abactos obdito pessulo reditu prohi-ant.
units.tr: From what has been demonstrated so far, I finally conclude firmly: those who wish the commonwealth restored, healed and safe in future, if they want to proceed in order and to promise themselves some fruit of their efforts, must above all take care that the Jesuits are driven out of the kingdom, but in such a way that, once they are banished, a bolted bar prevents their return.

units.la: Expulsa autem & expurgata hac acri & arrodente bile, Morbis noftratis paroxysmus genere & paulatim lenietur, reliquae partes affectae, Clerus praecipue, sanabiles & trabiliores reddentur, poterit quod luxatum est, per ocium, citra gravioris alicujus fymptomatis metum curari & restitui.
units.tr: Once this sharp and gnawing bile has been expelled and purged away, the paroxysm of our disease will gradually be softened in its kind, and the other affected parts, the clergy especially, will be made curable and more tractable. What has been dislocated can be cured and restored at leisure, without fear of any more serious symptom.

units.la: Quandiu vero hic Incendij febrilis fomes intra Reipublicae viscera retinebitur, nulla bis salutis & securitatis spes relinquitur. Quodcunque enim machinabimur, quibuscunque emplastratis vulnera ligare & obducere studeamus, opera & oleum nobis peribunt, manque in hac corporis Polonici Cacochymia ad levissimam quamque occasionem recrudefcet. Neque enim Iesuitæ, ut cætera omnia sanentur, ad Regni Poloniæ legumq; Polo[?] nicarum similaritatem in æternum reducentur, ut illa sub hoc, qui adhuc qualiter cunq; du[?] rant, statu probent.
units.tr: As long as the fuel of this feverish fire is kept within the vitals of the commonwealth, no hope of health and safety is left to us. For whatever we contrive, whatever plasters we strive to apply and bind over the wounds, our labour and oil will be wasted, and in this cachexia of the Polish body the disease will break out again at the slightest occasion. Nor will the Jesuits, so that everything else may be healed, be brought back for all time to the likeness of the Kingdom of Poland and its Polish laws, so that those laws might prove themselves under this condition, however they still endure.

units.la: Ideoq; ne eos quidem audiendos censeo, qui ut res minus odiosa sit, non universalem pur[?] gationem censent instituendam, sed per partes tantum bilis istius detractionem & immi[?] nutionem faciendam putant. Verbi gratia, sunt qui eos tantùm extra regnum propellendo[?] existimant, qui vel clandestinarum machinationum contra regnum cooperatores aut sal[?] tem conscij fuisse deprehenduntur, vel quorum seditiosus feruor publicæ pacì præcipu[?] periculosus censetur. Sunt qui hanc Iesuitismi diminutionem à locis incipiendam sua[?] dent. Ut nempe ex primariis Regni Vrbibus aut ubicunque ab eis Reipublicæ insigne ali[?] quod periculum metuendum esset, removeantur. Sunt deniq;, qui putent, publica securitas[?] sufficienter prospectum iri, si latis legibus in arctiores carceres redigantur. Hæc igitur com[?] silia paucis discutiamus.
units.tr: Therefore I think we should not even listen to those who, so that the matter may seem less odious, say that a universal purging should not be undertaken, but think that this bile should be drawn off and diminished only piece by piece. For example, some think that only those should be driven out of the kingdom who are found to have been either accomplices in secret plots against the kingdom or at least aware of them, or whose seditious fervour is judged especially dangerous to public peace. Some think this lessening of Jesuitism should begin with places, namely that they should be removed from the chief cities of the kingdom, or from wherever some danger to the commonwealth is feared from them. Finally, some think public safety will be sufficiently provided for if, by stricter laws, they are driven into narrower prisons. Let us therefore discuss these proposals briefly.

units.la: De his primum in genere sic dico: Cum quacunq; Iesuitarum offensione, sive eos in uni[?] versum expellamus, sive audaciam illorum ad certam quotam restringamus, Pontificiæ indignationis invidiam nobis ex æquo metuendam esse: quam tamen plerique, omnium maxi[?] me cavendam censent. Hoc saltem discriminis erit, ut si partem aliquam Iefuitismi intra viscera retinuerimus, tanto plus nobis periculi ab eodem Pontifice futurum sit. Cum igitur[?] cum particulari offensione tantundem difficultatis subeundum sit, quantum cum totali ex[?] purgatione, cur non hanc ut utilissimam & certissimam præferemus? Imò hanc ego tibi ce[?]
units.tr: On these, first, I say in general: whatever the offence the Jesuits give, whether we expel them altogether or restrict their audacity to a certain quota, we must equally fear the odium of Papal indignation, which, however, most people think should be guarded against above all. This only will be the difference: if we keep some part of Jesuitism within our vitals, so much more danger will come to us from the same Pontiff. Since, then, a partial offence involves as much difficulty as a total purging, why should we not prefer the latter as the most useful and most certain? Indeed, I myself give you this...

units.la: Maximam præscribo: Iesuitas facilius ex regno expulsum, quàm intra regnum i[?] ordinem redactum iri.
units.tr: I prescribe this maxim: that the Jesuits can more easily be expelled from the kingdom than be brought back into order within it.

units.la: Dico amplius, eos vehementer errare, qui sperant, Bilem hanc ita caute posse moveri[?] ut non protinus exardescat & exasperetur, & ut non omnes vindictæ occasiones studiosissi[?] me conquisituri sint, quodcunque forte ad tempus, propter præsentem necessitatem simulent[?] Quæ occasiones ingeniis istis intra & extra regnum nunquam defutura sunt. Quod si ergo resumptis aliquando animis & viribus, denuo aliquid & forte periculosus quiddam mo[?] liantur, quid tum facto opus erit? Num quotannis in Iesuitarum gratiam Generalem[?] Rokosch celebrabimus? Deinde in specie iis qui nocentissimum quenque ex Iesuitis exter[?] minandum censent respondeo: Nec causam nec culpam earum rerum, quarum Iesuitæ in[?] simulantur, ita partiri & separari posse, ut alter altero mitius aut durius tractandus sit[?] Sic enim jam ostensum est, sestam hanc tam arctè inter se compastam esse, ut totum cor[?] pus & cum hoc omnia eius Individua membra, in harum præcipuè rerum praxi, d[?] quibus nobis sermo est, in unum conspirent, & ad unum scopum mente & corpore se[?] rantur.
units.tr: I say further that those are gravely mistaken who hope that this bile can be stirred so cautiously that it will not immediately flare up and grow fierce, and that they will not all most eagerly seek occasions for revenge, however they may dissemble for the time being because of the present necessity. Such occasions will never be lacking to those minds, inside and outside the kingdom. But if, once they have taken heart and strength again, they then plot something once more, perhaps something dangerous, what will we need to do then? Shall we celebrate a General Rokosz every year for the Jesuits' sake? Then, in particular, to those who think the most guilty Jesuits should be exterminated, I answer: the cause and the guilt of those things with which the Jesuits are charged cannot be divided and separated so that one must be treated more gently or more harshly than another. For it has already been shown that this body is so tightly bound together that the whole body, and with it all its individual members, conspire into one, especially in the practice of those matters we are discussing, and are directed in mind and body to one goal.

units.la: In una itaq; eademq; culpa omnes æqualiter hærent: differentia si quæ est, in ingeniosarum[?] virium saltem inæqualitate consistit, ut quod unus, aut alter fecit, omnes facturi fuerint[?] si vires aut occasio non defuissent. Nec crdeo te audivisse quòd Iesuita aliquis à tribulibu[?] suis, ob quodcunq; etiâ detestandum facinus, publicè damnatus aut etiam reprehensus sit. I[?] hoc enim genere non peccât: dummodo facinoris perpetratio in illum finem dirigatur, quem[?] Iesuitis in specie propositum esse ostendimus. Quod autem de nonnullorum seditioso feruor[?] affertur, illud per se speciosum est, ego tamen sic existimo, Illos nondum pessimos aut etiam[?]
units.tr: Therefore all cling equally to one and the same guilt. Any difference lies only in the unequal strength of their talents, so that what one or another has done, all would have done had strength or opportunity not been lacking. Nor do I think you have heard that any Jesuit has been publicly condemned or even rebuked by his brethren for any detestable crime whatever. For in this kind of thing they do not sin, provided the commission of the crime is directed to that end which we have shown is proposed to the Jesuits in particular. As for what is alleged about the seditious fervour of some, that is in itself specious; yet I judge that those men are not yet the most wicked or even...

units.la: Reip. periculosissimos esse, qui Cracoviæ, Posnaniæ, &c. ædes exurunt, Cæmeteria inva[?] dunt, sepultorum corpora refossa immaniter violant. Contra hanc enim rabiem, licet i[?] huncusq; diem impunita manserit, vel tandem remedium aliquod invenietur. Sed illas po[?] tius vulpeculas nobis observandas censeo, qui per Sudetas montes Alpiumq; juga hinc ina[?] commeantes, exoticarum artium spiritum ferunt & perferunt. Denique remedium hoc, si[?] tam bene caderet, ut nocentissimi qui sunt, exterminarentur, nos tamen saltem ad tem[?] pus relevaret, dummodo relevaret: tam diu nimirum donec his alij septuplo peiores[?] submitterentur. Num vero hoc satis justum operæ pretium censeri debebit? Illi[?] iquam operæ, quam Reipub. tantis sumptibus, tanta Nobilitatis defatigatione, nec sine ojtro periculo præstare conamur?
units.tr: Those who burn houses at Kraków, Poznań and elsewhere, invade cemeteries, and savagely violate the dug-up bodies of the buried, are not yet the most dangerous to the commonwealth. For against this frenzy, although it has gone unpunished to this day, some remedy will at last be found. But I think rather that those little foxes should be watched, who come hither across the Sudeten mountains and the Alpine ridges, bearing and spreading the spirit of foreign arts. Finally, this remedy, even if it turned out so well that the most guilty were exterminated, would nevertheless relieve us at least for a time, if it relieved us at all, namely until others seven times worse were sent in their place. Will this really be judged a sufficiently worthwhile result? Is it worth the labour we strive to perform at such great expense to the commonwealth, with such great weariness of the nobility, and not without serious danger?

units.la: Qui vero eos ex Aula & primarijs Regni Vrbibus expellendos suadent, illi quidem aliquanto fortius consulere videntur, sed non multo plus quam priores proficiunt. Videntur quidem certæ Reipub. partes nonnihil sublevari, videntur etiam Iesuitis præcipuæ noendi occasiones eadem ratione præcidi; Ego que jam dudum ita perjuasus sum, nullum ravius in Rempub. peccatum à nobis commissum esse, quàm quod Iesuitis in hisce Regni arcibus ad expediendas suas machinas tantum spacij concesimus. Id quod forte tum denum senseri sumus, si aliquid fortasis periculi à meridie & occidente nobis ingrueret.
units.tr: But those who advise that they be expelled from the Court and from the chief cities of the Kingdom seem to counsel rather more boldly, yet they achieve not much more than the former. Certain parts of the Commonwealth do indeed seem to be somewhat relieved, and the Jesuits seem to be cut off from their chief opportunities for harm by the same means. For my own part I have long been persuaded that no greater error has been committed by us against the Commonwealth than this: that we have granted the Jesuits such room in these citadels of the Kingdom to carry out their machinations. We may perhaps only feel this when some danger threatens us from the south and the west.

units.la: Hæc tamen admirari cogor, quibus rationibus consilij hujus autores ducantur, quod in Reipub. curatione potiorem Vrbium quàm equestris Ordinis, ipsiusque adeò Cleri respectum habeant? Eos itaque libenter interrogarem, quid putent singularis auxilij ad Remub. redituram, si primariæ Regni civitates exonerentur, & pestis hæc interim liberè in Nobilitatem grassetur? sicque peregrinismo huic liceat reliqui Cleri animos continere, sollicitare & in transversum agere? Ecquam illi tum rebus nostris spem securitatis iciunt? Hi ergo in eo periculose falluntur, quòd existimant, malum Iesuiticum intra Urbium ædificia, ita contineri, ut ibidem tantum aut saltem potissimum Reipublicæ noceat: Cum hæc primum ipsius Aulæ, ut ostensum est, deinde publica animorum pestis sit, à qua Nobilitati & Clero & per hos demum Reipub. præcipuè metuendum sit.
units.tr: I am nevertheless compelled to wonder on what grounds the authors of this plan are led, since in the care of the Commonwealth they have more regard for the cities than for the equestrian order, and indeed for the clergy itself. I would therefore gladly ask them what they think will be the particular help to the Commonwealth if the chief cities of the Kingdom are relieved while this plague meanwhile rages freely among the nobility; and thus this foreign contagion is allowed to restrain, stir up and turn against us the minds of the rest of the clergy. What hope of safety do they then hold out for our affairs? They are dangerously mistaken in this, in thinking that the Jesuit evil is so contained within the walls of the cities that it harms the Commonwealth only there, or at least chiefly there. Since, as has been shown, it is first a plague of the Court itself, and then a public plague of minds, by which the nobility, the clergy, and through them at last the Commonwealth, are chiefly to be feared.

units.la: Quin immò, dum Iesuitas in universum extra regnum propellendos suadeo, in eo Cleri Polonici quam maximum respectum habeo, cujus ex cessus non aliter, quam bilis hujus ferentis subtractione corrigi posse existimo. Ex his ergo iterum perspicitur ne hujus quidem consilij eum inter nos effectum sperandum esse, quo nobis adres nostras componendas & firmandas opus est.
units.tr: Indeed, while I advise that the Jesuits be driven out of the kingdom altogether, I have the greatest possible regard for the Polish clergy, whose excess I think can be corrected in no other way than by the removal of this bile that causes the fever. From these things it is again clear that we ought not to hope for the effect of this plan among us, which is needed for composing and strengthening our affairs.

units.la: Restant ij qui Iesuitas non solum ex Aula removendos & ex Vrbibus expellendos, sed etiam latis legibus intra Monachorum claustra redigendos & Ordinariorum juris dictioni, hoc enim à nonnullis additur, subijciendos consulunt.
units.tr: There remain those who advise that the Jesuits be not only removed from the Court and expelled from the cities, but also, by broad laws, confined within the cloisters of the monks and made subject to the jurisdiction of the ordinaries (for this, I am told, is added by some).

units.la: Videntur & hi aliquanto longius progredi, quibus ego ad vitandam majorem invidiam omnino parendum suaderem, si ulla saltem consilio huic spes subesset. Sed hanc sequentia nihil in universum præcidunt. Primum Iesuitas ita animatos esse certò novi, ut omnia potius moturi, omnia turbaturi sint, quàm ut splendoris & existimationis illius, qua ipsorum ordo habet supra reliquos Religiosorum ordines, ipsumque Clerum universum etinet, vel minimam jacturam subeant. Iesuita autem si ex Aula excludatur, si in versan-do Reipub. clavo non omnibus aliis præpolleat, si à publico ita arceatur, ut claustro includatur alium quàm proprium militiæ suæ Ducem superiorem agnoscere cogatur, si denique omnium arcanorum explorandorum occasio ei adimatur, à summo ad infima sibi redactus videbitur, ut qui jam nil amplius quàm vulgaris Monachus futurus sit. Quod dedecus gens ista non mitiori indignationis affectu aversatur, quàm si nobilis aliquis Regni, dignitarius subdito in abjectissimæ plebis censum detrudatur. Cælum itaque potius ruere patientur, quàm ut hanc in se ignominiam admittant.
units.tr: These also seem to go rather far, and to them I would have strongly advised yielding, to avoid greater odium, if there were any hope at all in this plan. But the following considerations entirely cut away that hope. First, I know for certain that the Jesuits are so disposed that they will stir up and throw everything into confusion rather than suffer even the slightest loss of that splendour and reputation which their order holds above the other religious orders, and which it keeps over the whole clergy. But if a Jesuit is shut out of the Court, if he no longer excels in steering the helm of the Commonwealth above all others, if he is so kept from public affairs that he is shut up in a cloister and compelled to acknowledge a superior leader other than his own commander of the militia, and if finally the opportunity of exploring all secrets is taken from him, he will seem to have been reduced from the highest to the lowest, as one who is now to be nothing more than an ordinary monk. This nation shuns that disgrace with no milder feeling of indignation than if some noble of the Kingdom, a dignitary, were thrust down into the census of the most abject common people. They would therefore sooner allow the sky to fall than admit this infamy upon themselves.

units.la: Esto tamen ut hic eos patientiores offendamus, quàm ego sperem. Quæro igitur secundo loco, quibus vinculis eos constrictum fimus? Certis legibus, inquies, publicis & constitutionibus. Bene dicis, Egoque fateor hæc justa esse in Foro politico coherendæ libidinis media, quantùm vis habentis per illa non prospe profecerimus.
units.tr: Yet grant that we offend them here more than I hope. I ask, therefore, secondly, by what bonds we shall have bound them? By certain public laws and constitutions, you will say. You are right, and I admit that these are just means, in the political forum, for restraining lust, however much power they have; but through them we have not made much progress.

units.la: Verùm hei culterius quærere cogor, Eccui hujusmodi legum & constitutionum, si quæ facta erunt, executionem commendaturi simus? Ordinariis locorum, respondebis, Ego vero agnosco ad ipsos munus hoc ex Regni legibus spectare; sed quid si ipsi tam otiosam Provinciam recipere nolint, aut excommunicationis Pontificiæ metu non audint? Veruntamen sive recipiant sive repudient, nec sic quidem Reipub. securitati prospicietur: Primum enim antiqua illa disciplinæ severitas apud nos hodie multum remisit, quâ apud Romanos olim parentes de liberis, si forte in Remp. peccâssent, supplicia sumebant.
units.tr: But I am compelled to ask further: to whose execution shall we commend such laws and constitutions, if any are made? To the ordinaries of the places, you will answer. I indeed acknowledge that this office belongs to them by the laws of the Kingdom; but what if they are unwilling to undertake so idle a charge, or do not dare for fear of the Papal excommunication? Yet whether they accept or reject it, the safety of the Commonwealth will not be provided for even so. For first, that ancient severity of discipline has among us today greatly relaxed, by which among the Romans of old parents exacted punishments upon their children, if perchance they had sinned against the Commonwealth.

units.la: DE NEFARIIS FACINORIBVS
units.tr: Concerning Nefarious Crimes

units.la: Verendum{a}q; propterea erit ne optimo cuique ex hoc ordine, & qui alias in ReMpub. recti affectus est, illud in hac custodia vel imprudenti accidat, quod Vir ille Dei 3. Reg. 20. in historia Achab sibi evenisse fingit, ut dum ipse aliis rebus intentus est, captivus, cuius custodiam suscéperat aufugerit. Deinde experientia testatur, Ordinarios locorum habenu magis Iesuitis parere & obnoxios esse, quàm quod hi illorum auctoritatem aut juris dictio nem multum curent. Quin immò hi pro Episcoporum pædagogis se gerunt, quos etiam, u Aulæ Rom. Corycæos, metuere & observare coguntur. Qualem ergo coercitionem ab ij expectare poterimus?
units.tr: There is therefore reason to fear that, in such custody, something may happen to the best men of this order, and to anyone otherwise well disposed to the Commonwealth, through carelessness, just as that man of God in 3 Reg. 20 imagines happening to himself in the story of Ahab: while he himself is busy with other matters, the prisoner whose guard he had taken on escapes. Furthermore, experience shows that the ordinaries of the places are more obedient to the Jesuits and subject to them than the Jesuits trouble themselves much about the authority or jurisdiction of those ordinaries. Indeed, the Jesuits act as tutors to the bishops, whom they are compelled to fear and to court, like the Corycaeans of the Roman court. What sort of restraint, then, can we expect from them?

units.la: Tertiò sic dico, quodcunq; de his omnibus fiat, Nos tamen contra gentem hanc legibu nostris nihil profecturos, in quo me experientia ipsa jam erudiit. Quid enim? Confœderatio publica annon Lex est, annon Constitutio est, annon Polonorum jus est, publicis Re gis & Nobilitatis juramentis sancitum & confirmatum? Sed quid per hanc eandem hastenus contra hanc pestem Politicam proficimus? Annon rabies ista per hoc efficacissimum (sic quidem Majoribus nostris videbatur) remedium irritata potius est quam cohibita? Quam petulanti lingua stiloq; Styrico livor iste hoc salutare instituum incessit, deride & exsibilat? Tam laxum & molle capistrum Dæmon iste tam impatienter fert, quâ igitu ratione arctius duriúsve quiddam feret? Cumq; hoc isti constitutioni faciant, per quam Iesuitismus proprie non laeditur, ecquid de illis fiet, quas in suam perniciem factas recordabuntur?
units.tr: Thirdly, I say this: whatever is done about all these matters, we will achieve nothing against this people by our laws, and experience has already taught me this. For what? Is not the public confederation a law? Is it not a constitution? Is it not the right of the Poles, sanctioned and confirmed by the public oaths of the King and the Nobility? Yet what have we gained so far against this political plague through this very instrument? Has not that rage been provoked by this most effective remedy (so our ancestors thought it would be), rather than restrained? With what insolent tongue and Styrian pen has that envy attacked and hissed at this salutary institution? That demon bears such a loose and soft bridle so impatiently: by what reasoning, then, will he bear something tighter or harsher? And since they treat that constitution in this way, by which Jesuitism as such is not harmed, what will become of them when they recall the laws that were made for their own ruin?

units.la: Et quid tandem Iesuitis nos proscribere tentabimus, cum suis ipsimet constitutionibus, quæ contra hanc, de qua conquerimur, intemperiem ad specie inter ipsosmet latæ sunt, non parent? Anno enim superioris seculi 93. Iesuitarum superiores cum animad verterent, Res Gallicas suorum potissimum scelere jam ferme perditas, coacto Romæ generali totius Ordinis conventu, statuto sanxerunt: Patres societatis Iesu, cum omnibus qui ordini illi ascripti sunt, à caussis, & negociis secularibus in universum abstinere debere, &c. Huic igitur decreto ecquomodo hactenus inter nos paruerunt?
units.tr: And why should we finally try to banish the Jesuits, when they do not obey their own constitutions, which were enacted to appear as a remedy against the very excess of which we complain? For in the year 1593 of the last century, when the Jesuit superiors saw that French affairs were almost ruined, chiefly by the crimes of their own men, they called a general assembly of the whole Order at Rome and decreed by statute: the Fathers of the Society of Jesus, together with all who are enrolled in that Order, ought to abstain entirely from worldly causes and business, etc. How, then, have they hitherto obeyed this decree among us?

units.la: Sic igitur tandem contra hos etiam concludo, consultius esse, ut tam fera Bestia prorsus abdicetur, quàm ut Cavea intra domum inclusa, cum perpetuæ solicitudinis cruciati custodiatur.
units.tr: So, finally, I conclude against these men as well: it is more advisable that such a savage beast be utterly cast out, than that it be kept shut up in a cage within the house, to be tormented by constant anxiety.

units.la: Dixi autem, Iesuitas non solum expellendos, sed etiam contra reditum omnia diligenter præcavenda esse. Neque enim expulsi quiescent, ut non omnem lapidem moveant, qui ipsis redire liceat, ut sic hanc vestri Iesuiticæ injectam maculam vicissim eluant. Deque nos Galliæ admonere debet, in cujus Aula Iesuitarum absentium practicæ tantum potuerunt, ut cum ex cusi Dentis in ore regio lacuna resarciri nunquam posset, Iesuitæ tamen reclamantibus Parlamentis & obnitente prudentissimo quoque non solum restituti sint: sed etiam Pyramis illa, perpetrati scelcris æterna index fuerit demolita.
units.tr: I have said, moreover, that the Jesuits must not only be expelled, but that every precaution must be taken against their return. For the expelled will not rest, but will move every stone, so that they may return and in turn wash away the stain of Jesuitism that has been cast upon you. France ought to warn us here, at whose court the practices of absent Jesuits had such power that, although the gap left by the knocked-out tooth in the royal mouth could never be repaired, the Jesuits were nonetheless restored, despite the protests of the Parlements and the opposition of every most prudent man; and that pyramid, the eternal witness of the crime committed, was torn down.

units.la: Hoc autem inter nos hac fortassis ratione omnium rectissimè præcavebitur: Si primum bona illorum immobilia in alios usus ad publicam Regni, præcipuè tamen nobilitatis, cui major illorum pars detracta est, utilitatem convertantur. Quod sic commodissime fiet: Si bonis literis confultum cupimus, quarum videlicet interitum plærique sibi per Iesuitarum expulsionem imaginantur, detur opera, ut ex iisdem Cracoviensi Academiæ de viris bonis, doctis & in omni disciplinarum genere probe versatis extra ordinem prospiciatur. Aut si ita placet, præter hanc alia intra regnum Academia instituatur. Deinde alibi in regno schole hinc inde aperiantur, in quibus non solum eruditis Præceptoribus honesta stipendia constituantur: sed etiam pauperibus Scholasticis, iis nempe qui ingeniis valent, sed propter fortunæ tenuitatem literarum studia commodè prosequi nequeunt, de victu & custentatione providebitur. Idq; tanto majori curæ, quod ex Nobilitate etiam omnibus temporibus inveniantur, qui hujusmodi studiorum subsidiis opus habent. Et hæc ego distribuum in regno ceu publica Gymnasia esse vellem: Quorum cura & inspectio certis ex Nobilitate utriusque ordinis viris & qualificatis personis commendari posset. Hoc si fieret, Iu- ventuti nostræ, quæ in spem honorum & ad Reipub. ministeria educatur, cum pietate & boni niis literis Patriae Legumque patriarum & reverentia a teneris implantaretur, & eipub.de viris idoneis ad eum modum prospiceretur, ut eidem ab exterorum factionibus insidiis minus periculi esset. Iesuitarum etiam expulsorum desiderium si quod erit, intra ucos annos porsus evanescceret & obliteraretur.
units.tr: Among us, this will perhaps be most rightly guarded against in the following way: first, if their immovable goods are turned to other uses for the public benefit of the Kingdom, and especially of the nobility, from whom the greater part of them was taken. This will be done most conveniently as follows: if we wish to provide for good letters, whose ruin most people imagine will follow from the expulsion of the Jesuits, let care be taken that from the same funds the Academy of Kraków be provided, outside the ordinary budget, with good, learned men thoroughly versed in every branch of learning. Or, if it so pleases, let another academy be founded within the kingdom besides this one. Next, let schools be opened in various places throughout the kingdom, in which not only learned teachers are given honourable salaries, but provision is also made for food and maintenance for poor scholars, namely those who have talent but, because of the slenderness of their fortunes, cannot pursue their studies with ease. This will be all the more important because there are always found among the nobility also some who need such support for their studies. I would wish these to be established in the kingdom as public gymnasia, whose care and supervision could be entrusted to certain men of both orders of the nobility and to qualified persons. If this were done, our youth, who are educated for the hope of honours and for the ministries of the Commonwealth, would be planted from childhood with piety and good letters, with love and reverence for the fatherland and its ancestral laws; and provision would be made for the Commonwealth of men fit for the task, so that it would be less exposed to danger from the snares of foreign factions. Even the longing for the expelled Jesuits, if any remains, would within a few years wholly vanish and be forgotten.

units.la: Tertio si quid superesset, ut omnino superfuturum puto, publica ex eo Nosocomia instituantur in eorum usum, qui in bellis se pro Repub. strenue gesserunt, & vel vulneribus debilitati sunt, vel per aetatem militiae labores non amplius perferre possunt, &c. Ut haec militaris virtutis quasi Asyla constituantur, ubi benemeritorum & emeritorum illa non turbeneficus honeste & liberaliter sustentetur. Cujus sanctissimi & utilissimi Instituti exempla in Urbibus Belgicis me videre memini, cujus etiam specimen nobis praebuit laudatissimae memoriae R. Stephanus, quando in Varsaviae hujusmodi pro debilitatis militibus Xenodochium instituit & dotavit. A cujus tamen praeclara & plane regia voluntate & intentione nimis cito recessum est.
units.tr: Thirdly, if anything should remain, as I think will certainly be the case, public hospitals should be established for the use of those who have served the Commonwealth bravely in wars and who are either weakened by wounds or, by reason of age, can no longer endure the labours of soldiering, etc. In this way these would be set up as refuges, as it were, of military virtue, where those who have earned or completed their service might be honourably and generously supported, not in beggary. I remember seeing examples of this most holy and most useful institution in the cities of Belgium; and the late King Stephen, of most laudable memory, also gave us a specimen of it when he founded and endowed such a hospice in Warsaw for disabled soldiers. Yet a great deal too quickly we have departed from his splendid and truly royal will and intention.

units.la: Nec ego video, quomodo Iesuitarum bona vel sanctius vel utilius collocari queant: animirum ut quae semel piis usibus destinata sunt, iisdem maneant, & ipsius interim Nobilitatis damnum, quod a Iesuitis Iesuitarumque artibus se accepisse queritur, aliquo modo farciatur, & sic Reip. commodis utrobique optime consulatur.
units.tr: Nor do I see how the goods of the Jesuits could be placed to any holier or more useful end, namely that what has once been destined for pious uses should remain so, and that the loss suffered by the nobility itself, which it complains it has received from the Jesuits and their arts, should be made good in some way; and thus the interests of the Commonwealth would be best served on both counts.

units.la: Facta ad eum modum bonorum Iesuiticorum dispensatione per peculiare statutum sub infamia aut alia aliqua severa poena interdici posset: Ne quis primum de revocandis aut admittendis Iesuitis ullo tempore publice aut privatim mentionem facere audeat. Neve deceps ulla ex Regno juventus, nobilis praesertim, a cujus salutari institutione Patriae sanguis pendet, ad Iesuitas extra regnum se conferat, iisdemque se disponendam committat. Ne in domi in expurgando Iesuitarum fermento laboramus, illud ab extra nobis nihil tale subicantibus obrepat.
units.tr: Once the Jesuit goods have been so distributed, it could be forbidden by a special statute, under infamy or some other severe penalty, first, that anyone should ever dare to mention publicly or privately the recalling or readmitting of the Jesuits. Likewise, that no youth from the kingdom, especially the nobility, on whose sound upbringing the blood of the fatherland depends, should betake themselves outside the kingdom to the Jesuits and commit themselves to be trained by them. Let us not labour at home to purge the leaven of the Jesuits only to have something of that sort creep in upon us from abroad.

units.la: Tandem opinor diligenter providere oportere, ne per Officinas Typographicas talia publicum spargantur, quae praesenti Reipub. statui & Regni hujus libertati quocunque modo adversantur. Qualia nimirum illa haetenus fuerunt, quae Iesuitae adhuc sub moderatione Regiae Majestatis regno, Cracoviae & alibi contra confoederationem publicam in vulgus ediderunt. Talia inquam quae per ipsorum jugulum reditura fuissent, si Legum publicarum vigor, ea observantia in Polonia esset, quali in bene constituta Repub. esse debet. Ubi tamen Vafricies ista hoc insuper dolo ut plurimam usa est, ut hujusmodi pestilentia scripta sub alienis, certorum nimirum Praelatorum, nominibus emiserint, ut nimirum ratione universum Clerum in invidia publica consortium pertraherent, & dispersio in urbes facinore ejus vindicationem Reipub. difficiliorem facerent.
units.tr: Finally, I think it must be carefully provided that such writings as in any way oppose the present state of the Commonwealth and the liberty of this kingdom are not spread among the public through the printing presses. Such writings, of course, have hitherto been those which the Jesuits, while still under the governance of His Royal Majesty, published among the common people in the kingdom, at Kraków and elsewhere, against the public confederation: writings which would have come back to bite them, had the force of the public laws and that observance which ought to exist in a well-ordered commonwealth existed in Poland. Yet that Jesuit craftiness has used this further trick, that it has put out such pestilential writings under the names of others, namely certain prelates, so that by this means it might draw the whole clergy into public hatred, and by scattering them through the cities make the punishment of that crime more difficult for the Commonwealth to exact.

units.la: ORATIO EQVITIS POLONI CONTRA IESVITAS.
units.tr: THE SPEECH OF A POLISH KNIGHT AGAINST THE JESUITS.

units.la: Huc etiam referenda est ORATIO Equitis Poloni, & quidem Pontificiae religionis, quam habuit in frequentissimo procerum Poloniae Conventu, in qua similiter deteguntur & narrantur Iesuitarum artes, dolus, fraudes, imposturas, & multa nefaria facinora, non solum in Polonia, sed etiam in aliis Regnis ac provinciis ab ipsis patrata. Inter alia sic inquit: Ego Rom. Ecclesiae propemodum annus, dico hanc unam Monachorum familiam, quae a Iesu Salvatore nomen habet, ad perniciem multarum Rerumpublicarum esse institutam. Magna spe ingredior in reliquum orationis meae cursum, quia jam periculosissimum istum scopulum vobis tacentibus sum praeter setus. Quid igitur causae est? ut ita sentiam de istis hominibus, quorum admirabilis pietas, singularis quaedam in omni disciplinari genere scientia, a multis commendatur, & qui primo loco, ordine & authoritate digni sunt habiti? quasnam rationes adferam istius tanti criminis? perarduum mihi erit demonstrare. Quo me vertam? aut quos testes producam? Sunt homines Ecclesiastici ordinis honestissimi, atque ornatissimi, tanta amicitia et tanta necessitudine cum isto ordine Iesuitico conjuncti, ut etiamsi boni viri non essent, plurimum momenti tamen habere deberet illorum Oratio contra Iesuitas, ita aute boni Catholici sunt, ut etiamsi inimicissimi essent Iesuitis, tamen illis credi oporteret. Quid igitur isti dicunt? Sunt haec vobis nova & inopinata Senatores Amplissimi? num primum ista crimina aures vestrae accipiunt? Nonne soletis interesse concionibus, in quibus affirmare solent constanter & graviter, ea voce & motu corporis, ea gravitate & constantia viri doctissimi nostri Theologi, Iesuitas eam pestem esse, quae animadverti non posset, antequam totum Respublica corpus inflammet: eorum mores, gestus, habitum, oculorum conformationem, oris & vultus moderationem, ad res a majoribus nostris bene inventas, atque institutas ad illas, inquam, res omnes, per manus nobis traditas, debilitandas, atque evertendas hunc Monachorum ordinem comparatum esse. Novum istud est Senatores? non his vocibus, non his exclamationibus resonuit primarium templum Lublinense? non summum etiam templum Cracoviense plenum atque refertum his Iesuitarum ornamentis atque testimoniis, ad perpetuam & loci, & temporis, & hominis memoriam? Non fuit hoc, inquam, in istis templis decantatum? Testes sunt viri Senatorij: magna authorita& shy;te, consilio, prudentia ornati, & caeteris ornamentis honoris, ingenij, industriae clarissimi, qui hoc affirmant. Quid dicam de illustri Episcopo Cracoviensi? quem honoris & amplitudinis causa nomino: cujus ea est aetas, prudentia, authoritas, eruditio, humanitas, judicium, constantia, ingenij acumen, ut ad ejus orationem juramentum vestrum adhibere possitis. Quid igitur is dicit? affirmavit constanter & graviter; voce & vultu ad rei indignitatem compositio, istam novam non ante multos annos inventam Monachorum fa­miliam, quae Iesu Salvatoris nomine ornata est, ad Ecclesiae Rom. dogmata evertenda comparatam esse, & ad excitanda seditionum incendia, ad evertendos Reip. nostrae bonos & omnium comprobatione institutos mores. Iohannes vero Zomoiscius Regni Cancellarius, & exercituum summus imperator: cujus prudentiam, rei militaris scientiam, virtutem, authoritatem, felicitatem, fortitudinem omnis semper mirabitur aetas, affirmavit vere & sapienter, ut omnia saepe dicere solet, istis sacerdotibus in templis et suggestis locum aliquem concedendum esse: ut vero ex monasteriis & templis ad Reip. negotia gerenda accedant, hoc nullo pacto ferri oportere. Quid ego nunc producam Doctorem Picum, civem Cracoviensem, & virum Senatorium: quem vere Philosophum subtilissimum, & Medicum exercitatissimum possumus appellare, in cujus vita extat imago antiquae virtutis: cujus oratio exemplum est copiosae loquentiae sapientiae: is certe ita de Iesuitis judicat, ut saepe affirmet, pessime cum patria nostra actum esse, quae istos non jam dudum ejecerit. Quid ego vobis nunc adferam voces singulorum hominum? quid pro­ducam in medium querimonias earum viduarum, quae non prius istorum salvatorum arte deprehendere potuerunt, antequam domos suas spoliatas animadverterent; omnibus vasis argenteis, omnibus ornamentis aureis, in quibus aliqua ars, aut pretium ita singulare existeret, ut posset eorum cupiditatem incendere. O tempora, o mores, haec jam agitantur in foro, jactantur in Palatijs, recitantur in omnibus locis, damnantur in templis, in consp[ectu] Trinitatis: ante imaginem Christi, omnium sanctarum atque sanctorum, haec declamantur, ad commovendos sanctos atque sanctas ista saepe & multum, vehementer & graviter, copiose & ornate ab illis exponuntur, qui religionibus sanctorum atque sanctarum praesunt: & a vobis ista ignorantur? Verum utilissimi sunt propter Scholas: multos jam ludos literarios aperuerunt: magno motu fit concursus juventutis, magna nobilium pars, eaque fere praecipua, ab illis erudiri suos filios cupit: propter magnam doctrinae, fidei, gravitatis, constantiae exisitimationem, & propter singularem quandam docendi rationem. Eodem accedit, ut nullis praemiis laborum propositis, magnos tamen labores suscipiant, & sustineant. Heu me miserum: cur ego vos, quos semper laudavi, cogor reprehendere? Non videtis, non intelligitis Senatores? haec omnia ad perturbandam quietem pertinere? non ne animadvertitis plurimas Scholas ab illis jam dissipatas esse? unam Scholam celeberrimam Cracoviensem, viris doctissimis in omni disciplinarum genere ornatissimam, jam sordi litudine foedam atque squalidam, nulla antiqua ornamenta retinere? Habuit Polonia ante ista istos Iesuiticos Monachos, habuit viros eruditissimos, oratores vehementissimos, Philosophos acutissimos, Iureconsultos prudentissimos, Theologos omni dicendi gravitate, copia atque ornatu instructissimos: habuit nostra patria Scholas, ex quibus, tamquam ex equo Trojano, prodierunt plurimi doctissimi viri: Vna Academia Cracoviensis quatuor illia litteratorum juvenum numerabat. Prodibant ex illa Schola illi viri, quorum ingenium, prudentiam, authoritate ista adhuc miratur aetas. Iam prope vigesimus annus est, ex quo Iesuitas istos in regno nostro videmus, qui ita Scholas suas instituunt, ut omnem industriam, diligentiae laudem aliis eripere cupiant: Saepe admodum ludos Comoediarum, Tragoediarum, omni splendore, copia & ornatu instructos, exhibent: in quibus ludis summam laudem & utilitatem positam esse existimant: & hac propemodum una arte multos discipulos sibi pertrahunt: tamen neque inter istos tam praeclaros Magistros, neque inter discipulos videmus illos, qui possint aliquo genere eruditionis cum illis antiquis nostrae Scholae magistris & doctoribus contendere. Habuimus illo seculo Lucam concionatorem, cujus ea dicendi vis fuit, ut quamcunque in partem voluisset, animos hominum flectere facile poterit. Credo adhuc vos memoriam retinere illius concionatoris, quem Leopolitam nostri Poloni appellabant: erat ille homo eā morum elegantiā, & humanitate, ut semper auditorum suorum animis atque auribus novam quandam voluptatem adferret, eo ingenii acumine, eā doctrinā, ut semper orationis suae subtilitate redderet doctiores suos auditores. Quanta, & quam multa laudes debentur Hosio Cardinali, Cromero Varmiensi Episcopo, Orichovio, Fricio? Hic me incendit quaedam cupiditas, ut de istis viris paulo copiosius differam. Sed vetuo, ne ex commemoratione illorum virtutum & eruditionis, recrudescant vestra ulnera, quae patria nostra ex morte istorum hominum accepit. Erant illi viri quaedam sulcherrima & clarissima Ecclesiae Romanae lumina: Habetis, ut opinor, in animis vestris praeclarum illud Fricii volumen de Republica. Extant multi libri Hosij Cardinalis, Cromeri: Orichovij orationes adhuc in multorum manibus versantur: & nulla iam futura est aetas, ut opinor, quae illorum memoriam obscuret: Iam si Bembi, Sadoleti, Contareni, Reginaldi Poli, & reliquorum summorum hominum libros enumerare laudare, ut aequum est, possem, dies mepotius, quam oratio deficeret. Quid horum simile habent Iesuitae? Prodeunt quoque quaedam illorum lucubrationes. Vtinam illum laborem, quem in scribendis illis libris susceperunt, in suas Tragoedias, vel Comoedias potius contulissent: ita enim illa sunt refutata ab haereticis, ita profligata, ut luculentam quoque plagam tota Ecclesia nostra Rom. acceperit. Provocarunt Lublini superiore anno Antitrinitarios & Anabaptistas ad disputandum: canebant triumphum ante victoriam: in ea disputatione nihil praeter redundantem quandam verborum volubilitatem, & tragicos clamores, quibus in clamoribus omnes Iesuiticae laudes positae sunt, praestiterunt: & tantum-modo plebis, & anicularum & collusorum atque suorum compransorum approbationem consecuti sunt: & cum rationum vi Antitrinitarios vincere debuerint, & eam victoriam, antequam certatum esset, litterarum monumentis tradiderint, cum exitum ille triumphus ante victoriam habuit, ut Ariani minis, convitiis, terroribus, clamoribus fuerint esti: & primarius quidam illorum hominum Niemojevius etiam verbera senserit. Dolebamus, Senatores Amplissimi, Ecclesiae Rom. dignitatem ab istis hominibus ita delusam, ut multi ex illo loco, Romanae Ecclesiae observantissimi, animo dubio & fluctuante disserint. Prodijt libellus Possevini Itali, tanquam fax quaedam ad excitandum incendium: cuius authoritatem si voluissetis sequi, nonne jam domestico dissidio eversam Rempublicam aspiceremus? Quae ista est ratio Senatores: virum eruditissimum non suae eruditionis arma & doctrinae instrumenta ad vincendos suos adversarios conferre, sed ad barbaram crudelitatem & feritatem decurrere. Mederi volunt patriae nostrae: honesta haec ratio est. Verum si scalpellum adhibeatur ad sanam corporis partem, si viri boni, utiles ves patriae e Rep. exterminentur: non medicina, sed carnificina est. Quamobrem Concilium non convocatur? Cur publica disputatio non instituitur? Quamobrem istae facula ad sim excitandam adhibentur? Non est magnum negotium homini erudito, vincere eum, qui literarum cognitione non est excultus: praesertim si eo quoque accedat bonitas causae. Qui ad gladium, ad ignem, ad aquam, ad cades, ad vim decurrit, fateatur se facilius hominem jugulare, quam erudire posse: animum carnificis, & barbari atque crudelis praedonis, quam Theologi mentem erudiam habere.
units.tr: To this belongs also the SPEECH of a Polish knight, and indeed of the Roman Catholic religion, which he delivered in the most crowded assembly of the nobles of Poland. In it the arts, deceits, frauds, impostures, and many wicked crimes of the Jesuits are similarly exposed and recounted, committed by them not only in Poland but also in other kingdoms and provinces. Among other things he speaks as follows: "I, who am almost a year old in the Roman Church, say that this one family of monks, which takes its name from Jesus the Saviour, was established for the ruin of many commonwealths. I enter the rest of my speech with great hope, since I have now passed by this most dangerous rock while you keep silent. What, then, is the reason? Why should I think this way about these men, whose admirable piety and singular skill in every kind of discipline are commended by many, and who have been held worthy of the first place, rank, and authority? What reasons shall I adduce for so great a charge? It will be very hard for me to prove. Where shall I turn? Or what witnesses shall I produce? There are men of the ecclesiastical order, most honourable and most distinguished, so closely joined in friendship and intimacy with that Jesuit order that, even if they were not good men, their speech against the Jesuits ought nevertheless to carry great weight; and they are so good Catholics that, even if they were the bitterest enemies of the Jesuits, they would still have to be believed. What then do these men say? Are these things new and unexpected to you, most distinguished senators? Do your ears hear these charges for the first time?
