Unless you restrain their power, joined as it is with monstrous greed, see, most distinguished Senators, that at this time, when the Commonwealth above all needs your wisdom and authority, you do not appear to have failed the fatherland, and you and all yours, to whom you owe almost everything.

units.la: DE NEFARIIS FACINORIBVS DE TVRBIS IN MOSCOVIA à IE- SVITIS EXCITATIS PRO DE- METRIO.
units.tr: On the wicked deeds of the disturbances in Muscovy stirred up by the Jesuits on behalf of Demetrius.

units.la: IN Moscovia, amplissimo illo Septentrionis tractu, ingentes turbas Iesuitæ excitárunt. Mortuo enim Basilide, magno Duce Moscoviæ, & alio in eius locum electo, Iesuitæ Demetrium quendam, qui ipsis supra modum favebat, subornárunt, & variis artibus, dolis ac fraudibus, tanquā Basilidis filium, adeóque legitimum regni hæredem intrudere conati sunt. Hic Demetrius apud Regem Poloniæ diligenter instando, Iesuitis eum strenuè adiuvantibus, tandem obtinuit, ut auxiliares sibi copiæ adversus Moscoviæ Ducem decernerentur. Moscus sibi non parum ab illis timens, insigni usus stratagemate, regni sui aliquam partem Demetrio possidendam obtulit: cúmque ille occupatum illam venisset, facto per insidias in eum impetu, ingentem stragē edidit, devictóq; Demetrio, coepit illum. Custodiâ autem liberatus, collecto novo exercitu, copias Magni Ducis fudit, & aliquot arces celeriter occupavit, ac tandem regno potitus est.
units.tr: In Muscovy, that vast northern region, the Jesuits stirred up great disorders. When Basil, Grand Duke of Muscovy, died and another was chosen in his place, the Jesuits induced a certain Demetrius, who favoured them beyond measure, to put himself forward. By various arts, tricks and frauds they tried to thrust him upon the realm as the son of Basil and so the lawful heir. Demetrius pressed the King of Poland hard, and with the Jesuits strenuously helping him, he finally obtained that auxiliary troops be assigned to him against the Grand Duke of Muscovy. The Muscovite, greatly fearing them, used a remarkable stratagem and offered Demetrius a part of his kingdom to hold. When Demetrius came there to take possession, the Muscovite made a surprise attack by ambush, inflicted a huge slaughter, overcame Demetrius and captured him. Freed from custody, however, Demetrius gathered a new army, routed the Grand Duke's forces, quickly seized several strongholds, and at last gained possession of the kingdom.

units.la: Post aliquod vero tempus à subditis suis tali occasione trucidatus occubuit. Suborta erat in multorum animis suspicio, quòd Iesuitis, ob navatam sibi & præstitam fidelem operam, vehementer faveret, aliis non obscuris indicijs, eum non Basilidis filium esse, quem se ex instinctu Iesuitarum venditaverat, sed dolis, fraudibus & impostturis Iesuitarum, acVi Demetrij in regnum intrusum esse. Hinc cum, Iesuitis eum adhortantibus, religionem & ceremonias mutare inciperet, & Polonis, quos magnâ copiâ secum adduxerat, plus, quàm Moscovitis exhibere honoris videretur, necuti, consueto eius loci more, copulatio matrimonialis, à Patriarcha fieret, permittere vellet, sed Iesuitam sacra & solennitates peragere oporteret, tantam in subditorum animis commotionem excitavit, tantùmque in se odium provocavit, ut congregati magno numero capta occasione, cùm finitis nuptijs genio Duxindulgeret, multosq; Polonos & Iesuitas convivio excepisset, irruptionem ex improviso in Palatium eius secerint, cumque cum omnibus Polonis & Iesuitis trucidárint. Hunc rumorem de occiso Demetrio, & turbis in Moscovia excitatis, factio Iesuitica aliquandiu studiosissimè compressit, ne veritas deprehensa Polonis artes eorum magis suspectas redderet: qui alias propter factionis Iesuiticae in Aula potentiam & insolentiam graviter aliquandiu tumultuati sunt.
units.tr: After some time, however, he was murdered by his own subjects on a suitable occasion. Many people had come to suspect, because he was greatly favouring the Jesuits for the service they had rendered and he had proved faithful to them, and by other not obscure indications, that he was not the son of Basil, as he had falsely claimed at the Jesuits' urging, but had been forced upon the kingdom by the deceits, frauds and impostures of the Jesuits and by the power of Demetrius. Hence, when he, at the urging of the Jesuits, began to change the religion and ceremonies, and seemed to show more honour to the Poles, whom he had brought with him in large numbers, than to the Muscovites, and wished to allow a marriage to be solemnised by the Patriarch in the usual manner of that place, but with a Jesuit performing the sacred rites, he stirred up such a commotion among his subjects and provoked such hatred against himself that they gathered in great numbers and, seizing the occasion when, after the wedding was over, he was indulging his genius at a feast, which he had given to many Poles and Jesuits, they burst unexpectedly into his palace and slaughtered him together with all the Poles and Jesuits. The Jesuit faction for some time most zealously suppressed the report of Demetrius's murder and of the disturbances stirred up in Muscovy, lest the truth being discovered should make their arts more suspect to the Poles; the Poles, on the other hand, had for some time been greatly stirred up by the power and insolence of the Jesuit faction at court.

units.la: DE HVNGARICIS MOTIBVS.
units.tr: ON THE HUNGARIAN DISTURBANCES.

units.la: TEstatur etiam Conradus Graserus Francus in sua Plagæ Regiæ historia pag. 186. Iesuitas sub belli Hungarici ultimi æstum aliquot nobilissimas Provincias, hactenus pacatas, in ipso Ianizarorum conspectu, suis artibus tentâsse, turbâsse, totamq; vicinam cum ipsis Christianorum castris ambiguo motu & diffidentiâ replevisse.
units.tr: Conrad Graser, a Franconian, also bears witness in his History of the Royal Plague (p. 186) that during the heat of the last Hungarian war the Jesuits tried and disturbed some very noble provinces, hitherto peaceful, by their own devices, right before the eyes of the Janissaries, and filled the whole neighbouring region, together with the Christian camps themselves, with uncertain agitation and distrust.

units.la: DE TVRBIS IN TRANSSYLVANIA à IESVITIS EXCITATIS.
units.tr: On the disturbances stirred up in Transylvania by the Jesuits.

units.la: TRanssylvani etiam omnium suarum miseriarum & calamitatum, quas hactenus perpessi sunt, causam in Iesuitas, eorundemq; audacissimas molitiones publica voce conferunt, & quas adhuc metuunt, non aliunde sibi, quàm ex Iesuitarum artibus imaginantur: ob hanc causam etiam publico Ordinum decreto ex hac Provincia eiecti sunt Anno 1590. sub mensis Ianuarij initium.
units.tr: The Transylvanians, too, openly blame the Jesuits and their most audacious schemes for all the miseries and calamities they have suffered until now. They imagine that whatever they still fear can come from nothing but the Jesuits' arts. For this reason they were expelled from this province by a public decree of the Estates at the beginning of January 1590.

units.la: Non tamen cessárunt seditiosi homines. Nam post eiectionem suam, auctores fuerunt
units.tr: Nevertheless the seditious men did not desist. For after their expulsion they were the authors of further disturbances:

units.la: Iesuitæ ex Transylvania eiecti. ēs fuerunt clandestinis suis consiliis, ut Sigismundus Bathorius Transsylvaniæ Princeps, varios motus cōcitaret, nonnullos ad perniciem persequeretur, bello inextricabili se implicaret, acdenique miser & inglorius vivere cogeretur.
units.tr: the Jesuits, expelled from Transylvania, by their secret counsels stirred up various movements against Sigismund Báthory, Prince of Transylvania, pursued some of his followers to their ruin, involved him in an inextricable war, and at last forced him to live a wretched and inglorious life.

units.la: Eorum opera quoq; Stephanus Potscaius, Transsylvaniæ Princeps, cruentæ hujus se animosè opponens, tandem veneno propinato è medio sublatus est anno 1607.
units.tr: After some years, by trickery and finally by a bloody conspiracy, they again try to prepare their way into this province, as is clear from a letter of Charles Zeroin, Baron, which reads as follows.

units.la: Post aliquot etiam annos dolis, ac tandem coniuratione sanguinolenta adium sibi rursus in hanc Provinciam parare conantur, ut ex literis Caroli Zeroini Baronis intelligitur, quæ sic habent.
units.tr: Some years later, by trickery and finally by a bloody conspiracy, they tried once more to prepare a way for themselves into this province, as is understood from the letter of Charles Zeroini, Baron, which runs as follows.

units.la: De Transsylvaniæ novis motibus nescio quid ad vos relatū sit: fertur ita rem habere.
units.tr: I do not know what has been reported to you about the new disturbances in Transylvania; the matter is said to stand thus.

units.la: Erat in aula Principis præcipuæ nobilitatis vir, Religione Pontificius, gente & nomine Balthasar Kornis. Is permissu Principis, cujus gratiam adulatione & obsequio sibi conciliaverat, alebat in familia Iesuitam peculiari privilegio, cum nemini id præterea concedetur, ex lege quā Monachi ipsi aditu Provinciæ prohibētur. Erat autem annexa concessioni ditio, ut sacra tantum curaret, Rēmp. non attingeret, neminem ex reliqua societate alliceret, juventuti informandæ nullam operam daret, & si quæ aliæ sunt, quibus genus istud hominum maximam orbis partem in veneratio nem & admirationem sui pridem pellexit; At vir bonus, qui aere facilius caruisset, quam ab instituto sodalitij sui recessisset, vel tandem illum, Dum solicitè instigare, ut patribus accessum in provinciam aperiret, Principem in partes suas pertraheret, cultū Papisticum restitueret, qui diligetem quidem & sedula opera ei navabat, sed cū nihil proficeret, nihilq; impetraret, ad alia consilia, impellere haud dubiè Iesuita conversus est. Inde insidiæ Principi fieri ceptæ, in caput eius conjuratū, alij magnæ authoritatis viri, & inter eos Cancellarius Bendis, qui fugâ postea salutem sibi peperit, in consortium pertractī, sed ut accidere plerumq; solet, infelici eventu; detecta enim conspiratio est. Vbi ad notitiam Principis pervenit, ille dissimulare initiò, ubi periculū augeri, consilia procedere vidit, accitis ijs, quorū fidei maximè se permittebat, re aperit, militem clam accīri & in insidijs collocari extra urbem jubet. Inde venatum proficiscitur, stipatus fortissimorum virorum non contemnenda manu, educit una conjuratos, qui ignari quid animi essent, Principem comitantur, & occasione arreptâ, quo d superiores se viribus esse aut paresse salte exīstimarent, aggredi instituunt. Necmora, unus è complicibus eductō acinace relā illum petit, at is curru, quo ad insidias tegendas vehebatur, exiliens, generosissimo equo confestim conscenso, vim repellit. Accurrunt satellites, accurrit ex insidijs miles; comprehenduntur præcipui ex conjuratis, & necantur. Reversus in urbem magnam adversariorum stragem edidit: sic securitati suæ in posterum prospexit. Sunt qui his molitionibus Cardinalem Forgatium & fratrem Sigismundum cum alijs quibusdam implicare volunt, mihi tamen nil de ijs constat, Iesuitas vero Authores Tragædiæ hujus fuisse minimè ambigo, dudum jam per Europam ab his artibus celebres.
units.tr: At the Prince's court there was a man of the leading nobility, a Papist by religion, named Balthasar Kornis by family and name. With the Prince's permission, whose favour he had won by flattery and obsequiousness, he kept a Jesuit in his household under a special privilege, although this was granted to no one else, since by law monks are barred from entering the province. The grant, however, was attached to a condition: the Jesuit was to attend only to sacred matters, not meddle in affairs of state, draw no one else from the society, give no effort to the instruction of youth, and abstain from whatever other things it was by which that kind of men had long ago drawn the greater part of the world into veneration and admiration of themselves. But the good man, who would sooner have gone without money than withdraw from the institute of his fellowship, urged the Jesuit diligently and persistently to open the way for the Fathers into the province and to draw the Prince to their side, so as to restore Papist worship. The Jesuit did indeed devote careful and industrious effort to this, but since he accomplished nothing and obtained nothing, he undoubtedly turned to other plans, and began to drive Kornis towards them.

units.la: DE TVRBIS IN STYRIA, CARINTHIA ET CARNIOLA à IESVITIS EXCITATIS.
units.tr: ON THE DISTURBANCES IN STYRIA, CARINTHIA AND CARNIOLA STIRRED UP BY THE JESUITS.

units.la: ANno Domini 1604. Francofurti ad Mœnum à Ioan. Regio in lucē est edita historia sævissimæ & inhumanis persecutionis in nominatis Provinciis à Iesuitis institutæ, cuius hæc fere summa est. Vt Iesuitæ in omnes terras & provincias longe lateque fraude dolisque irrepserunt, ita & in Styriam suis sese artibus exiguo quidem ab initio numero, at mox in immensum sic aucto, ut jam vix Styria, Carinthia & Carniola simul illos capere posset, intruserunt. Et cum id genus hominum nil nisi crudelitatem sub hypocrisi spiret, ibidem eandem, præsertim Græcij, quæ est Styriæ Metropolis, quam aliis in locis antehac & tentarunt & egerunt Tragœdiam, mutatis solummodò personis, renovarunt. Et ut proprium eorum esse solet, Caroli Archiducis Austriæ superioris animum adversus subditos innocentes & fideles exacerbârunt, atq; eo unâ cum iis qui stant ab illorum partibus adduxerunt, ut persecutionem gravissimam, temporibus iis, quae alias ob Turcicam expeditionem, aliaque incommoda periculosissima erant, adversus Protestantes institueret. Cuius iemel atque iterum praeludia quidem incepta & praemissa fuerunt, nihil tamen, quod alicuius fuisset momenti, effectum est, Carolo Archiduce morte sublato. Nihilominus Iesuitae toti in hanc curam unice incubuerunt, ut propositum suum in essectum producerent, & veram religionem, quae illis sudes erat in oculis, ex tota Styria eijcerent.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1604, at Frankfurt on the Main, Johann Regius published the history of a most savage and inhuman persecution, instituted by the Jesuits in the provinces named above. The substance of it is roughly this. Just as the Jesuits have crept by fraud and trickery into all lands and provinces far and wide, so too they slipped into Styria by their arts. At first they were few in number, but they soon multiplied so greatly that Styria, Carinthia and Carniola together could scarcely hold them. Since that sort of men breathes nothing but cruelty under a cloak of hypocrisy, they renewed there the same tragedy, especially at Graz, the metropolis of Styria, which they had attempted and enacted before in other places, with only the persons changed. As is their habit, they inflamed the mind of Archduke Charles of Upper Austria against innocent and faithful subjects. Together with those who sided with them, they brought him to institute a most grievous persecution of the Protestants, at a time that was otherwise most dangerous and troubled by the Turkish campaign and other perilous difficulties. The preludes to this were begun and put forward once and again, but nothing of any moment was accomplished, because Archduke Charles was removed by death. Nevertheless the Jesuits devoted themselves wholly and solely to this task, so that they might bring their purpose to effect and cast out the true religion, which was a thorn in their eyes, from the whole of Styria.

units.la: Tandem igitur, ubi de processu quodam astutissime excogitato deliberâssent, in scenam eruperunt, & Tragoediam, quam diu secum privatim meditati erant, instituerunt. Mense enim Septemb. anni 1598 Parochus Graecensis M. Laurentius Sonnabent, qui quondam Praeceptor iuniorum Principum fuit, Filiorum Caroli, scriptum aliquod instinctu Iesuitarum Ministro Graecensi misit, quo authoritate, qua tunc se pollere iactitabat, ei mandat, ut ab omni religionis Protestantium exercitio desistat: sibi enim hanc curam demandatam esse, & ad suum munus id spectare dicebat.
units.tr: At length, therefore, having deliberated on a certain most cunningly devised plan, they came out onto the stage and staged the tragedy which they had long been privately turning over in their minds. For in September 1598 the parish priest of Graz, Master Laurentius Sonnabent, who had once been tutor to the young princes, the sons of Charles, sent to the Graz minister, at the instigation of the Jesuits, a certain writing. By the authority which he then boasted he possessed, it ordered him to desist from every exercise of the Protestant religion. He said that this care had been entrusted to him and belonged to his office.

units.la: Sed hoc scripto non territi Ministri, Sonnabendius illis relictis, Domino Ordinarios Styriae (sic nominantur Quicumviri, penes quos summa rerum potestas est) aggreditur, Ministros graviter apud eos accusat, & ut illi, quem magistratum suum legitimum appellarent, concionatoribus suis munere publico fungendi potestatem interdicant, petit. Domini Ordinarii memores privilegiorum suorum, nitentes promissis Caroli Patris moderni Principis, non ignari impudentissimorum Iesuitarum postulatorum & technarum, quas antehac saepe molití erant, silentio hominem dimittunt. Ille vero filum Ariadnes iam dudum expeditum secutus, & Ministerium Protestantium, & Dominos Ordinarios Styriae proceres illustres apud Ferdinandum iam Styriae Archiducem accusat, & ut is pro ea, qua instructus esset divinitus authoritate, & amore erga Romanam Ecclesiam praeditus, petitioni suae satisfaciat, & Concionatores Protes-tantes coherceat, ne illi ab eo neque vocati neque ordinati in urbe, in qua ipse Princeps residet, ipso invito res sacras administrent, sed inde potius expellantur etiam atque etiam cotendit.
units.tr: But the ministers were not frightened by this writing. Leaving Sonnabend aside, they approached the Lords Ordinary of Styria (so the Quinqueviri are called, in whose hands the highest power of government lies). They accused the ministers severely before them and asked that they forbid the preachers, whom the ministers call their lawful magistrate, to perform public duties. The Lords Ordinary, mindful of their privileges, relying on the promises of Charles, the present Prince's father, and not unaware of the most shameless demands and tricks of the Jesuits, which they had often attempted before, dismissed the man in silence. But he, following the thread of Ariadne, long since laid out, accused both the Protestant ministry and the Lords Ordinary of Styria, illustrious nobles, before Ferdinand, now Archduke of Styria. He urged again and again that Ferdinand, as one endowed with the authority divinely given him and with love for the Roman Church, should grant his petition and restrain the Protestant preachers. They were neither called nor ordained by him, yet they administered sacred things in the city where the Prince himself resides, against his will; they should rather be expelled from it.

units.la: Princeps a Iesuitis Praeceptoribus iam antea edoctus petitioni Parochi Iecu dat, & Dominis Ordinariis Edictum severissimum mittit mandatque illis, deoperam, ut Ministri Protestantes ab officio concionandi desistant, & intra 14 dies finibus totius Styriae expellantur. Actum 13. Sept. Anno 1598.
units.tr: The Prince, already instructed beforehand by the Jesuit tutors, granted the petition of the parish priest of Graz. He sent the Lords Ordinary a most severe edict, and commanded them to see to it that the Protestant ministers desist from the office of preaching and are expelled from all the borders of Styria within fourteen days. Done 13 September 1598.

units.la: Domini Ordinarii perlectis his literis scripto prolixo respondent, partim se excusantes, quod mandato huic sine praescitu reliquorum Dominorum Provincialium morem gerere non possint, partim petentes ut ab hoc propositio in hisce periculosissimis temporibus, quibus Provincia aliis maioribus conflictatur incommodis quam ut inde eluctari possit, desistat, Iesuitas animum suum exulcerare non patiatur adversus subditos innocentes, ut contra iuramentum, quo ex privilegiis Provinciae obligatus esset, quicquam committat, commemoratione simul incommodorum, quae inde secutura esset, adiecta. Sed tantum abfuit ut scripto illo gravissimo ab instituto suo averteretur Ferdinandus, ut indies magis magisque Iesuitis facem submini-stran-tibus, ad persequutionem accenderetur. Ac proinde 23. Septemb. mandatum alterum, non quidem ut artea Dominis Ordinariis, sed Ecclesiae & Scholae Ministris mittit, quo praecipit ut in hoc ipso momento, sub capitis poena, a docendi & concionandi officio, ta-m in Schola quam Ecclesia desistant, & intra octiduum omnibus suis finibus excedant.
units.tr: The Lords Ordinary, having read these letters, replied in a lengthy writing. Partly they excused themselves, because they could not comply with this command without the knowledge of the remaining Provincial Lords. Partly they begged that he abandon the proposal in these most perilous times, when the province was already struggling with other troubles greater than it could extricate itself from. They begged that he not allow the Jesuits to inflame his mind against innocent subjects, and that he not commit anything contrary to the oath by which he was bound under the privileges of the province. They added a reminder of the troubles that would follow from it. But Ferdinand was so far from being turned from his purpose by that most serious writing that, as the Jesuits supplied fuel day by day, he was inflamed more and more to persecution. And so, on 23 September, he sent a second command, not to the Lords Ordinary this time but to the ministers of the church and school. It ordered that, at that very moment and under penalty of death, they desist from the office of teaching and preaching in both school and church, and that within eight days they leave all his lands.

units.la: Hoc mandatum ubi accepissent Ministri, Dominos Provinciales adeunt ipsi pfiscp remaperiunt. Convocantur & Ordinarij & Provincialium quidam, qui um Græcij erant, in domum Capitanei Provincialis, quo & Ministri accerlun‐ ur. Deliberatio instituitur, an illo die (qui erat Veneris & precibus publicis lestinatus, quo etiam Eucharistia ijs, qui die precedente confesi erant, distri‐ uebatur) concio fit intermittenda. Ministri negant, Capitaneus periculum imminens exponit, & ut exeuntes de hac re deliberarent monet. Revocati re‐ pondent, omnino sibi in sententia persistendum esse videri, velleque quævis pericula subire potius, quam docendi Provinciam & concionandi officium screre. Discedere iterum & expectare responsum iubentur. Interim dum belli supplices ad Principem mittuntur, & à Principe respondetur, tempus, quod concionibus destinatum erat Iesuitarum consilio cunctando, præterlabi‐ ur, & sic conciones ab illo die intermittere in posterum coguntur. Ac licet stiduum ipsis præscripserit Princeps, tamen expectare illud, ut elaberetur, ræ summo expellendi eos ardore, noluit, sed vigesimo octavo Septembris po‐ remum illis mandatum mittit, & ut illâ adhuc die urbe exeant, sub capitis pe‐ culo præcipit.
units.tr: When the ministers had received this command, they went to the Provincial Lords themselves and found them. The Lords Ordinary and some of the Provincials who were from Graz were summoned to the house of the Provincial Captain, and the ministers were summoned there too. A deliberation was held on whether the sermon should be suspended that day, which was a Friday set apart for public prayers, and on which the Eucharist was also distributed to those who had confessed the day before. The ministers refused. The Captain set out the imminent danger and advised them to go out and deliberate on the matter. When they were recalled, they replied that they seemed bound to persist entirely in their opinion, and that they would rather undergo any danger than give up the teaching of the province and the office of preaching. They were ordered to withdraw again and wait for an answer. Meanwhile humble supplications were sent to the Prince, and an answer was given by the Prince. Through the Jesuits' delaying, the time set aside for sermons slipped away, and so from that day on they were compelled to suspend the sermons. Although the Prince had prescribed a period of eight days, he was not willing to wait for it to run out, so eager was he to expel them at once. On 28 September he sent them a final command, and ordered under penalty of death that they leave the city that very day.

units.la: Illustres quidem Domini Ordinarij, nec non Provincialium pars maxima ihil non agit supplicibus libellis & scriptis gravissimis, quæ vel cautem Mar‐ esiam emollire potuissent, ut manere Ministris suis liceret. Sed Iesuitarum in‐ igationes plus quàm totius provinciæ illustrissimæ supplicationes humillimæ oterant. Et ut conatus ille succederet, rem ita comparârant. Abijt paulo ante archidux, paucissimis illum comitantibus, in Italiam, ut ferebatur ad Prin‐ pem Ferrariensem: eâ verò occasione Romam quoque profectus est ad Pon‐ tificem, qui, ut aiebant, mensâ eum dignari noluit, antequam ei Cœnâ Domi‐ ica ab ipso ministrata promisisset, se Lutheranos ex Provincijs suis expulsu‐ im. Redeunte illo, mox advolant Regis Hispaniarum, Pontificis & Princi‐ um quorundam Italiæ Legati, militibus non paucis stipati, eo quidem ro‐ ine, ut sororem Archiducis Regi Hispaniarum adducerent, ut verò eventus ocuit, ut Iesuitarum voluntati satisficeret. Cùm enim illi cum militibus in ibe essent congregati, persecutio instituitur, & acerrimè urgetur. Archidu‐ isa se non abiturum in Hispaniam protestatur, antequam Ministros in exi‐ um eiectos videret. Proceres terrentur, Ordinarij coguntur, cives minis & vi hercentur, res eo deducitur, ut Ministri Ecclesiæ & Scholæ omnes uno ec‐ emque die Græcio eijcerentur, quorum numerus novendecim erat persona‐ um: Factum 28. Septemb. Anni 1598, qui profestus fuit Michaelis Archangeli, tqp ita ex urbe illa clarissima, & paulo post ex universa Styria Evangelij lux, iæ tanto labore, magnostudio, multis laboribus exhaustis diu propugnata & efensa erat ab illustribus Styriæ Proceribus, tam cito Iesuitarum rabie expulsa eiecta est. Nocte hunc diem proximè præcedente, fulgura & tonitrua tam ter‐ bilia exaudita sunt, tempore non consueto, ut nemo non portentosa illa esse bitraretur. Neq; defuerunt, qui Ministris salutem ea attulisse & sicas Hispa‐ orum ac Italorum à cervicibus eorum avertisse perhiberet. Ab hoc etiam tem‐ ore pluvia per sex integras septimanas cōtínuó feré durabat, ut plurimum da‐ ni aquarū eluviones dederint, & annonæ caritas maxima secuta sit. Domini Ordinarij Comitijs habitis gravissimè de Iesuitarum technis conqueruntur: in teris etiam ex Comitijs ad Principem missis, pacis publicæ hostes, tecto tamen omine, & perturbatores Rerumpub. appellantur, eosq; accusant, quòd subin‐ ehortentur Principem, ut privilegia suis Provincijs data, concessiones item, nventiones, conditiones, pacificationes religionis & pacta omnia quantum‐ is sigillis & iuramentis approbata & confirmata, infringat, rescindat & irrita eddat: Ministros quoq; in integrum restituiâ Principe supplicitér flagitanti
units.tr: The illustrious Lords Ordinary, and the greater part of the Provincials, left nothing undone: they presented supplicating petitions and most grave writings, which could have softened even the Marpesian rock, so that the ministers might be allowed to remain. But the Jesuits' incitements counted for more than the most humble supplications of the whole most illustrious province. To make their attempt succeed, they had arranged matters thus. The archduke had shortly before set out for Italy with very few attendants, as was reported, to the Prince of Ferrara. On that occasion he also went on to Rome to the Pontiff, who, as they said, would not deign to dine with him until he had promised to expel the Lutherans from his provinces, the Lord's Supper being administered to him by the Pontiff himself. On his return, soon legates of the King of Spain, of the Pontiff and of some Italian princes flew in, attended by not a few soldiers. Their purpose, to be sure, was to bring the archduke's sister to the King of Spain, but, as the outcome showed, they were also there to satisfy the wishes of the Jesuits. When they had gathered there with the soldiers, the persecution was instituted and pressed most fiercely. The archduke protested that he would not leave for Spain before he saw the ministers cast out into exile. The nobles were terrified, the Lords Ordinary were compelled, and the citizens were coerced by threats and violence. The matter was brought to such a point that all the ministers of church and school were cast out of Graz on one and the same day; their number was nineteen persons. This was done on 28 September 1598, the feast of Michael the Archangel. And so from that most famous city, and soon after from the whole of Styria, the light of the Gospel was driven out and expelled so quickly by the rage of the Jesuits. It had been long defended and maintained by the illustrious nobles of Styria with such labour, great zeal and many toils. On the night immediately before this day, thunder and lightning were heard, so terrible and at an unusual time that everyone judged them portentous. Nor were there lacking those who reported that these had brought salvation to the ministers and turned the daggers of the Spaniards and Italians from their necks. From this time too, rain continued almost without break for six whole weeks, so that it did the greatest damage through floods of water, and a great dearth of grain followed. The Lords Ordinary, having held an assembly, complained very gravely of the Jesuits' tricks. In letters also sent from the assembly to the Prince, the Jesuits are called enemies of the public peace, though in a veiled way, and disturbers of the commonwealth. They are accused of constantly urging the Prince to break, rescind and annul the privileges given to their provinces, likewise the concessions, agreements, conditions, pacifications of religion and all pacts approved and confirmed by however many seals and oaths. The Lords Ordinary also humbly demand of the Prince, who is pleading with them, that he restore the ministers in full.

units.la: dfruftra.
units.tr: in vain.

units.la: Finitis Comitijs Provincialibus, reliquæ etiam civitates in Styria iubeñtur, ut Ministros suos dimittant: cui mandato plurimæ morem gerunt. Incolæ vero Ferrifodinarū id facere recusant. Milites igitur eo mittuntur, qui civitatem expugnant, cives miserrimè captivos plenis plaustris Græcium mittunt ibique indignissimis modis multantur. Vrbe hac expugnata & capta, Arcem Illustris ac Generosi Domini Iohannis Hoffmanni adeunt, & templum illi vicinum, in quo sepulchrum huius familiæ erat, pulvere tormentario subiecto evertunt, ut ossa hinc inde dispergerentur. Non diu post Græcij templum, in quo Evangelicæ concionës habitæ sunt, militibus cinctum occupant, altare destruunt, corpus Vuilhelmi Zimmermanni Theologi ex sepulchro effossum in Murrham fluvium urbem allabentem proiciunt. Civibus gravissimè interdicunt, etiam sub capitis periculo, ne extra urbem sacra synaxi utantur, infantesque baptizari & matrimonia confirmari sinant: imò ne quis Psalmos Germanicos saltem domi suæ canat. Quidam Magister Iuris Advocatus, quòd paucula quædam ut populicus, ad populum verba fecisset, in carcerem conijcitur. Alij levibus de causis puniuntur & grandi ære multantur, ut non pauci quibus religio cordi erat relictis suis bonis alio commigrarint, ut suam ex tyrannide Iesuitarum, qui hic omnibus non solum interfuerunt, sed etiam præfuerunt, conscientiam & vitam vindicarent.
units.tr: When the provincial diet had ended, the other towns in Styria were also ordered to dismiss their ministers, and most of them obeyed this command. The inhabitants of the ironworks, however, refused to do so. Soldiers were therefore sent there, who stormed the town, and they sent the citizens, most wretchedly captured, away in full wagons to Graz, where they were punished in the most shameful ways. After this town was stormed and taken, they went to the castle of the illustrious and noble lord Johann Hoffmann, and they overthrew the church next to it, in which this family's tomb was, by setting gunpowder under it, so that the bones were scattered here and there. Not long afterwards, they seized the church at Graz in which the evangelical sermons had been preached, surrounded it with soldiers, destroyed the altar, and dug up the body of the theologian Wilhelm Zimmermann from its grave and threw it into the river Mur, which flows past the town. They strictly forbade the citizens, even on pain of death, to use the sacred synaxis outside the town, or to allow their infants to be baptised or their marriages to be confirmed. Indeed, no one was allowed to sing even the German Psalms at home. A certain master of laws and advocate, because he had spoken a few words to the people in a popular manner, was thrown into prison. Others were punished for slight causes and fined heavy sums of money, so that not a few who held to the religion left their goods behind and moved elsewhere, to defend their conscience and their life from the tyranny of the Jesuits, who here not only took part in everything but also directed it.

units.la: Quod in Styria, id etiam in Carinthia factum & perpetratum est, quod malo Iesuitae, quàm meis verbis referre. Sic igitur Martinus Episcopus Secoviensis ad magni nominis virum Augustæ Vindelicorum scripsit. Illustris ac Generose Domine N. N. Dn. charissime, & observande; postquam pridie Nativitatis B. Mariæ Virginis ad vestram illustrem Dominationem literas dedi, quibus significavi totam Styriam circa religionem Dei prapotentis beneficio reformatam esse; sequenti die ibidem in templo Parochiali Carinthiaco fecimus initium reformationis. Commissarii mihi adjuncti erant Dn. Iohannes Comes ab Ortenburg, Carinthiæ Supremus Capitaneus, Hartmannus Zingel eiusdem Provinciæ Vicedominus; D. Angelus Cosleda, Serenissimi Consiliarius; & Iohannes Christoph. à Franck. Guardiæ nostræ Capitaneus. Eodem igitur plane modo sicut & Styria, Carinthia à nobis reformata; inprimis hæretica templa cum cæmeteriis, sectariorum Prædicantium ædibus, ubique partim arietibus, partim pulvere tormentario sunt eversa. Prædicantes ubique ex Provincia expulsi, uxores privativæ & concubinæ ab eorum consortio abactæ, illisque reditus sub pæna proscriptionis in omnibus Provinciis interdicti. Omnes Catholicæ Ecclesiæ, quæ erant in hæreticorum potestate, sunt recuperatæ, Catholicis Pastoribus impositis: Omnes civitates, omnia oppida, omnes pagi diligenter reformati: pertinaces hæretici ex omnibus suæ Celsit. Provinciis proscripti. In omnibus fere, maximè verò principalioribus locis exhortationes me ad populum in tertiam & quartam vesperæ horam habitæ. Communio sub utraque specie in omnibus locis, & viva voce & per patentes literas (authoritate Apostolica à Dn. Nuntio Apostolico Episcopo Adriensi mihi concessa) à me sublata. Insuper literæ patentes Archidiaconis Gmuntensi, Frisacensi, Curcensi, Laventinensi & Aquitensi, & nonnullis Prælatis datæ, salutaria continentes remedia, quibus reformatio maneat stabilita, & ad Ecclesiam reductis omnis occasio ad vomitum redeundi fit præcisa. Multa millia librorum publicè in variis locis combusta, quam plurima animarum millia ad ovile Christi divinâ gratiâ reducta. Et sit tota Carinthia spatio trium mensium integra reformata, innumerabilibus hominibus de suo ad Ecclesiam reditu sibimet ipsis gratulantibus. Turba rusticorum & Villacenses sunt quidem tumultuati, attamen illorum furor non diu duravit. Civitas quoque Clangenfurt contra nos semper fuit in armis, denique nos ab ingressu prohibuit donec tantum per TERRIBILE mandatum commutata reformationi se subjecerit. Itaque pridie S. Martini vexillum 5 o o. militum ex Clangenfurt in civitatem Volckmarck est translatum, eodemque die omnes sectarij prædicantes ex eadem civitate discesserunt. cesserunt. Quibus omnibus postquam Clangenfurtensis civitas ita fuit evacuata, nos festo sancti Martini cum nostro militum vexillo ingressi sumus, tota in armis contra illum positâ civitatem. Sequenti postea die, quæ erat Dominica, in templo Parochiali populum, qui erat numerosissimus, orationem in quartam usque horam habui, & postmodum hac rebelli civitate, more solito, in omnibus per triduum reformata, domumque discessimus. Reformationis & Carinthiacæ & Styriacæ Acta forsan aliquando publicis typis committentur. Hæc quoque commissio, per quam feliciter & præter omnem expectationem (Deo sit laus) sine omni sanguinis effusione peracta, ita nostro Serenissimo cuit, ut inde plurimum ceperit voluptatis. Hæretici multa de rapinis nostrorum milium, & de tyrannide, quam nos Commissarij in populum exercuissemus, sparserunt, sed omnia ea quum sint salsissima, & mendacia per se evanescere soleant, nulla pro innocentia strâ declaratione Apologiâ opus erit. Hæc libentius ad Vestram Illustr. Dominationem scripsi, quum existimem, hanc narrationem saltem aliquam illius doloris, quem Vestra Illustr. Dominatio ob Canisfam, proh dolor, turpiter amissam percipit, mitigationem fore, iptim Græcij die 21. Novemb.
units.tr: What was done in Styria was also done and carried out in Carinthia, which I would rather report in the words of the Jesuits than in my own. So Bishop Martin of Seckau wrote to a man of great name at Augsburg: Illustrious and noble lord N. N., most dear and esteemed. After I wrote to your illustrious lordship on the day before the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, informing you that the whole of Styria had been reformed in religion by the blessing of almighty God, on the following day we began the reformation in the parish church of Carinthia there. The commissioners joined with me were Lord Johann, Count of Ortenburg, Supreme Captain of Carinthia; Hartmann Zingel, Vice-Dominus of the same province; Dr Angelus Cosleda, councillor of his Most Serene Highness; and Johann Christoph von Franck, captain of our guard. In exactly the same way as Styria, Carinthia was reformed by us. Above all, the heretical churches with their graveyards, and the houses of the sectarian preachers, were everywhere overthrown, partly with battering rams and partly with gunpowder. The preachers were expelled from the province everywhere; their wives and concubines were driven from their company; and for them any income was forbidden in all the provinces, under penalty of outlawry. All the Catholic churches that had been in the power of the heretics were recovered, and Catholic ministers were placed in them. All the cities, all the towns, and all the villages were carefully reformed, and the obstinate heretics were outlawed from all the provinces of his Highness. In almost all places, and most of all in the more important ones, I gave exhortations to the people at the third and fourth hour of the afternoon. Communion under both kinds was abolished by me in all places, both by word of mouth and by open letters (by apostolic authority granted to me by the lord Apostolic Nuncio, the Bishop of Adria). Moreover, open letters were given to the archdeacons of Gmünd, Friesach, Gurk, Lavant and Aquileia, and to some prelates, containing salutary remedies by which the reformation may remain established, and by which every occasion of returning to the vomit is cut off from those who have been brought back to the Church. Many thousands of books were publicly burnt in various places, and very many thousands of souls were brought back to the fold of Christ by divine grace. And the whole of Carinthia has been reformed in the space of three months, with countless people rejoicing in their own return to the Church. The rustic crowd and the men of Villach did indeed riot, but their fury did not last long. The city of Klagenfurt also was always in arms against us, and at last it kept us from entering until, moved only by a terrible mandate, it submitted itself to the reformation. Thus on the day before St Martin's day 500 soldiers' banner was transferred from Klagenfurt to the town of Völkermarkt, and on the same day all the sectarian preachers left that town. When all this had been done and the city of Klagenfurt had been so emptied, we entered on St Martin's feast with our banner of soldiers, the whole city being placed under arms against us. On the following day, which was a Sunday, I preached to the people, who were very numerous, in the parish church until the fourth hour, and afterwards, the rebellious city having been reformed in the usual way over three days, we went home. The acts of the reformation both of Carinthia and of Styria will perhaps one day be committed to the public press. This commission, which was carried out happily and beyond all expectation (God be praised) without any shedding of blood, was so pleasing to our most Serene Prince that he took great delight in it. The heretics have spread many reports about the plunderings of our soldiers and the tyranny which we commissioners were supposed to have exercised over the people; but since all these things are most false, and lies tend to vanish of themselves, no apology will be needed to declare our innocence. I have written these things more willingly to your illustrious lordship, since I think this account will be some alleviation of that grief which your illustrious lordship feels, alas, over the shameful loss of Kanizsa. Given at Graz, 21 November.

units.la: Ex hac Epistola Lector iudicet de Reformationibus Iesuitarum.
units.tr: Let the reader judge from this letter concerning the reformations of the Jesuits.

units.la: Palàm etiam præse tulerunt Iesuitæ, Nullâ re hactenus intra Europam plus ccatum esse, quàm nimiâ Monarcharum in persequendis Hæreticis, exequendq; Pontificum Rom. iussibus lenitate. Hoc q; inter illos adeò certum est, ut ne uxquidem Albanus, quamvis crudelissimè sævierit, eis per omnia satisfecerit, vel ipso Albano teste. Et familia Austriaca eminentissima ad persecutiones ius permoveri non potuit, qua unus atq; alter eius surculus Iesuitis formandus disponedus traditus fuisset. Philippum II. quoq; Hispaniarum Regem à monitis consiliis, in quæ ab initio propendebat, ad quæ etiam à Maximiliano Parmele & Affine, misso ad id Carolo fratre incitabatur, Iesuitæ inprimis averterunt, & obtinuerunt ut Inquisitionem Hispanicam in Belgio & Tridentini Concilij executionem per vim introducere maluerit, quàm aviti sui Patrimonij culentissimam partem pacatè possidere.
units.tr: The Jesuits have also openly declared that nothing has hitherto done more harm within Europe than the mildness of the monarchs in persecuting heretics and in carrying out the commands of the Roman Pontiffs. This is so certain among them that not even Alba, although he raged most cruelly, satisfied them in every respect, as Alba himself bears witness. Nor could the most eminent Austrian house be moved to persecution by any right, since one or another of its offshoots was handed over to the Jesuits to be formed and disposed. Above all, the Jesuits turned Philip II, King of Spain, away from the sounder counsels towards which he had at first inclined, and to which he was also urged by Maximilian, his brother-in-law, who had sent his brother Charles for this purpose; and they brought it about that he preferred to introduce the Spanish Inquisition into Belgium by force, and the execution of the Council of Trent, rather than peacefully possess the most fertile part of his grandfather's patrimony.

units.la: DE NEFARIIS FACINORIBVS IN BEL- GIO ET VICINIS REGIONIBVS PATRATIS À IESVITIS.
units.tr: ON THE WICKED DEEDS PERPETRATED BY THE JESUITS IN THE NETHERLANDS AND NEIGHBOURING REGIONS.

units.la: NON prius etiam acquieverunt Iesuitæ Furiarum instar, quam Auriacus Princeps Vvilhelmus tandem miserabili & condolenda morte, sclopeto, à Balthasare Gerhardi Burgundo, proditorie petitus, interficeretur anno 1584. Iulij. Chron. Belg. t. 1. p. 451.
units.tr: The Jesuits, raging like the Furies, did not rest until Prince William of Orange was at last killed by a pistol shot, in a wretched and lamentable death, treacherously attacked by Balthasar Gerhard the Burgundian, in the year 1584, in July. Chron. Belg. vol. 1, p. 451.

units.la: Idem etiam Mauritij, Principis Auriaci filij fortissimi iugulu insidios eper Petrum de Pennes, Michaelem Renicher, Petrum de Four & sicarios plures alios misisse, & mortem illi præsentissimam, instinctu prorsus diabolico, intentâsse anno 1594. & rursus anno 1598. Chron. Belg. testatur t. 1. p. 719. & t. 2. p. 93.
units.tr: The same men also sent Peter de Pennes, Michael Renicher, Peter de Four and several other assassins to attack the throat of Maurice, Prince of Orange, that most brave son, and in 1594, and again in 1598, they aimed at his life, which was in immediate danger, moved entirely by the devil. The Chronicle of the Netherlands bears witness, vol. 1, p. 719, and vol. 2, p. 93.

units.la: DE OCCVPATO IVLIACO ARTIBVS AC DOLIS IESVITARVM EX LITERIS MAGNI CV- IVSDAM ET NOBILISSIMI VIRI ANNO 1609. AVG. 10.
units.tr: Concerning the Occupation of Jülich by the Arts and Frauds of the Jesuits, from the letter of a great and most noble man, dated 10 August 1609

units.la: EOPOLDVS Iuliacum ipsum nomine Cæsaris tanquam Imperij seque ster occupavit, sed mirâ arte & Iesuitarum Coloniensium ope, apud quos es aliquot deliberandi causa, antequam rem aggrederetur, vestitu Iesuitico dutus hæsit. Intercedebat Iesuitis illis cum Rusenburgio Iuliaci præfecto. magna & notitia & familiaritas, itaque Primarius Pater illius Collegij septe aut octo aliis fratribus, inter quos & Archidux Leopoldus, stipatus visendi praefecti causa Iuliacum excurrit: eo ubi advenerat, petit introeundi copiam, quam obtinuit, etiam pro comitibus suis, qui ubi perlustrando in praecipuum arcis cō clave à Praefecto deducti essent, primarius iste Iesuita illū alloquitur & quaerit, si Imperator illi praeciperet, ut castrum illud in manus alterius traderet, an etiā parceret? ille testabatur, se ordinibus Provinciarum de novo obstrictum, non aliis quam illis reddere debere, posse tamen illud mandatum tale esse, quod ipsi parere necessum foret; quid, inquit Iesuita, si Imperator alicui ex suis agnatis aliquod mandatum dedisset, ut illud ei redderes, parereresne, an non? si utrumque viderem, respondit, deliberarem; at, inquit Iesuita, quid si iam in arce cum tali mandato esset ânne cum iterum expellere velles? ad haec verba attonitus respondit, minimè, imò recognoscerem in eo Imperatorem & parerem: sic Iesuita ostendit Leopoldum, qui ipsi mandatum Caesareum exhibuit statim; & paulo post iuramentum fidelitatis ab ipso exegit, & à caeteris militibus praesidiariis recusantes autem arce exegit. Quid tibi de hoc Iesuitarum stratagemate videtur? nisi astutum & vafrum hoc hominum genus in ordinem redigatur, vel extra orbem potius in abyssum unde illi prosiluerunt, repellatur, hi tandem imperium orbis rapere conabuntur.
units.tr: Leopold seized Jülich itself in the name of the Emperor, as though it were the Emperor's own fortress, but he did so by a remarkable art and with the help of the Jesuits of Cologne. He had stayed with them for some days, in order to deliberate before he undertook the business, and had gone about in Jesuit dress. Those Jesuits had great acquaintance and familiarity with Rusenburg, the prefect of Jülich. So the chief Father of that college, accompanied by seven or eight other brothers, among whom was Archduke Leopold, set out for Jülich to visit the prefect. When he arrived there, he asked for admission, and obtained it, also for his companions. When they had been led by the prefect through the citadel, looking at everything, and had reached the principal room of the fortress, this chief Jesuit addressed him and asked whether, if the Emperor ordered him to hand that castle over into another's hands, he would spare it. He replied that he was bound anew by the oaths to the orders of the Provinces, and ought to surrender it to no one but them; yet such a command might be of a kind that he would have to obey it. "What," said the Jesuit, "if the Emperor had given some command to one of his kinsmen, that you should hand it over to him: would you obey, or not?" "If I saw both," he answered, "I would deliberate." "But," said the Jesuit, "what if, already in the fortress, with such a command, you were to wish to expel him again?" Astonished at these words, he replied: "By no means; rather I would recognise in him the Emperor and obey him." Thus the Jesuit revealed Leopold, who at once showed him the Imperial command; and shortly afterwards he exacted an oath of fidelity from him, and from the other garrison soldiers, and those who refused he removed from the fortress. What do you think of this stratagem of the Jesuits? Unless this crafty and sly breed of men is brought into order, or rather driven out of the world into the abyss from which they sprang, they will at last try to seize the empire of the world.

units.la: IESVITAE EX OMNIBVS BELGII PROVIN- CIIS VNITIS SEV CONFOEDERATIS OB MVLTA N- EFARIA FACINORA PRIVATIM ET PVPLICE ATTENTATA, EXCEDERE IV- BENTVR.
units.tr: THE JESUITS ARE TO BE EXPELLED FROM ALL THE UNITED OR CONFEDERATED PROVINCES OF BELGIUM ON ACCOUNT OF THE MANY NEFARIOUS CRIMES ATTEMPTED PRIVATELY AND PUBLICLY.

units.la: Iesuitas anno Christi 1612, gravis in Belgio afflixit fortuna. Ibi enim Mandatum ab ordinibus confoederatis publicatum est, quo relatu ad se dicunt, multos sacrificulos, monachos & alios id genus Ecclesiasticos, maxime vero Iesuitas in confoederatas Belgij Provincias quotidie confluere, ibique exotericas suas doctrinas inter subditos desseminare, contrarias verbo Dei superstitiones hominibus instillare, & id maxime agere, ut tyrannidē & potestatē Pont. Rom. quā non solum in spiritualibus super omnia Concilia, sed etiam in secularibus super omnes Reges, Principes, & Respub. statuunt, affirmantes, eum illis omnibus eorumque regnis & Provinciis imperare, & subditos ab obedientia eorum absolvere posse, quod quidem ad seditionem in populo excitandam necessario comparatum sit, multisque nefarijs consultationibus & machinationibus occasionem praebeat, velut ex Galliae, Britanniaeque regnis & Ducatu Veneto desumpta eius rei exempla recenti adhuc memoria versentur. Quandoquidem igitur unitarum Provinciarum Statibus necessarium iam ante visum fuerit, eiusmodi edicta publicare, quibus caveretur, ne subditi iisdem Provinciarum venenatis istis, & tam vera Christiana fidei, quam honestis politicis constitutionibus adversantibus opinionibus inficerentur, infecti vero & jurejurando Pontificijs istis erroribus addicti ad officia & munera publica nulla admitterentur, ad praecavenda omnia perniciosa Respub. conventicula, & tacitas occultasque contributiones, pecuniarumque exactiones evitandas, necessarium vero fit, unice id curare, ut pax & concordia inter subditos Belgicarum Provinciarum cum vicinis regionibus conservetur, nec quid contra libertatem Provinciarum, sub honesta conversationum & commerciorum specie tentetur, edicta sese omnia tam in Provincijs istis quam vicinis regionibus condita evolvisse, deliberato cum Mauritio Nassovia Comite consilio, decrevisse, decernere etiam & imperare: ut sacrificuli, monachi, Iesuitae & alij id genus Ecclesiastici, Clerici & religioni Rom. addicti, cuiuscunque ordinis & dignitatis sint, quos duorum mensium à publicatione huius edicti tempore, in unitas Belgij Provincias venire contigerit, primo statim advectus fui loco, & eis porro ubi pernoctare voluerint omnib. nomina sua coram Praefecto & Magistratu
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1612 the Jesuits suffered a grievous reversal of fortune in Belgium. For a mandate was published there by the confederated States, in which they state that they had been informed that many priests, monks and other ecclesiastics of that kind, and above all Jesuits, flock daily into the confederated provinces of Belgium, there spread their exoteric doctrines among the subjects, instil into people superstitions contrary to the Word of God, and especially work to establish the tyranny and power of the Roman Pontiff, which they claim extends not only over all councils in spiritual matters but also over all kings, princes and commonwealths in secular ones, affirming that he rules over all of them and their kingdoms and provinces, and can absolve subjects from their obedience. This is indeed calculated to stir up sedition among the people and gives occasion for many wicked plots and schemes, as examples of this from the kingdoms of France and Britain and the Duchy of Venice are still fresh in memory. Since therefore it has already seemed necessary to the States of the United Provinces to publish edicts of this kind, by which it is provided that subjects are not infected with these poisonous opinions of the Provinces, which are opposed both to the true Christian faith and to honest political institutions, and that those so infected and bound by oath to these Papist errors are admitted to no public offices or posts; and in order to guard against all conventicles harmful to the commonwealth, and to avoid secret and covert contributions and exactions of money; and it is necessary above all to take care that peace and concord be preserved among the subjects of the Belgian Provinces and with the neighbouring regions, and that nothing be attempted against the liberty of the Provinces under the honest pretext of conversation and commerce: having reviewed all the edicts issued both in these Provinces and in the neighbouring regions, and having after deliberation with Count Maurice of Nassau resolved, decreed, enjoined and commanded: that priests, monks, Jesuits and other ecclesiastics of this kind, clerics and those attached to the Roman religion, of whatever order and rank, who happen to come into the United Provinces of Belgium within two months of the publication of this edict, shall, immediately upon arrival, at the first place they reach, and wherever they wish to lodge overnight, declare all their names before the Prefect and Magistrate

units.la: isti ius profiteantur, & quae causa sit adventus sui, ubi item hospitium suum habeant, aperiant, idem etiam elapso duorum mensium spatio facere teneantur, omnes modo dictae personae, quae jam antea ad Provincias istas veniunt, nec sede tamen ibi certa habeant, Praefectis ista omnia fideliter cognoscant, & ad superiores Magistratus referentur, ne forte quid ab hujusmodi personis, quod in provinciarum perniciem cadat, tentetur. Quod si vero quis nomen suum in professus deprehendatur, is 50. florenis multatus, solum vertere cogatur, ita ut nunquam Provincias istas unitas sub proscriptionis publicae poena redire possit. Imperare autem jam & mandare omnibus, & singulis, apud quos Iesuitae, Monachi & alij Clerici Ecclesiastici, Rom. religionis homines diversuri sunt, ut diligenter an nominum suorum professionem fecerint inquirant, vel ipsimet ante tertiam mansionis eorum noctem, eam apud Praefectos & Magistratus sub poena 100. florenorum faciant, excusatione omni, quasi personas istas non viderint, posthabita & neglecta, exceptis tamen publicis diversoriis, utpote de quorum notitia certi aliquid affirmari non possit. Prohibere porro & interdicere omnibus provinciarum illarum incolis, ne publicato hoc mandato, in ullo sese Collegium aut Scholam Iesuitarum inferant, sub poena, quod perpetuo tempore inutiles censeri debeant, qui ad officium aliquod vel munus publicum in Provinciis admittantur, vel canonicatu & beneficiis ullis fruantur, insuper ex suis bonis 100. florenorum multam singulis mensibus persolvere cogantur, quannam subire etiam teneantur ões, qui ante publicationem hujus mandati, in scholas & Collegia Iesuitarum se contulerint, neque intra duorum mensium spacium egressi fuerint. Quod si vel aliqui bona nulla habeant, a parentibus vel tutoribus, eorum multa ista exigatur, nisi forte aliter & contra eorum voluntatem in scholas & Collegia ista se contulerint, quo casu parentibus tutoribusque interdictum velint, ne pecuniam ipsis vel aliud quid sive directe sive per individuum mittat afferrive curent, sub modo dicta 100. florenorum multa ex propriis suis bonis aestanda. Omnem aut alienationem bonorum suorum ab illis, qui contra mandatum hoc in scholis & Collegijs Iesuiticis manserint, sive per donationem, sive per testamenta, codicillos aut dispositiones alias factas, nulla omnino & nullius efficaciae sese declarare. Mandare jam ut ad nullum officium vel munus publicum admittantur, sive indigenae sive advenae, qui post duorum mensium a publicatione Mandati defluxu, gradum aliquem honoris apud eos, praeto de defendendis Rom. superstitionib. juramento, acceperint, & ut illi, qui post facta anno 76. pacificatione Gadavi, juramentum illud praestiterunt, & ad officia aliqua adhibiti sunt, intra duorum mensium post publicationem hanc spacium a juramento isto expediant, & juramento fidelitatis hisce Provincijs locis, ubi habitant, se adstringant, nisi jam antea juramento fidelitatis praestito, superstitionib. istis nuncium remiserint, quam renunciatione & juramenti praestationem ratam habere velint. Imperare porro omnibus, qui sub juramento Pontificio gradu aliquem vel adepti sunt, vel porro etiam adipiscentur, & in unitarum Provinciarum loco aliquo, vel jam habitent, vel in posterum habituri sint, ut primo vel post publicationem edicti huius, vel post adventum suum in has Provincias, mense, coram loci istius Magistratu comparent, & juramentum fidelitatis praestent, sub poena, ut Provincijs istis excedant, perlutis post primum mensem 50. post alterum vero 100. florenis, tertio vero mense, nisi discesserint, publice proscribantur. Mandare praeterea omnibus unitarum Provinc. incolis & advenis, ut in nullo templo vel privato loco alio, sive in agro, sive navib. conventu ullu sive virorum sive mulierum instituant, Missas celebrent, superstitiones Papisticas docendo, legendo admonendo exerceant, aut conventicula Rom. religioni addictarum personarum foveant, iamsi nec sacrificulus, nec monachus, nec clericus eis ullus adsit, qui exercitia ista perat, sub quocunque etiam praetextu id fiat, sive publice sive privatim, sub poena 200. florenorum, eos persolvere cogaturis, in cujus vel domo, vel agro, vel navi conventicula ista habita fuerint: illi vero, qui missas celebrarint, vel exercitia superstitionis Pontificiae alia peregerint, extranei sint perpetuae proscriptionis, & arbitraria quadam alia insuper poena, sin indigenae, perpetuae ite relegationis & omnium beneficiorum privationis poena afficiantur, nec a quoniam hospitio excipiantur, multa hospitii 100. florenorum, pro prima vice, 200. pro secunda, 300. cum perpetua proscriptione pro tertia vice irrogata. Illi vero, qui Missae & aliarum superstitionum Papisticarum exercitio interfuerint, beneficijs suis omnibus privetur, & ita florenis pro singulis vicibus, quoties cunq; id fecisse vel deprehendantur, vel convincantur, persolvant, quam multam omnes etiam alij, qui in conventiculis istis deprehensi fuerint, una cum optimi sui vestimenti amissione praestare teneantur, habita consideratione, quod si quis doctrinam aliquam, politicae Provinciarum gubernationi repugnantem & obedientiae subditorum contrariam attulerit, capitis supplicio, tanquam pacis & tranquillitatis publicae turbator afficiendus sit. Constituere porro, & decernere, ut qui sub specie quasi Rom. religionis addicti esse nt, a sacrificulo aut monacho, vel rebaptizari se, vel matrimonio novo copulari curaverint, praeter arbitrariam Magistratus poenam, 100. florenos persolvant, omnes vero alij, qui vel baptismo vel copulationi isti maritali adfuerint, 50. florenos numerent, sacrificulus vero vel Monachus, qui id fecerit, simili poena adficiatur. Qui autem conventicula ejusmodi instituere & introducere in loco aliquo conati fuerint, quadruplo majori quam qui illis adfuerint, multa afficiantur. Sed & hoc tandem imperare, ne quis vel in Provincijs habitans, vel in illis commercia sua agitans, ullam contributionem pecuniarum faciat, quae ex Provincijs ad loca alia transferantur, & vel ad Templialicujus extruendi, vel Collegij instituendi usum adhibeatur, nec quicquam expendat aut contribuat sine expresso Magistratus Provinciarum consensu, constituta in eos, qui vel exactiones ista facere, vel contributam pecuniam ex provincijs abducere ausi fuerint, poena capitali & omnium bonorum confiscatione; In eos vero, qui contributione aliquam fecerint, poena Magistratus arbitraria, & multa quadrupli statuta, quarum multarum tertia pars Praefetis sive Magistratui, tertia delatoribus cedere, tertia item in usum Reipubl. converti debeat, nec tamen specialibus interim in hoc negotio pro Provincijs promulgatis edictis quicquam hoc edicto derogetur.
units.tr: in this place, and state the reason for their coming, and likewise disclose where they have their lodging; and all the persons mentioned above who have already come to these Provinces, but have no fixed residence there, shall be bound to do the same after the lapse of the two months; the Prefects shall faithfully record all these things and report them to the higher Magistrates, lest anything be attempted by such persons that tends to the ruin of the Provinces. But if anyone is caught having professed his name in this way, he shall be fined fifty florins and forced to leave the country, so that he may never return to these United Provinces under penalty of public outlawry. Moreover, all and each of those with whom Jesuits, monks and other Roman-religion clerics and ecclesiastics are to lodge are now ordered and commanded to make careful inquiry whether these persons have made their declaration, or themselves to make it before the Prefects and Magistrates before the third night of their stay, under a penalty of one hundred florins, with no excuse, as if they had not seen these persons, set aside and neglected; excepting, however, public inns, since nothing certain can be affirmed about them from their knowledge. Furthermore, all inhabitants of those Provinces are forbidden and prohibited, once this mandate is published, to enter any college or school of the Jesuits, under penalty that those who are admitted to any office or public post in the Provinces, or enjoy any canonry or benefice, shall be deemed unfit for ever, and shall in addition be compelled to pay a fine of one hundred florins from their goods every month; and those too shall be bound to pay this who entered the schools and colleges of the Jesuits before the publication of this mandate and did not leave within a two-month period. But if any of them have no goods, the fine shall be exacted from their parents or guardians, unless they entered those schools and colleges otherwise and against their will, in which case the parents and guardians are forbidden to send or to have sent money or anything else to them, either directly or through an intermediary, under penalty of the aforesaid fine of one hundred florins to be paid from their own goods. All alienation of their property by those who remain in the Jesuit schools and colleges against this mandate, whether by gift, will, codicil or any other disposition, is declared wholly null and of no force. Furthermore, it is ordered that no one shall be admitted to any office or public post, whether native or foreign, who after the lapse of two months from the publication of the mandate has received any degree of honour among them, especially by oath to defend the superstitions of Rome; and that those who took that oath after the pacification of Ghent in the year 1576 and were employed in some office shall, within two months after this publication, be released from that oath and bind themselves by an oath of fidelity to these Provinces in the places where they live, unless, having already taken the oath of fidelity, they have renounced those superstitions, which renunciation and the taking of the oath they wish to hold valid. Moreover, all who have obtained, or shall obtain in future, any degree under the Papist oath, and who either now live or in future will live in any place of the United Provinces, are ordered to appear before the Magistrate of that place within a month, either after the publication of this edict or after their arrival in these Provinces, and to take the oath of fidelity, under penalty that they leave the Provinces: a fine of fifty florins after the first month, of one hundred after the second, and if they have not departed by the third month, they shall be publicly outlawed. Furthermore, all inhabitants and newcomers of the United Provinces are commanded that in no temple, private place, field or ship they establish any assembly of men or women, celebrate Masses, or practise Papist superstitions by teaching, reading or exhorting, or foster conventicles of persons attached to the Roman religion, even if no priest, monk or cleric is present to conduct these exercises, and whatever the pretext under which it is done, whether publicly or privately, under a penalty of two hundred florins, to be paid by the owner of the house, field or ship in which such conventicles were held; and those who celebrated Masses or conducted other exercises of Papist superstition shall be banished for ever if they are foreigners, and subjected to some further discretionary penalty; if they are natives, they shall be punished with perpetual exile and deprivation of all benefices, and no one shall receive them as guests, under a fine for lodging of one hundred florins for the first offence, two hundred for the second, and three hundred with perpetual outlawry for the third. But those who were present at the Mass and other exercises of Papist superstitions shall be deprived of all their benefices, and shall pay so many florins for each occasion on which they are found or convicted of having done so; and all others also who were caught at these conventicles shall be bound to pay this fine together with the loss of their best clothing, it being considered that if anyone has brought in any doctrine opposed to the political government of the Provinces and contrary to the obedience of subjects, he shall be put to death as a disturber of public peace and tranquillity. Furthermore, it is decreed and ordained that those who have caused themselves, under the pretence of belonging to the Roman religion, to be rebaptized or newly married by a priest or monk, shall pay one hundred florins, in addition to the discretionary penalty of the Magistrate; all others who were present at the baptism or that marriage shall pay fifty florins each, and the priest or monk who did it shall be punished with a similar penalty. But those who have tried to set up and introduce such conventicles in any place shall be fined four times as much as those who attended them. Finally, it is also ordered that no one, whether living in the Provinces or conducting business in them, shall make any contribution of money that is transferred from the Provinces to other places and used for building a temple of any kind or founding a college; nor shall anyone spend or contribute anything without the express consent of the Magistrates of the Provinces. Those who have dared to make such exactions or to take money contributed in the Provinces out of them shall be punished by death and confiscation of all their goods; those who have made any contribution shall be subject to a discretionary penalty of the Magistrate and a fine of four times the amount, one third of which fines is to go to the Prefect or Magistrate, one third to the informers, and one third is to be applied to the use of the Commonwealth; nor is anything in this edict to be derogated from by the special edicts promulgated in the meantime for the Provinces on this matter.

units.la: Mandatum hoc 27. Martij Hagae Comitis publicatum, causam adverse parti praebuit, ut nullum unitarum Provinciarum incolam in suis ditionibus regionibusq; ultra decem vel ad summum 14. dies, quicquid etiam negotij expediendum ibi haberet, nisi professio nem faciens ad Missae officium venisset, tolerare voluerint.
units.tr: This mandate, published at The Hague by the Count on 27 March, gave the opposing side an occasion: they wished that no inhabitant of the United Provinces be tolerated in their lands and regions for more than ten days, or at most fourteen, whatever business he had to transact there, unless he came to the Mass after making profession of the Catholic faith.

units.la: Hoc tamen quantumvis severissimo Edicto parum Illustrissimi Ordines obtinuerunt. Nam anno millesimo sexcentesimo decimo sexto in lucem editus est libellus hoc titulo: Iesuitica per unitas Belgij Provincias Negotiatio. In eo continentur scripta quaedam Iesuitica, reperta inter chartas cuiusdam Patris & Sacrificuli Iesuiticae Societatis. In scriptis ac literis istis videlicet, quibus artibus, quantoque studio suam, quam vocant, Negotiationem in unitis Provincijs Iesuitae exerceant, & Pontificiam religionem, cum Dominatione Iesuitica in Ecclesiae & Reipubl. Reformatae pernitiem propagare conentur. Adscribam Indicem quorundam saltem, quae in his scriptis notatu digna reperiuntur.
units.tr: Yet, however severe this edict was, the Most Illustrious Estates gained little by it. For in the year 1616 a little book was published under this title: The Jesuit Trade in the United Provinces of Belgium. It contains certain Jesuit writings, found among the papers of a certain Father and priest of the Jesuit Society. In these writings and letters, namely, it is set out by what arts and with how much zeal the Jesuits carry on their so-called Trade in the United Provinces, and how they strive to spread the Papist religion, with Jesuit domination, to the ruin of the Reformed Church and commonwealth. I shall add an index of at least some of the matters found in these writings that are worth noting.

units.la: 1. Complures Iesuitas in Provincias Belgicas foederatas a Superioribus emitti.
units.tr: 1. That a number of Jesuits are sent by their Superiors into the Dutch Belgian Provinces.

units.la: 2. Non tantum ut veteres Pontificios confirment, sed etiam, ut omnibus modis novos lucrifaciant.
units.tr: 2. Not only to confirm the old Papists, but also to win over new ones by every means.

units.la: 3. Atque adeo ut integras Provincias ad consensum in Religione Papistica perducant.
units.tr: 3. And indeed to bring whole Provinces to agreement in the Papist religion.

units.la: 4. Illud ut effectum dent, non solum plebem eos seducere, sed vel in primis id opera dare, ut eos, qui authoritate valent & rerum potiuntur, in nassam suam pertrahant, quorum opera Iesuitica negotiationem per totam Provinciam fructuosius exerceant.
units.tr: 4. To achieve this, they should not only mislead the common people, but above all take pains to draw into their net those who hold authority and power, through whose work the Jesuit trade may be carried on more profitably throughout the whole Province.

units.la: 5. Talibus eos permittere, ut fiant Secreto Catholici, quod ajunt, modo se totos ad eorum nutum & consilia Iesuitarum accommodent.
units.tr: 5. To allow such men to become, as they say, secret Catholics, provided that they wholly accommodate themselves to the nod and counsels of the Jesuits.

units.la: 6. Quin etiam cum talibus eos dispensare in audiendis Reformatorum concionibus carnium esu, ut eo tutius lateant, & res Papisticas commodius juvent.
units.tr: 6. Moreover, to grant such men dispensation from eating meat when they attend the sermons of the Reformed, so that they may lie hidden more safely and aid Papist affairs more conveniently.

units.la: 7. Permittere etiam illis, ut Senatui Reformatorum intersint, in deprehensionem & dispationem conventuum Pontificiorum una cum caeteris consentiant, modo genuini sint Papistae eoq; id faciant fine, ut se occultent, & consilia, quae adversus Papistas habentur, impediant, eosdem urgente necessitate praemoneant, omniqúe occasione Papisticam religionem propagent.
units.tr: 7. Also to permit them to attend the Senate of the Reformed, and to agree with the others in detecting and breaking up Papist assemblies, provided they are genuine Papists, and to do so for this purpose: that they may conceal themselves, and hinder the plans that are made against the Papists, warn the Papists when urgent need requires, and advance the Papist religion on every occasion.

units.la: 8. Omni eos arte & studio Belgicam juventutem tentare.
units.tr: 8. To try the Belgian youth by every art and effort.

units.la: 9. Eos invigilare super externis & internis; & versari in utroque homine & utroque sæculo.
units.tr: 9. That they keep watch over external and internal affairs, and be busy in both man and both world.

units.la: 10. Dumq; isthæc omnia jussu Superiorum gnaviter exequuntur, nolle tamen censeri in rerum numero, qui se rebus station immisceant.
units.tr: 10. And while they diligently carry out all these things by the command of their Superiors, they are nonetheless unwilling to be counted among those who mix themselves in affairs of state.

units.la: 11. Distribui fæderatum Belgium in Provincias, & unicuiq; emissario Iesuitico afsignari certum & fixum locum residentiæ, e quo se movere ipsi non liceat absque Superiorum consensu.
units.tr: 11. That the confederated Belgium be divided into Provinces, and that a certain and fixed place of residence be assigned to each Jesuit agent, from which it is not lawful for him to move without the consent of his Superiors.

units.la: 12. Excursiones etiam ad vicina loca singulis imperari.
units.tr: 12. Excursions to nearby places are also to be ordered for each one.

units.la: 13. Habere eos in Provinciis unitis Superiorem missionis, quem vocant, ad quem tenentur recurrere incidentibus difficultatibus.
units.tr: 13. That they have in the United Provinces a Superior of the mission, as they call him, to whom they are bound to have recourse when difficulties arise.

units.la: 14. Iesuitas numerum Pontificiorum in singulis urbibus, & decreta ab ijs in rem Pontificiam facta referre in libros usui ipsi destinatos.
units.tr: 14. The Jesuits are to report the number of Papists in each town, and the decrees made by them in favour of the Papist cause, into books destined for their own use.

units.la: 15. Pecunias quoq; eorum directione colligi, & à Quæstoribus in usus communes rei Pontificiæ asservari.
units.tr: 15. Money also is to be collected under their direction, and kept by the treasurers for the common uses of the Papist cause.

units.la: 16. Emissos & in Belgio residentes Iesuitas teneri sæpissimè ad Superiores scribere omnibus tam politicis, quam Ecclesiasticis, ut omnium locorum conditio illis plenissimè notescat.
units.tr: 16. The Jesuits sent out and residing in Belgium are bound very often to write to their Superiors, both on political and ecclesiastical matters, so that the condition of all places may become fully known to them.

units.la: 17. In hunc finem certa capita illis præscripta esse, quæ in literis scribendis sequantur.
units.tr: 17. For this purpose certain headings are prescribed to them, which they follow in writing letters.

units.la: 18. Habere eos stylum ipsis solis (non externis) cognitum, & plerumque de rebus suis scribere tamquam de sæculari Mercatura, sive negotiatione, item rationibus & computo, exhiti, soluti, &c.
units.tr: 18. They have a style known to themselves alone (not to outsiders), and for the most part they write of their affairs as of secular merchandise or trade, likewise with accounts and reckonings: received, paid, and so on.

units.la: 19. Cum tabellarijs literas perferendas committunt, non exprimere eos in inscriptione nomen Iesuitæ, ad quem pertinent, sed nomen alicujus Civis, aut Mercatoris Pontificij, qui sciat, ad quem sint curandæ literæ ex duabus prioribus literis nominis Iesuitæ inscriptioni subjectis.
units.tr: 19. When they entrust letters to couriers, they do not write out in the address the name of the Jesuit to whom they belong, but the name of some citizen or Papist merchant who knows to whom the letters are to be delivered, the first two letters of the Jesuit's name being added beneath the address.

units.la: 20. Superiores de ijs, quæ ab emissis Iesuitis perscribuntur, statuere, &, si postulet necessitas, consulere Provincialem aut Generalem Romæ residentem, ut pro re nata Romæ & Bruxellis imperent aut disponant, quæ ad commodum Iesuiticæ Negotiationis spectare possint.
units.tr: 20. The Superiors decide on the matters reported by the Jesuits sent out, and, if necessity requires, consult the Provincial or the General residing at Rome, so that they may order or arrange at Rome and Brussels, as the occasion arises, whatever may serve the advantage of the Jesuit trade.

units.la: 21. Non sufficere, ut sæpè & diligenter de omnibus scribant emissarij, sed requiri insuper, ut aliquoties (minimum semel in anno) ad Superiores excurrant, & de omnibus quam accuratissimè eos certiores faciant, eaque, quæ literis committi non expedit, coram audiant & videant.
units.tr: 21. It is not enough for the agents to write often and diligently about everything; it is further required that they go to their Superiors at intervals (at least once a year), and inform them of everything as accurately as possible, and hear and see in person those matters which it is not advisable to commit to letters.

units.la: 22. Præter ordinarie in his partibus residentes, etiam emitti extraordinarios, qui residionem, maximè ædes Nobilium & potentiarum perambulent.
units.tr: 22. Besides those who reside ordinarily in these parts, extraordinary agents are also sent out, who walk about through the residence, especially the houses of nobles and powerful men.

units.la: 23. Iesuitas ut plurimum commoda veteribus sacrificulis præripere, ijsque expulsos longè & latè dominari propter authoritatem, quâ pollent Bruxellis & potissimùm Romæ.
units.tr: 23. The Jesuits for the most part snatch the advantages away from the old priests, and those who have been expelled rule far and wide on account of the authority they hold at Brussels and especially at Rome.

units.la: 24. Extat etiam in his scriptis Epistola Iesuitæ cujusdam, in qua ad Illustrissimum quendam scribit, Pontificios pacem cum Reformatis facere non posse, nisi fiant Pontifices: Unde potest intelligi, quid Evangelici sibi de pace Pontificia secundum Iesuitas sibi polliceri debeant, si Papismum amplecti nolint.
units.tr: 24. There is also extant among these writings a letter of a certain Jesuit, in which he writes to a certain most illustrious man that the Papists cannot make peace with the Reformed unless they themselves become Popes. From this it can be understood what the Evangelicals ought to promise themselves of Papist peace, according to the Jesuits, if they refuse to embrace Papism.

units.la: QVID ARTIBVS SVIS NEFARIIS IESVITAE AQVISGRANI TENTARINT ATQVE ETIAM OBTINVERINT
units.tr: How the Jesuits at Aachen, by their wicked arts, attempted and even succeeded in obtaining their ends
