Propositio hæc (inquit) Papa potestatem habet, ad deponendos Reges hæreticos & pertinaces, suo regno in rebus ad salutem animæ pertinentibus perniciosos, inter dogmata fidei tenenda & credenda est. Nam continetur in verbis Christi, Petro singulariter & peculiari ratione di&is: Quodcunq; ligaveris, & quodcunq; solveris, & pasce oves meas: Prout Catholica Ecclesia, quæ est columna & firmamentum veritatis, illa intellexit, & apertissimè declaravit Bonifacius 8. in Extravagante Unam sanctam de majoritate & obedientia, concludens esse veritatem hanc de necessitate salutis.
units.tr: From the same book 6, chapter 844, number 8: "This proposition, that the Pope has the power to depose heretical and obstinate kings who are harmful to their kingdom in matters pertaining to the salvation of the soul, is to be held and believed among the articles of faith. For it is contained in the words of Christ, spoken singularly and in a peculiar manner to Peter: 'Whatsoever you shall bind, and whatsoever you shall loose,' and 'feed my sheep.' As the Catholic Church, which is the pillar and ground of truth, has understood these words and most plainly declared, Boniface VIII in the Extravagant Unam sanctam concerning the majority and obedience, concluding that this truth is necessary for salvation."

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Quinto docent, Veneno Imperatores, Reges, Principes à subditis vel ministris suis necari posse, fi modo Theologi, Jesuitæ, viri eruditi & graves illos pro tyrannis & excommunicatis habeant; Ita tamen, ut ii, qui perimendus est, nihil adjuvet, nec sibi ipsi mortem consciscat.
units.tr: Fifthly, they teach that emperors, kings and princes may be poisoned by their subjects or servants, provided that theologians, Jesuits, learned and serious men regard them as tyrants and excommunicated. But this holds only if the person to be killed does nothing to help the act and does not bring death upon himself.

units.la: Ioan. Mariana Iesuita Toletanus de Rege lib. 1. c. 7. p. 65. & feq. cuius caput tulus est, An liceat Regem veneno occidere? & postea, An facultas fit, sicut armis, sic veneno, herbifq; lethalibus tyrannum occidere? inquit; Quid interest, ferro, an veneno perimas? veneno quod fit, minori periculo, & majori spe impunitatis fit. Hoc tamen tempera mento, me auctore, veneno uti licebit; Si non ipse, qui perimitur, venenum haurire cogitur, quo concepto pereat, sed externis ab alio adhibeatur, nihil adjuvante eo, qui perimendus est, nimirum cum veneni tanta vis est, ut fella eo, aut veste delibuta, vim interficiendi habeat. Et in fine eiusdem c. p. 68. concludit: In ejus vitam grassari quacunq; arte concessum ne cogatur tantum sciens aut imprudens sibi mortem consciscere.
units.tr: Juan de Mariana, a Jesuit of Toledo, in his book On the King, book 1, chapter 7, pp. 65 ff., whose chapter heading is "Whether it is lawful to kill a king with poison?" and afterwards "Whether it is permitted to kill a tyrant with poison and deadly herbs just as with arms?", says: "What difference does it make whether you kill with iron or with poison? Poison carries less danger and offers a greater hope of impunity. Yet, on my authority, poison may be used with this qualification: that the one who is killed is not himself forced to drink the poison, by which he dies once he has taken it, but that it is applied externally by another, the intended victim doing nothing to help, namely when the poison is so strong that it can kill when smeared on a saddle or a garment." And at the end of the same chapter, p. 68, he concludes: "It is allowed to plot against his life by any art whatsoever, provided that he is not forced, knowingly or unknowingly, to bring death upon himself."

units.la: Et ex hac Marianæ doctrina fluxit, Quod Iesuita Richardus V Valpot fociu Marianæ ante annos 12. Anglum Eduardum Squirre Veneno instruxit, quo Reginæ Angliæ & Effexio non edendum aut bibendum præberet, sed quo fel iam tantum ita inungeret, ut ex eius contactu utrque moreretur. Memoria Ligæ Tom. 4. pag. 15. & fequent; Memorial. Ligæ Tom. 6. pag. 251, 252, 256, 261. & Tom. 1. pag. 13. & 16. Catechif. Iefuit. pag. 222. Mariana de Rege pagina 54. Cæso Rege ingens sibi nomen fecit. Et pagina 57. Ab omni memoria conjuratos deramus, in magna laude fuisse, quicunque tyrannos opprimere aggressi sunt. Et pagina 74. Si hujusmodi post designatum facinus evaserint, instar heroum in omni vita fufcipiuntur: Sin secus accidat, Grata superis, grata hominibus hostia cadunt, nobili conatu ad memoriam posteritatis memoriam illustrati. Et sic in eiusdem libri limine præfatur Magister Provincialis Petrus de Onna: Si ad hanc præscriptam formam actiones & consilia referantur, nam magnum atque incredibile operæpretium existet. In lib. etiam 4. de iusta Henrici III. Regis Galliæ abdicatione, & in Guil. Roffæi de iusta Reip. Chriftianæ in reges impios & hæreticos authoritate, &c. probare conantur, Omnes hæreticos & politicos seu pacis amates Papistas quoq; occidendos, atq; ipsum imprimis Henricum IV. Regem Galliæ: Et in hunc finem in præfatione prioris libri di&tus Rex vocatur Impius, hæreticus, relapsus, tyrannus, sacrilegus, impurus, incestuosus, homicida, excommunicatus. Et Ludovicus Aurell. vocat eum culinarem canem, pogonatum Julianum, bipedum nequiffimum, apostatam, fœtidum, Satanæ stercus. Sequitur in di&o libro de iusta Henr. IV. abdic. Admonere itaque non cessemus, omnes omnium vires in execrandum istud caput eiufq; assertores colligantur, utq; omni ratione fiat, ut anathema ista è medio abigantur.
units.tr: From this teaching of Mariana there followed the fact that the Jesuit Richard Valpot, a companion of Mariana, some twelve years ago equipped the Englishman Edward Squire with poison, with which he was to offer the Queen of England and Essex not something to eat or drink, but with which he was to smear the saddle so that both would die by contact with it. (See Memorial of the League, vol. 4, pp. 15 ff.; Memorial of the League, vol. 6, pp. 251, 252, 256, 261, and vol. 1, pp. 13 and 16; Catechism of the Jesuits, p. 222.) Mariana, On the King, p. 54: "After the king was slain, he made for himself a great name." P. 57: "We have it from all memory that those who have undertaken to crush tyrants have been held in great esteem." P. 74: "If such men escape after the deed has been planned, they are received throughout their lives as heroes; but if things turn out otherwise, they fall as a sacrifice pleasing to the gods and to men, made illustrious for posterity's memory by a noble effort." Thus in the preface of the same book the Provincial Master Petrus de Onna introduces it: "If actions and counsels are referred to this prescribed form, it will be a great and incredible benefit." In book 4, on the lawful deposition of Henry III, King of France, and in William Rossaeus, on the lawful authority of the Christian commonwealth over impious and heretical kings, and so on, they try to prove that all heretics and politiques, or lovers of peace, even Papists, are to be killed, and above all Henry IV, King of France. To this end, in the preface of the earlier book, the said king is called impious, heretic, relapsed, tyrant, sacrilegious, impure, incestuous, murderer, and excommunicate. And Ludovicus Aurellus calls him a kitchen dog, a bearded Julian, the most wicked of bipeds, an apostate, a stinking creature, Satan's dung. The said book on the deposition of Henry IV goes on: "Let us therefore not cease to admonish that the strength of all be gathered against that accursed head and its defenders, and that by every means this anathema be removed from the midst."

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Sexto docent Haereticos Magistratus, hoc est, Evangelicos, pro excommunicatis habendos, si non de facto, tamen de iure, ideo ipso proscribendos, abdicandos, & e medio tollendos esse.
units.tr: Sixth, they teach that heretical magistrates, that is, Evangelicals, are to be regarded as excommunicated, if not in fact yet at least in law; and that for this reason they are to be outlawed, deposed, and removed from the world.

units.la: Symancha de Excommunicatione tit. 27. sect. 1. pag. 116. b. Haeretici, inquit, ipso jure sunt excommunicati, & a communione fidelium diris proscriptionibus feriuntur, & quotannis in Coena Domini excommunicantur a Papa. Facit autem Regem vel alium Principem non esse haereticum professum, sed animi sensa sibi ipsi occultare, quid loco ille tunc habendus? Symancha ibidem respondet: Quaeri autem solet, an hereticus occultus excommunicatus sit ipso jure, & in alias etiam poenas incidat contra haereticos statutas? Cui quaestioni simpliciter jurisperiti respondent, quod etsi haeresis occulta sit, nihilominus haereticus occultus incidit in illas poenas. Sive igitur ille sit manifestus sive occultus haereticus, nil plane interest, in utrumque enim censuris & diris effulminatus. Sed si Princeps ita excommunicationis vinculo innodatus & abdicatus sinum Ecclesiae redeat, iterum ne regnum recuperabit? Respondet rursus: Si reges aut alii Principes facti sunt haeretici, protinus subjecti & vasalli ab eorum dominio liberantur, nec jus hoc recuperabunt, quamvis postea reconciliantur Ecclesiae. Mater tamen Ecclesiae nunquam claudit gremium redeunti. Hoc verum agnoscunt, distincta tamen distinctione, quoad animam, verum quoad Regnum hoc non recuperat, quia coniunctis sententiis hoc omnes tenent, modo non sit ad damnum Ecclesiae. Concedatur autem eiusmodi abdicatum Principem relinquere filium legitimum et certum haeredem, qui paterni criminis labe non sit inquinatus, illene in Regia dignitate succedet? neutiquam; perfundetur. Haeresis enim est lepra & morbus haereditarius, & ex leprosis parentibus leprosi generantur filii: ita asserit Symancha, propter haeresim Regis, non solum Rex regno privatur, sed & eius filij a regni successione pelluntur. Crespvellus in Philopatre, seu Responsione ad edictum Elizabethae Reginae, Sect. 2. num. 162. pag. centesima quinquagesima tertia. Certe, ait, non tantum licet, sed summa etiam juris divini necessitate ac praecepto, imo etiam conscientiae arctissimo vinculo, & extremo etiam animarum suarum periculo ac discrimine Christianis omnibus hoc solum incumbit, ob haeresis manifestum crimen Principes deturbare, vel obsistere ne admittantur, si praestare possunt. Franciscus Verona Constantinus in sua Apologia pro Iohanne Castello art. 2. cap. 2. pluribus docet, Quod non obstante decreto Concilij Constantiensis privatim & singulis licitum sit, Reges & Principes haereseos & tyrannidis damnatos occidere. Treshamus in libro de officio Principis Christiani cap. 5. Si Princeps, inquit, haereticus sit, & obstinate & pertinaciter intolerabilis, summi Pastoris divina potestate deponatur, & aliud caput constituatur, cui subditi se jungant, & legitimo ordine & auctoritate tyrannidem amoveant. Henricus Garnetus etiam, Osvvaldus Tesmond & Ioan. Gerard alijque Iesuitae Thomae Vvhitero, Guidoni Fauukes, Thomae Batesio, necnon Rob. Catesbeyo, Thomae Percio, Ioan. & Christophoro Vuright, alijsque persuaserunt, Angliae Regem, omnesque regni illius Proceres & praesules, esse haereticos excommunicatos; ideoque licitum meritoriumque esse, eos simul omnes e medio quacunque ratione tollere, ut testantur Acta Henrici Garneti & aliorum. Sic etiam Vrbanus II. Papa decrevit, eos non habendos pro homicidis, quos adversus excommunicatos zelo Catholicae matris Ecclesiae ardentes, aliquos eorum trucidasse contigerit. C. excommunicatorum. 23. q. 5.
units.tr: Symancha, On Excommunication, title 27, section 1, page 116 b: "Heretics," he says, "are excommunicated by law itself, and they are struck with dire proscriptions from the communion of the faithful, and every year on the Lord's Supper they are excommunicated by the Pope." But suppose the King or another prince has not professed heresy openly, but keeps the sentiments of his mind hidden: what is he then to be regarded as? Symancha answers in the same place: "It is usually asked whether a secret heretic is excommunicated by law and incurs also the other penalties laid down against heretics. To this question the jurists simply reply that even if the heresy is secret, a secret heretic nonetheless incurs those penalties." So whether he is a manifest or a secret heretic makes no real difference, for in either case he is struck with censures and dire curses. But if a prince, bound and cut off by the chain of excommunication, returns to the bosom of the Church, will he recover his kingdom again? He answers again: "If kings or other princes have become heretics, their subjects and vassals are at once freed from their dominion, and they will not recover this right, even though they are afterwards reconciled to the Church." Yet the mother Church never shuts her bosom to one who returns. They acknowledge this as true, but with a distinction: "as to the soul, yes; as to the kingdom, no, it is not recovered; for all hold this together with the sentences, provided it is not to the harm of the Church." Suppose, however, that such a deposed prince leaves a legitimate and undoubted heir, who is not stained with the stain of his father's crime: will he succeed to the royal dignity? By no means; he will be cut off. For heresy is a leprosy and a hereditary disease, and leprous children are born of leprous parents; so Symancha asserts: "On account of the King's heresy, not only is the King deprived of the kingdom, but his sons also are driven away from the succession to the kingdom." Crespvellus, in Philopater, or Answer to the edict of Queen Elizabeth, section 2, number 162, page 153: "Certainly," he says, "it is not only lawful, but by the highest necessity and precept of divine law, and even by the most binding tie of conscience, and at the extreme peril and hazard of their souls, that this alone is incumbent on all Christians: to depose princes on account of the manifest crime of heresy, or to resist their admission, if they are able to do so." Francis Verona Constantinus, in his Apology for John Castel, article 2, chapter 2, teaches at length that, notwithstanding the decree of the Council of Constance, it is lawful for private persons, and for individuals, to kill kings and princes condemned for heresy and tyranny. Tresham, in the book On the Office of a Christian Prince, chapter 5: "If a prince," he says, "is a heretic, and obstinately and pertinaciously intolerable, let him be deposed by the divine power of the supreme Pastor, and another head be appointed, to whom the subjects may join themselves, and by lawful order and authority remove the tyranny." Henry Garnet also, Oswald Tesmond, John Gerard and other Jesuits persuaded Thomas Winter, Guy Fawkes, Thomas Bates, and likewise Robert Catesby, Thomas Percy, John and Christopher Wright, and others, that the King of England, and all the nobles and prelates of that kingdom, are excommunicated heretics; and therefore that it is lawful and meritorious to remove them all together from the world by whatever means, as the Acts of Henry Garnet and others attest. Thus also Pope Urban II decreed that those should not be regarded as murderers whom, burning with zeal for the Catholic mother Church against the excommunicated, it happened that they slew. C. excommunicatorum, 23, q. 5.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Septimo docent, Principes Christianos à Romana Religione deficientes, abdicandos.
units.tr: Seventhly, they teach that Christian princes who fall away from the Roman religion must be deposed.

units.la: Crefvvellus Iesuita in suo libro cui Philopater titulum fecit pag. 109. scribit; Quemcunque Principem Christianum, sit à religione Catholica manifeste deflexerit, & alios avocare voluerit, excidere statim omni potestate ac dignitate, ex ipsa vi juris tum humani, tum divini, hoc ante dictam sententiam supremi Pastoris ac judicis contra ipsum prolatam, & subditos quoscunque liberos esse ab omni juramenti obligatione, quod de obedientia tanquam Principi legitimo praestitissent: possseque & debere, si vires habeant, istiusmodi hominem tanquam apostatam, haereticum & Christi Domini defertorem, & Reipublicae suae inimicum hostemque ex hominum Christianorum dominatu eji-cere: Atque hanc esse certam, definitam & indubitatam virorum doctissimorum sen-tentiam.
units.tr: Crefvvellus the Jesuit, in his book which he entitled Philopater, page 109, writes: Whatever Christian prince has manifestly turned aside from the Catholic religion, and wishes to draw others away with him, immediately loses all power and dignity, by the very force of law both human and divine, once the sentence of the supreme Pastor and judge has been pronounced against him; and all his subjects are free from every bond of the oath by which they had sworn obedience to him as their lawful prince. And it is and ought to be the case that, if they have the strength, they may and must drive such a man out of the rule of Christian men, as an apostate, a heretic, a deserter of Christ the Lord, and an enemy and foe of their commonwealth. This, he says, is the certain, settled and indubitable opinion of the most learned men.

units.la: Rursus: Regnandi, inquit, jus amittit, qui religionem Romanam deserit.
units.tr: Again: He who forsakes the Roman religion, he says, loses the right to reign.

units.la: Mariana lib. 1. de Rege cap. 6. docet, Cum talibus, qui sacra Patria (Romanam religionem) abjiciunt, tanquam cum canibus rabidis agendum. Et pag. 58. Mogunt. edit. Laudandum eum dicit, qui vitae suae periculo publicam utilitatem redimat & hujusmodi Regem omnium telis exagitandum, quasi crudele monstrum terrae in-cubans.
units.tr: Mariana, book 1, On the King, chapter 6, teaches: One must deal with such people, who cast off the sacred fatherland (the Roman religion), as with rabid dogs. And on page 58 of the Mainz edition: He says that the man is to be praised who redeems the public good at the risk of his own life, and that such a king is to be harried with the weapons of all, as a cruel monster lying upon the earth.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Octavo docent, Principes Christianos, haereticis faventes deponendos.
units.tr: Eighthly, they teach that Christian princes who favour heretics are to be deposed.

units.la: Treshamus in libro de officio Principis Christiani, manifeste definit & concludit; Si quis Rex haereticum favore prosequatur, ipso facto regnum amittit. Et cap. 5. Princeps indulgendo haereticis, non solum DEUM offendit, sed perdit regnum & gentem. Tales Stapletonus in Oratione contra Politicos Duaci habita B. 103. haereticis & Turcis deteriores dicit.
units.tr: Treshamus, in his book on the office of a Christian prince, states and concludes plainly: "If any king favours a heretic, he loses his kingdom by that very fact." And in chapter 5: "A prince who indulges heretics not only offends God, but loses his kingdom and his people." Stapleton, in his oration against the Politicians delivered at Douai (p. 103), calls such princes worse than heretics and Turks.

units.la: Iesuitae in lib. 4. cap. 3. de iusta Henrici Tertii abdicat; citant & probant Concilii Lateranensis Constitut. 3. quae sic habet: Qui Principes terram suam non ab haeresi purgaverint, ab eorum fidelitate soluti Vasalli denunciantur, & caetera alia possidenda dentur.
units.tr: The Jesuits, in book 4, chapter 3, on the lawful deposition of Henry III, cite and rely on the third constitution of the Lateran Council, which reads: "Those princes who do not purge their land of heresy are declared by denunciation to be released from the allegiance of their vassals, and the other lands are to be given over to be possessed."

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Nono docent, Ut haereticus (Evangelicus seu Orthodoxus) sit infamis ipso jure, nec ad publica officia, seu Consilia, nec ad eligendos aliquos, neque ad testimonium admittatur: utque nullus ei super quocunque negotio, sed ipse aliis respondere cogatur: &, si judex exstiterit, sententia eius nullam obtineat firmitatem. Sic Simmancha de Haeret. q. 46. n. 58. Inprimis Conradus Brunus de Haeret. lib. 5. cap. 7. & sequq. Vide etiam c. exco-municamus de Haeret.
units.tr: Ninthly, they teach that a heretic (that is, an Evangelical or Orthodox person) is infamous by law itself, and is admitted neither to public offices or councils, nor to the choosing of anyone, nor to giving testimony; that no one is bound to answer him in any matter whatever, while he himself is compelled to answer others; and that, if he has been a judge, his sentence has no firmness whatever. So Simancas, On Heresy, q. 46, n. 58. Above all, Conrad Brun, On Heresy, bk. 5, ch. 7 and following. See also the chapter Excommunicamus, On Heresy.

units.la: X. De Ect
units.tr: X. On the Ect-

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: DECIMO docent Iesuitæ, Hæreticis (Evangelicis) fidem prorsus illam habendam esse.
units.tr: Tenthly, the Jesuits teach that faith is by no means to be kept with heretics (Evangelicals).

units.la: Simancha Instit. cath. tit. 46. Art. 52. Ad pœnam quoque, inquit, pertinet & hæreticorum odium, quo fides illis data servanda non sit. Rationem hanc addit: Si enim tyrannis, piratis & cæteris prædonibus, fides servanda non est, qui corpus occidunt; longe minus hæreticis pertinacibus, qui occidunt animas, Et mox: Cum hæreticis nullum mercium, nulla pax Catholicis esse debet. Quamobrem fides illis data, etiam juramento firmata, contra publicum bonum, contra salutem animarum, contra jura divina & humana, NVLLO MODO SERVANDA EST.
units.tr: Simancha, Instit. cath. tit. 46, art. 52: Hatred of heretics also belongs to the punishment, by which the faith given to them need not be kept. He adds this reason: For if faith is not to be kept with tyrants, pirates and other robbers, who kill the body, much less with obstinate heretics, who kill souls. And soon after: With heretics there should be no trade or peace for Catholics. Therefore faith given to them, even when confirmed by oath, against the public good, against the salvation of souls, and against divine and human law, IS IN NO WAY TO BE KEPT.

units.la: APPROBATIO DOCTRINAE IESVI- TARVM DE INTERFICIENDIS RE- GIBVS.
units.tr: THE APPROVAL OF THE JESUITS' DOCTRINE ON THE KILLING OF KINGS

units.la: Approbavit etiam præter superiores hanc doctrinam Iesuitarum de interficiendis Regibus &c. Censura libelli Marianæ de Rege & Regis institutione, regia authoritate à Fr. Petro de Onna Magistro Provinciali facta, quæ sic verbo ad verbum habet: Disertum plane & eruditum virum Iohannem Marianam esse (ut alia desint) tres libri satis indicant, quos de Rege & Regis institutione confecit elegantes & graves. Eos regia authoritate diligenter & attente perlegi, iterum & tertiò facturus, si per tempus & otium licuisset. Ita semel leeti placuerunt. In simili argumento auctores non pauci Regni & Reip. statum componunt. Nostler Regem à primis annis fuscep tum, ijs præceptis instruit, quæ eo loco digna sunt. Quippe in Deum conjectis oculis, ut sapiens architectus, ad eam regulam institutæ fabricæ fundamentis molem universam imponit. Æquum proinde judico, ut hoc opus typis mandatum, in luce & hominum manibus versetur, eorumque præsertim, qui ad Reip. gubernacula sedent. Qui si ad præscriptam eo formam actiones & consilia retulerint, næ magnum atque incredibile operæpretium efflet. Datum in nostro S. Mariæ de mercede redemptionis captivorum cœnobio, Mariti die 30. Mensis Decemb. Anno 1598.
units.tr: Besides the superiors, the Jesuits' doctrine on killing kings was also approved by the censure of Mariana's book on the King and the Institution of the King, issued under royal authority by Fr. Pedro de Oña, Provincial Master. It reads word for word as follows: That John Mariana is a learned and eloquent man (to say nothing else) is shown well enough by the three books he has written, elegant and weighty, On the King and the Institution of the King. I have read them carefully and attentively under royal authority, and I would read them a second and third time if time and leisure allowed. They pleased me so much on each reading. Many authors compose works on the same subject concerning the state of kingdoms and commonwealths. Our author instructs the King, from his earliest years, in those precepts which are worthy of that place. Indeed, with his eyes fixed on God, like a wise architect, he lays the whole mass of his work upon the foundations of the rule by which it was established. I therefore judge it right that this work be committed to print, and brought to light and into the hands of men, especially of those who sit at the helm of the commonwealth. If they shape their actions and counsels according to the form prescribed here, it will be of great and incredible benefit. Given at our monastery of St. Mary of the Ransom of Captives at Madrid, on Tuesday, the 30th day of December, in the year 1598.

units.la: Facultas autem imprimendi hos libros hæc est: Stephanus Hoieda Visitator Societatis Iesu in Provincia Toletana, potestate speciali facta à N. Patre Generali Claudio Aquaviva, do facultatem, ut imprimantur libri tres de Rege & Regis institutione, quos ripsit & composuit P. Iohannes Mariana eiusdem Societatis, quippe approbatos prius à viris gravibus & doctis, ex eodem nostro Ordine. In cuius rei fidem has literas dedi meo nomine subscriptas, & mei officij sigillo munitas. Madriti in Collegio nostro, quarto Non. Decemb. Anno 1599.
units.tr: The permission to print these books is as follows: Stephanus Hoieda, Visitor of the Society of Jesus in the Toledan Province, by special authority granted by our Father General Claudio Aquaviva, grants permission that the three books On the King and the Institution of the King, which were written and composed by Fr. John Mariana of the same Society, be printed, since they were previously approved by grave and learned men of our own Order. In witness of this I have given these letters, signed with my name and sealed with the seal of my office. At Madrid, in our College, on the fourth day before the Nones of December, in the year 1599.

units.la: Allatus est quoque ad Regem Angliæ liber, ut Cafaubonus in epistola ad Frontonem Ducæum Iesuitam pag. 26. refert, scriptus, ut videtur in Italia, atque etiam ibidem excusus: cuius libelli duæ partes sunt. Prior Epistolam continet P. Cottonis Iesuitæ declaratoriam ad Reginam Galliæ, in sermone Anglicum versam: Posterior dissertationem adversus eos, qui post Henrici Magni cædem, doctrinam Iesuiticam accusarunt tanquam cædis illius præcipuam causam. In hac parte, ubi primò doctrina de occidendis Principibus Iesuitis no proari testatus est: mox ad Marianæ defensionem Anonymus ille scriptor accingit: præfatus id à se propterea fieri, quod Pater Cotton in Epistola sua Marianam reliquerit indefensum, vellé se quod Epistolæ illi deest, supplere affirmatigitur, Marianam tota illa disputatione non de Regibus loqui, sed de tyrannis: quod apertissimum mendacium est. Tyrannus enim in Scholæ Sorbonicæ & aliis antiquæ simplicitatis legitimo Principi opponitur, & eum significat, qui Imperium non suum, per vim aut malas artes invadit: Mariana autem de Henrico Tertio Rege legitimo, non de aliquo invasore loquuntur. Iesuitis autem Tyrannus appellatur, omnis legitimus Rex, qui a Pontifice est excommunicatus. Tum additi libellus, tractaria a Mariana quaestionem a plurimis agitatam: quos omnes cum moderatione superaverit Mariana, satis ex eo posse intelligi, illos, qui Marianae librum eiusmodi doctrinae praetextu Lutetiae condemnarunt, non Marianam, sed Iesuitas, imo non Iesuitas, sed ipsum IESV Christi sanctissimum nomen odisse. Verba auctoris sunt haec: Illi sunt inimici sancti nominis IESV, qui condemnarunt Marianam propter talem doctrinam. En Lector unius Iesuitae, aut e magnis Iesuitarum patronis unius, sed non solius, iudicium, de prudentissimis Parlamenti Parisiensis Senatoribus, qui illam institutionem Marianae flammis meritissime addixerunt. Hinc igitur apparet, paucos esse hodie, qui Marianae illam dirissimam doctrinam detestentur. Et quare, obsecro, parricidarum magistrum execrarentur, quibus parricidia placet, parricidae laudantur, et beatitudine martyrum digni censentur: plane eiusdem hominis est, Marianae probare iudicium, et proditores ac parricidas consecratione seu Canonisatione dignos iudicare.
units.tr: A book was also brought to the King of England, as Casaubon reports in his letter to the Jesuit Fronton Du Duc, p. 26. It was apparently written in Italy and also printed there. It has two parts. The first contains a declaratory letter by the Jesuit Father Cotton, translated into English, addressed to the Queen of France. The second is a dissertation against those who, after the murder of Henry the Great, accused Jesuit doctrine of being the principal cause of that murder. In this second part, after first asserting that the doctrine on killing princes is not taught by the Jesuits, that anonymous writer immediately sets himself to defend Mariana. He says that he does so because Father Cotton left Mariana undefended in his letter, and that he wishes to supply what is lacking in that letter. He affirms that Mariana in that whole discussion speaks not of kings but of tyrants, which is a most obvious lie. For in the Sorbonne school and other authors of older simplicity, a tyrant is opposed to the lawful prince, and signifies one who invades a realm that is not his, by force or wicked arts; but Mariana speaks of Henry III, a lawful king, and not of some usurper. Yet among the Jesuits, every lawful king who has been excommunicated by the Pope is called a tyrant. Then he adds the treatise in which Mariana examines a question debated by many, and he says that it can well be understood from this that Mariana surpassed them all in moderation; and that those who condemned Mariana's book at Paris under the pretext of such doctrine hated not Mariana, nor the Jesuits, but indeed not the Jesuits, but the most holy name of Jesus Christ itself. The author's words are these: They are the enemies of the holy name of Jesus who condemned Mariana for such a doctrine. Behold, reader, the judgment of one Jesuit, or of one of the great patrons of the Jesuits, but not of them all, concerning the most prudent senators of the Parliament of Paris, who most deservedly consigned that teaching of Mariana to the flames. Hence it appears that there are few today who detest that most dreadful doctrine of Mariana. And why, I ask, should men execrate the teacher of parricides, when they are pleased by parricide, praise the parricides, and judge them worthy of the blessedness of martyrs? It is plainly the mark of the same man to approve Mariana's judgment and to think traitors and parricides worthy of consecration or canonization.

units.la: Approbavit eandem doctrinam de interficiendis Regibus Ioh. Alvarus Provincialis Conimbricae in Hispania, commendatione libri Fr. Suarez, cui titulus est, Defensio fidei Catholicae et Apostolicae adversus Anglicanae sectae errores, etc. Sic enim illa habet: Ego Ioan. Alvarus, Societatis Iesu in Lusitania Provincia Visitator simul ac Provincialis, e facultate ad id mihi facta a Reverendo admodum P. nostro Generali Claudio Aquaviva, facultatem concedo, ut hoc opus de schismate Anglicano a Patre Francisco Suarez Societatis nostrae, Sacraeque Theologiae Doctore et in Conimbricensi Academia primario Professore compositum, et eiusdem Societatis graviorum doctorum hominum iudicio approbatum, typis mandetur. In quorum fidem has literas manu nostra subscriptas, sigillo nostro munitas dedimus. Conimbricae 5. Aprilis anno 1612.
units.tr: The same doctrine on the killing of kings was also approved by John Alvarez, Provincial at Coimbra in Spain, with a commendation of the book by Fr. Suárez, entitled A Defence of the Catholic and Apostolic Faith against the Errors of the Anglican Sect, etc. For it reads thus: I, John Alvarez, Visitor and at the same time Provincial of the Society of Jesus in the Province of Lusitania, by the authority granted to me for this purpose by our most Reverend Father General Claudio Aquaviva, grant permission that this work on the Anglican schism, composed by Father Francisco Suárez of our Society, Doctor of Sacred Theology and chief Professor in the Academy of Coimbra, and approved by the judgment of the graver learned men of the same Society, be committed to print. In witness of this we have given these letters, signed with our hand and sealed with our seal. At Coimbra, 5 April, in the year 1612.

units.la: DAMNATVR IESVITARVM DOCTRINA DE INTERFICIENDIS REGIBVS
units.tr: THE DOCTRINE OF THE JESUITS ON THE KILLING OF KINGS IS CONDEMNED

units.la: Debebant vero Iesuitae meminisse decreti Urbani Papae, quod extat c. 24. q. 3. quo sancitur, Quod talia docentes, consulentes aut defendentes, longe damnabiliores sint dicentibus aut facientibus. Et quod Seneca ad Alexandrum dixit: Quid interest, leoni Lysimachum obicias, an ipse dentibus laceres? Tuum illud os est, tua illa feritas: O quam cuperes tibi potius vingues esse, tibi risum edendorum hominum capacem.
units.tr: The Jesuits ought to have remembered the decree of Pope Urban, which is found at C. 24, q. 3, and which lays down that those who teach, advise or defend such things are far more damnable than those who say or do them. They should also have remembered what Seneca said to Alexander: What difference does it make whether you throw Lysimachus to a lion or tear him apart with your own teeth? That mouth is yours, that savagery is yours. Oh, how you would wish to have claws rather than teeth, and a mind capable of finding laughter in the devouring of men!

units.la: Damnarunt etiam hanc Iesuitarum doctrinam aliquot Toletana Concilia, nempe, quartum, quintum, sextum et decimum. In his Conciliis extat Canon, in quo Hispani ipsi sententiam contra Iesuitas pronunciarunt. Canon enim ille sic habet: Qui cunque nostrum, aut populorum totius Hispaniae coniuratione, aut machinatione violaverit iuramentum datum conservando Regi: aut etiam Regem interfecerit, aut regno suo privarit, aut praesumptione tyrannica usurpaverit potestatem regiam, is excommunicatur in conspectu Angelorum ac hominum, et pellatur ex Ecclesia, et societate Christianorum, cum omnibus suis affectis, cum ratione quandoquidem conjunctum est, eandem poenam sequi illos, qui eiusdem criminis rei. Verba haec alta voce et ter repetita fuerunt in Concilio coram toto coetu, et petitum, ut quilibet ea approbaret. Tunc igitur a toto clero et populo responsum fuit: Quicunque adversatus fuerit sanctae vestrae constitutioni, is excommunicator excommunicatione omnium maxima et periculosissima, Anathema esto maranatha et exterminator sine remissione in perpetuum, usque ad adventum Domini, et parte possideat cum Juda Scariothe, ipse et socii eius, Amen. Habet hic Iesuita quod diligenter perpendant.
units.tr: Several Councils of Toledo also condemned this Jesuit doctrine, namely the fourth, fifth, sixth and tenth. In these Councils there is a canon in which the Spaniards themselves pronounced sentence against the Jesuits. The canon reads as follows: Whoever among us, or among the peoples of all Spain, by conspiracy or plotting violates the oath given to preserve the King, or kills the King, or deprives him of his kingdom, or by tyrannical presumption usurps the royal power, let him be excommunicated in the sight of angels and men, and cast out from the Church and the fellowship of Christians, together with all his associates; since it is reasonable that those who are guilty of the same crime should suffer the same penalty. These words were read aloud three times in the Council, before the whole assembly, and everyone was asked to approve them. Then the whole clergy and people replied: Whoever opposes your holy constitution, let him be excommunicated with the greatest and most dangerous excommunication, anathema maranatha, and an exterminator without remission forever, until the coming of the Lord; and let him, and his associates, have their portion with Judas Iscariot. Amen. Here the Jesuit has something which they should weigh carefully.

units.la: Damnavit hanc doctrinam quoque Concilium Meldense anno 1540. celebratum cap. 14.
units.tr: The Council of Meaux, held in 1540, also condemned this doctrine, in chapter 14.

units.la: Damnavit etiam hanc doctrinam tamquam impiam, hæreticam & omnium modis perniciosam ante annos ducentos Constantiense Concilium Sessione 15, cuius verba in sequenti Sorbonæ Censura referemus. Ioannes Mariana eodem capite sexto libro primo in fine dicit; Hoc decretum Romano Pontifici Martino V. probatum non invenio: non Eugenio aut successoribus. Rursus: Concilium illud non sine Ecclesiæ motu, tricipiti Pontificum dissidio, celebratum fuisse scimus. Sed ec improbatum a Pontificibus istis decretum hoc fuisse Mariana invenit. Approbarunt etiam hoc Concilium reliqui Pontificij Scriptores, & multi quoque e Iesuitis.
units.tr: Long ago, two hundred years back, the Council of Constance also condemned this doctrine as impious, heretical and in every way pernicious, in its fifteenth session; I shall cite its words in the Sorbonne censure that follows. John Mariana, in the sixth chapter of his first book, near the end, says: I do not find that this decree was approved by the Roman Pontiff Martin V, nor by Eugenius or his successors. Again: We know that that Council was held not without disturbance to the Church, amid the threefold division among the Pontiffs. But Mariana finds that this decree was not approved even by those Pontiffs. The other Papist writers, and many of the Jesuits too, have also approved this Council.

units.la: Iohannes Gerson quoque, qui huic Concilio interfuit, hanc doctrinam violationem omnium legum, divina, naturalis & humana vocat. Idem ait: Doctrina hæc itenter hæreticalis, imo & sacrilega est, quæ etiam secularibus illiteratis, nedum Christianis, sed & Iudæis & Paganis & Barbaris debet esse notissima. Item: Quod nec Rex esset, sine juris ordine non vocatum, & non convictum interficere: quanto minus alium: Quales oro densiores, fugibiliores horribiliores que tenebræ, quam errorum & hæsium circa prima præceptorum moralium principia, ut sunt: non pejerabis, non occides, non insidiaberis? ut est videre in operibus Gersonis Tom. 1. in Orationibus & Propositionibus coram concilio & commissariis Anno 1415. & 1416. habitis.
units.tr: John Gerson too, who attended this Council, calls this doctrine a violation of all laws, divine, natural and human. He also says: This doctrine is heretical, indeed even sacrilegious, and it ought to be best known not only to Christians but also to Jews, pagans and barbarians, even to the unlettered laity. Likewise: Since a king could not be put to death without the due order of law, and without being summoned and convicted, how much less could anyone else be? What darker, more fearful and more horrible darkness is there, I beg you, than that of errors and heresies concerning the first principles of moral precepts, such as: you shall not swear falsely, you shall not kill, you shall not lie in wait? This may be seen in the works of Gerson, vol. 1, in the orations and propositions delivered before the Council and the commissioners in 1415 and 1416.

units.la: Damnavit eandem doctrinam Facultas Theologica Parisiensis in Censura contra impios & execrabiles Regum ac Principum parricidas, post cædem Henrici 4. Galliarum Regis a Francisco Ravaillac patratam, edita. Ea sic de verbo ad verbum se habet.
units.tr: The Theological Faculty of Paris also condemned the same doctrine, in its censure against the impious and execrable murderers of kings and princes, published after the killing of Henry IV, King of France, perpetrated by François Ravaillac. The censure reads word for word as follows.

units.la: ANNO DOMINI 1610. cum sacra Theologiæ facultas, ob festa Pentecostes & Comitia privata inter viros selectos Ordinis Theologici in præsenti negotio agitata, suos statos & ordinarios conventus prima aut secunda die Iunij habere non potuisset, illos in diem quartum Iunij transtulit, atque omnes Magistros Theologiæ, in eim obedientiæ, quam emisso sacramento facultati spoponderunt, in Collegium Sorbonicum convocavit, ubi post Missam de Sancto Spiritu more solito celebratam deliberaverunt super executione Senatus Consulti, cujus summa hæc est.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1610, since the sacred Faculty of Theology could not hold its usual ordinary meetings on the first or second day of June, because of the feast of Pentecost and the private assemblies of select men of the Theological Order, which were occupied with the present business, it transferred them to the fourth day of June, and summoned all the Masters of Theology, in that obedience which they had promised the Faculty by an oath, to the Sorbonne College. There, after Mass of the Holy Spirit had been celebrated as usual, they deliberated on the execution of the decree of the Senate, the substance of which is this.

units.la: Curia Parlamenti, de curiis majore, rerum capitalium, atque Editi una congregatis, procedendo ad judicium & litem capitalem ac extraordinariam, Cognitoris generalis Regis postulatione instructam, adversus nefandissimum, crudelissimum & execratissimum parricidium, in sacratam personam Henrici quarti Regis patratum, edito Cognitore generali regio, decrevit atque decernit, ut diligentia & procuratione Decani & Syndici Facultatis Theologiæ, eadem Facultas quam primum convocetur ad deliberandum super confirmatione decreti prædictæ Facultatis, quod die 13. Decembris anno 1413. a centum quadraginta & uno Theologis ejusdem Facultatis conflitutum, decreto definitur: Eminentis licitum esse quacunque occasione, causa aut pretextu quæsito, sacrosanctis Regum & aliorum Principum supremorum personis vim inferre: Deinde, ut Decretum eodem in ejusdem Facultatis Comitijs statuetur, omnium Doctorum, qui Comitijs & deliberationi interfuerint, nec non etiam omnium Baccalaureorum, qui cursum Theologiæ decurrunt, syngraphis muniatur; quo tum demum, audito super ea re Cognitore generali regio, Curia decernat quod justum & rationi conforme erit. Datum in Parlamento 7. Maij, Anno Dom. 1610. Signatum Voysin.
units.tr: The Court of Parliament, with the Grand Chamber, the criminal chambers and the Edict court gathered together, proceeding to judgement and to a capital and extraordinary suit, equipped with the petition of the King's general prosecutor, against the most abominable, most cruel and most execrable parricide committed against the sacred person of King Henry IV, and with the King's general prosecutor having issued his charge, has decreed and does decree: that by the diligence and management of the Dean and Syndic of the Faculty of Theology, the same Faculty be convened as soon as possible to deliberate on the confirmation of the decree of the aforesaid Faculty, which was established on 13 December 1413 by one hundred and forty-one Theologians of the same Faculty, and is defined by that decree: that it is lawful, on whatever occasion, cause or pretext sought, to do violence to the most sacred persons of kings and other supreme princes. Further, that the decree be enacted in the assembly of the same Faculty, and be confirmed by the signatures of all the Doctors who took part in the assembly and deliberation, and also of all the Bachelors who are pursuing the course in Theology; whereupon, after hearing the King's general prosecutor on this matter, the Court shall decree what is just and in accordance with reason. Given in Parliament, 7 May, in the year of the Lord 1610. Signed, Voysin.

units.la: Itaque eadem sacra Facultas, ut mandato amplissimi Ordinis, tam justa et necessaria præcipientis, obtemperaret, primum privata, deinde publica habuit Comitia. Considerans autem sibi ex officio incumbere, ut suam Censuram & Iudicium doctrinale, cunctis illud posscentibus declaret, atque Parisiensem Academiam a primis in incunabulis, parentem & alumnam optimæ ac saluberrimæ doctrinæ, perpetuo extitisse fe, bonum, & tranquillitatem Reipub. ab ordine, ordinem porrò & pacem, secundum Deum Opt. Max. à Regum & Principum salute pendere; ac solius esse Principis & potestatis politicæ gladio uti, Rom. 13. insuper paucis ab hinc annis, nonnulla peregrina, seditiosa atque impia dogmata invaluisse, quibus plerique privati homines dementati, sacrosanctos Reges & Principes, execranda appellatione TYRANNI contaminare; hoc quidem nefario praetextu, nec non religionis, pietatis, aut boni publici juvandi vel promovendi specie, in sacrosancta Regum & Principum capita conspirare, suasque manus parricidas sacro illorum sanguine cruentare; ac continuò patentissimam fenestram aperire non horrent, ad perfidiam, ad fraudes, insidias, proditiones, populorum internecionem, Urbium, Provinciarum ac regnorum florentissimorum excidia, & ad alia innumerabilia nequitiæ genera, quæ civilia aut externa bella concomitari solent. Demum tam pestifera & diabolica dogmata hodie in causa esse, ut qui decessionem ab Ecclesia Catholica & Romana fecerunt, in suo errore obdurescant, virosque religiosos, Doctores & Prælatos Catholicos, quamquam infontes, quasi talia docerent vel auctorarent, fugiant ac detestentur.
units.tr: Accordingly, the same sacred Faculty, so as to obey the command of so distinguished an Order, a command so just and necessary, first held a private assembly and then a public one. Considering that it lay upon it, by virtue of its office, to declare its censure and doctrinal judgement to all who wished to know it; and that the University of Paris, from its earliest beginnings, has always been the parent and nursling of the best and most wholesome doctrine; that the welfare and tranquillity of the commonwealth, and order, and further order and peace, depend, under God Most Good and Most Great, on the safety of kings and princes; and that it belongs to the prince alone to use the sword of political power (Rom. 13). Moreover, within these few years, various foreign, seditious and impious doctrines have gained ground, by which many private men, driven out of their minds, dare to defile the sacrosanct kings and princes with the accursed name of TYRANTS; and under this wicked pretext, and under the appearance of promoting or advancing religion, piety or the public good, to conspire against the sacrosanct heads of kings and princes and to stain their parricidal hands with the sacred blood of those men; and they do not shrink from opening a wide window to perfidy, frauds, ambushes, betrayals, the slaughter of peoples, the destruction of cities, provinces and most flourishing kingdoms, and to countless other kinds of wickedness which usually accompany civil or foreign wars. Lastly, such pestilent and diabolical doctrines are today the cause of those who have departed from the Catholic and Roman Church hardening themselves in their error, and of their shunning and detesting religious men, Catholic teachers and prelates, although they are innocent, as if they taught or authorised such things.

units.la: Eadem inquam Facultas hæc & similia considerare perpendens, magnâ animorum consensione & alacritate, ista peregrina & seditiosa dogmata, velut impia, hæretica, focietati civili, paci & tranquillitati publicæ, ac religioni Catholicæ penitus contraria, execratur, atque condemnat, in cujus rei fidem & testimonium, decretum antiquum sibi de integro renovandum esse duxit, quod ducentis ab hinc annis, a centum quadraginta & uno Theologis sanctum fuit, in condemnatione hujus execrabilis Propositionis: Quilibet Tyrannus potest & debet licite & meritorie occidi a quocunque suo vasallo aut subdito, & per quemcunque modum, maximè per insidias, & per adulationes, non obstante quocunque juramento aut confœderatione factâ apud eum, non expectando sententiam aut mandatum Judicis cujuscunque. Sequitur vero Censura Facultatis.
units.tr: This same Faculty, I say, considering these and similar matters with careful thought, with great unanimity and eagerness of mind, execrates and condemns these foreign and seditious doctrines as impious, heretical, and utterly contrary to civil society, to public peace and tranquillity, and to the Catholic religion. In witness and testimony of this, it has judged that the ancient decree, which was sanctioned two hundred years ago by one hundred and forty-one Theologians in condemnation of this execrable proposition: Any tyrant may and ought lawfully and meritoriously to be killed by any vassal or subject of his, and by whatever means, most of all by ambushes and flatteries, notwithstanding any oath or agreement made with him, without awaiting the sentence or mandate of any judge whatever, must be renewed afresh by it. The censure of the Faculty follows.

units.la: Hæc assertio sic generaliter posita; & secundum acceptionem hujus vocabuli TYRANNVS, est error in nostra fide, & doctrina bonorum morum, & est contra præceptum Dei, NON OCCIDES; Glossa propria auctoritate: & contra hoc quod dicit Dominus noster, OMNES QVI GLADIVM ACCEPERINT; Glossa, propria auctoritate: GLADIO PERIBVNT. Item, hæc assertio vergit in subversionem totius Reipublicæ & uniuscujusq; Regis aut Principis. Item, dat viam & licentiam ad plura alia mala, & ad fraudes, & ad violationes fidei; & juramenti, & ad proditiones, & generaliter ad omnem inobedientiam subjecti ad dominum suum; & ad omnem infidelitatem & diffidentiam unius ad alterum, & consequenter ad æternam damnationem. Item, qui affirmat obstinatè talem errorem, & alios qui inde sequuntur, est hæreticus, & tanquam hæreticus debet puniri, etiam post suam mortem. Notetur in decretis 23. q. 5. etc. Actu Ann. 1413. die Mercurii 13. Decemb. Quæ Censura Facultatis Parisiensis in Synodo Constantiensi Sess. 15. Anno 1415. prid. Non. Julij his conceptis verbis comprobata fuit; Præcipuâ sollicitudine volens hæc sacrosancta Synodus ad extirpationem errorum & hæresium in diversis mundi partibus invalescentium providere, sicut tenetur & ad hoc collecta est; nuper accepit, quod nonnullæ assertiones erroneæ in fide; & bonis moribus, ac multipliciter scandalosæ, totiusque Reip. statum & ordinem subvertere molientes, dogmatizatæ sunt; inter quas hæc assertio delata est: QVILIBET Tyrannus, potest & debet licite & meritorie occidi per quemcunque vasallum suum vel subditum, etiam per clanculares insidias, & subtiles blanditias, vel adulationes, non obstante quorumcunque præstito juramento seu confœderatione factis cum eo, non expectata sententia Judicis cujuscunq. ADVERSVS hunc errorem surgere, & ipsum funditus tollere, praehabitâ deliberatione maturâ; declarat, decernit atque diffinit hujusmodi doctrinam erroneam esse in fide, & in moribus, ipsamque tamquam hæreticam, scandalosam, & ad fraudes, deceptiones, & mendacia, proditiones, perjuria, vias dantem, reprobat & condemnat. Declarat insuper, decernit & diffinit, quod pertinaciter doctrinam hanc perniciosissimam asserentes ferentes sunt haeretici, & tanquam tales, juxta canonicas sanctiones puniendi.
units.tr: This assertion, put in such general terms and taking TYRANT in the sense this word bears, is an error against our faith and the doctrine of good morals, and it is contrary to God's command, "You shall not kill" (Gloss, on its own authority), and contrary to what our Lord says, "All who take the sword shall perish by the sword" (Gloss, on its own authority). Further, this assertion tends to the subversion of the whole commonwealth and of every king or prince. Further, it opens the way and gives licence to many other evils, to frauds, to violations of faith and oaths, to treacheries, and generally to every disobedience of a subject towards his lord, to every unfaithfulness and distrust of one person towards another, and consequently to eternal damnation. Further, whoever obstinately affirms such an error, and the others that follow from it, is a heretic, and as a heretic he must be punished, even after his death. See the Decretum, 23, q. 5, etc. This was done in the year 1413, on Wednesday, 13 December. This censure of the Faculty of Paris was approved in these words by the Council of Constance, in its fifteenth session, in the year 1415, on the day before the Nones of July: "This most holy Synod, wishing with the greatest care to provide for the extirpation of errors and heresies growing strong in various parts of the world, as it is bound and gathered to do, has lately learned that certain erroneous assertions in faith and good morals, many times scandalous, and tending to overthrow the state and order of the whole commonwealth, have been propagated; among them this assertion has been reported: ANY tyrant may and ought lawfully and meritoriously to be killed by any vassal or subject of his, even by secret ambushes and subtle flatteries or adulations, notwithstanding any oath or covenant made with him, without awaiting the sentence of any judge whatever." Rising against this error and utterly removing it, after mature deliberation beforehand, the Synod declares, decrees and defines that this erroneous doctrine is in faith and in morals, and it condemns and rejects it as heretical, scandalous, and giving the way to frauds, deceptions, lies, treacheries and perjuries. It further declares, decrees and defines that those who stubbornly assert this most pernicious doctrine are heretics, and as such are to be punished according to the canonical sanctions.

units.la: Sacra igitur Facultas sancit, strictè accuratèq; exploratis omnium et singulorum Doctorum suffragijs, primò antiquam illam Censuram Facultatis, Synodi Constantiensis sanctione firmatam, non modò iterari, verùm etiam omnium hominum animis inculcari debere. Secundò censet, seditiosum, impium & haereticum esse, quocunq; quaesito colore, à quocunque subdito, vasallo, aut extraneo, sacris Regum & Principum personis vim inferre. Tertiò statuit, ut omnes Doctores & Baccalaurei Theologiae, quo die in statuta & articulos Facultatis jurare consueverunt, in hoc similiter decretum jurent, ac syngraphae suae appositione obtestentur, se illius veritatem docendo & concionando diligenter explicaturos. Quarto, ut haec Acta, tum Latinè, tum Gallicè typis mandentur ac evulgentur.
units.tr: The sacred Faculty therefore, after a strict and careful examination of the votes of all and each of the Doctors, first decrees that the old censure of the Faculty, confirmed by the sanction of the Council of Constance, must not only be repeated but also impressed on the minds of all men. Secondly, it judges that to inflict violence on the sacred persons of kings and princes, from whatever pretext, by any subject, vassal or foreigner, is seditious, impious and heretical. Thirdly, it ordains that all the Doctors and Bachelors of Theology shall swear, on the day on which they are accustomed to swear to the statutes and articles of the Faculty, to this decree likewise, and shall bind themselves by affixing their signature to it, that they will diligently explain its truth in their teaching and preaching. Fourthly, that these Acts be published and spread abroad in print, both in Latin and in French.

units.la: De mandato Domini Decani & Sacratissimae Facultatis Theologicae. De la Court cum syngrapha.
units.tr: By the command of the Dean and the most sacred Theological Faculty. De la Court, with signature.

units.la: Censurâ & sententiâ hac Facultatis Theologicae Parisiensis Parlamenti idem exhibita, eam 8. Iun. approbavit & confirmavit. Decrevit insuper primo, ut haec Censura inter Acta publica Parlamenti referatur & scribatur. Secundò in instantiam Procuratoris regij praecepit, ut in Conventu Facultatis huius quotannis 4. Iunij, & proximâ inde Dominica in omnibus parochialibus temlis, atque etiam suburbijs Lutetiae populo publicè praelegatur. Tertiò, ut Joannis Marianae liber, in quo haec doctrina de parricidijs Regum ac Principum manifestè approbatur & defenditur, in area ante summum ac primarium templum Lutetiae in ignem conjiciatur & comburatur, in aeternam rei memoriam, quod doctrina haec in eo contenta, sit haeretica, impia, perniciosa & erronea. Quarto, prohibuit, ne quis, cuiuscunque sit status, conditionis vel ordinis, hanc doctrinam vel viva voce, vel editis libris spargat atq; defendat.
units.tr: The Parliament of Paris approved and confirmed this censure and sentence of the Faculty of Theology of Paris, displaying it on 8 June. It further decreed, first, that this censure be entered and written among the public Acts of Parliament. Secondly, at the request of the King's Procurator, it ordered that it be publicly read to the people in the Faculty's assembly each year on 4 June, and on the Sunday following, in all the parish churches and also in the suburbs of Paris. Thirdly, that the book of Juan de Mariana, in which this doctrine of the murder of kings and princes is plainly approved and defended, be thrown into the fire and burned in the square before the chief and principal church of Paris, as an eternal memorial that the doctrine contained in it is heretical, impious, pernicious and erroneous. Fourthly, it forbade anyone, of whatever rank, condition or order, to spread or defend this doctrine either by word of mouth or in published books.

units.la: Recte autem ille & prudenter, quisquis fit, Gallos sic monuit: Galli, si sapitis, quid librum traditis igni? Authores vestris pellite limitibus. In cineres abiit liber unus, mille relicti, Horum turba loquax, mutus at ille furit. Hortos qui cupiunt penitus purgare veneno, Radices properant vellere, non folia.
units.tr: Rightly and wisely, whoever he was, warned the French thus: "Frenchmen, if you are wise, why do you hand the book over to the fire? Drive its authors beyond your borders. One book has gone up in ashes, a thousand remain; the chattering crowd of them, and that silent one rages. Those who wish to purge their gardens thoroughly of poison hasten to pull up the roots, not the leaves."

units.la: Improbavit eandem Ludovicus Richeomus Iesuita in Expostulat. Apologiae pro Societ. Iesu Latinâ cap. 21. pag. 178. & c. 28. pag. 218. Doctrina, inquit, ista de Tyranno occidendo, est exitialis, & ab universa Ecclesia improbata, & in Constantiensi Concilio condemnata. Item: Illa doctrina est Anabaptistarum, & in Oecumenico Constantiensi Concilio damnata. Item: Alterum, inquit, illud esse tyrannorum genus, qui more ac legibus ad regni administrationem acciti, more tyrannico tamen imperant, nos attingere ac laedere nemo privatus debet, aut subditus: hinc est quod David Saulo Regi nunquam est ausus manum inferre. Simul tamen concedit Richeomus, illud genus tyrannorum, qui ditiones non suas vi occupant, privatis occidere fas esse.
units.tr: Ludovicus Richeomus, the Jesuit, likewise disapproved of this doctrine in his Latin Expostulatio Apologiae pro Societate Iesu, chapter 21, page 178, and chapter 28, page 218. "This doctrine," he says, "concerning the killing of a tyrant is deadly, and has been rejected by the whole Church and condemned at the Council of Constance." Again: "That doctrine belongs to the Anabaptists, and was condemned at the Ecumenical Council of Constance." Again, he says, "there is another kind of tyrant, who, called to the administration of the kingdom by custom and law, yet rules in a tyrannical manner; no private person or subject ought to touch or harm him; hence it is that David never dared to lay hands on King Saul." Yet at the same time Richeomus concedes that it is lawful for private persons to kill that kind of tyrant who seizes by force lands which are not his own.

units.la: Condemnavit denuò Parlamentum Parisiense hanc Iesuitarum doctrinam Decreto suo, quo igni adiudicavit Francisci Suarez librum, in quo doctrina haec confirmatur. Decretum sic de verbo ad verbum habet.
units.tr: The Parliament of Paris again condemned this Jesuit doctrine by its decree, by which it adjudged to the fire the book of Francisco Suárez in which this doctrine is confirmed. The decree runs thus, word for word:

units.la: DECRETVM PARLAMENTI PARISIENSIS latum 26. & exsecutioni mandatum 27. Iun. 1614.
units.tr: THE DECREE OF THE PARIS PARLIAMENT, passed 26 June and carried into effect 27 June 1614.

units.la: Contra librum, excusum Coloniae, Anno eodem cum hoc titulo
units.tr: Against the book printed at Cologne in the same year, with this title:

units.la: FRANCISCI SVAREZ, Granatensis, e societate Iesu, Doctoris Theologi, Defensio fidei Catholicae & Apostolicae adversus An- glicanae sectae errores, &c.
units.tr: FRANCISCO SUAREZ, of Granada, of the Society of Jesus, Doctor of Theology, A Defence of the Catholic and Apostolic Faith against the errors of the English sect, &c.

units.la: Qui
units.tr: Which

units.la: Continet maximas & Propositiones contrarias potestati supremae Regum, ordinatae & stabilitae a Deo, ad securitatem personarum, quieti & tranquillitati statui ipsorum.
units.tr: Contains maxims and propositions contrary to the supreme power of kings, ordained and established by God, for the safety of their persons and the peace and tranquillity of their state.

units.la: EXTRACTVM e registris Parlamenti.
units.tr: EXTRACT from the registers of Parliament.

units.la: VIso a Curia, magnis Cameris, Turnelli & Editi congregatis libro, impressio Coloniae, anno praesente, cum hoc titulo: Francisci Suarez, Granatensis, e societate Iesu, Doctoris Theologi, defensio fidei Catholicae & Apostolicae, adversus Anglicanae sectae errores, &c. continente libro tertio, cap. 23. pag. 376. 79. 80. 82. cap. 29. pag. 410. 11. 12. 13. 14. 15. 17. 18. 19. 20. cap. 6. pag. 834. cap. 8. pag. 844. & alibi multas propositiones contrarias potestati supremae Regum, ordinatorum & stabilitorum a Deo, ad quietem & tranquillitatem statuum ipsorum, &c. quod licitum sit subditis ipsorum & peregrinis personas ipsorum invadere: facta conclusione per Procuratorem generalem omnibus consideratis, Curia praedicta declaravit, & declarat, propositiones & maximas in dicto libro contentas, scandalosas & seditiosas esse, tendereque ad subversionem statuum & ad permovendos subditos Regum & Principum supremorum, & aliorum, ut violenta maxime sacratissimis ipsorum personis inferant: sententias item, quae mentionem faciunt Regum Ludovici & Philippi Pulchri, falsas & calumniosas esse. Quapropter decrevit & decernit, ut praedictus liber Suarezii in Curia Palatii, per ministrum supremae iustitiae comburatur. Similiter interdicit bibliopolis & typografis, imprimere, vendere, aut mutuo sumere, & quibuscunque personis, cuiuscunque conditionis & qualitatis, habere, scribere & tenere, sive docere in scholis, aut alibi, uti etiam disputare, praedictas maximas & propositiones.
units.tr: The Court, the Great Chambers, the Tournelle and the Edict having gathered and having seen the book printed at Cologne this year with this title: Francisco Suarez, of Granada, of the Society of Jesus, Doctor of Theology, A Defence of the Catholic and Apostolic Faith against the errors of the English sect, &c., which contains in book three, chapter 23, pages 376, 379, 380, 382; chapter 29, pages 410, 411, 412, 413, 414, 415, 417, 418, 419, 420; chapter 6, page 834; chapter 8, page 844; and elsewhere, many propositions contrary to the supreme power of kings, ordained and established by God, to the peace and tranquillity of their states, &c., namely that it is lawful for their subjects and for foreigners to attack their persons; and after the Procurator General's submission had been fully considered, the said Court has declared and does declare that the propositions and maxims contained in the said book are scandalous and seditious, and tend to the overthrow of states and to stirring up the subjects of kings and of supreme princes, and of others, to inflict violence especially on their most sacred persons; likewise that the passages which mention Kings Louis and Philip the Fair are false and slanderous. Wherefore it has decreed and does decree that the said book of Suarez be burned in the Court of the Palace by the minister of the supreme justice. Likewise it forbids booksellers and printers to print, sell or lend the said maxims and propositions, and forbids all persons, of whatever condition and rank, to possess, write or hold them, or to teach them in schools or elsewhere, or likewise to dispute them.

units.la: Praeterea decernit, juxta decretum diei 8. Iun. 1616. ut Decretum facultatis Theologiae diei 4. Iun. ejusdem anni, super renovatione censurae doctrinalis ejusdem Facultatis anno 1408. confirmatae per concilium Constantiense, una cum praesenti Decreto & illorum 1578. & 95. recitentur singulis annis 4. Iun. tam in praedicta Facultate, quam in Collegiis Sacerdotum & Scholasticorum Collegii Claromontani, & quatuor Mendicantium, & ut ad instantiam Procuratoris Generalis Regis institutur informatio transgressionum nominati Editi, & prohibitio de ejusmodi libris scribendis & servandis.
units.tr: Furthermore it decrees, in accordance with the decree of 8 June 1616, that the decree of the Faculty of Theology of 4 June of the same year, concerning the renewal of the doctrinal censure of the same Faculty, confirmed in 1408 by the Council of Constance, together with the present decree and those of 1578 and 1595, be read out every year on 4 June, both in the said Faculty and in the colleges of priests and scholars of the Collège de Clermont and of the four mendicant orders; and that, at the instance of the King's Procurator General, an inquiry be instituted into violations of the named edict and into the prohibition of writing and keeping books of this kind.

units.la: Actum in Parlamento d. 26. Iun. 1614. subscripsit Voysin.
units.tr: Done in Parliament, 26 June 1614. Signed, Voysin.

units.la: Praeterea decretum est, ut Patres, Ignacius Armandus, Rector in hac civitate, Coton, Fronton, Sirmundus, proxima die in Curiam vocentur, eisque demonstretur, quod contra Declarationem & decretum ipsorum Generalis, anni 1610. liber iste Suarezii & impressus, et in hanc civitatem illatus sit, contra auctoritatem Regis, ejusque securitatem per nè & status: quib. etiam injungetur, ut Generali suo significent, eum prædictū decretum renovare & publicare debere: cujus quidem rei actum instituent intra spatium semere, & provident, ut eiusmodi libri in posterum nec componantur, nec mittantur in luem à Societate sua, continentes propositiones tam damnabiles & perniciosas. Injungetur uin etiam eis, ut exhortentur populum in concionibus suis, ad doctrinam supra commemoatis propositionibus contrariam. Alioquin Curia procedet contra transgressores, ut reos esse majestatis & perturbatores quietis publicæ.
units.tr: Furthermore it has been decreed that the Fathers Ignatius Armandus, Rector in this city, Coton, Fronton, and Sirmond be summoned to the Court on the next day, and that it be shown to them that, contrary to the declaration and decree of their General of the year 1610, this book of Suarez has been printed and brought into this city, against the authority of the King and the security of his person and state. They shall also be ordered to report to their General that he must renew and publish the said decree; they are to see that this is done within the space of a week, and to take care that books of this kind, containing propositions so damnable and pernicious, are neither composed nor sent out by their Society in future. They shall also be ordered to exhort the people in their sermons to the doctrine contrary to the propositions mentioned above. Otherwise the Court will proceed against the transgressors as guilty of treason and as disturbers of the public peace.

units.la: Decretum prædictum, & quod insuper conclusum fuit, publicata sunt præsentibus Patribus Ignacio Armando, Carolo de Turre, qui loco Cottonis absentis comparuerat, Frontone Ducæo, et Iacobo Sirmondo. Et decretum executioni mandatum est ante graus majores Palatij, 27. Jun. 1614.
units.tr: The aforesaid decree, and what was further resolved, was published in the presence of the Fathers Ignatius Armandus, Charles de la Tour, who had appeared in place of the absent Coton, Fronton Du Duc, and James Sirmond. The decree was carried into effect before the great gate of the Palace, 27 June 1614.

units.la: Libro Suarezij Iesuitæ à Parlamento Parisiensi sic condemnato & per carni-ficem publicè cremato, sequente anno tertio quoque in Gallia Status de do-trina hac declaratio in hanc sententiam publicata est: Exorta, inquiunt, superio-ribus annis, & seditiosis libris propagata doctrina impia, quæ supremi Magistratus pote-ati insidiatur, cum de indubitato Regis jure satis omnibus constet, rogatum eum submisse-elit, ut quemadmodum pro eo, qui supremam potestatem ab ipso Deo immediatè acceperit, ab omnibus agnoscatur & habeatur, sic non permittat, ut ulla aliqua potestas, sive Ecclestica sive politica tantum sibi juris sumat, ut prætendere aliquid in Regiam suam Ma-estatem, & subditos ab obedientia ipsi debita, ob quamcunque causam absolvere possit. Hanc nim memorabilem & verbo divino congruentem, conservandæq; salutis publicæ maximè onveniente regulam, ab omnibus, cujus cunq; status & conditionis, subditis pro sanctâ & inviolabili lege habendam, & officiariis ministris q; omnibus & singulis antequam vel beeficiorum participes fiant, vel ad officia sua admittantur, jurejurando acceptandam & subscriptione sigilloq; proprio confirmandam esse: Contrariam verò, eam potissimum, quæ icere Reges vel interficere, vel exauctorare, & obedientiâ ipsorum se subtrahere statuit, mpiam & veritati utilitatiq; publicæ contrariam; omnes, quibus id perscriptum repeatur, libros tanquam seditiosos, execrandos & damnandos, & auctores quoscunq; talia cribentes & in publicum edentes, exteros quidem, pro juratis Regiæ Majestatis hostibus, ndigenas verò & cujuscunq; status et conditionis sint, pro seditiosis, rebellibus, legum vio-atoribus, & criminis læsæ Majestatis reos habendos esse. Imperandum igitur omnibus pa-entibus, ut liberis, præceptoribus, ut discipulis, professoribus, ut studiosis; & concio-atoribus, ut auditoribus suis Regulam hanc diligenter inculcent. Quod si edito ab exteris Ecclesiæ Ministris & D. d. libello, aliquid vel directè vel obliquè adversus regulam hanc prolatum fuerit, necessitatem Ecclesiasticis eiusdem ordinis, illud, sine omni personaum respectu, refutandi, ni crimen læsæ Majestatis incurrere velint, imponendam esse.
units.tr: After the book of the Jesuit Suarez had been so condemned by the Parisian Parliament and publicly burned by the executioner, in the following year, the Estates of France likewise published a declaration of this doctrine, to this effect: "Impious doctrine has arisen in recent years and been spread by seditious books, which lies in wait against the power of the supreme magistrate. Since the indubitable right of the King is sufficiently known to all, we humbly ask that, just as he who has received supreme power immediately from God himself is acknowledged and held as such by all, so he will not permit any power, whether ecclesiastical or political, to assume for itself the right to attempt anything against his royal majesty, or to absolve subjects from the obedience owed to him, for any cause whatever. For this memorable rule, which agrees with the divine word and is most suited to the preservation of public safety, is to be held by all subjects, of whatever state and condition, as a holy and inviolable law, and is to be accepted by all officials and ministers, before they are made partakers of benefices or admitted to their offices, by oath, and confirmed by their own signature and seal. But the contrary doctrine, especially that which teaches that kings may be struck down or killed or deposed, and that subjects may withdraw from obedience to them, is impious and contrary to truth and the public good. All books in which this is written are to be regarded as seditious, accursed and condemned, and all authors who write and publish such things are to be held, if foreigners, as sworn enemies of the royal majesty, and if natives, of whatever state or condition, as seditious, rebellious, violators of the laws and guilty of treason. Therefore all pastors, parents, teachers, pupils, professors, students, preachers and their hearers are commanded to inculcate this rule diligently. And if anything, directly or indirectly, is brought forward against this rule in a book published by foreign ministers of the Church or doctors, the clergy of the same order are to be bound to refute it, without any regard to persons, unless they wish to incur the crime of treason."

units.la: Iesuitæ quoq;, ut à se averterent odia Regum ac Principum, nec non etiam omnium hominum, quæ in ipsos & Ordinem universum concitabantur ex Mariana aliorumq; libris, in quibus parricidia Regum defenduntur, in conventu provinciali, quem Parisiis habuerunt, cum relatum esset de dicto Marianaelibro, hoc est, quem Procuratorem ad propositum Generalem Societatis provinciæ nomine destinârunt, mandatum dederunt, Ageret cum Generali, ut compeceret eos qui libros hos edunt, e quibus Regis, totiusq; Regni Gallici offensio & odia iure timerentur, neve eos, qui iam emissi essent, recudi patere-tur.
units.tr: The Jesuits too, in order to turn away from themselves the hatred of kings and princes, and indeed of all men, which was stirred up against them and their whole Order by the books of Mariana and others, in which the murders of kings are defended, at the provincial assembly which they held in Paris, when the said book of Mariana had been reported, sent a Procurator to their General on behalf of the province, and gave him a commission to deal with the General so that he would restrain those who publish these books, from which the offence and hatred of the King and of the whole kingdom of France might rightly be feared, and that they would not allow those already issued to be reprinted.

units.la: Damnavit deniq; hos Affasinos & parricidas, eorumq; doctrinam nobilisimus & amplissimus vir Iacobus Augustus Thuanus consiliarius Regius, & Curiæ supremæ Parisiensis Præses hac elegantissimâ Elegiâ in parricidas. Rursus ab immiti Furiâ bacchantur Averno, Vipereasq; rotat torva Megæra comas:
units.tr: Finally, this noble and distinguished man, James Augustus de Thou, royal councillor and President of the Supreme Court of Paris, condemned these assassins and murderers and their doctrine in this most elegant elegy against the parricides: "Again the Fury raves from Avernus with savage rage, and grim Megaera whirls her viper locks.

units.la: Rursus Trinacrijs puer ablactatus in antris Sacrilegâ stringit tela cruenta manu. Notus & Eoo tantum Assasinus in axe; Pro pudor, in nostro visitur orbe frequens. Scilicet has artes nuper gens gnara nocendi, Exitio inuexit, Gallia, nata tuo, Hesperiæ fuscis gens emissaria ab oris, Fucum affectatâ quæ grauitate tegit, Nata magistratum conuellere, nata ministris Subtrahere obsequium præsulibusq; suum: Geryonæ quæ dum placeat faueátq; trifauci, Terrarum reliquos non facit assis heros, Et cælo facinus dignum putat, omnia sæui In Regis longas tradere sceptra manus.
units.tr: Again, a boy weaned in the Trinacrian caves brandishes bloody weapons in a sacrilegious hand. An assassin known only in the Eastern chariot, alas for shame, is seen often in our world. Surely this skilled race, expert in harm, has brought these arts, born to your ruin, Gaul: a race sent out from the dusky shores of Hesperia, who hides deceit beneath a feigned gravity; born to overthrow the magistrates, born to withdraw obedience from ministers and from their own prelates; while it pleases the three-throated Geryon and favours him, the hero counts the rest of the lands as worth nothing, and thinks any deed worthy of heaven that hands over all the sceptres of the realm to the long hands of a wicked king. What the Gallic custom has taught in its discipline of morals, having cast off through fear the laws of right, to loosen the bonds of rulers and teach horrible treason against kings and their doomed lives; it denies that faith must be kept, and with subtle quibbles twists the stern commands of the great God."

units.la: Quæ disciplinam morum, quæ Gallica venit, Exuto, legum soluere iura, metu, Et vileis regnantum animas, ipsosq; necandos Horrenda Reges proditione docet, Seruandamq; fidem negat, argutisq; cauillis Detorquet magni jussa seuera Dei.
units.tr: They teach the discipline of manners that came from France: to loosen the bonds of law once fear is cast off, to make kings' lives cheap, and to teach that kings themselves may be murdered by a dreadful treachery. They deny that faith must be kept, and with clever sophistries they twist the stern commands of the great God.

units.la: Sunt tamen, & cur sunt? qui nunc quoq; crimine in isto Obtendant causam Religionis agi. Accusentq; bonos ultro, excusentq; nocenteis Et patrocinio consiliòq; juvent. Hosne superstitio male sanos excitet æstus, Quiq; atrâ vexat pectora bile furor, An pietas simulata, mea nil quærere refert, Damnandum in magnis cum sit utrumq; viris:
units.tr: Yet there are some, and why are there? who even now, in this crime, pretend that the cause being pursued is that of religion. They accuse good men without cause and excuse the guilty, and they help them with patronage and counsel. Is it superstition that stirs up these fevered passions in men who are not sound in mind, or is it a furious rage that torments their hearts with black bile? Or is it a simulated piety? It makes no difference to me, since both deserve condemnation in great men.

units.la: Quos magicis aureis claudentis cantibus anguis Esse instar cautos pagina sacra jubet, Candoremq; simul mitis seruare columbæ, Fallereq; & falli grande putare nefas.
units.tr: The sacred page bids us be wary of those who, like a serpent, enclose themselves with magic songs of gold, and at the same time to keep the innocence of the gentle dove, and to regard it as a great wrong either to deceive or to be deceived.

units.la: Nos patimur segnes, lentiq; sedemus adiram, Et pietas ipsa religione perit. Si modo relligio est, alere intra viscera tetram, Quæ jam se corpus fundit in omne, luem: Si modo relligio est, patrijs, sine murmure, sulcis Accipere hostili seminaja stamanu.
units.tr: We suffer it, sluggish, and sit idle while the plague approaches slowly, and piety itself perishes through religion. If it is religion to nourish within our bowels a foul pestilence that already spreads through the whole body, if it is religion to receive without complaint the seeds of a hostile hand into our ancestral furrows.

units.la: Semina corrupti succi, lentiq; veneni, Noxia doctrinæ semina pestiferæ. Concipit inde malum quippe inconsulta juventus, Mox concepto alios inficit ipsa malo: Iamq; ferè totus sacer ordo, & Gallica pubes, Plebsq;, a vido virus combibit ore nocens. Iam turgent venæ, cor palpitat, ilia tendunt, Nullaq; pars toto corpore sana manet. Atq; utinam nunquam tibi crus, dux Loyola sestæ, Icisset læva missa sagitta manu. Gallia Cantabrico cum quondam & Iberia bello Propatrijs facerent pralia aperta focis.
units.tr: The seeds of a corrupt juice and of a slow poison, the harmful seeds of a pestilent doctrine. Thence, of course, the unadvised youth conceives the evil, and soon, having conceived it, it infects others with the same evil. And now almost the whole sacred order, the French youth and the common people alike, drink in the noxious poison from its greedy mouth. Now the veins swell, the heart throbs, the entrails are stretched, and no part of the whole body remains sound. And would that the sword, sent from your left hand, O Loyola, had never wounded your leg, when once Gaul and Iberia were waging war in Cantabria and fighting open battles for their native hearths.

units.la: Quam
units.tr: How

units.la: Quàm bello plus pace noces, & ad otia versus
units.tr: How much more you harm by peace than by war, and how you turn

units.la: Crudelem animum vertis ad insidias.
